500003|2026-03.headline: Aegis Logistics FY26 PAT rose 41% to INR1,107 crore and Q4 PAT rose 43% to INR455 crore, led by LPG distribution margins of about INR7,000 per ton.
500003|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue grew 23% to INR8,333 crore, normalized EBITDA rose 36% to INR1,599 crore, and PAT crossed INR1,000 crore for the first time. Q4 was the strongest quarter, with revenue up 52% to INR2,594 crore and normalized EBITDA up 54% to INR670 crore. The LPG segment drove the result, with distribution volumes up 45% in FY26 and 71% in Q4, while the Liquid segment was flat on revenue and EBITDA fell 5% for the year. Management outlined a large capex pipeline (about $1.2 billion to March 2027, about INR5,000 crore in FY28, about $5 billion through 2030/31) and said it expects to maintain FY27 momentum.

segments.name: LPG
segments.commentary: FY26 terminal throughput reached 5.15 million tons (+14%), distribution volumes 7.54 lakh MT (+45%) and sourcing sales 6.07 lakh MT (+2%). Q4 LPG revenue INR2,410 crore (+65%) and EBITDA INR549 crore (+136%), with Q4 distribution volume at a record 2.34 lakh MT (+71%).

segments.name: Liquid
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR644 crore and EBITDA INR472 crore (-5%), reflecting phasing of capacity additions and no major take-or-pay contribution versus last year. Q4 revenue INR184 crore and EBITDA INR126 crore.

guidance_outlook: Distribution margin guided at about INR7,000 per ton, which management expects to sustain through FY27 and beyond; FY26 average was about INR7,000 versus about INR4,000 in FY25.

Cumulative capex of about $1.2 billion by March 2027; about INR5,000 crore capex in FY28; about $5 billion pipeline through 2030/31 (management clarified the target is December 2030 and that heavy spending falls in FY29-FY31).
Long-term EPS CAGR guidance of about 25% reiterated; management said it is conservative and that it has beaten its own guidance.
Target of about 2 million tons of gas distribution (LPG plus ammonia) by FY28.

Ammonia: expected utilization about 25% in year one, then growing 30-40% a year; ammonia throughput margin INR2,500-3,000 per ton; distribution about 200,000 tons initially, growing 20-30% a year, margin up to INR5,000 per ton.
LPG supply shortfall improved from about 50% in April to about 30% in May; management expects normalcy around Q2 FY27 but declined to forecast precisely.
risks_watch: Distribution margin sustainability: the INR7,000 per ton level is tied to elevated energy prices and the war; management says it expects scale-driven procurement gains from FY28 but offered no quantified path.
LPG supply normalization: shortfall still about 30% in May; management expects normalcy around Q2 FY27 with no firm date.
Execution timing: JNPT, Mumbai, Kandla CRL 4, Pipavav jetty and ammonia terminal, and Kandla-Gorakhpur pipeline are all targeted for H1 FY27 or year-end FY27; slippage would delay volumes.
Capex step-up from about INR800 crore in FY26 to about $1.2 billion by March 2027 and about $5 billion by 2030; funding mix and gearing (about 0.6x) to watch.
Vadhavan port (about INR20,000 crore) remains a nonbinding MoU subject to approvals and land allocation; its inclusion in the capex pipeline is uncertain.
Ammonia economics are new and unproven for the company; utilization and margin targets are management estimates.
500003|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and bullish on growth and the energy-transition opportunity, but conservative on numbers: management declined to raise the 25% EPS CAGR guidance and said it prefers to under-promise. Evasive on exact timing of LPG normalization and on precise FY28-30 ammonia volumes.
key_quotes: We are a very conservative company and I think 25% CAGR growth is not small.
Going forward, we feel the INR7,000-odd margins should be sustainable as beyond '26, '27, we would see our distribution volumes really of a scale that brings procurement efficiencies.
So, we are very bullish. We have a partner, Itochu, along with us.
our sort of philosophy here at Aegis is really to not to overpromise, always to under promise, and hopefully overdeliver.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp Q4 jump in gas segment profitability per ton, was there a one-off, and what is the normalized level?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the margin averaged about INR7,000/MT vs INR4,000 in the prior year, with volume surge also contributing; it expects INR7,000-odd to be sustainable as scale brings procurement efficiencies, and full-year effects of Pipavav and Mangalore cryogenic terminals will add to EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: When will LPG supply fully normalize, and what is the FY27 and FY28 capex guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: LPG shortfall fell from about 50% in April to about 30% in May; normalcy is expected sometime in Q2. Capex is about $1.2 billion by March 2027 and about INR5,000 crore in FY28, both organic and inorganic.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Vadhavan MoU included in the capex pipeline, and what is the exact capex split of FY26 and FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said part of Vadhavan could be included in the $5 billion pipeline depending on land allotment and permits, but not all of it. The $5 billion is through December 2030 (not FY30), with heavy spend in FY29-FY31.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ammonia economics for utilization and margins, and does ammonia distribution reach INR5,000/ton?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilization is expected at about 25% in year one, then growing 30-40% a year; throughput margin INR2,500-3,000/MT; distribution starts at about 200,000 tons, growing 20-30% a year, with margin up to INR5,000/MT depending on the market.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin gain is from volumes versus price, and how will revenue trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said part of the rise from about INR4,000 to INR7,000 comes from volume-led procurement efficiencies (volumes went from about 5.2 lakh to 7.5 lakh MT) and part from margin improvement; it expects revenue to grow year on year as volume offsets price normalization.

qa_highlights.question: Why not raise the 25% EPS CAGR guidance, and what are the FY30 ammonia and LPG volume targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is conservative, has beaten its own guidance, and achieved 32% EPS CAGR over five years; EPS has moved from INR6 to INR26 with the CAGR guidance unchanged. It declined to give a precise FY30 ammonia volume, citing dependence on terminals commissioned and locations secured, but pointed to a 3 million ton ammonia supply-demand gap by 2029 per CRISIL.

500003|2026-06.headline: Aegis Logistics Q1 FY27 PAT rose 212% YoY to INR545 crore and normalized EBITDA 184% to INR727 crore, driven by a record LPG distribution quarter.
500003|2026-06.overview: Management reported record Q1 FY27 results, with PAT of INR545 crore (up 212% YoY) and normalized EBITDA of INR727 crore (up 184%). The Gas division posted its highest-ever EBITDA of INR591 crore (up 296% YoY), with distribution volumes of 2.77 lakh MT (up 91% YoY, up 19% QoQ). Liquids EBITDA rose 28% to INR136 crore on INR178 crore revenue. Management announced several port and capacity milestones, including commissioning of a 36,000 MT ammonia terminal at Pipavav and a Board-approved 52,000 MT LPG tank at JNPA.

qa_highlights.question: Is distribution volume growth ahead of expectations, and are the customer contracts sticky?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 2 million MT aim predates the war and reflects infrastructure build-out; new cryogenic terminals at Pipavav and Mangalore have added ullage and geography.

qa_highlights.question: How should EBITDA per ton be viewed near term and structurally?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR7,000+ per MT is sustainable. It expects the margin not to fall back to INR4,000, citing procurement gains from VLGC shipping as volumes rise.

qa_highlights.question: What are the per-unit margins for sourcing, logistics and distribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Liquids EBITDA is divided by capacity (about 2 million CBM). Logistics throughput gives close to INR1,000/MT EBITDA. Sourcing is a low contributor, at about $85-90/MT.

qa_highlights.question: What is the volume growth outlook beyond 25% CAGR?
qa_highlights.answer: 25% is the benchmark for logistics; anything above depends on the enablers. Distribution growth is expected to be higher, closer to 50%.

qa_highlights.question: Why not fill more storage given the ITOCHU partnership and the LPG supply deficit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not take inventory or price positions and will distribute on a monthly basis, rather than act as a trader.

qa_highlights.question: How will the cash across subsidiaries fund the capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: AVTL is self-funded through equity, and ITOCHU is planned to rise to 25% over three years. Standalone cash is around INR2,700 crore, and consolidated liquidity exceeds INR5,940 crore. Management will hold cash until it finds opportunities.

risks_watch: Distribution margin sustainability: management guides INR7,000+/MT for FY27-28 on VLGC freight savings, but Q1 and Q4 margins were not INR5,000 and no quarterly margin disclosure is given; track blended FY27 margin.

Geopolitical dependence: management links distribution volume and margin gains partly to Middle East war disruption and says normalization would change the mix; the 2 million MT aim now looks like 1 million MT this year and 1.5 million MT next year.

Capital deployment: roughly $1.2 billion capex in FY27 and a $5 billion pipeline through FY2030-31, funded by equity, accruals and debt at about 0.6 gearing; cash is spread across subsidiaries and AVTL depends on ITOCHU equity rising to 25% over three years.
Ammonia: Pipavav 36,000 MT terminal commissioned with a 15-year take-or-pay with Hindustan Zinc; ammonia distribution margins not disclosed and management asked to wait a quarter.

500008|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose about 15-16% to INR3,530 crore, with lead-acid margin near 12% despite raw-material inflation.
500008|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was about INR3,530 crore, up close to 15% YoY, with about 92% from Lead Acid Batteries and about INR280 crore from New Energy. Lead-acid revenue grew about 12% and 4-wheeler and 2-wheeler OEM volumes grew more than 30%, while aftermarket grew 5-6%. Standalone EBITDA margin was about 11%, and lead-acid operating margin was about 11.6% after adjusting for lithium pack trading, with management citing raw-material and alloy cost spikes linked to the geopolitical conflict. FY26 consolidated revenue was INR13,814 crore (up about 7.5%) with a 10.8% consolidated margin; the company guided FY27 capex of INR1,500-1,700 crore, mostly in New Energy.

qa_highlights.question: Is equipment for the 2 GWh cell line ordered, and what are the commissioning constraints?
qa_highlights.answer: Equipment has been ordered; the constraint is limited visas for Chinese engineers to commission it, with a few visas issued and engineers on ground at CQP.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Gotion partnership and LFP plant timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Technology licensing from China is being discouraged by Beijing; management says product development is now largely India-driven. The Gotion tie-up was corporate-to-corporate with no government approval sought. First capacity next year will be NMC; LFP is 2028 or later.

qa_highlights.question: What are the BESS margins once stabilised?
qa_highlights.answer: Initial operating margin about 6-7%, with upside as scale improves; the BESS plant is seen as a strategic lever for ESS cell manufacturing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 outlook for replacement and industrial segments, and Q4 growth by segment?
qa_highlights.answer: OEM 2W and 4W grew more than 30%, aftermarket 5-6%, other industrial 3-4%, telecom declining; FY27 growth guided at mid to high single digit.

qa_highlights.question: How much raw material inflation and price hikes should be expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Lead and alloys about 70% of RM; plastics about 10% with possible 40% increase; another 2-3% price increase likely, possibly insufficient to offset full cost pressure.

qa_highlights.question: Who is the offtaker for the 16 GWh capacity, and what is the ROCE on the capex?
qa_highlights.answer: No binding offtake for the 2 GWh; EV programs have take-or-pay style safeguards; ESS to be offtaken partly by own systems. At 8-10 GWh scale, EBITDA margin 10-11% and ROCE expected low double-digit; cost disadvantage vs China imports of about 15-20% expected to be bridged over time with localisation.

qa_highlights.question: Will lead-acid capacity be underutilised as EV penetration rises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees a long runway for lead-acid given ICE OE growth, replacement demand and auxiliary batteries; telecom plant still running at 30-40 million Ah; capacity unlocked within existing footprint.

500008|2026-06.headline: Amara Raja Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose ~24% to ~INR4,215 crore, but consolidated EBITDA margin fell to 9.6% on input costs and strategic spends.

Standalone EBITDA margin was about 10.1% and consolidated 9.6%, hit by raw material inflation (alloy, sulfuric acid, poly), brand spends including IPL, Amaron Assist pilot, Factory of the Future costs and higher warranty provisions. Management took ~3% price hikes in June with a further 2-3% planned in the current month, but B2B pass-through lags. Automotive international volumes fell about 20% on Middle East disruption, and management expects recovery in subsequent quarters.

MMR sales about INR59,500 crores in 2QFY27 (up 11% YoY); commercial leasing 21 million sq ft in Q2 (up 6% YoY), GCCs about 41% of leasing.

Sustenance sales (around INR3 billion per quarter per analyst) below expectation; management said 78% of inventory sold, with some projects (Birla Mrida) lagging.

qa_highlights.question: What were gross presales and cancellations in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reported only net sales of INR298 crores and did not give gross or cancellation figures.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Niyaara Tower C GDV raised by about INR2,000-3,000 crores, and what does it mean for launch timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Amalgamating the original Niyaara plot with the Wadia plot allowed FSI to be loaded onto Tower C, raising its GDV by INR3,000 crores; net Worli GDV rises INR1,900 crores after deferring other value. Launch now targeted Q2 FY28, with no consideration paid for the FSI reconfiguration.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 presales falling short, and why not prepone launches such as Arika phase 2 or Vashi?

qa_highlights.question: How is BD progressing against the INR10,000-15,000 crores guidance?

qa_highlights.question: Why are NCR cancellations rising at Arika and Pravaah?

qa_highlights.question: How much EBITDA and revenue will Niyaara Tower A recognise in FY28 and FY29?

qa_highlights.question: What is the commercial rental and capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Annual rental income target raised from INR150 crores to above INR1,500 crores over time, including Century Bhavan redevelopment (INR400-450 crores) and the 1.3 million sq ft Worli commercial building; the 2.3 million sq ft Wadia plot is excluded from this target.

500042|2026-03.headline: BASF India FY26 PBT before exceptionals rose to Rs 564 crore from Rs 600 crore equivalent comparison; Q4 PBT Rs 90 crore vs Rs 25 crore a year ago.

Q4 showed volume-led growth (about 12-15% volume growth YoY, sales up about 10%) and PBT before exceptionals of Rs 90 crore against Rs 25 crore in March 2025. Working capital rose about Rs 600-800 crore, pushing FY26 operating cash flow to about minus Rs 110 crore versus Rs 370 crore last year. Management flagged the West Asia conflict, feedstock inflation, rupee depreciation and a possible demand softening in the coming months, and said no plants were shut down.

qa_highlights.question: Why have agro margins compressed over FY25-FY26 despite new launches, and are these the normalised margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited erratic monsoons, soft commodity prices (chilli acreage and intensity down), and high channel inventories. It said the 12 launches in four years are about 25% of ag sales and carry higher margins, and that channel inventory is healthy. It gave no view on normalised margins.

qa_highlights.question: How are raw material cost increases being passed on, and is demand responding?

qa_highlights.question: Is there any new CAPEX planned, and how much will be spent in FY27?

500043|2026-03.headline: Bata India posted a second straight quarter of 5%+ value growth in Q4 FY26; like-to-like PBT grew about 11% after excluding four non-cash items.
500043|2026-03.overview: Management reported a second consecutive quarter of accelerating, volume-backed growth of 5%+ in value, with broad-based growth across channels and categories. Reported PBT fell about 94% due to exceptional items, mainly a plant closure (VRS) cost and a INR220 million FX impact on a licensing liability. Excluding four non-cash items, like-to-like PBT grew about 11% and cash flow from operations grew about 18%. Inventory fell 13% YoY and 28% over two years while availability rose about 1,000 bps, and ZBM stores were scaled to about 700 by May 2026.

segments.name: Retail (COCO/ZBM)
segments.commentary: Volume-led DOS growth; ZBM stores at about 550 last quarter with about 50-55% of COCO sales, rising to about 700 stores (about 70% of sales) by end-May 2026. Target of 800-850 stores by quarter end.

segments.name: Franchise (FOFO)
segments.commentary: Franchise stores crossed 700 with double-digit growth and higher overall profitability; franchise share is close to double digit of revenue. Management targets nearing 1,000 stores in the next 12 months.

segments.name: Multi-brand distribution (MBO)
segments.commentary: Expanded to about 1,670 towns; channel is showing early signs of growth after pressure in towns below 1,000. Distribution is about 10-12% of revenue.

segments.name: E-commerce
segments.commentary: Fastest-growing channel across B2B, B2C and dot-com; about 8-10% of revenue per CFO, about 12-13% per CEO. Over 700 stores fulfil online orders.

segments.name: Brands: Hush Puppies and Power/HP premium
segments.commentary: Hush Puppies is about 18-20% of turnover and the fastest-growing brand. Premium HP and Power portfolio is outpacing overall growth.

segments.commentary: About 35-40% of revenue; declined for about 3 years but has stabilised and is now growing roughly in line with the overall ~5% top line.

guidance_outlook: Inventory is about 70-75% of the way through the reduction programme, with a target turn of about 3 versus about 2.7 currently, without compromising availability.

Raw material inflation is about 5-6% blended as of the last review; price increases of 5-6% are planned but not yet rolled out.
Franchise store count to approach 1,000 within about 12 months; ZBM stores to reach about 800-850 by the current quarter end.
Management declined to give forward-looking guidance on bata.com or overall D2C growth for FY27.
capex_capacity: One manufacturing facility closed in the quarter, with a related VRS exceptional cost; management is removing legacy factories and consolidating to a few large suppliers.

Marketing spend is about 1.5x prior levels, with digital about 80-85% of the spend.
Sneakers proposition under development to target younger consumers; details to be shared later.

Full-price sales are growing faster, with markdowns lower; gross margin optics are diluted by franchise mix and a one-off INR60 million provision reversal in the base quarter.
Trade receivables rose about 65% YoY, attributed to channel mix (wholesale, franchise, B2B e-commerce) and base effect; management says provisions for doubtful debts show no deterioration.
Minimum wage hikes in Haryana, UP and Karnataka are seen as structural; the company is spread across 30 states and only 3-4 are affected so far.

qa_highlights.question: Is inventory at a desirable level, and why is lower discounting not showing in gross margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Turns are about 2.7 against a target of about 3. Gross margin optics are diluted by the shift to franchise (lower GM%, accretive to EBIT) and a INR60 million provision reversal in base Q4 FY25.

qa_highlights.question: What raw material and minimum wage impact is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended raw material inflation is about 5-6% and is being covered by inventory, hedges and price elasticity-led pricing. Management sees no direct impact yet, and wage hikes are structural but partly offset because many stores already pay above minimum wage.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the Bata brand's revenue growth been stagnant, and what changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to inventory simplification, which had deteriorated and is now recovering, along with franchise expansion, SIS, digital, and product and marketing levers.

qa_highlights.question: How long will vendor and store revamps take to reach the bottom line?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees underlying operating leverage coming through from store revamp, inventory decluttering and supplier consolidation, with benefits in coming periods.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade receivables rise about 65% YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Due to channel mix, with more credit in wholesale, franchise and B2B e-commerce, plus a base effect. Management says the quality is fine and doubtful-debt provisions are steady.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue split between below and above INR1,000 products, and what is Hush Puppies' contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Below INR1,000 is about 35-40% of revenue and has stabilised. Hush Puppies is about 18-20% of turnover. Management will provide the exact split offline, and it could not give FY25/FY26 volume growth on the call.

qa_highlights.question: What is the channel mix?
qa_highlights.answer: COCO is about 65% and non-COCO about 35%. Within non-COCO, franchise is close to double digit, e-commerce about 8-10% and distribution about 10-12%.

segments.commentary: Q4 NSR INR51,000/t; April INR56,700/t and mid-May about INR56,000/t. Flat price increase in March was about INR1,400/t. A safeguard duty on flat imports is in place.

segments.name: Bokaro Steel Plant
segments.commentary: EBITDA recovered sharply in H2 FY26 after FY25 breakdowns and a Hot Strip Mill repair that ran 2 months beyond plan. Better flat-product NSR and SMS fixes also helped, and management expects further improvement in FY27.

segments.name: Salem (stainless)
segments.commentary: Still loss-making. CR mill yield is 83-84% against a 90% target, and LPG has been replaced with PNG. Management plans to feed imported stainless slabs to idle CR and SR mill capacity.

segments.name: NSL / RINL volumes
segments.commentary: NSL total volume was 1.12 mn tons in FY26, with Q4 near 0.1 mn tons. Sales of RINL products began in February, at about 48,000-50,000 tons in Q4, and are guided at 0.6-0.7 mn tons in FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 sales volume target of 22 mn tons (about 22.5 mn tons including RINL products), up from 19.9 mn tons in FY26.
FY27 crude steel production target of 22.5 mn tons against stated capacity of 21 mn tons, to be reached through debottlenecking and operational efficiency.

Capex guidance: INR15,000 crore in FY27, INR18,000-19,000 crore in FY28, and INR20,000-25,000 crore per year after that, to be funded mainly from internal accruals with incremental long-term borrowings.
Coke rate target to fall by about INR20/kg in FY27 after the earlier reduction; management aims for a further drop in coke rate.

Employee strength is 49,752 as of 1 April 2026, with a further reduction of 3,400-3,500 expected in each of FY27 and FY28. A VRS targeting 500-1,000 exits is under way. Pay revision from 1 January 2027 is not yet in the guidance and will be provided for in Q4 FY27.

Q1 FY27 inventory: management aims for no build-up in Q1 and expects Q2 to be sluggish with inventory reduction in Q3 and Q4. Coking coal cost is up about INR2,000/t to about INR21,500/t, implying a cost impact of INR1,400-1,500/t on production cost.
capex_capacity: Crude steel capacity is 21 mn tons; FY26 output was 19.43 mn tons. FY27 target is 22.5 mn tons through debottlenecking and operating beyond rated capacity.

New capacity expansion projects at IISCO (about 4.5 mn tons, INR35,000-36,000 crore), Bhilai (about 3.5 mn tons, about INR30,000 crore, yet to be announced) and Bokaro (about 3 mn tons, about INR18,000 crore) are the three cleared expansions.

IISCO packages are tendered and groundwork is starting, with spending rising from FY28 and some spending in Q4 FY27. Bokaro and Bhilai spending is mainly expected from FY29; new capacity is expected from FY30-31.
Capex in FY27 covers debottlenecking, AMR (asset modernisation/replacement) and expansion projects.
Iron ore: FY26 production was 38 mn tons with a 56 mn ton target for FY27 and 80 mn tons as the longer-term ramp-up goal. The Chiria mine is a new lease, not a renewal.
demand_pricing: Indian steel consumption grew about 8% in FY26 while production grew 11%. India became a marginal net exporter, with exports of 6.5 mn tons and imports of 6.6 mn tons.
Q1 demand is expected to be muted, with destocking, then a pickup from Q3. Rupee depreciation and firmer international prices support landed cost and selling prices.

Cost pressure: the Middle East situation pushed up limestone/flux costs (CFR from about $23-24 to about $35/t), with an impact of only INR100-200/t on saleable steel. Fuel constraints were managed through PNG and LPG banks.
Rail freight prices: FY25 arrears were about INR1,800 crore; FY26 provisional rates are lower, and the FY25 rate finalisation could affect FY27. Management said the direction is unclear.
Flat safeguard duty and cheaper import blends are limiting import volumes.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 and FY28 volume guidance and capex plans?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 sales target of 22 mn tons (vs 19.9 mn in FY26); FY27 capex INR15,000 crore against about INR9,100 crore in FY26; FY28 about INR18,000-19,000 crore; then INR20,000-25,000 crore per year.

qa_highlights.question: Realisations in Q4 and April-May, and cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 blended NSR about INR52,000/t; April about INR57,000/t. Coking coal rose from INR18,200/t in Q4 to about INR21,000 in April and INR21,800 in May. Q1 consumption cost impact is smaller because of about 30 days of inventory.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity and the path to 22.5 mn tons?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is 21 mn tons. Growth to 22.5 mn tons comes from debottlenecking and efficiency gains, with new capacity only from FY30-31. Management said output could reach 23 mn tons later.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Q3 to Q4 EBITDA bridge explained?
qa_highlights.answer: Input prices were a INR272 crore headwind, offset by a INR429 crore gain from better raw-material usage (higher PCI, more oxygen, better iron ore use).

qa_highlights.question: Can 100%+ utilisation be sustained given the capacity figures?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said DPR capacity is not a hard limit for blast furnaces and SMS; productivity can exceed design, citing examples of 2.3 going to 3 and the operations of peers.

qa_highlights.question: How will the capex be funded and what is the leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects internal accruals to cover most of FY27 capex, with incremental long-term borrowings beyond that. Net debt to equity is 0.37 and is expected to fall further in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will working capital rise with the monsoon season?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims for no inventory build in Q1 but said Q2 will be challenging, with inventory reduction planned for Q3 and Q4.

risks_watch: Wage revision from 1 January 2027: the impact is not yet in guidance and may be booked in Q4 FY27; past revisions were about 15%.
Coking coal and imported coal costs are rising, with the Q1 cost impact estimated at INR1,400-1,500/t against a NSR tailwind.
Q1 and Q2 demand softness and destocking; inventory build risk.
Rail freight price finalisation for FY25 could go either way in FY27.
Middle East supply disruption affecting fuel, flux and raw material routes (Strait of Hormuz).
Salem Steel Plant losses and BISL disinvestment status; the Chiria mining lease is still pending.
Achieving 22 mn tons on the 21 mn ton stated capacity and funding INR15,000 crore capex in FY27.
500113|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on FY26 profit growth, volume records and the clean audit position, with a clear FY27 target. Cautious on Q1-Q2 demand and on the outcome of the wage revision and rail price decisions, which management called unclear.
key_quotes: So far as expansions are concerned, actually, we've cleared for 3 plants.

Company has posted highest ever sales volume at 19.9 million tons, almost like 20 million tons, which margina lly -- I mean, it is close to 20 million tons with a growth of 11% as compared to the previous year.
after a pretty long time, many years and decades, you can say, that the balance sheet of '25 -'26 is totally clean from the qualifications.
But overall, in sellable steel, its impact will be hardly INR100 or INR200.
So you can say that the cost impact will be around INR1,400 to INR1,500 per ton.

500113|2026-06.headline: SAIL Q1 FY27 EBITDA rose over 50% to INR4,356 crore (16.7% margin) despite 4.8 Mt crude steel output, aided by advanced capital repairs and better NSR.
500113|2026-06.overview: SAIL reported Q1 FY27 EBITDA of INR4,356 crore versus INR2,925 crore a year earlier, with margin of 16.7% and EBITDA per tonne of INR10,464. PBT and PAT rose to INR2,159 crore and INR1,636 crore from INR890 crore and INR685 crore. Crude steel output fell to 4.8 Mt (4.9 Mt CPLY) and sales volume dropped about 7-8% to 4.2 Mt, as major capital repairs at IISCO, Durgapur and Bokaro were advanced into Q1 by design. Average NSR was INR57,100/t, up about INR5,000/t from Q4 FY26, and borrowings were flat at INR21,729 crore versus INR21,663 crore at 1 March 2026.

financial_highlights.change: up more than 50% vs CPLY INR2,925 crore
vs INR685 crore CPLY, about 150% growth
up about INR5,000/t vs Q4 FY26 (INR52,000/t)
vs INR21,663 crore on 1 March 2026; about INR21,400 crore today
from about 0.38-0.39 at start of year
vs Q1 target of INR2,306 crore
vs INR2,944 crore CPLY; includes differential VRS cost

segments.name: Iron ore / mines (third-party sales)
segments.commentary: Q1 iron ore sales turnover INR574 crore vs INR157 crore CPLY, with volume 1.1 Mt vs 0.31 Mt; EBITDA about INR150 crore. Sales are mainly from Odisha group of mines, and Chhattisgarh auctions have fructified for Q2.

segments.name: Product mix
segments.commentary: Flats about 52.7% and longs about 34.8% of sales; semis fell to about 11-12.5% from 14% in Q1 FY26. Finished steel share rose to 89% from 86%.

segments.name: NMDC Steel / RINL
segments.commentary: NMDC Steel marketing sales were nil vs 3.73 lakh t CPLY; RINL semis sales were about 93,000 t (new this year). NSL plus RINL combined was about 2.76 lakh t CPLY.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 volume guidance maintained, with growth over FY26 expected by year-end; Q2-Q4 production to exceed last year's levels.
Q2 NSR expected to be about INR1,000-2,000/t lower than Q1; July NSR averaged INR55,600/t (flats INR56,900, longs INR54,200).
Imported coking coal cost expected to fall about INR1,000-2,000/t from August; Q2 coal cost seen INR1,000-1,500/t below Q1 (Q1 imported INR21,300/t).
FY27 capex target INR15,000 crore, rising to over INR20,000 crore in FY28 and about INR25,000-26,000 crore thereafter.
Cost reduction of about INR2,000/t targeted in FY27 from Q2 onward; by FY29 variable cost down INR3,000-4,000/t from IISCO expansion, with fixed cost up INR1,500-2,000/t, net about INR2,000/t.
Inventory to be held flat in Q2 and reduced in Q3 and Q4 to lower FY27 inventory year-on-year.
Railway price revision for FY27 expected in FY28; management says no further downward hit to P&L expected.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex INR2,575 crore against Q1 target INR2,306 crore; full-year target INR15,000 crore.
Major capital repairs advanced into Q1 at IISCO, Durgapur and Bokaro, reducing crude steel output by about 0.1 Mt vs CPLY.
Durgapur: TMT bar mill planned to produce 0.8-0.9 Mt/yr, expected September to December 2027; this will sharply reduce semis availability from Durgapur.
Captive Tasra coking coal mine under development, production expected around December 2026; captive mine coal cost estimated INR5,000-6,000/t vs indigenous average INR13,100/t.
Subgrade iron ore fines inventory about 32 Mt; first auction of about 3 Mt put up, with rates awaited.
demand_pricing: Indian steel consumption grew more than 8% YoY in Q1 FY27 while production grew about 3%; net imports about 0.4-0.5 Mt vs about 0.3 Mt CPLY.
Gap between primary and secondary TMT narrowed to about INR5,000/t.
June to July long-product prices fell about INR2,000-3,000/t; recent upward momentum of INR500-1,000/t expected. Flat product prices fell about INR1,000/t between June and July.
Safeguard duty of 11.5% remains in place (second year of three-year term). Anti-dumping investigation has been initiated and may bring relief.
Government imposed definitive anti-dumping duty on met coke; management says no impact as SAIL has captive coke capacity matching its needs.
Coal mix: about 85% imported, 15% indigenous (of which about 5% from captive mines). Imported coking coal: hard about 62%, soft about 23%.
Rail price: provisional FY27 price about INR74,000/t, which management expects to be revised upward.

qa_highlights.question: What were Q1 NSR vs Q4, and how do July prices and Q2 NSR look?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 NSR was INR57,100/t vs Q4 INR52,000/t. Monsoon-driven seasonal decline expected in Q2, with Q2 NSR about INR1,000-2,000/t lower than Q1; longs more affected than flats.

qa_highlights.question: Is full-year volume guidance intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; management maintained full-year volume guidance and expects growth over last year by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for coal costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Imported coal was INR21,300/t in Q1 vs INR18,100/t in Q4. Index fell from about 235 to 220; coal cost expected to fall INR1,000-2,000/t from August.

qa_highlights.question: Is third-party iron ore sales growth sustainable, and what about subgrade inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Mines sales more than doubled YoY, adding about INR400 crore turnover and INR150 crore profit. Target of about 8 Mt for captive mines; subgrade inventory about 32 Mt with 3 Mt first auction in progress.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 capex and beyond?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 target INR15,000 crore; FY28 above INR20,000 crore; later years INR25,000-26,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost-reduction plan through FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR2,000/t cost cut in FY27 from Q2; by FY29 IISCO expansion cuts variable cost INR3,000-4,000/t, with fixed cost up INR1,500-2,000/t, net about INR2,000/t.

qa_highlights.question: How much did the Gulf conflict affect input costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Fuel impact limited due to in-plant gas use; flux cost up on freight but offset by lower usage, saving about INR25 crore. Limestone and imported coal costs rose; coal up about INR3,500/t YoY.

risks_watch: Q2 seasonal weakness: monsoon-driven NSR decline and rain-hit demand; management aims to hold inventory flat in Q2.
Logistics constraints (rake availability) still limit mine sales; subgrade auction outcome pending.
Pay commission from 1 January 2027; wage provision decision deferred to Q4 FY27.
Railway price revision (FY27 price to be set in FY28) and anti-dumping outcome on flats.
Working capital borrowings reduction and inventory reduction in Q3-Q4 to meet deleveraging goal.
Production volume recovery in Q2-Q4 after Q1 maintenance; Tasra captive coal timing (around December 2026).
500113|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on profitability and cost trajectory, with the margin and per-tonne EBITDA framed as best-in-years. Cautious and hedged on Q2 pricing and volume, with many figures described as guesswork and some answers unclear or deflected.
key_quotes: EBITDA margin at 16.7% is one of the best since '21 -'22, when the steel market at that time was at its peak and coal price was at its bottom in '21 -'22.
EBITDA per tonne also crossed a benchmark figure of INR10,000 per tonne and stood at INR10,464 per tonne in quarter 1 '26 -'27.
Yes, we are maintaining the full year volume, and we'll be having a growth over last year by the year-end.
So far as capex is concerned, this year, we're planning a target of INR15,000 crores, and this is going to increase in the next 2, 3 years because our expanses are on.

500114|2026-06.headline: Titan Q1 FY27: customs-duty gain of ₹407 crore and a ₹75-80 bps gold MTM gain lifted jewellery margin; normalised TMZ EBIT margin 10.9%.
500114|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as strong, with growth across jewellery, watches, eyecare, subsidiaries and brands, and a rise in buyer growth. Results included one-off gains: ₹407 crore consolidated gain from the customs duty hike (6% to 15%; ₹386 crore in Tanishq/Mia/Zoya, ₹21 crore in CaratLane) and a 75-80 bps MTM gain in jewellery EBIT from gold price divergence, both expected to reverse or be realised over the next 2-3 quarters. Management said the 10.9% normalised TMZ EBIT margin compares with 11.3% in Q1 FY26 once the 50 bps one-off in the base quarter is considered. May saw about three weeks of softness (PM call-out, customs change, Adhik Maas) that management says recovered in June. Jewellery guidance was unchanged, with management reiterating a double-digit value growth target and an 11% EBIT margin centre of gravity.

financial_highlights.change: Of which ₹386 crore Tanishq/Mia/Zoya and ₹21 crore CaratLane; to be realised as inventory sells over next couple of quarters
vs 11.3% in Q1 FY26 normalised for 50 bps one-off; vs 11.8% reported in base quarter per analyst

financial_highlights.metric: Gold MTM gain in jewellery EBIT
financial_highlights.change: Expected to reverse in coming quarters
vs 18.6% in Q1 FY26 normalised; standard costing benefit far lower than ~₹50 crore last year
Management recalled figure, not confirmed on the call

segments.name: Jewellery (Tanishq, Mia, Zoya)
segments.commentary: Normalised EBIT margin 10.9% after ₹386 crore customs gain and 75-80 bps MTM gain; studded demand recovered since Q4 FY26 and studded share rose; plain gold softened late July.

segments.name: Watches
segments.commentary: Reported EBIT margin looks muted; normalised 17.8% vs 18.6% last year after much smaller standard costing revaluation benefit.

segments.name: CaratLane
segments.commentary: ₹21 crore customs duty gain included; management sees margin trending to double-digit, around 10%, long term.

segments.name: TEAL (Titan Engineering & Automation)
segments.commentary: Project business with lumpy margins; Q1 boosted by refit/retrofit servicing; normalised margin to gravitate to 12-15-16%.

segments.name: International (Damas and others)
segments.commentary: Damas made a loss due to war-related fall in Middle East footfall and ticket size; rest of international portfolio earns mid-single-digit EBIT (5-6%); management expects full-year positive international EBIT.

guidance_outlook: Jewellery EBIT margin centre of gravity around 11% (plus/minus), unchanged; management said gross-margin initiatives and studded mix should help more in H2 than H1.
Customs duty gains to flow through in Q2 and Q3; management declined to quantify full-year impact.
Double-digit healthy value growth in jewellery remains the target; FY30 goals unchanged per management.
CaratLane to move towards double-digit EBIT margin (around 10%) over time; TEAL normalised margin 12-16%.
Management said July was not bad overall but plain gold softened towards end-July; no near-term quarterly guidance given.
capex_capacity: No capacity or capex figures were discussed on the call.
demand_pricing: Buyer growth about 5% for the quarter per analyst question; May weakness from PM call-out (May 10), customs change (May 13) and Adhik Maas (from May 17) recovered in June.
Studded jewellery demand rising since Q4 FY26; coin growth expected to moderate; plain gold softened late July.
Competitive intensity unchanged; no easing in making charges, with regional variation (e.g. Gujarat).
Festival of Diamonds offer is a flat 20% off diamond value, similar to the prior Jan-Feb offer.
Natural diamond retail prices stable; lab-grown vs natural narrative reportedly less prominent.
Cash-for-gold scheme launched in all stores in June; limited traction so far; margin-neutral per management.

qa_highlights.question: Has postponed demand returned, and will growth improve in the current quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Arun Narayan said May softness lasted about 3 weeks; June recovered and management believes lost May demand was regained in June, with no carry-over into Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Would management revisit jewellery EBIT growth or margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashok Sonthalia said no new guidance; the earlier 11% centre-of-gravity view stands given gold price volatility.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 50 bps one-off and 80 bps MTM reverse, and how much customs gain comes later?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the MTM gain will reverse as inventory is realised over 2-3 quarters; customs gain runs into Q2 and Q3, but no full-year quantum was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Damas lose money, and what is the international margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed war-related footfall and ticket size declines in Dubai and Saudi; the rest of the international portfolio makes 5-6% EBIT, and the full year is expected to stay EBIT-positive.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins hold up if gold inflation falls to zero and growth slows?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would push buyer acquisition, that the FY30 plan is unchanged, and that quarterly numbers may vary.

qa_highlights.question: What is the source of the exchange share increase and its margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Exchange-linked sales exceed 50% of business; the share spiked during a three-week May overdrive and then normalised; no margin direction was given.

risks_watch: Gold price volatility and softer plain gold demand from late July; buyer growth sensitivity to price direction.
Reversal of the 75-80 bps MTM gain and the 50 bps base-quarter one-off, plus customs gain timing; watch H2 margin against a high base.
Damas international losses while Middle East conflict continues.
Rising exchange share and competitive discounting in studded jewellery and in Gujarat.
Whether May-June catch-up holds through Q2 and July demand softness persists.
500114|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, buyers and studded momentum, but cautious on margin and guidance: management refused to change jewellery margin or full-year customs-gain guidance, citing gold volatility and the gains' reversal.
key_quotes: It's been another fantastic quarter, and I must say this quarter has been even better than the previous quarters.
So the normalized margin considering both custom duty gain and MTM gain, the normalized EBIT margin for our Tanishq Mia Zoya business would be 10.9%, the number for this quarter.
We are not changing it.
So for us to target a healthy double-digit growth in jewellery is inevitable.

500117|2026-06.headline: DCW Q1 FY27 EBITDA fell 28% YoY to INR41.4 crore as PVC losses (West Asia VCM shortage, duty suspension) hit Basic Chemicals to a negative INR14 crore EBITDA.
500117|2026-06.overview: Revenue rose 14% YoY to INR542 crore, led by Specialty Chemicals (INR177 crore, 33% of revenue, up 38% YoY), but fell 11% QoQ on a one-time Q4 Synthetic Rutile inventory liquidation base effect. Consolidated EBITDA including other income was INR41.4 crore, down 28% YoY and 41% QoQ, with management attributing the drop mainly to PVC disruption. Basic Chemicals EBITDA was negative INR14 crore, while Specialty EBITDA grew about 20% YoY. Management guided that PVC conditions have improved since Q1 and that FY27 should close better than FY26, while also announcing a INR250 crore capex programme and an intent to be effectively net debt free by end-FY27.

financial_highlights.change: +38% YoY (as stated in opening remarks); +6% QoQ

financial_highlights.value: Not stated in INR; margin 29.1% (analyst-computed from Q1 FY26 33.6%)
Negative INR14 crore (-5.2% margin per analyst)

financial_highlights.change: from migration to new tax regime (25.17% vs 34.9%)

segments.name: Specialty Chemicals (CPVC, SIOP)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR177 crore, up 38% YoY with CPVC volumes up 59% and SIOP volumes up about 3%. EBITDA grew about 20% YoY and 35% QoQ; margin about 29% vs 33.6% a year ago, which management linked to PVC-CPVC spread volatility.

segments.name: Basic Chemicals (PVC, caustic soda, soda ash, Synthetic Rutile)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR361 crore, down 18% QoQ on Q4 Synthetic Rutile inventory liquidation. EBITDA negative INR14 crore; management estimated a sequential PVC contribution swing of INR50-55 crore, with caustic soda and Synthetic Rutile margins improving.

guidance_outlook: FY27 expected to close at a better level than FY26, based on current visibility (management).
Basic Chemicals expected to do better than Q1; management says breakeven in Q2 is more than believed if normalcy holds.
Steady-state EBITDA assessed at about INR300 crore, replacing the earlier INR400 crore target.
Legacy long-term debt expected to be fully repaid in FY27 (repayments about INR135 crore); effectively net debt free by end-FY27 before new borrowings.
Targeting minimum incremental ROCE of 20% on new investments.
Expects to borrow slightly more than repayments for the capex, with a 1-1.5% negative carry on cash-to-borrowing.
capex_capacity: INR250 crore programme over 2-3 years; first part is SIOP capacity expansion from about 30,000 tpa to 45,000 tpa, with Phase 1 adding 7,000 tpa by Q4 FY28 and infrastructure sized for a further 8,000 tpa.
Captive power infrastructure at Sahupuram facility, targeted for Q4 FY28, to lower power costs across Specialty and Basic Chemicals.
SIOP expansion is brownfield; expected margin around 35-36% and product price north of INR80,000/ton (management).
Current PVC capacity about 1 lakh tpa; CPVC about 50,000 tpa; SIOP capacity 28 kt fully tied up this year after debottlenecking.
Synthetic Rutile capacity about 48,000-50,000 tpa; caustic soda realistic capacity about 90,000 tpa.
demand_pricing: PVC: West Asia conflict cut VCM availability from traditional Asian suppliers, forcing spot purchases from China at higher prices; import duty suspension let in lower-priced imports. Duties now reinstated and a minimum import price (MIP, about USD/INR80 per ton equivalent) introduced for suspension-grade PVC.
Management said current import parity is about USD820-860/ton, well above MIP, and expects prices to stay at these levels at least this quarter.
PVC/VCM spread was estimated at north of INR25,000/ton; PVC-to-CPVC spread lags because of existing customer orders.
Synthetic Rutile: prices recovered vs last year's inventory-correction slump; customer mix improved and high-priced deliveries are back-ended.

SIOP: around 60% of output exported, mainly to the US; management says no tariff impact on exports. Volumes are seasonally higher in Q3 and Q4. Ammonia cost increases were passed through to customers.
Caustic soda margins expanded QoQ and YoY; chlorine is now fully consumed captively for CPVC, improving caustic ECU realisation.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the QoQ revenue decline came from captive PVC use, lower PVC output and the Synthetic Rutile base effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Q4 Synthetic Rutile liquidation base effect was the main driver, plus a few days of PVC plant shutdown; it did not quantify the split, but said the Synthetic Rutile effect alone would have exceeded the top-line decline.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Specialty margins compress and is about 29% the new normal?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins depend on the dynamic PVC-CPVC spread, which is volatile. SIOP margins are robust, and a steady-state margin is hard to pin down because roughly 40-50% of PVC goes into CPVC.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Basic Chemicals' loss came from PVC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave only a directional estimate: a sequential contribution swing of INR50-55 crore in PVC. It confirmed PVC was the only loss-making Basic Chemicals product, with caustic soda, soda ash and Synthetic Rutile profitable.

qa_highlights.question: Does the INR400 crore EBITDA target still stand?
qa_highlights.answer: No. It was set when CPVC margins were about 40%. Management now sees steady-state EBITDA of about INR300 crore, subject to the spread holding.

qa_highlights.question: Would a share buyback be considered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is still considering a buyback and will announce it at an opportune time if it decides to proceed.

qa_highlights.question: How is VCM sourced, and can it be derisked or backward integrated?
qa_highlights.answer: Supply moved from a single Qatar producer to a global distributor sourcing across Asia. Management ruled out backward integration at current scale; storage expansion would add only about 10-15 days of inventory.

risks_watch: Whether VCM supply from the global distributor and import parity (about USD820-860/ton) hold through the quarter, and whether PVC prices stay clear of the MIP level.
PVC-to-CPVC spread lag: management flagged that old customer orders priced at lower spreads will weigh on Specialty margins as PVC prices rise.
Basic Chemicals breakeven in Q2 FY27 depends on the situation staying normal; management said July still carried stock bought at high VCM costs.

Execution and funding of the INR250 crore capex: SIOP Phase 1 (7,000 tpa) and Sahupuram captive power both targeted for Q4 FY28; borrowing slightly above repayments of about INR135 crore, with negative carry of 1-1.5%.

500136|2026-03.headline: Ester Industries Q4 FY26 consolidated adjusted EBITDA of INR53.6 crore (15.5% margin) excluding INR10.24 crore FX-loan MTM; reported net loss of INR27.5 crore for FY26.
500136|2026-03.overview: Management framed Q4 FY26 as an inflection point, citing moderation of Chinese dumping and US tariff disruption plus higher BOPET prices and a weaker rupee lifting spreads. Consolidated total income rose 7.2% YoY to INR345.1 crore in Q4, with reported EBITDA of INR43.3 crore (12.6%) and PAT of INR7.9 crore. Full-year consolidated net loss of INR27.5 crore was driven mainly by non-cash MTM losses on euro-denominated term loans and a INR2.7 crore labour-code gratuity charge. Management expects BOPET margins to hold for 18 to 24 months, though Specialty Polymers softened in the quarter on demand loss in one marquee product and mix shift.

segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 films revenue INR321 crore (+14.9% YoY) on 19,656 MT volume (+2.3% YoY); FY26 volume 80,517 MT (+5.1%). VAS products were 25% of FY26 volume, growing 14.5% in volume despite US tariff-related loss.

segments.name: Specialty Polymers
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR179.3 crore (+16% from INR155.2 crore) on 3,836 MT (+21%); segment EBIT INR58.7 crore at 32.7% margin. Q4 volume was 658 MT and revenue INR22.62 crore, with lower demand for one marquee product and mix shift toward lower-margin VAP products.

segments.name: Chips
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue grew about 2.2x YoY to INR65.7 crore on higher third-party volumes. Q4 segment EBIT INR42 crore (+73% YoY), margin 13% (+440 bps).

segments.name: rPET
segments.commentary: FY26 volume 5,325 MT (+258%), revenue INR59.3 crore (3.7x from INR16.2 crore). Q4 volume 1,677 MT (+126% YoY). A 20,000 MT per annum rPET extruder was commissioned in Hyderabad.

segments.name: Ester Filmtech (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Q4 sales volume 9,886 MT (+53.3%), utilisation 85% vs 59%. Reported EBITDA INR18.6 crore (14.1%); adjusted INR24.6 crore (18.7%). FY26 total income INR455.4 crore (+29.3%).

guidance_outlook: Management expects meaningful BOPET margin improvement in FY27 and beyond; sustained BOPET margins projected for about 18 to 24 months.
Q1 FY27 12-micron VA spread expected at INR30 to INR35/kg, versus INR32 to INR33 in Q4 FY26.
FY27 capex about INR70 crore consolidated: INR15 crore for new projects (stated IRR above 20%) and the balance for sustenance and maintenance; FY27 repayments about INR85 crore.
Borrowings targeted below INR40 crore by 31 March 2027, implying significant net debt reduction; cost of funds 9-10% consolidated.

ELITe (textile-to-textile chemical recycling JV) expected operational around end-CY28 (management also said commencement by Q4 CY28 / Q1 CY29); no P&L impact in FY27. First phase of about 70,000 tonnes targets close to USD150 million revenue at full utilisation with 40-45% EBITDA margin.

Management targets Specialty Polymers revenue of about INR200 crore in FY27 (not formally committed) and 20% growth annually; targets VAS share of films to 60%+ and Specialty Polymers share of about 20-25% in 2-3 years.
Expected ROCE above 20% over the next 8 to 10 quarters; historical ROCE about 32% (FY21) and 28% (FY20).
capex_capacity: Consolidated FY27 capex about INR70 crore, with INR15 crore for new high-return projects and the rest for sustenance and maintenance across both companies.
Existing assets could support about INR2,000-2,200 crore turnover at 100% utilisation, per management, with only sustenance capex needed before ELITe.
Ester Filmtech utilisation 85% in Q4 FY26; Ester Industries 72%; consolidated about 78%. Management says film lines could run at 100% but chooses balanced operation to avoid low-margin volume.
Hyderabad rPET extruder (20,000 MT per annum) commissioned to support PCR film demand and sale of film-grade and textile-grade rPET.

ELITe JV (50:50 with Ester Loop Infinite Technologies): FEED completed by Tata Consulting Engineers; Toyo Engineering appointed as engineering consultant; land acquisition in progress, expected in the next few months.
demand_pricing: Management says Indian BOPET industry operating rates are about 80%; demand growth expected at 8-10% p.a. versus 6-8% previously, supported by FMCG growth and PWMR-driven substitution from BOPP/BOPE.
Average 12-micron VA spread in Q4 FY26 was INR32-33/kg; management expects INR30-35/kg for the current quarter.
Raw material (PTA/MEG chips) moved sharply in March-April; management said it rose about 40% in April, passed through by value-add, and is now about INR100/kg of chips.
US reciprocal tariffs were struck down by the US Supreme Court; a 10% global tariff is now in place and is under legal challenge.
DGTR anti-dumping duties on Chinese and other BOPET imports recommended; Ministry of Finance notification still pending.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ~15.5% adjusted EBITDA margin sustainable, and what is steady-state margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins would likely stay near 15% depending on market conditions and will be far better than the last 12-15 months average; BOPET margin support expected for 18-24 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ELITe contribution and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: No P&L impact in FY27. Operations expected by end CY28 (later stated as Q4 CY28 to Q1 CY29), so major benefit from FY30; first phase about 70,000 tonnes, close to USD150 million revenue at full utilisation with 40-45% EBITDA margin.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Specialty Polymers margins and revenue soften in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited seasonality, lower demand for one key specialty product (still under assessment, not quantified), and mix shift toward lower-margin VAP products. Management says FY26 volume and value grew about 20%.

qa_highlights.question: Debt reduction plan and FY27 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Total debt about INR730-732 crore (long-term about INR380 crore). FY27 repayments about INR85 crore; capex about INR70 crore; borrowings to be kept below INR40 crore, implying INR45 crore reduction.

qa_highlights.question: How is euro-loan FX exposure being handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Euro moved from about INR84 at loan sanction to about INR112 now, with about INR24 appreciation in 12-15 months. Management will partly offset via exports and take hedges opportunistically; Euribor 2.2%, with 75 bps markup, keeps cost of debt at Ester Filmtech under 7% in rupee terms.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the cost base is crude-linked and does feedstock hit margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said raw material is a pass-through and value-add adjusts with supply-demand, so feedstock does not erode margins; VA is driven mainly by operating rates.

risks_watch: Specialty Polymers: unresolved demand loss for one marquee product; concentration risk on few products and customers acknowledged by management.
Currency: euro-denominated term loans with large MTM losses (INR37.4 crore FY26 consolidated); hedging still opportunistic.
ELITe project timing has already slipped (land acquisition pending); project depends on land and EU ESPR demand by end CY28.
Anti-dumping duties still need Ministry of Finance notification; Chinese pricing and US tariff litigation remain open.
Ester Filmtech state subsidy of INR9.57 crore approved but not yet received; upside if collected, not in P&L.
500136|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the BOPET cycle turn and FY27 outlook, but evasive on the Specialty Polymers demand issue, declining to quantify the product impact or commit to segment targets beyond 'confident'. Timelines for ELITe were acknowledged as slipping.

500136|2026-06.headline: Ester Industries Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA up 103% to INR58.9 crore, margin 13.3% vs 8.3%, PAT INR18.6 crore vs loss INR7.2 crore.

Ester Filmtech (100% subsidiary) turned EBITDA-positive at INR19.5 crore and PAT-positive at INR4.7 crore. Specialty Polymers volumes and revenue fell year on year on demand pressure in one high-margin product, though EBIT margin rose to 45.3%. Management said part of the other income (~INR10 crore) was one-time, and declined to give firm FY27/FY28 guidance.

financial_highlights.change: Income +62.7% YoY; PAT vs loss of INR16.5 crore

segments.name: Polyester Film (consolidated)
segments.commentary: Volumes 22,120 MT (+2.7% YoY); VAS volumes 6,368 MT (+23%), share of volume ~29% vs 24% a year ago. Capacity utilisation 84% vs 82%; BOPET standalone 85%.

segments.commentary: Volume 725 MT vs 954 MT; revenue INR32.7 crore vs INR48.1 crore. EBIT INR14.8 crore, margin 45.3% vs 31.7% on better product mix.

guidance_outlook: No firm FY27 or FY28 revenue, EBITDA or PAT guidance; management cited 'sustainable growth' in revenue and profitability.
Management expects good earnings for the next 6 to 8 quarters, supported by supply-demand balance and stable prices.
Management aims for VAS share of 50-60% over the next 2 to 3 years; about 35% by exit quarter of FY27.

Specialty Polymers: flat to single-digit growth in FY27, 20%+ revenue CAGR targeted over 3 to 5 years from FY28; absolute EBITDA and EBIT growth expected from FY28 even as percentage margins normalise.
Targeted FY27 gross debt repayment of about INR100 crore (gross debt to ~INR620 crore by year-end).
Management expects rPET to exceed 100% of rated capacity by exit of FY27; Q2 utilisation expected above Q1.

capex_capacity: Rated rPET capacity about 28,000 tons per annum (management also cited 30,000 TPA in prepared remarks).
No major capex planned for FY27 beyond sustenance and maintenance capex in standalone and Specialty Polymers.

Specialty Polymers: demand pressure on one high-margin specialty product; pipeline expected to mature in H2, especially Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Can Q1 run-rate be sustained for the remaining three quarters, and were there one-off gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged an other income component and said it was one-time; it expects sustainable good earnings for the next 6 to 8 quarters on supply-demand balance and stable prices.

qa_highlights.question: Which segments will drive the INR2,000-2,200 crore revenue goal and how will margins evolve over 2 to 3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers are price (global prices expected to hold above the last 2-3 years), higher utilisation in films, specialty polymers and rPET, a rising share of high-priced specialty products, and operational efficiency. Management said it should reach the target in 2 to 3 years.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Q1 spreads and the premium on value-added products; will spreads hold through year-end?
qa_highlights.answer: Spreads for 12-micron corona commodity film were INR28-30 per kg in Q1. VAS products carry a premium of INR25 or more, with offline coated products higher; spreads are holding in the current quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What VAS contribution can be expected by year-end?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said VAS could reach up to 35% of the portfolio by the exit quarter of FY27, versus 29% in Q1 and a 50-60% target over 2 to 3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did rPET volumes fall sequentially and when will external sales pick up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it temporary: internal rPET demand for packaging films rose, so external sales dipped. External sales are expected to recover from September, with a larger effect in October to December.

qa_highlights.question: Will ELITe face competition, given other players are already building textile-to-textile capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management argued the market is large, that its technology handles polyester-cotton blends and low-cost feedstock that competitors cannot, and that Loop has more than 10 years of work and contracts 1.5 years ahead of commissioning. All ELITe output is to be exported, and management agreed a premium is likely.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Specialty Polymers and its margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to flat to single-digit growth in FY27, with a pipeline maturing in H2, and a 20% plus CAGR over 3 to 5 years. Margins may normalise in percentage terms, but absolute EBITDA and EBIT should grow from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What are the other income split, cash balance, debt repayment and JV funding plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Other income of about INR9.8 crore comprised treasury income of about INR3 crore, FD and investment interest of about INR3.5 crore, and FX gain of about INR1 crore, with the rest balance. Gross debt is INR720-722 crore, targeted to fall by INR100 crore to about INR620 crore by year-end. Cash is about INR235 crore, of which about INR140 crore is earmarked for the JV. ELITe debt will sit at JV level.

risks_watch: Sustainability of earnings: management attributes part of the other income to one-time gains (treasury, FX), so the Q1 PAT run-rate may not repeat.

500144|2026-03.headline: Finolex Cables Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 22% YoY to a record electrical segment INR 1,697 crores, but margins were squeezed by Middle East-driven input costs.
500144|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew about 22% YoY and QoQ, with EBITDA up 7% YoY and PAT up 6% YoY, while full-year revenue rose about 19% and PAT about 14%. Management said late-quarter Middle East disruption, rupee depreciation and higher raw material costs left margins slightly under pressure, and inventory was built up by about INR 300 crores. Communication cables grew about 30% YoY in Q4 after flat full-year revenue, helped by hardening fiber prices, while the EHV JV turned profitable. qa_highlights.question: Will the 100 MT preform plant lift margins by about 100 bps once it is fully functional?

Preform contract repricing could raise raw material costs once older contracts reset.
FMEG remains weak; catching up on the lost fan and pipe season is uncertain.

500147|2026-03.headline: Standalone revenue rose 162% YoY to INR2,000 million in Q1 CY26 with EBITDA of INR114 million, while consolidated EBITDA margin was only 1.4%.
500147|2026-03.overview: John Cockerill India reported its first quarter of consolidated results, including China, Belgium and Germany entities from January 2026. Standalone revenue grew 162% YoY to INR2,000 million and standalone EBITDA turned positive at INR114 million (about 5.7% margin), but management attributed margin pressure to hiring costs, a mix shift toward large projects, and one-off integration expenses. Consolidated revenue was INR3.4 billion (+56% YoY) with EBITDA of INR49 million (1.4% margin). Consolidated order book was about INR33 billion and standalone order book about INR13 billion (+101% YoY). Management targets a consolidated EBITDA margin of around 3% now and more than 10% over three years, while fundraising and USA consolidation timing remain undecided.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR2,000 million and EBITDA INR114 million in Q1 CY26; margin dented by hiring upfront costs, a shift to large projects from value-added services, and consolidation one-offs. Management expects margin improvement from next quarter as Q1 and H2 FY25 orders convert.

Cost restructuring from West to East (India/China) planned over 18 months; benefits expected over 12-18 months.
Margin improvement expected from next quarter as recently won orders start converting.
Value services targeted at 30-35% of mix over the next three to five years.
Management expects new technology (JVD, Volteron) revenue in coming quarters; Volteron has no revenue yet and its commercial strategy is being reshaped.
Rolls coating facility at Taloja expected to be commissioned shortly; capex described as limited for an engineering company.

Capex described as limited because JCIL is an engineering company; main P&L effect is R&D and new-technology costs, not capex.

JVD technology still being fine-tuned; revenue expected in coming quarters. Volteron commercialisation expected on a medium-term horizon.

Management expects positive order trend over 24 months, led by India (capacity doubling by 2030) and China, plus growing interest in JVD green-steel technology.

Europe described as a standby market; management expects new EU import quotas to drive demand next year. US seen as a market with the best steel price per ton, with consolidation and Nippon Steel's US Steel purchase expected to drive investment.
Relationship with SAIL under an MoU signed a little over a year ago; management would not disclose details, saying projects are being built up.
Consolidated order book executable mainly over about three years; value services over 12-18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating leverage not show despite record revenue, and why did employee costs rise 34% YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO cited three factors: upfront hiring and organisational realignment costs, a mix shift toward large projects (JSW, Tata) versus value-added services, and one-off consolidation/integration expenses.

qa_highlights.question: Consolidated order book executability?
qa_highlights.answer: Most of the approximately INR33 billion is executable over about three years; a smaller value services portion runs 12-18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Post-consolidation margin path?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated EBITDA about 3% currently; target above 10% over three years, with mid-path progress by the start of next year, via a West-to-East cost shift over 18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Fundraise deferred? Promoter stake and USA consolidation timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Board still exploring funding options with another board meeting planned in 2-3 weeks. Promoter stake to stay at current level for now. USA consolidation faces technical issues; target by end of year or a slight postponement.

qa_highlights.question: Acquisition price versus revenue for the European, Chinese and US businesses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said total SPA price is around EUR50 million including USA; the analyst's arithmetic was disputed and the discussion was taken offline.

qa_highlights.question: Composition of other income of about INR66 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly interest income plus sale of old assets and scrap; Q1 other income stated as INR93 million.

qa_highlights.question: Will standalone and consolidated margins converge?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects convergence through moving activity to India/China, converting R&D into orders, and structural streamlining over 12-18 months; iron and steel (upstream) has no contract in hand yet.

risks_watch: Consolidated EBITDA margin of 1.4% versus standalone margin of about 5.7%; delivery of the targeted ~3% and later 10%+ depends on cost realignment.
JVD and Volteron R&D costs are running ahead of revenue; Volteron IP sits with the promoter and strategy is under discussion.
Fundraise plan deferred; board decision expected in 2-3 weeks. Promoter stake change possible.
USA business consolidation timing uncertain (end of year or postponement) with technical issues.
Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and European energy costs may cause short-term volatility.
Transcript shows analyst disputes over acquisition pricing and other income, taken offline; watch for disclosure follow-up.

We see right now more the cost than the benefit. The benefits will come in the next quarters.
So, either we are able to achieve that by the end of the year or maybe it will be discussion on maybe postponing slightly, but not so much. It's just timing.

500147|2026-06.headline: John Cockerill India Q2 CY26 standalone revenue up 82% YoY to ~INR149 crore; consolidated INR299 crore (+18% YoY), order book ~INR4,500 crore.
500147|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue rose 82% YoY to about INR149 crore and consolidated revenue reached about INR299 crore, up 18% YoY, but both fell sequentially as Q1 benefited from closing older projects. Management attributed weaker Q2 margins to upfront costs on newly started projects, organisation-building spend and one-time consolidation costs after the China, Germany and Belgium entities were brought under the listed company. Order wins of about INR1,200 crore in the quarter lifted the consolidated order book to about INR4,500 crore (standalone about INR2,200 crore). Management expects revenue and margins to build in H2 as new projects ramp, though it gave no quantified guidance.

financial_highlights.change: Expected marginally lower in next two quarters

qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, as a north-star; two streams: organic (JVD, Volteron) and external acquisitions, which are under investigation. Volteron IP sits with John Cockerill SA, not the listed entity, and is not yet commercial.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the CY25 pro-forma revenue (~INR2,000 crore) far above reported (~INR960 crore), and can the US entity bridge the gap?
qa_highlights.answer: INR2,000 crore was a guideline; US is not a large contributor. Revenue depends on order progress. Management expects significant H2 improvement and said the gap should not be very far if US is included.

qa_highlights.question: Why did John Cockerill SA reduce holding from ~75% to ~70.4%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to group priorities; SA remains a large shareholder and will get convertible preferential shares that would take it back to 72%+.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost structure outlook (employee cost ~INR68 crore, other expenses ~INR70 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost to rise with execution hiring; other expenses marginally below current level in next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Standalone and consolidated order book, service revenue, and top-customer concentration?

500148|2026-03.headline: UFlex Q4 FY26 EBITDA rose 31.8% YoY to Rs 6,265 mn at a 15.3% margin, the highest in 14 quarters, though management flagged spreads moderating in Q1 FY27.

Management attributed the jump to a March spike in film spreads, as raw material increases were more than passed through. Management said spreads for BOPET and BOPP have since moderated significantly, and it declined to give an FY27 EBITDA margin range.

qa_highlights.question: Will leverage come down and what is the peak debt?

qa_highlights.question: What is the aseptic volume outlook for FY27?

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin trajectory and cost of debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-film packaging margins expected to hold, film margins may moderate. Blended cost of funds about 9% (was above 9%); refinancing is premature, with cheaper overseas funding expected to help.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company commit to an EBITDA margin range for FY27?

500148|2026-06.headline: UFlex Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 38% YoY to Rs 53,972 million and EBITDA rose 92% to Rs 9,198 million, with margin at 17%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 15.5% normalized margin sustainable and how much currency impact?

qa_highlights.question: Plans for surplus cash: debt reduction vs capex vs shareholder returns?
