qa_highlights.question: Interest rate and rating outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Rated AA by CRISIL and India Ratings; interest cost fell 0.3-0.4% this quarter and management targets a further 1% reduction in the next year.

risks_watch: Egypt Aseptic (12 billion packs) commissioning slipping beyond H1 FY27; management flagged a possible 1-2 week slip and about 2 billion packs in FY27 assumes a 1 October start
Q2 normalization after exceptional Q1 realizations; management declined QoQ benchmarking and flagged shipment timing risk from West Asia and Bab-el-Mandeb disruptions
Sustainability of pricing: BOPP up 25-32% and BOPET up 30-35% since February 2026; management said prices could correct if the West Asia crisis eases
Aseptic pressure from duty-free Indonesian imports under the India trade treaty; Aseptic volumes down 8.4% YoY company-wide and management expects recovery only from Q3

Guidance inconsistency on the call: 35% vs 30%-plus growth, FY27 EBITDA margin of about 14%-plus, and the 15.5% normalized margin treated as sustainable over three years; Q1 forex impact of Rs 825 mn (about Rs 70 crore per the Q&A)

Debt-EBITDA reduction from about 4.5x to about 3.5x, with a target of about 3x in FY28; interest cost cut of about 1% targeted over the next year; FY26-FY29 CAGR of at least 10% still to be confirmed by IR
key_quotes: Whatever numbers we have achieved in Q1, they are very much sustainable.
Generally, we should not give guidance because guidance in today's market scenario is very difficult.
We are derisking our top-line model in such a way that where we are present at least 75% of our turnover should come from near to our customer policy, that is what we are adopting.
I can quote 10% or something, but that will be misleading, so what I'll request is for Surajit to share the number with you once we have the calculations.
500148|2026-06.management_tone: Management was confident on Q1 delivery and on FY27 growth of about 35%, and repeatedly stressed that margins are sustainable for three years. It was evasive on quarterly benchmarking, declining QoQ normalization guidance and pointing investors to YoY comparisons, and it did not give a firm FY29 CAGR, deferring to IR.

500153|2026-03.headline: Ganesh Benzoplast Q4 FY26 consol PAT swung to INR152 mn from a loss, but JNPT rental reset (~INR23 cr rise) compresses LST margins for 2-3 years.
500153|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue rose 12% YoY to INR1,115 mn and PAT turned to INR152 mn from a INR132 mn loss in Q4 FY25. Full-year FY26 consol revenue grew 10% to INR4,114 mn and PAT rose 93% to INR733 mn, with EPS of INR10.19. Management attributed the margin dip to a 30-year JNPT lease rental reset, with the old plots' rental rising to about INR25 cr from about INR2 cr, partly offset by a one-time INR9 cr income. Expansion of about 50,000 kL at JNPT is under way, with management guiding to commissioning by calendar year-end 2026.

segments.name: LST (JNPT, Kochi, Goa terminals)
segments.commentary: JNPT running at about 100% utilisation, Kochi at 80-85%+, Goa close to zero after bunkering demand left post mining ban. Management said rental segment EBITDA margin was about 45-47%, unchanged, per an analyst's read of prior disclosures; the company did not restate the segment margin split this quarter.

segments.name: Chemical division
segments.commentary: Management said Q4 had two exceptional charges: recertification costs for UK/Europe and settlement of staff dues and salary hikes. Excluding these, Chemical PAT would have risen at least 15% YoY. Chemical capex is limited to small debottlenecking.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: Large INR175 cr JSW port order; engineering complete, groundwork expected after monsoon. Margins described as higher single digit. Value executed not disclosed.

guidance_outlook: JNPT expansion of about 50,000 kL (about 40,000-49,000 kL phase) to be completed by December 2026 (calendar year-end), with revenue expected from Q4 FY26/calendar year-end.
A further about 60,000 kL capacity is planned for next year; combined capex for both phases is about INR100 cr. Installed capacity to rise about 15%.

Management expects rentals to rise 5-6% annually on existing tanks, and the EBITDA margin to recover over 2-3 years; another view was that the cost is recovered in 15-18 months with new tanks at about 80% EBITDA margin.
Goa petroleum modification (blended petrol approvals) to start after monsoon and finish by 31 March 2027; no contract signed yet. Capex about INR2 cr.
Chemical expected to remain on a steady path with no major capacity project.
capex_capacity: Total installed capacity about 3.50 lakh kL; about 2.80 lakh kL sits on JNPT plots, per management.
JNPT utilisation almost 100%, Goa close to zero, Kochi above 80-85%, overall about 95%.
JNPT expansion of about 50,000 kL under way at capex of INR40-50 cr for this phase; 3 large 45,000 kL tanks are being built.
Ammonia storage and LPG bullets capex of around INR450-500 cr is still under discussion and not initiated; about 5-6 acres of JNPT land is set aside.
Visakhapatnam LOI progress is on hold because of a dispute between a prior plot holder and the Visakhapatnam port.
demand_pricing: JNPT rentals are a mix of long-term storage contracts and spot. Management said no exceptional demand arose from the war-related supply disruption, so no pricing windfall was taken.

Management said JNPT lease rental reset happens every 30 years (last in 2025, next in 2055). The old plots' rental rose to about INR25 cr from about INR2 cr, a provision booked in Q4 for the cumulative amount.
A one-time exceptional income of INR9 cr came from termination of an LPG arrangement (around Feb-March 2025 per management).
Management said the company is pursuing a Singapore subsidiary for chemical basket trade, still at a preliminary stage.
Receivables over 6 months have risen because of extended credit terms in EPC; retention money is paid after one year. Management said there is no bad debt issue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity utilisation and why is Goa near zero?
qa_highlights.answer: JNPT is near 100%, Cochin 80-85%+, Goa close to zero since the bunkering business left after the Goa mining ban; overall about 95%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PAT fall because of rental expense?
qa_highlights.answer: The JNPT land was acquired in 1995, and the 30-year rental reset took effect in 2025. Old-plot rent rose to about INR25 cr from about INR2 cr.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Chemical slow in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no slowdown. Two exceptional items (UK/Europe recertification and staff dues/salary settlement) hit the quarter; excluding them, Chemical PAT would have risen at least 15%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did consol EBITDA margin fall from about 21-22% in Q3 to about 18-19% in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the full INR25 cr annual lease rental was provisioned in Q4 cumulatively, and the YoY margin drop was about INR6 cr against the INR23 cr rise. The company expects to pass the cost to customers and recover it in 15-18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 50% capex complete by Q1 or the full phase?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the entire 49,000 kL phase will be completed by December 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company add ports outside JNPT, Kochi and Goa?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will only deploy capital where ROI matches or beats JNPT. No such opportunity has been found, though it is open to overseas deals with back-to-back contracts.

risks_watch: JNPT rental reset compresses LST margin; recovery timeline of 2-3 years depends on 5-6% annual rental escalation.
Goa terminal near zero utilisation, with INR10-12 lakh/month holding cost; petroleum handling there has no signed contract.
Expansion timing: 50,000 kL due by December 2026 and 60,000 kL next year; any slip would delay revenue.
Receivables over 6 months rising because of EPC credit terms and retention money.
Visakhapatnam LOI on hold; ammonia/LPG bullet capex of INR450-500 cr not yet initiated.
Management could not give the JSW EPC executed value or the Goa total historical investment on the call.
500153|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the JNPT expansion and long-term rental escalation, but defensive on margin compression and receivables. Several answers were vague or deferred (Goa investment, EPC progress, segment margin split), and some management statements conflicted on timing.
key_quotes: So, this is every 30 years, there is a reset in the rentals by the ports.
Chemical is also running more or less on steady state.
So, the combined capex for both of the capacities together is approximately INR100 crores.

vs loss of INR158 mn in Q4 FY25

500153|2026-09.headline: Ganesh Benzoplast to divest JNPA, Goa and Cochin liquid tank farms plus Daund rail for INR1,154 crore, with INR500 crore due around January 2027.
500153|2026-09.overview: Management, on an investor call held October 7, 2026, outlined the sale of the LST (liquid storage tank) businesses at JNPA, Goa and Cochin, together with the JNPA-linked Daund rail business, for INR1,154 crore plus an exit-linked consideration. Payment is staged: about INR500 crore by January 2027, about INR300 crore by March 2027, and the balance INR354 crore over 12 to 18 months tied to port approvals and tank commissioning. Of the first INR500 crore, about INR190-200 crore goes to tax and bank-limit closure and about INR200 crore to a buyback and special dividend, with INR100 crore for chemical expansion and EPC book growth. Management guided chemical PAT to about INR18 crore in FY26 rising to INR60-70 crore over 4-5 years, and EPC PAT to about INR150 crore by around FY30. Much of the Q&A probed the rationale for exiting the higher-margin LST business and the lack of quarter-wise numbers.

financial_highlights.metric: Divestment consideration (JNPA, Goa, Cochin LST + Daund rail)
financial_highlights.change: plus further consideration linked to investor exit valuation (not quantified)

financial_highlights.metric: Planned shareholder return from first tranche (buyback + special dividend)

financial_highlights.change: vs INR5 crore PAT in FY24 (full year)
management says profit up ~1,000% over last 2 years
management now expects above INR200 crore

segments.name: LST (liquid tank farm) – divested
segments.commentary: JNPA, Goa and Cochin liquid tank farms and JNPA-linked Daund rail are being sold for INR1,154 crore. JNPA expected in books until about Dec 2026/Jan 2027, with Cochin and Goa removed gradually over the next calendar year. Company retains a small stake in a Kandla terminal, described as insignificant; a non-compete applies.

segments.name: Chemical (benzoic acid, sodium benzoate)
segments.commentary: Two plants, each about 1,000 tons/month; utilisation about 70-80%. One plant is being doubled, with completion expected July 2027. REACH certification obtained for UK and EU; orders over 600 tons received, expected to reach about 2,000 tons/year. Management targets chemical PAT of INR60-70 crore over 4-5 years.

segments.name: EPC (tankage, pipeline, petroleum)
segments.commentary: Order book expected to be about INR500-600 crore next year, with EPC revenue of about INR250 crore per annum from FY28 onward per management. Targeted 5% share of a INR70,000 crore 5-year petroleum-related EPC opportunity implies about INR150 crore PAT. EBITDA margin assumption 7-8% on a conservative basis, PAT margin basis not clearly specified.

guidance_outlook: Chemical PAT expected to be INR60-70 crore over 4-5 years (from INR18 crore in FY26); management says chemical profitability to rise 3-4x in 4-5 years.
EPC PAT of about INR150 crore targeted by around 2030, assuming 5% share of INR70,000 crore 5-year petroleum EPC pipeline.
Total PAT target of about INR210 crore in 3-5 years versus about INR70 crore currently; FY28 PAT growth target of 15-20% YoY.
Chemical revenue to rise about 20-25% in the year after capacity commissioning and about 70-80% in the following year, per management.
Debt expected to stay at minimum; company does not expect to need significant bank debt, although bank limits are needed for guarantees.
Further tranche proceeds to be used for expansion or shareholder returns, decided by the board based on capex visibility.
capex_capacity: Chemical capacity doubling at one plant (of two, about 1,000 tons/month each), targeted completion July 2027.
Stage 1 capex across chemical and EPC of not more than about INR150 crore.
New agro and specialty derivative plants planned with technology and licence partners; to be funded later, with back-to-back buyback arrangements with customers under discussion.
Management says no balance capex remains on the JNPA port asset, and that about 43 tanks are under construction at JNPA (per management answer on LST growth capex).
Capex to continue over the next 1-2 years; first stage expected to be complete by FY28.
demand_pricing: REACH certification enabled UK and EU exports; over 600 tons of orders received.
Management says the chemical business profit grew from INR5 crore (FY24) to INR15-16 crore (FY25), INR18 crore (FY26) with turnover broadly flat.
Crude-linked raw material costs: management says it passes through fluctuations to customers but cannot rule out margin impact at high crude prices.
Chemical EBITDA margin cited by analyst at 11-12%; management expects to sustain or improve it without a firm number.
EPC contract wins include KKR (about INR300 crore), GACL/NALCO JV pipeline, ANA Oleo, Allana, Adani MPL and Jindal projects.

qa_highlights.question: Deepesh Sancheti (Maanya Finance): what is the timeline for the next INR300 crore tranche, and how will EPC working capital be funded after debt is repaid?
qa_highlights.answer: Balance INR354 crore spread over 12-18 months, milestone-linked to port approvals and tank commissioning. Bank guarantee lines used for EPC will be temporarily replaced with deal funds and reinstated; management says sufficient cash will come from tranches and PAT for EPC working capital.

qa_highlights.question: Romil Savaliya (CJ Shah Family Office): why has chemical top line been flat for years, and what is changing in EPC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it focuses on profitability, not turnover: chemical PAT went from INR5 crore in FY24 to about INR15-16 crore in FY25 and INR18 crore in FY26 on similar turnover. EPC is being moved from a support role for LST to an independent division targeting about INR150 crore PAT in 4-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Nishita (Sapphire Capital): what is the rationale for divesting the higher-margin LST business, and what is chemical capacity and utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Rationale cited as projected cost increases and market movement over 2-3 years, plus the value offered by the buyer, which management said it judged fair. Chemical has two plants of about 1,000 tons/month each; one is being doubled by July 2027; utilisation is about 70-80%. Q1 chemical PAT of INR6 crore is chemical only, and EPC quarterly turnover was not given.

qa_highlights.question: Bhavesh Patel (Patel Investments): will the 40-45% shareholder return apply to later tranches, and what is FY28 PAT expectation and debt outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: The buyback and special dividend apply to the first tranche only; later tranches depend on capex visibility and board decisions. Management targets 15-20% PAT growth YoY into FY28 from about INR70 crore. No significant bank debt is expected, though bank limits are needed for guarantees.

qa_highlights.question: Saurabh (Mangalam): is there a non-compete, will the company re-enter LST, and how exposed is chemical margin to crude?
qa_highlights.answer: A standard non-compete applies; the Kandla stake is a carve-out and insignificant; no plan to return to LST near term. Crude pass-through is attempted but margin impact cannot be ruled out at high crude.

qa_highlights.question: Prateek Kothari (CRK Stock Broking): what is the first tranche's use of funds and what is the chemical top-line ballpark?
qa_highlights.answer: Of the first INR500 crore, about INR200 crore goes to shareholders, about INR190-200 crore to tax and bank-limit closure, and the balance to chemical and EPC growth. Chemical FY26 revenue was about INR180 crore, now expected above INR200 crore; revenue expected to rise 20-25% in the year after commissioning and 70-80% in the following year.

qa_highlights.question: Krupa Sanjay Desai (Electrum Capital): what EPC revenue and margin are expected?
qa_highlights.answer: EPC revenue this year about INR50-60 crore given seasonality; about INR250 crore per year from next year with KKR and other contracts. Management cited a general expectation of about 10% margin but planned at 7-8%, specified as PAT; the INR150 crore EPC PAT is expected by about 2030.

risks_watch: Timing of the INR500 crore (about January 2027) and INR300 crore (March 2027) tranches depends on port approvals and shareholder approval; the INR354 crore balance is milestone-linked with no fixed date.
Q1 FY27 chemical PAT of INR6 crore (about 10% margin on INR60 crore revenue) is well above the FY26 run-rate; management says it aims to sustain it, but gave no firm guidance.
Loss of JNPA LST earnings from around the March 2027 quarter, with Cochin and Goa rolling off over the next calendar year; the group's profit base will shift to chemical and EPC.
Chemical capacity doubling at one plant targeted for July 2027; execution and ramp-up timing is key to the 20-25% and 70-80% revenue step-ups.
Crude-linked raw material costs could compress chemical margins; management cannot rule this out.

EPC targets (order book INR500-600 crore next year, INR2,500-3,000 crore in 4-5 years, 5% of INR70,000 crore pipeline) are unquantified attempts; working capital needs post-debt repayment are unclear.
Quarterly EPC turnover and profit were not provided; management will share on request, so segment disclosure remains limited.
key_quotes: So, combined with the chemical PAT of about INR60 crores and the EPC PAT about INR150 crores, you're looking at your company going in the next 3 to 4, 5 years to about INR210 crores of PAT, which is currently at 70.
And one important thing of about the buyback that you should know is that the promoters will not be participating in it.
But I cannot commit or I cannot speculate that no margins will ever be hit on how crude behaves suddenly, but we have -- I believe, enough systems in place to sustain any reasonable fluctuations.
So, capex will keep happening through the next 1 or 2 years continuously.
500153|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and promotional on the growth outlook for chemical and EPC, with an emphasis on shareholder returns. Cautious and evasive on specific numbers and timelines: management repeatedly declined to speculate on future figures, gave port-approval timing only as "expected", and did not answer the ownership question about CJ Shah family stake.

500165|2026-06.headline: Kansai Nerolac Q1 FY27 standalone revenue grew 10.2% with PBDIT up 7.7%; management targets 13-14% margins for FY27 despite input cost pressure.
500165|2026-06.overview: Standalone net revenue grew 10.2% YoY, PBDIT 7.7% and PBT 5.1%; consolidated revenue rose 9.8%, PBDIT 8.3% and PBT 5.8%. Decorative value growth was high single digit with volume growth low single digit, as the company deliberately shed low-margin volume. Industrial coatings grew double digit in value, but price increases lagged, with about 5% realised so far at customer level. Management announced a INR601 crore capacity expansion across automotive, powder coating and resin, spread over about 2 to 2.5 years, and kept its margin ambition intact.

financial_highlights.metric: Industrial price hike achieved so far
financial_highlights.change: Still under negotiation; effective ask from 1 April

segments.name: Decorative
segments.commentary: Value growth high single digit; volume growth low single digit as premium mix was prioritised over low-margin, high-volume products. Economy grew mid-single digit and super premium grew double digit. Margins were stable YoY despite higher ad spend.

segments.name: Industrial (Automotive, Performance Coatings, Powder)
segments.commentary: Value growth double digit. Automotive and powder coating saw strong growth; liquid performance coatings led by construction equipment, drums and coil coating. Gross contribution fell about 1.3% as price increases lagged cost inflation.

segments.name: Auto Refinish
segments.commentary: Growth was flat. Management cited notable premium PU body shop wins and a transition from solvent-borne to waterborne systems that is on plan.

segments.name: Construction chemicals and premium wood finish
segments.commentary: Construction chemicals grew double digit; premium wood finish grew high single digit.

guidance_outlook: FY27 margin ambition of 13-14% is retained, subject to the geopolitical situation not worsening.
Q2 decorative price increase of about 3% expected to flow through; industrial price increase of another 3-5% expected in Q2.

Q2 will carry high-cost inventory and a seasonally weaker quarter, but management expects to maintain margins versus last year's same quarter, helped by sourcing, value engineering and formula optimisation.
Medium term, aim to reach the higher end of the 14%+ margin range within 2-3 years through premiumisation, industrial growth and fixed-cost leverage.
Expected ROCE on incremental capex is towards 18%, with per-KL capex on new capacity lower than the current programme.
Management expects a slightly better festive season, with Diwali in November giving October more painting days in Q3.
capex_capacity: INR601 crore capex for automotive, powder coating and resin capacity at Sayakha, Bawal and Hosur.
Capacity addition of 66,000 KL per year plus resin capacity of close to 10,000 metric tons per year.
The INR601 crore outlay is spread over about 2 to 2.5 years; normal annual capex is INR150-200 crore.
Part of the spend is front-loaded infrastructure, so future incremental capacity will be cheaper per KL.
Industrial capacity is expected to be full in about 2 years, requiring the addition.
demand_pricing: Competitive intensity in decorative remains high, with new entrants still testing the market; no change in pricing discipline, dealer incentives or scheme intensity versus last year or Q4 exit.
Network expansion: 1,700 dealers added in Q1; network additions targeted at 5-10% a year.
Industrial price hike to date about 5%, with more discussions expected to add in Q2.
Solvent inflation was sharp, but solvent inventory is only about 15 days, which made it hard to hedge.
Some free-product schemes continue in certain markets, not specific to the company's focus towns.
Input cost inflation peaked in June and has since eased slightly.

qa_highlights.question: Is decorative volume growth in line with the market, and is competition easing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume growth is not below competitors, but the company is deliberately avoiding low-margin, high-volume products. Competitive intensity remains high and is expected to persist through this year.

qa_highlights.question: Why are margins flat YoY when the market leader expanded margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Industrial price increases lag by 1-2 quarters, so the price-cost gap hit industrial gross contribution by about 1.3%. Ad spend rose in Q1 but was offset by mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the value growth split in decorative and industrial?
qa_highlights.answer: Decorative value growth is high single digit and industrial is double digit. Q1 mix is heavier on decorative, and the mix changes each quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the capex and what returns are expected?
qa_highlights.answer: INR601 crore over about 2-2.5 years on top of normal capex of INR150-200 crore per year. Management expects ROCE towards 18%, with lower per-KL capex on new capacity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the pricing growth in Q1 and Q2 on a consolidated basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated pricing was about 4-5% in Q1. Q2 adds about 3% in decorative and another 3-5% in industrial.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any backward integration plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the new resin capacity is backward integration for automotive paint, but raw material integration is not on the card. The Kansai Group's global network can supply intermediates as needed.

risks_watch: Geopolitical escalation (West Asia crisis) could raise crude-linked raw material costs and disrupt supply chains.
Rupee depreciation may lift import costs; industrial price negotiations may still be incomplete in Q2.
Decorative volume growth is low single digit, and the company is ceding share in low-margin segments.
Ad and dealer investment is rising, and margin benefit depends on whether premium mix gains come through.
Whether the INR601 crore capacity delivers the targeted ~18% ROCE.
Auto Refinish growth was flat, and the solvent-to-waterborne transition is still in progress.
500165|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term plan and on margin resilience, but cautious on near-term industrial pricing and the geopolitical outlook. Management was candid that decorative volume is lagging by design and that competition is not easing.
key_quotes: And that is why I guess for this year, at least that intensity will remain and people will test water in terms of this new set equilibrium.
With that, I'm very confident that this year also, our endeavour is to maintain 13% to 14%.
And on the midterm, I think our endeavour is obviously go to higher end of 14% plus kind of a thing.

500171|2026-06.headline: GHCL Q1 FY27 EBITDA rose to INR233 crore (29.1% margin), which management says is transient and should not be read as run-rate.
500171|2026-06.overview: Revenue was INR798 crore, down from INR808 crore QoQ and INR823 crore YoY, while EBITDA rose to INR233 crore from INR194 crore QoQ and INR225 crore YoY. Management attributed the margin uplift to better realisation, lower-cost raw material and energy inventory, and cost efficiencies, and repeatedly guided investors to judge margins annually rather than quarterly. PAT including a INR40 crore post-tax exceptional item (ESOS Trust settlement) was INR191 crore; PAT before exceptionals was INR151 crore. Vacuum Salt and Bromine projects are commissioning, while the Greenfield soda ash project remains stalled on land acquisition with no timeline given.

segments.name: Soda ash (core, domestic and export)
segments.commentary: Margin lift attributed to realisation, low-cost inventory and efficiencies; management declined to quantify the realisation increase per tonne. Volumes played a smaller role per management.

segments.name: Vacuum Salt and Bromine (new downstream projects)
segments.commentary: Both plants are mechanically commissioned; commercial production of Vacuum Salt expected in Q2 FY27, Bromine output seasonally low in Q2 with production ramping in Q3-Q4. Management guided to INR150-170 crore revenue at 40-45% EBITDA margin at full utilisation, expected in FY28.

guidance_outlook: Margins expected to moderate from the Q1 level and revert to a normalised trend, driven by softer domestic demand, higher captive industry production and softening realisation; management asked investors to assess margins annually.
Vacuum Salt and Bromine: full utilisation expected in FY28; management said both plants should run at intended capacity during FY27 with gradual, phased scale-up.
FY27 capex guided at roughly INR140-150 crore, mainly for the two downstream projects plus factory infrastructure and regular capex.
Solar glass soda ash demand expected to rise from about 1.5 lakh tonnes to about 3.5 lakh tonnes as new capacity commissions around Jan-Mar 2027.
Dividend payout: last three years about 80-87% of profit distributed via dividend and buyback; management said Board would consider higher payout, with policy around 25%.
capex_capacity: Vacuum Salt project: commissioning checks and production trial completed; commercial production expected Q2 FY27, with gradual phased scale-up.
Bromine project: pre-commissioning complete; output seasonally lower in monsoon (Q2), production expected Q3-Q4 FY27.
Greenfield soda ash project: delayed primarily by land acquisition; no revised timeline, cost or return profile given. Management will update once land clarity is achieved.
No other pipeline projects beyond the two downstream projects and the Greenfield project, per management.
FY27 capex about INR140-150 crore.
demand_pricing: Global soda ash: supply exceeds demand, prices weak for about two to three years; China demand recovery slower than expected and Chinese inventories high. Management believes Chinese synthetic (Solvay) producers are making cash losses.
Some early Chinese capacity rationalisation and a short-term US plant closure noted; meaningful supply reduction still some way off.
India demand soft in Q1 due to conflict and domestic dynamics; management expects this to persist near term into monsoon, with some rise in imports.

Imports: about 80,000-82,000 tonnes/month in Q1 FY26 (about 20% of demand), fell to about 45,000-46,000 tonnes/month in Q4 FY26, and rose to about 73,000-74,000 tonnes/month recently. July data not yet available. Major sources: US, Turkey, and some China.

Landed cost of imported natural soda ash to India cited at about USD 180-190/tonne; base import duty about 7.5%, no anti-dumping duty. Safeguard quantitative restrictions under government consideration, no outcome yet.

qa_highlights.question: Will Vacuum Salt and Bromine reach optimal utilisation in FY28, and what revenue and margin are possible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed FY28 full utilisation; indicated INR150-160 crore revenue (later cited INR160-170 crore) at about 40-45% EBITDA margin for the two projects combined.

qa_highlights.question: Return on capital for the Greenfield soda ash project at current prices, and reasons for delay?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said current prices should not be treated as sustainable and that long-term numbers given in the past still apply. Delay is due to land acquisition; no timeline given.

qa_highlights.question: Quantify realisation gains versus cost gains in Q1 margin.
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify; said margin gain was a mix of partial price increase, efficiencies and low-cost inventory, and asked analysts to focus on annual margin.

qa_highlights.question: Dividend payout plans given strong cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Payout was about 80-87% over three years via dividend and buyback; Board will consider. Management noted policy around 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Imports and trade protection status?
qa_highlights.answer: Imports rose to about 73,000-74,000 tonnes/month from 45,000-46,000 in Q4 FY26; no ADD in place; safeguard QRs still under government consideration.

risks_watch: Margin normalisation: management expects moderation from the 29.1% level as energy costs rise after the ceasefire breakdown and realisation softens.
Greenfield soda ash project: no timeline, cost or return update; land acquisition unresolved, and global oversupply could alter returns.
Import pressure: monthly imports up sharply from Q4 FY26 lows; safeguard QR decision pending.
Ramp-up risk for Vacuum Salt and Bromine: Bromine volumes seasonally weak in Q2; ramp pace described as gradual and phased.

qa_highlights.question: What is the defence order book and what is the acquisition's effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Defence order book is about Rs 300 crore excluding the acquisition, about Rs 2,300 crore including it. Acquisition to complete within calendar 2026; export defence orders about Rs 2,200 crore. BMP-2 modernisation shortlisted, Army trials started 20 May with about 1.5 months to complete.

qa_highlights.question: What is the data-centre connectivity revenue outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 100 crore in Q1 FY27 and about Rs 800 crore for FY27, with orders of about Rs 850 crore in hand. Capacity to rise 5x, with deliveries of cable starting this month and connectivity about a month later.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Army (EPC) contract restore profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the Army contract signing in mid-Q2 FY27, after which EPC revenue would rise and losses fall significantly. It did not commit to breakeven.

qa_highlights.question: How will debt and working capital evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt-equity is about 0.3 and is expected to stay in that range, funded partly by internal accruals. Segment assets rose about Rs 400 crore net of segment liabilities (about Rs 600 crore liability increase).

risks_watch: Geopolitical disruption (e.g., Suez Canal closure) and government contract timing (Army contract signing and trials) could delay revenue and margin recovery.
Preform price increases from the next calendar year, with some older contracts priced below current market, could compress margins if pass-through is incomplete.
Restructuring committee with E&Y evaluating group simplification; outcome and impact on the defence subsidiary (HASPL) structure remain undisclosed.
Management said it is reviewing further fibre capacity expansion, indicating possible additional capex beyond the current plan.
Export concentration (about 60% of revenue) and US hyperscaler dependence; a shift in Chinese competitive pricing could affect realisations.
Q1 included about Rs 300 crore of Q4 unbilled revenue billed in the quarter; watch whether Q2 revenue holds near Rs 1,900 crore.
500183|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and expansive on demand, margins and growth, with frequent forward-looking claims on pricing and contracts. Evasive on specifics such as pricing details, order-level margins, restructuring outcomes and the Army contract timing, which were described as confidential or still pending.
key_quotes: Based on the progress achieved in the first quarter, healthy order inflows, favourable industry dynamics, expanding global opportunities and improving execution capabilities, we, to the best of our estimates, can raise our aspirations for FY27 to a revenue growth of 40% and above.
I am pleased to share that the Company has achieved EBITDA margin of more than 23.25% in the very first quarter itself.
There's nothing called a particular high-value or high-margin order which we have executed.
So this 23% margin is something minimum we would be able to protect to the best of my information at this point of time out of the orders I have, raw material cost I have.

500183|2026-09.headline: HFCL Q2 FY27 consolidated PAT ₹394.22 crore (+448% YoY) on revenue ₹2,541.79 crore; order book ₹28,900 crore; management guides ≥80% FY27 revenue growth.
500183|2026-09.overview: Management reported its best-ever quarter: consolidated revenue ₹2,541.79 crore (up ~143.6% YoY, +32.7% QoQ), EBITDA ₹658.00 crore (25.89% margin), and PAT ₹394.22 crore (15.51% margin). H1 FY27 PBT was ₹870.12 crore and PAT ₹639.86 crore. Guidance was raised from ~20% to ~40% and now to at least 80% revenue growth for FY27, with defence and connectivity solutions cited as new growth legs. Several answers were qualitative or deferred, notably on the defence ramp-up, EPC restructuring timing and FY28 guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 guidance of 80%+ growth conservative, implying flat-to-lower H2?

qa_highlights.question: Margin trajectory over next 2 years?

qa_highlights.question: Split of telecom revenue between conventional telcos and hyperscalers, and utilisation?

qa_highlights.question: Defence revenue bridge from ~₹80 crore H1 to ₹500 crore FY27?

qa_highlights.question: When will the EPC segment turn profitable?

500184|2026-06.headline: Himadri Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 28% to INR1,432 Crores, with PAT up 27% to INR228 Crores at a 16% margin.
500184|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 28% YoY to INR1,432 Crores, EBITDA rose 33% to INR313 Crores (22% margin), and PAT reached INR228 Crores. Standalone EBITDA grew 29% to INR301 Crores at a 24% margin. Management announced an indigenous CNT plant (200 MTPA, about INR70 Crores capex) and a super speciality carbon black conversion (6,000 MTPA, INR170 Crores capex), and reported that the 200 MTPA anode plant was commissioned in April 2026. Other-segment EBIT fell to about INR1 Crore from about INR25 Crores because mining did not operate pending licences, and an FX loss weighed on the quarter.

financial_highlights.change: Down from about INR25 Crores in the prior quarter, due to no mining income

segments.name: Birla Tyres
segments.commentary: Commercial operations began 29 May 2025; quarterly revenue is cited at about INR127 Crores and is consolidated but not in standalone. Management targets INR3,000 Crores top line in 4-5 years and EBITDA breakeven in FY27, with a PCR plant by FY28. Distribution spans 49 distributors and over 1,000 dealers.

segments.name: Coal tar and carbon black (core)
segments.commentary: Holds over 65% domestic coal tar pitch share with 600,000 MTPA distillation capacity, and carbon black capacity is 250,000 MT including 130,000 MT speciality grades. Anthraquinone and carbazole capacity of 5,300 MTPA is due in two phases: 2,600 MTPA in Q2 FY27 and 2,700 MTPA in Q2 FY28.

segments.name: New energy materials
segments.commentary: A 200 MTPA anode plant at Mahistikry was commissioned in April 2026, with anode capex of about INR120 Crores to date. LFP cathode initial 2,000 MTPA is due in Q3 FY27 as Phase 1 of a 40,000 MTPA expansion (about INR1,125 Crores) that is due in FY28.

segments.commentary: No mining operations in Q1 as environmental and licensing approvals are awaited, with timing of 3 to 6 months cited. Segment EBIT fell to about INR1 Crore from about INR25 Crores.

guidance_outlook: Management maintained the INR1,100 Crores PAT target for FY28 and said nothing had changed, but gave no FY27 guidance.

Total capex announced is about INR2,000 Crores (LFP INR1,125 Crores, new announcements INR368 Crores, Birla Tyres INR500 Crores this year), with about INR1,000 Crores expected in each of FY27 and FY28.
Management said free cash flow will fund the capex with no incremental debt.
Management expects top-line growth from both volume and value next quarter.
Birla Tyres is expected to reach EBITDA breakeven and be cash positive in FY27.
Management said 40,000 MTPA LFP would yield about INR3,000 Crores top line at current prices, and 200,000 MTPA LFP would need about INR4,800 Crores capex.
capex_capacity: CNT: 200 MTPA plant, about INR70 Crores capex, commissioning targeted for Q4 FY27.
Super speciality carbon black: conversion of 6,000 MTPA existing capacity for INR170 Crores, with capacity start in FY28.
Anode: 200 MTPA plant commissioned April 2026, with no further anode capex announced; natural graphite and silicon carbon capacity planned.

LFP pricing is said to be at parity with China, and management claims a cost advantage from India-based production and non-China raw materials.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other-segment EBIT drop from INR25 Crores to about INR1 Crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Mining did not operate this quarter while licences are awaited, so the mining profit did not recur; higher Birla Tyres revenue offset top-line effects.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue potential of the new capex?
qa_highlights.answer: 40,000 MTPA LFP at today's prices gives about INR3,000 Crores top line; anthraquinone/carbazole about INR250-300 Crores; super speciality carbon black about 3x capex (about INR500 Crores); CNT less than INR100 Crores; 200 MTPA anode about INR120-130 Crores.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FX loss a recurring issue and what drove other income?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no hedging policy change and the FX loss was a one-off for the currency volatility; other income came from FD and mutual fund deployment, borrowings in CPs and mark-to-market gains on IBC, Sicona and Birla Tyres NCDs, and may swing 30-40% QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: Will the LFP and new capex be debt-funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said free cash flow will cover the capex with no incremental debt.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company increase its stake in IBC?
qa_highlights.answer: No; management called IBC a strategic investment and said it is not looking to raise its stake further.

qa_highlights.question: What are the margins on the new CNT and SSCB products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose margins, saying they are significantly higher than existing speciality carbon black.

qa_highlights.question: Is the LFP cathode economics viable against Chinese pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Excel-based cost comparisons are not reliable, cited cost advantages, and declined to disclose lithium carbonate sourcing.

risks_watch: Mining remains idle pending environmental clearance, which could take 3-6 months, with segment EBIT near zero.

Birla Tyres is not yet EBITDA positive, and its breakeven is targeted within FY27 after the TBB to OTR conversion.
Analysts questioned whether LFP pricing at China parity leaves a positive gross spread; management declined to disclose input costs.
Other income is volatile (30-40% QoQ swing) and the FX loss needs to be watched next quarter.
500184|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and expansive on long-term growth and new products, but evasive on specifics: margins, lithium sourcing, customer timelines and FY27 guidance were withheld, with 'competitive nature' cited for limited disclosure.
key_quotes: Our Coal Tar Pitch business continues to anchor the company.
We don't give quarter and year guidelines, never.

500184|2026-09.headline: Himadri Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose to INR 1,543 crore (+44% YoY) and PAT to INR 240 crore (+28%), while per-tonne EBITDA eased sequentially to about INR 21,000.
500184|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 standalone EBITDA was INR 308 crore (+27% YoY) and PAT INR 240 crore (+28% YoY); consolidated revenue was INR 1,691 crore and PAT INR 231 crore (+31%). Management attributed the sequential per-tonne EBITDA dip (from about INR 22,700-22,800 to about INR 21,000) to a raw-material pass-through lag, higher freight costs, and a higher export share (33% vs 26%). New carbon nanotube, LFP and anthraquinone/carbazole capacities are on schedule, with commissioning timelines reiterated, and the proposed merger of the Birla Tyres business into Himadri was announced. Mining is expected to restart this quarter after environmental clearance was received.

Per-tonne EBITDA is guided to a range of about INR 20,000-24,000 going forward; management says it is confident of staying above INR 20,000 on a sustainable basis.

Capex spend of about INR 250 crore in Q2 FY27; total FY27 spend guided at INR 800-900 crore. Management said the roughly INR 1,500 crore programme over two years will be funded from internal accruals, not debt.
Most new capacity is expected to show full impact from FY29, per the analyst's read of management's reply.
Management expects working capital to normalise over the next two quarters and operating cash flow to turn positive on an annual basis.

Anthraquinone and carbazole: 5,300 TPA total, with both phases commissioned together by Q4 FY27 to avoid a three-month shutdown.

demand_pricing: Volume grew 11% YoY in Q2 FY27 (1,46,000 tonnes cited on the call); revenue rose 58% YoY, driven by volume and higher raw-material-linked selling prices.

Battery materials: management expects pricing to be in line with Chinese suppliers; anode products are at sample stage, with no realisation guidance given.
Carbon black demand described as robust; ENERGEX grades received approval for high-voltage cable and battery applications and have started commercial orders.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the sharp gross margin moderation, and when will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are stable and that per-tonne EBITDA was about INR 21,000 vs INR 17,900 YoY and INR 22,700-22,800 QoQ. The dip was attributed to pricing pass-through timing, higher freight and a higher export share, all described as temporary.

qa_highlights.question: Are the new LFP, anthraquinone and carbazole products margin-accretive from start?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed yes, saying they would add to incremental margin from the start. For LFP, margin guidance was deferred until commercial discussions begin after the 2,000 TPA plant.

qa_highlights.question: How much capex has been spent, and what is planned for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 250 crore spent in Q2 FY27, with INR 800-900 crore expected in FY27. Commercial dates for projects fall before FY28, so most capacity impact is expected from FY29.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status and revenue potential of mining?
qa_highlights.answer: Environmental clearance was received in October 2026 and operations are to start in the current quarter. The longer-term top-line potential is about INR 500 crore, depending on volume.

qa_highlights.question: Why did carbon black EBITDA per tonne fall vs the peer, and is there a sweet spot from coal tar?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said raw-material prices are correlated, so there is no pricing edge. The advantage is clean, self-produced feedstock for speciality carbon black, and the decline was attributed to freight and export mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the funding plan for the remaining capex?

500186|2026-03.headline: HOEC's Q4 FY26 call: FY26 profit and revenue turned negative after HPCL crude sale reversal; management targets 10,000-11,000 boepd by mid-2027.
500186|2026-03.overview: Management, led by new MD & CEO Baroruchi Mishra with CFO Allen Joseph Andrade, reported FY26 revenue, EBITDA and PAT all negative, mainly due to reversal of a crude sale to HPCL (revenue would otherwise have been INR559 crores). Standalone PAT was INR288 crores versus INR344 crores a year earlier, and lifting cost was $28.4/bbl versus $28.6/bbl. Production is about 15 thousand boe/d with a further 4-7 thousand boe/d locked in by lack of infrastructure, and management targets 10,000-11,000 boe/d by mid-2027, 22,000 by 2028 and 32,000 by 2029. Most of the Q&A focused on HPCL crude settlement, the Dirok gas pipeline connection, B-80 workovers, and funding, where management gave few hard numbers and deferred FY27 debt and EBITDA guidance to next quarter.

segments.name: B-80 (Offshore, Mumbai High area)
segments.commentary: 2P reserves of 26 MMboe with about 1 MMboe produced to date; 2 subsea wells need workover, deferred from last quarter for lack of funds, and 3 new wells planned post-monsoon. Target 4,000-5,000 bbl/d plus 7.5-10 MMscfd gas from the program.

segments.name: PY-1 (Offshore/onshore gas, Krishna-Godavari-type gas processing link)
segments.commentary: Historically 45-50 MMscfd at start-up, now largely shut in. Plan is 2 development wells plus coiled tubing intervention, adding about 12-15 MMscfd by mid-2027, with one exploration well in a 4-well campaign.

segments.name: Dirok (Assam, gas)
segments.commentary: Currently producing 0.3-0.4 MMscm/d (about 15 MMscfd gross) versus 1.1-1.2 MMscm/d potential, constrained by DNPL pipeline (1 MMscmd flowing vs 2.5 MMscmd capacity). Potential 45 MMscfd, 70 MMscfd with 3 more wells once the DFL-Duliajan 24-inch, 175 km line is built in 2-3 years. Condensate 200-250 bbl/d now, 700-900 bbl/d at 45 MMscfd (gross).

segments.name: Kharsang (oil and gas)
segments.commentary: 9 wells drilled and production doubled; 9 more wells planned in the coming campaign. Gross production about 700+ bbl/d; significant gas found.

segments.name: B-15 (new award)
segments.commentary: 15 MMboe in-place reserves; FDP concept selection under way, FEED to follow, then FID. 3-5 wells possible; target 4,000-5,000 bbl/d and about 10 MMscfd, timing not committed.

segments.name: Cambay (Gujarat)
segments.commentary: Focus on workovers, production enhancement and secondary recovery for low-cost incremental output.

segments.name: Greater Dirok / Umatara
segments.commentary: Exploration and appraisal upside; North Dirok exploration well (4,000-5,000 m) could add 10-15 MMscfd if successful.

guidance_outlook: Production target of 10,000-11,000 boe/d by June 2027, with management saying it is confident of above 8,000 boe/d at minimum.
Production ramp to 22,000 boe/d in 2028 and 32,000 boe/d in 2029.
Reserves: 1P about 40 MMboe, 2P about 60 MMboe, 3P about 109 MMboe; management values 1P-2P at USD3-5 billion depending on oil price.
FY27 and FY28 debt and EBITDA outlook deferred to next quarter's call.
HPCL crude proceeds expected over 2-3 months; Dirok pipeline connection hoped for in 1-2 months but no firm date given.
capex_capacity: Drilling plan: 20 wells in various stages of preparation; Kharsang 9 more wells, PY-1 2 development wells plus 1 exploration well, B-80 3 wells plus 2 workovers, Dirok 3 wells (all contingent on pipeline, funds and rig availability).
Two rigs planned, one each for PY-1/Kharsang and B-80; target to complete B-80 three wells and two workovers by May 2027, when rig tow insurance expires.
Dirok evacuation depends on NRL connection of 55 km DNPL replacement section (laid, not yet tied in; NRL shutdown possibly needed) and on the DFL-Duliajan 24-inch, 175 km line in 2-3 years.
Funding: internal accruals plus bank facilities under discussion; equity raise not ruled out but not committed.
demand_pricing: HPCL crude sale cancelled and resold to third-party buyers on a Brent-minus-X basis; first few weeks at a firm price agreed under the COSA, then Brent-linked.
Physical lifting of about 300-700 tonnes per week from HPCL refinery; full proceeds expected over 2-3 months.
Buyers accepted crude on an as-is, where-is basis after third-party sample analysis; management says B-80 samples show zero contamination from wells.
Last crude cargo sold at USD109/bbl (per management).

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 net production target, split by field?
qa_highlights.answer: 10,000-11,000 boe/d by June 2027; PY-1 about 12-15 MMscfd, B-80 4,000-5,000 bbl/d, Assam 70 MMscfd target, Kharsang doubling again with 9 wells. Management stressed that timing depends on drilling, financing and rigs.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 and FY28 debt and EBITDA outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Not given; management deferred this to the next quarter to avoid giving a number that could change.

qa_highlights.question: When will the HPCL revenue be realised?

qa_highlights.question: When will Dirok gas flow via the national grid / DNPL, and at what rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects flow in 1-2 months but cannot give a firm date. Current 0.3-0.4 MMscmd could rise to 0.8-0.9 MMscmd, against 1.1-1.2 potential, depending on pipeline allocation.

qa_highlights.question: How will B-15 and B-80 ramp, and what is the pace?
qa_highlights.answer: B-80: 3 wells and 2 workovers targeted by May 2027. B-15: 3-5 wells possible, FDP still at concept stage, with a 4,000-5,000 bbl/d target; tie-back to the B-80 facility or a separate export line is under evaluation.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company raise equity, and what are the costs of production?

risks_watch: HPCL conciliation outcome and whether HPCL reimbursement or compensation is required; inventory is carried at 31 March valuation against lower current prices, and the Q4 PAT benefited from the HPCL derecognition.
Funding gap: INR260 crores tied up in crude receivables delayed B-80 workovers; capex depends on bank facilities not yet sanctioned.
Dirok production depends on DNPL pipeline tie-in and NRL and other shippers' allocation; the gas pipeline is owned by Assam Gas Company.
Rig availability, monsoon timing and subsea Christmas-tree condition for B-80 workovers; possible slippage of 3-6 months.
Earlier timeline commitments (connectivity, pipeline) have slipped repeatedly, per analyst feedback; management's targets are conditional.

key_quotes: So, at this stage, allow me only to say that we will fund it both with our internal accruals and with facilities that we'd like to get from the banks to raise capital.
We are targeting to get to 10,000 to 11,000 barrels by June of next year.

500186|2026-06.headline: HOEC Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose to INR117.5 crore from negative INR194 crore, but PBT before exceptionals fell to INR12.5 crore on B-80 output loss and HPCL crude resale.
500186|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue from operations was INR117.5 crore versus a negative INR194 crore in Q4, which reflected reversal of the HPCL crude sale (INR259 crore). Kharsang output rose from about 12,300 to 17,400 BOE and crude realisation rose to about $95.5/bbl from $70.8/bbl. Standalone PBT before exceptionals fell to INR12.5 crore from INR30.4 crore, due to inventory-related cost offsets. B-80 output was hit by higher water cut, and the HPCL-stored crude is being resold to third parties at a slower pace than expected, with a further mark-to-market loss expected. Management is relying on debt to fund the B-80 workover and three-well programme.

segments.commentary: Production reduced by higher water cut from one producing well; compressor configuration changed and in test mode. Crude stored at HPCL Chembur is being sold via tankers; about 15% sold so far. Gas realisation around $15-16/MMBTU on exchange, average $16.5/MMBTU.

segments.commentary: Operated with ~27% stake; currently producing only 50-70% of well capability due to evacuation limits. DNPL line capacity degraded to ~1-1.5 MMSCMD versus 2.5 MMSCMD design; average gas realisation about $12.5/MMBTU.

segments.commentary: Three wells suffered serious production loss; rig-less intervention contracted and funded from own books. Two new wells deferred and contingent on take-or-pay gas agreement with GAIL or IOCL. Realisation about $10-12/MMBTU.

segments.commentary: Palej debottlenecking delivered 5-6% production increase last quarter; management guides 20-30% increase over time. Sucker rod pumps ordered and a new exploration block pending final approval.

segments.name: B-15 (new block)
segments.commentary: Recoverable reserves 16 MMBOE; FDP under preparation with three to four concepts, including tie-back to ONGC platform. Drilling planned in FY28.

B-80 crude inventory at HPCL Chembur expected to clear by end-October/early November 2026; sales from FSO in October in 120,000-150,000 bbl tranches.

Crude from B-80 resold to third parties; HPCL offtake continues by tanker with gantries added; realisation losses of INR4-6 crore incurred so far.

Oil sales to Digboi Refinery and mainly IOCL from Kharsang.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of B-80 crude stored at HPCL and when will it clear?

500188|2026-06.headline: Hindustan Zinc Q1 FY27 record EBITDA of INR8,074 crores (59% margin) and net profit of INR5,469 crores, with zinc COP at USD851/t.
500188|2026-06.overview: Hindustan Zinc posted its highest-ever quarterly revenue (INR13,747 crores, up 77% YoY), EBITDA (INR8,074 crores, up 109% YoY) and net profit (INR5,469 crores, up 145% YoY) in Q1 FY27. Mine metal output of 268,000 t was the highest first quarter in five years, and refined metal rose 4% YoY to 260,000 t. Zinc cost of production excluding royalty fell to USD851/t, the lowest since the underground transition, helped by by-product realisation and better grades. The company sold 10 kt of lead concentrate (about 9 t silver and 6 kt lead metal) and ended with net cash of INR5,572 crores. Leadership is changing: Arun Misra hands over to Amarendu Prakash as CEO from 1 August 2026, and Amit Gupta is the new CFO.

segments.name: Zinc (mined and refined)
segments.commentary: Mined metal output of 268,000 t and refined output of 260,000 t, with zinc COP at USD851/t excluding royalty. Management guides to 1.1 million t for FY27 and expects Q4 at 280–290 kt.

segments.name: Silver
segments.commentary: Silver output of 149 t, with 10–15 t estimated locked in WIP; excluding concentrate sales, about 158 t was extracted. Silver contributed about 46% of profitability; the company needs about 175 t per quarter to reach its 680 t target.

segments.name: Lead and lead concentrate
segments.commentary: Sold 10 kt of inferior-grade concentrate stock from the RD mine ramp-up, realising INR315 crores. Company policy remains not to sell concentrate, and remaining old inventory will be used in smelters first.

segments.name: Sulphuric acid and fertiliser
segments.commentary: Sulphuric acid prices are reported up about 200% YoY. The phosphoric acid portion of the fertiliser plant at Chanderiya is due in Q2, and the full fertiliser plant is due in Q1 FY28 pending environmental clearance; about INR500 crores spent to date.

guidance_outlook: FY27 mined metal guidance of 1.1 million t reiterated; management sees no need to revise it and expects no further smelter shutdowns.
Zinc COP guided at USD975–1,000/t, with Q1 beating it through by-product realisation.
FY27 growth capex guided at USD500–600 million; INR800 crores spent in Q1.
Net cash position expected to be maintained at FY27 exit, based on volume and price assumptions.
Dividend policy unchanged: minimum 30% of profit plus 5% of reserves.
250 KTPA Debari integrated smelter and about 650 kt total metal capacity including mines: estimated INR24,000–25,000 crores, 36-month build, Board approval expected by Q3 FY27.
Tailings reprocessing plant construction started; about 30–35 kt zinc expected after about 24 months, with a 6–8 month ramp-up.
capex_capacity: Debari 250 KTPA integrated zinc smelter: mine development started to match mining capacity; capex estimate at a straight-line rate of about INR12,000 crores per 250 kt, pending tender outcome in about one month.
Tailings reprocessing plant: construction started and site mobilisation for infrastructure completed; 30–35 kt zinc output expected.
Hot acid leaching plant at Dariba and phosphoric acid/fertiliser plant at Chanderiya: on track for Q2 completion (phosphoric acid portion); full fertiliser plant by Q1 FY28.
Rampura Agucha and Chanderiya/Dariba debottlenecking, plus the 160,000 t pa roaster, supported output in Q1.
REE/Yttrium block in Gundlupet, Karnataka: exploration 2–3 years; production expected around FY2031–32.
demand_pricing: Zinc averaged USD3,466/t in Q1 with a high of USD3,625/t; lead averaged USD1,954/t.
Silver moderated to USD73/troy oz from the prior quarter's higher levels.
Hedge book: 48 kt zinc open at USD3,162/t and 34 t silver at USD63/oz; no hedging done in FY27 so far.
Coal mix: linkage coal share fell to 36% from 54% a year earlier and 64% in Q4; imported coal costs were higher, lifting power and fuel costs QoQ.
Revenue was supported by stronger dollar, higher by-product realisation and concentrate sales.

qa_highlights.question: Why did power and fuel costs rise QoQ despite lower metal output and higher RE share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited lower linkage coal materialisation due to mine conditions, plus costlier imported coal, partly offset by higher RE power use.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company revise FY27 production guidance and is 1.1 Mt achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is confident in 1.1 Mt: 260 kt in Q1 implies about 1,040 kt on a straight-line basis, and Q4 typically reaches 280–290 kt. No revision is planned.

qa_highlights.question: What net cash position is expected at FY27 exit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to remain a net cash company at FY27 exit, based on its volume and price assumptions.

qa_highlights.question: Clarify the SEBI observations on related party transactions and the corrective steps taken.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said omnibus approvals have value limits; an alarm now triggers at 80% of the approved value, prompting Board and Audit Committee re-approval.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline and capex for the 600+ kt smelter project?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex for the 650 kt including mines is estimated at INR24,000–25,000 crores; tendering is ongoing, a 36-month build is expected after Board approval, and Board approval is targeted by Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Silver guidance and what is needed per quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says silver grades should improve in Q2–Q4 with better PPM ore, with the strongest output in Q4; the 680 t target is seen as achievable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the fertiliser/phosphoric acid timeline and economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Only the phosphoric acid portion is due in Q2; the fertiliser plant is pending environmental clearance and is expected by Q1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Any update on government stake sale and dividend policy after the Vedanta demerger?
qa_highlights.answer: Government stake sale is for the government to comment on. Dividend policy is unchanged: minimum 30% of profit plus 5% of reserves, with INR11/share already paid.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of the USD50/t QoQ COP reduction and by-product effect?
qa_highlights.answer: COP is in line with the USD975–1,000/t guidance; the additional benefit comes from by-product realisation, which is credited through the COP, and no separate quantification was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is the royalty ratio to revenue at a multi-quarter low because of sulphuric acid?
qa_highlights.answer: Sulphuric acid carries no royalty. Mineral royalty is set as a percentage of the LME price, so it is not a fixed percentage of revenue.

Government stake sale speculation; no update from management.

500188|2026-09.headline: Hindustan Zinc Q2 FY27 EBITDA hit a record INR9,285 crore (+108% YoY) at 62% margin, with net profit of INR6,412 crore; zinc COP guidance cut to $825-850/t.
500188|2026-09.overview: Hindustan Zinc reported record Q2 FY27 results, with revenue from operations of INR15,093 crore (+77% YoY), EBITDA of INR9,285 crore and net profit of INR6,412 crore (+142% YoY). Mined metal output rose 5% YoY to a record Q2 and refined metal rose 7%, while zinc COP fell to $703/t (down 29%). Management revised full-year zinc COP guidance down sharply to $825-850/t from $975-1,000/t, partly offset by about $50/t of geopolitical cost escalation. Net cash closed at INR11,268 crore after free cash flow before growth capex of INR6,389 crore in the quarter.

segments.name: Zinc (mined and refined)

qa_highlights.question: Can COP go below the revised $825-850/t guidance given sulfuric acid strength?
