500201|2026-03.headline: India Glycols FY26 net revenue rose 11.8% to INR4,211 crores, with EBITDA up 24.5% to INR654 crores and margin at 15.5%.
500201|2026-03.overview: FY26 showed strong operating performance: gross revenue INR9,827 crores (+8.7%), net revenue INR4,211 crores (+11.8%), EBITDA INR654 crores (+24.5%) and PAT INR293 crores (+26.8%). Q4 net revenue rose 13.1% to INR976 crores with EBITDA of INR167 crores (+13.3%). Bio-Fuels and Chemicals drove margin gains, while Chemicals sales fell and Ennature Biopharma margins stayed under pressure. Management said the Middle East war had a mixed but slightly positive effect via ethanol competitiveness, though export business to the Middle East was on hold. Debt was reduced by prepaying about INR804 crores in the quarter, including INR467 crores from a November 2025 equity issue.

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: FY26 net revenue INR1,203 crores (-10.4%), EBIT INR141 crores (+12.5%), EBIT margin 11.7%. Q4 net revenue INR301 crores (+18.8%), EBIT INR37 crores (+37.4%), margin 12.2%.

segments.name: Potable Spirits (IMFL + IMIL)
segments.commentary: FY26 top-line INR1,331 crores (+14.4%), EBIT INR285 crores (+11.1%). Q4 top-line INR306 crores (+7.9%), EBIT INR68 crores, margin 22.1%. IMFL is about 31% of segment revenue per management, with Amrut about 5-6%.

segments.name: Bio-Fuels
segments.commentary: FY26 top-line INR1,470 crores (+40.9%), EBIT INR115 crores (+103.3%), margin 7.8%. Q4 top-line INR305 crores (+11.6%), EBIT INR30 crores (+90.0%), margin 9.9%.

segments.name: Ennature Biopharma
segments.commentary: FY26 top-line broadly flat with a nominal decline, margins under pressure. Q4 top-line grew 23.2%, but EBIT was only INR3 crores.

guidance_outlook: Management expects improved profitability and top-line growth in Chemicals for FY27, and expects performance chemicals to more than double in FY27 (hoped, not projected).

Interest cost expected to stay around INR25 crores per quarter; FY27 scheduled term-loan repayment about INR268 crores (liquor INR168 crores, chemicals INR100 crores), plus further prepayments of high-cost debt.
Management expects the JV share of profit to improve drastically from FY26 INR46.42 crores as 49% JV is consolidated into the Chemicals business.
Plan to sell a further 24% JV equity in FY28-29 per agreement, proceeds to repay term loans and make the Chemical business debt-free by FY28-29 (hoped).

Management aims for high double-digit IMFL growth via geographic expansion (Kerala, Andhra Pradesh, Rajasthan) and new brands; no formal margin guidance for Potable Spirits beyond Q4's 22% EBIT margin.
capex_capacity: Capex of about INR830 crores in FY26, with about INR600 crores spent in the last six months; about INR400 crores capitalised from grain distilleries at Gorakhpur and Kashipur.
Plant shutdown from 17 March to 2 April 2026 for catalyst change, reducing production and some sales; EO supply to the Clariant JV stopped for 15-20 days.
Ethanol capacity now slightly exceeds in-house Bio-Fuels consumption; grain-based (dual feedstock) ethanol flexibility retained.
Ennature Biopharma investing in manufacturing capability and branded nutraceutical clinical studies, with some studies to complete in FY27.
demand_pricing: Potable Spirits: IMIL is about 75% of segment volume but about 52% of UP value; IMFL is about 16% of UP volume and 34% of value. IMFL volumes grew 30% in the year, with UP IMFL top-line growth of 25% last year.
IMIL growth was 21% in Uttarakhand and 11% in UP; Amazing Vodka reached a 21% market share in Uttarakhand vs 18% last year.
Bacardi bottling revenue sits in miscellaneous income, with filling charges estimated at 2-3% of Potable revenue.
Grain prices fell from about INR24/kg mid-2025 to about INR21-22/kg in Q4 FY26; DDGS prices improved.

Imported ethanol prices rose sharply on freight and other factors, while domestic prices were stable or slightly lower; the Middle East war raised crude and constrained MEG and ethanol availability, which improved ethanol-based product competitiveness.
Oilfield chemical exports to the Middle East, largely for New Park, are on hold due to the war; propylene oxide prices and availability were also affected.
Chemicals sales declined due to Chinese low-cost glycol ethers, weaker gases sales after argon price spikes, and lower EO sales to the JV when EO was uncompetitive versus Reliance.

qa_highlights.question: How was business disturbed by the plant shutdown, and what is the Potable Spirits split and margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Shutdown for catalyst change (about every 1.5 years) affected EO supply to the Clariant JV and some specialty products, not MEG. IMFL is about 25% and IMIL about 75% of Potable Spirits (Raju Vaziraney, although later data cite IMFL at 31% of revenue). Management did not guide to a margin number, saying Q4's 22% EBIT margin is not assured to be sustained.

qa_highlights.question: Why did BSPC/Chemicals top-line decline, and are plants at optimal level?
qa_highlights.answer: Glycol ethers lost share to cheaper Chinese and propylene/butylene-based material, gases declined on high argon prices in the prior year, and EO sales to the JV fell. Management expects improved profitability and top-line growth in FY27 and said the large EO price delta with Reliance has narrowed.

qa_highlights.question: Why was JV profit INR13 crores in Q4 and what is the JV monetisation plan?
qa_highlights.answer: JV profit improved on mix and imported traded materials from Clariant; FY26 share of profit was INR46.42 crores vs INR46.40 crores. The company plans to sell a further 24% equity in FY28-29 per the agreement to repay term loans and make Chemicals debt-free.

qa_highlights.question: Finance cost run-rate and FY27 debt repayment?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR804 crores prepaid in Q4 (INR467 crores from promoter equity, rest internal cash). Interest cost to stay around INR25 crores per quarter. FY27 scheduled repayment is INR268 crores (liquor INR168 crores, chemicals INR100 crores), plus prepayments.

qa_highlights.question: Silver sale during shutdown and grain availability?
qa_highlights.answer: Silver sold for INR98 crores against purchase cost of INR51 crores; no profit was booked because catalyst consumption was not yet provided. Grain stocks are adequate and prices are stable; grain was about 73% of ethanol feedstock in FY26 with maize about 46%.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the Ennature Biopharma outlook and nicotine pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is shifting nicotine to value-added long-term customers and diversifying into branded nutraceuticals with clinical studies. EBITDA improvement may not show in FY27 despite customer acquisition.

risks_watch: Middle East war: export business for oilfield chemicals on hold; propylene oxide availability and prices affected; demand softening in some areas.
Ennature Biopharma margins under pressure from nicotine price competition and the Thiocolchicoside price cycle; EBIT was only INR3 crores in Q4.
Bio-Fuels profitability depends on government blending policy (20% achieved; talk of higher blending and flex-fuel) and feedstock prices.
Pending NCLT-approved demerger of a division; order expected around 21 May 2026 with a possible June 2026 order.
Chemicals volume recovery depends on JV EO offtake, which was affected by the shutdown and the Reliance price gap.
500201|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on the full year and on premiumisation and ethanol, but evasive on specifics: margin guidance, JV exit timing and the Amrut and Bacardi economics were deferred or left undisclosed. Cautious on Chemicals and Ennature, where management said results will improve but gave few numbers.
key_quotes: So whilst, if you remember when we started doing these calls, we spoke about certain challenges that the business had and a strategy to overcome those challenges both in terms of actions in the marketplace, diversifying our portfolio, taking some cost actions.
And as I have already told that in '28-'29, we are going to sell out 24% more equity as per the agreement.

Right now, to a large extent that has been adjusted, and we believe that the huge delta that we saw for a period of one-and-a- half-two years, hopefully in my opinion, maybe a thing of the past and we should see much better competitiveness on that front as well.

500201|2026-06.headline: India Glycols Q1 FY27 net revenue rose 9% to INR1,130 crore and record EBITDA of INR170 crore (+13%), with PAT up 32%.
500201|2026-06.overview: Consolidated net revenue reached INR1,130 crore (+9% YoY) and EBITDA INR170 crore (+13%), with EBITDA margin at 15.0% versus 14.3%. Management said PAT rose 32% and finance costs fell to INR25 crore from INR45 crore on debt reduction. The NCLT sanctioned the demerger scheme on 17 July 2026 and the company is now reporting under three entities. Management attributed part of the quarter's gains to the war-driven crude spike, which made bio-based EO competitive with Reliance's product again. Sequential EBITDA comparison is distorted by Q4 FY26 including about INR39 crore of Clariant dividend income.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR45 crore in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR694 crore; EBITDA INR120 crore; margin 17.3%
financial_highlights.change: EBITDA +17% YoY; margin vs 14.7% in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: India Glycols (chemicals, new structure) net revenue
financial_highlights.value: INR345 crore; EBITDA INR40 crore; margin 11.6%
INR90 crore; EBITDA INR10 crore; margin 11.1%

financial_highlights.metric: Q4 FY26 EBITDA (as stated on call)

segments.name: IGL Spirits (potable spirits)
segments.commentary: Spirits net revenue INR371 crore with EBITDA margin 22.9% (+207 bps). IMFL revenue grew 26% to 1.4 million cases (+55% volume); non-IMFL revenue was flat at INR279 crore with volume of 7.5 million cases (+6%).

segments.name: Bio-Fuel (ethanol)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR323 crore (+7%), EBIT INR27 crore (+19%), EBIT margin 8.4%; management also cited EBITDA margin of 10.8% (+250 bps).

segments.name: Chemicals (India Glycols)
segments.commentary: Chemicals revenue INR332 crore (+25%) at 11.4% EBITDA margin; small gases INR13 crore at 23.1% margin. Glycols value up 83%; green solvents and glycol ethers volume +6%, value +13%, gross margin close to 50%. Performance chemicals grew 40%, below target.

segments.name: Ennature Bio Pharma
segments.commentary: Best-ever quarter at INR83 crore revenue (per call) / INR90 crore net revenue under new structure, up 53-65%; EBITDA up ~188% per the prepared remarks. Nicotine sales doubled QoQ on European customer conversions; thiocolchicoside up 26% QoQ.

segments.name: Clariant JV (Kashipur)
segments.commentary: JV net revenue up 21% QoQ with EBITDA up in high double digits QoQ; JV profit cited at about INR21 crore versus about INR19 crore a year earlier.

guidance_outlook: IGL Spirits: EBITDA above INR500 crore for FY27 (INR120 crore already delivered in Q1); IMFL volume to roughly double versus FY26 (FY26 IMFL volume 3.4 million cases).
Spirits: management expects healthy double-digit growth in FY28 and aims to be debt-free from FY28; target EBITDA above INR1,000 crore in four to five years.

Chemicals aspiration (explicitly not a projection): EBITDA about INR400 crore and revenue about INR2,500 crore in four to five years; FY27 revenue aspiration INR150 crore-plus for the new performance chemicals business; margin targeted to rise toward 30% gross margin.
Ennature aspiration: EBITDA INR130-150 crore over the next four to five years.
Capex in chemicals expected to be small: INR5-20 crore incremental in the current year; no INR400-500 crore plant expected for at least two years.
capex_capacity: Chemicals capex plans: incremental INR5-10 crore, possibly up to INR15-20 crore this year, via modular expansion; new plant additions to date about INR50-60 crore.
Ennature started nicotine crude processing at its Kashipur plant, adding capacity.
Spirits: captive ENA capacity described as sufficient, supporting cost advantage in UP, Uttarakhand and Delhi.

Demerger: after effectiveness, Spirits, Bio-Fuel and Bio Pharma undertakings transfer to dedicated resulting companies; IGL Spirits will hold potable spirits, Bio-Fuel and biopolymers; Ennature retains nutraceuticals and APIs. Effective date not yet communicated.
demand_pricing: Spirits: management says the industry grew at a 4-5% CAGR over the last one to two years; IMFL growth attributed to launches in deluxe whisky, semi-premium vodka and white spirits. Prestige & Above volume ~0.5 million cases, roughly double last year.
Mix: revenue lagged volume in Spirits because of state mix (Delhi growth lower margin) and brand mix (mass premium grew faster).

Chemicals: ethylene oxide became similar to or slightly cheaper than Reliance's EO for a few months, increasing specialty chemicals off-take. Oil and gas and Middle East exports were hit by propylene oxide shortages and freight volatility (westbound freight up 5-20x).
Ennature: raw material availability and pricing volatile and a challenge in Q2 as well.

qa_highlights.question: What is the guidance for potable spirits for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 EBITDA above INR500 crore, with INR120 crore delivered in Q1; volume to double versus last year, with healthy double-digit growth expected next year.

qa_highlights.question: What capex is planned for the NSU (chemicals) business and how will it scale?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex limited to about INR5-20 crore this year; cumulative new plant investment about INR50-60 crore. Aspiration of INR150 crore-plus revenue this year and INR600-700 crore in 4-5 years, with margins improving over time.

qa_highlights.question: Are JV profits sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a fair assumption; JV PAT about INR19 crore a year ago versus INR21 crore now, with the improvement linked to narrower EO cost disadvantage.

qa_highlights.question: Prestige & Above volumes and IMFL revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: P&A about 0.5 million cases, roughly double last year. FY26 IMFL volume was 3.4 million cases; FY26 IMFL revenue was not disclosed and will be sent later.

qa_highlights.question: Why did volumes grow faster than revenue in Spirits?
qa_highlights.answer: Attributed to state mix (Delhi growth lower margin) and brand mix (mass premium growing faster); revenue growth expected to exceed volume growth as premium mix rises.

qa_highlights.question: What is the IMFL margin versus country liquor?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross margins in deluxe and semi-premium whisky are almost the same as in P&A and did not give separate EBITDA margins.

risks_watch: Demerger effectiveness date not yet communicated; NCLT sanctioned the scheme on 17 July 2026 and the three-entity reporting structure depends on effectiveness.

Sustainability of JV profit: JV PAT about INR21 crore this quarter versus about INR19 crore a year ago, linked to narrower EO cost disadvantage versus Reliance; management called it a fair assumption.
Ennature raw material availability and pricing volatile; described as a challenge in Q2 as well.
Chemicals performance chemicals growth of 40% was below target; oil and gas and Middle East exports hit by propylene oxide shortages and westbound freight volatility (5-20x).
Quarter-on-quarter EBITDA comparison distorted by Q4 FY26 Clariant dividend income of about INR39 crore; a shareholder query on quarterly EBITDA trend was deferred to email.
Spirits FY27 guidance (EBITDA above INR500 crore, IMFL volume roughly double) and FY26 IMFL revenue not yet disclosed; FY26 IMFL revenue to be sent later.
key_quotes: This is an aspiration, this is not something that we are giving as a projection.
I would like to underline it again that this is not a projection.
Revenue, I will have to get back to you. I do not have it off the book.
That is something which we cannot disclose.
500201|2026-06.management_tone: Management was confident and upbeat on Spirits and Ennature, but repeatedly qualified forward-looking figures as aspirations rather than guidance, for example the chemicals INR400 crore EBITDA target and the Ennature INR130-150 crore EBITDA target. It was more cautious on performance chemicals, which grew below target, and deferred several detailed questions (FY26 IMFL revenue, royalty to Amrut, quarterly EBITDA trend) to follow-up.

500209|2026-06.headline: Infosys cut FY27 cc revenue growth guidance to 1.5%–3% from 1.5%–3.5% after Q1 cc growth of 2.4% YoY; margin guidance held at 20%–22%.
500209|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was $5,082 mn, up 1% QoQ and 2.4% YoY in constant currency, with a one-off 50 bps hit from a EURS client program termination. Operating margin rose 20 bps QoQ to 21.1%, helped by 70 bps rupee tailwind and 20 bps from Project Maximus, while large deal TCV was $3.6 bn with 61% net new. Management cut the revenue range on softer volumes, weaker pricing from AI-led productivity asks and competition, and offshoring/onsite-mix shifts. The Board also named Ashiss Dash as CEO-designate, succeeding Salil Parekh on April 1, 2027.

financial_highlights.change: +1% QoQ, +2.4% YoY in constant currency; acquisitions contributed ~1.1% QoQ
61% net new; 22 large deals, 3 worth ~$400 mn each
up from 5.5% in Q3 FY26 per management
-4 days QoQ; 76 days incl. unbilled net of unearned vs 78 in Q4

segments.name: Financial Services
segments.commentary: Management expects FS growth above company average for the rest of FY27; ~$1 bn of large deal net new TCV and 5 large deal wins in FS and Communications combined.

segments.name: EURS
segments.commentary: Q1 hit by a one-off program termination (~50 bps); adjusted growth described as strong, and EURS expected to grow above company average.

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: Grew ~1.5% reported (1% cc per editor's note) despite a large European auto client decline; 3 large deal wins.

segments.name: Retail and CPG
segments.commentary: Consumer spend muted; large deal pipeline healthy but decision cycles longer; one of two segments flagged as still challenged along with Communications.

segments.name: Communications
segments.commentary: Operating environment challenging; clients prioritising near-term AI gains; one of two segments flagged as challenged.

segments.name: Life Sciences / Healthcare
segments.commentary: Expected benefit from the Optimum Healthcare acquisition (~1.7% contribution to FY27 revenue guidance from Optimum Healthcare and Stratus).

guidance_outlook: FY27 constant-currency revenue growth cut to 1.5%–3% YoY from prior 1.5%–3.5%; guidance includes ~1.7% from acquisitions (Optimum Healthcare, Stratus), slightly over 1% drag from a European manufacturing client, and 0.75%–1% from offshore shift.
Like-to-like organic guidance midpoint implied at ~0.8% versus ~2.2% at the prior midpoint, per the BNP Paribas exchange; management did not dispute the arithmetic.
Operating margin guidance maintained at 20%–22%, assuming wage-hike headwinds, AI investments and ~50 bps acquisition impact, offset by Project Maximus and currency.
Onsite mix excluding acquisitions expected to fall 75 bps to 1% for the year, a margin tailwind.
Salary hikes effective October for most employees, with the rest in January 2027.
Lower end of revenue guidance assumes further macro deterioration; top end assumes improvement, but less than assumed in April.
capex_capacity: Plan to hire 20,000 college graduates in FY27, matching FY26; over 4,000 hired in Q1 FY27.
Target of 6,000 Frontier Engineers over the next few years, mainly built through college hiring and internal reskilling.
Management decided not to enter AI infrastructure or data center business at this stage after internal board review.
No staff restructuring; reskilling done across the workforce, per management.
demand_pricing: Client spending remains selective; priorities are AI, modernization, cloud, productivity and consolidation, with discretionary spend scrutinised.
Pricing softer than expected: client productivity asks tied to AI plus rising competition; management says net pricing still increased.
AI-led deflation is a headwind at renewals and on non-large deals; management tracks compression internally but does not quantify it externally.
Six consolidation deals won, representing ~$700 mn net new; 20% of large deal TCV from vendor consolidation.
Management cites a conscious decision to walk away from European manufacturing deals that did not meet return thresholds.
Outcome-based pricing discussions increasing but not a large share of activity.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the upper end of revenue guidance lower and what is the macro view?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 volumes were soft through the quarter, one-off EURS termination came late in the quarter, and a European client deal was declined on economics; the upper end now assumes a less favourable macro recovery than in April.

qa_highlights.question: Is the one-time program termination fully absorbed in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said what is known has been taken in Q1, with no further known Q2 impact from that program.

qa_highlights.question: Can the AI deflation be quantified?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not quantify compression externally; it says contract scope is often redefined and adjacent work offsets some of it.

qa_highlights.question: Margin outlook given wage hikes and acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said FY27 wage-hike impact is lower than FY26 since FY26 carried a full-year effect of the April hike; currency, Project Maximus and lower onsite mix offset it, and 20%–22% guidance is held.

qa_highlights.question: Will headcount grow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said headcount will grow with revenue over time; no year-end headcount guidance was given and recruitment continues.

qa_highlights.question: Rupee impact on margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Every 1% rupee depreciation gives 15–17 bps margin benefit; ~45% revenue comes from non-US geographies, which partly offsets this.

risks_watch: Guidance is conditional on macro; the lower end assumes further deterioration, and pricing pressure from AI productivity asks could persist.
Q2 carry-over from soft Q1 volumes and the European manufacturing client's Q4 deal closure in December.
Undisclosed AI deflation on existing book; watch renewals and whether AI-first revenue growth (8.2%) keeps pace.
CEO transition: Salil Parekh's term ends March 31, 2027; Ashiss Dash takes over April 1, 2027 after a 6-month mentorship from October 1.
Attrition rising to 13% and talent competition from hyperscalers and AI services start-ups for Frontier Engineers.
Margin headwinds from acquisition amortisation, founder retention payouts and H2 wage hikes.
500209|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on AI strategy, margins and large deals, but cautious and somewhat defensive on the revenue cut, attributing it to macro uncertainty, client-specific events and pricing. Management avoided quantifying AI deflation and declined to comment on specific renewal losses.
key_quotes: Our AI services revenue was 8.2% of overall revenue in Q1.
So all of those are tailwinds, puts-and-takes all of that put together, we are still very confident of maintaining our margin guidance.
On the AI, I think there is a huge differentiation that I find from what we are working on.
we will compete aggressively in the market, but we are not going to underwrite uneconomic productivity assumptions.

500209|2026-09.headline: Infosys narrowed FY27 revenue growth guidance to 1%-2% cc from 1.5%-3%, citing pricing pressure and softer volumes, while Q2 AI revenue hit 10.5% of revenue, up 29% QoQ.
500209|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue grew 1.5% YoY and 1.2% QoQ in constant currency, with operating margin stable at 21%. Management cut the full-year revenue growth guidance to 1%-2% cc, blaming pricing pressure from competitive intensity, softer volumes, and weak discretionary spend in Retail and Hi-Tech, plus offshoring shift and a walked-away European manufacturing deal. Large deal TCV was $5.2 bn (62% net new), including a $2 bn+ seven-year net-new mega deal expected to add over 1% to FY28 growth. Operating margin guidance held at 20%-22%, with H2 headwinds from wage hikes, pricing and AI productivity sharing, partly offset by Project Maximus.

financial_highlights.change: Second-highest quarterly TCV in five years
down 7 days YoY; incl. unbilled 77 days, down 10 days

segments.commentary: Large deal signings above $3.5 bn in Q2 with seven FS deals; management called FS a strong vertical, though mortgage expected to slow on rate-hike expectations.

segments.name: Manufacturing

segments.name: Energy, Utilities, Resources & Services (EURS)

segments.name: Retail

segments.name: Hi-Tech

segments.name: Communications

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance revised to 1%-2% YoY cc from prior 1.5%-3%; lower end assumes further macro deterioration, upper end assumes improvement.
FY27 operating margin guidance unchanged at 20%-22%.

H2 margin headwinds: wage hikes (most effective October 2026, next phase January 2027), softer revenue seasonality, AI productivity sharing, and ramp-up of large deals; partly offset by Project Maximus.
Effective tax rate for FY27 expected at 29%-30%.
Offshoring impact and the walked-away European manufacturing deal together cost roughly 1.8%-2% of FY27 growth; the bulk of the manufacturing client impact lands in Q4.
Mega deal expected to contribute over 1% revenue growth in FY28; transition begins in the second half of Q4 FY27 with no real margin impact this year.
Capital allocation: 85% of free cash flow returned over five years via dividends and buybacks; interim dividend Rs 26.
capex_capacity: Utilization incl. trainees 85.4%, excluding trainees 81.9% due to fresher intake; management views 85% as optimum with limited headroom.
Net headcount up about 4,400 in H1; about 13,000 freshers hired in H1 against a target of around 20,000 for FY27.
Attrition about 12.7%; management estimates roughly 45,000 annual leavers to be backfilled.
Subcontractor cost held at 8%-9% of revenue (8.9% cited); management says reducing subcontractors by 1% of revenue would add 15-20 bps margin, with a floor around 5%-6%.
Frontier model partnerships and Topaz Fabric (15 foundation models) underpin AI delivery; FDE build-out of 6,000 over multiple years is progressing.
Project Maximus contributed 20 bps to Q2 margin.
demand_pricing: Pricing pressure from competitive intensity: the expected price increase at the start of the year did not materialize; management says peers are more aggressive on pricing.
Volumes softer than expected in Q2; discretionary spend selective, especially in Retail and Hi-Tech.
AI productivity demands from clients are passed through into pricing; management says the intensity has not changed, but AI-related productivity is now more widely exposed across the portfolio.
Management says the productivity effect is finite, while AI growth is secular; the vast majority of AI productivity benefit is already baked into large renewals signed.
Large deal margins are said to be similar to past deals; AI revenue margin not disclosed externally.
North America softer, Europe and rest of world stronger; India revenue up in Q2 on seasonality.

qa_highlights.question: Why narrow the guidance band and what drove the revision from 1.5%-3%?
qa_highlights.answer: Pricing pressure from competitive intensity, softer volumes, and slower discretionary spend in Retail and Hi-Tech; offshoring and the walked-away European manufacturing deal together account for roughly 1.8%-2% of growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is AI-led productivity worsening and how much AI revenue growth is there?
qa_highlights.answer: Productivity expectations are similar to before, with broader exposure across the portfolio; management cited 5.5% AI share at its Q3 FY26 AI Day as a proxy base for YoY, and AI revenue is described as new revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Will the mega deal lift next year's growth and what are the margins?
qa_highlights.answer: The $2 bn+ net-new deal is expected to add over 1% to FY28 growth, with a transition starting in the second half of Q4 FY27 and no real margin impact this year; no asset takeovers, some people transfers.

qa_highlights.question: Is Hi-Tech weakness the start of deflation spreading to other sectors?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Hi-Tech is mostly one US client ramp-down; FS, Energy Utilities, parts of Manufacturing and Healthcare are growing with strong discretionary spend.

qa_highlights.question: Is subcontractor cost a margin drag?
qa_highlights.answer: Subcontractors are 8%-9% of revenue and management aims to keep them in a broad band; reducing them by 1% would add 15-20 bps margin, but they will not go to zero.

qa_highlights.question: Is customer in-sourcing rising because of AI?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no AI-driven pattern of in-sourcing; clients instead ask Infosys to take on internal work and use AI to deliver it more efficiently.

risks_watch: Pricing: management expects pricing at the low end of guidance to deteriorate slightly and at the upper end to improve; competitive intensity on AI-productivity-linked deals may persist.
H2 seasonality: furloughs, lower working days and wage hikes in October and January could compress H2 margin toward the lower end.
Q4 manufacturing client impact (close to 1% of growth) and its potential carry-over into FY28.
Mega deal ramp timing and the conversion of large deal TCV ($8.8 bn H1) into revenue.
Retail and Hi-Tech demand weakness and whether it spreads beyond the identified clients; mortgage slowdown in FS.
Macro: 10-year yield near 5%, tariffs and Middle East conflict constraining discretionary spend; US PERM and H-1B changes with unclear cost impact.
500209|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on AI growth, large deals and margin resilience, but cautious on near-term revenue, with management openly calling Q2 growth below expectations. Evasive on AI margins, year-on-year AI growth and vertical-level guidance, citing non-disclosure.

500214|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA fell to INR 199 million (2.31% margin) on a 3% revenue rise, with Roha plant start-up costs and West Asia disruption driving the squeeze.
500214|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 operating income was INR 8,633 million (up about 3% YoY), with EBITDA of INR 199 million at a 2.31% margin and net profit of INR 243 million. For FY26, operating income rose about 7% to INR 29,148 million while EBITDA fell 29% to INR 2,102 million (7.21% margin) and PAT was INR 1,432 million (4.91%). Management attributed the weakness to West Asia crisis disruptions (about Rs 60 crore of deferred GCC engineering exports), input cost inflation (styrene, oleum), Roha plant depreciation and interest, and slow government fund flow on the UP Jal Jeevan project. Management declined to give FY27 sales, margin, or gross debt guidance until the second half of the year.

segments.name: Engineering

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 2,297 million (up about 3% YoY), EBIT INR 334 million. Management attributed about three-quarters of the segment margin decline (about 4 points on a full-year basis, to ~3% segment EBIT margin) to Roha costs, and the rest to input costs and deferred resin revenue from logistics disruption; Dammam (Saudi Arabia) plant has begun commercial production.

qa_highlights.question: Is Roha on track for 25%-30% utilisation and customer acquisition progress; can PBT break-even come this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it remains on track for 25% utilisation in the first full year and should meet it this FY, though styrene and oleum costs are headwinds. Break-even is being pursued but timing depends on the West Asia situation.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the chemicals margin decline is due to Roha versus Middle East logistics and input costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Three-quarters of the segment margin decline is from Roha; one-quarter from West Asia, input costs and deferred resin revenue. Roha's impact was just under 7% for Q4 and about 3% segment EBIT margin for the full year.

qa_highlights.question: How much engineering revenue was affected by the Middle East crisis and legacy projects?
qa_highlights.answer: The West Asia impact on engineering was Rs 60 crore; legacy and UP project effects are said to follow the same ratio as the last few quarters. Management said it would not give a finer split.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex, gross debt and sales/margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: No sales or margin guidance until H2 FY27. Maintenance capex Rs 30-40 crore and gross debt about Rs 384 crore; no major capex currently planned without expansion.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the jump in Q4 other income?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly FOREX gains on exports plus claims on an EPC contract; management did not quantify the split.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the Oman project excluded from reported order book?

500214|2026-06.headline: Ion Exchange Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA fell 49% YoY to INR 32 crore (4.54% margin) on 20% revenue growth to INR 701 crore, with treatment solutions still loss-making.
500214|2026-06.overview: Consolidated operating income rose 20% YoY to INR 701 crore, but EBITDA fell 49% to INR 32 crore and PAT was INR 3 crore (0.44% margin). Management split the former engineering segment into Treatment Solutions, Industrial Products and Lifecycle Services, and reported Specialty Chemicals and Consumer Products separately. Treatment Solutions posted a EBIT loss of INR 17 crore on legacy projects, while Industrial Products margin rose to 11.89%. Management said Roha resin capacity is ramping slower than expected and guidance will be reviewed by end of Q2.

segments.name: Treatment Solutions
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 210 crore (+14% YoY) with EBIT loss of INR 17 crore, hit by legacy projects including the UP project. Dispatches to GCC resumed post-quarter; a Hyundai contract of about USD 52 million (over INR 500 crore per Q&A) was won after quarter end.

segments.name: Industrial Products
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 105 crore (+14% YoY) and EBIT INR 13 crore, margin 11.89% vs under 6% a year ago, driven by water treatment solutions and membranes. Institutional products moved here from Consumer.

segments.name: Lifecycle Services
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 72 crore (+28% YoY) and EBIT INR 7 crore (9.92% margin vs 10.55%), with margin pressure from higher input costs. Includes a 20-year O&M concession in Oman with PDO.

segments.name: Specialty Chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 230 crore (+21% YoY) but EBIT INR 22 crore (-52% YoY), impacted by geopolitics and Roha ramp-up costs; Roha cost drag about 6% of segment margin. FX gain in the prior-year quarter also reversed (about 3-4 pts).

segments.name: Consumer Products

guidance_outlook: Management expects Specialty Chemicals capacity to grow at least 50% over the next couple of years as Roha reaches full capacity over about four years, with asset turnover just under 2x.
Roha utilisation guidance of 25% in year one is still held but described as softer than expected; management will review by end of Q2 FY27.
UP legacy project is not expected to close in FY27 and will spill into FY28, dependent on government fund flows; other large legacy project expected to see significant progress by FY27 end.
Consumer Products targeted to break even in FY27.

Pharma resin capacity at Ankleshwar (FDA-approved) to expand 6x, targeted within the next 12 months; described as asset-light, technology-led rather than capex-heavy.
Membrane business: second Goa plant under construction to add UF and MBR capacity; tie-up with MANN+HUMMEL for UF PVDF technology. Management targets 3x business growth over the years.
Standard plants capacity expanded across Hosur, Goa and Wada.
Management would not disclose capital earmarked for BOOT/BOO service projects, saying it will remain asset-light.
demand_pricing: Hyundai contract of about USD 52 million (over INR 500 crore) won post quarter end; supplied to an EPC, FOB Mumbai, kickoff under way.

qa_highlights.question: Portugal/Iberian acquisition: progress and margin profile versus India?
qa_highlights.answer: Acquisition was about three years ago and integration is complete; management declined to give geography-specific margins but said margins would be similar to or better than India, with four of five segments present there (not Consumer).

qa_highlights.question: Why reclassify segments and is a corporate action or separate listing planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Engineering was not showing the full picture of products, services and solutions; no separate listing or corporate action is planned, and about 60% of the company is now products, chemicals and services versus about 40% treatment solutions.

qa_highlights.question: Roha 5x capacity claim and link to resin revenue of about INR 500 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: 5x is a group-level resin capacity figure across Roha and Ankleshwar after debottlenecking; Phase I doubles capacity, and Phase II plus debottlenecking takes output to about 5x the original Ankleshwar capacity. Management aspires to about 10% of global resin volume and gave no segment split.

qa_highlights.question: Pharma resin 6x expansion: timeline, capex and revenue contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Expansion is in process and targeted within 12 months; management said capex is manageable and the constraint is technical know-how, with asset turn well above Roha's 2-2.5x. FY26 pharma revenue was not disclosed and the segment stays within Specialty Chemicals.

qa_highlights.question: Treatment Solutions profitability: why has EBIT fallen over five years and what is the path back?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to large legacy projects, now in final stages but with a sizable portion remaining, plus a move to selective bidding, advanced and emerging solutions, and walking away from difficult projects. Cost overruns on the large project were acknowledged as a meaningful impact.

qa_highlights.question: Did the WQA certification contribute to Q1 revenue, and what is the North America outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: No quantification was given for Q1 contribution; management said a significant, though not majority, part of Roha volume is expected to go to overseas markets, notably North America, after WQA certification.

qa_highlights.question: Roha 25% first-year utilisation guidance and Consumer breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Roha guidance of 25% is still held but has been softer than expected; management will update by end of Q2 FY27. Consumer Products breakeven is the first FY27 target, with single-digit margins to be discussed later.

qa_highlights.question: Specialty Chemicals margin compression: Roha drag and other factors?
qa_highlights.answer: Roha impact on segment margin was about 6%; the prior-year FX gain reversal was about 3-4 points; and pass-through of input cost increases lagged, with some moderation expected if crude stays near USD 80.

qa_highlights.question: UP legacy project: unexecuted portion, receivables and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Unexecuted UP portion is about 11% of the June order backlog of INR 2,473 crore; receivable exposure is materially unchanged over recent quarters. Closure is not expected in FY27 and will depend on government fund flows, which have started to come in.

Geopolitical disruption (West Asia) affecting invoicing and dispatches to GCC; Hyundai USD 52 million order (supplied via an EPC, FOB Mumbai) could be at risk if the crisis persists.
Capital intensity of BOOT/BOO and O&M concessions, such as the 20-year Oman PDO contract; management would not disclose capital earmarked.

Consumer Products breakeven target in FY27 and Lifecycle Services margin (9.92% vs 10.55%) to monitor next quarter; the company will also provide reconciliation data to bridge reclassified segment numbers.

500214|2026-06.management_tone: Candid about weakness: the CEO called the Q1 performance "disappointing" and said the legacy projects are not "out of the woods", while stressing a "clear path" back to double-digit profitability without a timeline. 500215|2026-06.headline: Sundrop Brands Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue grew 15% YoY (11% QoQ) with EBITDA steady at about 7% of sales, net of ESOP.
500215|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 15% YoY and 11% QoQ, with B2B up 18% and e-commerce up 32%. Gross margin improved about 110 bps despite commodity and packaging inflation, and EBITDA held at about 7%, the same level as Q4 FY26. A&P was reported about 12% lower YoY, but management says about 5% lower on a like-for-like basis after reclassifying trade spends as contra-revenue. Management reiterated a target of 300 bps annual margin expansion and about 12% EBITDA by FY30, with 200 bps from Del Monte-Sundrop synergies over 18 months.

financial_highlights.value: Up about 110 bps (stated as overall margin improvement)
financial_highlights.change: Material cost efficiency +40 bps; other expenses +70 bps
Same as Q4 FY26; ESOP-burdened about 5.66%

financial_highlights.change: Reclassification of trade spends to contra-revenue; like-for-like growth about 12% QoQ

financial_highlights.value: About 56% of total business, growing about 16%

financial_highlights.change: Q4 FY26 share of business about 62%

segments.name: Popcorn
segments.commentary: Growing about 18% with about 12% volume growth; Ready-to-Eat growing about 39% (vs 33% last year) while Ready-to-Cook grows about 9%. Management says it holds about 85% category share.

segments.name: Culinary (ketchup, mayo, dressings)
segments.commentary: Growth accelerated to 15% from about 10% last year, with volume growth of about 8%; B2B and exports to Southeast Asia contributing.

segments.name: Premium staples / edible oil
segments.commentary: Value growth about 16% and volume growth about 7%, with about 9% of growth from price pass-through; oil is about 20% of total business. Management targets 4-5% volume growth.

segments.name: Italian (olive oil, pasta, RTE olives)
segments.commentary: Value growth returned to about 8% and volume to 15-17%; olive oil volume grew close to 20%, pasta about 10%. Q1 realisations fell due to prior-year commodity deflation pass-through.

segments.name: Peanut butter / spreads
segments.commentary: Decline narrowed to about 3% in value and volume from 8-10% last year; e-commerce returned to 16% growth. Market is about 85% value-added; company holds about 33% of standard and 3% of value-added peanut butter.

segments.name: Juices
segments.commentary: Investment dropped; management says it was not core and did not show good results.

guidance_outlook: Management aims for mid-teens to high-teens revenue growth, with about 10% volume growth, 4-5% value growth from pricing and 4-5% from innovation as the long-term mix.
EBITDA target of about 12% by FY30 (about three years), from about 7% ESOP-adjusted today; ESOP cost to stay front-loaded for 18-21 months.

Overall ambition of about 300 bps annual margin expansion, split half reinvested in growth and half returned to shareholders; about 100 bps a year from scale, 80-100 bps from premiumisation and about 100 bps a year from synergies over two years.
Del Monte and Sundrop synergies estimated at about 200 bps, delivered over about 18 months; about 8 CFA consolidations targeted by end of this year, leaving 2 of Del Monte's 10 unique CFAs.
Italian business: value growth expected to move closer to 15% if volume growth of 15% is sustained; price stabilisation expected from Q2.
Single ERP for both businesses to be decided soon, with migration expected within about 12 months, before sales-force integration.
capex_capacity: Shift to a capital-efficient model: using third-party manufacturing and outsourced systems in place of own capex; management also says it is actively looking at inorganic opportunities.
Popcorn facilities at Kashipur and Kothur are running at rising utilisation, adding to profitability on instant popcorn.
Ready-to-Eat assorted manufacturing is improving plant utilisation and freight efficiency; direct factory-to-distributor shipping cuts freight and shelf-life packaging cost (4.5-5 month shelf life).
Salesforce automation: about 80% of outlets now billed on the platform, up from about 75% at the end of Q4 FY26.
demand_pricing: Edible oil: volume 7%, value about 15-16%, with about 9% from pass-through of per-kg price increases; management is now growing volume and aims for 4-5% volume growth.
Peanut butter: management says the market has moved to about 85% value-added formats (protein, chocolate, natural) where it has about 3% share; competition includes PE-backed brands.
Popcorn Rs. 10 RTC/RTE packs are expanding into East, West and South; e-commerce growth is led by Rs. 25-50 MRP packs, with bigger packs now about 36% of RTE mix (from about 33%).
Premium staples: management says it has a lower-priced variant (Sundrop Lite and Sundrop Heart Plus) as a safety net if sunflower oil inflation drives consumers down.
Italian realisation down about 6-10% in Q1 due to higher old-price inventory being sold after last year's commodity deflation; not quick-commerce discounting per management.

qa_highlights.question: Navin (Ithought PMS): Is the YoY dip in A&P a genuine efficiency gain or a shift in focus across brands/segments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said focus stayed on core categories invested since Q4 FY25 (Sundrop) and Q1 FY26 (Del Monte); Juices was dropped as non-core. Reported A&P down about 12% YoY, but after reclassifying trade spends to contra-revenue it is 21.4 vs 22.9 of sales, about 5% lower.

qa_highlights.question: Navin: Post the 4700BC acquisition by a large player, is there more competitive aggression in popcorn and what differs from ACT II's offerings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management holds about 85% popcorn category share and has not seen a significant shift in category behaviour since the acquisition. It has raised investment, is pushing Sweet Popcorn, and has added Cheese popcorn to e-commerce.

qa_highlights.question: Pritesh Chheda (Lucky Investments): What are the blended volume and value growth rates for core and non-core?
qa_highlights.answer: Core (about 60% of sales) grows about 14-15% in value and 9-10% in volume. Edible oil (about 20% of business) grew about 16% in value and 7% in volume. The remaining ~20% grows about 15% in value and 8% in volume, helped by CP manufacturing such as energy drinks. Overall, about 80% of the business grows 15-16% in value and 8-9% in volume.

qa_highlights.question: Pritesh Chheda: What are the key growth pillars and the expected value and volume mix?
qa_highlights.answer: For Popcorn, Ketchup and Mayo the pillars are distribution, media investment ahead of curve, and innovation; Italian is driven more by innovation and investment, and peanut butter by innovation. Management sees about 4-5% volume growth in most categories and aims for about 10% volume, plus 4-5% price and 4-5% innovation, targeting mid-teens to high-teens growth.

qa_highlights.question: Balaji Vaidyanath (Nafa Asset Management): Is the 6-10% Italian realisation decline due to quick-commerce discounting?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhinav Kapoor said no. Q1 is running on higher-cost inventory bought before last year's commodity deflation, with price pass-through having started only in Q2 last year. Prices are now stabilising and the effect should end from Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Balaji Vaidyanath: Is GT/MT growth likely low single digit given B2B at 18% and e-commerce at 32%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Popcorn, Italian and oil are primarily retail. Culinary is the only mixed retail and B2B business. B2B grows faster than retail, and retail is roughly 10-12% if B2B is at 18%. The company did not give a specific GT/MT number.

qa_highlights.question: Balaji Vaidyanath: How much of the 15% edible oil growth is price pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: Asheesh Sharma said about 9 points is price pass-through (per-kg increase passed on almost fully) with 7% volume, giving roughly 16% value growth.

qa_highlights.question: Percy Panthaki (IIFL Capital): What is the status of the Del Monte and Sundrop integration, and what savings are expected?
qa_highlights.answer: E-commerce is under a single operations team. Del Monte had 10 unique CFAs, with 2 already consolidated and a third underway; about 8 consolidations are targeted by year-end, leaving 2. ERP migration to a single system is expected within about 12 months, before sales-force integration. East distribution of Del Monte already runs through the Sundrop team. Synergies are about 200 bps over 18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Percy Panthaki: EBITDA goes from about 7% to about 12% in three years. What is the breakup beyond the 200 bps synergies?
qa_highlights.answer: ESOP cost (about 5.66% after ESOP) is front-loaded for 18-21 months, adding roughly 100 bps after that. Scale is worth about 100 bps a year, premiumisation 80-100 bps a year, and synergies about 100 bps a year for two years. Management aims for about 300 bps of margin expansion a year, split half to growth and half to shareholders. FY30 12% is the target.

qa_highlights.question: Shirish Pardeshi (Motilal Oswal): What is the economics and sustainability of the Rs. 10 popcorn RTC/RTE packs and their supply chain?
qa_highlights.answer: Assorted manufacturing and direct factory-to-distributor shipping cut freight and packaging cost, with a 4.5-5 month shelf life. RTE Rs. 10 has moved from margin-dilutive to margin-accretive over 18 months. Bigger packs are about one-third of the RTE mix (from one-fifth/one-third earlier), growing 42% against 33% for the rest, and e-commerce is growing about 55%.

qa_highlights.question: Shirish Pardeshi: Will premium staples volume (7%) hold if sunflower inflation drives price up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to lower-priced variants as a safety net: Sundrop Lite and Sundrop Heart Plus, with a new Sundrop Heart blend using less-inflated commodities. It targets 4-5% volume growth in the category, which is growing about 3-4%. The Sundrop Heart Jodi pack will continue through the festive season.

qa_highlights.question: Nachiket Kale (Emkay): What is the strategy for peanut butter given competition from new digital-first and PE-backed brands?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it lost the protein, natural and chocolate variant race because it lacked those products. The market is about 85% value-added and 15% standard. The company holds about 33% of standard and 3% of value-added peanut butter. It is launching new variants, investing in digital consumer acquisition, and aims for double-digit growth in the near term.

risks_watch: A&P optics: reported A&P is down about 12% YoY, but like-for-like is about 5% lower after the contra-revenue reclassification. Watch whether reclassification distorts sales and margin comparisons.
Input cost inflation in edible oil (sunflower), packaging and commodities. Management says price pass-through has so far protected margins, but B2B and some contracts have lagged price increases.
Peanut butter: still in decline at about 3% in value and volume, with only 3% share of value-added formats against 85% of the market. Competition from digital-first and PE-backed brands.
Italian business: realisation down 6-10% in Q1 from old inventory. Management expects stabilisation from Q2 and value growth of about 15% if volume growth holds at 15%.

guidance_outlook: Management expects EBITDA lost in Q1 to be recovered in H2 FY27 and full-year PAT to beat FY26.
Hi-Tech: double-digit revenue growth targeted for FY27; solar pump sales expected to pick up from September.
FY27 margin guidance: about 14% standalone and about 12-13% consolidated.

Debt: about Rs 680 crore of NCDs due in FY27, about Rs 230 crore in September 2026 and the rest in March 2027; management says internal cash flows will cover them, with refinancing term sheets in hand.
Legacy government receivables target for FY27 is Rs 422 crore (minimum Rs 380 crore for the remaining nine months); Rs 60 crore collected in Q1 and Rs 25-30 crore in July.
Food business IPO deferred; management says it will look at it from September if markets improve.
capex_capacity: Biochar plant recently started (mango stones, corn cob, cotton stalk feedstock); management expects financial impact from next fiscal, with carbon credits taking 6-9 months.

demand_pricing: Polymer prices rose about 50%; most increases were passed to customers, and some customers postponed purchases until prices fall.
Delayed monsoon onset in June pushed drip sales into the current quarter; July was positive and August-September are expected to be good.
Government-linked and subsidy-driven micro-irrigation sales were deliberately not pursued because of cash flow and long receivables; management estimated Rs 50-60 crore of sales were forgone.
Dam storage was about 67% of capacity; management expects about 85% by monsoon-end, supportive of the rabi season and next summer.

qa_highlights.question: How much legacy government receivables were recovered and how much project work is left?
qa_highlights.answer: Rs 60 crore received in Q1 and Rs 25-30 crore in July. Remaining project billing outside Pune is about Rs 40-50 crore, with no working capital needed; about 10-12 of 72 projects carry O&M over two to three years, which management called light.

qa_highlights.question: How will the Rs 674-680 crore of debt due this fiscal be repaid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited internal accruals first, then legacy receivable collections, asset monetisation (surplus land) and refinancing; it said Rs 1,300 crore of bank debt was repaid over three and a half years and that the company has never missed a payment in four years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Hi-Tech down about 22% and what is the margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Retail fell about 17% and projects about 63%; management called the drip decline a one-off from the delayed monsoon and polymer-driven postponements. Hi-Tech margin was 14.4% vs 16.6%, and management expects margins to recover to typical levels through the year.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk of write-offs on project receivables?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said provisions were made in FY21-22 after a project review and it does not expect material write-offs; net receivables of Rs 1,975 crore in June are largely good, with about 55% linked to government-related items.

qa_highlights.question: Why are working capital requirements higher than listed peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed this to legacy long-term project receivables and state-government orders paid after 6-12 months, and said the cycle should improve substantially in FY28 once project receivables are cleared.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of refinancing and the food-business IPO?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no pushback from lenders, a couple of term sheets are in hand, and talks are ongoing. The food-business IPO (about Rs 1,000 crore including PE exit) has been deferred due to weak valuations; the company will revisit it from September.

qa_highlights.question: Why is PAT negative when revenue is flat, and what are the coffee and biochar updates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the loss to higher raw-material costs and lower standalone India volumes, and expects a full-year PAT improvement. First coffee orders have come from the Coffee Board; the biochar business has started, with impact on numbers from next fiscal.

risks_watch: Refinancing of about Rs 230 crore NCD due in September 2026 and about Rs 450 crore due in March 2027 has not yet been completed; management relies on term sheets and internal cash flows.
Legacy government receivables of about Rs 800-900 crore and about Rs 500 crore of agency receivables above 180 days; collection pace against the Rs 380 crore minimum target is key.
Polymer price volatility and geopolitical oil-price movements may keep customers postponing purchases.
Weak Q1 adjusted PAT (Rs 3 crore) and reliance on H2 recovery; Q2 is seasonally muted.
Food-business IPO and Tamil Nadu land monetisation timelines have slipped repeatedly.

key_quotes: So, overall, reduction in EBITDA temporarily in this quarter, but we believe we should be able to catch up in the second half of the current fiscal year to cover what is lost.
And we are very confident on honoring the debt obli gation, we don't see that as an issue.

500233|2026-06.headline: Kajaria Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 20% to INR1,328 crore and EBITDA margin hit 19.6%, driven mainly by fuel-cost-led price hikes.
500233|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 20% YoY to INR1,328 crore, mainly from selling price increases after gas costs rose following the Middle East conflict, while volume grew 6% despite a weak April. EBITDA margin expanded to 19.6% from 16.72% a year earlier, and PAT rose to INR169 crore from INR109 crore. Management guided to double-digit volume growth over the next nine months, an 18-19% full-year EBITDA margin, and INR1,000 crore+ EBITDA, and announced two new capacity expansions (Srikalahasti and Gailpur). Morbi gas-price dislocation has narrowed the price gap between Kajaria and Morbi peers from about 40% to under 20%.

New lines use a 340-metre kiln versus 200 metres previously; machinery is a mix of SACMI and Chinese equipment.

Kajaria's price gap to Morbi narrowed from about 40% to under 20%; management says this shift is driving demand in North and East.

Management says the company is moving into institutional/project sales alongside retail, with two large builders won, and has about 1,800 dealers (450 exclusive), adding about 100 more this year (50 exclusive).

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 11% realisation growth came from each segment, and where do price hikes go from here?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Morbi cost increase was 40-45% versus 10-13% for North/South plants. Blended hikes were 13-14%, and non-Morbi plants took about 10%; prices are holding for now, but gas is volatile.

qa_highlights.question: Where will double-digit volume growth come from in the next nine months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited May-June recovery, July continuing the trend, stronger distribution, project wins with two large builders, and new dealer showrooms.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex and how much is maintenance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 capex is about INR400 crore, including maintenance capex, with projects spilling over into next year.

qa_highlights.question: Why build in-house capacity now and what is the margin differential versus outsourcing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the new lines are cheaper per MSM and more opex-efficient, and are highly ROC-accretive; outsourcing is used to fill near-term demand and is expected to fall next year.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA reach INR1,000 crore and when will promoters take remuneration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets INR1,000 crore+ EBITDA and 18-19% margin for the year. The promoters have said they will not take salary this year, and the timing for later is undecided.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Bathware still weak and what margin should be expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 is a correction year after hiring a new CBO in April. It gave no margin guidance but expects 35-40% value growth in the segment for the year.

risks_watch: Gas supply and cost volatility: Morbi gas moved from about INR48 to INR86-88 per SCM after the war; management says the situation is very volatile and it cannot forecast post-Q1 gas prices, so the price-hike sustainability is unproven.

Outsourcing dependence: about 29-30% outsourcing now, expected to rise in FY27 because capacity is flat; Morbi-sourced margins and availability could move with Morbi gas costs.
Execution of Srikalahasti (10 MSM, INR210 crore) and Gailpur (11 MSM, INR165 crore) plants, with Gailpur due by April 2027 and new lines starting in Q1 FY28; FY27 capex of about INR400 crore.
Bathware remains a drag in FY27 with no margin guidance; restructuring and a new CBO hired in April; value growth target of 35-40%.
Export run-rate fell to about INR1,000 crore per month in Q1 FY27 versus about INR16,000 crore in FY26 due to freight costs, though exports are under 1% of Kajaria turnover.
key_quotes: If you recall, last 2 quarters, we have not given any volume guidance. But this year, with a lot of confidence, we are saying next 9 months, we'll have a double -digit growth.
So we are looking at an EBITDA margin about 18% to 19% for the entire year. First quarter, we already got 19.6%.
We have no choice really this year because of the production constraint, we will outsource from Morbi, that is the only option.
I would not like to give any margin guidance on sanitaryware and faucet side this year.
500233|2026-06.management_tone: Management was confident on volume recovery, the 18-19% full-year EBITDA margin and the two capacity expansions, but was guarded and evasive on gas-cost outlook, forward pricing beyond the current level, and Morbi pricing, repeatedly saying the situation is too volatile to forecast. It declined to give segment-level or Morbi average realisation figures, spot gas detail, and institutional/retail split, and gave no margin guidance for Bathware.

500233|2026-09.headline: Kajaria Q2 FY27: volumes up 10% YoY, consolidated revenue up 24% to INR1,468 crore, EBITDA margin 19.5%, guided to stay around current levels.
500233|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 24% YoY to INR1,468 crore on 10% volume growth and price hikes taken in North and South plants (12-13%) and at Morbi (18-19%). EBITDA margin was 19.5% versus 17.94% a year earlier, and PAT rose to INR190 crore from INR133 crore. Management said export demand stayed subdued on freight and container constraints, while gas costs stayed high and are expected to remain tight. Management guided to double-digit volume growth over the next two quarters, stable margins, and new GVT capacity at Srikalahasti and Gailpur, with no further price hikes planned for now.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Srikalahasti capex increase and why are they adding capacity?

qa_highlights.question: Will volume growth dilute margins?

500238|2026-03.headline: Whirlpool of India Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 7% to INR 2,181 crore, but PBT margin fell to 5% on e-waste and energy-change costs.
500238|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew high single digits to INR 2,181 crore, helped by washers, air conditioners (up about 50%) and Elica (up 30%), with March 2026 the highest shipment month in company history. Profit fell sharply: EBITDA was INR 121 crore (5.6%, down 33.7%) and profit before exceptional items INR 110 crore (5%, down 29%), mainly from incremental e-waste provisions and unrecovered BEE energy-upgrade costs. Refrigerator market share fell triple digits in direct cool and frost free due to the January 2026 energy-regulation phase-in/phase-out and deliberate non-matching of competitor pricing. For FY26, revenue rose 1.4% to INR 8,034 crore, EBITDA was INR 481 crore (6%), and reported PBT fell 19% including a INR 38.8 crore one-time wage code charge. Management gave no margin guidance and flagged FY27 as a difficult year.

qa_highlights.question: What were the e-waste and energy-upcharge costs for Q4 and FY26, and will they recur in FY27? Is channel inventory normalising to allow recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not quantify the split. E-waste is provided at the highest rate under discussion with the ministry and recyclers; any rationalisation would be a benefit. The energy upcharge is a permanent BOM cost increase, and the next energy change is about three years away.

qa_highlights.question: What scenarios could play out with raw material, freight and regulatory cost increases: competitive rationalisation or consumer downtrading?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said anything could happen and called it a roll of the dice. It is focused on component supply through the Strait of Hormuz, forex (imported content 20-35%) and pricing, and it will protect volume if it is materially outpriced.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY26 AC revenue contribution, the aspiration, and the capital needed?
qa_highlights.answer: AC revenue is not disclosed; refrigerators are over 50% of revenue and washers 25-30%. The AC aim is strong but responsible growth, offtake-led, with no aspiration to be number one in AC for now.

qa_highlights.question: How will the cash balance be used, and is a buyback planned?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said cash will go to innovation, automation, cost capex, backward integration and possible inorganic deals; there is no dividend or buyback plan at present. Management said buyback has not been looked at yet.

qa_highlights.question: What is the three-to-five-year strategy, and why not a buyback despite the stock price?
qa_highlights.answer: The vision is to become the number one in refrigerators and washing machines in under 10 years, probably more than five. Management said it is focused on the next 12 to 24 months of investment and said executives bought shares personally.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the refrigerator industry stayed flat, and could BEE ratings help demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described a K-curve with the entry segment (direct cool and semi-automatic) lagging. Replacement demand is being postponed. It said higher star ratings raise cost and price, so the effect on demand is complex.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state margin outlook for Elica and the rest of the business, and what adjacency is being considered?
