500850|2026-06.headline: IHCL Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 15% to INR2,419 crores and PAT 21% to INR358 crores, with EBITDA margin at 31.1%.
500850|2026-06.overview: IHCL reported its 17th consecutive quarter of record performance, with consolidated revenue up 15% YoY to INR2,419 crores, EBITDA up 18% to INR753 crores and PAT up 21% to INR358 crores. Domestic RevPAR grew 14% and hotel segment revenue 17%, driven by leisure markets like Rajasthan and Goa while international properties, especially Dubai, lagged due to West Asia disruption. Standalone revenue grew 18% to INR1,298 crores with EBITDA up 30% to INR542 crores and margin of 41.8%. Management reiterated double-digit revenue growth for the year and said July and early Q2 trends were strong.

financial_highlights.change: c.+6 pts YoY (analyst cited 35% to 39%ish; mgmt said margin up 0.5%)

segments.name: Hotels
segments.commentary: Hotel segment revenue grew 17% and makes up about 87% of business; domestic RevPAR grew 14%, with double-digit RevPAR growth across all brands. Margin held at 32.6% despite about INR15 crores of Frankfurt ramp-up and TajSATS Noida kitchen costs.

segments.name: Growth brands (Ginger, Qmin, ama, Tree of Life)
segments.commentary: Ginger consolidated revenue INR183 crores, up 20% YoY with 39% EBITDA margin. Ama has 380+ bungalows, 196 operational; Tree of Life has 40+ resorts, 23 operational; Qmin at 100+ outlets.

segments.name: Acquisitions (Brij, Atmantan)
segments.commentary: Brij's 11 operational hotels generated INR11 crores revenue, up 42% YoY. Atmantan delivered INR19 crores consolidated revenue, up 19% YoY.

segments.name: TajSATS / air catering
segments.commentary: Air catering revenue rose 3% while EBITDA fell 1%, as second-largest airline capacity cuts hit flight catering volumes; non-flight catering grew mid-20s% at lower margin.

capex_capacity: Operational hotels at 382 with about 265 in pipeline; 20 hotels signed and 11 opened in Q1, 17 of signings under Gateway, Ginger and Tree of Life.
Frankfurt new asset ramping up, with pre-opening and start-up costs weighing on Q1 and July-August.
Taj Ganges Varanasi new 100-room wing commissioned March 2026, PBT-positive in first quarter, revenue up 44% and EBITDA margin 40%.
Taj Bandstand (Mumbai) targeted for 2030-2031 with about 450 keys and INR1,000 crores revenue; excavation 95% complete.
Ginger Bangalore Airport and a 350-room Ginger/Vivanta combo in 12-14 months; 300-room Ginger at Mopa Airport Goa under construction; Kolkata Airport Ginger under construction.

demand_pricing: Leisure markets strong: Rajasthan RevPAR up high 20s to 27-29%, Goa ARRs up double digit; big city hotels up low to mid-teens.
Standalone occupancy 82% vs 76% in the previous quarter; occupancy up about 6% on comparable domestic base.
Taj Palace room revenue up 32% and Fort Aguada room revenue up 45% after renovations.
International: Dubai business at about 80% of prior revenue in total (JLT 60%), Taj Exotica Palm below 50%; San Francisco recovering; New York pipe-burst cut 49 rooms.
Wedding and banqueting subdued; Africa Summit cancelled a week before start in May, hitting Delhi F&B and conference; government MICE slowed.

qa_highlights.question: Are MICE and domestic demand shifts from international travel accelerating into H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said trends continue into Q2 with no softening; leisure markets outperforming, and foreign arrivals still needed in Q3-Q4 for the sector.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone employee cost rise only 0.6% YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to a reversal from labour code benefits; normal payroll increases are 7-8%.

qa_highlights.question: Will full-year growth reach the upper end of 12-14% guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 is tracking ahead, with July stronger than Q1; it hopes to beat, but gave no explicit guidance raise.

qa_highlights.question: How will Frankfurt be accounted for?
qa_highlights.answer: Full revenue is booked; the asset's impact turns positive from September, after pre-opening costs in July and August.

qa_highlights.question: What is the international strategy and capital intent?
qa_highlights.answer: Capital-light model only, with no hotel purchases; leases on institutional-style returns of 5-7% and brand-led renovations in Singapore, Switzerland and London.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the like-for-like growth is affected by renovated assets?
qa_highlights.answer: Slide 9 excludes Taj Palace, Fort Aguada, Blue Diamond and Calicut, which were under renovation last year, to give an apples-to-apples comparison.

Dubai and Maldives/Sri Lanka exposure, with Palm leisure and Emirates connectivity still impaired.

Frankfurt ramp-up in July-August, and New York rooms returning in 2-3 months.
Ginger conversion pace (15 in Q1, targets of 40 in Q4) and quality of rebranding.

500850|2026-09.headline: IHCL raised FY27 consolidated revenue growth guidance to 15%-17% after Q2 revenue rose 22% to INR2,484 crores and standalone EBITDA margin hit 38.9%.
500850|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was strong: consolidated operating revenue grew 22% YoY to INR2,484 crores, operating EBITDA grew 24% to INR706 crores (28.4% margin, up 50 bps), and PAT rose 23% to INR349 crores. Standalone operating revenue grew 26% to INR1,336 crores and standalone EBITDA grew 40% to INR520 crores, with margin up 400 bps to 38.9%. Management raised FY27 consolidated revenue growth guidance to 15%-17% from 12%-14%, with Hotel segment growth of 17%-19%. Occupancy rose to 82% from 75%, and TajSATS remained a drag on margins.

financial_highlights.value: Revenue and EBITDA growth of 25% and 30%

segments.name: Hotels (consolidated)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 25% and EBITDA up 30% YoY; domestic hotel RevPAR up 25% and standalone RevPAR up 28%, with double-digit RevPAR growth across all brands.

segments.name: Management fees
segments.commentary: Income up 25% to INR156 crores, driven by 25% growth in managed room inventory, higher RevPAR, technical fees and new brand fees from branded residences and villas; management targets high-teens fee CAGR.

segments.name: Select service (Ginger, Qmin, Ama, Tree of Life)
segments.commentary: Ginger revenue INR193 crores (+25%) at 40% EBITDA margin; Ginger reached 100 operational hotels and targets 150 by March 31, 2027. Qmin has over 130 outlets, Ama over 400 villas and bungalows, Tree of Life over 50 resorts.

segments.name: TajSATS (air catering)
segments.commentary: EBITDA declined sequentially in Q2 due to airline schedule curtailments after West Asia fuel-price pressure; non-aviation institutional catering partly offset the decline. Management expects improvement in H2.

segments.name: International subsidiaries
segments.commentary: St. James' Court margins fell 360 bps YoY in H1 FY27 due to delayed renovation works and cost pressure; management expects London recovery with double-digit growth in October. Pierre (New York) is EBITDA-positive but not at target margins.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth raised to 15%-17% (from 12%-14%), i.e. 300 bps above prior guidance; Hotel segment revenue growth 17%-19%.
Implied H2 growth is well above the 14% midpoint arithmetic, per CFO, as TajSATS is a drag and H2 is seasonally strong; the guidance excludes OHL.
Plan to open 50 hotels in FY27; 30 expected in H2 (possibly 32-34). Standalone hotel count was 392 operational as of Oct 27, 2026, with 4 more openings in October.

Management to publish a revised portfolio target (700-hotel Accelerate 2030 target expected to be crossed early) by mid-November 2026; separate management-fee guidance expected by end of next quarter.
OHL merger: 25 IHCL shares for every 117 OHL shares; appointed date April 1, 2027; expected to add 6%-7% to standalone operating revenue in FY28, not in FY27 guidance.
Management expects more than INR1,000 crores of management fee income in roughly two years and about 5,000 keys opened per year.
capex_capacity: Portfolio at 670 hotels with over 69,000 keys (operational or under development) at end-H1 FY27; 47 hotels signed and 20 opened in H1 FY27.
Pipeline of over 34,800 keys, 94% capital-light (81% management contracts, 13% leases).
H1 FY27 capex is 20%-30% above the annual average of the preceding 7-8 years, per management.

Asset upgrades at Taj Palace New Delhi, President Mumbai, Taj West End Bengaluru, Taj Fort Aguada and Taj Lake Palace; Taj Palace New Delhi room revenue up 132% YoY and crossed INR100 crores monthly revenue in September.
Expected upcoming Frankfurt ramp-up after start-up challenges; London and San Francisco expected to improve in Q3.
demand_pricing: Occupancy rose to 82% from 75% in Q2 last year; standalone and domestic consolidated occupancy each up roughly 6%-7%, so growth was balanced between occupancy and ARR.
Demand supported by MICE events (BRICS Summit, Bloomberg event, fintech event); management said Q2 ex-BRICS would still have been a comfortable double-digit RevPAR number.
Wedding nights next year are expected at about 95 versus 60-65 normally, a tailwind for social MICE.
Domestic demand is the main pillar; foreign tourist arrivals have a 3.9% 10-year CAGR, and management sees upside if this reaches 5%-6%. Room nights were flat YoY in Q2 per management.

Tier 2/3 supply: management says demand growth of 15%-20% in these markets is largely met by unorganised players, and that the 12% capacity CAGR headline should be viewed with caution given project delays.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the H2 guidance implied by the revised numbers, and is occupancy at 82% sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth will be mostly rate-led plus new hotels and international recovery (London, Pierre, San Francisco, Frankfurt), with occupancy gains also in the mix; H2 guidance is conservative given the 30-34 hotel openings.

qa_highlights.question: Why did TajSATS EBITDA fall sequentially?
qa_highlights.answer: Airline schedule curtailments after West Asia fuel-price pressure, mainly from June; Q2 had the full impact. Non-flight catering grew, but at lower margin. FY27 is a consolidation year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 14% implied H2 growth conservative and what are the uplift drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said H2 growth would have to be higher than the 14% arithmetic to hit guidance, given TajSATS drag, a high Q4 base and seasonally strong MICE and weddings.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25% growth in Q2 driven by renovation base effects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said renovations are routine for iconic assets; H1 capex is 20%-30% above normal and the growth reflects structural demand shifts, not only a low base.

qa_highlights.question: Why keep international assets, given lower margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited strategic value of the global Taj brand; international consolidated margin of about 35% is stated as industry-leading, with London profitable and Pierre EBITDA-positive but not at 20%-25% margins.

qa_highlights.question: What can standalone RevPAR be without BRICS, and how sustainable is the 400 bps margin expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: No one-offs in Q2; margin gain from operating leverage, MICE, and management fee mix (booked standalone). Management did not give specific margin guidance but expects a positive margin trend despite new payroll and regulatory costs.

risks_watch: West Asia geopolitics: higher fuel prices and airline capacity cuts hit TajSATS and international travel; Dubai and Ras Al Khaimah fees affected.
TajSATS margin recovery in H2 depends on airline schedules and West Asia developments.
International subsidiaries: St. James' Court margin decline (360 bps in H1); London renovation and property-tax effects; Pierre profitability target still unresolved.
Depreciation up about 20% YoY on consolidated basis (34% on the non-standalone line) from acquisitions and new assets; watch for margin dilution.
Pending OHL merger (close expected before April 1, 2027) and revised portfolio and management-fee guidance due mid-November 2026 and end of next quarter.
Chennai and Kolkata lag other metros on FTA-dependent demand; management expects recovery in next one or two quarters.
500850|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, guidance and pipeline, with frank acknowledgement of TajSATS, international margins and West Asia headwinds. Management was somewhat defensive on the international portfolio and evasive on the exact H2 growth math and the Q2 ex-event RevPAR figure.
key_quotes: Accordingly, we are revising our full year growth guidance upwards to 15% to 17%.
So international is what makes Taj the world's strongest hotel brand.
I would say, optimistic on TajSATS going back to where it was and actually even improving upon it in the second half.
I think we are getting very close to finding a more sustainable solution, but this is not the one which will do 20% 25% EBITDA margin.

500870|2026-06.headline: Castrol India Q2 CY26 revenue rose 25% YoY to INR1,871 crore and EBITDA 41% YoY to INR494 crore, helped by inventory benefits and pricing.
500870|2026-06.overview: Castrol India reported strong Q2 (April–June 2026) with revenue from operations of INR1,871 crore (+25% YoY, +21% QoQ), EBITDA of INR494 crore (+41% YoY and QoQ) and PAT of INR348 crore (+43% YoY). Growth was described as broad-based across consumer, industrial and institutional businesses, with two price increases in January–June 2026 and some benefit from older, lower-cost inventory. Management said cost inflation from supply disruptions and commodity volatility began to hit late in the quarter and will be more visible in Q3. The company declared an interim dividend of INR6.25 per share.

segments.name: Consumer (B2C, retail/auto care)
segments.commentary: Broad-based volume growth driven by rural operations and urban premiumisation; POWER1 (premium motorcycle) grew ahead of rest of business. Rural business growing at double digits; rural outlets ~45,000.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: Growing at high double digits over last couple of years; about 15% of overall business per CFO. Growth from advanced solutions and expanded customer base.

segments.name: Institutional / B2B (OEMs)
segments.commentary: Works with OEMs such as Tata Motors and Maruti; growth tied to OEM volumes. No separate figures disclosed.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin management framework remains 21%–24%; pricing actions are set to keep margins within this band.
Commodity and feedstock inflation expected to become more visible in Q3 FY27, with some raw material increases expected to spill over into Q3.
Management says price actions taken so far are sufficient to offset raw material increases from Q2, but will take further pricing if base oil or FX move adversely.
Lubricant industry expected to grow 3%–4%; company aims to grow at about 2x market.
Capex of about INR100 crore per year, roughly half in manufacturing and half in market (dealer/workshop visibility).
Sourcing guidance of ~55% domestic / ~45% imported broadly unchanged, with quarterly tactical variation.
capex_capacity: Annual capex of about INR100 crore, split roughly equally between manufacturing (health, safety, capacity) and in-market investments.
Silvassa plant was shut for a few days in July 2026 due to heavy rain; fully back up with operating levels at Q2 peak per management.
Paharpur and Silvassa plants completed 9 years and 3 years respectively without significant recordable incident.

National footprint of ~160,000 outlets; auto care range in 40,000 outlets; 34,000 independent motorcycle workshops and 16,000 car workshops; 850 Castrol Auto Service (CAS) outlets; 950 rural service express units.
Building capabilities for specialised EV fluids and data-centre cooling fluids; data-centre business not yet material.
demand_pricing: Two price increases taken in January–June 2026 (late Q1 and Q2), in the low double-digit percentage range; pricing aimed at offsetting supply chain volatility and inflation.
Volume growth described as broad-based across consumer and industrial; company declined to disclose absolute volume (million litres) for the quarter, departing from past practice of sharing it.
Competitor reportedly took around 4 price increases between March and July 2026; management said it will not follow competitor pricing blindly and is guided by RM outlook and margin band.
Group III base oil prices elevated, impacted by Middle East crisis.
Inventory: about half of raw materials bought locally and half from international suppliers; company says it runs lean inventory and that Q2 benefited from older, cheaper inventory being consumed.
E20 fuel: most passenger car brands already compliant; impact on lubricants seen as limited to engine-level fuel-choice issues.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for the open offer linked to the BP/Stonepeak Castrol global divestment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the deal is progressing but is large and multi-country; open offer timing depends on deal closure, after which SEBI and shareholder notifications and prescribed timelines apply. No timeline given.

qa_highlights.question: Volume vs pricing split and Silvassa flood impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth is broad-based but no specific figures given; price increases were in low double digits. Silvassa plant was halted briefly in July for safety and is now at peak operating levels, with no impact.

qa_highlights.question: Was there an inventory gain in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said older inventory bought at softer prices was consumed in the quarter, benefiting margins; it declined to quantify and said profitability grew healthily even excluding this.

qa_highlights.question: Dividend policy?
qa_highlights.answer: No fixed payout percentage; dividend yield usually around 5% including interim and final; special dividends given occasionally. Interim window was advanced this year. Past three years' payout has been in the 80%–90% range per the questioner, which management did not confirm as policy.

qa_highlights.question: Why are price hikes not enough to offset Q3 raw material cost, given diesel prices fell after June?
qa_highlights.answer: Pricing was modelled on inventory and FX scenarios for Q2 and H2; current pricing is seen as broadly reflecting Q3 costs, but the environment is volatile and further price action is possible. Structural cost reductions are also underway.

qa_highlights.question: OCI loss of ~INR66 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a fair-value revaluation of the Ki Mobility investment made about 4 years ago, using listed comparable companies, reviewed every six months; expected to move up and down with peers.

risks_watch: Commodity and base oil (Group III) cost inflation expected to hit Q3 margins more visibly; margin band 21%–24%.
Foreign exchange movements affecting input costs.
Possible volume trade-off or downtrading from the price increases, especially with competitor pricing reportedly higher.
Dependence on Silvassa plant and monsoon/weather disruptions.
Pending BP/Stonepeak divestment of Castrol global, with open offer timing uncertain.
Lack of volume disclosure reduces visibility into volume vs price split.
500870|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the quarter's results and the broad-based growth story, but cautious on the outlook, citing inflation, volatility and monsoon conditions. Management was evasive on volume figures, inventory gain quantification, the open offer timeline and data-centre revenue.
key_quotes: And this is in context of a very volatile operating environment marked by supply disruptions and commodity cost inflation.
We, therefore, expect the impact of commodity and feedstock inflation to become more visible in the third quarter.
I think we pride ourselves on a very lean inventory profile.

500870|2026-09.headline: Castrol India Q3 CY26 revenue rose 27% YoY to INR 1,735 crore, but EBITDA fell 19% to INR 262 crore (~15% margin) on raw material inflation.
500870|2026-09.overview: Q3 revenue from operations was INR 1,735 crore, up 27% YoY but down 7% QoQ, while EBITDA fell 19% YoY to INR 262 crore and PAT fell 23% YoY to INR 176 crore. Management attributed the squeeze to a sharp rise in commodity and raw material costs (cited as a 60-plus percent increase in the raw material bill) and adverse currency moves, partly offset by early-year pricing actions. Over nine months, revenue grew 20% to INR 5,151 crore, EBITDA rose 11% to INR 1,086 crore and PAT rose 9% to INR 766 crore. Management declined to give forward quarterly guidance and said margins will sit outside the 21-24% EBITDA band in the short to medium term.

segments.name: Industrial lubricants
segments.commentary: Delivered another quarter of double-digit volume growth in the September quarter; added close to 400 customers net over the full year and 9 months, with growth in steel and cement and new metalworking fluid launches (Hysol 35 XBB, Hysol 61 XBB, boron-free). Management said industrial margin is healthy and above last year's level.

segments.name: Automotive / consumer and commercial vehicle
segments.commentary: No separate volume figures given. Management said Q2 and Q3 were managed together and volume growth looked healthy; company claims market share held across categories. Institutional customers include Tata, Maruti and JCB.

segments.name: Thermal management / data-centre cooling
segments.commentary: Early-stage. Two latest products certified by NVIDIA about 1.5 months before the call for direct-to-chip cooling; business is in ongoing pilots and not a substantial part of revenue or profit today.

guidance_outlook: No quarterly guidance given; management cited unprecedented raw material volatility.
Medium-term EBITDA margin expected to fall outside the 21-24% band in the short to medium term; the 21-24% band remains the target over time.
Management said it will operate within a 21-24% EBITDA frame over the medium term while growing volume at least 1.5x to 2x the market growth rate.
Plant utilisation expected to stay in the 70-80% range through the year.
Market growth in India estimated at 3-4% in a normal year; this year may see headwinds, with Castrol tracking ahead.
Capex historically INR 100-150 crore per year, focused on plant innovation, capacity and consumer/trade visibility.

Stonepeak acquisition of Castrol from BP: completion targeted by end CY26 per the deal; management said licence work across 50+ countries is progressing well, with SEBI disclosure to follow on completion.
capex_capacity: Plants run at around 70-80% utilisation; expected to remain in the same range through the year, with seasonal flex.
Historical capex of INR 100-150 crore per year; no specific CY27 capex figure given.
Localisation of inputs and reformulation are being used to reduce bill of materials and cash cost.
Supply-chain efficiency work under way for 6-7 months to partly offset raw material inflation.
demand_pricing: Raw material bill up 60-plus percent in Q3; COGS as a percentage of sales up 61% YoY.
Pricing actions taken early in the year; further pricing to be taken as and when required, calibrated by sector, with no forward guidance.
About 40% of business is B2B; some B2B contracts have price-flex clauses for input-cost pass-through, while B2C pricing varies by channel.
Base oil prices: Base Oil 2 down about 5% and Base Oil 3 down about 7% in Q3 per an analyst; management said the cost environment remains substantially challenged versus last year.
Crude oil went from about $120 in Q2 to about $80, and is now back at $114-115 per management.

Network of about 167,000 outlets, including 46,000 in rural small-town India; Auto Care in 50,000 stores; about 870 Castrol Auto Service centres, 37,000 independent bike workshops and 16,000 multi-brand workshops; Rural Service Express at over 1,000 locations.

qa_highlights.question: What is the volume guidance and how is pricing balanced against market share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no guidance for the next few months given the unprecedented raw material moves; it reiterated the aim to gain volume and share, with pricing balanced to let consumers move to new price points.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex and margin guidance for CY27, and hedging plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex historically INR 100-150 crore; investments prioritise growth drivers. Margin protection is to come from a mix of pricing and cost prudence; no hedging detail was given.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the Stonepeak acquisition and the DPS filing in India?
qa_highlights.answer: Licence work across more than 50 countries is progressing well; SEBI will be informed on completion, with no timeline beyond that.

qa_highlights.question: Is Castrol refocusing on the OEM business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not call out OEM as a separate focus; it said it works with OEMs such as Tata, Maruti and JCB on new engine platform technology.

qa_highlights.question: Segment-wise sales and Q3 volume trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth ahead of market over nine months; industrial grew double digits in Q3; automotive volumes were described as healthy across Q2 and Q3 combined, with no specific figures.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reference margin per litre, and does lower absolute EBITDA imply lower volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said per-litre EBITDA is an internal frame, and the external measure is percentage margin: 26% in Q2, 15% in Q3, 21% over six and nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Are plants and margins expected to recover, and what levers are there?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 21-24% band will be reached only once volatility subsides, with levers in supplier diversification, localisation, reformulation and supply-chain efficiency.

qa_highlights.question: Data-centre cooling: size of opportunity and how sales are routed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said products are globally approved and sold through Castrol India, with NVIDIA certification as a base requirement; it declined to size the opportunity, saying it is not yet material.

risks_watch: Raw material and crude/FX volatility: margin per litre is the stated measure, but guidance has been withdrawn.
Q4 CY26 margin and volume recovery; watch pricing action and base oil rebates in Oct-Dec.
Volume softness in the short to medium term given market headwinds.
Stonepeak-BP transaction: completion by end CY26 and any change to the timeline.
Limited disclosure: analysts pressed for segment and volume detail, and an analyst asked for more specific guidance.
500870|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on long-term strategy and the industrial and rural growth engines, but cautious and non-committal on near-term margins and guidance, citing raw material and currency volatility. Management was evasive on volume split, data-centre sizing and the timeline for the Stonepeak deal.
key_quotes: We are not giving a guidance for the next few months because it's unprecedented in terms of the raw material price movement, right?
For us, margin per liter is a true measure. And on that basis, we have fully absorbed cost inflation.
We will hold ourselves to the frame of operating the business at 21% to 24% EBITDA.

500877|2026-06.headline: Apollo Tyres Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue INR 74bn (+12.8% YoY), EBITDA margin 11.7% (down ~150bp) on ~17% raw material inflation.
500877|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 12.8% YoY to INR 74bn but was flat-ish sequentially, with consolidated EBITDA margin down about 150bp YoY to 11.7% on raw material cost pressure. India delivered its highest-ever revenue of INR 54.6bn (+15.6% YoY, +4.3% QoQ), largely volume-led, with India EBITDA margin at 12% versus 13.6%. Europe revenue was EUR147m (+0.5% YoY) with EBITDA of EUR13m (8.9% margin), hit by Enschede closure transition and agri revenue loss. Management said price increases lag raw material inflation and that most of the catch-up flows into Q2 and H2.

financial_highlights.change: India capex INR 500 crore in Q1

financial_highlights.metric: Raw material cost increase in Q1
financial_highlights.change: Rubber INR 225/kg, synthetic INR 250, carbon black INR 125, steel cord INR 165 (as quoted)

segments.name: India operations
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 54.6bn (+15.6% YoY), double-digit growth across all segments; volume growth Replacement 13%, OEM 10%, Exports 15%. TBB was the only category without double-digit growth. Price increases ~3-4% realised in Q1 versus 7-9% taken.

segments.name: Europe operations
segments.commentary: Revenue EUR147m (+0.5% YoY) and EBITDA EUR13m (8.9%). PCR replacement grew double digits; agri revenue fell high-teens QoQ and small single digits YoY. Without Enschede overlap costs, margin would have been ~11%.

segments.name: Reifen
segments.commentary: Revenue EUR43m in Q1 with ~3% EBITDA margin, as disclosed on the call.

guidance_outlook: Raw material inflation of ~8% sequentially expected in Q2 for India; Europe RM basket up 8% in Q1 with hit mainly in Q2.

India needs ~15-16% total price increase to cover commodity inflation; ~11%+ currently in place (9% TBR, 11% other categories); at least 1-2 more hikes needed; July hike 1-2%, similar hike expected in August.
Europe needs ~10% price increase across Q1-Q2; only 3-4% implemented so far.
Europe full-year EBITDA target: high teens margin once manufacturing footprint transition completes.
Net debt/EBITDA expected to rise slightly this year as company becomes a net borrower; capex to rise in Q2 and Q3.
Rubber expected to cool from Q3 as seasonal impact fades; crude-linked cost relief expected with a quarter lag.
capex_capacity: Enschede (Netherlands) plant stopped production in June 2026; ~750,000 tyres/year shifting largely to Hungary, completion Sept-Oct 2026; financial benefits from H2 FY27.
Hungary PCR capacity rising from ~17,000 to ~21,000 car tyres per day, starting H2 FY27; Hungary expanding by 4,000 PCR tyres/day, AP (India) plant expanding double that.
Lower-end 14-15 inch tyres moving from Hungary to India; Spacemaster spare tyre production now in Baroda; India new capacity to start towards end of FY27 and ramp through FY28.
High-end agri (OHT) capacity limited at Kalamassery (Kochi); no economic small-scale alternative; offtake partner identified near Asia-Europe cusp, midterm plan is offtake.
India capex was ~INR 1,200-1,300 crore annually in recent past; FY27 group capex guided above INR 3,000 crore.
Management says India running in the 90s on capacity utilisation and will stay tight through FY27.
demand_pricing: India replacement momentum strong; July started strongly and Q2 YoY growth expected to be good though QoQ muted due to rains and seasonality.
Europe: anti-dumping duty on Chinese tyres expected to help Apollo brand at lower end; Vredestein PCR does not compete with Chinese.
Exports growth driven by Europe; West Asia impacted by war and US underperformed due to dealer inventory issues.
Competition has broadly followed price increases of similar magnitude, per management.
Management market share estimates (internal): TBR replacement upwards of 30% (regained lost share); PCR replacement 21%+.
UHP mix in Europe stayed at around 40%, per management recollection.
Advertising and sales promotion spend cut by roughly 50% QoQ; management said no further reduction expected.

qa_highlights.question: India volume growth by channel and outlook; Europe anti-dumping and capacity shift timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Replacement +13%, OEM +10%, exports +15% volume growth; Q2 seasonal. Enschede-to-Hungary shift to complete Sept-Oct 2026; Spacemaster already in Baroda.

qa_highlights.question: How much India and Europe price hikes have been taken vs needed?
qa_highlights.answer: India: 7-9% implemented in Q1 (only 3-4% flowed into revenue), 11%+ now against 15-16% needed. Europe: 3-4% implemented against ~10% needed.

qa_highlights.question: Europe margin without overlap costs and steady-state target?
qa_highlights.answer: ~11% margin without overlap; full-year Europe target high-teens EBITDA margin after footprint change.

qa_highlights.question: Capex and net debt trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 consolidated capex INR 650 crore; India INR 500 crore; capex to step up in Q2-Q3; company to become net borrower with slight rise in net debt/EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Other expenses and staff cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: A&P cut ~50% QoQ but no further reduction expected; minor increments effective June 1 with full impact from Q2, no further increment planned.

qa_highlights.question: Raw material outlook: rupee, rubber, crude?
qa_highlights.answer: ~7-8% of RM inflation from rupee depreciation (from INR 88); ~50% of RM imported; domestic rubber ~50-50 mix; rubber expected to cool from Q3; crude relief with a quarter lag.

qa_highlights.question: Competitive pricing behaviour and market share?
qa_highlights.answer: Competition has followed price increases of similar magnitude; TBR share back above 30%, PCR replacement 21%+ (internal estimates).

risks_watch: Raw material pass-through lag: India needs ~15-16% total price increase versus ~11%+ in place, with at least 1-2 more hikes needed; OEM formula pricing flows with a quarter lag and truck contracts are negotiated.
Europe price gap: only 3-4% implemented against ~10% needed for Q1-Q2, and Europe RM basket up 8% with the hit mainly in Q2.

Europe execution: Enschede-to-Hungary transfer to complete Sept-Oct 2026; high-end agri relies on an unnamed offtake partner, with about 20-25% of agri volume offtaken and a couple of quarters needed to stabilise customer approvals.
Capex and leverage: FY27 group capex guided above INR 3,000 crore, rising in Q2-Q3; company turns net borrower and net debt/EBITDA rises slightly from 0.4x.

Commodity reversal and price correction: rubber expected to cool from Q3 and crude relief with a quarter lag, but management flagged possible price correction in Q4 if RM falls sharply; export weakness in West Asia and US.
key_quotes: The revenue for the quarter was INR 54.6 billion, representing a healthy growth of 15.6% Y-o-Y and 4.3% sequentially.
So the current quantum of price increase is about 9% in TBR and 11% in other categories.
So I would admit to you that we'll have to get back to you. I can't give you a conclusive answer if there's been a pre-buy.
We are currently running into the 90s.
500877|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on India demand and pricing momentum (July start strong, capacity running in the 90s), but cautious on Europe margins and near-term raw material costs, which management said remain volatile. Answers were often hedged or deferred, e.g. pre-buy question ("I can't give you a conclusive answer") and debt trajectory, with the outgoing CFO handling the call.

500940|2026-03.headline: Finolex Q4 FY26 EBITDA nearly doubled to INR332 crore on inventory gains and VCM-linked margins, but volumes stayed flat at 101,772 tonnes.
500940|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 12% YoY to INR1,314 crore, with EBITDA up to INR332 crore from INR171 crore and PBT up 65% to INR334 crore. Volumes were broadly flat YoY at 101,772 tonnes, as agri demand did not pick up in Q4 and farmers held back on expectations of lower prices. Management attributed part of the margin jump to an inventory gain of about INR35-40 crore and to backward-integration fuel cost advantages, and guided FY27 EBITDA margin to sub-15%. The company guided FY27 volume growth of higher single digit to lower double digit on a full-year basis.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR171 crore in Q4 FY25 (nearly doubled)
Up YoY; analyst-calculated ~22% ex inventory gain
vs INR144 crore in Q4 FY25
Flat vs 102,253 tonnes in Q4 FY25
Flat vs INR4,142 crore in FY25
FY25 dividend was INR3.60 per share

segments.name: PVC pipes (agri vs non-agri)
segments.commentary: Agri was about 63% of FY26 mix versus 67% in FY25; management's ideal long-run split is 50:50 over 4-5 years. Agri is about 65-70% of volume per CFO, and Q4 saw agri volume fall while non-agri rose.

segments.name: Fittings
segments.commentary: Fittings were about 9% of Q4 volume (9% in Q4 FY25) and about 11% of FY26 volume (10% in FY25). Fitting volume growth is around 9-10%.

segments.name: CPVC
segments.commentary: CPVC was about 7-8% of overall volume in Q4 (6-7% a year ago) and CPVC portfolio volume is growing about 8-9%; CPVC fittings grow faster.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin target is sub-15% (mid to lower double digit), described as conservative given geopolitical uncertainty; management expects to deliver higher margin toward year-end.
FY27 volume growth target of higher single digit to lower double digit on a full-year basis, not quarterly.
Q1 FY27 margin not guided; April was subdued and management will assess May and June.
Maintenance and debottlenecking capex of roughly INR100 crore per year, with extruder upgrades; capacity is 520,000 tonnes and sufficient for current and probably next year's volume.
Dividend decision on accumulated cash (about INR2,563 crore net cash) is pending with the Board; no timeline given.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity rose to 520,000 tonnes in FY26 from 492,000 tonnes at end FY25.

International business is about 13% of core revenue; Greaves International Trading FZE set up in Dubai for Middle East and Africa.

qa_highlights.question: How has margin erosion split between OEM and aftermarket/retail?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said commodity costs hit all products. OEM contracts have indexing with a lag, while aftermarket pricing is easier to pass on; price increases have been taken in both.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin drop is investment versus commodity cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Manish Poddar attributed about 1.5 percentage points to additional investments; the rest is the inflation-price lag, which should narrow in Q2 and fully in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Is GEML's growth sustainable and when does it turn EBITDA-positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Vikas Singh said per-unit losses have fallen sharply and EBITDA could turn positive in 4 to 6 quarters, without committing to timing or scale.

qa_highlights.question: Why does GFL, an EV financing NBFC, exist in a pruned portfolio, and is it brand-agnostic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said GFL is part of the EV ecosystem; its share of GEML financing is near double digits and rising. Vikas Singh said financing partners are brand-agnostic by nature.

qa_highlights.question: Is there enough cash for the investee investments?
qa_highlights.answer: Manish Poddar said standalone liquidity as of March 2026 covers the INR50 crore GFL and INR331 crore GEML investments plus Q1-Q2 capex and dividends, and that the core business generates enough cash.

qa_highlights.question: Is motorcycle entry planned for GEML?
qa_highlights.answer: Vikas Singh said motorcycle prototypes are underway; the scooter opportunity is also large and prioritisation is under leadership review with no timing decided.

risks_watch: Margins: Q1 margin down 2-2.5 pts; recovery depends on Q2-H2 pricing and cost savings, and the full-year target is contingent on H2 catch-up.
Commodity and geopolitical cost pressure (West Asia developments) may outlast the pricing actions.
GEML is still loss-making with a 4-6 quarter timeline to positive EBITDA; management gave no firm timing.
Excel revenue of about INR66-70 crores and export-led recovery depend on new Europe and US customers.
Greaves Technologies had earlier slippages; management said it is still stabilising and cited one pilot design-work order.
Unallocable expenses of INR25.82 crores in segment results; the company said these are now folded into core business P&L (slide 27).
key_quotes: Now our ability to mitigate those differs slightly by the segment of customers.
And to sum it up, we're absolutely on track with our commitment to Greaves.Next strategy and the margin targets that we have set for ourselves.
We're not in a position really to comment in terms of how soon and how much, but we are very confident and that's what the entire team is working towards.
At this stage, I don't want to reveal more detail because the discussions are still evolving.
501455|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on demand and GEML momentum, with management repeatedly reiterating FY27 margin and 16-20% growth targets. More cautious and evasive on margin recovery timing, GEML EBITDA breakeven (declined to give specifics) and data-centre/AI product details (withheld as discussions are evolving).

502090|2026-03.headline: Sagar Cements guides FY27 volumes to about 7 million tonnes (FY26: 6.1 Mt) and Q4 EBITDA/tonne rose to ₹445 from ₹218.
502090|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 volumes grew 8% YoY and full-year volumes grew 11% to 6.1 million tonnes, with revenue up 20% in the quarter helped by non-trade pricing. Q4 EBITDA per tonne was ₹445 against ₹218 a year earlier, and quarterly PAT was ₹100 crore. Management flagged a fuel cost shock from the West Asia conflict (pet coke at $136-140 CIF versus about $120 earlier), with impact expected from mid-Q2 if prices do not ease. Management also announced a Superfine Building Materials division and in-principle approval for merging Andhra Cements into the parent.

segments.name: Plants (Q4 utilisation)
segments.commentary: Mattampally 59%, Gudipadu 84%, Bayyavaram 69%, Jeerabad 95%, Jajpur 44%, Dachepalli 38%. Jeerabad is cited as consistently running around 90%.

segments.name: Superfine Building Materials (new division)
segments.commentary: Approved by the board on 13 May 2026. It will use GGBS and fly ash to make superfine products (Blaine target 10,000-20,000) for UHPC, repairs and cladding. Management guides a minimum 30% margin; revenue and EBITDA numbers are deferred to next quarter.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume target of about 7 million tonnes, relying on about 0.5 Mt from Jeerabad upgrade (expected by end-Q1), about 0.9 Mt from Andhra ramp-up and the balance from market growth of 12-15%.
FY27 EBITDA per tonne expected to be close to ₹600 if prices stay flat, with about ₹150/tonne from internal cost savings (WHRS, Andhra preheater, grinding units).

Pet coke and coal cost pressure: about ₹200/tonne at clinker and ₹100-150/tonne at cement on current blend, with impact from mid-Q2 if prices stay high. Management also pencilled in about ₹225-250/tonne in total fuel and miscellaneous cost increases, assumed to be passed through.
FY27 budget: ₹580 crore cost, about ₹100 crore lower than the prior year's cost base according to management's comments.

Capex: ₹190 crore pending on three ongoing projects (Andhra ₹140 crore, Gudipadu ₹17 crore, Jeerabad ₹33 crore). Maintenance capex about ₹50 crore per year. Some projects to be funded through lease or equipment finance.
Vizag land monetisation (about 100 acres, net about ₹3.5 crore per acre): ₹350 crore pencilled over 18-24 months, with ₹150 crore in year 1 after the government GO, and ₹150 crore assumed in FY27.
Net debt guidance for FY27 is to pay debt down from operating cash flow; year-end net debt was about ₹1,550 crore versus the earlier guidance of about ₹1,300 crore.
capex_capacity: WHRS: 2.8 MW of 4.35 MW (AQC boiler) commissioned on 12 May 2026; remaining 1.55 MW (preheater boiler) due by end-June 2026.
Jeerabad grinding expansion and Dachepalli expansion in progress; Jeerabad due before end of Q1 FY27.
Andhra Cements grinding expansion due by September 2026; new VRM for cement grinding due by September 2026.
Andhra clinker kcal consumption about 700 kcal/tonne of clinker versus about 775-780 earlier.
Madhya Pradesh incentives of about ₹171 crore over seven years; about ₹65 crore received so far, about ₹110 crore remaining over four years.
demand_pricing: Industry demand held up in the first two months of Q4 but slowed in late Q4 due to labour shortages, the festive season and unseasonal rains. Q4 volume growth was 8%, and Q1 FY27 to date is up about 7% YoY.
Price hike of about ₹25-30 per bag in second week of April (non-trade led) across regions; Hyderabad retail about ₹295 and wholesale about ₹268 after the hike.
Prices have been flat since mid-April, with some pressure in central and eastern markets (₹5 hike in Indore not sustained) and a slight negative bias there; south has held the April hike.
Demand outlook: AP and Telangana strong; Tamil Nadu 5-10%, Karnataka 5%, Odisha 5%, Madhya Pradesh 5-7.5%.
Management said bags cost fell about ₹2/bag, but the war impact on explosives and diesel (₹23.75/litre hike in commercial diesel) is expected to add about ₹100/tonne.
Superfine products priced around ₹30,000/tonne versus ₹2,500-3,000/tonne for low-Blaine GGBS, with low volumes expected initially.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected cost impact from the West Asia crisis?
qa_highlights.answer: Pet coke has risen from around $120 to $136-140 CIF, adding about ₹200/tonne at clinker and ₹100-150/tonne at cement. Inventory cover runs to mid-Q2, and imported coal is being partly switched to domestic coal, with the outcome known by end-Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise 28% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Around ₹11.5 crore was one-offs: about ₹7.5 crore mine bearing land (MBL) cess and about ₹3.24 crore DMF expense at a subsidiary, covering roughly 3-3.5 years of accrual. Promotional spend also rose. Excluding one-offs, growth is about 26%.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 volume of 7 Mt be achieved given past misses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target relies on Jeerabad (+0.5 Mt), Andhra ramp-up (+0.9 Mt) and market growth; it chooses not to chase share at the expense of cash.

qa_highlights.question: Will Jeerabad clinker sales continue in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Some clinker sales are expected during the phased ramp-up, subject to clinker prices, with margin held at that location's level.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any cost reduction left after Andhra stabilised?
qa_highlights.answer: Andhra clinker cost is now in line; the new VRM (by September) should deliver the planned savings. Margins are expected to be better in FY27 than FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Why did net debt rise above guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Promoter unsecured debt for the Andhra project was drawn after the planned rights issue became an OFS, and solar capex was accelerated for short payback. Debt is expected to fall from operating cash flow.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital days rose sharply: why?
qa_highlights.answer: Credit days were extended in a difficult market, fuel prices were higher, and volumes grew. About ₹80 crore of US coal was bought in March on 180-day LC credit. Moderation is expected.

qa_highlights.question: Vizag land GO status and sale timing?
qa_highlights.answer: GVMC and UDA approvals are in place; the state GO is awaited, expected within six months. Management is assuming ₹350 crore over 18-24 months at the old reckoner rate of ₹4 crore per acre.

qa_highlights.question: Operating cost gap between standalone and Andhra?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the gap is mainly logistics and market spread, with the Andhra cost gap closing after investments; detail to be discussed offline.

risks_watch: Fuel cost inflation: pet coke and coal may add ₹100-150/tonne at cement from mid-Q2 if prices do not ease; a ₹225-250/tonne total cost pass-through is assumed.
Pricing: the April hike is holding in the south, but central and eastern prices are flat to slightly negative.
Execution: Jeerabad upgrade (0.5 Mt), Andhra ramp-up (0.9 Mt), WHRS completion by end-June and VRM by September; past volume guidance has been missed.
Debt and working capital: year-end net debt about ₹1,550 crore, above prior guidance; working capital elevated; funding of ₹190 crore capex needs lease finance.
Vizag land monetisation depends on the state GO, which is still awaited; ₹150 crore is pencilled into FY27.
Incentive receipts: about ₹23 crore outstanding at March 2026, expected mid-July 2026.
502090|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on volume and margin recovery, with the Andhra turnaround and cost savings presented as key drivers. Cautious and somewhat evasive on fuel costs, the Superfine division financials and land sale timing, which management deferred to later updates.
key_quotes: We are more than hopeful to achieve 7 million tonnes for the current year.
We don't chase market share. We actually conserve the cash.
I think in the current year itself, we should be very close to ₹600 because the significant improvement for us has come from the cost itself

502090|2026-06.headline: Sagar Cements Q1 FY27: volumes up ~13% YoY but loss after tax of ₹28 crore and EBITDA of ₹451/tonne on West Asia-driven cost inflation.
502090|2026-06.overview: Volumes grew about 13% YoY and revenue rose 5% YoY, with realisations broadly stable. Profitability moderated as energy, fuel and packaging costs rose amid West Asia tensions, leaving EBITDA at ₹451 per tonne and a loss after tax of ₹28 crore. Management maintained a 7 million tonne volume target for FY27 (excluding clinker) and reiterated FY27 EBITDA guidance of ₹500–550 per tonne, down from the earlier ~₹600 reference raised by an analyst. Capex completed in the quarter includes Jeerabad 0.5 million tonne expansion and the remaining 1.55 MW of Gudipadu waste heat recovery; the 0.75 million tonne Andhra Cements expansion is expected by quarter-end.

segments.name: Gudipadu (AP)

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume target of ~7 million tonnes, excluding clinker sales; management sees FY28 volume growth in double digits.
FY27 EBITDA guidance of ₹500–550 per tonne, assuming prices stay flat; management said ₹550 is 'definitely doable'.
Q2 FY27 to see cost increase from maintenance shutdowns at three plants (Mattampally, Jeerabad among them) and inventory cost adjustment; management expects recovery in Q3 and Q4.
Management pencilled in ~₹100/tonne cost inflation (₹50 power and fuel, ₹50 miscellaneous), offset by efficiency gains; inventory covers operations up to mid-October.
No capex plans beyond ~₹30–40 crore annual maintenance through 2028, apart from ~₹240 crore of ongoing capex spread over FY27 and FY28.
Vizag land monetisation of ₹150 crore pencilled for FY27 and ~₹200 crore for FY28, pending a generic Government GO.

July demand expected to track Q1 trend, with labour availability back.

Tamil Nadu ban on transport of rough stones and aggregates to other states: management sees no impact.
Heat waves and election-related labour shortages in Eastern and Southern India disrupted Q1 execution.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 7 million tonne FY27 volume target ex-clinker, and how much clinker will be sold in Q2 and beyond?
qa_highlights.answer: The 7 mt target excludes clinker. Clinker is still sold to Andhra Cements' sister unit Bayyavaram and some outside, and some at Jeerabad until ramp-up; management would not quantify volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Is double-digit volume growth possible in FY28, and what is the Q2 cost inflation and is the ~₹600/t EBITDA guidance intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says FY27 and FY28 both see double-digit volume growth. Full-year cost pressure is about ₹100/t across fuel, raw material and miscellaneous, offset by savings; Q2 gets extra inventory and maintenance cost at three plants. Guidance is ₹500–550/t, assuming flat prices, not ~₹600.

qa_highlights.question: Are prices stable versus Q1 averages?
qa_highlights.answer: Prices have been flat from March exit to July and June to July; realisation was up about ₹50–60/t, with the cause unclear (mix or price hikes).

qa_highlights.question: Status of Vizag land sale and FY27 realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Awaiting a generic Government GO after the government signalled it would replace a case-specific order; the ₹150 crore for FY27 is still seen as doable. Management said buyer engagement exists but timelines were the issue.

qa_highlights.question: Which regions drive incremental H2 FY27 demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Almost all incremental volume comes from the South (~80% of footprint). Madpradesh is also expected to rise after the 0.5 mt Jeerabad expansion, supporting the ~15% growth projected for the year.

qa_highlights.question: How does Andhra Cements' cost structure compare with Mattampally, and how should the three units be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Variable cost at Andhra is ₹100–125/t higher than Mattampally because it buys grid power without waste heat recovery; management says the kcal and unit metrics are at par. Andhra carries most of the debt, and management offered to share modelling details offline.

qa_highlights.question: Can Q1 EBITDA of ~₹425/t reach ₹600/t for full year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ₹550/t is 'definitely doable', citing Gudipadu WHR savings, Jeerabad expansion and the Andhra cement mill due end-September, assuming stable prices.

qa_highlights.question: Is capex going to rise, and what is the debt reduction path?
qa_highlights.answer: No new capex beyond ₹30–40 crore annual maintenance through 2028. About ₹240 crore of ongoing capex spreads over FY27 and FY28; operating cash flow is not yet reflected in the gross debt path.

qa_highlights.question: What are the levers to manage power and fuel costs if the West Asia crisis escalates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has no control over prices and can only manage consumption, which it says is efficient. Inventory covers operations to mid-October; ₹100/t inflation is pencilled in (₹50 fuel, ₹50 other), and clinker is at its peak.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the Tamil Nadu ban on rough stone and aggregate transport, and what limestone auction premiums are seen?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no impact. Recent Telangana limestone auctions, about a year or 18 months old, went at 50–75% premiums; other auctions are pending in TN, AP and Telangana.

qa_highlights.question: Will the land sale and volume ramp support the net debt projection?
qa_highlights.answer: Parth Bhavsar asked about net debt trajectory. Management said the ₹150 crore land sale is in FY27 and about ₹200 crore in FY28.

risks_watch: Cost pressure: ~₹100/t FY27 inflation pencilled in, with clinker at peak; inventory covers operations only up to mid-October, and Q2 faces extra inventory and maintenance cost at Mattampally and Jeerabad.
Guidance credibility: FY27 EBITDA guidance of ₹500–550/t depends on flat prices, cost savings from Gudipadu WHR, Jeerabad ramp-up and the Andhra mill (end-September); Q1 was ₹451/t.
Pricing: realisation gains of ₹50–60/t are not attributed; management says a price hike is needed eventually but timing and size are uncertain given competitive intensity.
Vizag land monetisation (₹150 crore FY27, ~₹200 crore FY28) still awaits a generic Government GO, and the buyer timeline is unclear.
Debt: gross debt ₹1,704 crore and D/E 0.78:1; the operating cash flow debt reduction is not yet in the plan, and ~₹240 crore of ongoing capex runs through FY28.
Andhra Cements: utilisation near 50% vs ~60% target by end-FY27, with grid-power cost ₹100–125/t above Mattampally until its waste heat recovery is built in the next couple of years.
key_quotes: We remain confident of achieving volumes of approximately 7 million tons in FY 2027, supported by our expanding market presence and ongoing operational initiatives.
What we have indicated and what we remain committed is around ₹500 to ₹550 EBITDA per tonne.
₹550 is definitely doable, as I mentioned to you.
I don't think we have ability to control the inflation. We only have ability to control the quantity of usage.
502090|2026-06.management_tone: Management was confident on volume (7 mt FY27, double-digit growth in FY28) and on the ₹500–550/t EBITDA guidance, but cautious on near-term costs and pricing. Answers on the Vizag GO, Andhra cost modelling and clinker volumes were less specific, with some items deferred to offline discussion.

502219|2026-06.headline: Borosil Renewables Q1 FY27 standalone sales rose 53% YoY to INR405.69 crore and EBITDA to INR142 crore (35% margin), helped by a fuel surcharge.
502219|2026-06.overview: Standalone sales were INR405.69 crore, up 53% YoY from INR332.26 crore, while EBITDA rose to INR142 crore at 35% of sales versus 27.9% a year ago. Average ex-factory realisation rose to INR160.30 per sq m from INR150.20 in Q4 FY26, including a INR9.50 fuel surcharge introduced from 10 March 2026 after the West Asia war raised fuel costs. Management said the surcharge is now being cut as fuel prices ease, and that the 600 TPD furnace expansion is on track for commissioning in Q1 FY27-end (January to March 2027). Reported PAT of about INR169 crore in Q4 FY26 was inflated by a INR75 crore tax write-back, so the sequential PAT comparison is not like-for-like.

segments.commentary: Early-stage on-grid residential kit (module, inverter, battery) sold as a system. Q1 revenue about INR1.3 crore against an internal FY27 target of about INR36 crore; EBITDA margin expected in single digits, versus 30-35% for glass.

guidance_outlook: 600 TPD expansion at the existing site: construction targeted by December 2026, commissioning January to March 2027 (SG4 and SG5, about one month apart). Management says revenue should be modelled from 1 April 2027, though the internal target is 1 March.
Once the 600 TPD is commissioned, sales are expected to rise about 60%, adding about INR80-85 crore of quarterly EBITDA at current run-rate and prices.
Realisation to fall as the INR9.50 fuel surcharge is passed back to customers; management says cost declines should offset this, so profit is not expected to be affected.

Management declined to give a formal guidance but said it expects to continue at similar revenue and EBITDA levels if conditions hold; expects extra profitability this year because prices were at full levels all year.
Ambition to grow from about INR2,500 crore to at least INR4,000 crore revenue in 3-4 years after March 2027; next expansion decision expected within about 6 months.
capex_capacity: Current capacity 1,000 TPD; expansion of 600 TPD at existing location takes it to 1,600 TPD, with the expansion fully funded per management.

Furnace SG1 and SG2 refurbishment: timing not fixed, possibly Q4 FY27 to Q2 FY28, likely after SG4/SG5 are commissioned. A rebuild needs about 75 days of shutdown plus 15 days to restart, so about 90 days with no output from the furnace being rebuilt.
Any further capacity beyond the 600 TPD expansion would be a new building and facility, sized at 600 or 1,200 TPD, and not an add-on to the current layout.
Domestic solar glass capacity expected to reach 7,700 TPD by March 2027 (about 51 GW), against about 2,600 TPD (18 GW) today and about 11,000 TPD demand for 62 GW of module requirement.

Module capacity in India is 203 GW; solar cell capacity is 30 GW, expected to rise to 75 GW by 2027 under ALMM-2 (effective 1 June 2026). ALMM-3 for ingot and wafer starts 28 June, with about 50 GW expected by 2029.
demand_pricing: Management says domestic industry supplies only about 25% of demand; even at 7,700 TPD, supply would cover only 75%, so pricing is expected to hold, with import-parity pricing as the reference.
Exports to the US are very small and in niche applications; the company is focused on the domestic market.
A significant portion of new domestic capacity is captive, so the open-market supply gain is limited, according to management.
Management expects module makers to consolidate over the next 1-1.5 years because module capacity far exceeds requirement; Mono PERC players and those without cell supply may drop volumes.
CVD of 9.71% on solar glass imports from Malaysia extended for five more years from 2 June 2026, on top of anti-dumping duties on China and Vietnam since December 2024.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PAT fall from INR169 crore in Q4 to INR87 crore in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 FY26 PAT included a INR75 crore tax write-back tied to the write-off of the German subsidiary investment (INR325 crore provision). Excluding it, performance was not inferior.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital days rose from 34 to 152; is that right?
qa_highlights.answer: Management disputed the 152-day figure, saying working capital is about 60 days, with a slight rise from stores inventory.

qa_highlights.question: Will domestic prices fall as capacity grows to 7,700 TPD?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said demand is robust, with domestic supply covering only about 25% now, and that pricing is anchored to import parity, so no pricing challenge is foreseen.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rooftop solar business worth?
qa_highlights.answer: Internal FY27 revenue target is about INR36 crore, Q1 revenue about INR1.3 crore, with single-digit EBITDA margins because it is a trading-style solution business.

qa_highlights.question: Any equity raise or debt plan?
qa_highlights.answer: The current expansion is fully funded. Future projects will be funded from internal cash, with some debt if the project is large. No near-term equity raise is planned.

qa_highlights.question: How is the gross margin around 80% calculated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management put gross margin at about 78% on a manufacturing-cost basis, with raw material at about 23-24% of sales, and said margin volatility is not expected.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost of the SG1 patch repair and the volume effect of furnace rebuilds?
qa_highlights.answer: A four-day patch on one furnace cost about INR3 crore in lost output. A full rebuild would shut the furnace for about 90 days, causing a volume loss in the year it happens.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tax rate for the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 25.2% should be assumed for the full year.

risks_watch: Fuel-surcharge unwind: the INR9.50 per sq m surcharge is being reduced as fuel prices ease, so realisation could fall from INR160.30 even with stable costs. Management says the cost decline offsets it.
Commissioning risk: the 600 TPD expansion (SG4, SG5) must be commissioned by March 2027, with revenue only from April 2027. Any delay pushes the 60% volume uplift later.
Furnace SG1/SG2 rebuild: about 90 days of lost output per furnace, timing not fixed (Q4 FY27 to Q2 FY28); this could reduce FY28 volumes against the 1,600 TPD capacity.
Customer concentration: top 10 customers are about 65-68% of volume, and module consolidation could affect volumes.
Capacity additions in domestic glass (to 7,700 TPD by March 2027) could pressure prices, though management expects supply to stay short.
Rooftop solar and the overseas subsidiaries are small and early, with unclear profitability; the call gave no segment-level data.
Management declined to comment on press reports of a strategic investment. Next-phase project choice (glass furnace or adjacent business) is due in about 5-6 months.

502986|2026-06.headline: Vardhman Q1 FY27 margins rose on spinning yarn-size gains and raw-material trading gains; fabric utilisation remains weak as US orders slipped.

Management expects the spinning margin to moderate as cheap inventory runs out, but sees a 13-14% margin as a reasonable direction. Capex is mostly complete, with biomass boilers starting and the Dhar (PM MITRA) site dependent on land and power by around December 2026 and June 2027.

503101|2026-03.headline: FY26 consolidated PAT of INR 206 crores, the company's highest ever, alongside INR 900 crores QIP and INR 576 crores FY26 presales (MNRL share).
503101|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as transformational, citing record PAT of INR 206 crores on total income of INR 639 crores and EBITDA of INR 261 crores. The INR 900 crore QIP was used for about INR 340 crores of debt repayment, roughly a third for existing project execution, and about INR 300 crores earmarked for new acquisitions, of which only about INR 54 crores (call also cited ~INR 50 crores) was deployed. The company acquired controlling interests in three Kanjurmarg entities (~INR 70 crores investment) with a six-project pipeline of over INR 840 crores GDV, and took a 90% stake in Sunset Spaces Pvt Ltd. The amalgamation has received no-adverse-observation letters from BSE and NSE and documents have been filed with NCLT, with hearing awaited.

segments.name: Marathon Futurex (Lower Parel, commercial)
segments.commentary: Presales rose 15% YoY to INR 466 crores on leasing and absorption; management says prices firmed about 15% YoY and rates rose 50-60% over five to six years. Inventory may take 12-15 months to exhaust.

segments.name: Monte South (Byculla, luxury residential, 40% revenue share)
segments.commentary: Presales of INR 391 crores in FY26. Tower B has OC up to the 45th floor, with the 45th-65th floors topped out and expected complete by December 2026. Tower C is built to 17 floors; Tower D is unlaunched; a commercial Tower 5 may launch in 12-18 months.

segments.name: Marathon Nexzone (Panvel)
segments.commentary: Presales of INR 104 crores. Phase 3 launched with about 4.9 lakh sq ft carpet area and INR 600 crores GDV. Phase 2 towers Antilia, Triton and Atria received full OC.

segments.name: Neo series (Bhandup)
segments.commentary: NeoValley, NeoPark, NeoSquare and Bhandup projects together recorded about INR 65 crores presales; NeoSquare received OC. Newly launched Neohome has INR 370 crores GDV.

segments.name: Mulund Millennium (commercial)
segments.commentary: Contributed about INR 21 crores presales in FY26 from small offices and retail spaces.

segments.name: Kanjurmarg (acquired, PTC/B2B model)
segments.commentary: Six residential projects with GDV over INR 840 crores; one project at 5th slab of a 23-storey building; about INR 225 crores+ of GDV to launch within 12 months. Company holds 50% controlling interest and one-third economic interest in the transit camp model.

guidance_outlook: Management expects EBITDA margins of 30-40% on the Kanjurmarg projects, in line with current company margins.
Remaining INR 250 crores-odd of the INR 300 crore new-project allocation is yet to be spent on acquisitions.
Monte South Tower B floors 45-65 expected to complete by December 2026, adding to revenue recognition.
Post-merger, around 418 acres of land is expected to come into the listed entity; management cited Panvel plotted development possibly launching in FY27 or FY28.
Bonus issue timing is uncertain; management said it may or may not happen after amalgamation.
Strategic focus for FY27: accelerate execution, expand presales, pursue redevelopment and acquisitions, scale PTC-led B2B vertical, maintain prudent capital allocation.
capex_capacity: Unsold value of the listed entity (MNRL share) around INR 6,500 crores, plus the INR 840 crores Kanjurmarg pipeline; the company said this covers about five years of inventory.
Unsold launched inventory is about INR 2,000 crores, with cost to complete about INR 1,600 crores.
Management's thumb rule: unsold/unlaunched projects need about 60% of cost still to be spent.
Revenue recognised on percentage-of-completion basis; completion percentages are shown in the presentation.
demand_pricing: Management says Grade A office demand in South and Central Mumbai is strong; supply is lower than before, and Futurex prices firmed about 15% YoY.
Futurex serves more than 300 institutional and leasing clients, including Nykaa, ZEE, L'Oreal, SBI and HDFC; leasing ticket sizes start from 1,500-2,000 sq ft.
Luxury segment inventory at premium addresses is said to be tight, supporting pricing at Monte South.
Infrastructure tailwinds cited: Navi Mumbai airport, Atal Setu, Panvel-Karjat rail, EduCity, Kharghar commercial complex, GMLR (Goregaon-Mulund Link Road) and Dombivli bullet train station.
BMC cleared 384 unauthorised structures in Mulund, Amar Nagar and Khindipada for the eastern GMLR section (about 12 km).

qa_highlights.question: Launch timelines, capital deployment and margins for the Kanjurmarg projects?
qa_highlights.answer: GDV is over INR 840 crores and could go higher depending on PTC or pre-sale model. About 10% is ongoing; more than INR 225 crores will launch within 12 months. Expected EBITDA margins are 30-40%.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the amalgamation?
qa_highlights.answer: No-adverse-observation letters received from BSE and NSE; all documents filed with NCLT. Company awaits the hearing; stakeholder meetings to be dispensed with given NOCs.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR 900 crore QIP be allocated?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 340 crores repaid as debt, about one-third for existing project execution, and about INR 300 crores for new acquisitions. More than 30 projects evaluated; about three shortlisted; two acquired (Sunset Spaces and Kanjurmarg).

qa_highlights.question: Will commercial share of the portfolio increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to balance the portfolio by adding a new commercial project as each is sold; Monte South Tower 5 is a future commercial project.

qa_highlights.question: Remaining balance-sheet and unsold inventory question for Monte South and the 50% share?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue is recognised on percentage of completion; sold area's revenue is recognised per completion, and unsold value is yet to be recognised. Tower A delivered, Tower B has OC to 45th floor, Tower C launched with 17 floors built, Tower D unlaunched.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be a bonus issue after amalgamation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it cannot commit; policy has been bonus after a few years, and currently 97% of capital is bonus capital.

qa_highlights.question: Demand outlook for premium office assets in South and Central Mumbai?
qa_highlights.answer: Samyag Shah said demand is very strong, supported by both institutional sales and leasing; Futurex inventory could last 12-15 months and a new commercial portfolio is planned.

risks_watch: Kanjurmarg pipeline (GDV INR 840 crores+) is not yet launched beyond the ongoing project; launch timing relies on the next 12 months.
Amalgamation depends on NCLT approval; timing of hearing not specified.
About INR 250 crores of the INR 300 crore acquisition allocation remains unspent.

Collections in Q4 (INR 203 crores) were well below booking value (INR 156 crores) only in the sense of lower bookings; FY26 collections of INR 781 crores vs INR 576 crores presales should be tracked for sustainability.
Cost-to-complete of about INR 1,600 crores on launched inventory will need funding from the balance sheet.
Monte South Tower B completion and Tower D launch timing are key delivery milestones.
503101|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and promotional on growth, pipeline and demand; management was specific on numbers but gave no firm timelines on the amalgamation, bonus issue or new launches, and repeatedly qualified forward-looking statements.
key_quotes: I am proud to share the company has reported its highest ever profit in its history with profit after tax of INR 206 crores for the full year.
We try to balance our portfolio. So as soon as one commercial portfolio gets completed and sold, we try to add a new one.
That's very difficult to say right now. I mean Marathon has always had a policy of declaring bonus after a few years.

financial_highlights.change: Described as highest ever in company history

financial_highlights.value: approx. 48,000 sq ft (Q4) / approx. 2,29,000 sq ft (FY26)

503101|2026-06.headline: Marathon Nextgen Q1 FY27 total income hit INR 217 crores, a multi-quarter high, with PAT of INR 52 crores and INR 900 crores of new redevelopment GDV added.
503101|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 total income of INR 217 crores (multi-quarter high), EBITDA of INR 66 crores and PAT of INR 52 crores. Sales on the existing portfolio were 38,000 sq ft with booking value of INR 86 crores and collections of INR 118 crores (MNRL's 40% share of Monte South); including the merged portfolio, sales were 46,000 sq ft, booking value INR 108 crores and collections INR 146 crores. Two redevelopment projects (Versova and Sewri, INR 450 crores GDV each) were added, and the company says it is debt-free with about INR 200 crores of acquisition capital after a INR 900 crore QIP. The merger with group entities is awaiting NCLT shareholder and creditor meetings in early September 2026.

segments.name: Monte South (Byculla, JV, 40% stake)
segments.commentary: Sold ~35,000 sq ft with booking value INR 125 crores and collections INR 140 crores. Tower A has OC; Tower B has RCC to 65th floor and part OC to 45th floor, with balance OC expected this FY; Tower C RCC at 28th floor.

segments.name: Marathon Nexzone (Panvel)
segments.commentary: Sold 14,000 sq ft with booking value INR 17 crores and collections INR 43 crores. Full OC received for Cedar and Daffodil towers, enabling handovers.

segments.name: Bhandup (NeoPark, NeoSquare)
segments.commentary: Sales of 8,000 sq ft with booking value INR 14 crores and collections INR 9 crores. NeoSquare has OC; NeoValley and NeoPark under construction per schedule.

segments.name: Commercial (Futurex and Millennium)
segments.commentary: Futurex combined sales ~4,000 sq ft, booking INR 19 crores, collections INR 23 crores; Futurex has OC. Millennium sold over 1,000 sq ft, booking INR 3 crores, collections INR 1 crore; under construction.

segments.name: PTC (Permanent Transit Camp) vertical
segments.commentary: Started after Kanjurmarg land acquisition in Q4 FY26, focused on Bhandup; no presales yet, but management expects some in coming quarters.

guidance_outlook: Management said FY27 outlook is positive and better than last year, but declined to give forward numbers; bookings from newly launched Bhandup and Panvel phases expected to show in coming quarters (booking recognised on registration).
Collections this year expected to be on the heavier side, supported by ready-to-move inventory (about 3-month TAT on sales at Futurex and Monte South) and percentage-completion receipts.
Surplus capital of about INR 200 crores expected to be fully deployed into new projects this FY27.
Target EBITDA margin of 30-35% for project acquisitions.

Merger: shareholder and creditor meetings planned for first week of September 2026, followed by a second NCLT hearing; completion timing uncertain, dependent on NCLT dates (management said it was not sure whether it would complete by December).
capex_capacity: Upcoming pipeline GDV: Monte South Commercial ~INR 3,400 crores; Monte South Residential Tower D ~INR 1,600 crores; Marathon Neo Series (Bhandup) ~INR 2,800 crores.
Existing portfolio estimated unsold GDV ~INR 8,000 crores.
Redevelopment additions: Versova (via subsidiary Sunset Spaces, ~1.5 acres, GDV >INR 450 crores, first society redevelopment) and Sewri (cluster redevelopment JDA, ~7,500 sq m, GDV ~INR 450 crores).
Merger to bring over 400 acres of land, several ongoing projects and ready inventory at Futurex into the listed entity.
Panvel-Karjat corridor deadline cited as December 2026; Monte South commercial to launch ~5 minutes from Futurex.
demand_pricing: Management cited strong demand at Monte South (footfalls up sharply), commercial space (limited Grade A supply near Futurex), and newly launched Bhandup and Panvel phases.
Ready-to-move inventory at Monte South Towers A and B is sold at a premium, per management.
Redevelopment selection: prime locations and strict financial metrics; management said it avoids high-premium deals that may get stuck.
PTC demand from neighbouring redevelopment projects in Bhandup; area serves western suburbs (around Malad, P-South ward), Mulund, Ghatkopar and parts of Chembur.

qa_highlights.question: What are the launch timelines for the INR 900 crore redevelopment GDV, and how much more can be added in 12-24 months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the two new projects (Sewri and Versova, INR 450 crores each) add INR 900 crores in the quarter; no launch timeline or further 12-24 month addition was quantified.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 business outlook and which projects will drive acceleration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give forward numbers but said the outlook is positive and better than last year, citing Monte South, commercial, and new Bhandup and Panvel phases, with bookings flowing in later quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How will collections trend over the next 2-3 quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Ready-to-move sales at Futurex and Monte South convert to collections in about 3 months; Monte South Tower C is at the 28th slab, with about 40% collection on that basis. Collections expected to be heavier this year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income fall this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: A Futurex investment-property floor was not sold in the quarter, so no rental/sale income was recognised from it.

qa_highlights.question: Will the amalgamation complete by December 2026 or slip into 2027?
qa_highlights.answer: Shareholder and stakeholder meetings are planned for early September, followed by a second NCLT hearing; management said it is not sure of the timeline because NCLT benches are heavily loaded.

qa_highlights.question: How large is the redevelopment pipeline beyond INR 900 crores, and how are deals selected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Mumbai redevelopment opportunity is very large; selection focuses on prime locations and strict margin thresholds, and it avoids over-priced deals that can stall.

qa_highlights.question: How much capital will be deployed in FY27 and what return thresholds apply?
qa_highlights.answer: Target EBITDA margin 30-35% on acquisitions; about INR 200 crores of surplus capital to be fully deployed this FY.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PTC vertical's pipeline and outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: PTC business started after the Q4 FY26 Kanjurmarg land acquisition; strong demand from neighbouring redevelopments; presales may start in next few quarters.

financial_highlights.change: Futurex investment-property floor not sold in quarter

So the numbers of this year, of course, I mean, I won't be able to answer in terms of future-looking things.
We are not sure about that because that depends on the NCLT's available dates and processes that NCLT follows.
We have always had our EBITDA margins of 30-35% as a target for acquiring projects.
