demand_pricing: Consumer division: Q4 FY26 revenue INR50.9 crore (vs INR48.5 crore) and FY26 INR183.5 crore (vs INR179.4 crore, about 2% growth); management said demand is improving on expanded distribution, innovation and new launches.

Consumer channel mix: about 50% modern trade, 40% general trade and 8-10% army/CSD; general trade covers about 50,000 outlets directly, with presence in about 25 of them. Food products are roughly 10% of consumer sales and edible oils roughly 90%.
Consumer margin: division EBITDA margin about 8.3%; management said food categories are profitable from year one or two and no loss-making categories are pursued.

Bulk division: Q4 FY26 revenue INR100 crore (vs INR56.1 crore) and FY26 INR198.3 crore (vs INR158.6 crore); Q4 EBITDA INR2.7 crore vs INR0.9 lakh a year earlier. One solvent extraction plant in Pilibhit shut for non-viability.

Ethanol demand: PSU OMC cycle-one order for ESY 2025-26 (to 31 October 2026) is 47.9 crore litres, about 150 KLPD at 330 operating days, versus 130 KLPD earlier. Management said PSU OMCs are about 90% of the market and private OMCs about 10%; fresh tenders expected by end-June 2026. Rebidding for next cycle from 1 November, in September-October.
risks_watch: Ethanol overcapacity and underutilisation across the industry, with management saying the surge in capacity happened over the last three years; watch PSU OMC and private OMC tender volumes from end-June 2026 and the 1 November rebid.
Export policy for 1G ethanol and whether the expanded plants will be authorised for exports; management declined to speculate and said policy would come over the next few weeks.
Ethanol margin sustainability: Q4 included an exceptional item and softer grain prices; management guides 12-15% long-term, versus about 17% for FY26.
Consumer execution risk and growth reacceleration after about 2% FY26 revenue growth; monitor Q1 FY27 consumer revenue against Q4 FY26 INR50.9 crore.
Pending food-sector acquisition: management said nothing is firmed up yet, so timing and size are unknown.
Auditor transition: management said the change was a planned succession, but the resignation was reported recently; monitor the new auditor's appointment and any further disclosures.

519126|2026-03.headline: HFL posted record FY26 PAT of INR149 crores (+29% YoY) and guides FY27 PAT of INR200-220 crores, while cash flow lagged on working capital.
519126|2026-03.overview: Hindustan Foods delivered record FY26 profitability: total income rose 17% to INR4,264 crores, EBITDA 20% to INR377 crores, and PAT 29% to INR149 crores. Q4 FY26 total income was INR1,120 crores (+17% YoY), EBITDA INR104 crores (+28%), and PAT INR41.5 crores (+32%). Footwear was hit hardest by petrochemical and freight inflation in Q4 and expected to remain affected in Q1 FY27, while pass-through in other verticals continues. Management reiterated FY27 PAT guidance of INR200-220 crores but moved the GST inversion-driven shift from gross to net revenue recognition to Q2-Q3 FY27, and withheld sales and segment profitability guidance.

financial_highlights.metric: PBT before exceptional items Q4 FY26

financial_highlights.change: After normalising new and underutilised assets

financial_highlights.metric: Gross block incl. CWIP and advances (Mar-26)

segments.name: Footwear
segments.commentary: Sales expected at roughly INR500 crores in FY26 and INR700-800 crores in FY27 per management. Broke even in Q2 FY26 and said it is PAT positive, but Q4 margins were hit as polymer prices rose ~50-60% and freight rose; pass-through to customers is delayed and Q1 FY27 P&L expected to be affected.

segments.name: Ice cream
segments.commentary: Record volume growth in Q4 aided by season and new capacity. Panipat plant commissioned April 2026 (capacity ~20,000 tons vs ~35,000-40,000 tons made in FY26). Cone facility acquired and stick facility commissioned; INR50 crore brownfield expansion planned at Lucknow and Panipat.

segments.name: Beverages
segments.commentary: Record volume growth in the season. New bottling capacity in Aurangabad and South India due in FY27; targets becoming largest independent bottler in India by end FY27, operating as shared manufacturing. INR50 crore investment signed for FY27.

segments.name: Home and Personal Care
segments.commentary: Steady momentum in FY26. Aurangabad personal care facility integrated from 1 April 2026. Silvassa liquid detergent and Lucknow detergent bar projects expected operational in FY27. INR50 crore HPC investment signed for FY27. Management cites strong engagement in home care.

segments.name: Healthcare
segments.commentary: Added customers and completed several domestic and international audits; signed 3-4 new customers for the inherited facility (Baddi, acquired from Reckitt, ~INR220 crore difference between paid and book value). Establishing dedicated ayurvedic wellness facility at Baddi. No revenue or profit figures disclosed.

guidance_outlook: FY27 PAT guidance of INR200-220 crores reiterated; management did not give sales guidance.
Target of 20% EBITDA growth and 20% ROE mandated for each of the five verticals.
Planned FY27 capex of about INR2,150 crores (gross block) with a 60:40 dedicated-to-shared split; INR150 crores of new contracts signed since April 2026.
Gross-to-net revenue recognition shift for some food businesses moved from Q1-Q2 to Q2-Q3 FY27; management says no impact on absolute EBITDA or PAT, but margins will look better.
Footwear profitability not guided; customer price pass-through expected to be concluded within about a month.
Management says EBITDA margin of 10% is achievable; PAT margin of 10% unlikely on a like-to-like basis.
capex_capacity: Gross block including CWIP and advances reached INR1,800 crores at March 2026; FY26 capex was above INR700 crores, with a gap of about INR190 crores against the earlier INR2,000 crore-odd gross block target.
Panipat ice cream plant commissioned April 2026 in under 10 months; about INR200 crores invested, earnings start FY27.
Silvassa liquid detergent and Lucknow detergent bar projects expected operational in FY27; new beverage bottling capacity in Aurangabad and South India due in FY27.
Baddi ayurvedic wellness facility under establishment, alongside modernisation at the existing Baddi facility; footwear capacity expansion across North and South India.
Management says underutilised assets of about INR508 crores are ramping up; ROCE threshold for new projects is about 18% IRR.
demand_pricing: Footwear polymer prices up roughly 50-60% and freight up; footwear is the only division where raw material pass-through is not immediate. Customers are reportedly supportive.
Most other businesses pass through raw material and packaging cost increases immediately.
Management sees strong customer engagement in home care, beverages and ice cream; export push for healthcare planned, with US modern trade talks under way.
Gross-to-net shift stems from GST inverted duty structure from September 2025: food inputs such as packaging attract higher GST than the 5% on finished foods.
Management declined to name customers, including Reliance's ice cream entry.

qa_highlights.question: Footwear FY26 sales and profitability, and FY27 targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said sales reached about INR500 crores in FY26 and expects INR700-800 crores in FY27. It declined to give a profitability target, citing raw material volatility and ongoing customer talks. CFO said the division broke even in Q2 and is now PAT positive.

qa_highlights.question: Gross block split between dedicated and shared facilities after completing capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Mayank Samdani said the split is about 61% dedicated and 39% shared currently and will stay in a similar range on INR2,150 crores of planned gross block.

qa_highlights.question: Which segment moves to net revenue model and what is the impact on revenue and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Sameer Kothari said this is mainly food, where packaging and some raw materials carry higher GST. The timeline slipped to Q2-Q3 FY27. Bottom-line EBITDA and PAT are unaffected, but margins will look better as sales fall.

qa_highlights.question: How will cost pressure in footwear not hit FY27 PAT guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said diversification across categories should offset footwear headwinds through more than compensatory growth elsewhere. It remains confident in the PAT guidance but cannot yet see how long the uncertainty will last.

qa_highlights.question: Segment-wise profitability and shared versus dedicated ROCE?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined segment EBITDA, promising disclosure by year end, and shared that the gross block by segment is in the presentation. Shared manufacturing targets higher ROCE than dedicated. Dedicated ROE targets are 16-22% pre-tax. Footwear is 100% shared.

qa_highlights.question: Financing of incremental capex given working capital pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Sameer Kothari said working capital credit has been secured across product lines and is not constraining capex. Net debt to equity is 0.84x with cash buffer, but management will be more cautious and not go all out on investments.

risks_watch: Footwear margin pressure from polymer and freight costs, with pass-through to customers not yet concluded and Q1 FY27 P&L expected to be affected.
Gross-to-net revenue shift (Q2-Q3 FY27) will reduce reported sales; customer agreement count was not disclosed and must be confirmed next call.
Working capital and inventory build pressured cash flow; cash flow was described as less than satisfactory.

Reconciliation gaps: net capital employed uses two-year average equity and net debt less cash; Baddi acquisition creates a roughly INR220 crore difference in gross block; investor query on reconciliation was deferred offline.
Only INR150 crores of new contracts signed since April 2026; FY27 capex achievement against INR2,150 crores depends on further announcements.
LPG shortage temporarily affected two factories.
519126|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the FY27 PAT guidance and the long-term 20% growth mandate, but cautious on footwear, sales guidance, cash flow and capex pace. Management was defensive on the reconciliation of capital employed and ROCE figures and deflected some questions to later calls.
key_quotes: So we should be about INR700 crores to INR800 crores of turnover as far as shoes is concerned in this FY27.

We will stick to the guidance of the PAT, which for next year, we've given a very clear guidance even last quarter, and we've reiterated it in this quarter, which is we are confident that we should be able to get to a PAT of between INR200 crores to INR220 crores for FY27.
this will not affect our bottom line numbers, whether it is of EBITDA or whether it is of the PAT in absolute way.

519126|2026-06.headline: Hindustan Foods Q1 FY27 PAT rose 33% YoY to INR42.8 crore, a record, while footwear cost pressure of ~INR6 crore weighed; FY27 PAT guidance of INR200-220 crore reaffirmed.
519126|2026-06.overview: Total income rose 18% YoY to INR1,207 crore and EBITDA rose 26% to INR106.3 crore, with PBT up 33% to INR56.6 crore. Footwear absorbed about INR6 crore of raw material, freight and minimum-wage cost pressure, with the Haryana wage hike the main driver. Management reaffirmed FY27 PAT guidance of INR200-220 crore and announced INR190 crore of new projects, taking FY27 commitments to INR340 crore plus INR150 crore carried forward. A Silvassa plant disruption from July rains is expected to be fully resolved by end-August.

financial_highlights.metric: Footwear cost pressure (raw material, freight, wages)

segments.name: Home & Personal Care
segments.commentary: Running at maximum capacity with a record quarter; Aurangabad personal care integration complete. Silvassa brownfield expected to start in Q2 FY27 and Lucknow greenfield later this year. INR50 crore Lucknow project (bar and liquid lines) announced.

segments.name: Food & Beverages
segments.commentary: Coimbatore, Nashik and Mysuru at record production; beverages had an excellent season. INR210 crore of beverage projects across Coimbatore, Mysuru, Goa, Aurangabad and Hyderabad, expected online by Dec/Jan. Greek yogurt facility being added in Goa.

segments.name: Ice Cream
segments.commentary: Strong summer with record volumes; Panipat facility commissioned in Q1. INR80 crore Panipat expansion announced; Nashik cone and ice cream utilisation improving with new customers.

segments.name: Footwear
segments.commentary: Q1 utilisation was poor due to imported material and freight disruption, and cost pressure hit margins. Management says utilisation is about 80-90% from August; order book full from Q2 FY27 and the business is expected to pay off in H2 FY27. Price pass-through now being achieved from Q1 onward per management.

segments.name: Healthcare / OTC Pharma
segments.commentary: Baddi site approved; commercial production started for 2 more multinational companies. Management expects Baddi to reach 100% utilisation within 6-12 months. Class III medical device certification started at Chennai.

guidance_outlook: FY27 PAT guidance of INR200-220 crore reaffirmed; management said it is too early to signal the lower end and will revisit in a couple of quarters.
Capacity commercialisation of more than INR500 crore expected in FY27 including carry-forward projects.
Management expects footwear to return to profitability in coming months and to pay off in H2 FY27.
Profit growth expected to outpace revenue growth because customers increasingly supply raw and packing material, so only conversion cost is booked as revenue.
Continued 1:1 debt-equity funding for projects; growth to rely on internal accruals with ROCE threshold of 18%.
capex_capacity: FY27 new project commitments of INR340 crore (INR190 crore newly authorised), plus INR150 crore carried forward from FY26.
Breakdown: Food & Beverages INR210 crore; Ice Cream INR80 crore (Panipat); Home & Personal Care INR50 crore (Lucknow).
Silvassa flood disruption from July rains: partially restored, fully operational by end-August; management says it is insured and has no material long-term impact.
Lucknow greenfield facility due for commissioning later in FY27; Silvassa brownfield to start in Q2 FY27.
Pipeline of inquiries about INR1,000 crore, not yet confirmed; policy is to announce capex only after signing.
demand_pricing: Footwear raw material prices rose ~50-60% (polymer, fabric) and freight rose up to 4x; footwear pricing is fixed 6-12 months ahead, so costs could not be passed through in Q1.
Haryana/NCR minimum wage hike of ~30% hit footwear and was described as a local, one-off issue; other contracts have pass-through clauses.
Footwear order book full for Q2 FY27 onward, with new domestic and multinational customer wins and some lapsed customers returning.
HPC demand has improved materially over the last three months per management, with liquid home care volumes growing near double digits.
US personal care order is on hold due to tariff ambiguity and freight; product development, trials and mould investment are complete.
Middle East export discussions (UAE, Saudi Arabia) put on hold; Dr. Scholl portfolio exported to UK, EU, Australia, NZ and Japan.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company negotiate better terms with customers given GST inversion and weakening competition, and is there any asset revaluation planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Sameer Kothari said GST inversion is not the main driver of outsourcing and that the company is better placed to handle it. Assets have not been revalued and the business model does not depend on it; the value sits on the balance sheet.

qa_highlights.question: Can footwear raw-material cost increases be built into contracts structurally?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said shoe contracts are set 6-8 months ahead with fixed prices, so mid-season changes are not industry practice. Brands have agreed to absorb some cost for the coming season, and pass-through is now being achieved.

qa_highlights.question: Break down the INR340 crore of new projects by segment.
qa_highlights.answer: Food & Beverages INR210 crore across five units, Ice Cream INR80 crore at Panipat, and HPC INR50 crore at Lucknow for a bar and liquid line.

qa_highlights.question: Footwear utilisation and order book quality?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 utilisation was poor; utilisation is about 80-90% from August with a full order book and new logos, with the business expected to pay off in H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Footwear employee cost share and profit impact of INR210 crore beverage capex at 18% ROCE?
qa_highlights.answer: Footwear employee cost is about 35-40% of Q1 total. Beverage units are expected online by Dec/Jan on anchor-tenant basis; the analyst's ROCE maths was corrected to EBIT, with 1:1 debt-equity funding implying interest outflow.

qa_highlights.question: Gross block growth outlook over 3-5 years versus sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross block will grow faster than sales because customer-supplied raw material means only conversion cost is booked as revenue. It expects to fund growth from internal accruals at 1:1 leverage with an 18% ROCE threshold.

risks_watch: Footwear margin recovery depends on brands absorbing cost and on Middle East-driven material and freight costs easing; ~INR6 crore hit in Q1.
Silvassa restoration by end-August and insurance recovery; watch for any Q2 output shortfall.
Execution of INR500 crore capex this year, and whether Lucknow and Silvassa start on time.
US tariff ambiguity keeps personal care export orders on hold.
Management declined to give plant-level utilisation for shared sites; footwear ROCE is below the 18% threshold, per management.
key_quotes: we delivered our highest ever quarterly PAT with a growth of nearly 1/3, 33% over last year.
we are confident that our customers will support us in mitigating the losses incurred due to these causes and that the division will return to profitability in the coming months.
I think it's too early to say that, Virat. We have continued to reaffirm our guidance.
I think the shoe business should finally start paying off in the second half of this financial year.
519126|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the core business and FY27 PAT guidance of INR200-220 crore, which was reaffirmed. Cautious and somewhat defensive on footwear: it is described as temporarily stressed, management repeatedly declined to give plant-level utilisation or category EBITDA, and it was reluctant to say GST inversion is a tailwind or to give a hit ratio on the project pipeline.

519183|2026-03.headline: ADF Foods Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue hit a record INR196.7 crore (+23.7% YoY), with EBITDA margin at 17.4%, but Middle East (GCC) exposure clouds FY27 guidance.
519183|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue rose 23.7% YoY to a record INR196.7 crore, with EBITDA of INR34.3 crore (17.4% margin, +190 bps) and PAT of INR25.9 crore (+57.6%). Standalone FY26 revenue grew 10.3% to INR527.9 crore with EBITDA margin of 24.8%. The Surat greenfield plant began commercial production in March 2026, but West Asia disruption stopped GCC shipments in March and April, and management cut its outlook to a conditional range if the disruption persists. Net cash surplus stands at INR78.2 crore and the final dividend is 30% of face value (60% for FY26).

segments.name: Ashoka (flagship brand)
segments.commentary: Management guided Ashoka to grow about 30-35% in FY27; FY26 Ashoka revenue was about INR308 crore per an analyst's calculation that management did not dispute. Core markets are North America (incl. Canada), UK and Europe, with Australia and New Zealand also growing.

segments.name: Truly Indian (mainstream US brand)
segments.commentary: Management expects Truly Indian revenue of INR75-80 crore in FY27 if things go well. Listed in about 3,000 US stores including Costco, Raley's, Safeway-Albertsons and Whole Foods; repeat rotations are seen at some Costco divisions.

segments.name: B2B and private label
segments.commentary: B2B and private label make up about 20% of revenue. Distribution business added new regional brands and Ashoka SKUs (staples, oils, flour), with SKUs rising from about 440 to about 600.

segments.name: GCC / Middle East
segments.commentary: About 15% of revenue (described as under 15%). Shipments were nil in March and about 80-85% of GCC business was lost, with only 1-2 ports operating in April.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of INR925-1,000 crore, conditional on West Asia stabilising within about a month; management said it would revisit guidance if disruption continues.
If GCC contribution stays at zero, FY27 growth is about 12-15% (roughly INR800-850 crore); with GCC normalised, growth of 30%+ and the INR925-1,000 crore band.
Surat plant expected to contribute INR40-50 crore revenue in FY27; full capacity implies upwards of INR200-250 crore (Phase 2 included), with full utilisation targeted in year 3.
Management expects to maintain high-teen consolidated EBITDA margins; Surat margins at full capacity expected to be similar to existing facilities.
Freight costs up about 3-4% of revenue in March; management said this is expected to ease over about the next two months. Analyst was told to add about 1 percentage point of freight in the base.
PLI incentive expected to be similar in FY27 (about INR16 crore) and is the final year of the scheme.
Capex of INR20-25 crore in FY27 (pizza base line, Surat balance payments), plus INR15-20 crore for Nadiad and Nashik debottlenecking; a further US warehouse is planned around Q3 FY27.
Potential INR30 crore quarterly revenue risk from GCC on a run-rate basis, as an analyst framed it and management confirmed.
capex_capacity: Approximately INR124 crore capex over the last 2 years across Nadiad, Nashik brownfield and Surat greenfield; Surat total investment including Phase 2 is a little above INR100 crore.
Surat Phase 1 (2 product lines) commenced production in the third week of March 2026; Phase 2 adds a product line (pizza base) in Q3 FY27.
Surat utilisation expected at about 35-40% in Phase 1 during FY27; Phase 2 contributes only 10-15% utilisation in FY27.
Average capacity utilisation across product lines was about 70-75% in FY26.
US warehouse: freezer space above 100% utilised (using outside storage); ambient space about 85% utilised. Another distribution centre planned, probably in Q3 FY27.
Debottlenecking at Nadiad and Nashik (flatbread and snack lines) drove most of the FY26 volume growth.
demand_pricing: Q4 FY26 growth was about 60-65% volume-driven, with the balance from product mix and rupee depreciation; management said prices were not increased.
Truly Indian initial traction is mainly distribution-led, with some repeats at Costco and other chains; management sees the Indian ethnic category at an inflection point in the US mainstream channel.
No impact seen from GLP-1 drugs (Ozempic) on demand; the whole range is vegetarian and vegan.
GCC shipments were nil in March 2026 because shipping lines were not taking containers. Other markets saw longer transit times and higher freight rates but no loss of sales.
Freight costs rose sharply in March 2026 as vessels were jammed and US routes lengthened; the company shares freight cost with GCC distributors 50:50 on those routes.
Tariff refund: applications filed for upwards of USD 1.5 million following a Supreme Court directive; nothing received in FY26, and any refund will be accrued in the year received.

qa_highlights.question: How does FY27 guidance of INR925-1,000 crore reconcile with the growth drivers, given Ashoka and Truly Indian?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the INR925-1,000 crore band, conditional on the Middle East reopening. Ashoka is expected to grow 30-35% and Truly Indian INR75-80 crore. With zero GCC, growth is 12-15% (about INR800-850 crore).

qa_highlights.question: What is the Middle East (GCC) impact and worst-case scenario?
qa_highlights.answer: GCC is under 15% of revenue. About 80-85% of GCC business has been lost, with nil March shipments. In the zero-GCC case, FY27 growth is about 12-15%.

qa_highlights.question: Surat plant ramp-up and revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 Surat contribution is INR40-50 crore; full capacity implies INR200-250 crore once Phase 2 is complete. Full utilisation is targeted in year 3.

qa_highlights.question: How much freight-cost increase should be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight rose by about 3-4% of revenue in March. The CFO said about 1 percentage point should be added to the base, with normalisation expected over about two months.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plans and total Surat spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Surat total is a little above INR100 crore. FY27 capex is INR20-25 crore (pizza line and balance payments) plus INR15-20 crore for Nadiad and Nashik debottlenecking.

qa_highlights.question: Will PLI incentive continue after FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 is the final year of the PLI scheme, expected at a similar level (about INR16 crore). The scheme covered 50% of marketing spend.

risks_watch: West Asia / GCC disruption: about 15% of revenue, with nil March shipments and only 1-2 ports open in April; guidance depends on normalisation within about 1-2 months.
Freight and logistics costs: March spike of about 3-4% of revenue; management expects normalisation but this is unproven.
Loss of PLI incentive after FY27 (about INR16 crore per year) will remove a support to margins.
Surat ramp-up: Phase 2 starts in Q3 FY27 and contributes only 10-15% utilisation in FY27; execution risk.
Freezer capacity in the US warehouse is above 100%, which requires outside storage and a new distribution centre.
519183|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the Q4 and FY26 results and on brand momentum, but cautious and conditional on guidance. Management repeatedly tied FY27 targets to a West Asia recovery and said it would revisit guidance if disruption continues; some answers on Middle East figures and the revenue bridge were vague.
key_quotes: So the Middle East has been -- I mean, because of the current situation in the month of March and April, we've not been able to service that market apart from a few ports because there are no shipping companies which are taking containers there.
So if the situation in the Middle East continues, of course, it will have an impact, and then we will look at revising our guidance.
The majority of the growth has come through with volume growth.
Surat total investment in Surat with Phase 2 completion will be a little above INR100 crores.

519183|2026-06.headline: ADF Foods Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 25.9% YoY to INR167.3 crore, but EBITDA margin of 17.7% was flattered by INR19.69 crore tariff refund; freight cost ~3% of revenue.
519183|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 25.9% YoY to INR167.3 crore, the fourth straight quarter of double-digit growth, with consolidated EBITDA up 26% to INR29.7 crore (17.7% margin) and PAT up 13.4% to INR17.3 crore. Management said the figures include tariff-refund benefit, and that adjusting for freight (~3% of revenue) the margin would be about 13.4% to 16.4% depending on the basis quoted on the call. Standalone revenue rose 20.5% to INR120.9 crore with EBITDA margin of 22.8%. Shipments were constrained by container and vessel shortages, with about 30% of ready goods unshipped in June, and management reiterated FY27 revenue above INR900 crore with high-teens EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Processed foods
segments.commentary: Revenue INR144 crore, up 28.5% YoY, with segment EBITDA of INR31.2 crore (21.6%). Management attributed the margin to product mix and frozen foods momentum.

segments.name: Distribution
segments.commentary: Revenue INR23.2 crore at 11.5% margin. Management said quarterly segment margins are seasonal and full-year margins will track historical ranges.

segments.name: Brands (Ashoka, Truly Indian, Soul)
segments.commentary: Ashoka growing above 30% in the latest quarter, with a 5-year revenue CAGR above 20%. Truly Indian is in 3,000+ US stores, with about 60% of growth from existing stores and 40% from new listings. Soul relaunch is still slow.

segments.name: B2B / private label
segments.commentary: Management put the sales split at about 75% own brands and 25% B2B and private label.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue upwards of INR900 crore, conditional on geopolitical and shipping conditions easing.
High-teens EBITDA margin guided for FY27 and beyond, excluding tariff refunds; management expects a return to 16-17% over about nine months as freight pass-through takes effect.
Freight pass-through began in Q1 FY27: about 75% in the US and 65-70% of total business overall, with some markets deliberately not passed on.
Surat revenue of about INR40-50 crore expected in FY27, with management saying the number is intact.
Surat full-scale utilisation expected in 2-3 years; about 30% utilisation this year and full utilisation around FY30.
Depreciation to rise by INR25-30 crore as Surat Phase 2 lines come in around Q3, with a further INR20-25 crore capex in FY27.
PLI scheme (about INR16 crore in FY26, about 2% of revenue) is in its final year; management hopes for an extension.
Q2 shipments expected to carry forward from Q1, but the carry-forward could slip into Q3 if container constraints persist.
Management said there are no further US tariff refunds expected; a USD2.8 million court award is under recovery discussion.
capex_capacity: Surat greenfield facility (frozen foods) began commercial deliveries and initial container shipments after commencing trial production in late March 2026; about 15 containers shipped in early Q1.
Surat at full capacity is expected to deliver a little under INR300 crore in revenue. Combined with brownfield capacity, total potential is about INR1,250 crore ex-agency at full ramp.
Phase 2 lines at Surat are expected in Q3, with residual capex of INR20-25 crore for FY27.
Management expects full utilisation of the combined capacity around FY30.
demand_pricing: Order book described as the strongest in company history for June, July and August, but about 30% of ready goods could not be shipped in June because of container and vessel shortages.
Management said consumer demand for ready-to-eat, frozen and shelf-stable Indian foods remains healthy across markets.
Pricing: freight costs passed through to customers from Q1 FY27 (about 3% of revenue impact). Tariff benefits will be passed back selectively by category to support market share.
Competition in Truly Indian is mainly from local US manufacturers of Indian-style foods, not Indian brands.
Management said the UK and Europe region should grow at high double digits, supported by a planned Ireland step-down subsidiary and FTAs.
West Asia disruption: March was very weak with no shipments; shipments resumed from end-April and are back near the 15% share of business previously affected.

qa_highlights.question: What is Surat's utilisation and when will it reach the INR275 crore target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said full capacity will take 2-3 years; about 30% utilisation expected this year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the freight impact on margin and what is sustainable margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight impact about 3% of consolidated revenue; margin ex-freight was about 16.4% and about 13.4% after adjusting for tariff refund. Guidance is high-teens, with freight pass-through supporting recovery.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR900 crore revenue target achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it remains cautiously optimistic, conditional on easing geopolitical and shipping conditions; the order book and demand support it.

qa_highlights.question: Treatment of the remaining tariff refund balance in the balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: The balance will be evaluated against customer arrangements and recognised over the next few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PLI contribution and its impact after FY27?

Price increases to offset raw material inflation (steel, grinding wheels, coolants, currency): about 10% achieved as of the call, with the aim of completing most of the pass-through over the current and next quarter.
Bharuch CRB/SRB plant expected to reach about 70% utilisation by July-August 2026, improving monthly after that.
Jamshedpur rail expansion (about INR120 crore capex): first production targeted for November-December 2026, with asset turns of about 2x to start.
FY27 capex expected at about 8-10% of revenue (management pegged last two years at about 8.5%), covering Jamshedpur rail, GGB plain bearings at Bharuch and some heat-treatment investment.
Management said the 65:35 domestic-manufactured to imported mix may hold for the next 2-3 years.
capex_capacity: Bharuch new plant: all lines capitalised; smaller lines and spherical lines running near full, large-line PPAPs under way, and CRB lines running close to two shifts. More than 100 new part introductions underway. FY26 revenue from the plant about INR80 crore (Q4 about INR60 crore, Q3 about INR12 crore). Management said the plant is still close to breakeven.

Bharuch total investment about INR720 crore including forex; buildings about INR350 crore; plant and machinery roughly INR310-320 crore by management's estimate. Peak revenue said to be close to 2x asset turns, but management ruled out INR1,000 crore.
Jamshedpur rail expansion: about INR120 crore capex, imported robotic machines from Europe, all approvals in place. Management said the building was built with spare capacity.
Plain bearing expansion at Bharuch and renewable energy investments are progressing; management said both are broadly on track.
Capital is debt-free; management said it will consider further expansion (0-8 inch range for CV and tractors, M&A) if the project is right.
demand_pricing: Management said demand is stable across most segments and is not among its top three concerns; cost escalation and pass-through, Bharuch ramp-up/PPAP, and expansion projects are the top three.
Steel MRO is slow and steel melt was lower in the quarter; cement MRO is good. OE sentiment is wait-and-watch because of geopolitics.
North America export demand is gaining momentum even without a signed US trade deal; the US is about 50% of exports, per the analyst.
CV demand described as robust with cyclicality; tractors okay; rail slow and steady; aftermarket okay.
Pricing: price increases began mid-April 2026 for both pass-through and recovery; about 10% realised, with automotive customers expected to delay. Management hopes for retrospective recovery.
Management said the Indian bearing market is about USD 2-2.5 billion (about 65% mobile, 35% stationary) and expects process and distribution to grow fastest.

qa_highlights.question: How much price increase has been taken to offset raw material inflation, and will there be margin pressure in the next 1-2 quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Price pass-through has only begun, at about 10%; management expects the rest over the current and next quarter, with the automotive OEM segment lagging. Management did not quantify the margin impact.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for domestic rail, CV, and US exports?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 exports were INR222 crore (up about 40% QoQ, up about 66% YoY for the full year); rail was INR278 crore in Q4 (slight YoY decline); CV described as robust.

qa_highlights.question: Bharuch utilisation targets and FY26 revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 revenue about INR80 crore; utilisation expected to reach about 70% by July-August 2026, then improve monthly.

qa_highlights.question: Segment split for Q4 and FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4: rail 26%, mobile others 19%, distribution 15%, process 19%, exports 21% (total INR1,073 crore including intercompany). FY26 total INR3,419 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Jamshedpur capex timeline and asset turns; FY27 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Production targeted for November-December 2026 at about 2x asset turns to start. FY27 capex expected at 8-10% of revenue; no formal capex guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: Dividend level?
qa_highlights.answer: The FY26 final dividend was INR2.5 per share on INR10 face value, down from INR36 previously. Management said it pays large dividends every 3-4 years and will consider the shareholder's request.

risks_watch: Raw material and currency inflation may outpace price recovery; only about 10% of pass-through was achieved at the call.
Bharuch ramp-up depends on PPAP and customer approvals, and the plant is still near breakeven; the 70% utilisation target is by July-August 2026.
Steel MRO softness and wait-and-watch OE sentiment amid geopolitical uncertainty.
Dependence on North American exports and the unsigned US trade deal.
Imported share of sales is about 35%, and the trading mix will remain exposed to currency moves.
Jamshedpur rail commissioning (about INR120 crore) is targeted for December 2026.
522113|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on demand and execution, but cautious on cost pressure and the Bharuch ramp-up timing. Management declined to give numerical FY27 revenue or margin guidance, and it acknowledged a slight delay at Bharuch.
key_quotes: So, margins and revenue both, we want to be more than the market growth.
And we hope between this quarter and next quarter, we should be able to pass it on.
So demand is not currently an issue.
I would say that 65%-35% might be there for next 2, 3 years, easy, but the pie will keep on increasing.

financial_highlights.metric: Q4 FY26 standalone revenue from operations

financial_highlights.change: Q4 FY25 margin about 21% (excl. one-off BAPA adjustment); margin up about 10 bps on like-for-like basis per management

522113|2026-06.headline: Timken India Q1 FY27 revenue rose ~15% YoY to INR929 crore, with PBT of INR150 crore and PBT margin of 16.2%.
522113|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR929 crore, up almost 15% YoY, after a seasonally strong Q4 FY26 (highest standalone revenue of INR3,147 crore for FY26). PBT rose to INR150 crore from INR130 crore, with PBT margin at 16.2% versus 16.1% a year earlier, and EBITDA margin at 19.6%. Gross margin was 39.9%, up 100 bps YoY and roughly flat QoQ, which management attributed to heavy-truck and off-highway price increases offsetting unfavourable Q1 mix. The Bharuch plant is ramping up quickly, with revenue of about INR50 crore in the quarter and near breakeven.

segments.name: Rail
segments.commentary: INR200 crore, about 22% of Q1 revenue. Management described government railway buying as slow and sluggish, and said the year started with about 3% growth in rail.

segments.name: Mobile / others
segments.commentary: INR184 crore. Management said mobile (tractors, heavy trucks) is about 20% of the business and is where price increases are sticking.

segments.name: Distribution
segments.commentary: INR153.9 crore (about INR154 crore).

segments.name: Process
segments.commentary: INR186 crore, up about 28-30% YoY, driven by metals customers and wind (gearbox exports and domestic wind farms).

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: About INR200 crore, including about 1% export incentive. Intercompany push to America rose about 21%; Europe is down, China and ASEAN are down, and the US is up.

segments.name: Bharuch plant (within segments)
segments.commentary: About INR50 crore revenue in Q1, close to breakeven. Spherical roller bearing (SRB) line utilisation was about 40-45% in Q1, targeted at about 70% by August-September; CRB line utilisation is lower, with ramp toward Q2-end and Q3.

guidance_outlook: Bharuch SRB line expected to reach about 70% utilisation in August-September 2026; CRB line ramp toward end of Q2 and Q3.
Rail expansion at Jamshedpur expected to start commercial production by calendar year-end 2026; management said it will ramp up immediately after that.
FY27 capex expected at about 8-10% of sales, with project work described as on track; timing may spill some capex into FY28.
Further cost escalation seen as limited beyond the steel, carbide, coal and grinding increases already in the system; base oil described as the only volatile input.
Management said it will continue to pass on cost increases to heavy-truck and off-highway customers as contracts renew; rail and PSU/ARC contracts are fixed and will reprice only at renewal.
capex_capacity: Bharuch plant ramping up; three manufacturing lines; utilisation cannot be given at plant level but SRB demand is higher than CRB at this stage.
Rail investment at Jamshedpur on track; plain bearings investment at Bharuch on track.
Manufactured vs traded mix roughly 75/25, similar to prior quarters.
Gas conversion from LPG to natural gas completed across supply chain and plants.
demand_pricing: Revenue growth driven by resilient core-segment demand and both export and domestic execution.
Steel producers raised prices by about INR1,500-1,600 per tonne in January and about INR3,500 per tonne by April, around INR5,000 per tonne in total; most customers have started paying the increase.
Price pass-through is working in heavy truck and tractor/off-highway; rail, PSU and cement customers are on fixed annual rate contracts.
Process growth partly from metals projects (mills built in India for export) and wind.
Management said the US market is up, Europe and China are down, and ASEAN and Australia are flat to down.
No direct tariff figure given; management said the US landed tariff has moved over time and it would confirm the current rate.
Management said the parent's 80/20 portfolio review is aimed at performance improvement; no change in Indian strategy was announced.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue split for Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Rail INR200 crore (22%), mobile/others INR184 crore, distribution INR153.9 crore, process INR186 crore, exports about INR200 crore including 1% export incentive.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of parent's 80/20 strategy and belts divestment on India?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 80/20 is a Pareto-based performance tool that is being applied globally; it is not yet a change in strategy for India. The India focus stays on off-highway, rail and tractor/heavy-truck, with no two-wheeler, passenger car or washing-machine ball bearings.

qa_highlights.question: Bharuch ramp-up and utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 Bharuch revenue was about INR50 crore, close to breakeven. SRB utilisation was about 40-45% in Q1, expected to reach about 70% by August-September; CRB is lower with ramp toward Q2-end and Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Drivers of process and export growth and US outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Process grew about 30% YoY, from metals and wind. Exports to the US are growing, Europe is down, and the intercompany push to America is about 21%.

qa_highlights.question: Rail outlook and Jamshedpur ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Government railway procurement is slow due to funds diverted to infrastructure and defence; management expects this to be timing-related. Jamshedpur rail capacity is due to start commercial production by calendar year-end.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the cost inflation has been passed through to price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is hard to give an exact percentage; heavy truck and tractor customers have largely passed through cost escalation, while rail and PSU contracts will reprice at renewal.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 capex plan and allocation?
qa_highlights.answer: Plant-wise split not given; capex directionally in line with the 8-10% of sales range, with some timing spillover into the next fiscal.

risks_watch: Steel and other input cost inflation: about INR5,000 per tonne of steel price increases; pass-through is incomplete for rail and PSU contracts that are fixed until renewal.
Slow government railway procurement due to fund diversion to infrastructure and defence; it could delay the Jamshedpur ramp-up benefit.
Bharuch ramp-up needs to reach about 70% SRB utilisation by August-September and CRB later; any slippage would weigh on margins.
Parent's 80/20 review and divestments (belts, automotive OE): the Indian implications are unclear, and management said it will review which assets can be used for growth in India.
Export exposure to geopolitics; Europe, China and ASEAN are down; US tariff status was not confirmed on the call.
Base oil price volatility affecting grease costs; the Brent outlook and the Middle East conflict affect energy and gas costs.
NCLT approval of the Timken GGB Technology merger is pending.
key_quotes: We have delivered high double-digit revenue growth this quarter Y-o-Y, driven by resilient demand, especially in the core segments, and our execution both for export and domestic.
So, the revenues are growing with every passing week, and I will ask Sujit to add more colour to the whole thing so that you get a little bit more specific answer.
So railway is a little bit sluggish as we speak, but it is an issue of time, so it will come back.
It is tough to tell you exactly percentage. Different customers, different behaviour.
522113|2026-06.management_tone: Management sounded confident on Q1 execution, Bharuch ramp-up pace and cost pass-through in heavy-truck and tractor markets. It was cautious and deferred on exact price-recovery percentages, rail timing, US tariff rate and future cost escalation tied to the Middle East conflict and Brent.

522163|2026-06.headline: Diamond Power Q1 FY27 revenue rose 129% YoY to INR690 crores and PAT rose 191% to INR58.5 crores, with FY27 revenue guided at INR4,300–4,500 crores.
522163|2026-06.overview: Consolidated Q1 FY27 revenue was INR690 crores (up 129% YoY), EBITDA INR85 crores (12.3% margin, up ~200 bps) and PAT INR58.5 crores (8.5% margin). Management attributed the quarter's softness versus a normal Q1 to early, heavy monsoon flooding in Gujarat that hit medium and extra high voltage cable laying. The company completed a INR1,640 crore QIP (net INR1,614 crore), turning net worth positive at INR691 crore post-QIP from negative INR922 crore at June 30, 2026. Order book stood at INR3,688 crore as on August 11, 2026, and management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR4,300–4,500 crore and FY28 of INR7,500 crore.

financial_highlights.value: Negative INR922 crore at 30 Jun 2026; positive INR691 crore post-QIP
INR1,640 crore gross (INR1,614 crore net per Q&A)
INR3,688 crore as on 11 Aug 2026 (~$445 mn), across 12 product lines
financial_highlights.change: ~2x FY26 revenue; >INR1,000 crore fresh wins since April

financial_highlights.value: Negligible in Q1 due to carried-forward losses; benefit expected for at least two years

segments.name: Medium voltage (11–66 kV) and EHV (132 kV+) cables
segments.commentary: Largest order-book block; management targets moving mix up the voltage curve, with 66 kV and above EBITDA guided at 18–22%. A INR435 crore data center order sits in this band.

segments.name: Low voltage (1.1 kV) cables
segments.commentary: Q1 mix skewed toward LV and conductors because MV/EHV cannot be laid in flood conditions; LV EBITDA guided at 8–9%. New copper LV facility (brownfield, ~42,000 km capacity, revenue potential ~INR1,880 crore) targeted for FY28 commercial production.

segments.name: Conductors (incl. HTLS, AL-59)
segments.commentary: Conductor EBITDA guided at 9–10%. Management says AL-59 is now ~70% of the market and Diamond has stopped producing ACSR.

segments.name: Export
segments.commentary: Currently negligible. Team being built; certifications for Europe and US in progress. Internal target of INR500 crore export order book by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Timing of the fourth rod mill, the incremental silane line and the CCV line, and sixth CCV line delivery.
qa_highlights.answer: Rod mill by 15 Oct, silane line by 15 Sep, CCV line in March 2027; sixth CCV line to be ordered this month, delivery assurance for August 2027 and commissioning by December 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Net worth and use of QIP proceeds.
qa_highlights.answer: Net worth was negative INR922 crore at 30 June 2026 and is positive INR691 crore after the INR1,614 crore net QIP proceeds. Planned use: INR130 crore LV expansion, INR74 crore balancing equipment, INR325 crore general corporate purposes, INR350 crore promoter unsecured loan repayment, with about INR750 crore for working capital.

qa_highlights.question: Recovery expectation on the INR957 crore legacy receivables.
qa_highlights.answer: A special team is evaluating recovery; management expects about INR300 crore to be recovered over 12–18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Depreciation outlook after the audit qualification was resolved.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 depreciation will be the run-rate going forward, with pro-rata additions for new capex.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 phasing and utilisation for cables and conductors.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ramp will be gradual, with Q2 partly affected by rain and Q3–Q4 the strongest; utilisation is guided at ~40% for conductors and ~50–52% for cables in FY27, rising to ~60% each in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: EBITDA margin guidance and metal price sensitivity.
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is 11–13% EBITDA margin, depending on metal prices; management cited aluminium moving from about $3,800 in May to about $3,000 by end-June. Mix is expected to improve as MV and EHV volumes rise in Q2–Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Long-term debt and peak debt outlook.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no substantial debt, the INR400 crore promoter unsecured loan has been repaid post-QIP and the INR1,900 crore promoter-held bonds are 0.01% payable after 30 years, with a net present value of INR47 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Peer comparison given the flat Q-o-Q revenue.
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the Q1 softness to MV/EHV being laid at project sites that cannot be laid in rain, and said the peers' business is largely LV, so the cycle hits Diamond more.

qa_highlights.question: Customer concentration, including Adani.
qa_highlights.answer: Adani is about 40%+ of the order book, with a Board mandate to cut it to about 20% by year-end; the company is engaging about 670 active customers.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue mix at the INR14,000 crore peak and what could go wrong.
qa_highlights.answer: Conductors 30–35%, LV 10–15%, MV/EHV the remainder; data center target 20%, exports not yet sized beyond INR500 crore order target. Key risks are metal and polymer price moves requiring 20–30% more working capital, and execution capacity.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guided at INR4,300–4,500 crore, with management saying it is firmly on track and intends to hold the Q1 margin profile while delivering it.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 11–13%, dependent on metal prices; management said the absolute contribution stays steady under price-escalation contracts.
Q1 seasonality: management said an on-time monsoon would have added INR70–80 crore of top line and corresponding EBITDA in Q1.
FY28 revenue target of INR7,500 crore; management said the full-utilisation potential of INR14,000 crore is not expected in FY29.
Data center sales targeted at about INR750 crore in FY27 and INR1,500 crore in FY28 (about 20% of revenue); internal target of INR1,000 crore data center orders before 31 Mar 2027.
Export order book target of at least INR500 crore by year-end FY27; management said export guidance beyond this will be given after year-end.
Management said it expects around INR300 crore of legacy NCLT receivables (out of INR957 crore) to be recovered over 12–18 months.
capex_capacity: Two aluminium corrugation lines approved by the board for 66 kV and 132 kV cable capacity; capex about INR17 crore, achieved by converting one 33 kV line.

Sixth CCV line being ordered this month at an agreed price; delivery assurance for August 2027, commissioning expected by December 2027 with no additional civil or utility capex. Management said it triples capability in the target segment.

Two additional medium voltage cable lines under installation, said to be on schedule; one silane line expected by 15 Sep 2026, fourth rod mill by 15 Oct 2026, and one CCV line in March 2027 (per Q&A).

Copper LV and control cable facility converting old rod mill and legacy conductor plant (brownfield, no civil cost), about 42,000 km capacity and revenue potential about INR1,880 crore at full utilisation; commercial production FY28, commissioning before March 2027.

Capex per line per Q&A: silane line INR15–20 crore; CCV line about INR50 crore for the line plus about INR50 crore utilities and civil (about INR100 crore total), with revenue of about INR45–50 crore per line. Utilisation guided at conductors ~40% and cables ~50–52% in FY27, rising to ~60% each in FY28.
demand_pricing: Order book INR3,688 crore as on 11 Aug 2026 across 12 product lines, about 2x last year's revenue; over INR1,000 crore of fresh wins since April and about INR400 crore of orders in the last 6–7 days.
Order intake guided at INR275–325 crore per month; management said about INR2,800 crore of the book is to be executed before March 2027.
Adani Group share of the order book about 40%+, with a Board mandate to bring it to about 20% by year-end; around 670 active customers and 200+ in the current order book.

Gujarat disaster-management programme (Robust) estimated at INR22,000 crore over three years, of which INR16,000 crore is 11 kV and 33 kV MV cable; Rajesh Power 1,370 km order from Paschim Gujarat; management expects INR4,000–5,000 crore of Gujarat orders to be finalised by year-end.

Mix: management said MV and EHV cannot be laid in flooded sites, so Q1 skewed to LV and conductors; management said peers are mostly ~85% LV, whereas Diamond is ~70–80% MV/EHV. Conductor: AL-59 now ~70% of the market and Diamond has stopped making ACSR.
risks_watch: Phasing: FY27 guidance of INR4,300–4,500 crore implies INR1,200–1,250 crore per quarter for Q2–Q4 against INR690 crore in Q1. Watch Q2 revenue.
Metal and polymer price volatility affecting gross margin and the pass-through lag; management's margin range is 11–13%.
Commissioning timelines: silane line (15 Sep 2026), rod mill (15 Oct 2026), CCV lines in March 2027 and December 2027; the new LV facility is due by March 2027 and commercial output in FY28.
Export certifications for Europe and the US; first export order targeted by Q3–Q4 FY27.
Working capital needs rising with metal and polymer costs and the need for vendor and dealer financing.
Customer concentration: Adani at 40%+ of the order book against the 20% target.
Monsoon and project-site disruption affecting MV/EHV laying in Q2 (described as partially affected).
key_quotes: We are completely back-to-back on passing the increases in metal and polymers to all our customers.
Our guidance is between 11% to 13%. This again depends upon the metal price.
The EBITDA guidance for the next year, we are confident we will maintain it between what I am telling you today, but we will work on how to improve upon it.
So, the rod mill should start by 15th of October. The incremental MV silane line should start somewhere by 15th of September, and the CCV line will start in March 2027.
522163|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and expansive on demand, capacity and the FY27/FY28 targets, but measured on guidance specifics: the CEO-style speaker declined to give firm forward-looking assurances at the outset and repeatedly hedged margin and export numbers with metal-price and utilisation caveats. Tone was most defensive when addressing the Q-o-Q flatness versus peers and the Adani concentration.

522195|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 39.22% to ₹322.06 crore and EBITDA margin expanded to 26.80%, with management guiding ~30% growth to ₹500 crore gross revenue in FY27.
522195|2026-03.overview: Frontier Springs delivered FY26 revenue from operations of ₹322.06 crore (up 39.22%), EBITDA of ₹86.31 crore (up 73.80%) and PAT of ₹61.31 crore (up 76.88%). Q4 revenue was ₹82.54 crore (up 17.7% YoY, marginally above Q3) with EBITDA margin of 28.51%. Management guides FY27 gross revenue above ₹500 crore on an order book it put at ₹300-370 crore, and says it expects to hold margins at 23-24% or higher, while acknowledging steel-cost pressure could trim 1-2 points. Q&A centred on margin guidance, the FIBA product launch, air spring capacity and wagon tenders.

financial_highlights.change: up 17.7% YoY; marginally ahead of Q3 FY26
margin up 362 bps QoQ-stated as YoY in call and 462 bps YoY in call; call states both 362 bps and 462 bps

segments.name: Coil springs
segments.commentary: FY26 gross revenue cited by management as approximately ₹175 crore plus (analyst's recollection, confirmed as approximate gross figure). Management expects reasonable growth in FY27.

segments.name: Forging
segments.commentary: FY26 gross revenue cited as ₹60 crore plus. A new 6-ton hammer was installed; it currently runs one 8-hour shift against 16 hours of available capacity. Management expects the strongest growth here in FY27.

segments.name: Air springs (coach sets)
segments.commentary: FY26 gross revenue cited as approximately ₹150 crore. Capacity is 300 coach sets per month; output is 180-200 per month. Realisation cited at about ₹1.25 lakh per air spring, described as slightly improved.

segments.name: FIBA (failure indication and brake application system)
segments.commentary: New product with RDSO basic approval and patent done; trials on trains start now, with about 6 months to regular supply. Management sizes the market at ₹40-50 crore and expects ₹20-25 crore of revenue from FY27-28. Margin said to be similar to air and coil springs.

guidance_outlook: FY27 gross revenue target above ₹500 crore, described as around 30% growth, backed by an order book of ₹300-370 crore disclosed on the call.
Margin target of 23-24% for the year, with management saying 26-28% is possible; management conceded 1-2 points could be lost on existing tenders if steel stays firm.
Medium-term growth of 25% per year beyond FY27 was stated; management also said 20-25% average growth is achievable across the three product lines.
FY27 capex planned at ₹20-25 crore across all three divisions, after about ₹20 crore in FY26; no term loans taken in several years.

Q4 FY27 is expected to be the strongest quarter, with the 6-ton hammer contributing from the third quarter onward; management expects the first-half revenue run-rate to break out of the ₹80-83 crore band.
capex_capacity: Air spring capacity 300 coach sets per month, utilisation 180-200 per month (about 60-67%); final testing is the bottleneck, and two more testing machines are planned.
Overall plant utilisation about 70% per management; a new automated coil spring line from China is under negotiation.
A 6-ton forging hammer was installed in FY26, joining 1-ton and 3-ton hammers; utilisation is one 8-hour shift out of 16 hours available.
FY27 capex of ₹20-25 crore across coil, air and forging divisions, focused on capacity and less manpower-intensive automation.
demand_pricing: Management says the order book is ₹300-370 crore, mostly Railways. Orders come in daily, mainly small, and are not individually disclosed; the company agreed to post larger orders on the exchanges.
Railways' fixed-price contracts limit mid-contract price increases. Management is raising prices in new tenders to pass through steel and energy cost increases.
Railways' production plan for FY27 is about 6,000 passenger coaches and 1,200-1,400 locomotives, flat YoY; a large wagon tender is expected, with forging and springs supply.
Competition: no new spring or forging players, though more steel suppliers have been added by Railways, improving sourcing terms.
Q3 FY26 revenue was flagged as constrained by inspection delays, raw material delays and customer-side bottlenecks; the company is targeting a breakout above ₹82-83 crore per quarter.
Export: management said coil spring exports are not being pursued; forging exports to Europe and the US are being explored where margins are good.
Defence and non-rail forging (L&T, JCB, Caterpillar, cranes) are at sample or R&D stage; defence approvals are slow.

qa_highlights.question: What margin should be expected if steel prices stay high: 22-23% or 26-27%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 23-24% for FY27 'if not 26-28%', citing negotiations with steel and energy suppliers and price increases in future tenders.

qa_highlights.question: Why is there a gap between pass-through of commodity costs and the margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Existing tenders at fixed prices may be lower; if the year completes, margin could fall by 1-2 points, but management aims to hold current levels.

qa_highlights.question: Is there visibility for FY28-29 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific figure yet; management sees no order scarcity for 5-10 years and said growth of 25% is expected beyond FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Breakup of FY26 revenue by division and air spring capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Approximate gross figures: coil springs ₹175 crore plus, forging ₹60 crore plus, air springs ₹150 crore; air spring output 180-190 coach sets per month against 300 capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Why has quarterly revenue been stuck at ₹80-83 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Bottlenecks include delayed inspections by Railways inspectors and occasional raw material delays; management expects to break out in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FIBA opportunity and its FY27 contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Market of ₹40-50 crore; company is second indigenous source after imports, with 2-3 approved sources in total. Management expects ₹20-25 crore of revenue from FY27-28 once trials conclude.

risks_watch: Steel and energy costs: management concedes margin may fall 1-2 points on fixed-price existing tenders if steel stays firm.
Quarterly revenue has been stuck at ₹80-83 crore for three quarters; the FY27 ₹500 crore target depends on a sharp step-up.
Receivables are high at year end; management attributes this to high turnover and says there are zero bad debts. Next quarter's collections should be checked.
Timing of the large wagon tender and the FIBA trial and approval, both of which are needed for the second-half ramp-up.

qa_highlights.question: How are paste PVC and yarn prices trending, and is there an availability risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Prices rose significantly as a petroleum by-product and softened somewhat from March highs; availability is no longer an issue. Short-term impact is about a month because pass-through lags, while inventory averages it out long term.

qa_highlights.question: What were FY26 domestic and export growth, and the volume?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 value growth was 15% overall, with exports about 35.5% and domestic about 4%. Volume sold was 31 million meters, up about 4.5-5%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins rise to about 30%, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers cited were the export mix, currency gains, higher operating efficiency, cost control in other expenses and some March price pass-through. Management guided 25-26% as a base and said 25-30% is possible over the long term.

qa_highlights.question: Why was export growth guidance cut from 20%+ to 15-20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called 15-20% conservative and said export is running above that. Q4 general export was hit by a Middle East hold and US tariff effects, and the company is targeting new customers and platforms.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee expenses rise from INR 14 crore to INR 17 crore QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly a provisional impact of the new labour codes (effective 21 November 2025), booked in Q4 as a catch-up, plus some new hires.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan and capacity addition?

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 25% growth came from volume versus realisation?

qa_highlights.question: Why did margin fall sequentially from the previous quarter?

qa_highlights.question: Why hasn't gross margin improved despite a roughly 40% jump in export OEM?

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of the INR9 crore rise in other expenses QoQ?

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25-30% margin sustainable as a base?

522275|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 order intake of INR86.1bn (+188% YoY) lifted backlog to INR214.6bn; Q4 EBITDA margin hit a record 27.2%.
522275|2026-03.overview: GE Vernova T&D India reported a strong Q4 and full FY26, with revenue up 42% YoY in Q4 to INR16.4bn and 45% for the year to INR62.1bn. Profit before tax and exceptional items for FY26 rose to INR17.1bn from INR8.2bn, and the company ended the year with zero debt and about INR25bn of cash. Order intake was lifted by a large HVDC turnkey order from Adani Energy (VSC technology), and management guided to a mid-20s EBITDA margin for FY27. Management also announced a INR550mn disconnector and drives capacity at Vallam, Tamil Nadu, and a INR10 per share dividend.

segments.name: Domestic vs export
segments.commentary: Export orders in FY26 were about INR12bn versus INR32bn in FY25, which included one large export order; excluding large orders, base export orders grew 15-20%. Export was about 30% of FY25 revenue and new orders were about 92% domestic.

segments.name: Customer mix
segments.commentary: Backlog is 98% private customers, central utilities and PSUs; state utility exposure is under 2%.

segments.name: HVDC and projects
segments.commentary: A large HVDC turnkey order (Adani Energy, VSC) was booked in Q4, with execution mainly from FY28-29 onwards. Management does not disclose project versus product split.

guidance_outlook: Management endeavours to deliver mid-20s EBITDA margin going forward, after earlier guiding to low-20s and then mid-20s/high-20s in FY26.
Base order inflow expected to be around INR70bn (INR7,000 crore) and management remains confident of achieving it.
Two pending export RPT orders: a large export order where the decision is expected in H2 FY27, and a U.S. data-centre high-voltage order (about INR14-15bn) expected to be decided in Q1 FY27.
U.K. Grid Solutions purchase order (intra-group, feeding the Adani HVDC project) expected to be placed in the current quarter; it will not appear in the company's order book.
Capex of more than INR10bn to be phased from early FY27 through FY28, self-funded.
Management declined to give a split of Adani HVDC execution in early years; it said first two years would be lower than 30% and mostly engineering and supply-chain work.
capex_capacity: More than INR10bn of capex initiated across multiple product lines and facilities, to be phased through 2028.

INR550mn approved by the Board for new disconnector and drives capacity at Vallam, Tamil Nadu; disconnectors are being restarted for the Indian market, and some products will be global feeder factory output.
Air core reactor facility and HVDC thyristor valves and controls facility planned in India to raise local content.
Management did not give a revenue ballpark for the expanded capacity, citing that HVDC revenue depends on bought-out equipment and manpower rather than in-house capacity.
demand_pricing: Management says the TBCB pipeline has about 33 packages bid out, 21 of them at 765 kV; the only live HVDC tender is Barmer, whose bid deadline is being extended.
Data centres in India are about 1.5 GW installed, mostly at 220 kV; management expects a meaningful contribution once 400 kV and 765 kV data centres scale.
Transformer contracts carry price escalation clauses; for other products, cost inflation is built into tender pricing.
Management said Q4 domestic order finalisation was slightly dull, which it described as a conscious decision.

qa_highlights.question: Are export orders weak after FY25, and how will the RPT approvals translate into orders in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said excluding one large FY25 order, base export orders grew 15-20%. The pending RPT orders are a large export order (decision in H2 FY27), a U.S. data-centre order of about INR14-15bn (decision expected in Q1 FY27), and a U.K. Grid Solutions purchase order (intra-group).

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook for FY27 and what was the INR50mn Q4 other expense item?
qa_highlights.answer: Management maintains an endeavour toward mid-20s EBITDA margin. The Q4 other expenses included about INR500mn of notional mark-to-market loss on foreign currency derivatives; management agreed EBITDA would have been better without it.

qa_highlights.question: Is Prolec's U.S. low-voltage distribution strategy relevant to the Indian entity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said India has no distribution-transformer manufacturing set-up, and entering would need organic or inorganic capacity; it said it does not see that as a current strategy.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Adani HVDC execution profile and the Barmer/South Kalamb project share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said early-year execution would be lower than 30%, with most revenue from FY29. For Barmer-type projects, the supplier share depends on line length and scope, not a fixed rule of thumb.

qa_highlights.question: Will HVDC refurbishment projects move from LCC to VSC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said LCC-to-LCC refurbishment only requires valves and controls changes, whereas LCC-to-VSC is a wider scope with higher shutdown requirement and capex; it depends on customer choice.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company likely to sustain high margins and growth for longer?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cycle is broader this time, covering the U.S., Europe, Middle East and Australia, and that export exposure is meaningful; it did not give a timeline for margin moderation.

risks_watch: Customer decision delays on large export RPT orders (H2 FY27 for one, Q1 FY27 for the U.S. order) and their conversion to revenue.
HVDC pipeline timing: Barmer bid deadline keeps being extended, and the next project after Barmer is not clearly scheduled.
Execution of the Adani HVDC turnkey order depends on securing a supply chain, with revenue weighted to FY29 onwards.
Imports of HVDC components (thyristor valves, controls hardware) remain, so local content is still limited until the new facility comes up.
Foreign-exchange derivative mark-to-market charges can affect other expenses and quarterly EBITDA.
522275|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on demand, backlog and margins, but cautious on timing: management repeatedly declined to give quantified guidance on HVDC phasing, pipeline timing and export mix, and said quarterly order intake can be lumpy.
key_quotes: So, yes, we remain confident on achieving the base order number of INR7,000 crores.
Our order book remained strong in Q4, and we saw a booking of INR86.1 billion, up by 188% year-on-year compared to INR29.9 billion in quarter ended March '25.
During the fourth quarter, we achieved a record EBITDA margin of 27.2%.
So, this time, the cycle is different. The market is different and the longevity of the cycle looks to be more sustainable.

522275|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 38% YoY to INR18.4 billion, but order intake fell 30% to INR11.4 billion and gross margin slipped to 41.3%.
522275|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 38% YoY to INR18.4 billion and PBT rose to INR4.9 billion, with EBITDA margin at 25.1%, within the mid-20s guided band. Order intake fell 30% YoY to INR11.4 billion, mainly on weak TBCB realisations in Jan-Mar 2026, so backlog eased 2.5% QoQ to INR209.3 billion. Gross margin fell to 41.3% from 45.3% in FY26, which management attributed to lower export mix, lower execution savings on elevated commodity prices, and HV business ramp-up. Two large related-party (RPT) orders, INR3,000 crore and INR1,300 crore, were delayed or on hold, and the company still has no firm plan for surplus cash of about INR16 billion beyond announced uses.

qa_highlights.question: Are the INR3,000 crore and INR1,300 crore RPT orders being booked, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: None of the INR1,300 crore order is booked; it is expected in Q2 or Q3 FY27. The INR3,000 crore project is on hold at the customer over budget issues and would need fresh shareholder approval after the September AGM. Management said both are not lost.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there a jump in export orders, and what is the RPT pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Export pipeline improved on US utility demand for instrument transformers and 400 kV GIS opportunities. Management declined to comment on the new RPT pipeline beyond saying it will go to shareholders when projects become live.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin bridge from 45.3% FY26 gross margin to 41.3% in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: About 2-2.5 points from ramp-up of lower-margin HV business (offset at EBITDA level); 1-1.5 points from lower export share and a high-margin export order in FY26; and the rest from lower execution savings due to elevated commodity prices. EBITDA was 25.1%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the mid-20s EBITDA guidance intact, and how are commodity costs passed through?
qa_highlights.answer: Mid-20s EBITDA guidance for FY27 is maintained. Transformers have formula-based escalation; other turnkey work relies on forecast costs, so cost pressure shows up in execution 1-2 years out.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Power Grid TBCB timeline stretching to 24-30 months a problem?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not affect capacity utilisation; ordering cycles may lengthen by about 3-4 months for longer tenders.

qa_highlights.question: What will the company do with surplus cash?

qa_highlights.question: Chintan Shah: Having raised ₹2,500 crores against a ₹5,500 crore approval, will there be a further capital raise this year?

qa_highlights.question: Abhijit Tibrewal (Motilal Oswal): Are early delinquency trends in PL, business loans, LAP and CV showing any caution, given peer reports of early bounces among IT-sector salaried borrowers in South India?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no emerging stress: 6-MoB 30+ for the latest sourcing is 0.64% vs 1.05% in Q4; Stage 3 slippage improved ~13% and Stage 1 slippage ~5% QoQ; bounce rates are stable to lower; collection efficiency is ~99.6%.

qa_highlights.question: Abhijit Tibrewal: Among the six newer businesses, which has surprised positively and which has scaled slower, and has strategy changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Shopkeeper loans are the only product not being accelerated, given credit cost and ROA considerations. Gold has 460 branches with ~60 opened this fiscal. Education loans are around ₹144 crores monthly. CV and CD early vintages are performing better than historical data. Management also said agri and microfinance are not in the book.

qa_highlights.question: Abhijit Tibrewal: Cost of borrowing rose ~9 bps QoQ, so will it keep inching up?
qa_highlights.answer: Arvind Kapil said the increase is not a concern, citing NCDs at 25-30% of funding and a diversified borrowing mix. He said disbursement yield rose 50 bps this quarter after 40 bps last quarter, and the company should remain NIM accretive. No formal guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: Pranay Mehta (Investec): What growth and profitability can be expected over the next 8-10 quarters, and are more new products coming?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to the June 2028 exit ROA guidance of 3-3.5% from 1.98% today. It cited rising yields and better credit cost via calibration and collections. No specific new product launch was detailed.

qa_highlights.question: Pranay Mehta: Are NBFCs reporting stress in IT-sector distribution, and what is the company's view?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the six-product mix spans different economic cycles. Business loans are held at ~10-16% growth versus over 40% in used cars, and it will slow products where calibration needs it. It is watchful of macro indicators, and agri and microfinance are not in the book.

qa_highlights.question: Nischint (Kotak): Is the quarterly write-off run-rate of about ₹275-280 crores recurring, or is there a legacy element?
qa_highlights.answer: Shriram Iyer said write-offs have declined QoQ, the legacy portfolio is now immaterial, and write-offs should not rise. He confirmed ₹275-280 crores as the run-rate for the next few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Nischint: Is the fall in PCR (Stage 2 coverage near 18%) normalised, and what is the cost of funding outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: PCR is range-bound and is driven by product mix; the legacy high-ECL book has run off, and gold and education loan share increases will lower PCR over time. Sanjay Miranka said a small cost-of-funds uptick is possible but disbursement yield gains should offset it, with no NIM challenge seen. Gold LTV is 75%.

risks_watch: Opex/AUM may move 10-25 bps QoQ from gold branch clustering (~400 branch adds planned in FY27), which could offset ROA gains.
Cost of borrowing rose to 7.72% from 7.63%; management says disbursement yield gains will offset it, but no formal guidance was given.
Early-warning signals in salaried and IT-sector borrowers flagged by peers; management says none seen internally, so monitor 6-MoB 30+ and bounce rates next quarter.
Credit cost of 2.4% and write-offs of ₹275-280 crores per quarter must hold for the ROA trajectory; PCR is expected to remain range-bound.
Shopkeeper loans are deliberately held back, and business loans are growing only 10-16%, so the growth mix depends on prime PL, gold and education scaling.
Macro risk: management cites crude oil and fuel-price pressure on CVs and watches industry-wide retail stress; the 2028 exit ROA target of 3-3.5% depends on execution.
key_quotes: Our GNPA, which in finance companies, we do believe is a lead indicator , the GNPA for Q1 FY27 stands at 1.37% versus 1.44% in Q4FY27.
We did not just launch 6 businesses. We built 6 growth engines mounted on a single chas sis. That's important.
So write-offs have been reducing quarter -on-quarter and control over slippages because of the better collection efficiency.
So we don't see any challenge at NIM level.
524000|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on margins, asset quality and the 2028 ROA target, with management repeatedly describing the trajectory as structural. Cautious on opex/AUM (conservative 10-25 bps swings flagged) and deflects the IT-sector and cost-of-funds questions to data rather than offering firm guidance.

524000|2026-09.headline: Poonawalla Fincorp Q2 FY27: PAT up 22% QoQ to ₹375 crore, ROA 2.18%, credit cost down to 2.19%, AUM ₹74,008 crore.
524000|2026-09.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as an inflection point, with AUM up about 10.4% QoQ to ₹74,008 crore and PAT of ₹375 crore (up 21.8% QoQ). NIM plus fees rose 16 bps QoQ to 9.26%, while credit cost fell to 2.19% from 2.40-2.41% and GNPA fell to 1.20% from 1.37%. Opex-to-average AUM rose to 4.15% on frontloaded investments in collections, AI and gold branches, which management said sits within the 10-25 bps guided range. New products contributed 28% of disbursements, and the company is still building cross-sell.
