segments.name: Consumer durables
segments.commentary: Quarterly disbursement ₹606 crore vs ₹433 crore in Q1; 20,000 dealers across 360 locations.

guidance_outlook: Credit cost expected to keep sloping down and gradually stabilise; management said it is tracking better than plan, with a visible path over the next one to two years.
Opex-to-AUM expected to move on plan, with 300-400 branches invested in per year and gold branches breaking even in about 13 months.
Management targets a sustainable ROA with a 'peak' expected in about 2.5-3 years; a commitment on ROA by June 2028 was referenced.
A 25 bps lending rate increase was already passed through about a week before the call; pass-through of further hikes is expected to depend on product and market.

demand_pricing: Portfolio yield 14.08%, up about 45 bps QoQ; disbursement yield up about 20 bps QoQ after roughly 50 bps rise last quarter.
New products contributed 28% of disbursements (26% in Q1, 24% before that).
Management cites a gap of about 200 bps between portfolio yield and disbursement yield.

Management flagged possible fee compression from a proposed insurance commission regulation but said earnings could absorb it.

qa_highlights.question: How far has cross-sell progressed (products per customer now vs a year or two ago), and what is the target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a products-per-customer figure; said cross-sell has only just started and the metric will be more relevant in about a year, with improvement each quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How many new products are profitable, and what blended ROA is possible once they mature?
qa_highlights.answer: No product-level count given. Management said gold branches break even in about 13 months, new businesses are not yet at full ROA, and peak ROA is expected in about 2.5-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Where will credit cost settle, and how will product mix shift?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called 2.19% a first milestone that looks structural. CRO said 12 MoB 90-plus for origination post September 2024 improved by over 53% versus the book 12 months earlier, and credit cost is tracking better than plan.

qa_highlights.question: Sensitivity of borrowing cost to a 50 bps repo hike and fixed vs floating mix?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said cost of borrowing rose minimally during the tightening; NCDs are about 30% of borrowings and fixed-rate; pricing power allows pass-through. A 25 bps increase was already passed through.

qa_highlights.question: Trade-off between growth and profitability; sustainable ROA and the split of ROA gains between operating leverage and credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said all three levers (spread, opex-to-AUM, credit cost) contribute over the next two years. Quarterly opex may fluctuate because of AI investment; no specific split was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is asset quality improvement from underwriting or benign credit conditions? Are AI/ML models reducing loss rates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to proprietary models (30-35 models) and calibration. It cited bureau data showing consumer durable borrowers completing 9-month loans are about 40% better credit than industry.

qa_highlights.question: With most of the book under 12 months seasoned, why are write-offs still high, and what is the impact of the insurance commission regulation?
qa_highlights.answer: CRO said slippages were contained across stages and GNPA and write-offs are falling; core credit cost impairment is stable in absolute terms despite over 10% QoQ book growth. On insurance commissions, management said fee compression could be absorbed by lending spreads and operating leverage.

524000|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on credit cost, asset quality and ROA trajectory, repeatedly calling the 2.19% credit cost structural and the trend "strength-to-strength". More cautious on specifics: declined to give products-per-customer, product-level profitability counts, or a quantified insurance-commission impact, and deflected the write-off question to seasoning arguments.

524091|2026-03.headline: Carysil Q4 FY26 consolidated total income rose 16% to INR237 crores and PAT (after MI) jumped 42% to INR27 crores, with EBITDA margin at 20.3%.
524091|2026-03.overview: Carysil reported Q4 FY26 consolidated total income of INR237 crores (up 16% YoY), EBITDA of INR48 crores (up 33%, margin 20.3%, up 277 bps) and PAT after MI of INR27 crores (up 42%). For FY26, total income rose 14% to INR932 crores, EBITDA grew 30% to INR185 crores (margin 19.9% vs 17.3%) and PAT after MI rose 53% to INR98 crores. Management framed FY27 as a year of capacity expansion and execution, with a 250,000-unit quartz sink line due in Q4 FY27 and 70,000 units of stainless steel capacity commissioned on the call date. The company guided to 15-20% revenue growth and 18-20% EBITDA margin, while flagging freight, gas and MMA cost pressures.

qa_highlights.question: Why did stainless steel volumes grow about 50% YoY?

Price increases came in the later part of Q4 and were driven by higher crude-linked raw material and logistics costs; management said the spread is broadly unchanged because raw material costs were passed through.
Ethyl acetate spreads are better in April and May than in the March quarter, per management's confirmation.
Management said a Q4 inventory gain was not meaningful, as the price uptick came late in the quarter.
Management sees no supply problems on raw materials except for about one week in early March when crude-based chemicals and gas supply were disrupted.
Non-Ibu customers are mainly direct consumers rather than traders, which limits the upside from price moves.

qa_highlights.question: Greenfield land: timeline and capex quantum?

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q4 gross margin sustainable, or was it an inventory gain?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to efficiency, product mix and capacity utilisation, plus a late-quarter price rise; it said there was no meaningful inventory gain and that quarter-to-quarter prediction is risky.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 guidance being maintained or upgraded?

qa_highlights.question: Is the Ibuprofen margin under pressure, given a peer's stated plan to shut down?

qa_highlights.question: How much R&D spend, and what products are in the launch pipeline?

qa_highlights.question: Paracetamol utilisation and margin impact of the 3x capacity expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: The new 10,800 MT plant is at about 55% utilisation, targeted at 70-75% in FY27 and full in FY28; higher utilisation is expected to lower unit cost.

qa_highlights.question: US FDA status?

qa_highlights.question: Employee cost trend and guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Rise driven by variable pay provision and new plant headcount; employee cost guided at about 9-10% of revenue.

Paracetamol new-plant ramp (55% to 70-75%) needs to be delivered in FY27.
Heavy reliance on China-sourced starting materials (e.g. for Metformin) and on crude-linked supply.

524164|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on FY26 execution and FY27 targets, but cautious on near-term quarters, repeatedly steering analysts to full-year figures. 524164|2026-06.headline: IOL Chemicals Q1 FY27 revenue rose 37% YoY to INR756 crore and PAT 90% to INR64.5 crore, with EBITDA margin at 14.6%.

FY27 guidance was retained at 15-20% revenue growth, 14-15% EBITDA margin and 25-30% exports, with management saying revenue could exceed the INR2,600-2,700 crore range but not upgrading guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for paracetamol given weak demand in past years?

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q1 profit came from one-time inventory gains?

qa_highlights.question: How much of the EBITDA outperformance came from operating leverage versus mix?

qa_highlights.question: Is there a split of pharma growth between volume and price?

qa_highlights.question: Why was growth muted in prior quarters and how long will demand last?

524200|2026-03.headline: Vinati Organics FY26 standalone EBITDA rose 17% to INR741 crores and PAT 18% to INR488 crores, with the company still debt-free.
524200|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone net income including other income rose 17% QoQ to INR631 crores, EBITDA grew 20% QoQ to INR203 crores and PAT rose 27% QoQ to INR137 crores. For FY26, standalone net income was flat at INR2,281 crores while EBITDA and PAT grew 17% and 18%. Demand softened from October 2025 and management says it has since recovered. IBB volumes fell about 20% versus FY25 because of raw material unavailability linked to the Iran war, which management says is now resolved. qa_highlights.question: What is the VOPL revenue outlook?

qa_highlights.question: How much capex is planned in VOPL and how much CWIP is there?

qa_highlights.question: What is the ATBS capacity and cost of the two expansion phases?

qa_highlights.question: Will AO and butyl phenol revenue reach the targeted INR700-800 crores?

524208|2026-06.headline: Aarti Industries Q1 FY27 revenue rose 41% YoY to Rs 2,627 crore and EBITDA 79% to Rs 385 crore, with management refusing to guarantee the run rate.
524208|2026-06.overview: Revenue of Rs 2,627 crore (+41% YoY) and EBITDA of Rs 385 crore (+79% YoY) were lifted by raw-material price pass-through, product mix, and inventory and FX gains, which management sized at roughly Rs 50-60 crore. Volumes fell sequentially (energy -17% QoQ, non-energy -7%, overall about -12%) amid West Asia disruption and high raw-material prices. Zone IV commissioning is delayed by 3-6 months due to labour shortages, and management declined to commit to a forward EBITDA run rate. The Augene JV is near commissioning, and FY27 capex remains on track at Rs 700-800 crore.

segments.name: Energy (Fuel Additives)
segments.commentary: Fuel additives capacity expanded to 360 KTPA from 290 KTPA; West Asia share fell to about 2% from about 15%, and volumes were redirected to US, Africa, Europe and India. segments.name: Non-Energy - Polymers
segments.commentary: Demand was soft in Q1 on weak downstream US and China demand, and low shipments followed heavy Q4 FY26 bulk shipments to the US. Management expects recovery in Q2 and full-year growth.

segments.name: Non-Energy - Dyes & Pigments
segments.commentary: Demand remained subdued amid high raw-material prices and seasonality. Price increases in dyes and pigments and pharma were partly linked to China's VAT removal on the NCB chain.

segments.name: Non-Energy - Pharma and Agro
segments.commentary: Pharma demand was stable. Agrochemical volumes were marginally lower as customers resisted elevated raw-material-linked prices; recovery is expected in Q2.

guidance_outlook: FY28 EBITDA target of Rs 1,800 crore retained; the Augene JV is included in this guidance, but management said Zone IV ramp-up may be slower than originally assumed.
Management declined to guide to a sustainable quarterly EBITDA run rate, citing plus/minus 15-20% monthly price volatility; it expects volume growth to offset lost inventory gains.
Augene JV (50:50, consolidated at PAT level) expected to start operations in Q2 FY27, with steady-state revenue retained at Rs 300-400 crore.
FY27 capex on track at Rs 700-800 crore; capex intensity expected to fall significantly from FY28.

capex_capacity: Fuel additives capacity expanded to 360 KTPA from 290 KTPA; management said there is no fixed limit on further expansion, and it will first demonstrate utilisation over the next 12 months.

PEDA project in market seeding and expected to commercialise soon; DCB debottlenecking to 140 KTPA under evaluation.

Aarti Circularity plastic recycling plant with Re Sustainability slated for commissioning in H2 FY27.

Gasoline-naphtha cracks averaged $15-18/bbl, which management described as healthy, while the energy business remains volatile.

China's suspension of export tax rebates is creating opportunities for the NCB value chain.

qa_highlights.question: What were the FX and inventory gains in Q1, and what is the impact on the EBITDA base?

qa_highlights.question: Why was gross margin lower sequentially despite the inventory and FX benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarterly gross margin is not a reliable steady-state indicator, citing timing of raw-material purchases and product placement, freight, lower volumes raising operating costs, and the chemical business running on absolute rupee deltas rather than percentage margins.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Zone IV delay affect FY28 EBITDA visibility?

qa_highlights.question: Will the Augene JV affect reported EBITDA, and is it in the Rs 1,800 crore guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed that the Rs 1,800 crore FY28 guidance includes Augene EBITDA, while the Re Aarti JV is not expected to contribute meaningfully before FY28; reporting treatment for JVs is yet to be finalised.

qa_highlights.question: Is the energy business's volume, capacity and market share sustainable once West Asia normalises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the business remains in a market-development phase; the portfolio is diversified across US, Africa, Europe, Middle East and India (Southeast Asia not yet penetrated), and it expects utilisation gains rather than volume shifts when West Asia reopens.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the company stop disclosing absolute sales volumes?

Augene JV commissioning in Q2 FY27 and the Re Aarti JV reporting treatment, which management has yet to finalise; watch the Rs 300-400 crore steady-state revenue assumption and PAT-level consolidation.

I would again hesitate to hazard a guess.
So we did not see the EBITDA run rate can be maintained.
The actual sales numbers is something that we have removed from the slides because they was getting utilized in a situation which was not favourable for the company.
524208|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on demand, volume recovery and capacity, but cautious and evasive on earnings visibility: management repeatedly declined to quantify forward EBITDA, gross margin or inventory/FX gains, citing volatility. 524332|2026-03.headline: BCL Industries FY26 revenue INR2,913 crore, EBITDA INR251 crore (+18%), margin 8.6%; 150 KLPD Bathinda unit nearing commercial output.
524332|2026-03.overview: BCL Industries reported FY26 total revenue of INR2,913 crore, with EBITDA up 18% YoY to INR251 crore and margin up 130 bps to 8.6%. Q4 PAT was INR126 crore, up 23% YoY at a 4.3% margin. Ethanol allocation from OMCs was lower than expected, so the company diverted output to ENA and SBF, which kept utilisation near full but pressured realisations. The packaged edible oil business was exited, while the refinery and trading businesses continued. The 150 KLPD Bathinda grain-based distillery is in testing, taking total installed capacity to 900 KLPD.

segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 sales of almost 4.5 lakh cases, up 20% YoY. Punjab Special Whiskey relaunched in glass bottle and Punjab Raspberry added. Management cited 18-20% PML market growth.

segments.name: Refinery (edible oil and trading)
segments.commentary: Revenue under INR749 crore with EBITDA margin of 3.74% in FY26. Packaged edible oil exited; soft oil refinery continues, with bulk supply expected at INR700-800 crore per year.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 and FY28 revenue and EBITDA margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about INR300 crore from the 150 KLPD unit at full utilisation and similar or slightly better EBITDA margins as overheads stay flat.

qa_highlights.question: Can the new 150 KLPD unit run at 100% in year one?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management expects at least 75% utilisation from Q2 FY27, with rated capacity by early July after a 15-day trial production.

qa_highlights.question: Can distillery EBITDA hold at 11.8% in Q4 given peers guide 12-15%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins should hold, citing the paddy straw boiler and consolidation of vegetable oil operations. Pure ethanol could reach 15% at full OMC allocation, but ENA/SBF are raw-material linked and not fixed-margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 3-5 year strategy and real estate exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Real estate projects date from 2005-2010 and are winding down with no new projects. Focus is biofuel: Fatehabad ethanol, later CBG and sustainable aviation fuel, and a debt-free balance sheet within 5 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is net debt and cost of debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt about INR300-335 crore including fund and non-fund based; INR120 crore on interest subvention at about 4.25%; average cost below 7%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the OCF improvement sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said working capital release is not one-off: no capex currently, ENA/SBF cash-and-carry sales, OMC receivables cut to 21 days, and edible oil inventory liquidation adds to it.

qa_highlights.question: Why exit packaged edible oil and sell land?
qa_highlights.answer: City unit had to move due to red-category restrictions. Machines were shifted or sold, and about 18 acres of city land is being sold for about INR30 crore. Proceeds go to cash and expansion.

risks_watch: Ethanol allocation from OMCs remains below capacity; ENA/SBF pricing is competitive and raw-material linked.
Ramp-up of the 150 KLPD Bathinda unit to 75% by Q2 FY27 and rated capacity by early July 2026.
Timing of biodiesel price revision by OMCs; the 75 KLPD plant stays idle until then.
Grain (maize and rice) price pass-through is lagged in ENA/SBF; management says pass-through is not immediate.
Fatehabad 250 KLPD expansion and CBG timelines (about 2 years and 3 years) depend on policy and technology.
Recovery of residual edible oil inventory within 4-6 months and sale of 18-acre land parcel.

524332|2026-06.headline: BCL Industries Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA rose 17% YoY to INR 66 crore (10.5% margin) despite revenue falling to INR 623 crore from INR 820 crore.
524332|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue fell to INR 623 crore from INR 820 crore, mainly due to closure of the edible oil unit and exit from packaged oil. EBITDA rose 17% YoY to INR 66 crore, with margin up 370 bps to 10.5%, and PAT rose 6% to INR 36 crore (5.7% margin). Distillery EBITDA margin improved to 12.41%, while ENA realisations fell to INR 58/litre from INR 70/litre. A fire at a 200 KLPD Bathinda ethanol tank on 19 June 2026 shut that plant temporarily; management said insurance recovery is virtually certain and no net loss was booked. Management also completed the acquisition of the remaining 25% of Svaksha Distillery and reduced working capital borrowings, but deferred the Fatehabad 250 KLPD project and the Svaksha 75 KLPD biodiesel project.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 820 crore in Q1 FY26 (decline)
from 11.8% in Q4 FY26 and 10% in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Profit on sale of fixed assets (oil exit)

segments.name: Distillery
segments.commentary: EBITDA margin 12.41% in Q1 FY27 versus 11.8% in Q4 FY26 and 10% in Q1 FY26. ENA volume rose to 19,376 KL from 7,960 KL YoY, but ENA realisation fell to INR 58/litre from INR 70/litre. The 115 TPH paddy straw boiler meets 100% of steam and power needs.

segments.name: Country liquor (PML)
segments.commentary: Sold 6,37,993 boxes, up 42% QoQ and 46% YoY. Punjab Raspberry launched in Q4 FY26 and Jamun Vodka in July 2026. Management targets 30 lakh cases this year out of a market of about 1.25 crore cases per annum in Punjab.

segments.name: Edible oil / packaged oil (exited)
segments.commentary: Exit completed, including closure of the Bathinda oil and vanaspati unit. Soft oil refinery and trading continue as legacy operations. Revenue decline was mainly from this exit.

guidance_outlook: Management expects the 200 KLPD Bathinda plant to restart in about 15 days from the call, and that the new 150 KLPD Bathinda unit (commissioned in early July 2026) will substantially offset the lost volume.
Order book described as full for about the next three months, supported by OMC allocation of about 4.5 crore litres from a Supreme Court order covering until November.
Management guided to a sustained distillery/overall margin range of about 10% to 12%, while noting raw material and fuel price volatility.
Working capital limit to be reduced by INR 50 crore in August 2026; management aims to bring working capital utilisation towards zero over about 1.5 years.
No share buyback planned for now. Debt will rise only if a new capex project is started.
capex_capacity: Svaksha Distillery (350 KLPD, Kharagpur, West Bengal) became wholly owned on 30 June 2026 after the remaining 25% stake was acquired.
Newly added 150 KLPD Bathinda unit began commercial trials at end-June 2026 and was commissioned in the first half of July 2026.
200 KLPD Bathinda ethanol plant shut after the 19 June 2026 fire; the tank was holding about 90,000 litres at the time and is under repair.
Fatehabad 250 KLPD grain-based plant: orders and advances are on hold after social media backlash; machinery orders are reportedly finalised and management is waiting before starting construction.
Svaksha 75 KLPD biodiesel project is on hold because biodiesel prices are not remunerative. Goyal Distillery 250 KLPD project is on hold pending industry clarity.
Malt plant is at conceptualisation stage with no timeline. IMFL entry targeted for next year, with the company still working on it.
Bio-CBG is under active evaluation (Haryana policy noted), with paddy straw feedstock seen as tricky. The company is not making biodiesel.
demand_pricing: ENA and private ethanol supply face price pressure from oversupply. Average private ethanol price is about INR 58/litre ex-factory, mainly to Reliance.

Management said maize-based ethanol to OMCs is profitable, while FCI-rice-based ethanol is near cost. ENA and private ethanol margins are about the same. Blended average EBITDA is about 12%, roughly INR 9-10/litre on maize and ENA.
Maize procurement cost was about INR 22-23/kg last quarter. Current maize price is about INR 25/kg, and management said ENA prices have been revised upwards.
DDGS prices have eased INR 1-2/kg over 2-3 months to about INR 24-25/kg for both maize and rice based.
Management expects ethanol demand to improve only slightly next year, as sugarcane-based ethanol is unlikely to be allowed. Flex fuel demand is a long-term driver, with few FFV models on sale so far.
Management said E20 is in place for about 18 months with no major vehicle damage seen, but blending expansion beyond E20 may be delayed. Isobutanol and SAF are cited as future demand sources.

qa_highlights.question: At what price is ethanol sold to private players, and is it FCI rice or maize based?
qa_highlights.answer: Private ethanol buyers are mainly Reliance at an average ex-factory price of about INR 58/litre. Private buyers use damaged grain, while the company's own FCI-rice ethanol is tied to 40% of OMC allocation. Maize procurement cost was about INR 22-23/kg last quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Cause of the Bathinda fire and safeguards for other plants?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the likely cause was static charge, possibly from clothing of a nearby worker. The company has added facilities to prevent such incidents and called it rare.

qa_highlights.question: Demand outlook for grain ethanol after E20 and beyond?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand is expected to improve only slightly next year because sugarcane ethanol is unlikely to be allowed. Flex fuel is a long-term driver, with isobutanol and SAF as additional sources, and cooking fuel use was also cited.

qa_highlights.question: Unit economics across FCI-rice, OMC maize and ENA/private ethanol?
qa_highlights.answer: FCI-rice ethanol to OMCs is near cost. Maize-based ethanol to OMCs is quite profitable. ENA and private ethanol margins are about the same, with blended EBITDA margin near 12%, or roughly INR 9-10/litre on maize and ENA on average.

qa_highlights.question: Status of Goyal bio-CNG, biodiesel and the 250 KLPD Goyal Distillery project?
qa_highlights.answer: Bio-CNG is under active evaluation after a favourable new policy, though paddy straw is tricky, mainly due to by-product sale. The company is not making biodiesel. The 250 KLPD Goyal project is on hold pending industry clarity.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the Svaksha 75 KLPD biodiesel project on hold, and does maize oil locally sourced change this?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said biodiesel prices are not remunerative and biodiesel feedstock is largely imported, so government has focused less on it. Isobutanol is being tested to promote indigenous feedstock. Management said the government's view could not be commented on.

qa_highlights.question: Malt plant and IMFL entry timeline and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Malt plant is still at conceptualisation with no timeline. IMFL entry is being worked on and is hoped for next year. Management views country liquor as more profitable than competitive IMFL.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the 250 KLPD Fatehabad project after the July statement about construction by August?
qa_highlights.answer: Orders and advances are on hold after social media backlash against the ethanol policy. Machinery orders are finalised and the company is waiting before starting construction.

qa_highlights.question: Land sale timing, debt repayment and release of pledged shares?
qa_highlights.answer: No update on the land sale, as Bathinda real estate is slow and there is no rush. Working capital utilisation is low, some small loans were repaid, and banks released pledged shares. Working capital limit to be cut by INR 50 crore in August.

qa_highlights.question: Trend in DDGS realisations and Punjab country liquor market share?
qa_highlights.answer: DDGS prices eased INR 1-2/kg over 2-3 months to about INR 24-25/kg for maize and rice based. Punjab country liquor market is about 1.25 crore cases a year, with a 30 lakh case target for this year.

qa_highlights.question: Volume outlook, total debt level and capital allocation?
qa_highlights.answer: Volumes should stay about flat until the 200 KLPD unit restarts in about 15 days. Working capital utilisation is about INR 60 crore, with total debt around INR 360 crore including working capital. Debt rises only with a new capex project, and working capital is to be run towards zero over about 1.5 years. No buyback is planned.

qa_highlights.question: Ethanol mixing in diesel, E20 damage, and government mandates beyond E20?
qa_highlights.answer: Management distinguished ethanol-in-diesel, which faces a flash point issue, from isobutanol, which it said is still under trial and not shelved. It said E20 has run 18 months without major vehicle damage, but further blending could be delayed.

qa_highlights.question: Insurance cover and stock lost in the 200 KL tank, and expected restart?
qa_highlights.answer: The tank held about 90,000 litres at the time. The plant is being repaired and is expected to restart in about 15 days. Management said both stock loss and profit loss are covered by insurance, and the P&L impact is still being evaluated.

qa_highlights.question: Share of the Supreme Court-allowed OMC volume and the order book outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company is among the biggest gainers, with about 4.5 crore litres from both units under the Supreme Court order, covering until November. The order book is more than full for the next 3 months. Flex fuel demand will take time.

qa_highlights.question: Current maize price, margin outlook and state subsidy for CBG?
qa_highlights.answer: Maize is about INR 25/kg now. ENA prices have been revised upwards, but raw material and fuel costs are rising. Management guided margins at about 10-12% with variation. Haryana has a CBG policy and the central policy is also favourable.

risks_watch: Restart timing and insurance recovery for the 200 KLPD Bathinda plant, which was shut after the 19 June 2026 fire; P&L impact still under evaluation.
ENA and private ethanol price pressure from oversupply (ENA realisation INR 58/litre vs INR 70/litre), against rising maize (about INR 25/kg) and fuel costs.
Policy uncertainty on ethanol demand: blending beyond E20 may be delayed, sugarcane ethanol unlikely to be allowed, and flex fuel vehicle availability is minimal with one model on sale.
Order book depends on the one-time Supreme Court-linked OMC allocation (about 4.5 crore litres) which runs only until November; no visibility beyond that.
Deferred growth projects (Fatehabad 250 KLPD, Svaksha 75 KLPD biodiesel, Goyal 250 KLPD) and IMFL/malt plans with no timelines; watch for any restart decisions.
Working capital reduction (INR 50 crore cut in August) and debt trajectory towards zero working capital use over about 1.5 years; land sale in Bathinda has no timeline.

524342|2026-03.headline: Indo Borax Q4 FY26 revenue rose 25.7% to Rs 63.01 crore and PAT rose 41.9% to Rs 14.53 crore, with new promoter Zenrock in control.
524342|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 operating revenue was Rs 63.01 crore (up 25.7% YoY), with EBITDA of Rs 12.82 crore (20.4% margin) and PAT of Rs 14.53 crore (21.5% margin). FY26 revenue was Rs 215.45 crore (up 22.9%), EBITDA was flat at Rs 44.16 crore, and PAT was Rs 50.27 crore (up from Rs 42.51 crore). Management said the company changed control in January 2026 with Zenrock Chemicals as new promoter, and a new leadership team took over. A special dividend of Rs 30 per share plus a final dividend of Rs 10 per share (total Rs 40) was declared after monetising non-core assets. Management guided to Rs 250-plus crore revenue next year and 20-35% growth, but gave no formal numeric guidance, and no dividend policy has yet been declared.

financial_highlights.change: +41.9% YoY vs Rs 10.24 crore; PAT margin +250 bps

segments.name: Boric Acid Technical
segments.commentary: About 85-90% of current business per CEO; roughly 15,000-plus tons in FY26. Capacity is 20,000 tpa nameplate but historically 15,000-16,000 tons output, and it is running at full utilisation.

segments.name: Boric Acid I.P. Grade
segments.commentary: About 900 tons in FY26. Realisation is 10-15% higher than technical grade, using the same equipment with tighter specifications. Management intends to expand its share.

segments.name: DOT (Disodium Octaborate Tetrahydrate)
segments.commentary: 980 tons in FY26 (about 600 tons two years ago), out of 6,000 tpa capacity, so utilisation is low. Target is about 1,500 tons next year. Realisation is about Rs 150/kg and the Indian market is about 8,500 tons.

segments.name: Boron Oxide
segments.commentary: 4,000 tpa capacity project under construction; first lot expected in three to four quarters. Management pegs realisation at 2-3x Boric Acid pricing (cited 2.5x).

segments.name: Other / traded products
segments.commentary: Borax Pentahydrate (mostly traded), Gypsum (by-product, largest by volume), and other products together about 400 tons in FY26 per the CEO.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of about Rs 250-plus crore from debottlenecking and higher DOT sales, subject to raw material pricing.
Management said it is 'definitely surpassing' Q4 numbers in Q1 FY27 (April), though it did not give figures.
Revenue growth guided at 20-35% (about Rs 40-60 crore increments), with EBITDA margin maintained at or above the current 20-21% level.
Boron Oxide first lot expected in three to four quarters; CAPEX to be completed within FY27 plus a few months.
Capex plans for the next year are still under discussion and will be shared after board approval; a stated dividend policy is being framed but not yet declared.
capex_capacity: Nameplate capacity is about 26,000 tpa: 20,000 tpa Boric Acid and 6,000 tpa DOT. Boron Oxide 4,000 tpa is a project under way.

Boric Acid effective output is about 15,000-16,000 tons versus 20,000 nameplate due to planned shutdowns and raw material gaps. Management aims to add 1,000-1,500 tons through debottlenecking and tighter shutdown planning.
Possible Boric Acid capacity expansion is under internal board debate, not yet approved.
Management says cash on hand is sufficient for the capex budgeted over the next two years.
demand_pricing: Indian Boric Acid market is about 40,000 tpa, projected to reach about 53,000 tons by 2030 (8% CAGR). Steel and refractory accounts for 55-60% of demand. The company claims about 50% share.
Realisation was about Rs 127-128/kg in FY26 versus Rs 114-115/kg in FY25. EBITDA is about Rs 28-29/kg (20-21%) for Boric Acid.
Management said Boric Acid is sold out, and growth in value depends on price pass-through. Raw material costs rose sharply due to geopolitics, but management said pass-through has been achieved.
Raw material (boron ore/Ulexite) sourcing is concentrated in Turkey. The company is diversifying to South America and North America.
Top 10-15 customers have been stable for years, and management said the company has a premium price because of technical specifications, especially in steel refractories.

qa_highlights.question: Sales mix across Boric Acid Technical, I.P., DOT and Boron Oxide, and the EBITDA margin trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Boric Acid is about 90% of sales, DOT about 8%, others about 2%. Boric Acid EBITDA is about Rs 28-29/kg (20-21%), down from the 25-30% management said it earned in past years, and management said it expects to hold 20-22%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the peak revenue potential at full utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Without new capex, management said revenue could rise 25-30% over about 1.5 years, and up to 20-35% depending on raw material inflation and pricing. The base is about Rs 215 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Boron Oxide timeline and revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: First lot is expected in three to four quarters. Management said realisation is 2-3x Boric Acid, so it used 2.5x in its estimate.

qa_highlights.question: How did the new promoter's team (Zenrock) and the special dividend fit with reinvestment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cash was not fully distributed and enough remains for two years of budgeted capex. The dividend came from selling non-core assets (flats, cars) and was a one-time payout shared with old shareholders.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue and EBITDA guidance for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 revenue could be Rs 250 crore-plus, with growth of 20-35% and EBITDA margins held at or above current levels. Absolute numbers were not given to a retail participant due to insider trading policy.

qa_highlights.question: Promoter pledge and debt (raised by one participant)?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the company has zero debt. A participant cited Rs 400 crore of debt, and management referred the query to its IR team without answering.

risks_watch: Raw material cost volatility (boron ore sourced largely from Turkey) and geopolitical pressure on margins. Management says about 2 quarters of hedged purchasing.
DOT utilisation is very low (980 tons of 6,000 tpa). Management gave no clear reason for the slow growth, and a participant questioned quality or customer issues.
Governance and disclosure: promoter shares reportedly 100% pledged (not answered), a conflicting debt claim of Rs 400 crore, and a board-approved dividend policy still pending.
Zenrock's operating background was questioned; management said Zenrock is a holding company and the operating team is led by industry professionals.
Boron Oxide, new product lines and I.P. grade ramp are still at exploratory or project stage; timing is uncertain.
524342|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on near-term results and the Q1 run rate, but evasive on specifics: on new products, Boron Oxide applications, DOT growth history, capex size and pledge/debt questions, management deferred answers. Guidance came with heavy caveats on raw material pricing.
key_quotes: So, we are confident that we are in a good situation and a good chemical sector, where the entire value chain could pass on the price increases to the whole set of their customers.
We have no complaints to make, trust me. We are happy with our results in April.
We have zero debt in Indo Borax.

524342|2026-06.headline: Indo Borax Q1 FY27 revenue rose 31.3% to Rs 70.36 crore and PAT rose 59.3% to Rs 16.25 crore, but management guided Q2 to be softer.
524342|2026-06.overview: Operating revenue was Rs 70.36 crore (+31.34% YoY) with EBITDA of Rs 19.8 crore (+62.16%) at a 28.1% margin and PAT of Rs 16.25 crore (+59.31%) at a 22.3% margin, with EPS of Rs 5.07. Management attributed the quarter to improved capacity utilisation, higher realisations and new leadership after the Zenrock promoter change. The call was dominated by the proposed acquisition of a 64.26% stake in Kronox Lab Sciences from its promoters for about Rs 250 crore, funded partly by internal accruals, asset sales and a term loan. Management said Q2 margins will fall versus Q1 because of raw material inflation from the war and the monsoon-weak quarter, and reiterated FY27 guidance of Rs 250-260 crore revenue at about 20% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Boric acid (technical and IP grade)
segments.commentary: Management says about 80% of revenue comes from boric acid; IP grade is 7-8% of boric acid volume (about 100 tonnes vs 1,500 tonnes technical, per the speaker). Capacity utilisation expected at 96-98% of practical capacity, with output rising to about 18,000 tonnes this year from 15,917 tonnes last year.

segments.name: DOT (Disodium Octaborate Tetrahydrate)
segments.commentary: FY26 volume about 900 tonnes; FY27 target 1,500 tonnes against 6,000 tonnes nameplate. Contributes about 9% of revenue this year vs 7% last year. Margin expected broadly in line with boric acid.

segments.name: Kronox Lab Sciences (proposed acquisition)
segments.commentary: Vadodara-based listed specialty chemicals company with 185 products across excipients, reagents, API and nutraceuticals. Dahej expansion of Rs 110 crore planned in phases over 18-24 months, with benefits from FY29 and full impact in FY30-31; management expects 3-3.5x current revenue post-capex.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance Rs 250-260 crore vs Rs 215 crore in FY26, with EBITDA margin about 20% and absolute EBITDA growth of about 11-12%.
Q2 expected to be softer on monsoon-weak volumes and raw material inflation from the ongoing war; margins not expected to match Q1's 28.1%.
Q3 expected to pick up again.
Boron oxide and boric acid capacity additions planned; management expects these to lift margins in FY28.
Capex of about Rs 50 crore over the next two to three years (Boron oxide about Rs 20 crore, boric acid Rs 20-25 crore, plus contingency); the Rs 50 crore figure is a business-plan rounding.
capex_capacity: Nameplate capacity about 26,000 tonnes per year at Pithampur: about 20,000 tpa boric acid and 6,000 tpa DOT.
Practical output expected at about 18,000 tonnes this year vs 15,917 tonnes last year, after planned maintenance days.
Boron oxide capex about Rs 20 crore; boric acid capex Rs 20-25 crore, with plant size flexible between 5,000 and 20,000 tpa.
Kronox Dahej expansion of Rs 110 crore in phases: first phase about Rs 55-60 crore; benefits from FY29, full impact FY30-31; execution 18-24 months.
Management says there is capacity upside of 15-20% at existing Indo Borax plants through process changes.
demand_pricing: Indian boric acid market estimated at about 40,000 tpa, projected to grow about 8% CAGR to about 53,000 tpa by 2030; steel and refractory is 55-60% of demand.

Boric acid prices moved from about Rs 127/kg early in FY27 to about Rs 155-160/kg, per management, as costs rose during the war; some pass-through still pending and spot prices were soft in Q2 seasonally.
Management says Indo Borax prices at a premium to market (market plus), citing specifications.
DOT: management cites about 8,500 tonnes of imports and about 10,000 tonnes total market; Indo Borax targets 1,500 tonnes.
Kronox's Indian market growing about 11% CAGR per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Kronox's previous promoter exit, and what is the status of the Dahej capex delayed by environmental clearances?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment on the promoter's reasons. It said the Dahej land and design are ready, audits and studies are complete, and customers have been approached; the capex is to be executed as a first priority once the deal closes.

qa_highlights.question: Is Kronox to be merged into Indo Borax, and what is the group acquisition strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: No decision yet on merger; both entities will continue as separate listed companies for now. Future acquisitions by Zenrock will be evaluated case by case; Indo Borax will focus on integration.

qa_highlights.question: How will the acquisition be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 250 crore to promoters. Rs 134-135 crore from internal accruals plus Rs 48-50 crore from sale of two Mumbai office properties. A term loan is expected in a couple of weeks to fund the open offer (Rs 151 crore) and the remaining gap. Promoter group committed Rs 25 crore contingency; total funding Rs 432 crore vs about Rs 400 crore required.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs 50 crore capex plan consistent with the individual product items?
qa_highlights.answer: Confirmed: Boron oxide about Rs 20 crore and boric acid Rs 20-25 crore total about Rs 45 crore, rounded to Rs 50 crore including inflation and contingency.

qa_highlights.question: Will the open offer be tendered, and when does control transfer?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not wait for the open offer to complete; it is using the expedited SEBI route to take control, with the open offer running in parallel. The SEBI holding period currently applies.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for unpledging Indo Borax shares pledged for the acquisition?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific timeline; the pledge is standard for acquisition financing and is a work in progress.

524372|2026-03.headline: Orchid Pharma Q4 FY26 standalone revenue flat YoY at ~INR238 crore with EBITDA ~INR42.3 crore; FY26 EBITDA fell to INR101 crore from INR155 crore.
524372|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was about INR238 crore, broadly flat versus about INR237 crore in Q4 FY25, and EBITDA rose to about INR42.3 crore from about INR40 crore. Full-year FY26 revenue fell to INR811 crore from INR922 crore and EBITDA fell to INR101 crore from INR155 crore, with management attributing this to cephalosporin price erosion and inventory write-downs in Q1 to Q3. Management said gross margins recovered in Q4 and that the worst of the pricing cycle may be behind, while remaining cautious on a full industry recovery. The call also covered the pending Dhanuka Laboratories merger, the 7ACA project, Enmetazobactam out-licensing (no definitive deal signed yet), and a planned US sterile cephalosporin fill-finish push.

Management hopes for one deal this quarter and expects about 50% of these to be signed within six months.

qa_highlights.answer: Mridul Dhanuka said 25% is existing consumption and the rest will be converted into downstream intermediates sold from Orchid Chennai. Only about 20-25% of 7ACA will be sold to third parties; some downstream capacity addition is needed, reengineering existing plants first.

qa_highlights.question: What is the peak sales and timing for Enmetazobactam?
qa_highlights.answer: Lifetime sales are still held at $1-2 billion over the patent life. Peak sales are now expected in the fourth or fifth year after launch rather than the third.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Unichem margins and inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin guided at 12-13% for FY27, supported by closing Ireland, lower overheads and a US growth of about 10%. Inventory rose partly from a shift from air to sea freight (air fell from about 40% to 4-5%); management sees no concern.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of Lyka Labs, Krebs Bio and other subsidiaries?
qa_highlights.answer: Lyka is an associate; management said profitability is lower as new animal health and critical care teams mature. Trophic Wellness had about INR125 crores revenue and INR40 crores plus profit. Krebs Nellore is EBITDA positive; the second plant has polishing issues. Onyx Scientific has weak inquiry levels.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation (solvents, packaging, APIs) at 10-12% if petroleum prices stay high, with partial offset from price increases.
Freight and air cargo disruption tied to the Iran-US conflict and Strait of Hormuz; freight up about 25% in Q4 and expected to affect Q1 FY27.
Unichem margin recovery to 12-13% and inventory levels, given its US share losses and higher transit inventory.
Pisgah Labs formulation plant commissioning slipping from Q4 FY27 and Onyx Scientific's weak inquiry levels.
Domestic institutional business declining on government funding constraints (FY26 down about 24%).
Lyka (associate) profitability pressure from field force expansion.
524494|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on growth and margin delivery, with a cautious note on near-term input cost and freight pressure. Management was candid on Unichem's weakness and subsidiary losses, but gave few specifics on Lyka and Onyx.
key_quotes: So if we have 20 divisions in the year, we should be launching in domestic market around 18 to 20 products.
The improvement in overall margins is by and large because of product mix changes.
But I don't think so that will disturb my EBITDA margin significantly in the current year because, again, the product mix change and that's playing so overall, your margin.
So that has resulted in overall margin improvement on a stand-alone basis.

524494|2026-06.headline: Ipca Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose about 21% to INR2,788 crores and EBITDA margin reached 22.88%; FY27 growth guidance raised to 14-16%.
524494|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew about 21% YoY to INR2,788 crores, with consolidated EBITDA of INR638 crores (22.88% margin) versus INR425 crores (18.39%) a year earlier. Standalone EBITDA rose about 34% to INR557 crores. Management raised FY27 guidance: revenue growth to 14-16% (from 12-13%) and consolidated EBITDA margin to around 23% (from around 22%). Exports (+34%), domestic formulations (+13%) and institutional generics (+107%, helped by about INR40 crores of shipments slipping from March to April) drove the quarter. Management said margin gains came mainly from lower personnel and manufacturing costs as a share of sales, not material savings.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR425 crores, 18.39% in Q1 FY26 (+4.49 pp)

financial_highlights.value: about INR193 crores; zero short-term borrowings
financial_highlights.change: Dollar loans of about USD50 million fully repaid

segments.name: India formulations
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR1,082 crores, +13%; IQVIA-tracked growth about 11.7%, chronic +17.2% and acute +8.9%. Market share about 2.08%, rank about 16. Antimalarials fell about 24% and are now about 1% of business.

segments.name: Exports / ROW branded
segments.commentary: Export business about INR603 crores (+34%). Promotional branded ROW about INR143 crores (+16%from INR124 crores).

segments.name: Europe / UK generics
segments.commentary: European business up about 70%, from INR33 crores to INR137 crores, the main growth driver. US shipments up about 8%; Canada saw a minor decline.

segments.name: Unichem (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: US business up about 27%, with Ipca-portfolio sales to Unichem up about 37% and Unichem's own portfolio up about 9%. Brazil up about 52%. Unichem API rose from about INR33-34 crores to about INR58 crores.

segments.name: Lyka Labs (associate)
segments.commentary: Revenue flat and EBITDA reported negative. Management cited animal health, critical care and IVF as growth areas, with some divisions still below breakeven.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth raised to 14-16% from 12-13%.
FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin raised to around 23% from around 22%.
Institutional business to grow in single digits, with annual sales of about INR260-300 crores.
Unichem guidance (10% portfolio growth, 13% EBITDA margin) not revised yet; to be reviewed after more quarters.
FY28 guidance to be given with Q4 results.
Medium term: Ipca standalone margin could reach about 30% and consolidated margin about 25-26% in 2-3 years.
Long-run US growth of about 15-17% seen as possible.
FY27 capex of about INR700-800 crores; about INR100 crores extra for biotech pilot facilities and R&D.
capex_capacity: Pithampur: capacity additions for controlled-release and extended-release formulations under way.
API: new plants at Dewas and Wardha (intermediates) as Ratlam runs out of capacity; continuous-process conversions of existing intermediates.
Biotech: about 7 candidates in pipeline and capacity for 3-4 products a year; 2 products at engineering-batch stage, with results in line with expectations.
Sales force of about 7,000 medical reps; about 200 more to be added mid-year for new divisions.
demand_pricing: Domestic growth split: volume about 5%, price about 4.5-5%, new launches about 2%.
Management said there are no price renegotiations downward; prices are rising because costs are rising.

Freight costs rose sharply: South America containers from about USD3,000 to USD9,000-10,000; US from about 7,000-7,500 to 12,500-13,000; Europe from 3,000 to about 5,500. Container availability is also constrained.
Rupee depreciation (dollar up about 11% YoY) added about 5 pp to the 21% revenue growth; about 25% of that benefit was offset by higher material cost.
Materials cost moved up about 21%, in line with sales; management said material cost to sales would fall slightly relative to sales growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why did acute underperform, and what is the India outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management disputed underperformance, citing IPM growth of 4.5% vs Ipca's 8.9% acute growth. Antimalarials fell about 24%. Pain management grew about 13%, CV and diabetes about 17%, CNS about 19%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 12-13% guidance hold, and what is the institutional outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance was raised to 14-16%. Institutional growth is expected to be single digit, since the Q1 spike was largely about INR40 crores of delayed shipments.

qa_highlights.question: What are the US launch plans, and can growth reach 20-30%?
qa_highlights.answer: About 3-4 Ipca launches and 7-8 combined Ipca and Unichem launches a year. Mid-teens growth (15-17%) is possible; source-change approvals are progressing.

qa_highlights.question: Will material cost pressure hit margins in the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: No margin pressure expected; material cost should fall slightly relative to sales. Q1 margin gains came mainly from personnel and manufacturing cost ratios.

qa_highlights.question: Is rupee depreciation or price renegotiation affecting margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Prices are rising, not being renegotiated down. FX adds to revenue and is partly offset by dollar-linked costs such as freight, testing, salaries and non-trading offices.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt and interest position?
qa_highlights.answer: Long-term debt about INR193 crores with a INR70 crore term loan at year-end, repaid next year. No short-term borrowings. Interest cost to fall further.

qa_highlights.question: Where will margins settle over 2-3 years, and what are the biotech plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated margin about 25-26% in 2-3 years, with Ipca standalone up to about 30%. About 7 biosimilar candidates, mostly off-patent. Clinical revenue expected in FY29-30.

risks_watch: Freight and container availability: rates up about 3x and still rising in July-August; South America is hardest hit.
Malaria decline (about 24%) and institutional shipment timing, which can swing quarterly growth.
Unichem margin and guidance are not yet revised; Europe approvals take about 1.5 years after filing.
Biotech and biosimilar spending (about INR100 crores this year) could weigh on EBITDA before revenue arrives in FY29-30.
FY28 guidance is pending until Q4; rupee moves affect both revenue and dollar-linked costs.
key_quotes: Both on chronic and acute, we have outperformed the market, it's not that we have underperformed on acute.
No margin pressure. I would see that your sales -- compared to sales growth, material cost will little come down.
I think there are no such renegotiations of the prices where the prices are to be reduced, no.
So '28 guidelines, we will give at the time of quarter 4. Yes.
524494|2026-06.management_tone: Management was confident on growth and margin trajectory, raising FY27 guidance and dismissing concerns about India acute underperformance, price renegotiation and margin pressure from freight and material costs. It was evasive on FY28 guidance (deferred to Q4 results) and on specific biosimilar product names and launch timelines, and it was defensive on Lyka Labs' negative EBITDA.

524558|2026-06.headline: Neuland Q1 FY27 total income rose 16.3% YoY to INR650.1 crores, with EBITDA margin of 35.5% and PAT of INR147.4 crores.
524558|2026-06.overview: Total income grew 16.3% YoY to INR650.1 crores, driven mainly by commercial CMS products, with management calling the quarter broadly in line with expectations. EBITDA was INR231.1 crores (35.5% margin) and PAT rose to INR147.4 crores from INR13.7 crores a year earlier, helped by operating leverage, favourable mix and favourable exchange rates per management. Working capital days fell from 137 at end-FY26 to 84, and capex outflow was INR121.6 crores, mainly for R&D and peptide facilities. Management repeatedly stressed that quarterly performance is lumpy and declined to give FY27 numbers beyond reiterating a long-term ~20% growth aspiration.

financial_highlights.change: +16.3% YoY vs INR300.6 crores in Q1FY26

segments.name: Commercial CMS
segments.commentary: Majority of revenue and primary growth driver in Q1; management says it is driven by about 3 molecules, with lumpiness in orders but no one-offs. Management expects one more commercialisation this year and 1 to 2 next year.

segments.name: GDS (generics / specialty)
segments.commentary: Key contributors were Ezetimibe, Mirtazapine, Escitalopram and Aripiprazole. Management is expanding presence in Brazil, Japan, South Korea and Turkey and pursuing life-cycle management with innovators.

segments.name: Development revenue
segments.commentary: Management says at least 2 new advanced-clinical projects came in during FY27, some peptide-based; quantification declined. Development revenue was about INR90 crores in FY26 per analyst citation, not confirmed by management.

guidance_outlook: Management aspires to ~20% growth and expects FY27 and FY28 to grow at that rate, but declined to guide specific FY27 growth.
Long-term EBITDA margin target is 25%-plus; Q1 margin above that was partly due to favourable exchange rates and management advised against benchmarking to Q4 or Q1.
Management expects FY27 and FY28 to be good years, and expects development revenue to rise this year, with meaningful commercial contribution mainly from FY28.
ROCE may dip during expansion phases, though management expects to protect margins.
capex_capacity: Capex approved in Q1: about INR203 crores, of which INR196 crores is for strategic growth, largely Unit 1 capacity expansion.
Cumulative approved capex of INR1,460 crores over 13 quarters; INR870 crores spent to date, balance committed to projects under implementation.
Peptide commercial-scale plant to be commissioned next month, followed by manufacturing qualification; the building is new and will be subject to a future FDA inspection.
Acquired 6-7 acres of adjacent land at Unit 1; management says it is a short-term move, and larger new industrial land will be needed beyond 3-4 years.
Future capex will be much larger in quantum and more complex in modality, possibly including M&A or overseas investment.
demand_pricing: Management says the CMS order book from pipeline molecules is encouraging and will come through over the next few quarters.
Management says destocking is factored into order visibility and no abrupt destocking impact is expected.
Peptide customer interest is rising, with opportunities converting and giving more visibility on Module 1 utilisation; some projects are ready before commissioning.
Gland Pharma strategic collaboration covers sterile API manufacturing (aseptic) for niche generic molecules; asset-light arrangement.
Management says the largest molecule it can now visualise is INR500-1,000 crores per year, against about INR50 crores five years ago.

qa_highlights.question: What growth to expect for FY27, and any destocking risk on commercial contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated ~20% growth aspiration for FY27 and FY28 but gave no specific FY27 guidance; said no destocking surprises are expected and any destocking would play out beyond FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is commercial CMS growth broad-based or driven by a few programs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 3 molecules drive commercial CMS, active every quarter, with a healthy outlook for the next 5-6 years; lumpiness is expected but no one-offs in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 a normalised run-rate, and was Q4 inflated by stocking?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 was an inflated Q3-plus-Q4 spillover quarter and not a valid base; it declined to designate Q1 as a base and said there was no excess stocking in its view.

qa_highlights.question: Why has development revenue fallen versus FY22-24, and has selection changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said development revenue is product-specific and launch quantities are classified there; the pattern does not correlate with commercial revenue and selection criteria have not changed.

qa_highlights.question: Why partner with Gland Pharma and are the products generic?
qa_highlights.answer: Gland has sterile (aseptic) manufacturing expertise; Neuland avoids sterile-facility risk. Products are in the niche generic category and the partnership is asset-light, with scope for more products.

qa_highlights.question: Are margins structurally higher, and what about stock split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 25%-plus EBITDA is the long-term target and Q1 benefited from exchange rates; stock split is a Board matter and the suggestion will be discussed.

risks_watch: Lumpiness in commercial CMS orders from a handful of molecules; no near-term guidance given.
Peptide plant commissioning next month and a future FDA inspection of the new building; timing of peptide revenue depends on it.
Geopolitical and trade developments; management says no material impact so far but is monitoring supply chains.
Dependence on favourable exchange rates for margins, per management's own comment.
Capex step-up and possible ROCE dilution during expansion; possible overseas or M&A moves.
524558|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the long-term direction and peptides, but deliberately cautious and evasive on FY27 numbers, quarterly base and development revenue quantification. Management repeatedly warned that quarters are uneven and declined to guide to a number.
key_quotes: I think we've always aspired to grow at about 20%, and we expect that FY 27& FY28 also we expect to grow that way.
Please take it for granted that our business tends to be lumpy just the way Q4 was lumpy.
We believe this partnership creates differentiated platform in sterile APIs by combining complementary strengths of both organizations.

524654|2026-03.headline: Natural Capsules posted FY26 EBITDA loss of Rs 1.56 crore (-0.83% margin) on revenue of Rs 187.20 crore; FY27 guidance targets Rs 274 crore consolidated revenue.
524654|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 55% QoQ and 30% YoY to Rs 58.45 crore, with EBITDA recovering to Rs 1.33 crore (2.28% margin), helped by about Rs 6 crore of deferred Puducherry dispatches. For FY26, revenue grew 11% to Rs 187.20 crore, but EBITDA turned negative and net loss reached Rs 24.66 crore, driven by the Puducherry shutdown and pre-commercial API subsidiary costs. Commercial API sales started at the Tumkur facility in Q4 FY26, and a contract manufacturing deal with Fermbox Bio was signed. Management guided FY27 revenue of about Rs 274 crore, with restoring capsule-segment profitability as the primary target, while balance-sheet and liquidity pressure remained a stated concern.

segments.name: Gelatin capsules
segments.commentary: FY26 gelatin revenue about Rs 163 crore, against a guidance of about Rs 171 crore; Puducherry shutdown cost about Rs 6 crore. Management cites a 12-13% EBITDA margin, with lines running above 93% utilisation.

segments.name: HPMC capsules
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue only about Rs 8 crore against a Rs 25 crore target, with about Rs 3 crore from the US that stopped after July 2025. Installed capacity rose from 19.5 to 25 billion capsules per annum with the new HPMC line; management cites about 18% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: API (Natural Biogenetics / Natural Biogenex, Tumkur)
segments.commentary: Commercial API sales began in Q4 FY26, with about Rs 9 crore of API revenue in that quarter. Domestic API margins are guided at 2-3% gross and still negative at EBITDA; fixed cost is about Rs 15 crore a year. Utilisation is about 25-30%.

segments.name: Fermbox contract manufacturing
segments.commentary: Contract manufacturing with revenue sharing; FY27 forecast about Rs 14 crore with about 20% EBITDA assumed. Fermbox plans about Rs 60 crore of downstream equipment on site, owned by them.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue of about Rs 274 crore: gelatin about Rs 170 crore, HPMC about Rs 20 crore, domestic API about Rs 70 crore, Fermbox about Rs 14 crore.
HPMC revenue expected only from H2 FY27, subject to US customer machine-suitability approvals; FY27 HPMC base case assumes utilisation below 50%.
Management expects a very low consolidated net margin in FY27 and said EBITDA at API level could still be negative; restoring capsule-segment profitability is the primary FY27 target.
PLI-linked minimum import price benefits excluded from guidance; prednisolone and dexamethasone commercial-scale production targeted for Q3/Q4 FY27, betamethasone for Q4 FY27 per the call.
WHO GMP certification targeted in the next quarter; CEP filing and WHO GMP inspection around Q2 FY27; USFDA around Q3/Q4 FY27. Management said USFDA timeline is about 24 months.
Total debt expected at Rs 100-110 crore in FY27 and FY28, with annual repayments of Rs 10-12 crore; possible additional borrowing of Rs 20 crore over two years.
Rs 240-250 crore API revenue target retained for FY29, needing an additional Rs 25-30 crore to complete two clean rooms.
capex_capacity: New HPMC line commissioned in FY26 takes installed capacity from 19.5 to 25 billion capsules per annum; ready for double-zero production, with revenue expected from H2 FY27 subject to US approvals. Each HPMC line is about 750 million capsules a year, and two lines give about 1.5 billion.
Tumkur API facility: utilisation about 25-30%; management says the fixed cost burden is about Rs 15 crore a year.
Fermentation capacity freed up: about 40% spare after the enzymatic route, with Fermbox to use spare capacity under a no-compete clause.
Reaching the Rs 240-250 crore API target requires about Rs 25-30 crore to finish two clean rooms; infrastructure is already in place.
Pending HPMC approvals are machine-suitability checks: the new machine was installed in March 2026 and is in validation, with two to three months of customer stability testing.
demand_pricing: US Neutra/wellness demand is weak after the 2025 tariffs. Management expects improvement in 3-6 months, and HPMC exports to Mexico and Brazil are now the main export markets.

Steroidal API pricing in India is pressured by Chinese overcapacity. Management says Indian prices are much lower than Chinese export prices and sometimes below cost; generic-customer API margins are in the single digits.
Prednisolone and dexamethasone trial batches are about 10% above Chinese cost at kilo scale; the government's minimum import price on four products could close this gap.
Domestic API volumes are price-sensitive, and raw-material prices have risen after the Iran-US conflict hit petrochemical supply, per management.
Management said the company has about 36 days of order backlog across capsule types.

qa_highlights.question: How will management prioritise bandwidth and working capital across about five concurrent initiatives with near-zero cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Dedicated teams run each business; management said liquidity is a real pressure. Options under review include a BIRAC RDI application, preferential allotment (with promoter participation), and a rights issue, with limited promoter dilution.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 HPMC revenue assumption, and what if approval slips?
qa_highlights.answer: Base case is about Rs 20 crore of HPMC revenue, against about Rs 8 crore in FY26. Management did not quantify the impact of a delay.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Natural Biogenex claw-back linked to FY27 targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the claw-back refers to FY29 figures, is already in the shareholders' agreement, and there is no current discussion on extending it.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margins are assumed for FY27 capsules?
qa_highlights.answer: HPMC is assumed at 18% EBITDA and gelatin at about 13%, the same as the Q4 FY26 level, with some upside from a weaker rupee.

qa_highlights.question: Was PLI income received in FY26, and what is assumed for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No PLI income was received in FY26, and none is included in FY27 forecasts because of timing uncertainty.

qa_highlights.question: How much did the API guidance rely on Q4 run-rate, and what is the EBITDA outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: API guidance is based on Q4 API revenue of about Rs 9 crore, growing gradually. Domestic API EBITDA is expected to be negative to low single-digit, and consolidated net margin very low.

qa_highlights.question: How big can the Fermbox contract become?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it could grow well beyond Rs 14 crore, with multiple products from Europe and the US and a better profit share; the Rs 50 crore scenario was not confirmed.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the FY26 API target missed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited yield gaps on PLI products, the failed Chinese technology support, and volatile intermediate prices; intermediate-based domestic sales started only in December 2025 and the Chinese yield consultant visa did not come through.

risks_watch: Liquidity and balance-sheet pressure: near-zero cash, a loss-making consolidated P&L, and fundraising options still open.
HPMC revenue depends on US machine-suitability and stability approvals, and US demand is still weak.
API PLI minimum import price benefit depends on commercial-scale production demonstrations expected in Q3/Q4 FY27, and betamethasone is slated for later.
Regulatory timelines (WHO GMP in Q2 FY27, USFDA in about 24 months) have slipped in the past, per analyst questions.
Steroidal API pricing and Chinese overcapacity; raw-material cost inflation from petrochemical disruptions.
524654|2026-03.management_tone: Candid about the FY26 loss and the missed timelines, but guidance is framed as conservative. Management is confident on capsule-segment recovery and API regulatory progress, while evasive on fundraising details, PLI timing, and the Fermbox contract scale.
key_quotes: Restoring profitability at the console level is our primary financial target for FY27.
The Puducherry disruption is behind us.
So, we are confident that this 10% could be covered by the PLI incentive, which is our assumption now.

524669|2026-06.headline: Hester Q1 FY27 standalone PAT up 88% and gross margin up to 78%, while consolidated revenue fell 8% on Nepal and Africa weakness.
524669|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue from operations grew 14% YoY and EBITDA rose 95%, with gross margin improving from 69% to 78% on product mix and operational efficiencies. Consolidated revenue declined 8%, mainly on lower Nepal and Africa revenues. Consolidated profit included an exceptional gain from the Gates Foundation amendment that cut the Hester Africa soft loan from USD 12 million to USD 5 million, waived accrued interest and made the loan interest-free. Poultry grew 48% on institutional business and deeper penetration, while Animal Healthcare was held back by delayed government immunisation programmes (PPR, Lumpy Skin Disease / Goat Pox).

financial_highlights.metric: Hester Africa Gates Foundation soft loan
financial_highlights.value: Reduced from USD 12 million to USD 5 million, interest-free
financial_highlights.change: Exceptional accounting gain in consolidated profit

segments.name: Poultry Healthcare Division
segments.commentary: Grew 48% YoY on higher institutional business and deeper market penetration. Management said the low pathogenic avian influenza vaccine, approved in March 2026, contributed to the jump. Management also cited early traction in poultry health products (feed supplements, disinfectants).

segments.name: Animal Healthcare Division
segments.commentary: Impacted by timing of government immunisation programmes (PPR eradication, Lumpy Skin Disease Control Initiative, Goat Pox vaccine supply). Management described this as timing-related rather than a demand issue.

segments.name: International (Nepal and Africa)
segments.commentary: Revenues were low in the quarter and drove the consolidated decline. Management said strategic direction is unchanged, focused on registration, market development and commercial presence.

segments.name: Pet care
segments.commentary: Emerging, not reported separately and included within animal health. Product categories are antibiotics, anti-parasites and grooming products sold under the Hester brand.

guidance_outlook: Management declined to give directional guidance on Africa demand or when it would turn profitable, describing the region as a formative period.
Management said the delayed government vaccine tender business is expected to come through in the next quarter.
No numerical guidance was given on revenue, margins or capacity utilisation targets.
Management said it is not providing guidance on the capacity utilisation trajectory.
capex_capacity: Average plant capacity utilisation is around 60% to 65%, covering the whole manufacturing set-up (poultry, large animal, and the newly added fill-and-finish and BSL3 facilities).
New fill-and-finish and BSL3 facilities came online a couple of quarters ago. Management did not give a utilisation figure for these specifically.
Fixed assets rose by around Rs. 200 crore in FY26 (per analyst), with the new facilities cited as the driver. Management did not dispute the figure.
Pipeline products under development at the new facilities were not disclosed. Recombinant Brucella vaccine development is said to be progressing on timeline.
Regulatory dossiers were submitted in animal health during the quarter.
demand_pricing: Poultry growth came mainly from higher market share and deeper penetration; management said vaccine prices have only marginally increased.
Government tender timing caused animal vaccine sales to slip from Q1, with management expecting them to come in the next quarter.
Management said the poultry vaccine business is shared across India, Nepal and Africa; poultry exports from India are part of the consolidated poultry top line.
Management said the poultry distribution network is the same for vaccines and health products, with cross-selling of feed supplements and medicines under way.
Management said there was no material impact on the industry from the H5N1 culling compensation delay.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Ministry's recent decision on HPAI vaccine imports for testing, and how does Hester benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Priya Gandhi said it is premature to comment: the government still has to decide whether the vaccine will be imported or made in India.

qa_highlights.question: How does the poultry business's sharp growth compare with its historical track record? Is it cyclical or structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajiv Gandhi said the division pushed sales where opportunities arose, while animal health sales slipped due to tender delays. No value or volume split was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity utilisation, and can sales grow without new capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajiv Gandhi said average utilisation is about 60% to 65%, but noted that this is subjective given the mix of batch sizes.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the step-up in poultry revenue from about Rs. 45-48 crore to over Rs. 60 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajiv Gandhi attributed it to better placement and more aggressive market penetration, with price increases contributing little.

qa_highlights.question: Is cash conversion weak, given that receivables are higher?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashish Desai said operating cash flow is positive and conversion has improved. Rajiv Gandhi said higher receivables are seasonal and not a concern.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Africa operation's slow scale-up a natural gestation period or a tendering problem?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajiv Gandhi said it is a formative period in a new continent with economic and political strain. He declined to give directional guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Africa tax holiday timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashish Desai said the tax-free status runs until 2030.

risks_watch: Africa and Nepal revenue weakness, with no profitability timeline given and geopolitical constraints acknowledged by management.
Animal Healthcare dependence on government tender timing, with the next quarter expected to see catch-up sales.
Receivables rising, which management attributes to seasonality. Analysts questioned cash conversion.
Low utilisation (about 65%) despite the recent fill-and-finish and BSL3 capacity additions, with fixed assets up about Rs. 200 crore in FY26.
Regulatory and policy uncertainty on HPAI vaccine import or domestic manufacturing pathway.
Gates Foundation loan reduction, which boosted consolidated profit through a one-time exceptional gain rather than operations.
524669|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on standalone profitability and poultry growth, but evasive on Africa, Nepal, pet vaccines, utilisation numbers, pipeline products and HPAI policy, repeatedly declining to quantify or guide. Management dismissed the receivables and cash conversion concern as seasonal.
key_quotes: As we have consistently maintained, this remains a timing-related issue rather than a reflection of any underlying demand issue.
We would not want to get into any directional guidance or anything.

524715|2026-03.headline: Sun Pharma Q4 FY26 sales rose 13.6% to INR 145,598 mn, but EBITDA margin fell to 27.1% from 31.9% QoQ; FY27 guided to high single-digit top-line growth.
524715|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated sales were INR 145,598 mn, up 13.6% YoY, with EBITDA of INR 39,542 mn (up 6.4% YoY) and a 27.1% margin, down from 31.9% in Q3. Management attributed the sequential margin drop to lower milestone income, seasonality, lower lenalidomide contribution and elevated spend in several geographies, including the US, which it expects to normalise. FY26 sales reached INR 582 bn (+11.9%) with EBITDA of INR 177,314 mn (+16.1%, 30.3% margin). qa_highlights.answer: Management said the sale was a present-versus-future value decision rather than a liquidity need. Margins were lower because the land cost from the amalgamation was higher, and the one-time tax was elevated by the same cost basis.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company disclose GDV and cash flows?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will reflect cash flows and GDV going forward, with cash flows being the more important metric; an offline discussion was offered for the FY27 numbers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for Godhavi and Smile City?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said monetisation could come towards the later part of FY27, but details are not worked out given fluid developments in the area.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for the cash generated from the sale?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cash will fund land purchases in Ahmedabad and Million Minds development, which is being funded from internal accruals.

risks_watch: Thaltej sale consideration, buyer and margin remain undisclosed; a later disclosure is expected.
Million Minds rentals depend on closing the remaining 15-20% of leasable area under negotiation and on starting rentals in Q4 FY27.
FY27 PAT guidance (Rs 300-325 crore) relies on a large Q2-Q4 contribution after a Rs 42 crore Q1 PAT.
Revenue recognition for Malabar Retreat depends on construction completion, and the project is about 83% complete.
Godhavi monetisation timing and plans are still open.

Tone was defensive on the margin and tax questions, attributing them to a one-time amalgamation tax effect.

Monetization land under favorable market conditions enables us to accelerate cash generation, strengthen liquidity, and redeploy capital into opportunities that can deliver superior long-term returns.
