526371|2026-03.headline: NMDC guides FY27 production to 60 million tonnes and FY27 capex to about INR6,000 crore, with Q1 FY27 output up about 15% YoY.
526371|2026-03.overview: NMDC reported FY26 production above 50 million tonnes and an 11% PAT rise despite sluggish prices, with management citing a record capex of about INR3,300 crore. Management guided FY27 production to 60 million tonnes, with the first two months of Q1 FY27 about 15% higher YoY at roughly 10 million tonnes. New iron ore (Deposit 4, Deposit 13) and coal (Tokisud, Rohne) assets are being commissioned, and a INR3,000 crore blending yard at Vizag is sanctioned. The EBITDA margin was 33% group-level, down from 42%, due to a one-time HR coil trading arrangement with NMDC Steel; standalone iron ore EBITDA was stated at 42%.

segments.name: Iron ore (NMDC standalone)
segments.commentary: Standalone EBITDA margin at 42%, with FY27 guided at 42-43%. Kirandul FY26 about 21 million tonnes (to ~30 million by decade-end); Bacheli about 18-19 million tonnes (to ~35 million).

segments.name: NMDC Steel (NSL)
segments.commentary: NSL has turned profitable; the HR coil trading in the last quarter was a one-time cash-flow support and is not expected in Q1 FY27. NSL dues are being recovered at about INR100 crore per month, with full liquidation in 16-18 months (pre-demerger dues about INR2,500 crore, now about INR1,800 crore).

segments.name: Coal
segments.commentary: Tokisud (2.3 million tonnes peak, thermal, opened) targets 0.75-1 million tonnes in FY27 from Q2; Rohne (8 million tonnes peak coking coal) opens around end-Q3 FY27 with no FY27 production. Management expects INR500-600 crore revenue per 1 million tonnes at G10 grade, at 30-40% EBITDA (approximate).

segments.name: Pellets (KIOCL)
segments.commentary: KIOCL 3 million tonne job-work plant: FY26 about 2.4 million tonnes; FY27 target 3-3.3 million tonnes. Pellet grade achieved 66.5% Fe; targeting 67% DR-grade with a $20-30/t premium.

guidance_outlook: FY27 production guided at 60 million tonnes including NSL, built from Deposit 14 (+1 mt), NMZ (+1 mt), Kumaraswamy (+~3.3 mt), Deposit 5 (+2 mt to 12 mt), plus Deposit 4 (~1 mt) and Deposit 13 (~0.5 mt).
Deposit 4 expected to start commercial mining in Q2 FY27: about 1 mt in FY27, 2 mt in FY28, and 7 mt peak rated capacity after 1.5-2 more years.
Deposit 13 start targeted around Q2 FY27 after pending clearances: under 0.5 mt in FY27, about 2 mt next year, 10 mt initial peak rising to 20-21 mt in 4-5 years.
Capex guidance: about INR6,000 crore in FY27 (range INR6,000-7,000 crore); INR7,000-10,000 crore per year over the next 2-3 years; INR40,000-50,000 crore over 3 years to reach 100 mt.
Overseas critical mineral and mineral asset acquisitions: INR2,000-3,000 crore expected in FY27; a couple of overseas assets targeted this year.
Management reiterated a 100 million tonne target by end of decade and said the 60 mt FY27 guidance is achievable without the railway doubling, but 100 mt requires it.
No immediate plans to leverage the balance sheet; internal accruals expected to fund capex and acquisitions, with debt possible late FY27 only for large global acquisitions.
Iron ore prices expected to stay range-bound in FY27; monthly price calls to be taken.
capex_capacity: Railway: 131 km doubling; two sections remaining, one by end of June 2026 and the Bhansi-Bacheli section by December 2026; evacuation capacity to rise from 28-30 mt to ~40 mt, with 60 mt+ after doubling beyond Jagdalpur.
Slurry pipeline (15 mt, Bacheli to Nagarnar), Nagarnar pellet plant and Bacheli grinding mill in pre-commissioning; commissioning expected by end-June or mid-July 2026.
EC capacity 64.8 mt vs CTO ~55.4 mt; CTO enhancement sought in three places to ~58.8 mt. All mines reached EC capacity as of 1 April 2026 (Deposit 5 the exception in FY26).
Deposit 5 downhill conveyor and bottleneck fix due June-July 2026, enabling 12 mt. New infrastructure at Deposit 14, NMZ, 11 and 11C takes about 1.5 years, adding 5-6 mt.
INR3,000 crore blending yard at Vizag (board sanctioned, ~2-2.5 year build); Vizag land parcel ~1,100 acres; pellet plant at Vizag on drawing board, pending slurry pipeline route decision.
Expansion works (~INR15,000-20,000 crore worth of major tenders) expected to be awarded by end-June or July 2026.
demand_pricing: Management says demand is not a constraint even at 100 mt, citing JSW, AMNS (10 mt plant near Vizag, 17 mt total), JSPL and NSL expansions; NMDC's phosphorus content of 0.05% is a claimed differentiator.

Iron ore prices expected range-bound in Q1 FY27 after steel prices peaked Dec-Feb and stabilised in March-April; the company sets prices monthly, citing international prices, competitor prices and logistics, not a direct steel-price link.
RINL consumes 7-8 mt per year; bills discounted at ~10% premium with a 45-day payment lag; no recourse to NMDC in FY25 or FY26.
Blended/branded iron ore (Vizag) planned as a premium product; exports unattractive given 30% export duty, so pellets are preferred for export.
Iron ore realisation slightly down ~2% per an analyst question; no quantified FY27 realisation guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: Mine-wise bridge to 60 mt FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Deposit 14 +1 mt, NMZ +1 mt, Kumaraswamy +~3.3 mt (MPAP relief from 8.6 mt), Deposit 5 +2 mt (to 12 mt), totalling ~5.3 mt; plus Deposit 4 (~1 mt) and Deposit 13 (~0.5 mt) gives ~60 mt including NSL.

qa_highlights.question: Coal mine economics and grade?
qa_highlights.answer: Initial volume mostly via auction at prices above CIL FSA; 1 mt is estimated at INR500-600 crore revenue with 30-40% EBITDA. Grade is G10; figures described as very preliminary.

qa_highlights.question: Recovery of NSL and RINL receivables?
qa_highlights.answer: NSL dues cut from ~INR2,500 crore to ~INR1,800 crore; recovery at ~INR100 crore per month, 16-18 months for NSL, about a year and a half to two for the rest. RINL is 100% government-owned, with timing slower but no risk assumed.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plans and critical minerals spending?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex ~INR6,000 crore (range 6,000-7,000), then INR7,000-10,000 crore per year. Overseas acquisitions INR2,000-3,000 crore in FY27; domestic rare earth via GMDC MoU in Gujarat, no firm profitability guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Can 60 mt be reached without railway doubling?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, 60 mt is achievable without it, but 100 mt is not possible without the doubling completing (Vizag/Bhansi-Bacheli section due December 2026).

qa_highlights.question: Deposit 4, Deposit 13 and Rohne ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Deposit 4 ~1 mt in FY27, 2 mt in FY28, 7 mt peak; Deposit 13 under 0.5 mt FY27, 2 mt next year, 10 mt initially rising to 20-21 mt; Rohne opens around end-Q3 FY27 with no FY27 output and 8 mt peak coking coal.

qa_highlights.question: EBITDA guidance and realisation outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Iron ore EBITDA margin to be maintained at 42-43% for FY27; no specific per-tonne realisation or EBITDA-per-tonne figures were given.

risks_watch: Q1 FY27 output and CTO enhancement to ~58.8 mt (vs EC 64.8 mt) are needed to hit 60 mt; EC and forest clearances remain a continuous process.
Railway doubling completion (December 2026 for Bhansi-Bacheli) is a prerequisite for 100 mt.
NSL and RINL receivables recovery pace and any repeat of HR coil trading; the one-time trading hit margins in Q4 FY26.
Pending approvals for Deposit 13 and Rohne coal; Rohne has no FY27 output.
Govt pay revision: provisions already taken from 1 January 2026; further provisioning for executives from 1 January 2027.
Overseas acquisition pipeline and the decision to use debt for large global deals late FY27.

financial_highlights.change: Down from 42%, due to steel trading
About 15% higher YoY vs 8.2 million tonnes

key_quotes: We have touched 53 million tons of production, we have crossed that.
We'll not be able to do 100 without this, but 60 we can.

Noticeably cautious or evasive on realisation (prices "range-bound", no per-tonne guidance), on critical-mineral acquisition capex and profitability ("very speculative"), and on RINL receivables recovery timing.

526612|2026-06.headline: Blue Dart Q1 FY27 revenue rose to INR1,658 crore (from INR1,442 crore) and PAT reached INR87 crore, driven mainly by yield and fuel surcharge rather than volume.
526612|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR1,658 crore against INR1,442 crore a year earlier, with PAT of INR87 crore. Management attributed growth mainly to pricing: GPI-led increases, targeted repricing of loss-making lanes and customers, and fuel surcharge recovery after diesel and Brent prices rose from around March–May. Tonnage grew about 7% to 364,430 tons and shipments about 2% to 96.15 million, with air volume up about 2.6% and surface up about 9%. Management declined to quantify yield growth or give forward volume and margin guidance, citing seasonality and H2 resourcing challenges.

segments.name: Air
segments.commentary: About 60% of revenue but about 25% of kilos (1:3 air:surface by weight). Volume growth about 2.6%; growth is mainly yield-led. Freighter pallet utilisation 85–90%.

segments.name: Surface / Ground
segments.commentary: About 40% of revenue and about 75% of kilos. Volume up about 9%; B2B revenue up about 14%. Management says surface is the faster-growing segment and is approaching air in size.

segments.name: E-commerce
segments.commentary: Revenue up more than 10% YoY. Management says about 50-plus million of the 96.15 million shipments are e-commerce, and Blue Dart holds about 12–13% of outsourced/3PL e-commerce.

segments.name: B2B vs B2C
segments.commentary: Revenue mix about 70% B2B and 30% B2C (plus or minus 2%).

segments.name: BFSI (documents and cards)
segments.commentary: BFSI alone is about 10–15% of total revenue; documents plus cards together, including small parcels, about 25–30%. Management says BFSI is no longer a growing segment.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance. Management said it will not forecast volumes, citing seasonality, but expects Q2 to reflect the full fuel-surcharge increase from May onward.
Typical GPI realisation is about 4–5%, with extra customer-specific corrections on top.

Standalone annualised capex guided at INR100–150 crore, mostly replacement and expansion. Aviation capex is driven by maintenance and engine cycles, with roughly 20–25% of depreciation as ongoing capex.
H2 is expected to bring higher volumes, but resourcing flex will determine margins; management aims for stable, consistent margin improvement.
No major expansion plans; growth is expected to be organic. Possible consolidation and expansion of southern hubs (Bangalore, Chennai) and Mumbai, a few quarters away.
capex_capacity: Two major hubs added in North and a couple of medium-sized hubs in East in the prior period.
Freighter pallet utilisation at 85–90%; aircraft flown mainly at night and scheduled against available load.
Belly cargo is 30–40% of overall load in a typical month, and can reach 70–80% on lower-volume weekends. Blue Dart flies to 8 stations and carries belly cargo at 25–50 other locations.
The two aircraft acquired earlier are back to pre-acquisition pallet utilisation (as of 2024) and are integrated into the network.
demand_pricing: Growth came mainly from pricing: GPI increases, repricing of loss-making lanes and customers, and fuel surcharge pass-through. Management said yield was 'directionally' the main driver of revenue growth.
Fuel surcharge on surface is revised monthly based on local diesel prices, which rose in mid-May after about 5–6 years. Air fuel surcharge rose from April as Brent climbed from around mid-March.
Auto is a niche express vertical; management estimates it grows at about high-teens, in line with surface B2B. Market share is hard to quantify.
Management says e-commerce pricing remains competitive, with capacity still available in the market; Blue Dart positions itself as a premium player.
Management says it gained a very small but roughly stable market share in SME clients versus last year (informal assessment).

qa_highlights.question: Is the revenue growth mainly from pricing, given volume growth was only about 7%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed directionally. Pricing came from GPI increases, repricing of loss-making lanes and customers, and fuel surcharge recovery (fuel surcharge offset fuel cost rises, which also lifted yield).

qa_highlights.question: Why is e-commerce growth lower than the industry, and is it a focus area?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said e-commerce is a growth driver but not a mass-volume focus. It is prioritising premium, time-critical traffic that fits its capacity, and it is not targeting the largest e-commerce share.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex plans and new hubs?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone annualised capex is INR100–150 crore, mostly replacement and expansion. Two major northern hubs and some medium eastern hubs were added, and southern and Mumbai hub consolidation is being considered a few quarters away.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable are margins, and what is the H2 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 brings volume opportunity but also resourcing challenges. It aims to keep or improve margins through efficiency and better realisation, without quantifying either.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 2 recently acquired aircraft stabilised?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management said pallet utilisation was restored to pre-acquisition levels by 2024. The aircraft are part of the wider network, and capacity is not a constraint; yield is the main lever.

risks_watch: Growth quality: about 7% tonnage growth against about 15% revenue growth implies most of the increase came from pricing and surcharges, which may not persist.
Fuel: diesel and Brent rises were passed through with a lag; Q2 is expected to show the full surcharge effect, but any fall in fuel prices would reverse it.
Air volume growth of about 2.6% versus surface about 9% suggests air is stagnating in volume.
H2 resourcing: management flagged that peak-season flex will decide margins.
Competition in e-commerce pricing remains intense, with spare capacity in the market.
BFSI (documents and cards) is no longer growing, and the 25–30% documents-plus-parcels exposure needs monitoring.
Management declined to provide e-commerce split by air and surface, D2C share, or yield premium figures, limiting visibility.
526612|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the quarter's numbers and direction, but guarded on forward-looking detail: it declined to quantify yield, the e-commerce premium, and market share, and repeatedly deferred to seasonality rather than guiding.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR1,442 crore in Q1 FY26 (about +15%)

key_quotes: This seems to be a good quarter where what we have kind of put ourselves for seems to be bringing positive indications in terms of numbers moving in the right direction.

Blue Dart has been, I would say, focused on not playing on the volumes, but ensuring what we get as a piece from e-commerce works well to synergize with our capacities and adds profitability to the bottom line.

Iin short, from a capacity utilization, that has never been a challenge. It's a question of what kind of product that goes in, how critical or important it is for the customer to be able to pay the premium that ensures the profitability of the overall network.
So the effort will be to maintain or improve further. But we seem to be on the right path is what I would say.

526668|2026-06.headline: Kamat Hotels Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 10% to INR 91 crore and EBITDA 36% to INR 25 crore, margin 27% vs 22%.

financial_highlights.change: +10% YoY vs INR 83 crore in Q1 FY26
+36% YoY vs INR 18 crore in Q1 FY26
Achieved despite four new properties added

financial_highlights.metric: Same-store revenue (excl. Ira Mumbai and four new hotels)

financial_highlights.value: Revenue up 35% YoY; EBITDA up 50% YoY

financial_highlights.metric: Ira by Orchid (excl. Ira Mumbai) ARR / RevPAR
financial_highlights.value: ARR about INR 4,069 (flattish); RevPAR about INR 2,466 (about 3% growth)

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated debt / cash and FDs / net debt (as of last quarter)
financial_highlights.value: Debt INR 105 crore; cash and FDs INR 65 crore; net debt INR 38 crore

segments.name: Orchid Mumbai (business hotel)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 35% YoY and EBITDA up 50% YoY; occupancy reached about 91% with RevPAR up almost 40%, rates kept flat to sell more rooms.

segments.name: Orchid Pune (business hotel)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 27% YoY; management is rationalising costs to improve margins and sees upgrade potential to upper upscale.

segments.name: Ira by Orchid portfolio
segments.commentary: Reported negative RevPAR growth including Ira Mumbai, which closed on 31 March 2026; excluding Ira Mumbai, ARR about INR 4,069 and RevPAR about INR 2,466 (about 3% growth). Ira by Orchid Hyderabad is ramping up after a weak FY26.

segments.name: Newer leased properties (Orchid Panchgani, Orchid Rishikesh/Rishivan, Ira Hyderabad, Ira Bhavnagar)
segments.commentary: Four new hotels added in the last 2-3 quarters are still scaling up and carry higher operating costs. Management said Bhavnagar opened recently with strong banqueting response and will be in its full-year base next year.

qa_highlights.question: Are the properties due to open this quarter on schedule, or have LPG, construction or supply shortages delayed them?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no supply-chain impact from the war; Dwarka is due November-December, Gwalior around October-November, and Dehradun may slip about six months due to owner challenges.

qa_highlights.question: What occupancy trajectory is expected for Q2 and Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the Q1 occupancy growth trend to continue for the remaining three quarters, with business hotels typically above 75-80% and leisure properties seasonal.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a strategic pivot under the new CFO, and will the company move towards owned hotels?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is evaluating various growth options and will combine asset-light leases or revenue share with owned hotels (brownfield or land parcels); debt capacity up to INR 300 crore at three times forward EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Are any hotels opened before FY26 loss-making, and what is the plan for loss-makers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said hotels opened in FY24-FY25 are all profitable after lease charges; new hotels usually show losses in year one due to opening costs and take two to three years to stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company take price hikes given flat Orchid ARR?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said RevPAR is the key metric and that rates and occupancy are managed case by case depending on micro-market demand and competition.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the EBITDA margin improvement, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the margin improvement long-term, with a 30% target in two to three years through revenue growth and cost control, including renewable energy.

qa_highlights.question: What is the pipeline and expected room additions in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited about 400 keys over the next 12-15 months across Gwalior, Dehradun, Dwarka, Nashik, Rishikesh and Mandvi, with possible delays.

qa_highlights.question: What capex is planned for FY27 and FY28, and what was spent in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Most properties are leased, so capex is minimal; Mumbai and Pune renovation plans are being finalised, with guidance expected next quarter, and only normal repair and maintenance capex is planned for the next two years.

guidance_outlook: No formal numerical guidance for FY27 top line or EBITDA; management said it expects sequential (QoQ) growth in the coming quarters, supported by tailwinds.
Occupancy expected to keep its Q1 growth trend over the remaining three quarters; business hotels typically cross 75-80% occupancy and leisure properties are seasonal.
EBITDA margin target of 30%, to be reached in about two to three years, through higher revenue and cost control including renewable energy for some properties.
About 400 keys expected to be added in the next 12-15 months: Gwalior, Dehradun, Dwarka, Nashik, Rishikesh and Mandvi (Kutch), with possible delays.
Net debt to move towards zero; management said debt capacity of up to INR 300 crore exists at three times forward EBITDA.

capex_capacity: Opening timelines: Orchid Dwarka (63 rooms) targeted for November-December 2026; Gwalior targeted for around October-November 2026 (Diwali); Nashik targeted before the Kumbh; Dehradun may slip by about six months due to owner-side challenges; Rishikesh expansion and Mandvi are on track.

526797|2026-06.headline: Greenply Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 20.7% YoY to INR724.9 crore, with core EBITDA margin of 10.8%, up 50 bps YoY.
526797|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue reached INR724.9 crore (up 20.7% YoY) and core EBITDA was INR78.3 crore at a 10.8% margin. Plywood and MDF both delivered double-digit volume growth, but management said Q1 sales were lost to election-related labour disruption, lower plant utilisation (92-93% vs ~98-99% in Q4) and weak outsourcing. Price increases of 7-9% in MDF and 3-5% in plywood were taken, and the new MDF flooring line started commercial production on 20 July 2026. Management reaffirmed FY27 guidance of 10% plywood volume growth and 25-30% MDF volume growth, and a 10% plywood margin.

segments.name: Plywood
segments.commentary: Revenue INR526.6 crore, volume +13.8% YoY, realisation INR265/sq m (+4.3% QoQ), core EBITDA margin 8.4% (+50 bps YoY). Management said Q1 volumes were well below Q4 levels (~600+ crore quarterly run-rate referenced).

segments.name: MDF
segments.commentary: Revenue INR195.7 crore, volume ~58,000 cbm (+24.7% YoY), realisation INR33,525/cbm (+9.9% QoQ), EBITDA margin 17.3%. Gross margin fell ~300 bps QoQ, which management attributed to timber cost rise in monsoon season.

segments.name: Furniture & fittings JV (hardware)
segments.commentary: JV sales INR13.61 crore; PAT loss INR11.48 crore, Greenply share INR5.74 crore. Management targets FY27/FY28 revenue of INR120-150 crore and expects losses to reach zero around mid-next year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth target: 10% in plywood and 25-30% in MDF.
Plywood EBITDA margin guidance of ~10% reiterated; management said 600+ crore quarterly revenue at current cost base gives 10%+ margin and ~800 crore could give 13-15%.
MDF EBITDA margin sustainable at 16-17% on current capacity, possibly rising ~1% with second line operating leverage; management cited 17-18% ROCE as a medium-term target.
Balance sheet: peak debt of INR710-730 crore at 31 March 2027 and debt-equity of ~0.75x; expected to fall below 0.7x about six months later and to ~0.65-0.7x by year-end.
FY27 total capex about INR500 crore (parent ~INR47 crore incl. SAMET loss funding; GSPL ~INR100 crore; GSPPL ~INR300 crore).
Management expects timber prices to remain stable; any decline would be a windfall. Flooring line potential peak revenue INR75-80 crore.
Plywood ContiRoll technology: two factories fully implemented, two more during H1 FY27; P&L gains expected from Q4 FY27.
capex_capacity: MDF flooring manufacturing line commenced commercial production on 20 July 2026; revenue expected from late July 2026, with potential peak revenue of INR75-80 crore.

531266|2026-06.headline: VST Tillers Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11% to INR313.4 crores, but operational EBITDA margin fell about 45 bps to 12.85% on raw material inflation.

Operational EBITDA margin (excluding other income and fair value gains) was 12.85%, versus 13.3% a year earlier, with management attributing the drop to commodity and raw material inflation. Power tillers grew about 18% and power weeders about 56% in volume, while domestic tractors grew 4.5% and tractor exports were 275 units. Management declined to give a full-year FY27 outlook, saying it would be clearer in about a month, and said the July volume softness reflected a high base.

financial_highlights.metric: Operational EBITDA (excl. other income and fair value gain)

segments.name: Power tillers
segments.commentary: Volume grew about 18% in Q1; management cites 16-20% tiller growth over recent quarters and expects 15-20% to continue. Bajaj Finance retail financing volume roughly doubled to about 1,000 units from about 400 a year earlier, but still only 8-9% of retail sales versus a 15-20% target.

segments.name: Power weeders (SFM)
segments.commentary: Volume grew 56% in Q1 and management has been clocking 50-60% growth for several quarters. Retail counters added more than 500 in three months, taking the network toward a target of about 2,000 counters by year-end, on top of 750-800 SFM dealers.

segments.name: Tractors (domestic)
segments.commentary: Volume grew 4.5% in Q1 but supply lagged demand during ramp-up of the new variant, per management. Management expects Q2 growth, with substantial volume increases in Q3 and Q4; 40-50 HP is described as a crowded segment.

segments.name: Tractors (exports)
segments.commentary: 275 tractors sold in Q1. Europe: about 1,400-1,500 tractors per management, with entry into Turkey and the Nordics planned. Africa: 75 HP tractor shipments started. US expansion described as unclear.

segments.name: Reapers
segments.commentary: Seasonal product; volumes expected to pick up in Q2 with the harvest season. No figures given.

guidance_outlook: No FY27 outlook given; management said it is too early and will comment in about a month, since H2 depends on monsoon and rabi sowing.
Management said demand outlook is positive through September, with the next 15-20 days critical for kharif crop survival.
Long-term target of about 20,000 tractors by FY30 (including 5,000-6,000 international units); revenue vision of INR3,000 crores by 2030.
More than 30 tractor variants planned over the next three years; three global platforms (A, B, C) to launch over 12-36 months.
Tractor dealer additions targeted at 50-60 in FY27, versus 40-50 last year.
capex_capacity: A new production facility will need investment in roughly the next two years, per the CEO.
Tiller-tractor hybrid product (geared, with differential) to roll out from the factory starting this month, with substantial volume in Q3 and Q4.
International distributor logistics infrastructure delayed from Q1 but expected operational in Q3.
Hydrostatic transmission tractor being seeded for export markets, not sold in India.
Bangalore land of about 19 acres; manufacturing already moved out, only administrative office remains; no monetisation decision yet.
demand_pricing: Management says there is no demand issue in tillers; July volumes declined YoY against a very high base.
Tractor 40-50 HP segment is crowded and highly competitive; company is acquiring market share through product breadth.
Commodity inflation (steel, forgings, castings, aluminium, copper), elevated and volatile natural rubber prices, and high crude and freight costs weighed on margins.

Emission norm: Stage 5 for sub-25 HP tractors and tillers from October 2026, which management says will not create a big cost increase for end customers. Stage 5 for all tractors in 2032 could add 25-30% to tractor technology cost today, though this may fall over time.
Possible 100% US tariff under a bill in Congress is a risk to US expansion plans.

qa_highlights.question: Why is tractor growth lagging the industry despite new launches, and what is the strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 supply did not fully meet demand during the new-variant ramp-up; management expects Q2 growth and substantial increases in Q3-Q4. Strategy includes more than 30 variants over three years and state-by-state rollout of the FENTM series, starting with Gujarat, then Maharashtra.

qa_highlights.question: Update on the Bajaj Finance tie-up and other financing partnerships?
qa_highlights.answer: Retail financing reached about 1,000 units versus about 400 a year earlier, but only 8-9% of retail, against a 15-20% target. Other partners include Chola, TVS and nationalised banks.

qa_highlights.question: Is tiller export viable, and what new products are planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports were about 300 units last year. A geared tiller with differential for Europe and India and an electric tiller/weeder are in development.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any moderation in demand given July volume decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed July to a high base in tillers. It sees growth continuing at least through September, with tillers at 16-20% growth and weeders at 50-60%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capital allocation policy and non-core asset plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the policy is to maximise shareholder value and it expects to deploy capital over the next 18-24 months. No development on non-core assets yet.

qa_highlights.question: What are the implications of upcoming emission norms?
qa_highlights.answer: Stage 5 for sub-25 HP tractors and tillers from October 2026 is already ready. TREM 3A from April 2028 is covered. Full Stage 5 for tractors in 2032 may add 25-30% to technology cost at current prices.

risks_watch: EBITDA margin compression from raw material inflation; Q1 margin down about 45 bps YoY.
Tractor market share: domestic tractor growth of 4.5% trails the industry; July volumes were lower YoY.
Monsoon uncertainty over the next 15-20 days affects kharif output and rabi sowing.
Tariff risk to US expansion, and the possible 100% tariff bill in Congress.
Possible capex for a new facility in about two years; capital deployment plans to be disclosed in 18-24 months.
Management has not given a FY27 outlook; next update expected in about one month.
531266|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on long-term tractor and tiller growth targets, but cautious on near-term tractor volumes and on FY27 guidance, which it deferred pending monsoon clarity. Vague on capital deployment and inorganic plans.
key_quotes: And I have in last call also, in the last quarter I have said upwards of 15,000 numbers we will aim to reach, close to 20,000 numbers we will aim to reach in FY '30.
So giving an FY '27 outlook, I think it's a little too early.

531279|2026-06.headline: Trishakti Q1 FY27 total income up ~310% YoY to INR 1,680 lakh, EBITDA ~INR 1,087 lakh at ~65% margin, PAT INR 430 lakh.
531279|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 total income of INR 1,680 lakh (up nearly 310% YoY), EBITDA of INR 1,087 lakh (about four times YoY, ~65% margin), PBT of INR 538 lakh and PAT of INR 430 lakh, described as the strongest quarter in company history. Fleet utilisation was stated at 100% with fleet of roughly 155-158 machines. Management announced entry into wind energy equipment rental (900-ton cranes) and intent to expand into UAE and KSA, both subject to approvals. Executable order book for FY27 was put at INR 70-72 crore, with management saying signed contracts cover the full financial year.

segments.name: Crane / equipment rental (India core)
segments.commentary: Fleet of roughly 155-158 machines at 100% utilisation; FY27 executable order book INR 70-72 crore, with management guiding ~60% EBITDA and 25-30% PAT margin on that book. Management said payments from core business are received within 60 days.

segments.name: Wind energy equipment rental (new)
segments.commentary: Entry announced with 900-ton machines; first units expected in India in October; management expects revenue contribution in Q3-Q4 FY27 and yields similar to current fleet. No order book disclosed yet; 2-3 month advance LOIs referenced as possible.

segments.name: Tower cranes for data centres (new)
segments.commentary: Management disclosed two new machine types including 80-ton tower cranes for data-centre jobs; about INR 100 crore of CapEx placed for these and other machines, expected live in four to five months.

segments.name: UAE and KSA (planned)
segments.commentary: Planned entry via incorporation of new entities; management cited ~50-52% EBITDA margin expectation in KSA and yields of ~4% per month versus ~2.5% in India. Deployment targeted within two to three quarters; no roadmap or CapEx quantum given yet.

guidance_outlook: FY27 executable order book INR 70-72 crore, expected to deliver ~60% EBITDA and 25-30% PAT margin; revenue to rise as new machines start earning (~1.5 month lead time).
FY27 CapEx plan of INR 400 crore: ~INR 270 crore done, balance INR 130-140 crore to be spent in India in FY27; ~70% of balance already ordered per management.
Margins expected to normalise to 58-62% EBITDA once OEM warranty (about three years) ends and maintenance OpEx of 4-5% of top line starts.
Management expects utilisation to stay above 95-98%; fleet utilisation expected in the 90s after geographic diversification.
Borrowing cost expected to fall over the next few quarters as legacy 9.75% loans are repaid.
Management declined to give FY28 estimates; said a fuller roadmap would come in the December quarter call.
capex_capacity: Cumulative gross block: ~INR 270 crore per management; ~INR 235-240 crore excluding GST, per balance sheet comments.
FY26 CapEx was INR 210 crore against a guidance of INR 100 crore.

Wind energy 900-ton machines: 4-5 units could absorb the remaining INR 130 crore; OEM lead time about four months plus transport, ~5 months net; OEM output of ~2-5 machines per month cited as constraint.
Electric (EV) machines: ordered for two clients, ~2-month lead time, ~5% costlier than diesel units, expected in Q2 FY27.
UAE/KSA CapEx: no quantum given; management said a roadmap would follow once client demand data is collected by next month-end.
demand_pricing: Management says demand in India is strong, with post-monsoon mega-projects (including Reliance Kutch expansion) expected from October.
Client yields in India cited at ~2.5% per month; KSA yields cited at ~4% per month; KSA EBITDA margin expectation 50-52%.
Customers named: L&T, KEC, Afcon, Reliance; wind EPC players referred to as potential partners (names not given).
Management said the client bears diesel cost; Trishakti bears operator, helper and labour accommodation costs.
Competition: management said peers such as Sanghvi and Barker face supply constraints; no pricing data given. Wind market entry barriers cited as CapEx scale and OEM capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Current fleet size and wind energy segment economics, payback and order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Fleet 155-158 machines. Wind yields said to be similar to the current fleet; no existing wind client base; talks with large wind EPC companies; no payback figure given.

qa_highlights.question: Funding model for new cranes and debt position?
qa_highlights.answer: Banks now fund ~100% of machine cost (previously 20% down payment), with LTV ~50-60%; borrowings ~INR 80-85 crore; average cost ~8.5-8.75%; interest paid from month one with moratorium.

qa_highlights.question: Debtor days, reported around 200 days?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said core-business receipts are under 60 days and expects debtor days to fall to 60-70 in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why is utilisation and EBITDA better than peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Fleet is 2024-2027 vintage versus peers' 12-15 years; OEM covers maintenance for first three years; margin expected to fall to 58-62% later.

qa_highlights.question: Why expand into UAE and KSA, and what is the right to win?
qa_highlights.answer: Clients (L&T, KEC, Afcon, Reliance) asked for support abroad; KSA yields higher; management said it will target specific clients rather than compete on fleet size with peers such as Sanghvi.

qa_highlights.question: Seasonality and Q2 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 is softer for new CapEx due to monsoon; 100% utilisation with signed contracts for the full financial year.

risks_watch: Wind segment depends on 900-ton OEM supply (about 2-5 machines per month globally) and four-plus month lead times; no order book or revenue numbers disclosed yet.
UAE/KSA expansion relies on approvals, incorporation and client RFQs; management noted six-month demand halt in KSA and the paperwork delays; no CapEx quantum given.
Receivable days (~200 per analyst) versus management's 60-70 day target; watch next quarter's reported receivables.
Margin normalisation to 58-62% expected once OEM warranty ends, with 4-5% maintenance OpEx.
Quarterly revenue is 1.5-2 months of lag for newly commissioned machines; FY27 order book of INR 70-72 crore is small relative to the Q1 run-rate, so the disclosed figures need clarification.
Management declined FY28 estimates until December quarter.
531279|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and promotional on demand, margins and expansion, with repeated claims of 100% utilisation. Evasive on FY28 numbers, wind segment economics, UAE/KSA CapEx size, and receivable reconciliation; several answers were loosely framed.
key_quotes: Total income increased by nearly 310% YoY to INR 1,680 lakhs, while EBITDA grew by approximately four times YoY to INR 1,087 lakhs.
We continue to maintain 100% fleet utilization, reflecting the strong demand environment and the efficient deployment of our equipment across multiple infrastructure projects.
The demand is not the issue. The supply is the issue.
Currently, we are at 65% margins. Eventually, it will drop down to 58-62%.

financial_highlights.change: per management, at call; Q&A also cited INR 80-90 crore

financial_highlights.value: ~200 days (per analyst); management says core-business receipts under 60 days

531279|2026-09.headline: Trishakti Q2 FY27 revenue from operations rose 133% YoY to INR 1,551 lakhs, with EBITDA margin of 60.89%.
531279|2026-09.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 revenue from operations of INR 1,551 lakhs (up 133% YoY), EBITDA of INR 944 lakhs (up about 141%) and PAT of INR 519 lakhs (up 223%). H1 FY27 revenue was INR 2,989 lakhs, EBITDA INR 1,790 lakhs and PAT INR 949 lakhs. Management said about INR 370 crore of the INR 400 crore FY25-FY27 capex programme (incl. GST) is deployed, and announced "Mission 2030" targeting cumulative gross block above INR 1,000 crore by FY30. Receivable days rose over the past two years; management attributed this to a family settlement and said the cycle will normalise to about 60-65 days by year end.

financial_highlights.metric: Total H1 revenue incl. other income (per Q&A)
Gross block deployed vs FY25-27 programme (per Q&A)
financial_highlights.value: Approx INR 370 crore of INR 400 crore

segments.name: Crane and equipment rental (only segment discussed)
segments.commentary: Fleet includes rough terrain, all terrain, crawler, truck-mounted cranes, AWPs and 70-80m man lifts; management says fleet utilisation has been about 100% for three years. Management claims current ARR is about INR 78 crore after INR 40 crore of machines added in Q2.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of INR 60-65 crore retained; management said it expects to surpass this, with an executable order book of about INR 78 crore and core revenue from operations above INR 75 crore.
Mission 2030: cumulative gross block above INR 1,000 crore by FY30, possibly by FY29 if demand holds; peak revenue of around INR 300 crore cited.
Net debt expected at INR 400-500 crore until FY30; debt-to-equity to stay under 2 for the next 1-1.5 years; deleveraging expected after FY28.
Gross block expected to exceed INR 400 crore by FY27 year end, with INR 90-95 crore (ex-GST) in CWIP to be deployed in Q3 and about INR 125 crore of wind energy capex to arrive from early November.
ARR expected to reach about INR 120 crore from December 2026 to FY28 Q3 as CWIP machines deploy.
UAE and KSA expansion deferred until balance sheet deleverages; paperwork said to be 60-70% complete.
capex_capacity: INR 400 crore FY25-FY27 capex programme: about INR 370 crore deployed (incl. GST), more than 90% complete and ahead of schedule by about six months.
CWIP of about INR 77-78 crore ex-GST (INR 95 crore incl. GST) yet to be deployed in Q3 FY27; contracts reportedly already won for these machines.

Wind energy fleet expansion of about INR 125 crore; machines to arrive from early November; OEMs can supply only 4-5 machines per month in India; management targets replacing 250-300 machines as wind turbines shift from 3.3 to 5.2 MW.

Mission 2030 implies about INR 600-700 crore of incremental capex over three years (about 2.5% of net debt repaid monthly per management); 80-ton tower cranes for data centre work in transit, expected October-November.
Two 70-80m man lifts in fleet; management says about 20-22 such machines exist in India.
demand_pricing: Management says it receives RFQs daily as a central vendor to L&T, Reliance, Tata Steel and others; capex is concentrated in Gujarat and Odisha.
Management says crawler cranes above 150 tonnes are in strong demand; lower-tonnage truck-mounted cranes (80-100 t) are also in demand.
Fleet utilisation about 100% versus an industry figure of about 80% cited in the presentation; management attributes this to 11-12 month contracts versus competitors' 3-4 month contracts.

Management said rental yields are stable and not expected to rise; machine pricing in India is fixed by rental yields. Double-shift operation on 15-20% of machines is said to add about 50% revenue on those machines.
Management said a data centre tower crane generates much higher yield, and specialised 70-80m man lifts earn more than two times current fleet monthly revenue per machine.

qa_highlights.question: Why have debtor days risen over two years, and what is the plan to fix it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed a family settlement from three years ago that extended the cycle; about INR 75 lakh of provision was created this quarter and the cycle should return to about 60-65 days by year end. Management also said about INR 3 crore is over one year old, linked to the family settlement.

qa_highlights.question: How will the capex be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects net debt of INR 400-500 crore until FY30, funded by bank debt and internal accruals; most FY24-FY25 machines to be free of bank financing by FY28. Only fixed-rate loans apart from the CC limit, which was unused since January; 25 bps rate increase expected on new funding.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook on equity dilution and UAE/KSA expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt is the first priority and equity dilution is a final option; it could double the fleet by next year if debt is hard to raise. UAE and KSA expansion depends on internal accruals or equity; KSA local-stake rules reportedly changed after 1 May, allowing 100% ownership.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 revenue guidance INR 60-65 crore or INR 70-80 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance has always been INR 60-65 crore, and that INR 72 crore is only the current ARR; H1 revenue from operations was about INR 30 crore and it expects to beat guidance given the order book and H2 seasonality.

qa_highlights.question: Why are yields not improving with the new fleet, and is sustainability at risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yields are fixed and not expected to rise, but are sustainable; it cited three years of OEM free-of-cost servicing that defers opex, and buying power giving 5-10% machine discount versus competitors.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the receivable cycle elevated, and what caused the move in other current liabilities?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said month-end revenue is not billed for 10-12 days because overtime is computed, so trade receivables run high; the move to monthly GST filing shifted about INR 2.5-3 crore of billing, and cash flow should improve from this quarter. Other current liabilities relate to machine funding timing.

risks_watch: Receivable days remain elevated; management promises normalisation to about 60-65 days by Q4 FY27, with the annual report providing clarity.
Mission 2030 assumes fleet utilisation above 90% through FY30; management acknowledged this may be bold.
Debt-to-equity to remain under 2 for 1-1.5 years; net debt of INR 450-500 crore at peak, and possible equity dilution if debt funding is constrained.
Customer concentration in Gujarat and Odisha capex cycle; no soft commitments from customers for expansion, per management.
Machine import dependence above 250 tonnes and rising global machine costs; yields not expected to rise.
Gross block and revenue timing depend on delivery of wind energy and tower crane machines, now in transit.
531279|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and expansive on demand, utilisation and Mission 2030, but cautious on near-term balance sheet: management repeatedly deferred UAE/KSA expansion and equity dilution decisions. Answers on receivables and FY27 revenue guidance were somewhat repetitive, and some answers on yields and imported machine pricing were unclear.
key_quotes: Mission 2030 is not simply about owning more machines. It is about building a stronger Trishakti with greater capabilities, deeper customer relationships, and a larger role in India's infrastructure growth story.
We have already won contracts for all these INR 95 crores worth of machines.
Our guiding principle is simple. We want to grow with India, build for the long-term, and turn our ambition into measurable execution.

531335|2026-03.headline: Zydus Wellness Q4 FY26 net sales grew 62.1% on Comfort Click, but net profit fell 5.8% as seasonal brands dropped 9.8% in the domestic business.
531335|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 net sales rose 62.1% YoY, driven by the Comfort Click acquisition, with international like-to-like growth of 31.4% and domestic growth of only 1.7%. Domestic seasonal brands fell 9.8% as a delayed summer and rain in March and mid-April left retail and wholesale pipelines unfilled, while skin and hair care rose 39.7% and food and nutrition rose 9.4%. EBITDA grew 42.2% to INR 2,701 million, but net profit fell 5.8% due to higher finance costs from the acquisition debt, higher amortization of acquired brands and exceptional items. Management said operating leverage and the 17-18% EBITDA margin goal remain intact, while the seasonal recovery is expected from May onwards.

financial_highlights.metric: International incl. Comfort Click like-to-like growth (Q4)

financial_highlights.change: Seasonal -9.8%, skin and hair care +39.7%, food and nutrition +9.4%
Excluding exceptional items and amortization of acquired brands: +17%
Excluding exceptional items and amortization of acquired brands: +2.3%

segments.name: Seasonal brands (domestic)
segments.commentary: Q4 declined 9.8% and FY26 declined 18.8%; management attributed it to a delayed summer, March/April rains in the East and North, and missed retailer pipeline build. Seasonal carries above-average gross margin and EBITDA, so its weakness diluted the mix.

segments.name: Skin and hair care (domestic)
segments.commentary: Q4 grew 39.7% and FY26 grew 21.9%. Everyuth grew at strong double digits in FY26 and Cuticolor has been in the portfolio for about six months, sold in organized trade, modern trade and e-commerce.

segments.name: Food and nutrition (domestic)
segments.commentary: Q4 grew 9.4% and FY26 grew 15.5%. RiteBite Max Protein grew at roughly 50% in FY26 (about INR 244 crore per analyst), and management said actual branded growth is higher than reported due to contract manufacturing optimization.

segments.name: International incl. Comfort Click
segments.commentary: Like-to-like growth of 31.4% in Q4 and 29.5% in FY26. Comfort Click has been held for seven months; it is EPS accretive on a standalone basis in Q4, and the total-to-constant-currency gap is about 3%.

guidance_outlook: Management expects a recovery in seasonal brands from May onwards, and hopes some early-season misses can be recovered if summer progresses normally; it declined to forecast the full season.
Seasonal brands are expected to deliver consistent double-digit growth over three to four years, per management.
EBITDA margin aspiration of 17-18% reiterated for the next couple of years, measured excluding Comfort Click.
Comfort Click EPS accretive from Q4; management maintained its earlier guidance for the next two years.
Tax rate: FY26-27 is a mix of cash tax and deferred tax asset utilisation; FY27-28 is expected at about 25%, and FY28 at full cash tax.
Operating leverage expected to play out across the business excluding Comfort Click, which has largely variable spend.
capex_capacity: No capex, capacity, or utilisation figures were discussed on the call.

Launch activity in Q4: Max Protein Ultimate RTD, Max Protein Roots Ghee Jaggery Bar and Korean flavour chips; Sugar Free D'lite Choco Spread; Everyuth Tan Removal Face Wash; Glucon-D Recharge (liquid and sachets); seven Comfort Click launches across WeightWorld and Animigo.
Complan NutriGro was relaunched and moved to direct supply in the kids segment; VieMax by Complan launched in adult nutrition.
Channel expansion: Boots.com (UK) for WeightWorld and MaxMedix; Amazon UAE for vitamins and supplements.
Management said no divestments are planned, and capital allocation across brands is considered appropriate.
demand_pricing: Rural demand recovery continued to outpace the gradual urban improvement; quick commerce and e-commerce growth remained strong.
Quick commerce is about 7-8% of total domestic business; e-commerce is about 44-45% of organized trade.
Sugar Free Green reported its 20th consecutive quarter of double-digit growth; sweetener market share rose 24 bps (MAT March 2026); Nutralite grew at double digits despite gas supply headwinds.
Management said supply disruption from the Middle East conflict has been limited, affecting only a very small part of the business.
Gross margins were in line with plan; management cited brand-level margin improvements and exits from low-margin products.

qa_highlights.question: What weighed on seasonal growth and when will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed weak North and East markets, March/April rains, and a missing retailer pipeline build ahead of summer. It expects a recovery from May onwards but declined to forecast the season.

qa_highlights.question: How should margins be expected to move toward the 17-18% aspiration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross margins are in line with plan and the miss was driven by mix from weak seasonal sales. Umesh Parikh said operating leverage will play out across the business excluding Comfort Click.

qa_highlights.question: Is quick commerce changing the innovation and channel approach?
qa_highlights.answer: Dr. Sharvil Patel said the portfolio is designed for quick commerce consumers while keeping the traditional channel SKUs. Quick commerce is about 7-8% of domestic business.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Comfort Click margin trajectory and is it EPS accretive?
qa_highlights.answer: Umesh Parikh said Comfort Click is in line with or slightly ahead of expectations, and it became EPS accretive in Q4. The currency tailwind is about 3%, the gap between reported and constant-currency growth.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company divest slow-growing categories?
qa_highlights.answer: Dr. Sharvil Patel said there are no plans to divest any category and no major change in capital allocation.

qa_highlights.question: Is Cuticolor gaining traction?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Cuticolor is positioned as a derma-backed, Korean-origin safe hair colour sold in organized trade, modern trade and e-commerce, with repeat buying and early traction, after about six months in the portfolio.

risks_watch: Seasonal recovery depends on May-June temperatures and rainfall; a further weak season would hit the margin mix and FY27 growth.
Domestic growth was only 1.7% in Q4 and 2.4% in FY26, with the seasonal decline masking growth in the rest of the portfolio.
Net profit fell 5.8% in Q4 and 43.2% in FY26 despite EBITDA growth, as finance costs, amortization of acquired brands and exceptional items rose. Watch the tax mix in FY27.
Comfort Click's growth depends on European online VMS demand, FX (GBP/EUR) and the supply chain; the US and UAE are early-stage bets.
Watch whether the 17-18% EBITDA margin target is reached without Comfort Click, given that management gave no new timeline.
Management declined to disclose RiteBite and Nutralite brand-level growth and category data, and geographic segment disclosure is still under consideration.
531335|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the long term and on Comfort Click and RiteBite, but defensive on the near term: it attributed the seasonal miss to external weather and channel timing and gave no new margin timeline. Management avoided quantifying several questions, including brand-level growth, Comfort Click EBITDA and the timing of the margin target.
key_quotes: So our margins at a gross margin level has actually in line with what we have planned.
It's not about that we have to clean up every time. It is just that the pipeline buildup, which is in anticipation of summers, as the summer kick in, they start buying in advance.
So I think if we segment the portfolio, this concern remains. But now if you look at the new portfolio and as the expanded portfolio, the saliency of this business has reduced.
I think there are no new numbers. We've talked about in the next couple of years, we hope to get to our 17-18.

531335|2026-06.headline: Zydus Wellness Q1 FY27 consolidated net sales rose 66.7% YoY to INR 14,299 million, with EBITDA up 55.3% to INR 2,417 million, while reported net profit fell 7%.
531335|2026-06.overview: Consolidated sales grew 66.7% YoY to INR 14,299 million, helped by the Comfort Click consolidation, with EBITDA up 55.3% to INR 2,417 million and EBITDA margin up about 0.4% on a like-to-like basis. Reported net profit declined 7%, but profit excluding amortisation of acquired brands grew 26.5%. The domestic business grew 4.6%, with Skin & Hair Care up 34.5% and Food & Nutrition up 16%, while seasonal brands fell 12% due to unseasonal rains in the East and North. International (including Comfort Click) grew 24.8% like-to-like, and management said the summer weakness was recovering in the second half of the quarter.

financial_highlights.metric: Net profit excluding amortisation of acquired brands
International business (incl. Comfort Click) like-to-like growth
A&P as % of total sales (reported, incl. Comfort Click)
financial_highlights.change: Core like-for-like described as similar to last year

segments.name: Skin and Hair Care (domestic)
segments.commentary: Grew 34.5% in the quarter. Everyuth delivered strong double-digit growth, with its facial cleansing rank improving from fifth to fourth and tan removal ahead of internal expectations.

segments.name: Food and Nutrition (domestic)
segments.commentary: Grew 16%. Complan grew faster than the prior quarter despite category degrowth; RiteBite Max Protein grew more than double its historical rate; Nutralite delivered strong growth.

531431|2026-06.headline: Shakti Pumps Q1 FY27 revenue rose 37.9% YoY to INR859 crores, but EBITDA margin stayed near 9.6% on raw material and realisation pressure.

531761|2026-06.headline: Apollo Pipes Q1 FY27 volumes flat YoY; normalised consolidated EBITDA margin 7% after inventory write-downs, with Q2 guided to double-digit YoY volume growth.

Normalised consolidated business EBITDA margin was 7% (Apollo standalone 8%, Kisan standalone 6%), with the gap to reported numbers mostly inventory write-downs, plus about 0.5% cost from new businesses (Varanasi plant and Window profiles). Management says prices have stabilised since a MIP of $766/MT (about Rs.82/kg) was imposed about 12 days before the call, and expects Q2 to be better than Q1 and H2 better than H1. Management maintained high double-digit volume growth ambition and reiterated 7-8% business EBITDA margin for the next 12-15 months.

guidance_outlook: Full-year PAT of 100 crore-plus reiterated, described as a ballpark figure; no quarterly guidance given, citing SEBI limits and export volatility.

Real sales increment from the expanded capacity expected from FY28-FY29; no top-line or bottom-line numbers given.
Dividend payout to be maintained at about 25% even during the high-investment and debt phase.

South Korea: two customers have approved samples; bigger trial shipment is under way, with a first order targeted for October-December quarter.
Freight costs rose due to the US-Iran conflict and the Ukraine-Russia war; management said the rupee depreciation offsets part of this and demand has not been affected.

qa_highlights.question: What are realisations outlook for the next six months, and will domestic sales drive growth?

qa_highlights.question: Will profit stay around 100 crore for the year, and can raw material inflation be passed on?

qa_highlights.question: Why hold about 167 crore cash while borrowing 300 crore?

qa_highlights.question: Will branded domestic eggs become a substantial part of turnover within two to three years?

EC farm commissioning slippage (already about one week behind) and the 2.4 million bird target by September 28.
Debt rising to about 450 crore for the investment phase, with finance costs and dividend policy (25% payout) to watch.
Branded domestic egg strategy and business model still undecided; decision expected in about three months.
Freight cost increases from geopolitical events; South Korea first order targeted October-December.

532149|2026-06.headline: Bank of India Q1 FY27 net profit rose 36.23% YoY to Rs 3,068 crore; Global NIM eased to 2.52% and FY27 guidance was kept unchanged.
532149|2026-06.overview: Bank of India reported Q1 FY27 net profit of Rs 3,068 crore, up 36.23% YoY, with operating profit up 25.99% to Rs 5,051 crore and NII up 12.61% to Rs 6,833 crore. Asset quality improved on a YoY basis, with Gross NPA at 1.81% and Net NPA at 0.51%, and slippage ratio at 0.24%. Global business grew 16.57% YoY to Rs 17.55 lakh crore, with advances up 18.64%. Management reiterated FY27 guidance for advances growth of 15-16% and deposit growth of 13-14%, and raised a dollar-funding target of $4.2 billion through FCNR(B), OFCB/MTN and ECB routes by December 2026.

financial_highlights.change: GNPA -111 bps YoY; NNPA -24 bps YoY

segments.name: Advances
segments.commentary: Global gross advances Rs 7.98 lakh crore (+18.64% YoY); domestic advances Rs 6.74 lakh crore (+19.20%). RAM advances Rs 3.93 lakh crore (+19.75%), 58.30% of advances.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan book about Rs 57,000 crore at yield of about 9.10%, growing about 52% YoY; NPA below Rs 100 crore.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: International business touched about Rs 2.56 lakh crore; around 32% of international loan book is trade finance, which management plans to reduce.

segments.name: Mutual fund subsidiary
segments.commentary: Bank of India mutual fund AUM about Rs 16,000-17,000 crore; no near-term plan for public issue.

guidance_outlook: FY27 global advances growth guidance unchanged at 15-16%; global deposit growth guidance unchanged at 13-14%.
Global NIM guidance for FY27 at 2.55%-2.60%, though management said NIMs are under challenge.
Cost-to-income ratio at about 46% in Q1, but guided to 48%-49% on a consistent basis during FY27.
ROA guidance of 1% and above on a consistent quarter-on-quarter basis in FY27 (Q4 FY26 1.01%, Q1 FY27 about 1%).
FCNR(B) target of $1.2 billion by 30 September 2026; OFCB/MTN target about $2 billion by 31 December 2026; ECB target about $1 billion; total dollar raising about $4.2 billion by December 2026.
capex_capacity: Opened a dedicated Strategic Business Branch in Mumbai for high-value pool buyouts, co-lending, TReDS and supply chain financing.
Centralised Video KYC centre operationalised in Mumbai for end-to-end digital account opening.

ATM network rationalised: loss-making capex-model ATMs exited, reducing total ATM count by about 300.
Plans to add 19 emerging corporate credit branches' focus on Rs 25-250 crore mid-corporate advances; credit card base target of 3 lakh by end FY27.
demand_pricing: Corporate plus international pipeline about Rs 70,000 crore; total loan pipeline above Rs 1 lakh crore including RAM, digital, pool purchase, TReDS and supply chain financing.

Q1 fresh slippages including incremental NPA debits about Rs 1,800 crore vs Rs 2,100 crore in Q1 FY26; sectors under watch include chemicals, ceramics and oil/gas importers/exporters.
PSL income about Rs 277 crore in Q1; management said further PSL income possible in Q2 and Q3 but gave no number.

qa_highlights.question: Is stress visible in MSME and small loan accounts from the West Asia crisis, and what is the ECLGS position?

qa_highlights.question: What is the FCNR, OFCB/MTN and ECB plan and how does the leverage product work?

qa_highlights.question: Gold loan strategy and growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Gold loan book about Rs 57,000 crore at about 9.10% yield, growing about 52% YoY; NPA below Rs 100 crore; three-notice, 90-day auction SOP applied.

qa_highlights.question: Why did personal loans grow only 3%, and what is the credit card plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Guardrails were put on low-ticket and non-salaried personal loans, shifting to salaried and service-sector borrowers with NACH. Credit card base target is 3 lakh by end FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did CASA and retail term deposit ratios fall while cost of deposits dropped 15 bps?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a roughly 3% fall in CASA and retail term deposit share, as bulk deposits above Rs 3 crore were used to fund credit growth; cost of deposits was reduced via Rs 3-25 crore FD campaign and mix changes.

qa_highlights.question: Will NIM and CIR hold, and how will yields on advances move?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is NIM 2.55%-2.60% and CIR 48%-49% for FY27. Yields on advances expected to pause falling, supported by MCLR-linked loans, mid-corporate growth and reduced low-margin trade finance.

CIR guidance steps up to 48%-49% from about 46% in Q1, implying higher costs ahead.
Stress in chemicals, ceramics and oil/gas-linked import/export accounts; Q1 is seasonally high for slippages per management.
Declining CASA ratio (36.68%) and retail term deposits; cost of deposits benefit depends on bulk and FCNR mix.
Treasury gains in Q1 may not repeat as yields move adversely.

So , we are very confident that Quite a few.

532149|2026-09.headline: Bank of India Q2 FY27: H1 net profit about Rs 6,000 crore, Global NIM 2.47%, Gross NPA 1.60%; ECL front-loading planned from Q3, about 0.5% CRAR impact per year.
532149|2026-09.overview: Management reported strong YoY growth: global business up 21.13% to Rs 18.92 lakh crore, and global advances up 20.58%. Operating profit rose 33.18% to Rs 5,089 crore and net profit rose 25.32% to Rs 3,202 crore for Sept'26 (the Q2 figure as stated on the call). Asset quality improved, with Gross NPA at 1.60% and Net NPA at 0.42%, and credit cost fell to 0.12% from 0.15% in June'26. Global NIM eased 5 bps YoY to 2.47%, which management attributed mainly to FCNR-linked leverage. Management guided FY27 global advances growth of 15-16% and global deposit growth of 16-17%, and said ECL provisioning will begin from Q3 after Board approval.

financial_highlights.change: +Rs 20,539 crore YoY; ratio down from prior quarters
down 5 bps from 2.52% (management cited Sept'25 at 2.41%)

segments.name: Corporate and pipeline
segments.commentary: Corporate pipeline about Rs 65,000 crore as of 30 Sept; total pipeline across corporate, RAM, digital, pool/co-lending and supply chain about Rs 86,000-87,000 crore. Largest sector pipelines are renewable energy (over Rs 12,000 crore), power (over Rs 9,000 crore) and roads (over Rs 5,000 crore).

segments.name: RAM
segments.commentary: RAM advances up 18.68% YoY to Rs 4.13 lakh crore, 58.63% of gross advances, with RAM pipeline about Rs 20,000 crore.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan book about Rs 61,000 crore, mostly agriculture with some MSME and retail; gold loan NPA about 0.13%, LTV capped at 75%.

segments.name: Overseas book
segments.commentary: Overseas advances up 35.21% YoY to Rs 1.51 lakh crore against overseas deposits up 11.52% to Rs 1.37 lakh crore; FCNR raise of USD 2.2 billion was deployed into the international loan book.

segments.name: Supply chain / trade
segments.commentary: Supply chain book just over Rs 1,000 crore, with a Rs 1,500 crore first-year target; trade and MSME-linked assets grew about 10% in the quarter.

guidance_outlook: FY27 global advances growth guided at 15-16% and global deposit growth at 16-17%.
ROA guided above 1% on a quarterly basis; management said ROA was above 1% in March'26, June'26 and Sept'26, and expects above 1% in March'27. FY28 expected to be better.

ECL: provisions expected to start from Q3 FY27 after Board approval, with Q3 and Q4 as front-loading quarters; ECL regime applies from 1 April 2027. Ballpark CRAR impact about 0.5% per year over the next 4 years.
NIM expected to gain about 6-7 bps from the 25 bps repo hike, with deposit repricing staggered because about 60% of term deposits mature in 1 to 18 months.
Recovery in written-off accounts expected to sustain the run rate of about Rs 900-1,000 crore a quarter; non-interest income expected to hold above Rs 2,500 crore a quarter.
capex_capacity: Technology budget for opex and capex (core IT, digital, cybersecurity) said to be unchanged for FY27; Big Four consultants engaged on IT, digital and cybersecurity transformation.
AI policy approved by the Board; current AI use is predictive (Data Lake project), with analytics-led leads above Rs 21,000 crore.
Centralised supply chain branch in Mumbai handles pool, co-lending, trades and supply chain; 69 zones each asked to onboard one new supply chain vendor per month.
ECL: consultant onboarded; computation covers PD, LGD and SICR; Board note to be presented, with clarity expected by Q3.
demand_pricing: Domestic deposit and advances growth remained strong YoY, with management saying no impact from the macro headwinds is foreseen on FY27 business growth.
66% of domestic advances are repo-linked; the bank passed on the 25 bps repo hike on the day of the ALCO meeting.
Management said that about 7% of the retail portfolio is unsecured.
Infra: outstanding roughly flat YoY despite sanctions; some COD projects refinanced by other lenders at low rates, leading to churn; full disbursement takes 7-8 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How large is the ECL provisioning need, how much is already provided, and what is the road ahead?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the broad total will not be shared until the Board note; the CRAR impact is about 0.5% per year over 4 years, covered by profits (H1 profit above Rs 6,000 crore, run rate of about Rs 12,000 crore for FY27). No ECL provision has been made yet; front-loading expected from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Will the bank still meet its growth targets given global and drought headwinds?

qa_highlights.question: How much can NIM improve from the rate hike, and how will CASA be raised?

qa_highlights.question: What drove non-interest income, and why is other income down?
qa_highlights.answer: Recoveries from written-off accounts rose about 190% YoY to Rs 978 crore, and treasury/forex profit rose 157% to Rs 411 crore. Non-interest income was Rs 2,700 crore, up 25% YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Is there stress in the gold loan book after NBFC concerns?
qa_highlights.answer: Gold loan NPA is about 0.13%. Management said the SOP calls for two notices before auction, the CBS system monitors LTV, and the LTV is capped at 75%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the government stake and any capital raise plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Promoter holding is 73.8%, within the 75% SEBI limit. No government indication to reduce stake further and no capital raise plan.

NIM pressure from the FCNR leverage and falling CASA ratio (34.16%); pace of deposit repricing after the repo hike.
Dependence on lumpy recoveries from written-off accounts for non-interest income; 2-3 large accounts drove the quarter.

Overseas advances growing 35% YoY against 11.5% overseas deposit growth, which lifts reliance on FCNR funding.

key_quotes: So, ECL impact, we have already started doing the computation and other kinds of things, whether it is the PD, whether it is the LGD, SICR, and other kinds of things.
So, we expect that from Q3 onwards we will be making the provisions.
At present, we do not see any impact which may have on our business growth numbers for this financial year.

532156|2026-03.headline: Vaibhav Global FY26: PBT up 41% YoY, record FCF of INR272 crore, EBITDA margin 10.8%; FY27 guidance 9-11% revenue growth and 50-100 bps margin expansion.
532156|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was INR935 crore (+10% YoY) with EBITDA of INR96 crore (about 10.3%) and PBT of INR64 crore (+41% YoY). For FY26, revenue was INR3,691 crore, EBITDA margin rose 140 bps to 10.8%, and free cash flow hit a record INR272 crore. In-house brands crossed 50% of B2C sales about a year ahead of plan, and Germany reached full-year EBITDA breakeven. Management guided FY27 to 9-11% revenue growth and a 50-100 bps EBITDA margin improvement, but gave no constant-currency guidance. U.S. and U.K. growth stayed weak in Q4, and the Mindful Souls write-off of about INR25 crore was a notable one-off.

financial_highlights.change: ROE includes one-time MAT credit benefit per management

financial_highlights.value: INR6 per share (incl. final INR1.5 recommended)

segments.name: U.S.
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 1% in local currency; growth driven by digital mix, proprietary brands and AI-led marketing, with an in-house jewellery casting line in the U.S. helping offset tariffs.

segments.name: U.K.
segments.commentary: Q4 headline revenue flat (-1% local currency). Ideal World grew 15% while TJC declined 7%; U.K. EBITDA margin improved 220 bps YoY.

segments.name: Germany
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 7%; Germany achieved full-year FY26 EBITDA breakeven and is expected to contribute to group profit from FY27.

segments.name: Mindful Souls

segments.name: Product mix
segments.commentary: Lifestyle products are ~35% of total sales (medium-term target 50%). Lab-grown diamonds are ~11% of retail revenue at ASP around USD 250 (about 18 months old category).

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth guided at 9-11% (INR terms).
FY27 EBITDA margin expansion of 50-100 bps; gross margin and employee-cost efficiencies named as main sources, with shipping leverage unlikely this year.
Medium-term revenue growth guidance of 10-12% in INR.
Tax rate steady at around 22% for upcoming years.
Content and broadcasting spend to stay around 20% of sales; SG&A leverage not expected as TV savings are reinvested into digital.

Digital mix target of 50% of B2C sales by end of FY27; long-term peak EBITDA margin of 15% seen as achievable but no precise timeline.

New U.K. premises lease signed around February 2026; existing buildings to be vacated and move completed during FY27, consolidating 4 buildings into one.
100% of manufacturing power from solar; two U.S. sites and one each in U.K. and Germany run fully on renewable energy.

Digital ~44% of B2C sales in FY26; TV networks reached ~127 million households globally in Q4.

Elevated precious metal prices and cautious discretionary spend were cited as headwinds across core markets; tariff uncertainty persists.

qa_highlights.question: How can EBITDA margin rise back toward the 13-15% levels seen in FY22 when revenue is much larger?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Germany's breakeven and digital/paid media investments weighed on margin; margin rose from 7% (FY23) to 11% (FY26). Leverage expected in HR, SG&A and shipping; peak 15% seen as achievable over time but no precise timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Why not enter India, and will the company consider a buyback given the share price decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Sunil Agrawal said TV shopping never took off in India, so entry would be digital-only, to be considered after digital maturity in the Western markets. No buyback response was given on the call.

qa_highlights.question: Lifestyle 50% target versus in-house jewellery mix: are these contradictory?
qa_highlights.answer: Nitin Panwad clarified that in-house brands are 50% of B2C, of which 85% is jewellery and 15% lifestyle; the 35% lifestyle share and 50% medium-term target are for total group sales, including external and umbrella brands.

qa_highlights.question: Why are gross margins flat over three years despite digital mix shift, lab-grown and higher ASPs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said B2B sales growth (lower gross margin, no content cost) dilutes gross margin; Q4 gross margin rose ~180 bps and FY26 ~40 bps. Tariffs and metal spikes were a substantial headwind, and paid media channel margins are rising.

qa_highlights.question: Where will the 50-100 bps margin improvement come from, and what constant-currency growth to expect?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin first, then employee cost efficiency; shipping leverage unlikely this year and SG&A not expected to leverage. No constant-currency guidance given; INR guidance used given macro and business transition.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there a INR25 crore Mindful Souls write-off and what drove other expenses up ~16%?
qa_highlights.answer: Impairment reflects conservative testing as double-digit growth did not materialise; payback extended from 5 to 7 years. Other expenses rose on U.K. warehouse set-up, travel and AI technology spend, which management called temporary.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp rise in ROE and the ROU asset increase?
qa_highlights.answer: ROE was driven by PAT growth including a one-time MAT credit; normalised ROE still improves to ~15%. ROU increase is from a new U.K. premises lease signed around February 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Trends for U.S. growth and visibility from AI initiatives?
qa_highlights.answer: Sunil Agrawal cited AI across ad creatives, landing pages, conversion analytics and supply-chain forecasting, started about a year ago and accelerating recently. He expects U.S. and U.K. to reach double-digit growth in mid-to-long term but gave no timeline.
