qa_highlights.question: Why was the FY27 4-wheeler lighting guidance (INR100-150 crore in the prior quarter) cut?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target is pushed out by about two quarters, with FY27 slightly lower and 4-wheeler at about 2.5% of revenue. Orders are lumpy and conversion cycles with customers are longer.

qa_highlights.question: How will LED penetration move in 2-wheeler lighting?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said new models are coming with LEDs only and it expects about 70% LED in the next 24-30 months. It does not expect 100% because older models and aftermarket demand will continue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Yamaha?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Yamaha to be flat to growing for the year. Exports were weak on the cycle of European and US demand; domestic models such as R15, Aerox and XSR were slower in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin and cost pass-through outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided about 14% EBITDA margin for FY27. Raw material cost increases are expected to be passed on with a lag of a couple of quarters; the employee cost run-rate should hold for the next three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is capital allocation given about INR280 crore cash and no debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited organic and inorganic opportunities, plus possible future 4-wheeler and electronics capex. It will fund capex from internal accruals and would raise debt if needed for a larger opportunity.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company disclose wallet share by customer and segment?
qa_highlights.answer: An analyst asked for annual wallet share disclosure by segment. Management declined to share it in advance, citing customer confidentiality, and said it will announce models after customer launches.

risks_watch: 4-wheeler ramp has slipped again; FY28 is now the earliest meaningful scale-up, and analysts questioned competitive share gains.

Ramp of new wins: management expects H2 FY27 to be strong, but wins are phased transformational deals, so revenue conversion timing is uncertain.

532810|2026-03.headline: PFC FY26 standalone PAT hit a record INR 20,051 crore (+16% YoY), but FY27 spread guided lower at 2.40-2.50% and loan growth at ~10%.
532810|2026-03.overview: PFC reported its highest-ever standalone net profit of INR 20,051 crore for FY26, up 16% YoY, helped by 13% NII growth and about INR 1,800 crore of provision reversals. Net NPA fell to 0.13% and net credit-impaired ratio to a new low of 0.15%, after resolution of Sinnar Thermal and TRN Energy. Disbursements were INR 1,65,414 crore and loan book grew about 7% to ~INR 5.8 lakh crore, with management blaming elevated prepayments in a falling-rate cycle. Management guided FY27 spread to 2.40-2.50% and loan growth to around 10%, and outlined the proposed PFC-REC merger targeted for 1 April 2027.

financial_highlights.change: of which ~INR 800 crore from Sinnar/TRN resolution, ~INR 1,000 crore from DISCOM ECL reversal

financial_highlights.metric: Yield / cost of funds / spread / NIM FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR 18.55 per share total; final INR 3.95

segments.name: Renewables
segments.commentary: Group renewable book INR 1.65 lakh crore; PFC standalone renewables about 16% of lending. Major FY26 disbursements were hybrid solar-wind; ~INR 16,000 crore sanctioned for battery and pumped storage.

segments.name: Conventional generation
segments.commentary: About 50% of PFC lending now generation, of which 16% renewable and balance conventional (down from ~75% historically). Thermal and nuclear expansion cited as emerging opportunities.

DISCOM ECL provision reversal of ~INR 1,000 crore on improved ratings; AT&C losses 15.04%; DISCOMs posted first all-India PAT of ~INR 2,700 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 spread guided to 2.40%-2.50% (FY26 actual 2.46%), reflecting yield pressure from competitive pricing and forex-driven funding cost.
FY27 loan growth target around 10%; management says without FY26 prepayments growth would have been within the 10-11% guided range.
Management does not expect further RBI rate cuts in FY27 (repo held at 5.25%); expects prepayment pressure to moderate.
PFC-REC merger targeted to take effect 1 April 2027, subject to MCA, RBI, SEBI, cabinet and presidential approvals; government to retain government-company status.
Dividend to follow DIPAM policy of 30% of profit, subject to RBI NBFC dividend rules.
No specific FY27 disbursement guidance; FY26 sanctions INR 2.85 lakh crore with only ~INR 80,000 crore disbursed, so spillover expected.
capex_capacity: India installed capacity crossed 530 GW; about 55 GW non-fossil capacity added in FY26, a record (per management).
Peak power demand hit an all-time high of 256 GW in April 2026.
PFC sanctioned ~INR 16,000 crore cumulatively for battery and pumped storage projects.
Sanctioned-but-undisbursed pool estimated at INR 2.5-3 lakh crore (approximate, per management).
Infrastructure disbursements slow in construction phase; pick-up expected as projects approach commissioning.
demand_pricing: PFC consciously priced new lending competitively in FY26 amid banks' aggressive refinancing of commissioned renewable assets, which drove prepayments.
Banks most willing to refinance renewable portfolios given low gestation, early commissioning, certain cash flows and small ticket sizes.

Forex volatility (rupee depreciation vs USD and EUR, Middle East conflict, trade tariffs) raised FY26 funding costs; hedging covers 97% of USD 10.3 billion foreign currency borrowing, with management saying most mark-to-market losses are notional until maturity.
Borrowing mix: 80:20 domestic-foreign; 65% fixed-rate; 60% bonds, 20% bank term loans, 20% foreign currency (per management).
Repayments from borrowers in FY26 were about INR 1,28,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did disbursements and loan growth weaken despite stable disbursement volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said disbursements were broadly flat (INR 1,65,414 crore vs ~INR 1,68,000 crore) but DISCOMs shifted from short-tenor RBPF revolving loans (~6-month average) to 3-7 year loans, reducing rollover-driven disbursement counts; competition from banks also present.

qa_highlights.question: Why is only a fraction of sanctions disbursed and what is the timing?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 sanctions were ~INR 2.85 lakh crore with ~INR 80,000 crore disbursed; infrastructure disbursements are slow due to pre-commitment conditions, environmental and land approvals, and pick up near commissioning. Management said the balance is spilling over, not cancelled.

qa_highlights.question: How will the merger affect the government shareholding and borrowing limits?
qa_highlights.answer: Government shareholding would fall to about 41-42% post share swap; management said the government has committed to keep the merged entity a government company, with modalities yet to be decided. Single-borrower exposure limit to banks would fall from 25% to 20% for the merged entity, which management does not see as a challenge.

qa_highlights.question: What is the dividend and ROE outlook post-merger?
qa_highlights.answer: Dividend is 30% of PFC's standalone profit, of which PFC receives REC dividend as income; post-merger dividend will be declared on combined profit under DIPAM's 30% policy, subject to RBI rules. No ROE guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: How does PFC view the impact of a potential future rate hike?
qa_highlights.answer: About 65% of borrowings are fixed-rate and bond liabilities average 5-6 years, so repricing is gradual; lending rates are linked to the weighted cost of borrowing, so a rate rise would transmit slowly as older debt matures.

qa_highlights.question: Will the FY27 spread decline and what drives it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided 2.40-2.50% versus 2.46% in FY26, citing competitive lending rates, prepayment pressure and forex-driven funding costs; the spread is calculated on weighted average cost including foreign borrowings.

risks_watch: Continued prepayments and bank refinancing of commissioned renewable assets could keep loan growth below the ~10% target.
Rupee volatility and Middle East conflict could raise hedging and translation costs on USD 10.3 billion foreign borrowing; ~97% hedged.
Shiga Energy (INR 522 crore) co-lender approval pending within the INR 854 crore of Stage-3 assets resolved outside NCLT.
Stage-3 book of INR 6,323 crore across 19 projects; FY26 provision write-backs (~INR 1,800 crore) will not recur at the same level, so credit cost may rise.
Merger execution: government stake falling below 50%, creditor exposure limits, and workforce integration (about 520 PFC and about 1,000 combined employees per management).
New ECL norms from April 2027 under RBI; management says current policy broadly in sync with RBI IRAC norms.
532810|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on balance sheet strength, asset quality and the merger timeline, but cautious and somewhat defensive on loan growth, prepayments and spread compression. Management repeatedly deflected on exact disbursement, dividend and ROE figures, and said merger structure details are still under discussion.
key_quotes: Our net credit impaired asset ratio is at new low at 0.15%.
For FY27, we do not expect any further rate cut from RBI.
We are targeting for the merged entity to come into existence by 1st of April 2027.
So, spread is being worked out on the weighted average cost which constitutes both the domestic as well as the foreign borrowings.

532811|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 turnover rose 8.76% to INR1,322.30 crores but PAT fell 3.63% to INR80.14 crores; FY27 growth guided at 15-20%.
532811|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 turnover grew 8.76% YoY to INR1,322.30 crores, while PAT declined 3.63% to INR80.14 crores and EBITDA margin compressed to 9.35% from 10.17%. For FY26, turnover rose 11.38% to INR4,565.20 crores and PAT rose 31.17% to INR264.32 crores, with EBITDA margin at 9.52% versus 8.34%. Management blamed Q4 on labour flight from NCR and Bengal/Assam elections, NGT construction bans, a cash crunch in Assam, and war-driven LPG, fuel and supply-chain disruption. The company guided to 15-20% revenue growth and double-digit EBITDA margin for FY27, with an order inflow target of about INR8,000 crores, but gave no formal PAT guidance.

segments.commentary: Designs now approved and execution has picked up after a slow 1.5 years. FY27 execution target is about INR600 crores.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 15-20%, up from the 10-15% guidance given in prior years.
EBITDA margin expected to reach double digits in FY27 (currently 9.5% in FY26); management said margins will rise over the next two years as mechanisation takes effect.
FY27 order inflow target of about INR8,000 crores, including two L1 positions worth INR1,620.95 crores (RML Hospital Delhi and an Odisha government university project in Bhubaneswar).
FY27 capex about INR300 crores, down from an earlier guidance of about INR500 crores; FY26 capex was about INR274 crores.
Q1 FY27 expected to be very slow due to elections, labour exodus and Eid; ramp-up from Q2 and H2 significantly above H1.
Management said no guidance is prudent beyond FY27 given headwinds; a FY28 number was not given. Share buyback 'not in the offing'.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex about INR274 crores; FY27 capex planned at about INR300 crores, with depreciation rising in line.

Mechanisation (tower cranes, passenger hoists costing INR50-70 lakh each, batching plants, concrete pumps) is the stated response to labour shortage. Management estimated the IRR uplift at 7-10% and payback at 4-5 years on equipment with a 4-year life; other assets have a 7-8 year life.
Q4 depreciation was about INR29 crores; management expects a similar run-rate going forward.
Management is evaluating precast and pre-engineered building technologies, but said these would take 2-3 years to be used on projects.

Fixed-price orders are 11% of the order book; 89% of orders have built-in escalation clauses.
Government contracts use WPI-linked escalation with about a one-quarter lag; private contracts pass through volatile materials (cement, steel, grit, sand) roughly month-on-month.
Management is walking away from some projects, including with existing clients, and is raising bid margins by a couple of percentage points or more.
Pipeline has been slowed by the war, with developers delaying launches. The company is bidding selectively with existing or well-funded clients.
Competitors named: L&T, B&F, Nagarjuna, Shapoorji Pallonji, Kalpataru and Tata Projects.

qa_highlights.question: Will execution ramp up in FY27-28, and what growth should be expected?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 growth guided at 15-20% and order inflow target about INR8,000 crores. FY28 was not guided; management said FY28 is 'similar' and gave no firm number.

qa_highlights.question: Why are capex and depreciation rising while margins lag, and is this a new normal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the industry is at an inflection point due to labour shortage and taller, more complex buildings. Mechanisation benefits will take 2-3 years to show; FY27 capex is about INR300 crores, and depreciation is expected to grow in line.

qa_highlights.question: How are cost inflation and fuel-price increases being protected against?
qa_highlights.answer: Almost all contracts have escalation clauses; WPI-linked government recovery is lagging, and the company is seeking government compensation. Private contracts are pass-through for basic materials.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q4 margin fall was due to inflation vs. disruption?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the gross margin decline mainly to under-absorbed IDC and overheads from lost execution days, plus staff cost increments taken in January; inflation was a smaller factor, largely covered by escalation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the fixed-price share, and how is margin protected in the order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Fixed-price orders are 11% of the order book. The 89% escalation-linked share and a better mix (private/public, geography) underpin the double-digit margin target.

qa_highlights.question: Are IJPM and the two L1 projects likely to convert?
qa_highlights.answer: RML Hospital (Delhi) and an Odisha university project are old tenders with no LOA date. Either side can rebid or cancel if escalation has moved too far.

risks_watch: Prolonged war: fuel, metal and LPG prices, supply-chain delays (electrical panels now 4+ months vs 2 earlier), and a possible rupee impact.

Q1 FY27 expected to be very weak, so FY27 growth depends on a strong H2.

Government WPI-linked escalation is lagging; management has lodged representations with the government.
Pipeline slowdown and possible cancellation or rebidding of the two L1 orders.
Shareholders pressing for a buyback; management declined, citing the need for a war chest. Net cash position is INR817 crores.

So at the moment, the share buyback is not in the offing. That's not even crossed our mind.
Labour shortage is here to stay.

532814|2026-09.headline: Indian Bank Q2 FY27 net profit rose 14.71% to Rs 3,462 crore, helped by Rs 1,134 crore NSE MTM gain; guidance raised to 11-12% deposit and 13-14% advances growth.
532814|2026-09.overview: Indian Bank reported Q2 FY27 with total business up 14.22%, advances up 16.39% and deposits up 12.50% year on year. Profit was lifted by NSE-related gains (Rs 252 crore realised plus Rs 1,134 crore MTM), while operating profit excluding NSE grew about 18%. Management raised deposit and advances growth guidance, and flagged ECL provisioning (Rs 1,500 crore this quarter, Rs 2,500 crore cumulative) and a possible one-time HTM mark-to-market hit from 1 April. CASA ratio improved year on year to 39.36% but slipped sequentially on FCNR(B) inflows.

financial_highlights.value: Not stated in total; includes NSE gains of Rs 252 crore realised and Rs 1,134 crore MTM

financial_highlights.change: +8 bps YoY; domestic +1 bp QoQ, global +2 bps QoQ
Up from 38.87% YoY; slightly down QoQ
Down from Rs 1.62 lakh crore QoQ

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail advances grew 17.37% YoY; 92% of the retail book has CIBIL score above 750. Housing originated 60% via branches and 40% via DSAs, with zero co-lending.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agriculture advances grew 17.18% YoY. Agri gold loan book reached Rs 1.16 lakh crore, up about 22% YoY and 11% QoQ. Agri book outside drought-declared states is under Rs 1,000 crore.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME advances grew 19.06% YoY. About Rs 10,000 crore of MSME limits remains undrawn.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate advances grew 9.92% YoY. Pipeline of Rs 63,000 crore: Rs 30,000 crore sanctioned but undisbursed, Rs 10,000 crore in-principle approved, around Rs 23,000 crore early stage. Growth target now 10-12%.

segments.name: RAM
segments.commentary: RAM advances grew 17.74% YoY and constitute about 67% of the loan book.

segments.name: Treasury
segments.commentary: Treasury income ex-NSE was Rs 290 crore in Q2 (Rs 293 crore a year ago) and Rs 794 crore in H1 (Rs 854 crore). Net MTM loss of about Rs 11 crore. Management expects muted treasury income going forward.

segments.name: International book
segments.commentary: Loans against FCNR(B) deposits of about USD 2 billion were extended at preferential rates, with customers borrowing 90-96% of deposit value; this drove advances growth and is expected not to recur fully next quarter.

guidance_outlook: Deposit growth guidance raised to 11-12% from 9-11%.
Advances growth guidance raised to 13-14% from 11-13%; during Q&A CEO said 14-15% for next quarter and 12-13% in another comment.
NIM expected to expand 5-6 bps in Q3 FY27 (6-7 bps in one response); further moves depend on repo rate.
Recovery guidance unchanged; management expects to do better than guided.
Recurring ECL impact on credit cost maintained at 10-15 bps; one-time ECL impact expected at Rs 3,500 crore in total.
CRAR expected at around 17-17.5% by March-end; Rs 1,000-2,000 crore Tier 2 raise possible in January after Rs 1,000 crore maturity.
Bulk deposits to be raised cautiously; up to Rs 5,000 crore infrastructure bonds approved; CASA ratio target around 40%.
capex_capacity: Corporate credit capacity being built; corporate growth was 1-2% earlier, now targeted at 10-12% with credit training.

CRM launched in July added about Rs 1,500 crore of business in the quarter; fintech solutions to 223 companies and government departments added about Rs 5,000 crore; CMS-linked CASA about Rs 7,000 crore.
AI tools launched in Q2: TARA voice-based conversational banking and Smart Wealth personal finance tool; digital business grew 18% YoY.
Added about 2.5 lakh salary accounts this year so far against 3 lakh in full last year.
demand_pricing: Competition very high across segments; many banks lending housing below 7%. Management not chasing 20-25% growth, citing bottom-line and underwriting risk.
MCLR-linked book is 43.19% of advances; external benchmark-linked book is 49.65%. Benefit of 25 bp repo hike accrued from next day on external-linked loans.
Agri gold loan yield 8.85% (one-year MCLR), unchanged QoQ.
Working capital demand is stagnant: WCDL down Rs 1,000-2,000 crore and cash credit down Rs 1,000-2,000 crore over two to three quarters; management sees no crisis-led drawdown increase.
No stress seen in SME, agriculture or retail; SMA-2 accounts above Rs 25 crore total only about Rs 400 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standard asset provisions rise from Rs 733 crore to Rs 1,882 crore, and what drove miscellaneous income to Rs 468 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: ECL provision of Rs 1,500 crore this quarter and Rs 1,000 crore last quarter, totalling Rs 2,500 crore, against an expected total impact of Rs 3,500 crore. Other income includes Rs 271 crore of interest on an income tax refund, which may not recur.

qa_highlights.question: Where will treasury income come from?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects muted treasury income and does not expect high profits; not budgeted for high treasury gains. Forex income guidelines from RBI are being assessed.

qa_highlights.question: Will deposit and credit growth continue, and what drives NIM?
qa_highlights.answer: 12% deposit growth expected to be maintained; advances growth of 14-15% expected next quarter. NIM to rise 6-7 bps (later framed as 5-6 bps) this quarter, with bulk deposits repricing later.

qa_highlights.question: How much FCNR(B) was raised and how much is lent against it?
qa_highlights.answer: USD 2.3 billion (about Rs 21,000 crore) raised; fully utilised, with no surplus liquidity. Loans against it of roughly USD 2 billion, with customers borrowing 90-96% of deposit value.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECL recurring impact and is it passed on through pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Recurring impact of 10-15 bps maintained. Management does not expect clear pass-through to borrowers; models take 1.5-2 years to stabilise. LGD uses five years of history.

qa_highlights.question: What is the HTM mark-to-market exposure and could RBI provide an HTM reserve?
qa_highlights.answer: The Rs 3,500 crore covers only the credit book; HTM MTM would be additional, and the 10-year yield at 7.41% could cause a large impact across banks. Bank will first take it up with RBI.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of UCC guidelines on capital?
qa_highlights.answer: One-time CET1 and Tier 2 adjustment, with unutilised limits now included in credit RWA. CRAR at 16.21%, expected at 17-17.5% by March-end.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the borrowing increase and the LCR?
qa_highlights.answer: Only USD 400 million OFCB raised, no MTNs. Borrowings through repo and TREPS rose; OFCB funding at about Rs 10,000-11,000 crore is expected to remain. LCR 116%, with lower excess SLR affecting the ratio.

risks_watch: Recurring ECL impact of 10-15 bps on credit cost is maintained, but management says models take 1.5-2 years to stabilise and pass-through to borrowers is unlikely; watch credit cost against this range.
One-time ECL impact is expected at about Rs 3,500 crore in total, of which Rs 2,500 crore was provided in H1; the remaining Rs 1,000 crore is still to come.
HTM mark-to-market from 1 April is unresolved: the Rs 3,500 crore covers only the credit book, HTM MTM would be additional, and the bank will first approach RBI on possible relief.

FCNR(B) inflows of USD 2.3 billion are fully deployed into loans against deposits (about USD 2 billion) at preferential rates, and management expects this to not recur fully next quarter, so advances growth may slow.
NIM expansion depends on repo rate moves and on bulk deposit repricing; management is cautious on bulk deposits and CD rates have hardened recently.
Treasury income is expected to be muted; forex income guidelines from RBI are under assessment. Other income includes Rs 271 crore of one-time income tax refund interest.
LCR at 116% is affected by higher borrowings and lower excess SLR; OFCB funding of about Rs 10,000-11,000 crore is expected to stay on the book.
key_quotes: Treasury income will be muted going forward, and I do not expect very high profits from it.
So, 12% deposit growth is expected and we will be able to maintain.
It covers only the credit book. HTM will be over and above that, and we have to see.
I do not think Banks will be able to pass it on clearly, because some large loans are still being priced at very fine rates; passing it on will be very difficult.
532814|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on asset quality, deposits and the NSE-driven profit, with stated comfort on CRAR and growth. Cautious and non-committal on NIM trajectory, HTM mark-to-market exposure and recurring ECL pass-through, where management said it would wait and watch and that the regulator may not accept all assumptions.

532815|2026-03.headline: SMS Pharma FY26 revenue rose 13% to INR887 crores and EBITDA margin reached 20%; FY27 guidance is 15% revenue growth.
532815|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR238 crores with EBITDA of INR40 crores (17% margin) and gross margin down about 2% QoQ on higher solvent costs. For FY26, revenue grew 13% to INR887 crores, EBITDA rose 23% to INR171 crores (20% margin), and PAT rose 47% to INR102 crores, including INR14 crores from associate VKT Pharma. Management framed FY26 as a foundation-building year, with benefits expected in FY27 and FY28 from backward integration, new products and capacity. FY27 guidance is 15% revenue growth and an EBITDA margin above 20%, with management citing Middle East logistics risk as the reason for prudence.

financial_highlights.value: INR33 crores incl. INR12 crores from VKT Pharma; INR21 crores excluding associate share
financial_highlights.change: Ex-associate INR21 crores vs INR20 crores (as stated in call)

financial_highlights.value: INR102 crores; INR88 crores excluding VKT share
financial_highlights.change: +47% YoY reported; +28% ex-VKT vs INR67 crores in FY25

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall quarter on quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross margin fell about 2% QoQ because raw material consumption rose, driven by March solvent price increases caused by the war.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex breakup and timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Ibuprofen backward integration takes capacity from 500 to 800 MT per month; a brownfield block of 4-5 new APIs is also being built. Both are due by March 2027, with incremental revenue from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margins are achievable in the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the company's all-time high is about 22%, that it targets 22% in FY27 from 20% in FY26, and that it aims to exceed that afterwards.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the margin expansion, and which molecules?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited backward integration into intermediates, mainly for ibuprofen, plus the four or five new APIs, which are in new therapeutic categories and not the major ones. Management expects high-value share to rise to about 60%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the related-party transaction exposure with VKT Pharma and SMS Life Sciences?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SMS sells APIs to VKT (about INR40 crores), which it holds about 34-35% of. SMS Life Sciences is a promoter-linked company (about INR20 crores of procurement), with no investment by SMS Pharma. No plans to consolidate either entity.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue is ibuprofen?

532822|2026-03.headline: Vodafone Idea booked a Rs 55,622 Cr AGR-related exceptional gain, lifting Q4 FY26 net profit to Rs 51,970 Cr, while Q4 revenue grew 2.9% YoY to Rs 11,332 Cr.
532822|2026-03.overview: Vodafone Idea reported Q4 FY26 revenue of Rs 11,332 Cr (+2.9% YoY) and EBITDA of Rs 4,889 Cr (43.1% margin, +80 bps), with cash EBITDA of Rs 2,432 Cr (+4.8%). The headline profit reflects a one-time exceptional credit of Rs 55,622 Cr from the DoT AGR reassessment, which set dues at Rs 64,046 Cr versus the earlier frozen Rs 87,695 Cr. Operating KPIs improved: subscriber base stabilised at 192.8 Mn, customer ARPU rose 8.3% YoY to Rs 190, and 4G/5G mix reached 66.9%. Management reaffirmed a Rs 45,000 Cr three-year capex plan, which remains contingent on a pending SBI-led debt raise.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the strong sequential ARPU growth, and how much headroom remains versus peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited data usage growth of over 30%, Non-stop Hero (over 25% QoQ), and network additions. Levers include upgrading the 33% feature-phone base, converting smartphone users not on data, and moving 1.5-2 GB daily quota users to unlimited plans.

qa_highlights.question: Network opex fell sequentially despite site additions; is this sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Network cost was Rs 2,345 Cr versus Rs 2,361 Cr QoQ, helped by diesel reduction, electrification and self-optimised network. Management said cash-cost inflation will likely return as the efficiency benefit is lapped.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the debt raise and promoter shareholding after warrant and CLAM conversions?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt: SBI-led consortium is working on Rs 25,000 Cr funded and Rs 10,000 Cr non-funded facilities; no timeline given. Current holdings are Vodafone plc 16.07% and ABG 9.57%, which will change after conversions. No Board structure change expected.

qa_highlights.question: Why is churn elevated and how will customer additions improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Churn is about 4%, above industry; management is targeting a 0.5-0.6 pp cut as network investment arrests churn. Gross adds were held deliberately lower for better quality.

qa_highlights.question: How does management plan to reach a higher cash EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims for double-digit revenue growth and cash EBITDA margin above 35% in three to four years, from about 20.5% now. Levers are ARPU, industry pricing and lower churn in newly-built circles.

qa_highlights.question: How will spectrum payouts from FY28 be funded without further equity?
qa_highlights.answer: Tejas Mehta laid out Rs 105,000 Cr of sources over FY27-FY29 (cash EBITDA ~Rs 60,000 Cr, Rs 25,000 Cr funded debt plus rolling LC ~Rs 35,000 Cr, CLAM and tax refunds ~Rs 10,000 Cr), against uses of about Rs 100,000 Cr. Promoter infusion is additional.

532822|2026-06.headline: Vodafone Idea posted its first positive net subscriber addition since merger in Q1 FY27, with revenue up 6.0% YoY to Rs 11,689 Crore and Cash EBITDA up 13.5% to Rs 2,475 Crore.
532822|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 showed continued improvement: revenue rose 6.0% YoY to Rs 11,689 Crore, EBITDA reached Rs 5,034 Crore (43.1% margin), and Customer ARPU rose 10.2% YoY to Rs 195. Management reported the first positive net subscriber addition since the merger, led by postpaid and M2M, and a 24 bps YoY churn reduction. Capex was muted at Rs 1,930 Crore due to geopolitical supply-chain constraints, but orders of about Rs 9,000-9,100 Crore have been placed to be deployed over the next two quarters or less. Funding improved with Rs 1,183 Crore of warrant proceeds from the Aditya Birla Group, a first tranche of Rs 6,400 Crore in total, and rating upgrades to Crisil A-/Stable and ICRA A-(Stable).

532827|2026-03.headline: Page Industries Q4 FY26 revenue rose 14.1% to INR12,526 million on 10.8% volume growth; FY26 EBITDA margin 22%, guided to 19-21% for FY27.
532827|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 14.1% YoY to INR12,526 million, with volume up 10.8% to 54.5 million pieces and PAT up 9% to INR1,787 million. Management attributed the pickup to better consumer sentiment, a correction in distributor inventory that aligned secondary and primary sales, and product upgrades, with March the strongest month. EBITDA margin was 20.8% in the quarter and 22% for FY26, but management guided to a 19-21% range for FY27 citing marketing normalising to 5% of sales, input cost inflation and technology investments. Price increases were small: a 2% weighted average taken in January on product enhancements, with a further price increase planned in Q1 FY27 to cover input costs.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp volume acceleration to double digits, and what initiatives contributed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited better consumer demand in Q4 and recovery in athleisure after distributor inventory correction. Primary and secondary sales are now closely aligned, and March was strong. Management said upstocking was not encouraged and festive timing played little role.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 19-21% EBITDA margin range still hold after input cost inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management reiterated 19-21% for FY27, citing marketing at 5%, gross margin levels and salary costs as the basis. FY26 margin was higher because marketing was below 5% and gross margin held up.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY26 margin 22% and why should it moderate?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said FY26 benefited from marketing below 5% of sales and sustained gross margin. Normal marketing at 5% plus input inflation will pressure EBITDA, though not to the 22% level.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 2% price increase cover raw material inflation, and will there be more price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: The January 2% increase was for product enhancements, not inflation. A Q1 FY27 price increase is planned to cover input costs, with the pass-through share still undecided. Management said it would absorb costs if volumes were at risk.

qa_highlights.question: Will price hikes hurt volume elasticity in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to price only to the extent volumes are unaffected and would rather absorb cost temporarily in margin than cut volume.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of market share in economic segment and the new product pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said product upgrades launched in Q3 and Q4 were well received. Groove 3 is being extended to about 500 EBOs, select MBOs and e-commerce, and the men's Bonded collection outdoor campaign launched around 20 May.

qa_highlights.question: Are digital-first brands taking share, and is distribution friction behind us?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said e-commerce has grown for 3-4 years and Jockey ranks number one on major platforms in core categories. Auto replenishment has settled in for about 2.5 years, and a new distribution management system is being rolled out over the next year.

532835|2026-03.headline: ICRA Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 28.4% YoY, led by Research & Analytics (+56.8%) with Fintellix consolidated from October 2025.

Management flagged moderation in the Knowledge Services business and a margin-mix shift toward product-led businesses, and it sees near-term bond market softness offset by bank credit growth. segments.commentary: Revenue up 56.8% in Q4 and 29.8% for FY26, driven by Fintellix (consolidated from October 2025, roughly 26% EBITDA margin per notes). Excluding Fintellix, Knowledge Services grew modestly; Risk Management and Market Data grew healthily and turned profitable.

segments.name: Knowledge Services (KnowTech)

Fintellix shift from one-time licence plus smaller recurring fee toward annuity or subscription model is in progress, but not all clients are ready to adopt it.

qa_highlights.question: Reason for the Q4 FY26 EBITDA decline and whether new TBCB projects use service concession accounting?

qa_highlights.question: Phasing of capex and capitalisation in FY27?

532953|2026-06.headline: V-Guard Q1 FY27 revenue rose 23.5% YoY to INR1,810 crore and EBITDA margin widened to 10.5% from 8.4%.
532953|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 23.5% YoY to INR1,810 crore, with about 14% price and 9% volume contribution per management's blended split. EBITDA excluding other income rose 54.5% to INR191 crore, and PAT rose 76% to INR130 crore. Gross margin held at 36.9%, flat YoY, as management says roughly 75-80% of input cost inflation has been passed through. Management raised FY27 growth expectations to above 15% and reaffirmed a 9-10% EBITDA margin, while noting wires volumes were nearly flat under a large price increase.

segments.commentary: Revenue grew 19.2% YoY; induction cooktops spiked, other kitchen categories grew healthily, fans grew reasonably (pedestal fans short on inventory), and air coolers lost share due to weak North demand and competitor price delays.

segments.commentary: Revenue grew 18.3% YoY on a low base; management says integration is complete and a sales acceleration programme has started, with margin recovery expected to be more gradual than top-line recovery.

qa_highlights.answer: Blended growth split is about 14% price and 9% volume; about 80-85% of pricing actions are complete and roughly 75-80% of inflation has been passed through, with the gross margin expected to hold.

qa_highlights.question: Why is South growing faster than non-South for the fourth quarter in a row?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributes it mainly to weather: South had a good summer while North was disrupted by rain. It also said it took pricing ahead of competitors in non-South markets.

qa_highlights.question: Is the capex guidance still INR2-2.5 billion a year?

qa_highlights.answer: FY27 growth is expected to be more than 15%, with the 15% figure kept as the long-term aim. EBITDA margin is expected at 9-10%.

532967|2026-06.headline: Kiri Industries Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 63% YoY to INR 295 crore, with PAT of INR 270 crore driven mainly by INR 284 crore other income.

Standalone EBITDA was only INR 17 crore (5.86% margin), so PAT of INR 270 crore was largely a function of INR 284 crore other income, mainly treasury gains and inter-corporate loan interest. 533104|2026-06.headline: Globus Spirits Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13% to INR7,888 million, EBITDA up 33% to INR795 million, PAT up 49% to INR276 million (corrected figures).
533104|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 showed strong growth across manufacturing and consumer, with EBITDA margin of about 10% and PAT margin of about 4%. Manufacturing (ENA/ethanol) volumes reached 56.11 million litres at a record 89% utilisation, with EBITDA of about INR6.5 per litre within the INR5-7 guidance band. Prestige and above (P&A) revenue grew 35% YoY to INR550 million but still posted negative EBITDA of INR13 million, while Regular and Others (R&O) grew 10% with UP volumes scaling rapidly. Management flagged glass and PET cost-push of 10-17% and seasonal agri inflation in Q2, but said it is hedged within the margin band. Net debt was INR650 crore versus INR660 crore in March 2026. Several figures were corrected during the call: revenue should read INR7,888 million, PAT INR276 million and growth 49%, and EBITDA per litre INR6.5.

financial_highlights.value: INR7,888 million (corrected from INR7,887 million stated on call)
INR276 million (corrected from INR278 million stated on call)
INR6.5 (corrected from INR6.6 stated on call)

segments.name: Manufacturing (ENA/ethanol)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 11% YoY to INR4,720 million on 56.11 million litres sold, with 89% capacity utilisation on about 334 million litres installed capacity. EBITDA was about INR6.5 per litre, within the INR5-7 guidance band.

segments.name: Prestige and above (P&A)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 35% YoY and 38% QoQ to INR550 million, with volumes up 45% YoY to 0.42 million cases. EBITDA was negative INR13 million as spending went into distribution and brand building; brands cited were Terai, Snoski and Brothers & Co.

segments.name: Regular and Others (R&O)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 10% YoY to INR2,564 million, volumes up 13% YoY to 4.48 million cases and EBITDA up 13% YoY to INR440 million. UP R&O volumes grew 2.4x YoY and crossed 0.2 million cases per month.

guidance_outlook: Manufacturing EBITDA guided at INR5-7 per litre; management expects to stay in this range for all quarters of FY27.
R&O EBITDA margin guidance of 15-17%, with mix from lower-margin UP expected to pull margins toward 15-16% from the 17-18% of recent years.
Maintenance capex of about INR50-60 crore a year; no new ENA/ethanol capacity planned, with at most about 1% gain from technology. No capacity expansion planned through FY29.
P&A expected to reach profitability sooner rather than later, having moved from about negative 60% margin a couple of years ago to near breakeven.
Management expects the UK FTA to benefit the industry on Scotch costs, but said the timing and size of the benefit are uncertain and not yet visible in numbers.
West Bengal R&O re-entry expected within about 60 days of regulatory approvals, which management hopes come this quarter.
capex_capacity: Installed manufacturing capacity is about 334 million litres; Q1 utilisation was 89% against a guidance of about 85%.
UP plant utilisation was above 90% in Q1 per the CFO. About 25% of UP output is consumed captively and the rest sold in bulk, with optimisation still under way.
Capex has been limited to maintenance after UP commissioning; cash generation is being fed into P&A growth and debt paydown.
Management expects a 15-17% R&O margin band to hold while UP grows fast.
demand_pricing: Management expects ethanol demand for E20 blending to grow about 7-7.5% a year, in line with petrol growth; E85/E50 depends on car compatibility, which is limited for now.
Industry ethanol is in oversupply, but Globus ran at 89% by shifting ENA and ethanol mix and selling ENA in India and overseas, with overseas prices firming.
Glass and PET cost-push is 10-17% depending on brand and pack and is expected to persist; management says the company holds only slim packaging inventory.
Agri inflation is seasonal: Q2 and part of Q3 are inflationary, then prices ease as harvests arrive. Maize is partly hedged and FCI supplies a fixed-price portion; broken rice is unhedged.
UP is a large market of about 95 lakh cases a month. West Bengal IMIL is about 26-27 lakh cases a month, per management, slightly smaller than Rajasthan or Haryana.
Management says the company has 11 states total presence, with 4 core states plus Delhi and UP (5 core states overall), and a 6th state nearing core status.

qa_highlights.question: How will ethanol demand drivers develop given the E20 controversy, and could ethanol for cooking matter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said E20 is government policy, the controversy has not hurt offtake, and demand is growing about 7.5% YoY with sticky month-on-month volumes. Cooking-fuel ethanol adoption will be slow in India without distribution and canisters.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company expecting Bihar prohibition to be lifted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management believes prohibition in Bihar will eventually be reversed, but gave no firm timeline, estimating a change over about 1-2 years under the new Chief Minister.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of glass cost inflation on R&O and P&A?
qa_highlights.answer: Glass and PET cost-push is 10-17% by brand and pack and is expected to persist for some time, with energy costs also rising.

qa_highlights.question: Will UK FTA lower Scotch costs and expand gross profit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a tailwind as inventory transitions, but benefits depend on suppliers revising base prices. Rupee depreciation of about 20% against the pound limits the net impact, and the company is not a market maker on Scotch prices.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of R&O in West Bengal and how is the market structured?
qa_highlights.answer: Regulatory approvals are the last step and are expected this quarter; the company would return to the market about 60 days later. Management does not see the market turning unfavourable.

qa_highlights.question: How much growth can be achieved without capex, and at what utilisation is new capex needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has no plans for new ENA/ethanol capex beyond maintenance of INR50-60 crore a year; utilisation guidance is about 85%. Capacity is seen flat through FY29.

qa_highlights.question: What are the net debt and manufacturing margin trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt was INR650 crore against INR660 crore in March 2026. Manufacturing margin is within INR5-7 per litre and management is not concerned about changes in that range.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the IMFL brand mix shift across states, with some brands rising and others falling?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said brand growth varies by state because category mix differs (vodka, semi-premium and deluxe whisky markets). It said no brand is structurally declining and this will continue as the company enters new geographies.

qa_highlights.question: What is the UP ramp-up path and what is the margin outlook for R&O?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify quarterly UP additions but said UP is the next big bankable R&O opportunity, with a FY29 guideline already set.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company balance volume growth, input inflation and shareholder returns?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said manufacturing margin is protected by FCI fixed-price supply, maize hedging, and monthly pass-through in the flexi-price E&A business. P&A is self-funded from cash flow, with no further capacity expansion planned.

risks_watch: Glass and PET cost-push of 10-17% may squeeze R&O margins if pass-through lags.
Q2 agri inflation for broken rice (unhedged) and maize, plus the eastern India rainfall deficit.
West Bengal R&O re-entry depends on pending regulatory approvals; timing has slipped before.
P&A still loss-making at EBITDA level (negative INR13 million) and needs to reach profitability.
UP R&O mix is lowering margins toward 15-16%, and UP internal versus external sales mix is still being optimised.
Branded IMFL brand-level volatility across states; repeat behaviour for Mountain Oak and Brothers & Co. was questioned by analysts.
Ethanol overcapacity in the industry and policy ambiguity around E20 and higher blends.
533104|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on manufacturing and UP growth, with specific numbers and guidance reiterated. More guarded on timelines for West Bengal approvals, Bihar policy, UK FTA benefits and UP quarterly growth, where management declined to quantify.
key_quotes: Q1 has been a good start to the year.
Manufacturing is not a passive capacity business for us; it is an active operating platform.

The P&A business is not going to continue to grow in a manner where expenses are growing faster than revenue from approximately 60% or so negative margin a couple of years ago, we are now at nearly at breakeven.
We are firmly within that in Q1.

533106|2026-03.headline: Oil India FY26: consolidated income Rs 38,981 cr (+3% YoY), PAT Rs 7,551 cr (+7%), with Rs 11.5/share dividend repeated.
533106|2026-03.overview: Oil India's annual investors' meet (25 May 2026, transcript filed 29 May) covered FY26 results, a record 74-well drilling year and a 1.6x GRM uplift at subsidiary NRL. Consolidated EBITDA was Rs 13,498 cr (+5%) and PAT Rs 7,551 cr (+7%) despite crude realisation falling to $69/bbl from $78. Production was 6.64 MMtoe, with about 0.1 MMt lost to a 10-15 day economic blockade. Management reiterated the 9 MMTPA NRL expansion by March 2027, a roughly 100-well-a-year drilling plan, and offshore exploration reliant on the Samudra Manthan Mission for deep-water wells.

financial_highlights.change: ~60% drilling, ~25% capital projects, ~13% investments in subsidiaries/JVs
Down from $78; lowest in last 5 years

segments.name: Upstream (Oil India)
segments.commentary: Production 6.64 MMtoe (3.45 MMt oil, 3.15 BCM gas); daily crude peaked at ~81,354 bpd, with management citing 82,200+ bpd as of late May. Record 74 wells drilled (22 exploration, 52 development) and 307 workovers. 2P reserve replacement ratio 1.20 (vs 0.94) on 231 MMt reserves, 31-year reserve life.

segments.name: Midstream (pipelines)
segments.commentary: Numaligarh-Siliguri product pipeline expanded from 1.72 to 5.5 MMTPA, completed at Rs 750 crore vs Rs 860 crore approved outlay; PM inaugurated 13 March 2026. Duliajan-Numaligarh gas pipeline expanded from 1.2 to 2.5 MMSCMD, mechanically complete, awaiting a ~7-day NRL shutdown to commission.

segments.name: Downstream (NRL, 100% subsidiary of Oil India Ltd, 3 MMTPA)
segments.commentary: Record 103% crude throughput, 99.1% availability, 87.25% distillate yield and 727 TMT MS output; GRM 1.6x prior year. Navratna status conferred Dec 2025. Expansion to 9 MMTPA targeted for March 2027, with polypropylene unit on track; expansion capex ~Rs 46,000 crore including ~Rs 7,200 crore for PPU.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Mozambique force majeure lifted Nov 2025; two LNG trains of 13 MMTPA targeted for end-2028 or early 2029, with ~$1.8 billion committed and ~$300 million cost escalation pending CCEA approval. Russian assets (Taas, Vankor) have returned ~$1 billion in dividends. Libya 95/96 major commercial discovery.

segments.name: New energy and others
segments.commentary: Oil India Green Energy Ltd (wholly-owned) has ~2 GW renewable capacity in JVs pipeline and 2 CBG plants under construction, with 2 more awarded or in tender, against a target of 25 by 2030. 49 KTPA bamboo 2G ethanol plant inaugurated Sept 2025; NRL green hydrogen plant of 2.4 KTPA (Rs 138 crore) due by end-2026.

guidance_outlook: Production: 4 MMtoe achievable with ~100 wells drilled per year; long-term target 12 MMtoe by 2030 (from 10).
Gas: 3.35 BCM guided for FY27; ~5 BCM targeted by FY28 once Duliajan feeder line and DNPL expansion are commissioned.
NRL: CDU/VDU ~mid-July 2026 (~400 TMT output after that, mostly diesel), DHDT about a month later, PFCC/RPTU by Dec-Jan, full 9 MMTPA by March 2027 (stabilised by March 2028).
Capex: rollover of ~Rs 10,000 crore a year for ~100 onshore wells per year, plus shallow-water offshore drilling.

Offshore: deep-water well targeted for spud around June 2027; four-plus-four deep-water wells at ~Rs 1,200 crore each (Rs 4,800-5,000 crore), contingent on Samudra Manthan Mission sponsorship. Shallow-water wells ~Rs 800 crore each.
NRL excise duty: ~Rs 3,000 crore accrued in FY26, with 50% NE excise benefit and no sunset clause at 9 MMTPA; management expects calibration if FOB HSD prices fall.
capex_capacity: Drilling: 74 wells in FY26 (record); released drillable location inventory ~218 vs ~45 earlier; average Assam shelf depth ~4,300 m.

Offshore: deepest well (6,000 m, Kerala-Konkan) at ~3,400 m; Andaman well 3 drilling complete and testing; KG DSF appraisal well underway; gas occurrence in Andaman well 2 under appraisal with 600 sq km 3D seismic.
Feeder/evacuation: Duliajan feeder line (3.5 MMSCMD) authorised; PNGRB approval Feb 2026, mechanical completion FY28, offtake up 40%.
Gas capacity: production ~8 MMSCMD, ramp-up path to 13-15 MMSCMD with 15-18 pure gas wells identified.
Crude import pipeline Paradip-Numaligarh (9 MMTPA) 92% physically complete as of 30 April 2026; 99% ROU acquired.
demand_pricing: Realisation: crude at $69/bbl in FY26, lowest in 5 years; government moves on royalty and post-wellhead cost realisation cited as cash-flow support.

New well gas: 1.5 MMSCMD allocated to NRL, priced at 20% premium over APM, but only accrues once NRL is commissioned and allocation is confirmed; allocation priority runs CGD, fertiliser, refinery/petchem, then power.
Gas to NE CGD: ~50,000 SCMD allocated to NE Gas Distribution and Purbabharati Gas Distribution as NRL reseller.
Product demand: management cites 7-8% growth in refined product consumption; NRL export via Indo-Bangladesh pipeline optional, not the basis for 9 MMTPA.
Competition/partners: TotalEnergies signed technology service agreement (Nov 2025) for offshore seismic and exploration support, with a say in investment decisions.

qa_highlights.question: What is the offshore exploration capex and how will the capability gap be addressed?
qa_highlights.answer: Shallow-water well ~Rs 800 crore; deep-water wells ~Rs 1,200 crore each, four plus four wells (~Rs 4,800-5,000 crore), contingent on Samudra Manthan sponsorship. Government also identified Rs 3,200 crore for four stratigraphic wells jointly with ONGC.

qa_highlights.question: NRL excise duty benefit in FY26 and impact of recent duty cut?
qa_highlights.answer: ~Rs 3,000 crore accrued in FY26; no sunset clause on 50% NE excise benefit at 9 MMTPA. Management expects excise to be recalibrated against HSD FOB prices if they fall.

qa_highlights.question: NRL 9 MMTPA viability, and terms of the TotalEnergies arrangement?
qa_highlights.answer: Viability rests on domestic demand (7-8% growth) and NE/mainland logistics, with Panchgram, Singimari and Jogighopa depots and Siliguri tankage. TotalEnergies is a service agreement, with Total able to weigh in on investment decisions.

qa_highlights.question: NRL timelines, first product output, and capex spent/remaining?
qa_highlights.answer: Mother units by end-July; ~400 TMT output after that, mostly diesel. Full 9 MMT by March 2027, stabilised March 2028. Expansion capex ~Rs 46,000 crore including PPU (Rs 7,200 crore).

qa_highlights.question: FY27 production, gas and capex outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: 4 MMT with 100 wells; gas 3.35 BCM in FY27 and ~5 BCM 18 months out. Rollover capex ~Rs 10,000 crore per year.

qa_highlights.question: Current production exit rate and gas ramp path?
qa_highlights.answer: Current crude ~82,200 bpd, a record. Gas ~8 MMSCMD now; management says 13-15 MMSCMD possible with new pipelines, with first accrual only on allocation and commissioning.

qa_highlights.question: Mozambique incremental equity outflow?
qa_highlights.answer: ~$1.8 billion already committed; ~$300 million escalation pending CCEA. Further phases to be assessed after FID.

risks_watch: Samudra Manthan Mission notification and sponsorship mechanism still pending; deep-water capex is uncertain until notified.
NRL expansion timeline: DNPL commissioning depends on a 7-day NRL shutdown deferred by Middle East crisis; CDU/VDU mechanical completion due mid-July 2026.
New well gas premium (20%) depends on government allocation; accrual timing tied to CGD saturation in NE.
Excise benefit (~Rs 3,000 crore in FY26) may be recalibrated if product prices fall.
Production risk from economic blockades (lost ~0.1 MMt in FY26) and natural decline of 10-12% a year.
Mozambique cost escalation (~$300 million) awaiting CCEA approval.
key_quotes: Dr. Ranjit Rath, Chairman and Managing Director, Oil India Limited and Chairman of Numaligarh Refinery Limited.

The idea is that through a mechanism while the data collection in terms of 2D and 3D seismic data will be sponsored by the Government, the Government would also sponsor the deep water and ultra deep water wells which we intend to drill in our exploration acreage.

So, we would really come to know once it is notified, how many numbers of wells government is going to sponsor 100%, how many wells government is going to sponsor 50% or precisely how the mechanism would be.
So, excise to my opinion is going to get calibrated based on the overall FOB of HSD which is the driving force for the refinery transfer price which happens between NRL and the OMCs.
Now the question is this New well gas needs to be allocated by government.
533106|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on production records, NRL commissioning and offshore ambition, repeatedly stressing government support and "on track" delivery. Cautious or evasive on Samudra Manthan Mission mechanics, deep-water well sponsorship terms, and NRL excise recalibration, which management repeatedly deferred until notification or government approval.

533106|2026-06.headline: Oil India Q1 FY27 standalone PAT rose to INR2,870 crore from INR813 crore, on record EBITDA of INR4,605 crore and crude realisation of USD98.73/bbl.
533106|2026-06.overview: Standalone operating revenue hit a record INR7,958 crore and EBITDA a record INR4,605 crore, with margin above 54%. Crude output was 0.95 MMT, up 11%+ YoY, and daily output peaked at 10,921 MT on 27 June, later 11,017 MT on 3 August. Subsidiary NRL ran at 105% capacity utilisation with a GRM of USD35.95/bbl (about USD33 ex-inventory gain), and consolidated PAT was INR4,026 crore. Management guided to roughly 1 MMT crude per quarter and about 3.9–4 MMT for FY27, and gas evacuation hinges on DNPL/IGGL connectivity.

segments.name: Upstream (standalone crude and gas)
segments.commentary: Q1 FY27 production was 1.707 MMBoE, with crude at 0.95 MMT (+11%+ YoY) and gas up 0.4% QoQ. Gas off-take has been constrained at about 2.93 BCM by evacuation limits, and management targets 3.8 BCM next year and about 5 BCM by FY29.

segments.name: NRL (refining, material subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Capacity utilisation was 105%, distillate yield 87%, and GRM USD35.95/bbl vs USD5.02 a year earlier. Management said about USD2 of the GRM was inventory gain, and OMC discounts under SAED were netted off.

guidance_outlook: Crude production: about 1 MMT per quarter from now on, roughly 3.9 MMT for FY27 with a possible touch of 4 MMT; FY29 target of about 4.2 MMT from main producing areas, with upside from near-field exploration.
Capex: FY27 budget is INR8,600 crore (to be revised at the next review); Q1 spend was about INR3,050 crore, including INR1,230 crore on exploratory drilling.
Wells: FY27 target of 100 wells (42 exploratory, 57 development), up from 74 in FY26; a further 10% rise is intended for FY28.

NRL: CDU/VDU, DHDT and SRU to be commissioned by Oct–Nov 2026, remaining units by 31 March 2027, reaching about 75% of 9 MMT rated capacity by Q4 FY28; Paradip–Numaligarh pipeline mechanical completion targeted October and commissioning by December 2026.
Gas: 200 m connection within the NRL campus (2–3 months) to link DNPL with IGGL; DFL feeder line about 20% complete; big jump in evacuation expected from Q1 FY28 and about 5 BCM by FY29.
GST on royalty: about INR2,500 crore (excluding interest) is already provided; payment to be made, with no prospective interest. The Assam land tax is a contingent liability with no P&L impact.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex about INR3,050 crore: survey INR450 crore, exploratory drilling INR1,230 crore, development drilling INR700 crore, capital equipment and projects INR350 crore, subsidiaries/JVs/overseas INR350 crore. FY26 actual capex was INR13,026 crore.
Wells drilled in Q1: 17 (7 exploratory, 10 development). Drilling history: FY25 22 exploratory and 35 development; FY26 22 exploratory and 52 development.

Andaman: Vijayapuram-1 spend about INR1,000–1,050 crore; hydro-frac testing in August; fourth Andaman well by a jack-up rig targeted for December 2026; 600 sq km of new 3D seismic to be processed by October.

Deep water (Mahanadi and KG): 4,200 line km and 5,300 sq km of 3D acquired; first deep-water rig expected June–July 2027, second by March 2028. Government reimbursement of up to INR675 crore per well is proposed under the Samudra Manthan scheme.

NRL expansion: about INR30,000 crore spent to date, with INR34,000–35,000 crore expected for the refinery project and another INR7,200–7,300 crore for the PPU project. NRL debt is about INR19,000 crore.
demand_pricing: Crude realisation was USD98.73/bbl and gas USD7.19/MMBtu; new-well gas is priced outside APM, and incremental volumes will all be new-well gas.

NRL's GRM is about USD33 excluding the roughly USD2 inventory gain. Diesel and petrol discounts to OMCs under SAED ran at INR13/l to INR3/l for petrol and INR10/l to nil for diesel during the quarter, and have reappeared as a monthly recalibration.

Gas off-take from BCPL is stable at about 1.25–1.35 MMSCMD (about 4.25 MMSCMD returned to the grid by Oil India). NEEPCO is cutting gas use in favour of hydro, and excise benefit fell as government calibrated excise to hold retail prices.
NRL operating cost is about USD4.5–5/bbl, targeted to fall to about USD3.5/bbl as expansion units stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current crude run-rate, and can production sustain the 10,921 MT/day level?
qa_highlights.answer: Director Operations said the company expects about 1 MMT per quarter from here, citing workover, well intervention and optimisation; output reached 11,017 MT/day on 3 August.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for gas ramp-up from 2.93 BCM to about 5 BCM?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 and H1 FY28 would be flat to slow; the big jump is expected from Q1 FY28 once the 200 m NRL link and DFL/IGGL are complete, with about 1.5 MMSCMD of extra headroom from DNPL capacity expansion and 3.5–4 MMSCMD of evacuation planned.

qa_highlights.question: What is the normalised NRL GRM, and what is the exploration capex outlook given the government support?
qa_highlights.answer: NRL GRM was about USD35 including about USD2 inventory gain (about USD33 ex-gain). Exploration: 100 wells targeted in FY27 and a 10%+ rise intended thereafter, with deep-water programme funded in part by government schemes.

qa_highlights.question: What is the NRL expansion status and the Paradip–Numaligarh pipeline timing?
qa_highlights.answer: CDU/VDU mechanically complete, with three units to be commissioned by Oct–Nov 2026 and the rest by 31 March 2027; pipeline ROU is secured except about 8 km, with commissioning by December 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt position across the group?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone: USD1.4 bn loan for Mozambique. Singapore subsidiary: USD500 mn bond due May 2027. NRL: about INR19,000 crore. Total group debt about INR37,233 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did contract costs rise, and what is the GST-on-royalty payment outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Contract cost rose by about INR146 crore QoQ to INR615 crore, mainly offshore G&G costs. About INR2,500 crore GST on royalty (excl. interest) is already provided, to be paid with no prospective interest; the Assam land tax is a contingent liability.

risks_watch: Gas evacuation remains the binding constraint: BCPL and NEEPCO off-take is seasonal and the DFL/IGGL and 200 m NRL link are still pending.
NRL's GRM is inflated by SAED-linked discounts and an inventory gain of about USD2/bbl; the normalised GRM is about USD33 and the discount level is calibrated monthly.
Andaman Vijayapuram-1 and -3 testing is still pending; a write-down or capitalised-cost review is possible after the September decision.
Assam land tax case is being withdrawn via the state legislature; the contingent liability is removed only once withdrawal is effective.
Q2 gas volumes could dip with monsoon and tea-garden seasonality from October; exploration cost (G&G) inflated opex in Q1.
533106|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on production records and NRL operations, with repeated emphasis on execution and integrated planning. Cautious and hedged on gas evacuation timelines, which management tied to pipeline completion, and some answers were given loosely or deferred. Frequent line disconnects and unclear figures in Q&A reduced precision on several numbers.
key_quotes: So at present we are on a path where you can, we can see that we are going to achieve close to 1 MMT each quarter this year.

533148|2026-06.headline: JSW Energy added 873 MW in Q1 FY27 (about 1.1 GW since April) and holds ₹12,880 crore cash, while net debt is about ₹55,000 crore and TTM net leverage is 4.95x.
533148|2026-06.overview: Revenue was flat YoY at ₹5,437 crore and EBITDA rose 2% to ₹3,103 crore, while PAT fell to ₹533 crore (₹471 crore attributable) on higher depreciation (+20% to ₹890 crore) and interest (+16% to ₹1,519 crore) from new capacity. Net generation fell 5% YoY to 12.9 BU, with hydro down about 26% on weak hydrology and thermal down 6%, partly offset by solar up 29%. Management reiterated FY27 targets of 3 GW capacity addition and ₹20,000 crore capex, and outlined a pumped storage pipeline, the Maruti Clean Coal acquisition, and a 600 MW Mahanadi unit 4 for FY28.

segments.name: Renewables (solar and wind)
segments.commentary: Solar generation rose 29% and wind 3% YoY, supported by 1,168 MW of added capacity; renewables are about 61% of the 14.6 GW installed base. Solar PLF was about 21-22% in Q1 and management expects a higher second half.

segments.name: Hydro
segments.commentary: Portfolio generation fell about 26% YoY on weak hydrology (Sutlej basin -39%, Ravi -24%, national -7%) despite Tidong and Kutehr additions. Karcham, Baspa and Kutehr were above 100% PLF in July.

segments.name: Thermal
segments.commentary: Thermal generation fell 6% YoY to 8 BU; Mahanadi lost about 184 MU (about 7%) due to a 17-day evacuation outage, which management says falls under force majeure. Thermal fleet is 5.7 GW, with open capacity under 4%.

segments.name: Battery storage (BESS) assembly
segments.commentary: The 5 GWh battery plant won a first large external order of about ₹440 crore; management guides to about $2.75-3/kWh margin, roughly $15 million a year and close to ₹150 crore EBITDA.

guidance_outlook: FY27 target of 3 GW capacity addition and ₹20,000 crore capex reaffirmed; about 1.1 GW already added since April, with about 225 MW more in July.
Net leverage to be below 5x by 2030; FY28 capacity addition guided to be in the same range (about 3 GW), with FY28 connectivity details promised soon.
Mahanadi unit 4 (600 MW) targeted for commissioning in FY28, taking the plant from 1.8 GW to 3.6 GW; capex expected to be 25-30% lower than greenfield.

Preferential promoter allotment balance of about ₹1,875 crore due before June 2027; management expects operating cash flow plus fundraise proceeds to cover about ₹12,000-12,500 crore of the ₹20,000 crore capex.
Bhavali (1,500 MW) and Kandhaura (1,680 MW; 1,500 MW PPA signed with UP) pumped storage projects; management expects significantly high-teen IRRs. Narihalla (Karnataka) PPA expected soon.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 commissioning of 873 MW, including 150 MW early commissioning of Tidong Hydro (originally October 2026) that added ₹20-22 crore EBITDA in Q1.

Connectivity: 300 MW under TGNA expected to convert to GNA before 31 August; 400 MW O2 Power (Rajasthan) connectivity now expected September-October. Management says the remaining 1.9 GW of FY27 additions is fully connected, with about 530 MW off-grid captive.

Salboni 2x800 MW: TG order placed with Toshiba JSW Power Systems, land fully acquired, site work underway. GE Durgapur boiler facility acquisition expected by end of Q1; nameplate 1.1 GW, targeted 1.6 GW after debottlenecking.
Halol (Gujarat) wind blade plant commissioned 8 June 2026 with 450 blades per year (about 600 MW of wind); Chitradurga plant expected by FY27.

Pumped storage readiness: Bhavali has environment clearance, land mostly acquired, L&T civil and Voith electromechanical orders placed; Kandhaura awaiting forest clearance and connectivity, with readiness expected in Q4 FY27.
demand_pricing: Q1 FY27 national power demand grew 8.5% YoY (July month-to-date about 12%); peak demand hit 271 GW in May, above FY26's 245 GW peak.
DAM prices averaged ₹5.10/unit in Q1 FY27 vs about ₹4.40 in Q1 FY26 (about 16% higher).
API4 coal index rose to $113 in Q1 FY27 from $90 in Q1 FY26 (about 25%); management says it is resilient through its shift to domestic coal.
Management said it is seeing buyer interest for 600 MW-scale thermal PPAs, citing imported-coal replacement demand.
Maruti Clean Coal & Power (300 MW Chhattisgarh): 195 MW net PPA with Rajasthan discoms (14-year residual life), about 64 MW merchant; acquisition agreement signed.

qa_highlights.question: How is the thermal fleet handling sub-technical-minimum operation during midday solar hours?

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of boiler sourcing for Mahanadi unit 4 and Salboni?

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin on the BESS external order?

qa_highlights.question: Are the 1.9 GW of remaining FY27 projects connected, and what about FY28?

qa_highlights.question: What drove the lower thermal PLFs, especially at Utkal and Ratnagiri?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed Utkal's drop to a planned unit shutdown for annual availability in Q1, with availability above 91% in July. Ratnagiri's drop was a planned shutdown plus weaker June demand.

qa_highlights.question: Why is PAT under pressure and when will it improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said interest is higher during early years post-commissioning, and EBITDA-to-PBT conversion should improve as assets stabilise over 4-5 years.

risks_watch: Weak hydrology: Q1 hydro generation down about 26% YoY; monsoon recovery in July is the key check.

Project execution: pumped storage timelines, Mahanadi unit 4 (FY28), the GE boiler acquisition, and the Chitradurga blade plant by FY27.
Balance sheet: about ₹1,875 crore of promoter preferential money due before June 2027; gross debt about ₹74,000 crore, and FY28 funding needs still to be disclosed.
Mahanadi evacuation outage (17 days, about 184 MU) to be recognised under force majeure; the outcome is not yet confirmed.

we are absolutely 100% secured from connectivity and which is all commissioned also.

533150|2026-09.headline: Godrej Properties Q2 FY27 bookings fell 6% YoY to INR8,008 crore, but sustenance sales rose 83% to INR5,054 crore and collections hit INR5,318 crore.
533150|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 bookings were INR8,008 crore from 3,658 units (6.2 mn sq ft), down 6% YoY and 7% QoQ, while H1 bookings grew 7% to INR16,669 crore. Sustenance sales were the standout at INR5,054 crore. Collections rose 31% YoY to a record Q2 of INR5,318 crore and operating cash flow was INR1,584 crore. Reported P&L fell sharply: EBITDA down 72% to INR171 crore and net profit down 62% to INR154 crore, which management attributed to back-ended deliveries and JV exit accounting (Mahalunge, Orris). Management guided H2 bookings of INR22,500-25,000 crore and a strong Q3 launch pipeline.

financial_highlights.value: INR8,008 crore (3,658 units, 6.2 mn sq ft)

segments.commentary: Godrej Trilogy (Mumbai), Godrej Vanantara (Bengaluru), Godrej Samaris (Gurugram) and Godrej Brooklyn Avenue (Hyderabad) each contributed over INR500 crore to bookings. H2 cash collections of INR15,000 crore and operating cash flow of INR7,000 crore, with the company expecting to be free cash flow positive for the period.
Expects FY28 to show positive free cash flow and a 20% reported ROE.

Attributable share of sales was 85% in Q2 and 90% in H1.

Only about one-third of the annual launch pipeline was launched in H1; launches are picking up from October.

About 80% of Q3 approvals were secured before the quarter began; the residual is expected shortly after Diwali. For Q4, about 80% of approvals are targeted between end-November and mid-December, with the rest by mid-January.

Management said the company is not pushing price aggressively and is focused on end-user sales quality.
Sustenance was 60-40 vs launches historically; Q2 mix was 63% launch and 37% sustenance per management's framing of the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA and net profit fall sharply despite higher sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajendra Khetawat said the Mahalunge JV became a 100% owned project after the partner exit, so the bulk of profit had been recognised earlier through DM fees and overheads, which led to near-equal sales and cost of sales. The Orris settlement also picked up losses on consolidation in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: How long will sustenance sales stay high and what is the launch vs sustenance mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Gaurav Pandey said H2 launches will likely outperform sustenance, and the 60-40 launch-sustenance mix is a guide that can flip if launches slip. Sustenance strength reflects a deliberate push after Gurgaon and Mumbai launches slipped.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company exceed its H2 sales guidance and how much can it add to pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Pirojsha Godrej said the top end of the H2 range (INR25,000 crore) would imply a 40% five-year compounded booking growth. He said the company will not hold back if opportunities arise beyond the 15-20% FY28 growth target.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the H2 launch pipeline has approvals?
qa_highlights.answer: About 80% of Q3 requirements were secured before the quarter, with the rest expected after Diwali. For Q4, management targets about 80% approvals by mid-December and the rest by mid-January.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook on BD and competitive intensity for land?
qa_highlights.answer: Pirojsha Godrej said competition is ongoing but opportunities meeting return thresholds are available, and BD will remain opportunistic. Gaurav Pandey said one or two deals could close in the quarter if terms fit.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company near FCF-positive status in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Gaurav Pandey said there is a high probability of being FCF positive in Q4 under aggressive internal scenarios, while noting this is not an obsessive target. FY28 is described as almost certain for operating cash flow guidance.

Execution of FY28 reported ROE of 20% and positive FCF depends on project completion accounting.

I don't think we believe in this sort of trying to just optically show a very, very steady performance.

533151|2026-06.headline: D.B. Corp Q1 FY27 EBITDA rose about 19% to INR 1,647 million, with margin up 250 bps to 26.1% on advertising growth of about 10%.

Profit after tax rose about 25% YoY to INR 1,007 million. Advertising revenue grew about 10% to INR 4,320 million, with management attributing the growth to both volume and a small pricing contribution. Circulation was flat at INR 1,204 million, with copies down to about 38 lakh from 39 lakh in Q4 while cover price stayed at an average INR 4.93. Management said newsprint rose about 13% YoY and about 8% QoQ and expects further increases in Q2 before easing from Q3.

533151|2026-09.headline: D. B. Corp Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue fell to INR614 crore (from INR635 crore) and PAT to INR69 crore (from INR93 crore), largely on a festive shift into Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Q3 and full-year advertising and circulation revenue guidance?

qa_highlights.question: Why did circulation decline and are cover price hikes planned?

qa_highlights.question: What is the newsprint cost trend and inventory policy?

533155|2026-03.headline: Jubilant FoodWorks Q4 FY26 call: management flags 100-120 bps energy-led margin hit and short-term pressure, with no quantified margin timeline; stores to rise to 230-250 in FY27.

Q4 LFL was about 0.2% per an analyst; the call did not restate a reported figure. The drop in average order value followed the cut in minimum order value from Rs 149 to Rs 99 to win share. Management reiterated the 200 bps margin improvement target over the long term but declined to say how long near-term inflation pressure would last. Energy (LPG/PNG) was quantified at 100-120 bps, which the company said it has passed on through pricing, while wage and labour-code costs were discussed as further headwinds.

533179|2026-09.headline: Persistent Q2 FY27 revenue rose 20% YoY to USD 487.6M, but EBIT margin fell to 15% and reported PAT dropped 25.4% on Nagarro deal costs.

533293|2026-06.headline: KOEL Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 16% to INR1,461 crore, but EBITDA fell 4% and margin contracted to 11.2% on commodity costs and export weakness.
533293|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 16% YoY to INR1,461 crore, led by domestic power gen (+18%), industrial (+19%) and distribution & aftermarket (+20%), while international fell 11% to INR106 crore. Standalone EBITDA declined 4% YoY to INR165 crore and margin compressed to 11.2% from 13.5%, which management attributed to lower export volumes, elevated commodity costs and a lag between cost inflation and price realisation. Standalone net profit fell 9% to INR99 crore. Consolidated revenue rose 13% to INR2,000 crore, with consolidated net profit down 17% to INR111 crore. Management said pricing actions have been taken across most businesses and expects profitability to improve as they flow through over coming quarters.

533295|2026-06.headline: Punjab & Sind Bank Q1 FY27: business up 15.27% YoY to Rs 2,66,420 crore, advances up 19.35%, net profit up 23.05% to Rs 331 crore.

Asset quality improved on a YoY basis (GNPA 2.21%, NNPA 0.65%), but the quarter included about Rs 123.5 crore of provisions, of which about Rs 150 crore was ECL build-up, which management said was proactive.
