539876|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 11% YoY to Rs 2,283 Cr, with EBIT margin exiting near 10% versus 6.8% in H1.

Management said EBIT margin improved from 6.8% in H1 to about 10% in Q4, driven by operating leverage, premiumisation, pricing and cost optimisation. Consolidated EBITDA was Rs 271 Cr (11.9% margin). Butterfly returned to double-digit revenue and profit growth, and management took an impairment on its Butterfly carrying value, which is non-cash but hits ROCE and asset turnover. Management also announced a new super-premium product line, Crompton Rhion, and an identical dividend to last year.

YoY, Q4, with steady EBIT margins

segments.name: Small domestic appliances (SDA)
segments.commentary: Management said FY26 growth was in the early 20s percent and Q4 growth close to 30%, with a step-up in profitability. New launches included infrared cooktops, air fryers and premium juicers.

segments.commentary: Q4 growth of 14%. Government share of B2B mix fell about 500 bps in FY26. Y-o-Y margin said to be roughly flat despite materially higher ad spend in the quarter.

segments.name: Butterfly Gandhimathi
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue up 17% with steady EBIT margins and higher advertising spend. Management says it is back to strong double-digit growth in both revenue and profit, and an impairment was taken on its carrying value.

segments.commentary: Solar pumps revenue was about Rs 200 Cr last year and grew significantly this year. Wires rollout ramping from Tamil Nadu and Karnataka to other states over the year.
Solar rooftop execution stepped up in the last 2-3 months.

qa_highlights.question: What price increases were taken against the cost inflation, and how much has been passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Two ECD price increases since the war began, ahead of competition; about 7-8% cumulative in fans in FY26, mostly in Q4, which offset material inflation. Further inflation came in April, and management is waiting to see before deciding pricing for the rest of Q1 and Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY26 contribution and FY27 ramp-up from solar pumps and rooftops?
qa_highlights.answer: Solar pumps grew from about Rs 20 Cr three years ago to about Rs 200 Cr last year, and grew strongly again this year. Rooftop order book is about Rs 500 Cr, with about 5,000 homes installed. Management declined to give an FY27 contribution estimate.

qa_highlights.question: Why did lighting margins dip, and is growth troughing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins were roughly flat YoY despite higher ad spend. Growth came from a shift away from government B2B contracts (down about 500 bps), a higher-ASP B2C mix (panels, floodlights) and a reset supply chain and cost base.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Butterfly impairment's tax impact and is the merger still planned?

qa_highlights.question: What is the national rollout plan for wires?
qa_highlights.answer: Launched in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, with ramp-up across the country over the year and distribution via the full Crompton network. No specific revenue targets given.

qa_highlights.question: Is there channel or payment stress in the value chain?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said traditional-trade debtors are flat YoY, solar pump collections are on track, and FY26 operating cash flow crossed Rs 500 Cr. Management said builder and contractor exposure is small and no stress is seen so far.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation from the war and fresh April increases; margin recovery depends on pass-through and whether competitors follow on pricing.
Butterfly impairment hits ROCE and asset turnover; watch Butterfly growth in NEW markets outside the South.
Water heater BEE norms from July may add cost and pressure margins in LDA.

540005|2026-09.headline: LTM Q2 FY27 revenue rose 5.1% YoY in constant currency to USD 1.24bn, with order inflow of USD 1.3bn and EBIT margin at 15.6%.
540005|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was USD 1.235bn, up 1.1% QoQ and 5.1% YoY in constant currency, with INR revenue of Rs 11,808 crores (+13.6% YoY). EBIT margin expanded 10bps QoQ to 15.6%, while PAT margin fell to 11.7% from 12.7% because Q1 included a one-time gain on Voicing.AI. Cash conversion weakened sharply (OCF/PAT 39%, FCF/PAT 24%) due to gratuity funding under the labour codes, an ad hoc TDS timing effect, and advance tax. Order inflow of USD 1.3bn was AI-centric, short-tenure deals, and management is deliberately shifting KPIs away from TCV. Management reiterated that H2 will be better than H1, with the Saudi business (routed via a JV and classified under Tech) a drag this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is the seasonal Tech decline recurring every year, and what is the Saudi effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Tech decline reflects the annual renewal cycle of the top tech account (fiscal starting July) plus Saudi business routed through a JV with a tech company. Management expects Tech to return to normal growth from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Will TCV become less relevant, and will LTM disclose ACV?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI deals are shorter and faster to revenue, so TCV understates them. ACV disclosure is planned but deferred by about one more quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Can growth reach high-single or double digits by FY28, and is FY27 close to FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 lost about 0.6-0.7% of growth to Saudi, expects H2 better than H1, and aims for FY28 as the stronger year; FY27 growth near FY26 is an endeavour, not guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Is the top BFSI client's vendor spend cut a medium-term risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the consolidation from 50+ vendors to five is a multi-year benefit to LTM, with productivity headwinds already passed through in Q3-Q4 of last year.

qa_highlights.question: Why is payout low versus peers, and what are capital allocation plans?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said payout rose to about 45% from about 40%; reinvestment via M&A and organic investment (BlueVerse, GCC, talent) is prioritised. M&A is open but must be white-space and fairly priced.

qa_highlights.question: Has the macro or pricing environment changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said macro is unchanged over the last two to three quarters; traditional large-deal pricing is weakening, while AI rate cards carry a premium.

risks_watch: Saudi/Middle East disruption: Rest of World revenue fell 1.4% QoQ; management says it is beyond LTM's control.

TCV and order inflow visibility: deal mix shift to short-tenure AI deals makes TCV less comparable; ACV disclosure is pending.

540180|2026-06.headline: VBL Q2 CY2026 revenue rose 20.4% to Rs 84,512.3 mn and EBITDA 17.2% to Rs 23,430.4 mn, with India volume up 14.4%.
540180|2026-06.overview: Consolidated sales volume grew 19.8% to 466.7 million cases in the quarter, with net revenue up 20.4% year-on-year. India volume grew 14.4%, with growth of about 20% or more in every month since March except April, which was roughly flat due to El Nino-driven rain. International volumes rose 38.4%, including 11.8 million cases from the newly consolidated Twizza business in South Africa. EBITDA margin fell 76 bps to 27.7% on Twizza's lower margins, while India margin improved 38 bps. Management also extended the PepsiCo bottling licence to April 2049 and announced the Calpis tie-up with Asahi and the Devyani Kenya acquisition.

financial_highlights.metric: Revenue from operations (net of excise and GST)

financial_highlights.value: Rs 0.50 per share (25% of face value), cash outflow ~Rs 1,691 million

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Volume grew 14.4% in Q2 with 20%+ monthly growth from March except April (about flat). India EBITDA margin improved 38 bps on operating efficiencies, partly offset by higher transport and distribution costs. Low-sugar/no-sugar products were about 73% of consolidated volume in H1.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Volume rose 38.4% including 11.8 million cases from Twizza in South Africa; ex-Twizza growth was above 25%. Management said all African markets are growing except Zambia, which is small and slower. Twizza operates at lower margins, which diluted group EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Value-added dairy (VAD) and Nimbooz
segments.commentary: Management said VAD is growing above 40% and Nimbooz above 30% for the company, about 3x-4x the overall business. Growth figures were given only as ranges, with no absolute values.

segments.commentary: Management said this business is growing about 50%. No absolute figures or targets were given.

guidance_outlook: Management expects India growth of at least 20% month-on-month after June, with July tracking the same trend.
Management said India can keep growing in double digits despite a stronger competitive field from Campa and Coca-Cola, and argued the industry is growing about 20%.

Raw material costs have risen with the West Asia crisis. Part of the increase is booked in Q2 under average costing, and the balance will hit Q3. Management said the impact will not be large and pricing will hold.
Management said EBITDA margins can be maintained even in a high-crude year and would improve once the conflicts ease.
Energy drink labels must drop the word 'energy' within 90 days, per the regulator's guidance. Management said volumes are returning to STING as new labels roll out.
Management will not scale Rs 10 pricing for now, as it is not profitable for the company, unless monthly growth falls below 20%.
capex_capacity: H1 net capitalised capex of ~Rs 9,500 mn: ~Rs 2,000 mn brownfield India including a value-added dairy line at Supa, ~Rs 1,000 mn for a snack plant in Zimbabwe, and ~Rs 4,000 mn for market infrastructure (visi-coolers, glass bottles, pallets, vehicles).
Capital work-in-progress of ~Rs 4,900 mn at 30 June 2026, mainly South Africa expansion and a CSD line in Kenya.
Inorganic capex of Rs 11,314 mn for the Twizza Limited acquisition in South Africa.
Devyani Food Industries (Kenya) business acquisition agreed, giving a ready go-to-market for CSDs and energy drinks in Kenya.
Twizza in South Africa helped overcome capacity constraints, with the company strengthening its manufacturing and route-to-market footprint there.
demand_pricing: India Q2 volume +14.4%, with April about flat due to heavy rain. May seasonality has shifted (it used to be about 15% of business before 2025), and management says non-weather months show high double-digit growth.
Rs 10 price point: management said it has not scaled it up because it is not profitable and the company is growing 20%+ without it. Some markets are pushing Rs 10 packs, but the mix is small.
Pack changes: the company is upsizing and downsizing packs by market. Management said volume is reported on an 8-ounce basis, and realisation per 8-ounce case and gross margin are said to be stable.
Competition: Campa Cola is expanding at Rs 10 and Rs 20 price points, and management said the Rs 20 gap has narrowed. The 400 ml Rs 20 pack is driving recruitment.
GST cuts: management said the impact on dairy, water and soda was minimal. Some prices were held despite geopolitical cost pressure.
Management declined to give market share data, saying it does not track share.

qa_highlights.question: Is there room to scale the Rs 10 price point, and how much of the April weakness was rain versus competition from Campa?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not scaling Rs 10 because it is unprofitable. It said India is growing 20%+ month-on-month outside April, which was hit by El Nino.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company expanding into alcobev in India, and is it bidding for Bira?

qa_highlights.question: Can India grow at low double digits given stronger competitors and a high base?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman Ravi Jaipuria said H1 India growth was 14.4% and July is continuing at the same trend, so double-digit growth looks achievable. Varun Jaipuria said weather, not demand, was holding back growth in months without rain.

qa_highlights.question: Up to what crude level can margins be maintained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are maintainable even in a worse geopolitical year and that margins cannot get worse once conflicts ease. It did not give a crude threshold.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the energy drink labelling change on STING?

qa_highlights.question: Will the Calpis tie-up extend to other Asahi brands or other categories?

Monsoon and El Nino weather volatility, which hurt April and shifted the seasonal pattern of May.
Lower Twizza margins, which pulled group EBITDA margin down 76 bps; further integration and dilution is possible.
Energy drink labelling change, with a 90-day compliance deadline. Some volume shifted to CSD in June-July.
Rising competitive intensity from Campa Cola's Rs 10 and Rs 20 packs and Coca-Cola, which could pressure India volume and pricing.
Net debt of ~Rs 3,730 mn at consolidated level after the Twizza acquisition.
540180|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on volume momentum and margins, with management repeatedly citing 20%+ growth and calling the margin outlook comfortable. It was evasive on Rs 10 scale-up, market share, Bira and PepsiCo's share data, and deferred on the Calpis expansion and new categories.
key_quotes: If you see our growth, which is March onwards, we are growing healthily at 20% plus.
We can comfortably maintain our margins even in a year, which is the worst year for the geopolitical reasons and all the costing has gone up internationally.
Cans is 1- 2% of our business, nothing major.
Largely our portfolio is low sugar or Zero Sugar as you call it.

540203|2026-03.headline: Sheela Foam Q4 FY26 consolidated core EBITDA rose 90% YoY to INR121 crore at an 11.5% margin, with first-ever dividend of 20% recommended.
540203|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue grew 24% YoY to INR1,050 crore, and FY26 revenue rose 11% to INR3,821 crore, with management citing record foam production, top line and EBITDA. Core EBITDA for FY26 was INR414 crore (10.8% margin, up 261 bps), and consolidated PAT was INR92 crore in Q4 (about 7x YoY) and INR161 crore for FY26. Net debt fell INR156 crore in FY26, and the Board recommended a first-ever 20% dividend. Management flagged raw material (TDI, polyol) volatility from the Middle East conflict, saying prices were 25-35% higher on average, and that pass-through has largely been taken.

financial_highlights.value: INR161 crore; INR144 crore earned in H2

segments.name: Mattress (India, Sleepwell + Kurlon)
segments.commentary: Volumes grew 13% YoY in Q4 and 12% for FY26; value grew 13% in Q4 and 10% for FY26. Around 600 net new showrooms were added in FY26.

segments.name: Foam (India)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 volume grew 34% and value 36%, aided by better price realisation. FY26 volume grew 18% and value 14%. Management said B2B and comfort foam grew upwards of 15% annually.

segments.name: U2O (unorganised to organised, small-town India)
segments.commentary: Served through 8,400 dealers across over 5,000 towns in 24 states. FY26 volume grew 65% and value 111%, helped by a higher-priced second model and price increases.

segments.name: E-commerce
segments.commentary: Brand.com sales grew 136% YoY and platform sales 39% YoY in FY26; management cited a 52% value growth figure in Q&A.

segments.name: Australia (Joyce)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR422 crore with EBITDA margin of 10%, up almost 400 bps from FY25, driven by yield programmes, price renegotiation and supply-chain restructuring.

segments.name: Spain
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR391 crore with EBITDA margin of 10.4%, against 8.4% in FY25. Management sees a stable 30-32% gross margin range.

segments.name: Furlenco
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR370 crore (over 60% growth) and PAT of close to INR60 crore versus INR3 crore in FY25. Company holds about 43% fully diluted; FY27 revenue target is about INR500 crore.

segments.commentary: FY26 revenue of INR70 crore.

guidance_outlook: Targeted growth of 15%+ over the medium term, expected to be higher given raw material-led price increases; management is aiming for a 3-5 year horizon to become a full product player.
Management believes core EBITDA margin is in an 11-12% range and can move higher with growth; Q1-Q2 FY27 margin impact from raw materials expected at no more than 50-100 bps.
FY27 standalone depreciation guided at INR140-145 crore on a consolidated basis, roughly INR35 crore per quarter.
FY27 capex guided at INR125-150 crore including maintenance, debottlenecking, marketing capex for new stores, across India, Australia and Spain.
Consolidated finance cost guided at about INR50 crore for FY27 (about INR35 crore interest plus INR15 crore other charges).
India debt of about INR300 crore expected to be repaid in 1-1.5 years; Australia and Spain debt of about INR350 crore is self-liquidating.
Remaining Kurlon synergies of about INR40 crore (out of INR250 crore total) depend on new machines that are delayed about 1.5 quarters; installation expected by mid or end of Q1 FY27.
Furlenco IPO decision to be taken in the next 3-4 months; listing expected in about one year or later.
Dividend of 20% for FY26 recommended, subject to shareholder approval; first dividend in company history.
Pillows (about INR100 crore market) to be treated as a separate category going forward; brand.com and U2O remain focus areas.
Hope to cross 100 integrated Furlenco-Sheela stores in FY27 (currently over 40).
capex_capacity: FY27 capex guided at INR125-150 crore including maintenance, debottlenecking to support volume growth of about 15% in FY26, and new store marketing capex.

New imported machines for malleable-fibre comfort-layer production are under installation, delayed about 1.5 quarters, to support INR40 crore synergy.

Marketing spend for FY26 is around 4.5% of sales, similar to last year.

qa_highlights.question: Are margins under pressure in Q1-Q2 FY27 given higher-cost raw material inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Gupta said price changes flow through in 10-15 days and inventory costs match, so the gross margin impact is limited to about 50-100 bps. Volume growth, given a 30%+ contribution margin, should support EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Why is U2O value growth (111%) far above volume growth (65%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Rakesh Chahar said a higher-priced second model was introduced and both models saw price increases. U2O margins are between offline and e-commerce margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reason for the change in depreciation policy?

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Australia and Spain margins, and is a sale still under consideration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees Spain gross margins at 30-32% and Australian margins up about 4-5 points on a normal basis. The target is 10-12% EBITDA. Rahul Gautam said the company is open to a sale but is not actively pursuing one.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Furlenco plans and how is ROCE?

qa_highlights.question: How much of the remaining synergy is pending?

540203|2026-06.headline: Sheela Foam Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 26% to INR1,032 crore and EBITDA 45% to INR109 crore, with margin at 10.6%.
540203|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 26% YoY to INR1,032 crore and EBITDA rose 45% to INR109 crore, with margin up 139 bps to 10.6%. Standalone India revenue grew 20% to INR761 crore and EBITDA 13% to INR68 crore, with gross margin compressed by sharp raw-material (TDI/polyol) swings that management attributes to the Middle East conflict. Management chose to keep growing foam volumes, which was cash-accretive, and international subsidiaries (Australia, Spain) posted sharply higher margins on inventory gains. Management reiterated a 15% EBITDA margin target for next year and expects volumes to recover in the festive quarters.

segments.name: India mattresses
segments.commentary: Value up 15% and volume up 6% YoY. U2O channel revenue up 81% with volume up 19%, now about 10,000 dealers, helped by 5- and 6-inch mattresses.

segments.name: India foam
segments.commentary: Value up 26% and volume up 4% YoY; faster foam growth diluted gross margin but was cash-accretive as competitors lacked raw material.

segments.name: E-commerce
segments.commentary: Brand.com sales up 69% YoY, platforms up 19%; overall category up 30% with volumes up 23%.

segments.name: Staqo (IT)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 67% YoY with EBITDA margin around 28-30%; Presence 360 crossed 3.2 lakh users.

segments.name: Furlenco (associate)

guidance_outlook: Reiterated 15% EBITDA margin target for next year; management said there is no change to this stance, though Rachna Kukreja's question suggested earlier 11-12% FY27 guidance.
Expects more than 15% revenue growth for the full year and double-digit volume growth in both foam and mattresses for FY27.

International operations to grow about 5% in local currency with 10-12% EBITDA margins; for FY27, management is confident of crossing INR1,000 crore revenue and about INR120 crore EBITDA for overseas operations.
Synergy benefit of about INR40 crore still pending; machine under installation, with full impact expected in Q3.
Integration of Kurlon about 96-97% complete; roughly 75-80% of synergies realised, with the balance expected.
Expects volume recovery with Q3 (festive) and Q4 the strongest quarters; FY27 volume expected to exceed last year.
Expects ROCE to reach roughly 20-25% in three years from about 10% currently.
Debt: India debt above INR300 crore to be cleared in about one year; overseas debt of about INR350 crore to be repaid over five years. Balance sheet will not be debt free by year-end.
capex_capacity: Company-operated stores (COCO): about INR27 lakh capex per store plus INR20-22 lakh working capital; about INR50 lakh per store, so about INR25 crore for 50 stores. Stores are about 2,000 sq ft (range 1,800-3,000).
COCO store rollout: 22 existing stores upgraded; target 50 stores with about 42 operational.
Furlenco shop-in-shop: about 40-50 stores currently; first target 100 stores. Company has about 3,500 exclusive brand outlets.
Standalone synergy-related machine under installation, expected to deliver full impact in Q3.
Operating units reduced from 21 to 12 as part of Kurlon integration.
demand_pricing: Standalone India volume growth about 6%; management views sub-10% as satisfactory and says industry grew close to 5%.
U2O price increase taken last year to fix channel margins; value growth well ahead of volume as a result; management says the pricing level is now sustainable.
Raw material (TDI/polyol) prices swung roughly +40% to -20% in the period; prices spiked in March after the Feb 28 Iran conflict, eased in April, then rose again about a month before the call.
Management says price increases pass through commensurately, but in-pipe inventory on the high seas can lag on sharp falls and hit margin.
Foam share of COGS: TDI and polyol are 65-70% of COGS.
Premiumisation: ASP marginally up across segments; new products introduced to lift ASP; consumer-led promotions launched.
Organised mattress market combined share of Sleepwell and Kurlon close to 20%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Australia/Spain margin gain sustainable, and how much of it is inventory benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the gains came from longer-held low-cost inventory and yield and supply chain programmes. Overseas momentum should moderate as India recovers, with normal inventory levels by Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone volume growth slow to single digits and margins fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a price-volume trade-off after the steep price hikes, and expects double-digit volume growth for the year once volatility eases. Gross margins were hit mainly by foam, while incremental foam sales generated cash.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 15% EBITDA margin target and 13-14% FY28 guidance hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has not guided for 13% for FY27 (only 11-12%) but stands by its margin commitment; the current volatility makes it hard to comment, and gross margin has fallen more than the guided range.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and rollout of company-owned stores?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR27 lakh capex plus INR20-22 lakh working capital per store, with 42 operational of a 50-store target; about INR25 crore for another 50 COCO stores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Kurlon integration status and synergy realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Integration about 96-97% complete, operating units cut to 12 from 21, and roughly 75-80% of synergies realised, with the remainder on track.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Furlenco store rollout?
qa_highlights.answer: Furlenco is present in 40-50 shop-in-shop stores with a first target of 100, and will go only where it fits its micro-market strategy.

risks_watch: Raw material volatility: TDI/polyol (65-70% of COGS) swung roughly +40% to -20%; management expects volatility for at least a couple of months, possibly to October-November, so gross margin recovery timing is uncertain.

Volume recovery: standalone India volume grew about 6% against double-digit growth last year; management expects double-digit volume growth for FY27 and strongest volumes in Q3 and Q4, contingent on volatility subsiding.

So, we guided for 11% to 12%. We never guided for 13% for the current year. Yes, we do stand for it.
There is no change in stand on the margins. We have a target of 15% EBITDA margin for the next year.
So, there would definitely be volume recovery. I would say we would go back higher than what the volumes we clocked last year.

It declined to give a view on the 12-13% FY27 and 13-14% FY28 margin figures put to it and repeatedly said it would revisit once volatility eases.

540212|2026-03.headline: TCI Express Q4 FY26 revenue rose 6% YoY to INR 327 crore, EBITDA margin 11.3%, PAT flat at INR 21 crore amid fuel and labour cost pressure.
540212|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew about 6% YoY to INR 327 crore and 4% QoQ, with total income of INR 331 crore. EBITDA rose 11% YoY to INR 37 crore (11.3% margin) while PAT was flat at INR 21 crore (6.3% margin). Full-year revenue grew about 2% to INR 1,236 crore, with PAT of INR 90 crore (7.2% margin). segments.name: Multimodal (Air, Rail, C2C, e-commerce)
segments.commentary: About 18.5% of FY26 revenue, with management citing about 20% growth; target of 22% to 25% share over 2 to 3 years. Domestic and international air margins were hit this quarter, while rail and C2C margins were described as stable.

segments.name: Rail Express
segments.commentary: Management said rail gross profit is above 30% and realisation is about 2.5x surface. Rail volumes are not disclosed.

segments.name: E-commerce Express
segments.commentary: About 2.5% of business, with a target of 5%. Focus is on D2C and B2B merchant-to-warehouse movement with SME clients, not quick commerce.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth guided at about 10% to 11%, with revenue growth of about 15% including price hikes.
FY27 margin improvement of 100 to 150 basis points at EBITDA and PAT levels, conditional on fuel prices stabilising.
Q1 FY27 volume expected at high single-digit growth, improving QoQ through the year.
Multimodal growth guided at about 20% in FY27.
Depreciation run-rate of INR 30 to 32 crore per year after ROU additions; about INR 6 to 6.25 crore per quarter.
Capex plan revised from INR 500 crore to INR 400 crore for FY23 to FY27; about INR 130 crore planned for FY27. A new five-year plan will follow.
Branch expansion of about 100 branches in FY27 (40 surface, 60 rail, air and C2C).
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation was about 83.25% in Q4, improved QoQ.
Nagpur sorting centre upgraded and now owned; semi-automated, about 70,000 to 75,000 sq ft, with only 5% to 7% change in cut-off time.
Ahmedabad and Kolkata sorting centres under construction, to finish in FY27, with automation ramping up in the first half of FY28. Lucknow also in progress.

Next sorting centres planned for Chennai and Bangalore.

The company expects to benefit from air-to-surface and rail shifts as higher air prices push customers to other modes.

qa_highlights.question: Why has growth been restricted and margins fallen from 15% to 16% to 10% to 11%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the Gulf war and ATF spike, airline consolidation, airport privatisation, lower truck utilisation and a 100 bps hit from labour costs. It guided FY27 PAT margin recovery of 100 to 150 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 volume and revenue guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth of about 10% to 11% and revenue growth of about 15% for FY27, with Q1 at high single digits and QoQ improvement after that.

qa_highlights.question: Is the multimodal segment margin dilutive?

qa_highlights.question: Why did PAT fall sharply despite 12% revenue growth?

qa_highlights.question: What is the ACT acquisition's expected contribution and timing?

540611|2026-06.headline: AU SFB Q1 FY27 profit rose 37% YoY to INR796 cr, with NIM at 5.9% (+47 bps YoY) and deposits up 24% YoY.

Loans grew 23% YoY and deposits 24% YoY, both well ahead of private sector bank growth. Asset quality improved on a YoY basis, with slippages down 22% to INR798 crore and credit cost down 54 bps to 0.8%. Sequentially, NIM eased 7 bps and provisions rose 38% on seasonality, and an additional one-time INR23 crore provision was taken on unsecured products.

qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Tripathi said Q4 is seasonally strong, so YoY is the right comparison; commercial banking slippages are lower YoY and bank-level slippages improved about 150 bps. The QoQ uptick is in the SME book, which typically rises in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of ECL framework on steady-state credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impact is hard to quantify now. Models are being refined with external agencies, and Stage 3 provisions give comfort to cover incremental Stage 1 and 2 provisions. Management called the impact neutral given low LGDs; more clarity expected by end of Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Risk-adjusted yields and profitability of digital unsecured (credit cards and PL)?
qa_highlights.answer: Prince Tiwari said these are newer businesses and product-level risk-adjusted metrics are not yet meaningful. Credit cards are loss-making and PL is around breakeven, per management. Gaurav Jain said the card yield is subdued because the revolve book fell after underwriting tightening.

qa_highlights.question: NIM trajectory for the next two to three quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Gaurav Jain declined to give directional NIM guidance. Cost of funds has bottomed, with savings and deposit rates raised, so the cost line should be stable to slightly up depending on rates.

qa_highlights.question: MFI growth sustainability and CV credit environment?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Tripathi said the industry is recovering after degrowth and MFIN projects 17-18% growth. Q1 collection efficiency is 99.5%, and vehicle distribution has expanded in South, UP and East with no abnormal stress seen.

qa_highlights.question: Which CD ratio is used internally and NSFR range?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Agarwal said CD ratio ex-refinance is about 80% and is the internal measure. Prince Tiwari said the LCR range is about 115-120% and NSFR about 105-115%.

qa_highlights.question: ROA target of 1.8% and whether NIM is stable?
qa_highlights.answer: Gaurav Jain said there is no NIM guidance; opex and credit cost have room to improve versus FY26. Sanjay Agarwal said the bank is about 10 bps short of the target, with other income and credit cost each contributing.

qa_highlights.question: Employee count decline and MFI credit cost outlook?

540678|2026-06.headline: Cochin Shipyard Q1 FY27 PAT fell to INR 151.45 crore from INR 187.82 crore on turnover of INR 1,094.21 crore; ISRF JV with DP World's Drydocks World valued at INR 1,800 crore.

540692|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 14% to INR931 crore and EBITDA margin expanded 405 bps to 7.7%, while Q4 volume fell to 1,912 MT from 2,349 MT.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 volume fall while gross margin improved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited January worker issues and holiday-period disruption; margin was supported by stable farm-gate prices and inventory use.

qa_highlights.answer: Management expects an increase in volume, originally envisaging about 30% growth, with US recovery and EU/UK FTAs as drivers, subject to production and logistics.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Motor OD loss ratio deteriorate?

qa_highlights.question: Why did commission and other opex ratios rise in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a higher retail mix, which carries higher acquisition cost but better loss outcomes, and said opex changes are business as usual.

qa_highlights.question: How would the 25% expense-of-management limit affect the company?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company is well within the 30% EOM limit on an annual basis and sees the draft 25% limit as a positive for market share.

Distribution reform outcome: commission cuts, possible TP tariff changes, and POSP disruption in CV TP.
Commercial lines loss experience: Q1 large losses and Fire de-growth continuing; September Fire at -6.0%.
Base effect from GST reforms in Q3 and Q4 may moderate Motor growth.

540719|2026-06.headline: SBI Life Q1 FY27 VNB rose 29% to INR14.1bn, but VNB margin fell to 26.2% as GST and a one-off GTI group deal diluted mix.
540719|2026-06.overview: Individual rated premium grew 14% to INR39.7bn with private market share of 22.2%, and all product segments and channels grew. Profit after tax rose 22% to INR7.2bn, helped by supportive market conditions, while the GST impact was INR2.3bn for the quarter. VNB margin of 26.2% was down year on year, which management attributed mainly to a higher share of lumpy group business (GTI) in APE. Management said the margin was within its 26–28% guidance, at the lower end, and expects it to move to the upper end as individual mix normalises.

financial_highlights.change: Margin down YoY; GST impact INR2.3bn

segments.name: Individual rated premium / APE
segments.commentary: Individual APE INR39.9bn, +14% YoY; ULIP INR24.5bn (61% share vs 65% in Q1 FY26); guaranteed non-par savings INR9.7bn, +27%. Non-ULIP share of IRP reached 38%.

segments.name: Group business
segments.commentary: Group NBP INR32.9bn (37% of NBP), +41% YoY; group APE INR53.8bn, +36%; group protection APE INR12.3bn, +313%, driven by a large one-off GTI contract.

segments.name: Protection
segments.commentary: Individual protection APE INR1.9bn, +18%; pure protection +41% on individual APE; ROP share of individual protection 68% vs 73% a year ago.

segments.name: Bancassurance (SBI and RRBs)
segments.commentary: 47% of total APE; individual APE INR24.5bn, +10%; SBI branch productivity INR4.1mn, +7%. Other banks grew 19% on individual NBP and 31% on APE; their mix is about 80% non-ULIP.

segments.name: Agency
segments.commentary: Individual APE INR13.1bn, +20%; agent productivity INR2 lakh; non-ULIP share rose from 43% to 46%; 34,000+ agents added gross and 11 new branches opened.

segments.name: Other channels (direct, corporate agents, brokers, online)
segments.commentary: Grew 160% and contributed 28% of total APE; management did not split this into organic and group components.

guidance_outlook: IRP growth guidance of 14–15% for FY27 reaffirmed.
VNB margin guidance of 26–28% for FY27 maintained; management expects the margin to move toward the upper end as individual mix normalises.
GST drag expected for one more quarter (Q2 FY27), with the impact ending thereafter; GST was waived from 22 September, so about 2.5 months of impact remain in Q1.
Pure protection growth expected to keep outpacing ROP; the company is shifting focus from ROP to non-ROP and pure protection.
Regular-pay deferred annuity plan expected to launch within the next quarter.
Non-ULIP share of IRP targeted to be sustained at around this level for the year.
Other-expense ratio expected to normalise over the next three quarters, but higher stamp duty tied to sum assured growth will persist.
capex_capacity: Agency network: more than 100 branches opened over the last two to three years, and 11 new branches in Q1 FY27.
Agent additions: over 34,000 agents added on a gross basis in Q1 FY27.
New corporate agency tie-up with J&K Bank; business expected to start in the current quarter.
Automation: 99.9% of individual proposals submitted digitally; 67% processed through automated underwriting.
demand_pricing: Individual sum assured grew 46% YoY and group new business sum assured grew 265%; rider sum assured is 39% of individual sum assured.
Rider attachment on ULIP is about 45–50%, up from roughly 35% when introduced about 1–1.5 years ago; management expects it to hold or improve.
Non-par pricing is reviewed against yield movements; IRR for customers was raised in June after the yield curve moved.
The 61st-month persistency dip is attributed to the COVID cohort moving through policy years; management expects it to normalise by end-Q3 FY27.
Credit protect business was flat YoY; management expects an uptick in coming quarters.
Misselling ratio 0.02%; death claim settlement ratio 98.8%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 60 bps product-mix drag on VNB margin is due to the GTI group deal, and what is the normalised margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 60 bps mix drag relates only to GTI and that the company does not disclose product-wise margins. It said margin should return to normal as IRP share normalises. The 40 bps assumption-related item reflects the March 2026 annual review, and there was no assumption change in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Is the GST drag going to persist, and how do expenses look?
qa_highlights.answer: GST drag of about 1.1 percentage points in Q1 is expected to continue into Q2 and then fade. Management said the rise in other expenses reflects one-off stamp duty tied to higher sum assured and labour code impacts, and it expects these to normalise over the next three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will agency growth be sustainable and will the channel mix shift affect costs or margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Agency APE grew 20% in Q1, with the current quarter at 19%-plus. Management expects a stronger contribution from agency in the remaining three quarters and a balanced mix of banca and agency going forward. It did not discuss cost impact in detail.

qa_highlights.question: What proportion of ULIPs carry rider attachment, and how is protection classified?
qa_highlights.answer: Rider attachment on ULIPs is about 45–50%, up from roughly 35% when riders were introduced 1–1.5 years earlier. Riders are counted within individual protection, and rider APE was not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Why is individual protection growth lower than peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the shift from ROP to pure protection lowers ticket size, which makes headline growth look subdued. Individual protection grew 22% by its own measure against pure protection growth of 41%, with ROP share at 68%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the regular-pay deferred annuity plan launch slip, and what are the non-par and regulatory views?
qa_highlights.answer: The deferred annuity plan is expected in the next quarter and is being developed for an opportune time. On non-par, management said pricing is reviewed against yield movements. On regulation, management said it sees the company as well placed and expects future rules to be positive for the industry.

risks_watch: Group/GTI lumpiness: a large one-off group contract diluted Q1 VNB margin; sustainability of group APE mix and margin recovery to 26–28% range is the key test.
GST drag of about 110 bps on margin in Q1 FY27 with another quarter expected; watch whether Q2 drag falls as indicated.
Other-expense ratio rising (opex ratio 7.7% vs 6.3%) due to stamp duty and labour codes; watch cost discipline.
61st-month persistency dip due to COVID cohort; management expects normalisation by end-Q3 FY27.
Credit protect flat YoY; watch for the promised uptick.
Rider APE not disclosed; pure protection ticket size is smaller, so protection growth optics may stay weaker than peers.
Regulatory changes flagged as an open question by management; details not yet clear.
540719|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on top-line growth and the full-year IRP and VNB margin guidance, but defensive on the margin decline, which it attributed to one-off group business and GST. Management was evasive on quantifying the GTI margin drag and product-level margins, and declined to comment on individual contracts.
key_quotes: The margin guidance was 26% to 28%, and we are within the range, although at the lower end of that.
And going forward, with higher focus on individual policies, the margin is going to be towards the upper range of our guidance.
So the GST was waived from 22nd of September. So there will be some impact for 2.5 months in the current quarter also.
Hopefully within next quarter, you will be able to see that.

540725|2026-03.headline: Share India standalone Q4 FY26 PAT rose 368% YoY to INR 75 crore on revenue of INR 383 crore (+103%).
540725|2026-03.overview: Standalone Q4 FY26 revenue nearly doubled to INR 383 crore and PAT rose to INR 75 crore from INR 16 crore, with EPS of INR 17.6 versus INR 11.7. For FY26, standalone PAT rose 20% to INR 298 crore on revenue of INR 395 crore. Consolidated FY26 PAT was flat-to-down at INR 324 crore versus INR 328 crore, held back by fair value adjustments on investments held by group companies. Management pushed diversification into MTF, PMS, wealth distribution, debt (Share India Cred), AIF and commodities, while flagging RBI curbs on intraday bank limits for prop trading.

segments.name: Broking and trading (prop vs client)
segments.commentary: Prop contributed ~70% of revenue but ~49% of consolidated FY26 profit (~52% standalone). Client turnover reportedly exceeded prop turnover (53% vs 47%) for the first time; target 60% client share of turnover by year-end.

segments.name: MTF (margin trading finance)
segments.commentary: MTF book grew from INR 239 crore (FY25) to INR 424 crore (FY26); Dec-25 level was INR 457 crore. FY27 target INR 650 crore; FY28 vision also cited as INR 650 crore.

segments.name: NBFC
segments.commentary: Reported NIM of 17.64% for FY26, roughly flat with FY25; management said NIM will decline as the book shifts to secured lending.

segments.name: uTrade (algo platform)
segments.commentary: Active clients crossed 5,000 in FY26 (5,231 currently); still small in revenue, with focus on adoption. Multi-broker plan slowed by a SEBI circular requiring vendors to set up separately for each broker.

segments.name: Wealth management and PMS
segments.commentary: PMS launched in Q4 FY26 with AUM above INR 100 crore; FY27 target INR 200 crore. Third-party distribution team under Charu Sehgal to start operations in Q3. AIF CAT-3 application filed with SEBI, approval expected by end-Q2 FY27.

segments.name: Share India Cred (debt)
segments.commentary: Started operations in Q1 FY27 with six issues closed; FY27 target at least INR 500 crore of issues.

segments.name: Institutional business
segments.commentary: Institutional empanelments rose 35% from 137 to 186.

segments.name: Other subsidiaries
segments.commentary: NBFC, merchant banking, insurance and technology together contributed about 7% of FY26 bottom line. MSCI (Metropolitan Stock Exchange) cash segment doing INR 300-400 crore daily volume; Sizable stake held.

guidance_outlook: Annual EBITDA ~38% (+/-2%) and PAT margin ~22% (+/-2%) reaffirmed; management says no structural Q4 pressure.
MTF book target INR 650 crore by FY27, with mgmt saying INR 200 crore incremental is achievable if markets stay normal; deviation possible in low single digits on sentiment.
Target 30 new Tier-3 company-owned branches in next 2-3 years; 6 more targeted by FY27 year-end on top of 7 existing.
Prop share of profit targeted to fall to ~30% in three years; client share of turnover to reach 60% by FY27 year-end.
Share India Cred target INR 500 crore of issues in FY27; PMS AUM target INR 200 crore by FY27-end.
Silverleaf merger pending at NCLT; expected to conclude within about a quarter.
capex_capacity: Seven company-owned Tier-3 branches operating (Hyderabad, Indore, Bhopal, Varanasi, Agra, Raipur, Nagpur), with six more targeted by end FY27.
Target of at least INR 10-15 crore MTF per Tier-3 branch per year; 30 branches implied INR 300-500 crore.
AIF CAT-3 approval awaited from SEBI; wealth-management operations to start Q3 FY27.
Silverleaf merger pending at NCLT; post-merger plans include HFT trading.
MSCI exchange planning IPO segment, SME segment, and derivatives launch in FY27 (subject to approvals).
demand_pricing: Management said Q4 was volatile, with commodities (gold, silver, crude, natgas) driving turnover; cash ADTO rose to ~INR 2,000 crore in Q4 FY26 from ~INR 1,500 crore, and total ADTO rose to ~INR 4,500-5,000 crore from ~INR 1,400 crore in Q4 FY25 (figures as stated in call). Options were ~18% of Q4 ADTO.
MTF demand said to have risen in the last 1.5 months; Tier-3 pricing reportedly better because of less competition from sub-brokers.

RBI curbs: intraday bank limits for prop trading withdrawn; bank guarantees allowed for client business. Management estimates ~20% impact on overall deposits/limits used but minimal bottom-line effect; bank guarantees valid to 30 June can continue to expiry (up to March 2027).
SEBI market-making framework expected in 3-4 months; company is lobbying RBI for liquidity-provider relief.
Mgmt estimates INR 40,000-50,000 crore of capital to exit the market due to RBI curbs, which it expects to widen per-trade margins.

qa_highlights.question: Why do margins dip every March quarter and is that sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhinav Gupta said Q4 was weak in FY25 and FY26 due to volatile markets; management prefers annual view with EBITDA ~38% and PAT ~22% (+/-2%). Sachin Gupta said Q4 pressure is not structural.

qa_highlights.question: Status of uTrade multi-broker plans and monetisation model?
qa_highlights.answer: Sachin Gupta said talks with Motilal Oswal and Dhan stalled after a SEBI circular requiring third-party vendors to set up infrastructure separately per broker, which is costly. No monetisation details were given.

qa_highlights.question: At what MTF AUM does the interest spread become meaningful, given borrowing costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhinav Gupta said full-year borrowing costs will flow into FY27 and new NCD and third-party borrowing lines could cut costs by a few hundred basis points. Tier-3 direct branches are meant to remove mediators and lift NIM.

qa_highlights.question: Break up of brokerage vs prop income?
qa_highlights.answer: Prop contributes ~70% of revenue but ~49% of FY26 consolidated profit (52% standalone). Client turnover exceeded prop turnover for the first time (53% vs 47%).

qa_highlights.question: Impact of RBI regulation on prop business and Market Maker regime?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated ~20% impact on limits used and minimal impact on bottom line. Company sought liquidity-provider status; the company is hybrid-classified and can continue bank guarantees until expiry (up to March 2027).

qa_highlights.question: Ballpark revenue diversification in the next three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims for 70% client and 30% prop share of profit over three years. Non-broking segments were ~7% of FY26 bottom line; detailed split not disclosed.

risks_watch: RBI curbs on prop intraday limits effective around 1 July 2026; watch for actual impact on prop turnover and margins versus the ~20% management estimate.
Consolidated PAT flat YoY due to fair value losses on group investments; recurrence risk.
NIM compression expected in NBFC as lending shifts to secured products; MTF book is cyclical with market sentiment.
Regulatory changes: SEBI vendor-per-broker circular hurts uTrade multi-broker plans; market-making framework still pending.
Silverleaf NCLT approval and AIF CAT-3 approval timing are uncertain.
540725|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth and diversification, but defensive and hedged on the RBI prop curbs and market-dependent targets. Management repeatedly stressed that targets depend on normal markets and geopolitical stability.
key_quotes: So, the Company should be able to continue with the current margins. There is nothing like Q4 type of pressure on us.

So, hardly 20% impact in the overall limits will be there from the prop side, but on the bottom-line side, I don't think there will be much impact or there will be any impact, because per trade margin will improve.
So, MTF definitely depends on the market performance, and whatever the external reasons are, if market is performing good, demand for MTF goes up.

540725|2026-06.headline: Share India Q1 FY27 consolidated PAT rose 48% YoY to Rs 124.41 crore on revenue of Rs 448 crore; management targets ~20% growth this year.
540725|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as the company's strongest quarterly performance to date despite SEBI derivatives curbs and RBI funding restrictions on prop desks. Standalone revenue rose 28% YoY to Rs 349 crore and PAT rose 32% to Rs 90.85 crore; consolidated revenue rose 31% to Rs 448 crore and PAT rose 48% to Rs 124.41 crore, with consolidated PAT up 114% QoQ. Growth was attributed to MTF lending income, new subsidiaries (Share India Cred, GIFT City), PMS launch and merchant banking. Management plans CP and NCD issuance to offset funding constraints.

financial_highlights.value: Rs ~74 crore across six issues; EBITDA Rs 1.08 crore; PAT Rs 40 lakh

segments.commentary: Management said prop contributes ~52% of profitability and ~48% from broking; on revenue, prop is ~58-60%. Client volume is ~60% versus prop ~40%.

segments.name: MTF lending
segments.commentary: MTF book ~Rs 470 crore at end Q1, targeted at Rs 1,000 crore in two years; management called MTF the main source of sustainable interest income.

segments.name: PMS / wealth

AIF launch expected in Q3 FY27 pending regulatory approval; wealth distribution operations also targeted from Q3 FY27.
PMS AUM target ~Rs 250 crore by financial year end.
Plans to issue commercial paper (rated Crisil A1+) and NCDs to diversify funding; CP programme initiated.
capex_capacity: Seven new branches opened recently against a 30-branch target over two years; branches rolled out in tranches of about eight.

Acquisition of Enshrine (property-holding company, up to Rs 45 crore consideration) to secure ~18,000 sq ft carpet-area office in Mumbai (Interface 11 area); management cited property value above Rs 42 crore.
Silverleaf (HFT technology firm) acquisition previously announced; expected to add technology stack and HFT protocols and support geographic expansion.
AI, automation and in-house platform Techyon cited as technology investments.

Retail MTF demand in Tier-3 cities described as underserved, with limited broker options for MTF.
Mid and small-cap volatility affected MTF book; management said it held its numbers with mild growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the payback period for Tier-3 branches given lower ticket sizes?
qa_highlights.answer: Sachin Gupta said each branch should reach break-even in ~8 months by building a Rs 15 crore MTF book; branches not profitable after 12 months will be closed.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the stock underperforming despite low PE and high growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment on share price, attributing it to industry regulatory consolidation and cited diversification, institutional clients and subsidiaries as positives.

qa_highlights.question: What is the purpose of acquiring Silverleaf, the tech company?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhinav Gupta said Silverleaf (founded by IIT Bombay graduates, 12+ years in business) brings a technology stack and HFT protocols, supporting third-country expansion and back-end technology.

qa_highlights.question: What drove broking and trading performance and what is the prop vs broking split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the business has shifted toward lending via MTF (~Rs 465-470 crore) and fee streams from PMS, MF distribution and third-party products; prop contributes ~52% of profit and broking ~48%.

qa_highlights.question: Why pay up to Rs 45 crore for Enshrine, a company with Rs 2-3 crore turnover?
qa_highlights.answer: Kamlesh Shah said the acquisition is mainly to obtain a Mumbai property (~18,000 sq ft carpet area, valued above Rs 42 crore) to consolidate Mumbai offices.

qa_highlights.question: Is prop still a very high share of total revenue and PAT?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhinav Gupta said prop was ~58-60% of revenue and ~52% of profit now, versus ~85-90% of revenue and ~70-75% of profit 8-9 years ago.

Stock underperformance despite strong earnings; management attributed this to sector consolidation and external factors.

540735|2026-03.headline: IRIS RegTech targets INR500 crore revenue, needing ~30%+ growth over 4-5 years; FY26 revenue grew ~23% with EBITDA margin ~14%.
540735|2026-03.overview: Management framed FY26 as steady: total revenue grew about 23% and EBITDA margin was about 14%, with management asking analysts to judge the business on annual rather than quarterly numbers. IRIS CARBON ARR grew 33% on disclosure-management wins and iDEAL ARR grew 17%, while SupTech added 3 new logos including the Government of Qatar. Post the TaxTech divestment, cash was about INR155 crore and net worth rose to INR200 crore from INR76 crore. Management reiterated the INR500 crore revenue aspiration and said the Middle East crisis is a watch item rather than a current drag.

SaaS ARR growth target of about 35% (stated externally), with management saying internally it could be higher.
SupTech expected to grow at a lower rate than SaaS, with possible lumpy upside.
