qa_highlights.question: What is the roadmap to the INR500 crore revenue target and by when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated the INR500 crore aspiration, which needs growth slightly above 30% over 4-5 years. SaaS ARR targeted at about 35% growth; SupTech to grow slower, with possible surprises.

qa_highlights.question: How is AI helping, and does it raise competitive intensity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees AI as both opportunity and threat; it is building AI offerings and embedding AI in the development process. No competitive intensity increase seen so far from enterprises building in-house or AI-native entrants.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the Middle East crisis on the year?
qa_highlights.answer: SaaS impact seen as minimal given Europe and US focus. SupTech pipeline linked to Middle East regulators could see delays if the crisis persists beyond roughly June; 3-4 SupTech wins still expected.

qa_highlights.question: Use of the cash balance: M&A, product or marketing spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Organic growth first. Sales and marketing at about 1.1-1.2x net ARR, possibly a bit higher, with no EBITDA-negative mode. Inorganic options are open but disciplined; some capital to be retained.

qa_highlights.question: How will the ~30% growth be achieved: markets, products, headcount?
qa_highlights.answer: CARBON is the flagship with ESG added; adjacencies in capital-markets and energy reporting are early. iDEAL to expand into Africa, Middle East and Europe. iFile adding licensing, risk-based analytics and case management. Developed-market sales hiring has started.

qa_highlights.question: Why are receivable days falling and what is the comfort level?
qa_highlights.answer: Driven by enterprise SaaS mix rising and regulators paying promptly. Management says 75-80 days is comfortable; further improvement is progressively harder.

risks_watch: Middle East crisis could delay SupTech wins if it extends beyond roughly June 2026; government budgets may be hit by high oil prices.
Enterprise SaaS and AI disruption: management acknowledges volatility in enterprise software valuations and AI impact is uncertain.
Sales and marketing step-up at CARBON could pressure EBITDA margin from the ~14% base.
Peridot/MSME loan facilitation is at pilot stage with only 3 lenders; monetisation is unproven.
Regulator reluctance to adopt cloud and generic AI for confidential data may slow SupTech and AI-led product uptake.
Deployment of the ~INR155 crore cash into inorganic deals is undefined.
540735|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on SaaS growth and balance sheet, but cautious on the Middle East and AI, with management saying it is watchful but not unduly worried. Answers on M&A and the INR500 crore timeline were measured and non-committal on dates.
key_quotes: And we're already seeing 33% ARR growth, and we want to up it as we go forward.
We don't want to do a deal just because we have the capital.
We don't want to be doing this in EBITDA negative mode.
So I would start getting worried post June, I would say.

540743|2026-06.headline: Godrej Agrovet Q1 FY27 consolidated sales rose 10% to INR2,852 crore; Crop Care fell 16.2% on delayed monsoon, while management still targets double-digit FY27 PBT growth.
540743|2026-06.overview: Consolidated sales grew 10% YoY to INR2,852 crore despite a delayed monsoon and geopolitical-driven inflation. Animal Nutrition (revenue +12.6%, reported segment result +29%) and Oil Palm (revenue +28.9%, segment result +14.4%) carried the quarter. Crop Care revenue fell 16.2% on a dry June and slower kharif sowing, and Dairy margins were squeezed by milk procurement costs and packaging inflation. Astec reached EBITDA breakeven versus an INR11 crore loss a year ago. Management reiterated FY27 double-digit consolidated PBT growth (versus earlier mid-teens guidance) but deferred a firmer view on Crop Care until end-September.

financial_highlights.change: Cattle feed volume +15%; total segment volume +7%
Segment result +14.4%; EBIT margin ~17% vs 19% a year ago (per analyst)
vs EBITDA loss of INR11 crore in Q1 FY26
Value-added share of sales 49% vs 42% a year ago

segments.name: Animal Nutrition
segments.commentary: Revenue +12.6% on robust demand and better realisations; cattle feed volume +15% and overall segment volume +7%. Poultry volumes deliberately reduced in unprofitable geographies. Cattle feed is about 55-56% of the segment; fish feed about 7%.

segments.name: Oil Palm
segments.commentary: Revenue +28.9% on higher CPO and PKO realisations and volume; FFB volumes broadly flat versus a strong early-monsoon base. Segment result +14.4%, with margin down on a pricing-formula effect that management calls one-off.

segments.name: Crop Care
segments.commentary: Revenue -16.2% as a dry June and slow kharif sowing hit cotton herbicide volumes, with margin contraction. Ashitaka and Takai together contribute about 18-20% of Q1 sales; Ghassnash soybean herbicide launched.

segments.name: Astec LifeSciences
segments.commentary: EBITDA breakeven versus an INR11 crore loss a year ago; revenue moderately lower on product mix. Management guides FY27 revenue growth of more than 20%, with an 8-9% Q1 dip to be recovered; CDMO dissilience around 50-52%.

segments.name: Dairy (CDPL)
segments.commentary: Revenue +11.4% and volume +8%, but profitability hit by elevated milk procurement prices and packaging inflation. Route-to-market reconstitution (about 18-20 months) under new CEO Gaurav is starting.

segments.name: Godrej Foods
segments.commentary: Revenue broadly stable as live bird trading is planned to fall 15-20% a year and go near zero over 3-4 years. Branded B2C (Yummiez, Real Good) volume +28% and about 32% of the Foods business; profitability hit by input costs.

segments.name: Bangladesh JV (ACI Godrej Agrovet)
segments.commentary: Returned to growth, with double-digit growth in volume, revenue and PBT.

qa_highlights.question: What FFB volume growth and EBITDA trajectory can Oil Palm deliver over 3-5 years, and what capex and returns are involved in value addition?
qa_highlights.answer: Sunil Kataria guided FFB volume growth of high single digit to early double digit over 4-5 years, targeting double digit; specialty fats refinery to start in September, with a 16-18% IRR hurdle and about 200 bps EBITDA uplift at scale. He did not give an explicit EBITDA number.

qa_highlights.question: Can Crop Care recover in H2, and is the consolidated mid-teens PBT growth still achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was hit by a 40% June deficit; July is better than last year's base, and it will decide on the recovery by end-September. Consolidated growth now targeted at double digit, with the exact level to be given by end-Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Astec: revenue outlook and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Arijit Mukherjee said FY27 revenue growth is now expected at more than 20%, with the 8-9% Q1 dip to be recovered; CDMO margins intact and enterprise margin normalising as prices fall.

qa_highlights.question: Will the palm oil shift need extra capex, and what is the Foods/Dairy pricing picture?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex stays within the INR300-350 crore envelope already guided. Dairy volume grew 8% but packaging and milk costs hit margin; Foods B2C is in a 3-4 year investment phase, with live bird trading being wound down.

qa_highlights.question: How much maize inflation has Animal Nutrition passed through, and what is EBIT per tonne?
qa_highlights.answer: About 60-70% of commodity cost increases passed on; EBIT per tonne guidance held at roughly INR2,050-2,150, with Q1 EBITDA per tonne in that range or slightly higher.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Oil Palm segment margin fall from 19% to 17%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it mainly to a one-off pricing-formula change in the quarter and flat FFB, offset by better OER; expects margins to even out over the year.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Crop Care lagging peers, and what are margins on the new products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is segment-mix and macro driven (cotton herbicide concentration), not share loss; new products carry lower margin than Hitweed but healthy, with total Crop Care EBIT margin seen at about 26-27%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated PBT growth: management still targets double-digit growth, narrowed from the earlier mid-teens guidance; exact position in the range to be given by end-September (end Q2).

Astec LifeSciences: FY27 revenue growth guided at more than 20% (up from the ~20% earlier guidance); Q1 revenue dip of 8-9% to be recovered in later quarters; CDMO dissilience around 50-52% for the year, with some CDMO shift from H1 to H2.
Astec enterprise margin: Q1 benefited from low-priced raw material and war-driven finished goods price increases; prices now easing, margin normalising. CDMO margins intact.

Oil Palm: FFB volume growth of high single digit to early double digit over the next 4-5 years (LRP); management says it targets double digit; full-year FFB growth guided at high single digit to double digit; margin drop expected to even out over the year.
Animal Nutrition: EBIT per tonne guidance held at roughly INR2,050-2,150 per tonne.
Crop Care: no firm FY27 numbers; recovery quantum to be assessed by end-September after cotton herbicide season. Crop Care EBIT margin expected to hold around 26-27% despite tough year.

Dairy: milk procurement prices expected to stay at current elevated levels for 2-3 quarters; packaging inflation expected to ease by August; some impact may persist in Q2; cost initiatives to be doubled down on in H2.
Godrej Foods: live bird trading to decline 15-20% a year and go near zero over 3-4 years; branded B2C to be in investment phase for 3-4 years.
capex_capacity: Overall business-level capex guidance of roughly INR300-350 crore, phased over 3-4 quarters; includes the integrated palm oil complex (phase 1 started, nursery and CPO mill; seed garden in 18-24 months; refinery later) and specialty fats refinery (rollout late August/early September 2026); management says no new investment beyond this envelope.

Oil Palm area expansion: added about 17,000 hectares last year and on track to repeat this year; LRP target to take area from about 80,000 ha to about 150,000 ha, with Telangana and Northeast expansion; about 50% of plantations are juvenile (0-4 years).
New capex hurdle: IRR of around 16-18% required for new assets; management says the specialty fats downstream business, when scaled, adds roughly 200 bps to overall EBITDA profile.

Godrej Foods: investments in automation of plants and advertising behind branded B2C; NPD pipeline including chicken momos (launched about 4 months ago) and wet momos (planned in 3-4 months), and frozen chicken category push.
demand_pricing: Animal Nutrition: revenue +12.6% on demand and realisations; cattle feed volume +15%, fish feed volume up ~20%+ (about 7% of segment), cattle feed about 55-56% of segment; total segment volume +7% as poultry was deliberately cut in unprofitable geographies. Management says it passed on about 60-70% of commodity (maize) inflation.

Oil Palm: revenue +28.9% on higher CPO and PKO realisations; oil extraction ratio 18.8% vs 18.4%; FFB volume broadly flat against a strong early-monsoon base last year. Segment margin dipped on a pricing-formula change that management calls one-off.

Crop Care: revenue -16.2% on a 40% June rainfall deficit delaying sowing; cotton herbicide volume hit. Ashitaka (maize) and Takai (paddy insecticide) together 18-20% of Q1 sales; July said to be better than last year's base. Management said no share loss to competitors; cited product-mix differences versus peers.

Dairy (CDPL): volume +8% and value +11.5%; value-added share 49% vs 42%. Packaging inflation (linked to crude/LPG after Middle East conflict) and milk procurement prices hurt margin; industry passed on about 70% of price increases.

Godrej Foods: B2C (Yummiez and Real Good) volumes +28% (Yummiez +22%), about 32% of Foods business; overall Foods revenue only about 1-2% growth due to planned live bird decline; B2C value growth about 20%.
Bangladesh JV (ACI Godrej Agrovet): strong double-digit growth in volume, value and PBT under new leadership.
risks_watch: Crop Care recovery depends on the cotton herbicide season and erratic rainfall; management will give a firm view only by end-September.
Dairy margin pressure from elevated milk procurement prices (expected to persist 2-3 quarters) and packaging costs, with some impact likely in Q2.
Oil Palm Q1 margin decline (19% to 17% EBIT) attributed to a pricing formula; watch whether H2 margin recovers as management expects.
Astec: CDMO revenue shifting from H1 into H2, and the 8-9% Q1 dip must be recovered to hit the more-than-20% FY27 target.
Animal Nutrition: poultry volume cuts and maize cost volatility; the segment reported volume growth (+7%) lags cattle feed (+15%).
Godrej Foods reported top line stays near flat (1-2%) while B2C invests; profitability is pressured by input costs and the investment phase.
key_quotes: So I would say, yes, there has been a hit in the quarter 1, which has very clearly come because of this weather pattern.
Nothing crosses our bridge broadly beyond -- until we are doing an IRR of around 16% to 18%, and this meets that bridge for us.
But I think one thing we're still pretty confident of is that we'll be able to target a double -digit growth still.
We have a tight filter on this very clearly. This is a high ROCE business for us.
540743|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on Oil Palm, Animal Nutrition and Astec, but cautious on Crop Care and the consolidated guidance, which management says will be narrowed only at end-September. Several answers stressed one-off factors (packaging, pricing formula, weather) while deferring specifics on Crop Care and dairy margins.

540749|2026-06.headline: MAS Financial Q1 FY27: consolidated AUM up 21% to INR16,100 crores and PAT up 27% to INR110 crores; credit cost guided 1.25%-1.75%.
540749|2026-06.overview: Consolidated AUM grew about 21% YoY to INR16,100 crores and PAT rose about 27% to INR110 crores, with standalone PAT up 25% to INR105 crores. Asset quality was stable, with standalone GNPA at 2.58% and NNPA at 1.70%, flat QoQ, and a management overlay of INR17.60 crores held. Borrowing cost fell 55 bps YoY to 9.25%, while credit cost rose to about 1.6% of AUM, which management attributed to higher on-book mix, a 5 bps rise in Stage 1/2 provisioning and prudent write-offs. Management reiterated 20-25% AUM growth guidance, with the call leaning toward the upper end for FY27.

segments.name: MEL (Micro/MSME loans)
segments.commentary: Book grew 23% from INR5,009 crores to INR6,153 crores; MEL is about 77% of loan book combined with SME.

segments.name: SME loans
segments.commentary: Grew 21% from INR4,526 crores to INR5,485 crores.

segments.name: Two-wheeler loans
segments.commentary: Grew 19% from INR872 crores to INR1,039 crores; management said Q1 is seasonally muted, with festive Q3/Q4 stronger.

segments.name: Commercial vehicle (used CV)
segments.commentary: Grew 13% from INR967 crores to INR1,096 crores; eligible demand softer on fuel-cost-driven credit tightening, with growth push deferred 1-2 quarters.

segments.name: Salaried personal loans
segments.commentary: Grew 21% from INR1,131 crores to INR1,374 crores; about 9% of the loan book.

segments.name: Housing finance subsidiary
segments.commentary: AUM INR976 crores, GS3 0.98% and NS3 0.68%; PBT up 62% to INR5.70 crores; average yield about 14%, credit cost about 0.5%. Expansion into Tamil Nadu and Karnataka starts this quarter.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guidance maintained at 20-25%, with management saying the full year is very likely to be at the higher end of the range.
Credit cost to stay in a 1.25%-1.75% range, depending on product mix; management pointed to commercial vehicles as high-yield, high-loss.
ROA target of 2.75%-3.25%, with an aspiration of 3%+.
Net interest margin target of 8%-8.5% on a 7%-7.5% spread; incremental borrowing cost 9.2%-9.25%, expected to stay stable (9.2%-9.3% per Q&A).
Direct distribution share (currently 66%-67%) expected to reach 70%-72% in 1-1.5 years; off-book target kept at 20-25% of AUM.
Used CV growth expected to pick up only after 1-2 quarters; housing finance AUM expected to inch up in the next few quarters.
Credit rating upgrade being pursued, timing not given; sub-9% borrowing cost called far-fetched in the next 1-2 quarters.
capex_capacity: Distribution of 16,500 centres through 209 branches, with more than 200 NBFC partners providing about 33% of originations; direct share 67%.
Employee count reduced by 380 in Q1 due to technology adoption; no quantified headcount target given.
In-house tech team of close to 100 people; LOS live for all products, with BRE added and straight-through processing improving.
Branches opened after March 2024 expected to mature (sweat) by 2027-28 or earlier.
demand_pricing: Standalone MSME/SME demand stable across manufacturing and trading; eligible demand fell in Q1 due to tighter credit screens on energy-dependent sectors (restaurants, gas-dependent manufacturing, export businesses).
Used CV demand robust, but eligible demand lower because of fuel-cost tightening.
Two-wheeler Q1 degrowth QoQ attributed to seasonality; monsoon and Gujarat floods flagged as temporary and not expected to cause major stress.
Working capital demand rising for some businesses on higher input costs; underwriting parameters also tightened.
Write-offs were INR29 crores in March and INR19 crores in June, offset by higher ECL provisioning, keeping impairment cost flat QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: Why did credit cost rise from about 1.2-1.3% to about 1.6% of AUM despite the microfinance impact and Q4 write-offs last year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited higher on-book assets (on-book up 8.25% QoQ vs AUM up 5.5%), which added INR6-7 crores of Stage 1/2 provisioning from a 5 bps rise to 0.7%. Prudent write-offs and mix shift toward higher-yield commercial vehicles also contributed; ROA not affected.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20-25% growth guidance at risk given the West Asia conflict and energy-linked stress?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said energy-dependent segments were tightened early and stress was limited; eligible demand fell in Q1 and Q2 but normalised, and guidance is expected to hold with the upper end targeted.

qa_highlights.question: Will borrowing cost fall further from 9.25%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is hard to predict and depends on RBI and liquidity; the target is to stabilise at 9.2%-9.3%, with a credit rating upgrade being pursued.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reason for the Stage 1/2 provisioning increase and whether there are macro-related buffers?
qa_highlights.answer: Stage 1/2 provisioning rose to 0.7% from 0.65%, adding INR6-7 crores; management described it as a buffer.

qa_highlights.question: What was the nature of the INR10 crore OCPS redemption in the subsidiary MRHMFL?
qa_highlights.answer: The OCPS was refunded to the parent because the housing subsidiary's CRAR exceeded 37% and it did not need the capital.

qa_highlights.question: Why did off-book share fall and what is the housing finance growth plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Off-book is dynamic and chosen by price; target stays at 20-25%. Housing finance plans to expand into Tamil Nadu and Karnataka from Q1, with results expected in Q3-Q4.

risks_watch: Used CV: eligible demand softer on fuel-cost-driven credit tightening; management says growth push is 1-2 quarters away, and CV is high-yield, high-loss, so credit cost direction depends on mix.

Credit cost: rose to about 1.6% of AUM from about 1.2-1.3% a year earlier; management guides a 1.25%-1.75% range and Stage 1/2 provisioning went to 0.7% from 0.65% (INR6-7 crores), which management calls a buffer.
Energy-linked and West Asia stress: eligible demand fell in Q1 and Q2 and management says it has normalised; the next quarter will show whether this holds.
Borrowing cost: 9.25% average with incremental cost at 9.2%-9.3%; a sub-9% level is called far-fetched in the next 1-2 quarters, and the credit rating upgrade has no timing.

Off-book share fell below the 20%-25% target this quarter; management says it is opportunistic and the target is unchanged. Gujarat floods and monsoon effects on two-wheeler and collections are still unquantified.
key_quotes: So, very high possibility, yes. We are working on that quite optimistic. Can't predict, but you are thinking on the right lines.
So, that is the impact which translates to roughly around between INR5 crores to INR7 crores in provisioning.
Difficult to comment right now because the cost of borrowing is dependent on the macro situation.
So, currently, sub-9 immediately within next 1 or 2 quarters looks like a far -fetched assumption.
540749|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on headline growth, profitability and asset quality, with the 20%-25% AUM guidance reaffirmed and the upper end targeted. More cautious and non-committal on credit cost trajectory, borrowing cost, used CV recovery timing and the flood impact, where management repeatedly said it cannot yet predict or quantify.

540750|2026-06.headline: IEX Q1 FY27 consolidated PAT rose about 12% to Rs 134.8 crore on Rs 202.8 crore revenue, with electricity volume up 16% to 37.5 billion units.
540750|2026-06.overview: IEX reported Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue of Rs 202.8 crore and PAT of Rs 134.8 crore, up about 12% YoY, on electricity volume of 37.5 billion units (+16%). Real-Time Market growth was the main driver, with RTM up about 25% in Q1 and its share of mix reaching about 34% last year. Management used the analyst meet to push a set of new products (Green RTM, peak contracts, 11-month TAM, carbon trading, coal exchange) while pushing back on CERC's proposed market coupling and the Day-Ahead Market pilot, which it has challenged at APTEL and the Supreme Court. The call was mostly a policy and product narrative; no formal FY27 guidance was given.

segments.name: Electricity (DAM / RTM / TAM)
segments.commentary: RTM is now roughly the size of DAM; DAM share of mix fell from 95% in FY16 to about 39%, RTM rose to about 34% in FY26, and RTM is up about 25% in Q1 FY27. Term-Ahead Market and Green Market are about 7-8% of the mix.

segments.name: IGX (gas exchange, associate)
segments.commentary: FY26 volume 76.8 million MMBtu and PAT Rs 42 crore; Q1 FY27 volume 27.5 million MMBtu and PAT Rs 16 crore. DRHP filed for IPO of a 22.3% stake to bring IEX's 47.3% holding down to 25% under PNGRB rules, after a one-year extension.

segments.name: ICX (I-REC / environmental)
segments.commentary: Sole I-REC issuer in India; management cited about 200% growth in I-REC volumes last year. Q1 REC volumes were down sharply YoY, which management attributed to the first quarter and possible RPO buy-out confusion.

segments.name: Indian Coal Exchange (new)
segments.commentary: Incorporated as a separate company in June 2026; coal rules notified 4 June 2026 require e-auction and marketplace trades to move to exchanges within six months of launch. Market size cited at about 120 million tonnes today, with a target of at least 100 million tonnes in year one.

guidance_outlook: No formal FY27 volume or revenue guidance given; management expects RTM volumes to grow about 25-30% a year.
Management expects carbon credit trading to begin in FY27, with BEE targeting 1 October 2026.

Management expects the Green RTM, peak-power contracts (DAM and RTM) and 11-month TAM products to be approved by CERC; timing was not committed, and the 11-month TAM application has been pending for over two years.
Management sees the exchange-routed share of electricity rising to about 25% over five to six years, against about 14-15% short-term market today.
Management said it would consider a buyback in future, citing SEBI's revised market-buyback rules.
Management said the coal exchange's fee should exceed those of MSTC and M-Junction, since exchanges perform price discovery, clearing and settlement.
capex_capacity: Management cited about 80 GW of thermal capacity in the pipeline, 41 GW under construction with PPAs signed, 20 GW awarded, and 16 GW in planning; most is expected in FY31-FY33.
Management said it has built a hot standby for RTM and a DC-to-DR switch; both were positioned as ready for the proposed 5-minute bidding window.

BESS merchant capacity cited: ACME about 3,200 MWh, Juniper about 500 MWh, Adani about 3,400 MWh, with more than Rs 9,000 crore of BESS VGF support. Management said the arbitrage window may last 3-5 years.
The SECI 500 MW CfD pilot for peak power was cited as launched; it is a peak-power product, not solar.
demand_pricing: Management expects demand growth of about 5-5.5% a year, versus 11% in Q1 FY27 on heat and delayed monsoon. Peak demand touched about 271 GW in May and July.
Management said exchanges as a group grew 18% in FY26 against 1% demand growth.

On market coupling, CERC proposed Grid India as Market Coupling Operator, with DAM first. Management said it has challenged the July 2025 order at APTEL (order dated 13 February 2026) and is now before the Supreme Court; a second hearing was held on 27 July 2026.
Management said that even after coupling, DAM share could fall 20-40%, but said business impact would not be significant. The market-share loss figure is management's own estimate.
Management said top-10 sellers account for about 40% of the sell side and the top-buyer concentration is 50-60%, with 800-900 participants daily.

Management cited an RTM realisation issue in a Q&A: an analyst's per-unit realisation calculation (about 0.4 paisa vs 3.7 paisa a year earlier) was not reconciled; management pointed to incentives in REC and TAM.

financial_highlights.change: about 11% QoQ per management; YoY not stated

qa_highlights.question: What RTM share of the mix to expect over the next 3-5 years, and what could be the next star product after RTM (peak contracts, Green RTM, BESS)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said RTM has grown about 30-35% CAGR since 2020 and expects RTM volumes to keep growing 25-30% a year, possibly exceeding DAM volumes over time; it named BESS as a potential next growth product. No numeric RTM share target was given.

qa_highlights.question: Will IEX pursue a buyback given low valuations, and can IEX shareholders get a reservation in the IGX IPO?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said an IGX IPO reservation for IEX shareholders is not really possible as it is an independent IPO. It said a buyback will be considered in future, since SEBI has revised the rules for market buybacks.

qa_highlights.question: Why has RTM grown to near DAM size in India, unlike in Europe where DAM dominates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to 25-year PPAs covering about 85% of DISCOM demand, with DAM used for seasonal and daily shortfalls and RTM used to handle renewable variability; it said PPAs will persist because banks lend only against them.

qa_highlights.question: How far can exchange share of electricity grow given long-term PPAs dominate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said exchange-routed share could reach about 25% of generation in five to six years, versus about 14-15% in the short-term market today, as bilateral and trader transactions shrink.

qa_highlights.question: Who bears the cost of Grid India as Market Coupling Operator, and will MCO fees force IEX to cut fees?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said all costs are ultimately passed to consumers, directly or indirectly, and that cost allocation and fee questions are among the open issues Grid India has raised with CERC; no timeline or answer was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the likely timeline for final market coupling regulations, and what is the expected DAM market-share loss?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a timeline, citing the need to examine software, settlement and reliability, and compared it to availability-based tariff taking years. On share loss, management said it sees no material loss given customer integration, though it earlier estimated DAM share could fall 20-40%.

qa_highlights.question: Does the market coupling challenge affect CERC approval of the new products?
qa_highlights.answer: Goel said the legal challenge is against the order, not CERC, and that regulators and government are aligned on peak power products. He said delays are due to procedural hurdles and the products will be released over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why did REC volumes fall about 80% YoY and QoQ, and why is standalone realisation per unit down sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is early in the year and that a draft allowing RPO buy-out has created market confusion, which will lift REC volumes once clarified. On realisation, management pointed to incentives in REC and Term-Ahead Market and did not reconcile the 0.4 paisa vs 3.7 paisa comparison.

qa_highlights.question: What is the long-duration 11-month Term-Ahead contract timeline, given the application is over two years old?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is difficult to say when approval will come, as CERC is reviewing performance of the existing 3-month contracts and standardising longer contracts, and that contracts beyond 3 months are currently not significant in volume.

qa_highlights.question: How does the 0.3% social welfare gain claim and DAM coupling risk relate to customer concentration, and what is the buyer/seller concentration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said top-10 sellers account for about 40% of the sell side, buyer concentration is about 50-60% of volume, and 800-900 participants trade daily; it said concentration on the buy side has been falling.

qa_highlights.question: Why are sell bids in daytime far above cleared volumes, and is solar being curtailed in the exchange?
qa_highlights.answer: Rohit said about 10,000-12,000 MW clears in daytime, of which solar is only about 2,000-3,000 MW, and curtailment is mainly thermal, not solar; solar has not reached the stage of curtailment on the exchange.

qa_highlights.question: How long will BESS arbitrage last and are two cycles per year feasible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said two cycles are possible on 100-150 days, mainly in winter, and that arbitrage may last 3-5 years, with no definitive model; it cited FY26 arbitrage of Rs 4.81 per cycle versus Rs 5.03 in FY25 and Rs 3.80 in FY24.

risks_watch: Timing of CERC approval for Green RTM, peak power contracts and 11-month TAM; orders reserved, and the 11-month TAM application has been pending over two years.
Market coupling: Supreme Court hearing (second hearing 27 July 2026), Grid India's objections to MCO design, and management's own 20-40% DAM share-loss estimate.
Proposed RTM window cut from 15 to 5 minutes and gate closure from 75 to 50 minutes, which could reduce liquidity or affect bidding systems.
Q1 FY27 REC volume decline and a draft RPO buy-out rule that could change REC demand; realisation per unit fell sharply in the analyst's calculation and was not reconciled.
Coal exchange: registration and licensing under way, six-month transition away from e-auction, and competition from MSTC and M-Junction; fee levels not yet set.
IGX IPO (22.3% stake sale) and PNGRB stake dilution from 47.3% to 25%; IGX Q1 PAT of Rs 16 crore needs to hold.
key_quotes: And I am sure with the kind of trust which we have built over the years in these last 18 years, we should be able to retain significant market share even in the Day-Ahead Market.
So, as far as business is concerned, I do not think it is going to be significant.
So, it will be difficult for me to give any timeline on this , I can only tell you one thing that sometime in 1994-95 when availability--based tariff was first discussed in the country.
The IGX IPO is an independent IPO, but buyback, yes definitely, we will consider it in future because now SEBI also has revised its rules for doing the buyback through the market.
540750|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on growth drivers, RTM and BESS arbitrage, and the view that market coupling will have limited business impact. Noticeably cautious and non-committal on timelines for CERC approvals, market coupling regulations, the 11-month TAM contract, and the buyback, and openly declined several numeric questions.

540755|2026-03.headline: GIC Re FY26 profit after tax rose 25.23% to INR8,392.18 crores, with combined ratio down 2.79 points to 106.02%.

540762|2026-06.headline: TII Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 18% to Rs 2,366 Cr, but PBT fell to Rs 213 Cr on steel cost lag; management expects full recovery.
540762|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew to Rs 2,366 Cr from Rs 2,007 Cr, while standalone PBT declined to Rs 213 Cr from Rs 222 Cr, with management attributing margin pressure to steel price increases in Q4 and Q1 that pass through to customers with a 2-3 quarter lag. Engineering revenue rose 21% to Rs 1,566 Cr with flat PBIT at Rs 153 Cr, and Metal Formed Products PBIT fell to Rs 28 Cr from Rs 37 Cr despite 11.5% revenue growth. The e-mobility (Clean Mobility) business posted its highest-ever quarterly turnover of close to Rs 240 Cr and management said losses likely peaked, with volumes up about 64% QoQ. Management said steel price recovery, including Q1 under-recovery, will be fully recovered, while non-steel inflation (fuel, freight) recovery talks with OEMs are ongoing.

qa_highlights.question: Will the steel under-recovery be recovered cumulatively, not just passed through with lag?
qa_highlights.answer: Confirmed: steel price increases including Q1 will be fully recovered.

qa_highlights.question: What changed in MFP to drive 11.5% revenue growth, given railways was a drag?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth was volume-led with no price recovery yet; railways remained a drag and the Hyundai-dependent unit was weak, while a western region greenfield plant is delayed by six months.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the roughly Rs 40-50 Cr reduction in e-mobility negative EBIT, and is this one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Clean Mobility posted its highest-ever turnover of close to Rs 240 Cr with traction across all four businesses; volumes rose about 64% QoQ. Management confirmed it is routine volume-driven, not a one-off benefit.

qa_highlights.question: Are e-mobility losses past peak and what are breakeven timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Directionally yes, losses are past peak if volumes keep rising QoQ; one business expected to break even this year and two more in the next financial year.

qa_highlights.question: Why is three-wheeler billing (1,924 in Q1) above Vahan registrations?
qa_highlights.answer: Billing-to-registration lag of 30-45 days; FY26 billing was about 6,700 vs Vahan about 6,500, and Q4 billing was only about 1,200 due to a supply-link issue. Numbers tend to tally within 3-6 months.

qa_highlights.question: How much standalone capital will be infused into new ventures in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Rs 250 Cr infused in Q4 FY26 and another Rs 250 Cr expected in Q3 FY27, within an overall Rs 750 Cr guidance.

qa_highlights.question: How will non-steel inflation (fuel, freight) from the West Asia crisis be recovered, and when will margins normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Discussions with OEMs on non-steel recovery have started; an update is expected in about a quarter, and management is hopeful most of it will be recovered.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the cycles margin expansion and what is the target?
qa_highlights.answer: Strong Q1 seasonality (schools and colleges reopening) and higher market share; management targets about 2 more basis points (likely percentage points) of improvement, with about 5% margin as the current target.

qa_highlights.question: What is Orange Koi, and what is the plan?
qa_highlights.answer: A small metal injection moulding start-up acquired as a step into additive manufacturing; it sits in Others, with a strategy update expected in about two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Jayem outlook, and are its batteries for captive use?
qa_highlights.answer: Jayem faced design and development headwinds; a battery assembly line is being set up as a third revenue stream, initially for in-house SCV and three-wheeler use, with external sales later.

qa_highlights.question: What are group capex plans excluding CG Power?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 350 Cr for TI standalone and Rs 100 Cr for Shanthi Gears in FY27, with group ex-CG Power around Rs 600-700 Cr; spend goes to Engineering, MFP, TI Medical and 3xper CDMO.

qa_highlights.question: What is the structure and timing of external investors in TI Clean Mobility?
qa_highlights.answer: Three external investors hold CCPS that convert only at IPO, with no fixed timeline; stake will be set by valuation at that time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the demand outlook and export share for Engineering?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand expected to stay bullish for one or two quarters barring geopolitical disruption; exports grew at double-digit rates and are about 14% of TI revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What are the cell supply and price outlook for Clean Mobility?
qa_highlights.answer: Cell prices expected to stay firm at least through Q3 FY27 due to BESS demand; mitigation via pre-booking long lead-time orders and locking prices.

540777|2026-06.headline: HDFC Life Q1 FY27 VNB rose 9% to INR 879 crores at a 25% margin, with individual APE up 7% and HDFC Bank channel subdued.
540777|2026-06.overview: Individual APE grew 7% YoY and overall APE 9%, led by credit life and group, while channels excluding HDFC Bank grew about 17% with agency up 21%. VNB rose 9% to INR 879 crores and new business margin was 25%, up 100 bps QoQ, after absorbing about 60 bps residual GST impact. Profit after tax was INR 611 crores (up 12%, or 17% excluding GST), embedded value INR 65,860 crores and solvency 185%. 13-month persistency moderated about 200 bps to 84%, and HDFC Bank channel business stayed soft as the company ceded share during competitive pricing in FY26 and says it has now recovered.

financial_highlights.change: +100 bps QoQ; GST impact approx. 60 bps
Improved after INR 1,000 crore preferential allotment by HDFC Bank; additional sub-debt capacity INR 500 crores (about 4% upside)

segments.name: Non-bank alliances
segments.commentary: Retail protection grew 60% YoY, driven mainly by aggregators; market share across partners broadly stable.

segments.name: HDFC Bank channel
segments.commentary: Subdued growth as the bank base is large and the company let share go in competitive segments in 4-6 months of FY26. Share has recovered toward year-ago levels on a run-rate basis; HDFC Bank contributed 47% of retail APE this quarter.

segments.commentary: Grew about 15% in the quarter as competitive intensity moderated across other banks.

segments.name: Product mix (individual APE)
segments.commentary: Unit-linked 44%, non-par savings 22% (run-rate mid-20s by quarter-end), participating 15%, retail protection 8% (about 11% including riders), annuities 11% (nearly doubled from 5%). Protection grew over 40% YoY; credit protect grew 19%.

segments.name: HDFC Pension Fund Management (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Market share 43% with AUM of about INR 1.75 lakh crores, up 33% YoY.

guidance_outlook: FY27 aspiration unchanged: grow in line with or faster than the industry, and deliver VNB growth broadly in line with APE growth.
Industry growth base case about 15-17%; company needs to grow a little over 16% over the remaining nine months to match industry-level growth.
New business margin expected to remain range-bound around current levels (about 25%); management says the company will prioritise growth over margin expansion.
Residual GST impact of about 60 bps expected to be neutralised over the coming quarters; it will be in the base from H2.
Protection growth rates may moderate in H2 as the recent tailwind normalises; non-par share expected to improve gradually; unit-linked mix not expected to rise meaningfully.

qa_highlights.question: Why has margin improved only modestly over the last 7-8 years versus peers, and what is the basis for confidence in FY27 growth and VNB?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins expanded 100-150 bps per two-year period to FY22, then fell about 90 bps (FY22-24) on regulatory changes, with 26.3% in FY24 and a 100 bps surrender-charge impact in FY25; the GST impact was 300 bps, of which about 110 bps remained at FY26 end, 50 bps was absorbed in Q1 and about 60 bps is still to go. Growth confidence rests on agency (up 21%) and proprietary channels (up over 20%).

qa_highlights.question: Will non-par and product mix sustain, and what happens to margins if ULIP picks up?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said ULIP mix will not rise meaningfully, non-par expected to hold mid-20s share, annuities to stay well above last year, and NBM to stay around 25%-odd. Protection's share may stay roughly where it is, and growth may be higher in the next nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Has the HDFC Bank counter share recovered, and what is the target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said bank share has returned to roughly the level of a year ago on a run-rate basis, with pricing more benign; the company declined to give channel-wise growth guidance and said it is tracking selectively by segment (non-par, protection, par over unit-linked).

qa_highlights.question: Is the non-par recovery demand-led or a result of company pricing and yield-curve effects?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said it is a combination: competitor intensity has eased, the company can compete on sensible terms, headline rates are higher than a year ago, and customer asset allocation toward guaranteed products is also a driver. He said the company will not compete on price alone.

qa_highlights.question: What is the banca growth outlook, and how does HDFC Bank compare on a 2-year CAGR basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Banca beyond HDFC Bank grew about 15% in Q1. HDFC Bank was described as marginally lower or flattish YoY; on a 2-year CAGR basis it is similar to other banks at about 10%, and management guided 10-12% growth for HDFC Bank.

qa_highlights.question: How much runway does capital have before a fundraise, and what is the variable annuity opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Solvency is 185% with INR 500 crore sub-debt capacity (about 4% upside); management is comfortable with 15-18 months runway at the current run rate. Variable annuity: two product structures launched, aimed at customers willing to commit for a longer period, slightly younger and with lower ticket sizes; margins said to be above company average.

qa_highlights.question: What is the persistency outlook, given traditional persistency fell from 88-89% to about 83%?
qa_highlights.answer: Appointed Actuary cited a shift to lower ticket sizes after the tax change, a product feature that drove lapses (now moderated, about 40-50 bps effect), and the Q1 March-pace effect. Expected traditional persistency range is 84-85%; 87-88% was not expected in the near term.

540777|2026-09.headline: HDFC Life H1 FY27 VNB rose 12% to ₹2,037 crore at a 24.7% margin, while solvency fell to 180% on capital consumption.
540777|2026-09.overview: Q2 individual APE growth of 13% (overall) and 11% in H1 kept HDFC Life ahead of the private industry, with individual weighted received premium up 11% in Q2 and market share up 10bps to 16.2%. VNB reached ₹2,037 crore (up 12%, Q2 up 15%) and margin expanded to 24.7% from 24.5%. Persistency softened on unit-linked renewals and a non-par cohort, and the EV walk showed negative operating and investment variances from equity underperformance, yield rises and wider credit spreads. Solvency fell to 180%, prompting a ₹500 crore subordinated debt raise. Management spent much of the call on the IRDAI distribution-economics consultation paper, where it was non-committal on specifics.

financial_highlights.change: Regulatory requirement 150%; ₹500 crore sub-debt expected to add about 4 percentage points
Q2 individual weighted received premium +11% vs private industry +10%

segments.name: Agency
segments.commentary: Agency grew 13% in H1, faster than the company and the agency market. Branches opened in the last ~30 months contribute about 17% of agency business versus 12% a year ago; protection and annuity together are about 30% of channel mix versus 15% previously.

segments.name: Product mix (individual APE, H1)
segments.commentary: Unit-linked 45%, non-par savings 22% (from about 18%), participating 13%, annuity 12% (versus 4-5% previously), retail protection 8% (from about 7%). Retail protection grew 33% in H1; protection plus riders is 11% of APE; credit protect grew 19%.

segments.name: Subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Pension business AUM reached ₹1.8 lakh crore, up 28% YoY. MSCI ESG rating upgraded to AAA from AA.

guidance_outlook: Expects individual APE growth in FY27 to be in line with the industry, after 9% in H1.
VNB growth to be in line with APE or slightly ahead; management will prioritise VNB growth over margin, with margin an outcome of mix and competition.

qa_highlights.question: What changed at HDFC Bank that drove growth recovery, and did IRRs or commissions change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited granular branch-level engagement, a withdrawal of extra contests about a year ago, and fixing credit and people issues over the last 3-4 months. Rates were kept competitive with higher yields; no change in commercial payouts.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the EV walk operating variance is persistency, and what drove the investment variance?
qa_highlights.answer: Operating variance was primarily unit-linked persistency plus residual non-par run-off. Investment variance came from equity returns of about 3-3.5% versus 5% expected, a 25-30bps short-end yield rise, and wider credit spreads.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the capital consumption and how will solvency evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Long-term profitable products lock capital under the current regime; the sub-debt adds about 4 percentage points, and management expects to remain comfortably above 150% through FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How do the proposed commission limits affect VNB margin and EoM?
qa_highlights.answer: Expense ratio about 21%, with commissions more than half; under the proposed levels, commissions fall to half or less, so a 15% EoM is mathematically achievable, subject to scale and glide-path considerations.

qa_highlights.question: Is persistency pressure concentrated in TULIPs or the wider unit-linked book?
qa_highlights.answer: Not limited to any product: pressure is uniform across unit-linked. Recent unit-linked persistency variance is captured in the EV; management expects most to be recovered by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the credit life share, and what is the HDFC Bank share of it?
qa_highlights.answer: HDFC Bank contributes less than one-third of credit life business, which is diversified across MFIs, NBFCs, banks and the HDFC Group. Management would not disclose the bundled-versus-separate premium collection mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Palghar GST demand, and does the appeal change the provisioning stance?

Interest is excluded and management is confident on the merits, so no provision was taken; contingent liabilities rose to ₹2,207 crore from ₹1,870 crore.

540795|2026-06.headline: Dynamic Cables Q1 FY27 revenue rose 33% YoY to a record Q1 level, with EBITDA up 41% to INR38 crore and order book at INR811 crore.
540795|2026-06.overview: Management reported record first-quarter revenue, up 33% YoY, with EBITDA up 41% to INR38 crore (margin 10.9%) and PAT up 37% to INR25 crore. Growth was largely price-driven: volume grew only 5-6% against a high base of roughly 25-26% last year, as aluminium price spikes led to order postponements in April-May. The company entered the US market in the quarter with first supplies, and the new capacity expansion is on track for commissioning from September 2026, with meaningful revenue expected from Q4. Order book stood at INR811 crore as of 30 June 2026, with customers booking shorter cycles at elevated prices.

segments.name: Conductor
segments.commentary: 2% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Conductor volume growth was lower than cable volume growth in the quarter.

segments.name: Solar / renewable cables

segments.name: Railway signalling
segments.commentary: Temporarily held back due to weak margins and competition; not a shutdown. Zero contribution in last Q1, so no base effect this quarter.

US market: margins initially similar to domestic, with possible incremental margins later; no one-year target given.

qa_highlights.answer: Variable-price contracts carry a clause passing input cost changes to customers; for fixed-price orders, raw material is booked at order time to protect margins.

qa_highlights.answer: Volume grew 5-6% YoY; most of the balance of revenue growth came from aluminium-driven price increases. Base effect was high at about 25-26% volume growth last year.

qa_highlights.question: Why was growth weaker in Q1 and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Base effect, plus customer order postponements after a sharp input price rise in March-May. Management expects improvement as prices settle but calls the environment very uncertain.

qa_highlights.question: Is the new plant on schedule?

qa_highlights.question: Why is order book only about 10% up YoY?

Manufacturing revenue rose to INR9,227 crore from INR7,957 crore, while ROH revenue was INR20,524 crore. Order book rose to INR2,54,538 crore after FY26 fresh orders of INR97,028 crore. The main overhang is the delayed LCA Mk-1A delivery to the IAF, which management now targets for August-September 2026, tied to GE engine supply.

financial_highlights.change: +11% vs INR12,168 crore; ~30% of revenue, flat YoY

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR9,227 crore, about 28% of total, driven by ALH, AL-31FP and RD-33 deliveries. Management expects it to grow faster than ROH as LCA Mk-1A and HTT-40 deliveries start; mix is expected to move towards 50:50 over time.

segments.name: ROH (repair and overhaul) and spares
segments.commentary: FY26 ROH revenue INR20,524 crore, about 62% of total. Spares sales fell by about INR500-600 crore YoY, while R&O was flat because no new platform was added. ROH is expected to rise once LCA and LCH enter overhaul cycles, with LCA ROH expected in roughly three years.

segments.name: Exports and development
segments.commentary: Export revenue was INR501 crore in FY26, and the export order book is about INR400 crore. Development order book is about INR3,000 crore, roughly 10% of total mix.

segments.name: LCA Mk-1A (97 aircraft contract)
segments.commentary: Inventory for LCA is about INR7,500-8,100 crore including raw material and WIP. Management targets about 20 LCA deliveries in FY27, with the first deliveries expected August-September 2026 as GE engines arrive.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at double-digit, specified as about 10-12% minimum, versus about 7% in FY26.
EBITDA margin guided at around 30-31%, which management says will be maintained with manufacturing mix rising.
About 20 LCA Mk-1A deliveries targeted in FY27 (GE engine supply of around 20 expected), with first delivery August-September 2026; 1 engine expected in June, 2 per month from August.
HTT-40: about 20+ units planned for FY27, Honeywell engines expected from next month; LCH delivery as per contract in FY27-FY28.
Su-30 MKI: 1 aircraft due in FY27 and 11 in FY28-29 per contract.
Expected orders of about INR90,000 crore including ROH over the next 2 years, with 143 ALH and 40 Do-228 upgrades in approval.
Plan to invest about INR12,000 crore by 2030 in new manufacturing infrastructure (LCA Mk-2, GE F414, IMRH engines, SSLV).
capex_capacity: Third LCA Mk-1A production line at Nashik inaugurated 17 October 2025, establishing 8 aircraft per annum capacity; total LCA production lines now 3 (2 Bengaluru, 1 Nashik) with capacity of 24 LCA per year referenced.
HTT-40 now has two lines (Bengaluru and Nashik); ALH augmented in the helicopter division with private vendors helping on structures; ALH output of about 20-25 per year.
Management says none of the lines are idle; 20+ LCA airframes are built with engine ground runs complete, and 97-aircraft order will utilise facilities fully.
Su-30 MKI upgrade is in design phase, with CCS approval expected this fiscal; design to take 5-6 years before production.
Tejas Mk-2 prototype rollout targeted by March 2027 (joint design with ADA); rotary UAV (CATS Warrior) actual build underway with flight expected next year.
AL-31FP target of 32-35 engines per year; RD-33 has 15 engines left, to be delivered in FY27.
demand_pricing: Order book INR2,54,538 crore; FY26 fresh orders INR97,028 crore (manufacturing INR69,668 crore, ROH INR26,539 crore). Major wins: 97 LCA Mk-1A for IAF, 6 ALH Mk III for ICG, 8 Do-228 for ICG, 10 ALH Dhruv NG for Pawan Hans, 2 Hindustan-228 for Guyana.
Major platform order book of about INR2.84 lakh crore across LCA, Su-30, AL-31FP, Do-228, ALH, LCH, HTT-40 and RD-33.
Pipeline: 143 ALH for the Army, Su-30 upgrade, upgrade of 40 Do-228; ALH 137 is the largest contributor. Values not disclosed as contracts are not finalised.

Pricing: ROH is priced on cost-plus under the PPRC mechanism (10-15% margin cited); ERV (exchange rate) clause is in every contract including ROH; material escalation factored into contracts; 97 LCA purchase orders already placed, so no FY27 cost increase expected.

Revenue recognition for manufacturing is on delivery, not percentage of completion, so FY28-29 could be lumpy. Unbilled revenue relates to delivered aircraft awaiting documentation, not to undelivered inventory.

qa_highlights.question: When will the IAF accept the first LCA Mk-1A lot, and what are FY27 revenue and EBITDA guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: CMD said six GE engines received and aircraft flying; remaining tests to be discussed with IAF, targeting stabilisation by August or September. CFO guided double-digit revenue growth and EBITDA margin around 30-31%.

qa_highlights.question: What is holding up LCA delivery and how big is the issue?
qa_highlights.answer: CMD said testing refines already-tested items and is an iterative design and development process; declined to give details, saying HAL is confident of a September deadline.

qa_highlights.question: How many LCA are factored into guidance and how does GE supply ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Around 20 LCA planned for FY27. GE committed 15-20 more engines; 1 engine in June, 2 per month from August, and 15-20 by year-end. Engines take 30-45 days to convert to delivery.

qa_highlights.question: Will the lumpy LCA revenue and inventory of about INR9,000 crore be realised, and is there any penalty on GE?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory for LCA about INR7,500-8,100 crore. Penalty on GE is a commercial matter under PO terms; management declined to quantify until deliveries occur.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ROH growth slow, and what drives the margin mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Spares fell INR500-600 crore YoY; R&O flat as no new platform added. Manufacturing mix to move from 30:70 towards 50:50, with R&O margin slightly above manufacturing, but management sees no profitability stress.

qa_highlights.question: Provisioning was low in FY26 — what is the steady-state level?
qa_highlights.answer: FY25 included INR800 crore provision after a Su-30 accident; no equivalent event in FY26, so management declined to give a provision-to-revenue guidance.

risks_watch: LCA Mk-1A first delivery slipping beyond August-September 2026; testing and software refinements still in progress, and the 20-aircraft FY27 target depends on GE engine receipts (1 in June, 2 per month from August).
Global supply chain slowness at Tier 1 and Tier 2 vendors affecting components for Su-30, HTT-40 and LCH; Honeywell engine supply stabilised per management.
Unbilled revenue and inventory build (inventory about INR33,000 crore including ROH; unbilled tied to documentation); revenue recognition on delivery makes FY27 and FY28 lumpy.
Penalty on GE for engine delays not quantified; outcome uncertain.
Manpower constraints and private-sector competition; ALH 143-unit order and Su-30 upgrade contract not yet signed (CCS approval expected this FY).
Uttam radar integration not in 83-LCA batch; planned for 97-LCA batch subject to DRDO clearance.
541154|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on FY27 guidance and on ALH, HTT-40 and LCH timelines, but noticeably guarded on LCA: the CMD repeatedly declined to detail the technical issues and the penalty amount, and the timeline moved from earlier commitments to August-September.
key_quotes: We are confident that we will be able to meet the September deadline.
So we are expecting around 20.
And that 30% will be maintained.
Yes, the deliveries of ALH, we have no issues. We have delivered everything as per contract.

541163|2026-03.headline: Sandhar FY26 consolidated revenue INR 4,852 crore (+25%), EBITDA INR 513 crore (10.6% margin); FY27 guided to grow over 15% before any price re-trigger.
541163|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a record year: consolidated revenue rose 25% to INR 4,852 crore, EBITDA rose 28% to INR 513 crore at a 10.6% margin, and PAT rose 40% to INR 199 crore. Q4 consolidated revenue grew 29% YoY with an 11% EBITDA margin, and the India business grew 28% in FY26. Overseas subsidiaries swung to break-even at EBT in Q4 after a FY26 loss of EUR 2.56 million, though aluminium pass-through lags are expected to weigh on Q1 FY27. Management cited April manpower absenteeism and raw material shortages as the main near-term disruption, with May reported as better than April.

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated Q4 revenue and EBITDA margin

financial_highlights.value: Revenue INR 257 crore, EBITDA INR 28.25 crore

financial_highlights.change: Q4 EBITDA margin 14.6%, EBT about break-even
Working capital debt INR 564 crore; term loans INR 384 crore

segments.name: India business
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 4,384 crore (+28%), EBITDA INR 472 crore (+32%). Management said industry grew 12.7% while Sandhar India grew 28%; two-wheeler business grew 35.1% vs industry 12.9%.

segments.name: Overseas subsidiaries
segments.commentary: FY26 loss of EUR 2.56 million; Q4 EBITDA margin 14.6% and EBT roughly break-even. Revenue of about EUR 46 million with full-year decline of about 8.5% in euro terms, per analyst. Pass-through lag of about 180 days in overseas contracts.

segments.name: Joint ventures
segments.commentary: Five JVs generated revenue of INR 257 crore and EBITDA of INR 28.25 crore in FY26; Sandhar investment about INR 62 crore.

segments.name: EV business
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR 20 crore; 41,000 battery chargers and 5,500 motor control units sold. Targeted to double in FY27; EBT turnaround expected in FY28.

segments.name: New projects (Sundaram-Clayton die-casting, Khed City, Sanaswadi cabins/fabrication)
segments.commentary: INR 342 crore invested to generate INR 468 crore revenue in FY26; Sundaram-Clayton FY26 revenue INR 369 crore. Management expects about 2x-2.5x revenue (about INR 750 crore) in FY27. Turnaround timelines: Khed City and Sanaswadi from Q2 FY27, Sundaram-Clayton from Q3 FY27 (still EBT losses for FY27).

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth guided at over 15% (15-16%), excluding a likely price re-trigger on input cost increases.
EBITDA margin expected to improve by about 0.25% in FY27 for existing businesses; new projects will dilute, with 1.5-2 years to profitability.
Management targets doubling revenue every three to four years, with a stated post-tax ROCE target of 15%, peaking at 20%; at INR 10,000 crore revenue, PAT of about INR 450 crore was cited.
FY27 capex estimated at INR 275-310 crore (5-7% of revenue), covering growth, maintenance and upgradation.
Overseas business expected to return to planned levels once aluminium pass-through lag clears; Romania targeted for break-even in FY28.
Manpower availability expected to normalise by end-June 2026 per management, with May better than April.
capex_capacity: Capital work in progress closing balance INR 104-115 crore (figure cited differently on call); mostly expected to capitalise by end of Q2 FY27 as Sundaram-Clayton relocation, Khed City and Sanaswadi projects complete.
Sundaram-Clayton die-casting business shifting to own premises, targeted by end of Q2 FY27.
FY27 capex outlay of INR 275-310 crore expected.

Technology: telematics and smart-key products presented to customers; POCs next, development in FY27, production thereafter. Partnering on royalty-based technology transfer, not JVs; target to take to market within 12 months.
Smart Key locksets at about 5,000 per month and growing.
demand_pricing: Management said domestic auto demand is strong, but manpower constraints limit industry output; absenteeism reached around 20% at one point in April, and state minimum wages rose 30-40%.
Two-wheeler inventory at some customers fell from about 60 days to under 14 days; industry lost an estimated 200,000-300,000 vehicles.

Aluminium and gas costs rose sharply in March-April; India pass-through lag is about three months (aiming for 30 days), and overseas lag about 180 days (aiming for 90 days). Pass-through from June expected to recover April costs.
Price re-trigger expected across the industry as input costs rise; not included in the 15% growth guidance.
Working capital: overseas inventory holding about 54-55 days vs about 12-13 days in India.

qa_highlights.question: How will the planned doubling of revenue every 3-4 years be achieved, and which segments drive it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited two-wheelers, new businesses in sheet metal and casting, and proprietary products like locks and mirrors; it said a 15-16% growth guide is conservative and excludes the price re-trigger.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the new projects and their profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 342 crore invested generated INR 468 crore in FY26 and is expected to reach about INR 750 crore in FY27; Khed City and Sanaswadi turn around in Q2 FY27, Sundaram-Clayton in Q3 with EBT losses for FY27, EV and Romania in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margins improve and by how much?
qa_highlights.answer: Existing businesses are targeted to gain about 0.25% in EBITDA margin in FY27; new projects will dilute margins until they mature, with 1.5-2 years to turnaround.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt position and debt-to-equity trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross debt INR 948 crore, of which INR 564 crore is working capital debt; term loans INR 384 crore with about INR 103 crore repayable this year. Management called the debt-to-equity ratio healthy versus peers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did overseas borrowings rise in INR terms despite a small euro increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Bill discounting was reclassified to borrowings under Ind AS, and INR translation at the closing rate (about INR 111 per euro vs INR 108 in March) inflated the INR figure; the euro increase was about EUR 5 million.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company keep the overseas business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the overseas presence supports Indian customer relationships; it will revisit the business after the year but gave no decision.

qa_highlights.question: What is the company's competitive advantage in castings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited integrated capability across high- and low-pressure die casting, machining, zinc, magnesium and aluminium castings, from small to very large parts including engine blocks.

risks_watch: Aluminium and gas cost pass-through lags of three months in India and about 180 days overseas, which will hit Q1 FY27 margins.
Manpower shortages and wage hikes in several states could keep volumes below demand; management expects normalisation by end-June 2026.
New project losses (Sundaram-Clayton, EV, Romania) in FY27 could slow the margin improvement.
Working capital intensity: receivable days at 44 (consolidated) and inventory days at 54-55 for overseas operations; overseas debt in INR rose partly due to reclassification.
Price re-trigger not yet secured; the FY27 growth guidance excludes it.
Overseas business strategy unresolved; management will revisit after the year.
541163|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand and FY27 growth, while flagging near-term cost, manpower and pass-through lag headwinds. Management was conservative on guidance and deferred on overseas strategy and some numbers, and several answers were reconciled on the call.
key_quotes: So, even on a conservative level, I am happy to give a guidance of over a 15% growth in the overall revenue.
Sandhar has crossed the revenue mark of over INR 4,800 crores, which is an all-time high.

So, while EBITDA levels will remain constant around 11%, but with the volumes coming up and the revenue going up, automatically in terms of absolute returns, our multiplier will be giving us a more return on capital employed.
We are not looking at joint ventures at this time. We are considering transfer of technology or collaborations, which will be on the royalty basis.

541167|2026-03.headline: Yasho Q4 FY26 revenue rose 33% YoY to INR246.7 crore with EBITDA margin at 18.1%; FY27 utilisation target is 75%+.
541167|2026-03.overview: Consolidated FY26 revenue reached INR830 crore (up 22.7% YoY) with EBITDA of INR144 crore and margin of 17.4%, while Q4 revenue was INR246.72 crore (up 33%) with EBITDA of INR44.71 crore at 18.1%. Growth was entirely volume-led (FY26 volume up 33%), with management saying prices were under pressure until late March when 10-15% price increases started, mostly effective from April. Management guided to FY27 utilisation above 75% (from about 60% in FY26), volume growth of 35-45%, and a FY28 revenue target of INR1,500 crore tied to a 15-year long-term contract with INR51.4 crore advance. Leverage fell to 3.75x debt-to-EBITDA from 4.70x, and INR23.3 crore of FY27 liabilities were prepaid.

segments.name: Industrial Chemicals
segments.commentary: Contributed 87% of revenue in both Q4 and full FY26 and is the key growth driver; management says all volume growth came from the industrial segment, with a slight dip on the consumer side.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Accounted for 62% of FY26 revenue; Americas demand improved in Q4 as tariffs moderated, and Europe is seeing some slowdown. Management is also starting to enter Asia.

guidance_outlook: FY27 utilisation target above 75% (from above 60% in FY26); management also cited 70-75% and about 15 percentage points of utilisation uplift.
FY27 volume growth of 35-45% (clarified after several restatements); EBITDA margin expected at least 2-3 percentage points above FY26, with a stated aim of about 20%.

FY28 revenue target of INR1,500 crore, supported by asset utilisation of 85-90%, the MNC long-term contract going into commercial operation from early FY28, and FY27 capacity additions; management says margins will be maintained.
FY27 capex of INR125 crore, fully funded by internal accruals and entirely at Pakhajan; management says none of it relates to the long-term contract.
Gross margin guided at 40-42%.
Working capital to fall to about 170-175 days over 6-12 months from about 190 days.
Debt-to-EBITDA comfort zone of about 2.5x; absolute debt may rise while the ratio falls.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex INR75 crore: about INR25 crore R&D, INR40-42 crore Pakhajan, INR7-8 crore Vapi.
R&D facility completed October 2025 and fully operational.

Pakhajan has 2 production buildings built, with room for 4 more to be started one by one as demand ramps; a special project of about INR90 crore is running, and a further INR100 crore Pakhajan capex is under consideration.
Utilisation was above 60% in FY26 (60-62% through March); management declined to give plant-wise utilisation.
Management was unsure of the current total capacity figure, which was stated as 12,000 to 32,000 (unit not specified).
demand_pricing: Price increases of about 10-15% versus the pre-war base; these took effect only in the last 10 days of March and from April, as contracts were fixed quarterly or half-yearly until then.
About 40% of revenue comes from regular customers on quarterly or six-monthly pricing; about 60% is spot or relationship-based.
Pricing pressure and margin pressure through FY26, with product mix shifted away from low-margin products.
Import delays of 8-12 weeks versus 3-4 weeks normally; US export transit has risen to 60-70 days from 25 days.
Sulfur availability is challenging but available; solvents and sulfur-based chemistries show strong price volatility.
Chinese competitors described as very strong and aggressive in lubricant additives and industrial chemicals.
India-EU FTA expected around early January; Yasho has a European team about one year old.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR1,500 crore FY28 target visible and what drives it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited utilisation rising to 85-90% by FY28, the special project coming on stream in FY28, and new rubber and lube molecules; the visibility is partly customer commitments made on the table.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company moving into CDMO?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Yasho is not a CDMO and will not serve small-volume API-type orders of 20-100 metric tons. It will work with large-volume customers, with Pakhajan designed for 500-1,000 metric tons minimum per molecule.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Days have fallen from 215-216 in FY25 to about 190; the target is 170-175 over 6-12 months. Debtors are flat, and stock was useful in the supply crisis.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the FY27 volume growth is from price versus volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Management measures growth in volume terms, and says price increases only started in late March and April 2026. Currency gains are largely offset by imported raw materials.

qa_highlights.question: Does Yasho make its own formulations?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Yasho only makes pure chemicals and does not compete with its formulating customers.

qa_highlights.question: Is the MNC project capex included in the FY27 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: No. The INR125 crore FY27 capex is separate; the share of capex attributable to the MNC project is zero.

risks_watch: Supply chain disruption from the Middle East: import delays, raw material shortages, and high petrochemical prices; management says high inventory has offset this so far.
Chinese competition in lubricant additives and industrial chemicals.
Europe slowdown and the timing of the India-EU FTA (expected around early January).
Working capital reduction to 170-175 days depends on raw material availability.
Ramp to 75% utilisation and the FY28 INR1,500 crore target depend on the MNC contract and new molecules; each new molecule targeted at INR50 crore or more.
Ability to hold EBITDA margin as the customer price increases pass through, given management says costs cannot be fully passed on.
541167|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on volume and utilisation targets and on the FY28 ambition, but cautious and evasive on pricing outlook, raw material supply and the timing of new molecules. Management repeatedly declined to give plant-level data, product breakdowns or forward price views, and said it did not know when prices would normalise.
key_quotes: Consolidated revenue reached INR830 crores, up 22.7% year-on-year, while EBITDA stood at INR144 crores with margin improving to 17.4%, supported by product mix, operating leverage and cost optimization.
The company always measures growth in terms of volume.
We are purely chemical producers. We are in B2B. We are not in B2C segment.
Yasho is not governed for the CDMO kind of work.

541167|2026-06.headline: Yasho Q1 FY27 revenue hit record Rs 308 crore (volume +42% YoY) with EBITDA margin up to 24.2%; management guides to sustain margins.
541167|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue reached a record Rs 308 crore, driven by 42% YoY volume growth from customer approvals and additional offtake in industrial chemicals. EBITDA rose to Rs 74.42 crore (24.2% margin, vs 17% previously cited), with PAT of Rs 36 crore (11.7% margin). Net debt/EBITDA fell to 1.86x from 3.75x at Q4 FY26, bank loan ratings were upgraded to A- by CRISIL and ICRA, and working capital cycle shortened from 190 to 143 days. Management raised FY27 capex from Rs 125 crore to Rs 250 crore for two new buildings at Pakhajan and set a FY28 revenue target above Rs 1,600 crore.

financial_highlights.change: Highest quarterly revenue; 60% YoY growth per analyst question (not disputed)
From 3.75x at end of Q4 FY26

segments.name: Industrial chemicals
segments.commentary: Contributed nearly 89% of Q1 revenue; management expects this to rise to about 90% going forward. Management said new-product revenue is about 30% of sales over the last two years, with revenue rising from Rs 600 crore to Rs 850 crore.

segments.name: Exports / geographies
segments.commentary: Export is about 69% of revenue; US sales recovered after tariff issues eased, and Europe and Middle East are growing. Asia and Africa are early-stage, with margins described as at par or slightly lower than US/Europe.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins be sustained, given the Q1 benefit from the April price revision and operating leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the gains to product mix and higher utilisation rather than stock gains, citing commitments from marquee customers to maintain margins.

qa_highlights.question: What changed to move EBITDA margin from the historical 17-20% range to about 24%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited higher utilisation (about 50% to 65%), higher customer offtake, product mix, and R&D-led process optimisation.

qa_highlights.question: Phasing and revenue potential of the Pakhajan capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 1 about Rs 100 crore and Phase 2 about Rs 150 crore, at about 2.5x asset turn. Management said the Rs 1,600 crore FY28 guidance excludes these buildings.

qa_highlights.question: Supply chain or raw material risks given the current macro environment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is a genuine raw material supply issue, and export container bookings can take three to four weeks. Inventory fell, which drove working capital down.

qa_highlights.question: Margin differential between new and old products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said new products earn about 10-12% higher margin than older products. Newly launched products in the last 12 months carry better margins.

qa_highlights.question: Lube-additive and ICE exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not see EV adoption as a threat within a 10-year horizon, and that Rs 250 crore capex is not for lube alone.

guidance_outlook: Management expects to sustain the current EBITDA margin (about 24%) in FY27, though it said it cannot promise this beyond the next two to three years.
FY28 revenue target revised to more than Rs 1,600 crore; management said real growth from the new capacity comes from FY29.
Targets 30% to 40% annual revenue growth over the next few years.
FY27 capex raised to Rs 250 crore from Rs 125 crore; company expects about Rs 100 crore of borrowings in FY27.
Long-term agreement commercialisation expected in Q1 FY28, on track.
capex_capacity: Two new production buildings at Pakhajan facility for industrial chemicals, including new molecules and capacity for existing products. Phase 1 is about Rs 100 crore (operational Q1 FY28); Phase 2 is about Rs 150 crore (operational Q4 FY28). Management said the build takes at least 15 months.
Management expects about 2.5x asset turn on the Rs 250 crore capex.
Utilisation at the company level improved to over 65% (60-65% per another answer); management targets 70-75% and expects to add capacity once utilisation crosses 60-65%.
Management said about 60-65% of the new capacity is already covered by customer commitments.
Vapi plant shut; efforts moved to Pakhajan, which also has a pilot facility for R&D.
demand_pricing: Pricing is formula-based on raw material costs, reset quarterly or half-yearly, and management said long-term/contract business rose to more than 50% of revenue from 30-40% earlier.
Top customer is about 7% of revenue.
Management said the 42% volume growth reflects offtake, not pre-emptive buying; it expects volumes to grow sequentially.
Company is seeing more export traction than domestic; domestic sales are growing slowly.
Management cites a Rs 12-15 billion addressable market and an aspiration of $200-300 million revenue.
risks_watch: Raw material supply tightness and export container availability could affect output; management referenced a "war situation" in the macro backdrop.
Margin sustainability: management stated it wants to maintain margins for two to three years but cannot promise them.
Capex execution: Phase 1 and Phase 2 timelines depend on construction and commissioning within about 15 months.
Chinese capacity additions could pressure realisations; management did not give a direct answer.
Delivery times reportedly unchanged at 8-10 weeks higher than before (per analyst question).
key_quotes: The company achieved its highest quarterly revenue of Rs. 308 crores driven by a 42% increase in volume on a year-on-year basis.
Based on the current outlook, the company will endeavor to maintain current margins going forward.
We are not aiming immediately to go to $0.5 billion - $1 billion revenue. We are just talking about $200-$300 million revenue.
541167|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on near-term margins and growth, but evasive on specifics: declined to split Pakhajan-level utilisation, customer names, and Chinese competition, and repeatedly referred back to company-level metrics.

541195|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 turnover hit a record INR552.7 crore (+34.63% YoY) and PAT rose 38.49% to INR77.75 crore; FY26 turnover INR1,208.63 crore (+12.52%).
541195|2026-03.overview: Mishra Dhatu Nigam reported its highest-ever quarterly turnover of INR552.7 crore in Q4 FY26, with value of production up 19.15% to INR392.19 crore and PBT up 38.67% to INR107 crore. Management highlighted record titanium output of about 700 tonnes, an order book of about INR2,290 crore as of April 1, 2026, and new qualifications (NADCAP heat treatment, CEMILAC airworthiness for 10 alloys). Management guided to roughly 15% top-line growth in FY27 with a 20% ambition, and EBITDA margin of 23-25%, conditional on raw material and energy (LPG) supply stabilising.

segments.name: Investment casting
