segments.name: Fluoropolymers
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR848 crore, up 19% YoY and 14% QoQ, driven by value-added grades and higher volumes. Management expects FY27 growth of 15-20% and said newer grades (PFA, FKM) carry higher margins.

segments.name: Fluorochemicals (refrigerants, bulk chemicals)
segments.commentary: R-32 production and sales began in March 2026; over 10,000 tonnes capacity is operating, with a target of 20,000 tonnes. Caustic soda and fluoromethane pricing expected to stay range-bound in FY27.

segments.name: Battery materials (GFCL EV)
segments.commentary: LiPF6 salt capitalised 5 January 2026 and now commercially selling, with full qualification at most major electrolyte players. LFP cathode final qualification expected by Q3 FY27; binders qualified at major customers. Management says all commissioned capacity is contracted and expects a 3-digit crore quarterly revenue exit rate by Q4 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 total capex of INR3,150 crore: INR850 crore for GFL (INR150 crore refrigerants, INR222 crore electronic specialty chemicals, INR250 crore new fluoropolymers, INR230 crore backward integration and maintenance) and INR2,300 crore for GFCL EV.
Battery materials cumulative capex of INR6,000 crore by FY28 retained, targeting asset turns near 2x and EBITDA margins above 25%; full earnings potential expected by FY29.
Battery revenue expected to grow quarter-on-quarter with a significant rise; management expects a 3-digit crore quarterly run-rate by Q4 FY27.
Fluoropolymer volume and EBITDA growth expected to continue, with fluoropolymer demand growth of 15-20% in FY27.
Caustic soda and fluoromethane pricing expected range-bound in FY27.
Oman capex to proceed with no change in plan, per management.
capex_capacity: FY27 GFL capex INR850 crore: INR150 crore refrigerant gas capacity, INR222 crore high-purity electronic specialty chemicals for semiconductors, INR250 crore new fluoropolymer capacity, INR230 crore backward integration and maintenance.
R-32: over 10,000 tonnes achieved; target 20,000 tonnes, with ramp-up over time. No plan stated yet beyond 20,000 tonnes, though management said quota is available.

Battery materials: phase one capacity commissioned and contracted; LFP plant commissioned in early stage; natural graphite anode active material facility planned, which management said would take coverage to about 70% of LFP cell value.
Fluoropolymer capacities set up a few years ago are near optimum utilisation; new fluoropolymer capacity to be added.
Cumulative EV capex invested so far about INR1,900-2,000 crore; INR2,300 crore planned for FY27, with a similar amount likely in the following year to reach INR6,000 crore.
demand_pricing: Fluoropolymer prices rose; management said GFL also took a price increase and kept EBITDA margins despite higher raw material and logistics costs.
Fluoropolymer demand is driven by semiconductors, EVs, BESS, hydrogen, fuel cells, electrolysers and solar; management expects FY27 growth of 15-20%.
Refrigerant demand supported by residential AC, commercial refrigeration, cold chain and AI data-centre cooling; R-32 sold domestically and in exports, with some contracts in place.
Battery: anchor customers secured across products; management would not disclose whether contracts are take-or-pay.
Inventory: working capital cycle elevated because of Germany/US warehouse stock held as insurance for JIT customers and longer voyage times (7-8 weeks versus 3-4 weeks earlier).

qa_highlights.question: Will the fluoropolymer expansion be PTFE or new grades, and how is growth split?
qa_highlights.answer: Expansion is in new fluoropolymers; management gave no PTFE/new split, saying earlier capacities are almost at optimum utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the battery EBITDA loss so large in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said post-operational start, pre-operative and trial costs (about INR20 crore earlier, now about INR45 crore) flow through P&L, plus a one-time forex loss on buyer's credit now fully hedged.

qa_highlights.question: How much battery revenue can the invested capex generate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated about 2x asset turn after gestation of 9-12 months per plant; FY27 to see material salt volumes, LFP later after Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the R-32 expansion finished, and are there plans beyond 20,000 tonnes?
qa_highlights.answer: Over 10,000 tonnes operating from April; the 20,000 tonne target is still in progress. Further additions will depend on market and product mix, with quota numbers said to be clear internally.

qa_highlights.question: Is the EV capacity take-or-pay?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose contract terms, saying anchor customers, agreed specs and pricing are in writing.

qa_highlights.question: Will battery revenue reach a high three-digit crore quarterly run-rate by Q4 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said revenue will grow significantly QoQ and expects to reach a 3-digit crore figure by Q4 FY27.

risks_watch: Battery startup losses: costs now expensed with the plants capitalised; management expects them to ease but gave no timeline.
LFP cathode final qualification slated for Q3 FY27; revenue from LFP depends on it.
Working capital: inventory days rising; management attributes this to the high-stock model and longer transit times, with no target stated.
Middle East conflict: disruptions to logistics, input costs and currency, with forex swings noted as a cause of the battery loss.
R-32 ramp to 20,000 tonnes and whether it sells at expected volumes given weak Middle East demand in March.
542812|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on demand and the battery ramp, with a clear capex plan; cautious and sometimes evasive on contract terms, capacity utilisation numbers, the EBITDA of new grades and the reason for battery losses.
key_quotes: And now is the time for us to add capexes in new Fluoropolymers segment right now.
So, FY '27 will be a material quantity for salt, which I have already indicated very clearly.
It's a short-term thing because it's kind of a startup business.

542812|2026-06.headline: GFL Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 24% YoY to INR 1,588 crore and PAT more than doubled QoQ to INR 219 crore on R32-led fluorochemicals growth.
542812|2026-06.overview: Chemical segment revenue grew 23% YoY to INR 1,574 crore with EBITDA up 29% to INR 458 crore and segment PAT up 33% to INR 261 crore. Fluorochemicals was the standout, with revenue up 52% YoY and 44% QoQ on R32 sales, and existing R32 capacity is already at peak utilisation. Battery materials remain pre-revenue to small (INR 20-30 crore per quarter cited by an analyst), with a ramp promised from Q4 FY27 and a significant step-up in FY28. The Oman battery project has been put on hold and its capex is being moved to India, and the approved sovereign funding for Oman will not transfer.

segments.name: Fluoropolymers
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 15% YoY and 8% QoQ, driven by mix shift to higher-value grades and new-age applications (semiconductors, data centres, green hydrogen, batteries). Management guides 15-20% (later 17-20%) annual growth.

segments.name: Fluorochemicals (R32 and refrigerants)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 52% YoY and 44% QoQ, mainly R32. Existing R32 capacity is fully utilised; a R32 expansion (about 20,000 t total capacity cited by an analyst) is due in Q2 FY27. R134A is on track for commissioning in FY27.

segments.name: Bulk chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 11% YoY and 1% QoQ, primarily on better realisations; described as steady.

segments.name: Battery materials
segments.commentary: LiPF6 has nearly completed qualification and is in its growth phase; PVDF qualification is close; LFP and cathode active material revenue expected toward end-FY27. Current revenue is small, with dispatches on CIF terms recognised in the next quarter.

guidance_outlook: R32 capacity expansion to be commissioned in Q2 FY27; management expects full utilisation of the incremental R32 capacity in calendar 2027.
R134A capacity to be commissioned in FY27 (management said it is targeting earlier than year-end); capacity size not yet disclosed.
Battery materials: management says it is on track for a 3-digit INR crore quarterly revenue in Q4 FY27, with significant ramp-up in FY28 and full potential from FY28 onwards.
Gross block of INR 836 crore expected to rise to about INR 1,200 crore by end-FY27 as CWIP is capitalised.
FY27 capex plan held at about INR 2,300 crore in EV/battery and about INR 800 crore in chemicals; total announced plan of INR 6,000 crore over the next two years.
AHF (anhydrous hydrofluoric acid) capacity to come in phases, first set by end-FY27 or Q3, mainly for captive use.
capex_capacity: R32 capacity expansion due Q2 FY27; existing R32 capacity at peak utilisation.
R134A brownfield project at an existing refrigerant site, to be commissioned in FY27; TCE feedstock to be imported, not backward integrated.

Oman battery materials project (about USD 216 million capex) put on hold; capex being redirected to India. Sovereign funding of about INR 1,200 crore approved for Oman will not be available for India.
Land for battery expansion available at the existing Dahej B (Jolva) site; a second Dahej site is being added for FY27-end/FY28.
Fluoropolymer debottlenecking is done continuously, roughly every second quarter; new-age fluoropolymer capex sized in the previous quarter at about INR 250 crore.
demand_pricing: Fluoropolymer price increases were marginal and pass-through of input cost increases (methanol, sulfur, oil-linked inputs since March 2026); management said formula-based contracts protect margins.
R32 is sold globally: about 40-50% under long-term contracts, remainder spot or contract-to-contract. Domestic and export pricing described as 'very close'.
Management said 3M's exit is past and it has taken the impact; AGC's announced UK facility shutdown has begun generating customer enquiries, with traction expected in a quarter or two.
Domestic BESS demand projected at 220-250 GWh by 2030 (versus earlier global ~1,800 GWh view).

qa_highlights.question: Have Chinese peers' fluoropolymer price increases been passed on by GFL, and by how much?
qa_highlights.answer: Kapil Malhotra said only a marginal increase was taken to recover input costs; growth is mainly from higher-value grades where competition with Chinese players is limited.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20% growth visible for this year and next?
qa_highlights.answer: Bir Kapoor said it is absolutely visible; new fluoropolymer capacity is nearly fully utilised and further capacity will be added for semiconductor and battery applications, without disclosing specifics.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Oman funding shortfall require a fundraise?
qa_highlights.answer: Bir Kapoor said fundraising is ongoing and project-by-project; he does not see funding as a constraint for India capacity.

qa_highlights.question: How is fluoropolymer growth split between volume, price and mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to split it precisely, saying growth is primarily mix (higher grades) plus volume from new fluoropolymers, not price.

qa_highlights.question: Will R32 capacity be fully utilised in calendar 2027?
qa_highlights.answer: Bir Kapoor said full utilisation is expected as capacity is commissioned, based on contracts and market understanding.

risks_watch: Oman project shift to India: loss of about INR 1,200 crore sovereign funding for that project and need for new funding of about INR 4,000 crore for battery chemicals.

R32 and R134A quota allocation under the formula (baseline and production over 2024-26) is not yet clear; management declined to say which new players will receive quota. An analyst also raised a question on consumption quota that management could not answer and will follow up on.
Battery materials revenue remains small; ramp is contingent on customer qualification (about 1.5 years stabilisation cited) and CIF-term revenue timing.
Standalone-to-consolidated revenue gap widening sequentially, which management attributed to CIF consignments booked in Germany and US subsidiaries.
Raw material cost volatility (sulfur, fluorspar, methanol) with only formula-based or marginal pass-through in fluoropolymers.

Advanced Battery Materials segment after a very rigorous qualification and approval process will now start to contribute to our financials and growth.
542812|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on fluoropolymers, R32 demand and the 3M/AGC opportunity, and on the battery ramp (reiterating Q4 FY27 3-digit INR crore revenue). Evasive or non-committal on R134A capacity size, R32 quota allocation to new players, product-specific battery and anode capex, and the consumption-quota question, which was deferred for follow-up. Pricing answers were hedged: management called fluoropolymer price moves "marginal" and framed growth as mix and volume rather than price.

542830|2026-03.headline: IRCTC FY26 revenue from operations rose 11.55% to Rs 5,215 crore, but Q4 EBITDA margin fell to 27.33% on exceptional items.
542830|2026-03.overview: FY26 delivered record revenue from operations (Rs 5,215 crore, up 11.55%), total revenue (Rs 5,475 crore, up 11.64%), PBT (Rs 1,875 crore, up 6.72%) and EBITDA (Rs 1,666 crore, up 7.48%). Q4 revenue from operations rose 15.05% YoY to Rs 1,460 crore, but Q4 profit fell to Rs 447 crore from Rs 472 crore, weighed by exceptional items (CSR, ECL provisioning) and a prior-year Rs 48 crore legacy income item not repeating. Management attributed the Q4 margin dip to exceptional items, saying margin would be about 30% excluding them. Catering and tourism grew fast while the internet ticketing segment grew slower. The call was led by the Director (Tourism and Marketing) because the Director (Finance) was unavailable.

segments.name: Catering
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue Rs 2,399 crore (+12.89%). Q4 revenue Rs 671 crore (+26.84%), with margin hit by train catering mix, branded catering pilots, ECL and CSR charges; Q4 EBIT margin 6.3% vs 10.4%.

segments.name: Internet ticketing (IRCTC rail ticketing)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue Rs 1,536 crore (+7.71%), profit +7.55%. Q4 revenue Rs 390 crore (+4.56%) with EBITDA margin 76%; Q4 EBIT margin 76% vs 85% due to CSR (additional Rs 17 crore), direct costs (~Rs 8 crore) and UPI share (~Rs 8 crore). Claims 89% share of reserved rail tickets.

segments.name: Tourism
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue Rs 890 crore (+19.46%), profit +36.17%. Q4 revenue Rs 304 crore (+10.95%), EBITDA margin 16%; management said margin would be about 18% without CSR (Rs 1.5 crore) and lower margin on two Tejas Express trains.

segments.name: Rail Neer
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue Rs 391 crore (+3.17%), profit +21.74%. Q4 revenue Rs 95 crore (+3.26%) with margin improvement attributed to favourable preform (PET) rates and material cost economies.

guidance_outlook: Long-term EBITDA margin aspiration of about 30%; management declined to commit to mid-30s, saying it aims to maintain 30%.
Forward growth targets by segment: catering around 15%, tourism around 20%, internet ticketing around 7% (convenience fee income targeted at about 10% via unified portal and iPay).
Payment aggregator licence final application deadline is August 2026; management said it expects to meet it and has engaged a tech partner.
Tourism Q1 trend: management said it is 'very hopeful' on domestic tourism, without quantifying.
capex_capacity: Rail Neer: Ambernath expansion tendered from 2 lakh to 3 lakh bottles per day; Danapur from 1 lakh to 2 lakh bottles per day; partner tied up and work ongoing.
Four greenfield Rail Neer plants: land secured at Mysore and Prayagraj; Bhagalpur land deemed unsuitable and re-requested; Ranchi (Barpali) allotment indicated but no formal communication received.
Capital allocation priorities: e-ticketing infrastructure and security, four new Rail Neer plants, expansion of two existing plants, and entry into hotel business.
Asset-light model; cash balance described as strong.
demand_pricing: Q4 tickets booked: 13.39 crore total (AC 6.85 crore, non-AC 6.54 crore); UPI share 51.7%; convenience fee income Rs 247 crore.
Channel partners account for about 28% of ticket bookings; management said the share appears unchanged YoY.
Catering prices are administered by the Ministry of Railways; management declined to comment on a price revision despite gas cost pressure; last hike cited as 2019.
Commercial LPG cylinder shortage in Q4: mitigations included allowing vendors to cook in pantry cars (electric induction), and priority supply tie-ups with IOCL, BPCL and HPCL.
Election special trains contributed Rs 2.38 crore revenue in Q4 and Rs 6.77 crore in FY26.
Dividend payout around 50%; buyback decision rests with DIPAM (Ministry of Finance), and the board has apprised DIPAM.

qa_highlights.question: What exceptional items hit Q4 and by how much?
qa_highlights.answer: Prior-year Rs 48 crore legacy income not repeated; CSR booked Rs 31 crore vs Rs 7 crore last year (incremental ~Rs 24 crore); ECL provision Rs 16 crore vs Rs 8 crore last year. Other expenses were about Rs 109 crore vs a typical Rs 40-50 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did catering and internet ticketing EBIT margins fall sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited exceptional items: catering ECL Rs 16 crore (vs Rs 5 crore), CSR Rs 5 crore (vs Rs 1 crore), legacy item absent (Rs 33 crore last year), and about Rs 3 crore GST impact. For ticketing: CSR +Rs 17 crore, direct costs ~Rs 8 crore, UPI share ~Rs 8 crore. Analyst confirmed CSR and ECL sit in EBIT.

qa_highlights.question: Why was CSR booked in Q4 and will it recur?
qa_highlights.answer: CSR is 2% of the last three years' profit; projects were sanctioned in Q4. Management called it exceptional and said spreading it monthly would yield about Rs 32-36 crore a year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Vande Bharat catering model's lower margin change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the licensee fee and turnover both earn margin; the 5% GST on billed turnover, with no ITC credit, is borne by IRCTC on revenue increases.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a pending litigation over licence fee for prepaid and postpaid trains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the matter (CC-60 case) is under litigation and declined to quantify or give a timeline.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Rail Neer capacity and partner status?
qa_highlights.answer: Ambernath and Danapur expansions tendered; partner tie-ups in progress; channel partner talks for the 40% supply gap are ongoing but 'not very encouraging' so far.

qa_highlights.question: Did the August Kranti Rajdhani stop at Agra get considered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the route is Mathura-Mumbai via Kota and that a request to Indian Railways would be needed; no commitment was made.

risks_watch: Q4 margin compression: exceptional items (CSR, ECL) recurrence, and whether FY27 margins return to about 30%.
Internet ticketing growth slowed to 4.56% in Q4 and about 7.7% in FY26, despite 76% EBITDA margin; convenience fee unchanged for years and under review.
Catering: no fare revision yet; input cost (gas, LPG) pressure on licensees; 5% GST on Vande Bharat billing not recoverable.
Payment aggregator licence by August 2026 and unified portal launch timeline.
Litigation over prepaid/postpaid train licence fee enhancement; unrecognised revenue not quantified.
Rail Neer greenfield plant execution (Bhagalpur land, Ranchi allotment unconfirmed) and partner search.

542830|2026-06.headline: IRCTC Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18.1% to INR1,370 crore, but EBITDA fell 2.77% to INR386 crore as catering margins and internet ticketing spinoffs weakened.
542830|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations rose 18.1% YoY to INR1,370 crore, led by catering (INR732 crore, +33.8%) and tourism (INR168 crore, +13.5%). EBITDA was INR386 crore (28.17% margin), down 2.77% YoY, and PAT was about INR330 crore. Margins were pressured by a one-time HR/gratuity charge of about INR20 crore, proof-of-concept costs on six trains, a West Asia-driven resin cost spike in Rail Neer, and lower non-convenience fee income in internet ticketing. Management said the catering and HR effects are non-recurring and that the proof-of-concept trains will wind down by November.

segments.name: Internet Ticketing
segments.commentary: Revenue INR361 crore (+0.5%); EBIT margin fell to 80.33% from 84.12%, attributed to NGET infra refresh, about INR10 crore maintenance booking, and lower marketing/ad and agent income. About 89% of reserved tickets are booked online.

segments.name: Catering
segments.commentary: Revenue INR732 crore (+33.8%); segment margin 9.29% vs 10.42% in FY26. Management attributed the drop to about INR4 crore proof-of-concept cost on six trains and about INR10 crore HR/gratuity charge; catering onboard sales from prepaid trains rose to INR413 crore from INR301 crore.

segments.name: Rail Neer
segments.commentary: Revenue INR109 crore (+2.83%); margin about 10% vs 14-15% prior, driven by resin/petroleum cost rise (material cost INR55 crore to INR61 crore) linked to West Asia crisis. Management said profit fell only about INR4 crore overall.

segments.name: Tourism
segments.commentary: Revenue INR168 crore (+13.5%); EBITDA margin improved to 11.31% from 8.78% on better product mix and cost realisation, despite geopolitical disruption. Non-fare revenue from Tejas naming/wrap rights noted as a new lever.

guidance_outlook: Management expects catering margins to return to the traditional 10-12% range; proof-of-concept trains to finish by September (2 trains) and November (2 trains).
The one-time HR cost of about INR20 crore (catering INR10 crore) is not expected to recur in Q2.

Rail Neer augmentation: Ambernath from 2 lakh to 3 lakh bottles/day and Danapur from 1 lakh to 2 lakh bottles/day, targeted for FY27; four new plants (Prayagraj, Mysore, Ranchi, Bhagalpur) may spill into FY28.
About 20 Vande Bharat sleeper trains expected over the next year, with licence fee of about INR6 crore per train (up to INR120 crore).
Management aims to bring non-convenience fee back toward INR150 crore over time via iPay, e-wallet loyalty and agent business changes; no quarterly run-rate given.
Active-active disaster recovery planned at Secunderabad, with further investment expected in Q2-Q4.
capex_capacity: Rail Neer installed capacity about 17.77 lakh bottles/day after closure of one plant (from 18.4 lakh); supply about 15.5 lakh bottles/day against higher demand at some stations.
NGET infra refresh: about INR150 crore infused into PRS modernisation; ticketing throughput about 37,000 tickets per minute, targeted to exceed 1 lakh.
E-catering grew to about 1.69 lakh meals/day in FY27 from 1.05 lakh a year earlier; e-pantry live on 50+ trains, targeting about 100.
Catering services in 81 Vande Bharat trains run by IRCTC; other Vande Bharat catering is outsourced to empanelled licensees via limited tenders.
Payment aggregator (IRCTC Payments Ltd): final RBI application submitted by 4 August 2026 with SAR and MVP; RBI response expected within this financial year; TSP already engaged.
demand_pricing: Average daily tickets 14.58 lakh; Q1 total 13.27 crore (AC 6.92 crore, non-AC 6.35 crore). IRCTC share of railway ticketing rose to 88.92% from 88.78%.
UPI share of tickets 51.22% vs 48.72% a year earlier.

Catering revenue bridge: onboard sales INR413 crore (INR301 crore), licence fee from prepaid and other trains INR224 crore (INR192 crore), static units INR33 crore (INR20 crore), e-catering INR22 crore (INR9 crore), election specials INR41 crore (INR5 crore).
Opt-out for catering on prepaid trains estimated at roughly 25-30% (management said unconfirmed); complaint ratio about 0.0008% of 18 lakh daily meals.
Tourism OTA-linked income about INR21 crore of INR168 crore (12-13%); internet ticketing about 18% of total revenue excluding convenience fee, 26% including it.
Rail Neer priced at INR14 per bottle; third-party brands visible on non-AC trains and kiosks. Management attributed this to unauthorised vendors filling gaps at non-mandatory stations.

financial_highlights.change: +0.5% YoY; EBITDA margin above 80%, EBIT margin 80.33% vs 84.12%
+33.82% YoY; segment margin 9.29% vs 10.42% in FY26

qa_highlights.question: Reason for the resignation of Sanjay Jain and assurance on no material discrepancies?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it a completely personal decision, praised his leadership, and said he will continue supporting from outside. No discrepancies were addressed beyond that assurance.

qa_highlights.question: Why third-party bottled water brands are visible on non-AC trains and kiosks, and Rail Neer's incremental revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Rail Neer is priced at INR14 per bottle; installed capacity is about 17.77 lakh bottles/day after one plant closed (from 18.4 lakh) against supply of about 15.5 lakh. Gaps at mandatory stations are exploited by unauthorised vendors. Augmentation: Ambernath 2 to 3 lakh and Danapur 1 to 2 lakh bottles/day; four new plants at Prayagraj, Mysore, Ranchi and Bhagalpur, with timelines possibly spilling into FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Catering attachment rates, opt-in/opt-out mix and passenger-experience steps?
qa_highlights.answer: Opt-out for prepaid-train catering is roughly 15-30% (later said 25-30%, unconfirmed). Complaint ratio about 0.0008% of 18 lakh daily meals. E-catering grew to about 1.69 lakh meals/day from 1.05 lakh; e-pantry is live on 50+ trains, targeting about 100. Branded players are at policy-formulation stage.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the Tejas rebranding and tourism margin improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: IRCTC runs two private Tejas trains; non-fare revenue from naming and wrap rights is a policy-backed lever, with the Tejas naming done for the first time. It was described as a previously dormant revenue stream now being promoted through regional and zonal offices.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the catering revenue increase in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Catering revenue rose from INR547 crore to INR732 crore, a delta of about INR185 crore. Onboard sales from prepaid trains rose to INR413 crore from INR301 crore, licence fees from prepaid and other trains to INR224 crore from INR192 crore, static units to INR33 crore from INR20 crore, e-catering to INR22 crore from INR9 crore, and election specials to INR41 crore from INR5 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the payment aggregator licence (IRCTC Payments) and monetisation plans?
qa_highlights.answer: The final RBI application was submitted by the 4 August 2026 deadline, together with the SAR and MVP; RBI response is expected within this financial year, and a TSP is engaged. Current iPay volume is about 2.7 lakh transactions, and expansion would follow once the licence is granted.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of convenience and non-convenience fee, and why the internet ticketing EBIT margin fell?
qa_highlights.answer: Convenience fee rose to INR248 crore from about INR236 crore; non-convenience fee fell to INR113 crore from INR123 crore. Marketing and ad income dipped about INR3 crore (INR14.51 crore to INR11.03 crore), and agent business was restricted. About INR10 crore of maintenance was booked, and NGET infra refresh and active-active DR at Secunderabad are being invested in. EBIT margin was 80.33% vs 84.12%, and management said it normally sits at 80-85%.

qa_highlights.question: What caused the catering margin decline to 9.29% and the one-time HR cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Proof-of-concept on six trains cost more than INR4 crore. Total HR/gratuity one-time charge was about INR20 crore, of which INR10 crore was booked in catering, covering gratuity (INR20 lakh to INR25 lakh) and post-retirement benefits. Management said this will not recur next quarter, and the proof-of-concept trains will wind down by September (two trains) and November (two trains).

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Rail Neer margin decline and how big was the profit impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin fell from about 14-15% to about 10%, mainly due to resin and petroleum cost increases linked to the West Asia crisis; material cost rose from INR55 crore to INR61 crore. Management said overall profit fell by only about INR4 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What share of tourism and internet ticketing revenue comes from OTA partners and other channels?
qa_highlights.answer: Tourism OTA-linked income was about INR21 crore of INR168 crore (12-13%), or 5-7% from online hotels and ticketing alone. Internet ticketing revenue excluding convenience fee is about 18% of total revenue, and about 26% including it.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected run rate for non-convenience fee and the UPI share of tickets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a quarterly run-rate and said the figure will not revert to INR110-115 crore. qa_highlights.question: Vande Bharat catering model and steady-state margin given the GST treatment on prepaid trains?

qa_highlights.question: Why were write-offs high while credit cost was low?
qa_highlights.answer: Management wrote off a fully provided vintage of credit card and unsecured loans with low recovery prospects and no PSL benefit; it said this had no impact on credit cost, which was 24 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the IRDAI corporate agency consultation paper on fees?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimates a 0.5% to 1% drag on fee-to-income, so guidance may drop from 18% to 17% short term, with the bank aiming to recover through core fee lines.

qa_highlights.question: What is the balance sheet growth outlook and retail deposit traction?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated growth 30% to 50% faster than system; retail current account acquisition has started, and liability franchise takes two to three years to build. Asset growth is not the constraint.

qa_highlights.question: Is Fairfax or IDBI relevant to CSB, and is there a Fairfax deposit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Fairfax has no deposits with the bank and the board has not discussed the Fairfax/IDBI matter; the transaction is still incomplete.

qa_highlights.question: What are the ROA and NIM outlooks for this year and next?
qa_highlights.answer: ROA of 1.30-1.5% this year, 1.5-1.8% next year; NIM around 3.75-3.8%, with cost of funds targeted at about 6% next year to offset mix shift.

risks_watch: Gold loan tonnage down about 6% YoY and gold disbursements slowing; gold book mix must fall to about 50%.
Regulatory fee risk from IRDAI corporate agency draft; fee-to-income could fall 0.5-1%.
Asset quality trend needs two to three more quarters to confirm; management points to a declining non-gold SMA book.
Cost of funds at 6.55% and reliance on FCY borrowings, CDs and bulk deposits; CASA ratio slipped to 18.96%.
Opex growth (other opex +18% QoQ) and cost-to-income at 64.8% against the fee and NIM outlook.
Interpretation risk on write-offs: elevated write-offs of fully provided book alongside PCR rising to 87.65%.
542867|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on earnings momentum, ROA and the scale phase, but guarded on the timing of retail growth, CASA recovery and the fee impact from the IRDAI draft. Management declined to elaborate on the other income breakup and deflected the Fairfax/IDBI question as not yet relevant.
key_quotes: Overall, we had a fairly good quarter.

We will start seeing the growth on the SME side from this quarter onwards because most of the portfolio-related issues we faced in SME book for the last one-and-a-half years have been by and large corrected now.
I would say that we would aim to bring down the cost of funds to somewhere around 6% next financial year, which will give us a 50-basis points lift.

542904|2026-06.headline: Ujjivan SFB Q1 FY27 PAT rose to INR317 crore (ROA 2.2%, ROE 18.2%); FY27 ROA guidance raised to 1.8-2.0%.
542904|2026-06.overview: Gross loans reached INR42,903 crore (+28.9% YoY, +5.5% QoQ) and deposits INR48,129 crore (+25% YoY), with CASA up 37.8% YoY to INR12,930 crore. Net interest income was INR1,186 crore with NIM stable at 8.5%, and GNPA fell 10 bps to 2.17% with PCR at 85%. Management revised FY27 credit cost guidance to 0.9-1.0% of average total assets and raised ROA guidance to 1.8-2.0%, helped by deferred capacity-building spend (about INR250 crore planned for FY27, mostly from June onward) and lower opex (now about 6.4% of average assets).

segments.name: Micro banking (MFI)
segments.commentary: Book INR21,371 crore (+16.8% YoY), disbursements INR4,581 crore (+16.4% YoY). Bucket X collection efficiency 99.68%; slippages annualised about 1.72% vs 2.68% in Q4; provision coverage about 95%.

segments.name: Affordable housing and micro mortgages
segments.commentary: Combined gross book INR11,210 crore (+40.8% YoY). GNPA stable at 1.2% (affordable housing) and 0.6% (micro mortgages). Micro mortgage book about INR1,800 crore, yield about 19.5%, PAR rising from about 1.2% to 1.5%.

segments.name: Secured book
segments.commentary: Secured book INR21,638 crore (+42.7% YoY, +7.8% QoQ), now 50.4% of loans.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: Book INR3,470 crore (+54% YoY); new book GNPA 0.5%; MSME PAR down 13 bps. Ticket sizes rising, with LAP at INR80-90 lakh and working capital at INR1.1-1.2 crore; disbursement yield expected around 10.5%.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Book INR1,020 crore (+248.6% YoY); Q1 disbursements INR467 crore (+183.9% YoY). Sourced from 455 branches (106 added in the quarter); origination LTV 75%, book LTV about 56%.

segments.name: Vehicle loans
segments.commentary: Book INR1,036 crore (+85.1% YoY), GNPA 1.7%, served through 337 branches with a mid-premium and EV focus. New lines (gold, vehicle, agri) are 7% of the loan book and 9% of Q1 disbursements.

guidance_outlook: FY27 ROA guidance raised to 1.8-2.0% (from the earlier guidance), citing opex and credit cost.
FY27 credit cost guidance revised to 0.9-1.0% of average total assets (earlier basis: average gross loan book); credit cost was 0.9% in Q1.
FY27 opex expected at about 6.4% of average assets, lower than earlier plan, as capacity spend (about INR250 crore) is deferred to later quarters.
FY27 planned asset growth of 25% reaffirmed.
Target of 56% secured loan mix by March 2027 maintained.
Bulk deposit ratio to stay around 30%; no immediate further deposit rate hikes seen, with marginal cost-of-funds increase expected.
Opex to decline year-on-year in FY28 as investment intensity eases.

qa_highlights.question: Can yields be sustained in affordable housing and non-MFI segments, and is 2% ROA possible on a steady-state basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Affordable housing yield around 12.5% with ticket INR16-20 lakh and about 580-590 branches; some competitive pressure but yields maintained. Micro mortgage yields about 19.5%, and yields do not fall much at INR10-12 lakh tickets.

qa_highlights.question: Will cost of funds rise further, and is any more deposit rate hike needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Brajesh Cherian said no immediate upward revision is needed, only a marginal increase in cost of funds is expected, and this is built into the 1.8-2.0% ROA guidance. IBPC, refinance and securitisation are available.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity-building spend and does the guidance embed NIM compression?
qa_highlights.answer: Bala Kamath said about INR250 crore planned, with little spent in Q1 and spend starting in June; the 1.8-2.0% ROA guidance includes it. NIM guidance given at the start of the year is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the credit cost guidance cut and are there early warning signs in MFI?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashish Goel said MFI bucket X collection efficiency is 99.7% and July trends are similar; Q1 MFI slippages annualised about 1.72% vs 2.68% in Q4. Each 5-7 bps move in collections would only marginally change credit cost.

qa_highlights.question: What is the micro mortgage PAR and LGD outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: PAR rose from about 1.2% to about 1.5%; GNPA from about 0.47% to about 0.55%. Management says 18 and 24 MOB vintages have not exceeded about 2.5% and the book is still maturing; bucket X collection is 99.7-99.75%.

qa_highlights.question: How will opex trend after FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex is 6.4% of average assets in FY27; Sadananda Kamath said FY28 investment will be lower and opex will improve year-on-year, with exact figures to follow.

capex_capacity: Capacity-building spend planned at about INR250 crore for FY27; per management, little was spent in Q1 and spending started in June (marketing, IT, branch openings), building up over coming quarters.

Branch network at 814 as of June 2026 after 38 new branches in Q1; plan to add 144 branches in FY27 (106 yet to open). Gold loan active branches to rise from about 430-440 to about 575 by end-FY27; gold disbursement exit rate targeted at INR230-250 crore a month by March 2027 (June exit about INR170-175 crore a month).

Affordable housing capacity built at about INR350-375 crore disbursement a month; micro mortgage disbursement about INR100 crore a month, expected to reach INR140-150 crore by March 2027. Incremental book mix tilts toward micro mortgages.
Opex guided at about 6.4% of average assets for FY27; management expects FY28 opex to decline year-on-year as investment intensity eases.

New products: Unsecured Fast Track loan ready to scale after pilot; pre-owned car loans piloted in Karnataka, to test in 2-3 geographies this year; mid-corporate lending started in Q1; purchase invoice discounting added to MSME suite; co-branded credit card in testing. HCV/LCV only after FY27.
demand_pricing: Gross loans INR42,903 crore (+28.9% YoY, +5.5% QoQ); disbursements INR9,245 crore (+41.4% YoY). Secured book INR21,638 crore, 50.4% of loans.

Affordable housing and micro mortgages INR11,210 crore (+40.8% YoY). Micro mortgage book about INR1,800 crore at ~19.5% yield; affordable housing yield about 12.5%, ticket INR16-20 lakh.

risks_watch: Deposit competition and CASA mobilisation: management flagged tight liquidity and deposit pressure; cost of funds may tick up marginally despite no further repricing benefit.
Yield pressure as ticket sizes rise in MSME (disbursement yield about 10.5%, below book yield) and affordable housing faces competition.
Monsoon and kharif sowing: management flagged El Nino and kharif delays as a key H2 monitorable; credit cost guidance relies on stable MFI collections.
Micro mortgage PAR rising (about 1.2% to 1.5%); management expects a natural increase as the book matures, so this needs monitoring.
Execution risk on the INR250 crore capacity spend and the 144-branch plan, which must lift deposits to fund the 25% asset growth; FY27 ROA guidance of 1.8-2.0% relies on it.
key_quotes: Our strategy continues to remain centered on strengthening our liability franchise, building a diversified asset portfolio and maintaining prudent risk management practices to ensure profitability along with growth.
This deferred commencement of expenses, coupled with ongoing efficiency gains will result in full year opex to be lower than earlier planned and now would be around 6.4% of average assets.

We remain mindful of the prevailing funding rate environment and the continued competitive intensity in CASA mobilization, along with pricing pressures across key asset products and the resulting impact on margins.
542904|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on asset quality, credit cost and the raised ROA guidance, citing MFI collection efficiency of 99.7%. More cautious on liabilities, where management said deposit pressure is present and rate moves are being watched; it declined to give vertical-level profitability or product ROA.

542904|2026-09.headline: Ujjivan SFB posted record quarterly PAT of INR365 crores (ROA 2.4%, ROE 19.7%) in Q2 FY27, with deposits up 29.2% to INR50,643 crores.
542904|2026-09.overview: Ujjivan SFB reported strong Q2 FY27 growth: gross loans rose 32.1% YoY to INR45,699 crores and NII rose 35% YoY to INR1,244 crores, with NIM at 8.4%. Asset quality was stable, with GNPA at 2.1%, NNPA at 0.3%, and a credit cost of 0.7%. Management guided NIM down about 10 bps to around 8.35% in H2 after the 25 bps repo hike, and flagged that ROA could overshoot the guided range. qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the drought in Karnataka and Maharashtra on collections and credit cost?

qa_highlights.question: How much of the opex budget of about INR250 crores will be spent this year, and is extra provisioning planned?

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for CASA and deposit mobilization?

542905|2026-03.headline: Hindware FY26 consolidated EBITDA rose 27% to ₹233 crore on 9% margin, while Q4 revenue fell to ₹663 crore from ₹699 crore.

Bathware grew 10% in FY26 with margins up 160 bps, while pipes revenue declined and posted a PBT loss, with a March resin-price spike cutting inventory and sales. Home Innovation (consumer appliances) is being rationalised, with management guiding to EBITDA-positive in Q1 FY27.

542907|2026-03.headline: Prince Pipes Q4 FY26 revenue rose 18% to INR850 crore and EBITDA doubled to INR110 crore on 23% volume growth; management guides 11-13% margin.
542907|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 delivered record quarterly volumes of 62,167 MT (+23% YoY), with revenue of INR850 crore (+18%) and EBITDA of INR110 crore (+100%, 13% margin). Management says 11.6% EBITDA margin should be the base level; steady-state EBITDA margin target of at least 15%, expected in about two years.
Pharma revenue potential of Rs 30-50 crore in the second half of FY27 (Q2/Q3 compliance target), per analyst question on the Rs 70-75 crore figure.
Finance cost guided at Rs 9-10 crore per quarter run-rate going forward (Q1 interest about Rs 11 crore).
EO supply expected by around December 2026; FY28 expected to be better with a full year of additional EO.
Saudi Arabia project: about 1.5 years to first production after announcement; mix of EO and non-EO products; still in survey and feedstock/land allocation stage.

New R&D centre commissioned in Q4 FY26 and ramping up.

Saudi Arabia: initial operational and pre-operational spends only; capex not finalised.
demand_pricing: Volume grew ~10% YoY; balance of growth from higher pricing.
Pass-through of raw material price increases is achieved, but frequent up/down moves create buyer uncertainty; freight and vessel availability cost margin.
Phenol loss of about Rs 5 crore in Q4 FY26 due to delayed China shipments (noted as Q1 context by management); one-off RM block purchase also hurt the quarter; prices now back to earlier levels.
Growth shifted to non-EO products (esters, NMMO, NMM, NFM); agro demand subdued but non-EO agro inputs grew.
Single EO supplier in India, priced on world EO price; limited negotiating power.
Freight rates rose again after brief easing; new orders taken at higher freight.

qa_highlights.question: What margin improvement path and timing for EBITDA margin, given flat margins over 4-5 quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Ketan Sablok said 11.6% is close to last quarter and slightly below last year; margins to improve as utilisation rises, low-margin exits and pharma/aroma mix shift. Wait-and-see for at least two quarters due to pricing and RM pressure.

qa_highlights.question: Is 11.6% the base margin and what is steady-state?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 11.6% should be the base level. Base business ex-B2C is 14-15%; target is around 15% steady-state EBITDA margin within two years after B2C recalibration and asset monetisation.

qa_highlights.question: Exit of B2C business: investment, debt and margin effect?
qa_highlights.answer: No separate investment as assets are shared (Silvassa). Debt in institutional/B2C about Rs 50 crore. Exit releases at least 2-3% EBITDA margin. Institutional cleaning retained; only consumer/B2C exits.

qa_highlights.question: Pricing vs volume growth and growth levers without EO availability?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume ~10% YoY, rest from pricing. Growth from new non-EO products (esters, NMMO, NMM, NFM), trace minerals, vitamin and enzyme premixes; pharma to rise to Rs 70-75 crore this year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did domestic-focused peers gain while Rossari did not?
qa_highlights.answer: Single-molecule producers benefited; specialty players absorbed raw material hits. Phenol shipment delay from China cost about Rs 5 crore in the prior quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Saudi Arabia project timeline and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Survey and feedstock/land allocation still in progress; nothing finalised. About 1.5 years to first production after announcement; mix of EO and non-EO products.

qa_highlights.question: Interest cost rise and average cost of debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher interest because term loans for capex were capitalised earlier and are now expensed as assets commissioned; run-rate to be Rs 9-10 crore per quarter.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on B2C exits, asset monetisation and utilisation; management declined to guide quarterly numbers.
EO supply (single Indian supplier) expected only by about December 2026; EO-linked growth is delayed.
Raw material and freight volatility linked to West Asia/geopolitics; freight rates rose again after easing.
Thailand and Saudi Arabia ramp-up and pre-operative costs weigh on margins.
Pharma compliance timeline (Q2/Q3) gates the Rs 30-50 crore H2 revenue potential.
Interest costs rising as capitalised projects go into P&L; watch whether run-rate falls to Rs 9-10 crore.

543213|2026-09.headline: Rossari Q2 FY27 revenue rose 19% YoY to Rs 697.6 crore, a record, with EBITDA of Rs 87 crore (12.5% margin).
543213|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 set record revenue (Rs 697.6 crore, +19% YoY) and EBITDA (Rs 87 crore, +21% YoY), with growth led by volume and value-added products. Gross margin was 31.6%, up about 200 bps QoQ on product mix, but core B2B EBITDA margin fell to 14.1% from 14.8% YoY on freight and raw material costs. Management guided FY27 EBITDA margin to about 12% and revenue growth to mid-to-high teens, while citing uncertainty from the Middle East situation. Net debt fell to Rs 221 crore and working capital days improved to 86 from 97 at FY26 end.

segments.name: HPPC (Home, Personal Care & Industrial)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 541.9 crore, +18% YoY; H1 Rs 1,095.1 crore, +20% (H1 growth 24% per Sunil Chari). Growth led by personal care, agro surfactants, adjuvants and oil & gas; ethylene oxide constraints limited ethoxylate volumes and sequential revenue was broadly flat.

segments.name: Textile Specialty Chemicals
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 120.8 crore, +26% YoY and about +14% QoQ; H1 Rs 226.9 crore, +24%. Driven by exports to Bangladesh, Southeast Asia, Turkey and Latin America, plus the Thailand facility and the new fibre chemicals division.

segments.name: Animal Health & Nutrition (AHN)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 34.8 crore, +11% YoY; H1 Rs 72.8 crore, +19%. Q2 is seasonally the weakest quarter; management expects Q3 and Q4 to peak.

segments.name: Core B2B (ex institutional and B2C)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 619.9 crore, +21% YoY; EBITDA Rs 87.2 crore, +15% YoY, margin 14.1% vs 14.8% in Q2 FY26 and 13.5% in Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Institutional and B2C
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 77.7 crore, +3% YoY; EBITDA +Rs 0.2 crore vs loss of Rs 3.7 crore in Q2 FY26, after portfolio rationalisation. Management targets positive EBITDA in H2 and for full FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guided at about 12% plus/minus; management expects margin improvement only from FY28.
FY27 revenue growth guided at mid-teens to high-teens, down from the 12-14% initial view, given demand and logistics uncertainty.
Peak utilisation of the new ethoxylation facility at Dahej expected about 2 years after commissioning, around end-FY28; peak sales target remains 3x capex value.
Working capital days expected to stay in the 87-90 day range by end-March 2027.
Working capital debt expected to be repaid by about mid-2027; all cash flows to go to debt reduction for now.
Exports targeted at 30%+ of revenue by end of this year (Q2 export share 31%, H1 27%).
capex_capacity: Blended capacity utilisation about 60%; new ethoxylation facility (Dahej) at about 30% and ramping; full healthy utilisation expected by next year as Reliance EO capacity arrives.
Reliance ethylene oxide expansion expected in Q1 FY28; no confirmed incremental EO allocation yet, with confirmation hoped for in the next couple of months.
Capital work in progress was Rs 156 crore at 30 September; about Rs 50-75 crore more capex in H2 FY27, with most projects closing by end-2026 and no major capex in India in the following year.
Remaining projects cover pharma excipients, aroma chemicals, hydrogenation and biosurfactant expansion; no volume figures disclosed yet.

Saudi Arabia: Board approved leasing land to wholly owned subsidiary Rossari International Limited Company for a greenfield plant; early site work (fencing, boundary wall) in coming months. Project details, capex and timelines to come after Board approval, likely in 8-12 months.
Thailand blending facility ramping up for Southeast Asia customers; EXCiPACT registration obtained for the Unitop plant.
demand_pricing: Q2 growth was mostly volume-driven; some product prices were cut as raw material prices eased early in the quarter.
Freight costs roughly doubled to tripled versus last year; not all customers absorb the full freight increase. Phenol and other core raw materials are higher YoY.
Export revenue grew about 34% YoY and about 35% QoQ in Q2; export share 31% of revenue; H1 export share 27%.
Pharma exports were about Rs 50 crore last year; qualification takes 6 months to 2 years, and management expects strong growth this year.
Oil and gas focus markets are India, the Middle East, and Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan; US sales go through distributors with no segment data.
Management declined to give a specific H2 revenue outlook, citing the Middle East situation, shipping routes and container and ISO tank availability.

qa_highlights.question: Where is export growth coming from and what is the export outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Export revenue grew about 34% YoY and 35% QoQ, driven by HPPC and textiles in Southeast Asia, Africa and Latin America, with Thailand helping. Target is 30%+ of revenue from exports by end of FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity ramp-up and peak revenue at the new Dahej ethoxylation plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Peak utilisation is expected about 2 years after commissioning, around end-FY28. The 3x capex-to-peak-sales target is unchanged. Utilisation is about 30% today.

qa_highlights.question: Why did core B2B margin fall YoY, and how will it recover above 15%?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight costs (doubled to tripled) and raw material inflation compressed margins. Some pass-through has been achieved, but freight recovery is still a challenge. No specific recovery date was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Saudi Arabia project timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: The Board approved land leasing in KSA. Feasibility, feedstock and capex work is ongoing, and the next Board approval and detailed timelines are expected in 8-12 months.

qa_highlights.question: Will the gross margin benefit from acquisitions such as Unitop and the move to value-added products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Unitop and Tristar had lower gross margins at acquisition, and in-house ethoxylation now requires advance raw material purchases, which lengthened working capital. Gross margin is better than at end-2021 when the three businesses are combined.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the working capital debt and the net debt trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects working capital debt to be repaid by mid-2027. Net debt fell to Rs 221 crore; H1 operating cash flow was about Rs 131 crore.

risks_watch: Ethylene oxide supply from Reliance is a constraint; the expansion is expected in Q1 FY28, but incremental allocation is not yet confirmed.
Freight and logistics costs are high because of Middle East and Red Sea/Hormuz disruptions, and the core B2B margin fell 70 bps YoY to 14.1%.
The FY27 margin guide of about 12% is below H1 levels of about 12%; the company has not given a clear margin path beyond FY27.
Institutional and B2C is only at breakeven, and plans to sell this business remain undetermined in timing and value.
ROCE has fallen to low teens and is expected to recover only from next year; the Saudi capex return profile is not yet disclosed.
AHN growth has slowed; the seasonal peak in Q3 and Q4 must deliver.
543213|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on operations and balance sheet (record quarter, debt reduction, working capital gains) but cautious on the outlook. Management repeatedly declined to give H2 revenue or margin numbers, citing geopolitical and freight uncertainty, and gave only ranges.
key_quotes: We concluded the first half of FY27 on a very strong note.
Our new blending facility in Thailand is ramping up steadily.
But we don't want to hazard any guess, give anything, which after 6 months, the investors will say, you said it, and you couldn't do it?
So probably next year, we should start seeing improvements in the EBITDA percentage.

543214|2026-06.headline: NDR Auto Q1 FY27 revenue INR221.45 crore with EBITDA margin 11.88% and PAT INR16.40 crore; management guides 11-12% margin ahead.
543214|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR221.45 crore with EBITDA of INR26.44 crore (11.88% margin) and PAT of INR16.40 crore, despite sector commodity and supply-chain pressure. The company commenced NDR Hayashi sunshade operations in Bangalore in June 2026 and inaugurated the NDR Auto South seat-trim plant at Anantapur, with SOP guided for Q2 FY27. Management reiterated an INR3,000 crore revenue endeavour by 2030 (INR2,000 crore organic plus INR1,000 crore inorganic) and guided Bharat Seats to about INR3,500 crore by 2030. Order book is about INR650 crore, unchanged from last quarter per the call, and management said it is bidding for much more business.

financial_highlights.change: Revenue growth of 19.5% as cited by analyst (YoY); not restated by management

Consolidated JV loss for the quarter

segments.name: NDR Auto Components (seat frames, seat covers, non-seat)
segments.commentary: Seat frames and covers make up most of the order book; new ambient lighting orders for Maruti Suzuki are a smaller part, with start in 2028. Management says non-seat margins will be similar to seating, though new-product ROCEs will be slightly lower.

segments.name: Bharat Seats (JV)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 35% in Q1 FY27, which management said exceeded expectations; revenue target raised to about INR3,500 crore by 2030 from INR3,000-3,500 crore earlier. Premiumisation (ventilated/AC seats) flows to Bharat Seats as final assembler.

segments.name: NDR Auto South (100% subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Anantapur seat-trim and frame plant inaugurated; production starts in Q2 FY27 with revenue potential of INR70-80 crore at full run-rate, subject to model performance. Debt funding converted into equity.

segments.name: NDR Hayashi (JV)
segments.commentary: Sunshade production began in Bangalore in June 2026; JV is loss-making and expected to break even at about INR100-150 crore revenue. Original 5-6 year potential was INR200-300 crore.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin expected at about 11% to 12%, with commodities indexed to pass-through costs.
ROCE and margins expected to remain at similar levels as the business expands.
Capex of about INR40-50 crore annually for the next couple of years; INR150 crore combined capex across plants with asset turnover of about 4x.
INR3,000 crore revenue by 2030 remains an endeavour: about INR2,000 crore organic and INR1,000 crore inorganic (still being worked on).
Management expects a slight uptick in revenue growth as the South plant, SBR, NDR Safety and Latch projects start (early next year).
Hayashi JV losses to continue for some quarters until break-even; Aurangabad plant to be set up only after Toyota business is secured, with Toyota plant now seen starting calendar 2029.
capex_capacity: NDR Hayashi sunshade plant at Bangalore commenced operations in June 2026.
NDR Auto South plant at Anantapur inaugurated; SOP from Q2 FY27, with about INR8 crore extra spend mentioned on the South unit.
Upcoming plants: seat insert, seat latch, and seatbelt reminder system; NDR Safety, SBR and Latch projects starting early next year.
Two empty lands held; new plant to be announced only after acquiring business viable for it. Aurangabad land acquired, plant pending Toyota business.
Management said it has over one million seats made, supporting scale-based cost advantage.
demand_pricing: Order book about INR650 crore; management says it is bidding for much more business and will confirm quarterly.
Brezza: company supplies 100% of the model, same as outgoing model.
No customer pressure to cut selling prices; cost increases offset by operational efficiencies.
Diversification: Toyota and Kia bids in progress; other OEMs being worked with; Maruti remains core client.
Growth in Q1 seen as market-driven; Bharat Seats growth attributed to a strong market.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise sequentially and YoY, and is it one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited marketing spend for new customers and R&D on prototypes; costs will continue as the company grows aggressively, and it has hired people, so the current run-rate is the new normal.

qa_highlights.question: Will Hayashi JV losses shrink?
qa_highlights.answer: Losses will continue for some quarters until sales reach break-even, estimated at INR100-150 crore revenue; the full team and overhead are already in place while the plant is still small.

qa_highlights.question: Will Hayashi and Anantapur contribute by FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Sunshade business has started; ambient lighting contributes from 2028; South plant revenue to start in Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company revise the 2030 target upward?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Bharat Seats should be about INR3,500 crore by 2030; the group INR3,000 crore target remains an endeavour.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company disclose an EBITDA margin target for 2030?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave only a top-line target and declined to share an EBITDA margin range beyond the 11-12% near-term view.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Aurangabad plant timing linked to Toyota?
qa_highlights.answer: Plant set-up depends on winning Toyota business; management agreed Toyota's plant is now seen starting calendar 2029, so the timeline is pushed.

risks_watch: Hayashi JV losses continue until break-even at INR100-150 crore revenue; Toyota project delay pushes timeline.
Rising other expenses (marketing, R&D, hiring) could pressure margins if revenue growth lags.
Concentration on Maruti Suzuki; diversification to Toyota and Kia not yet won.
Order book flat at about INR650 crore QoQ; watch confirmations of new business.
Commodity cost pass-through via indexation; watch for pressure on the 11-12% margin band.
NDR South ramp-up and contribution not quantified by management; to be shared with results.
543214|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on operations and margins, with optimism on growth and Bharat Seats; cautious and evasive on specifics such as order-book breakdown, EBITDA margin guidance beyond 11-12%, Hayashi break-even timing, and the product mix of trims to frames.
key_quotes: Our EBITDA margins remained healthy at 11.88%, despite the environmental and supply chain challenges the sector has been faced with.
We are not facing any pressure from customers to reduce selling price. We have actually been able to set off our cost increases with operational efficiencies.
So, we will continue to have losses for some quarters until we touch a break-even point for sales.

543220|2026-03.headline: Max Healthcare Q4 FY26 revenue rose 10% YoY to INR 2,664 crore, but EBITDA margin slipped to 26.8% on chemo-drug discontinuation and higher ALOS.
543220|2026-03.overview: Network gross revenue grew 10% YoY and 2% QoQ to INR 2,664 crore, and operating EBITDA rose 8% YoY to INR 682 crore, marking the 22nd consecutive quarter of YoY growth. Margin fell to 26.8% from 27.2% a year ago, as higher ALOS (up 9% YoY) and the discontinuation of select high-value chemotherapy drugs for institutional patients weighed on ARPOB (INR 77,900) and oncology share. For FY26, revenue grew 16% to INR 10,538 crore, EBITDA rose 14% to INR 2,638 crore and PAT rose 22% to INR 1,631 crore. Management also completed control of Kalinga Hospital (250 beds, Bhubaneswar) and approved a INR 1,400 crore, 700-bed greenfield in Lucknow.

Gurugram Sector 56 (500 beds) commissioning targeted by end of FY27, after slipping from earlier second-half guidance; expected to start with about 200 beds and break even in FY28 (Dwarka precedent: broke even in 6 months).

543220|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the expansion pipeline, demand and new-hospital ramp-ups (Dwarka, Noida, Lucknow), but cautious and somewhat defensive on the chemo-drug discontinuation, which management said is largely permanent. Timelines for CGHS reversal and Gurugram were hedged with reasons for slippage.

qa_highlights.question: When will the brownfield beds contribute to EBITDA more meaningfully, and will occupancy ramp well?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said brownfield beds already contribute positively. Operating leverage will come as the balance beds open over the next couple of quarters, since costs are not linear. Occupancy stays high, but higher ALOS (+9% YoY) is temporary and lowers ARPOB.

qa_highlights.question: Will Gurugram be commissioned by end of this fiscal year and how many beds will open in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Commissioning is expected by end of FY27. Gurugram starts with about 200 beds and is expected to break even within FY28. Dwarka broke even in 6 months against 1-year guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why did oncology share drop sharply in Q4, and will it reverse?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the discontinuation of high-value chemo drugs affected day-care margins (about 16%, now below a 30%-of-MRP CGHS discount) and reduced oncology OBDs by about 5-6%. Some of the loss is permanent, with oncology share expected at 21-22%. CGHS reconsideration timing is uncertain.

qa_highlights.question: What is the chemo discontinuation impact on revenue and EBITDA, and is it annual or quarterly?
qa_highlights.answer: Annual chemotherapy billing is down about INR 200 crore gross (about INR 140 crore net of GST). Q4 has the full impact, with discontinuation starting October 2025. CGHS rate revision adds INR 100-110 crore annualised so far, with INR 30-40 crore still to come.

qa_highlights.question: Which hospitals have doctor cost pressure, and will Q4 doctor costs (about INR 435 crore) stay at this level?
qa_highlights.answer: Doctor hiring followed the 25-30% capacity addition in late 2024 and the current 20%+ brownfield rollout across Mohali, Nanavati, Smart and Lucknow. Management expects doctor cost ratios to decline with operating leverage. Kalinga will add manpower but will not move the needle.

qa_highlights.question: How do the Lucknow land bank and the Shaheed Path greenfield fit together, and is there cannibalisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Gomti Nagar (27 acres) will reach 570 beds, with another 200-300 beds planned there. Shaheed Path (5+ acres) is a 700-bed phased project over about 3 years, expandable to about 900 beds. It is a multi-location cluster strategy rather than cannibalisation.

capex_capacity: Brownfield: over the last two quarters, phased commissioning of more than 20% additional brownfield capacity at Mohali, Nanavati (Mumbai) and Max Smart (Delhi); remaining beds to be operationalised over the next 2-3 months. Management also expects another ~10% capacity from the 500-bed Gurugram greenfield on commissioning.

Initial operations expected at ~200 beds; breakeven targeted within FY28 (Dwarka precedent: 300 beds, started with 140, breakeven in 6 months vs 12-month guidance, H1 EBITDA loss ~INR 35 crore).

Dwarka brownfield of 200-plus beds being planned; Dwarka oncology centre to start next month.

Kalinga Hospital (Bhubaneswar, 250 beds, 10-acre site): controlling stake acquired in May 2026, consolidation from Q1 FY27; about INR 10 crore annual EBITDA; plans to revamp and expand. Acquisition consideration not discussed.

FY26 capital deployment: INR 1,627 crore into ongoing expansion projects and facility upgrades at newer units, INR 131 crore for land at Vaishali, INR 146 crore dividend paid; Q4 deployment INR 328 crore.
demand_pricing: Network Q4 occupancy above 75% despite higher operational beds; OBDs up 8% YoY and 4% QoQ; ALOS up 9% YoY due to simultaneous multi-location brownfield rollout, expected to tighten over time.

ARPOB INR 77,900 in Q4, after absorbing higher ALOS and discontinuation of select high-value chemotherapy drugs for institutional patients (CGHS). Chemo-drug discontinuation: discontinued since October 2025; annual chemotherapy billing down ~INR 200 crore (gross); net of GST ~INR 140 crore. Earlier drugs were billed at MRP with ~15-16% margins; CGHS now requires ~30% discount to MRP. Management says this is industry-wide but Max is most affected given oncology and institutional mix. Q4 carries the full impact.

CGHS rate revision: ~INR 100-110 crore annualised already flowing; balance INR 30-40 crore (super-specialty rates, at two hospitals so far) to flow over the coming months. Management said CGHS is reconsidering the chemo discount but timing is not fixed. ECHS and PSU patients lack dispensary access to drugs such as Keytruda.

Noida ramp-up: occupancy above 64-65% in Q4 with doctors hired; management says it is in line with expectations. Dwarka at 80-85% occupancy. Management cited a hockey-stick occupancy curve: units break even around 50-55% occupancy, and the real value comes from 60-65% to about 80%.

Other metrics: Max@Home revenue INR 73 crore (+30% YoY, 16 service lines, 15 cities); Max Lab revenue INR 52 crore (+14% YoY, 60+ cities, ~6 lakh patients); international patient revenue INR 227 crore (+12% YoY, 9% of hospital revenue); digital revenue INR 838 crore (~31% of revenue). Q4 doctor costs about INR 435 crore; management expects operating leverage from here.
Management stated the company sees 10-12% PAT margin as the industry's steady state. It said doctor compensation increases in micro-markets are transferred to patients over time.

543258|2026-03.headline: Indigo Paints Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 8.4% to INR397.9 crore; management signals margin sacrifice of 2-2.5pp to chase faster top-line growth.
543258|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone revenue grew 8.4% YoY to INR397.9 crore, with EBITDA of INR91.7 crore (23.0% margin) and gross margin of 48.6% versus 47.4% a year earlier, despite raw material costs rising 50-100% in March 2026 due to the Middle East conflict. Management said it will accept roughly 200-250bp lower gross margin, with EBITDA margin broadly unchanged, to accelerate top-line growth in FY27. demand_pricing: Management described demand as robust except for about one month of Adhik Maas, when wedding demand slowed in parts of the country. Management said July demand was strong and continuing like Q1, but declined to quantify the trend.

Recycled gold ('Shine with India' campaign) rose to over 46% of revenue in Q1, with June above 55%, as oil-driven forex pressure pushed the company to reduce imported gold.

Employee cost rose about 54% YoY standalone; management said this is more than the usual annual increment and worth about 0.2-0.3% of revenue, offset by operating leverage.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any bonus issue planned?

qa_highlights.question: Ex the one-off gain of INR410 crore, standalone PBT growth was only about 14%, so what drove the margin decline?

qa_highlights.question: Is the gold price fall boosting volumes?

qa_highlights.question: How much customs duty benefit is expected in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR60 crore in Q2, with some benefit possible in the running quarter but part to be shared with consumers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Candere?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Candere has been PAT positive since 2H FY26, will stay positive in FY27, and will add about 50 stores with focus on inventory throughput in existing stores.

qa_highlights.question: Is the employee cost increase one-time?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not one-time; it is above the usual annual increment, occurs once every few years, and operating leverage should absorb it.

risks_watch: Margin: exchange-led volumes dilute PBT margin by 0.2-0.3%; the full-year margin target depends on cash-for-gold scaling up.

qa_highlights.question: Does the INR600 crore project mean peak total revenue of INR4,000-4,500 crore, given current revenue of about INR2,500 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management rejected that reading. It said existing capacity can still ramp up and the ECH and CPVC expansions are due in a couple of months, and that epoxy and MPP together add INR1,300-1,500 crore at peak.

qa_highlights.question: What growth rate should be expected and is the target on top line or bottom line?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 15-20% CAGR over 3-5 years, with an internal aspiration of about 20%, for both top line and bottom line.

qa_highlights.question: How do the CPVC and PVC pricing respond to the recent MIP, and what is the outlook for CPVC demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the MIP mainly hit carbide-based PVC, not the ethylene-based PVC Epigral uses, so no major impact is expected. CPVC realisation is about INR110-115/kg. Demand is expected to pick up from Q3 with monsoon seasonality, though near-term overcapacity is likely as new capacity comes on.

qa_highlights.question: What are the chlorotoluenes and MPP capex, revenue and margin expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Chlorotoluenes capex of about INR250 crore is done, with expected revenue of INR300-350 crore at optimum. Including MPP, the combined top line is targeted at INR700-800 crore, at an estimated margin of about 22-23%, with 1.5-2 years to optimum utilisation.

risks_watch: Epoxy and MPP margins will be lower than the 22-24% range, with ROCE of about 20% the stated offset; the margin trajectory of the combined business is not guided numerically.
CPVC overcapacity as Grasim and others add capacity, with utilisation at 50-55% in Q1 FY27 and a demand recovery expected only from Q3.
Caustic oversupply risk for a couple of years from domestic capacity additions, with utilisation at about 75% and ECU easing from INR35,000-36,000 to INR31,000-32,000/t.
ECH realisation fell from INR200-210/kg at the war-time peak to about INR180-185/t currently; ECH and glycerin prices are volatile, linked to crude, propylene and biodiesel policy.
Execution: the pilot facility is due by September 2026, ECH capacity doubling to 100,000 tpa and the 75,000 tpa CPVC expansion are due in a couple of months, and the MPP is targeted for FY28.
Leverage and returns: net debt/EBITDA rose to 0.8x from 0.6x, ROCE fell to 16% from 24%, and the INR600 crore project is 60% debt-funded.
Capex of about INR400 crore each in FY27 and FY28 keeps balance-sheet strain and the ROCE trajectory in focus.
key_quotes: Quarter 1 FY27 presented a highly challenging operating environment across all the segments, including chemicals.
Even against this volatile backdrop Epigral demonstrated a resilience, delivering a revenue growth of 15% and EBITDA margin of 25%.
So definitely, EBITDA margin in terms of percentage, definitely, it is coming lower.
Rather than giving guidance on margin, I can tell you that ROCE, we are targeting in the range of 20%.
543332|2026-06.management_tone: Management was confident on long-term growth, expansion execution and the epoxy and MPP projects, but cautious and at times evasive on near-term pricing and margins. It declined to give a breakup of the INR600 crore capex or a numeric margin guide for the new projects, and said near-term PVC, ECH and caustic prices are too volatile to forecast.

543334|2026-06.headline: Nuvoco Q1 FY27: volume up 5% YoY to 5.3 mt and EBITDA up 7% to INR572 crore, highest-ever Q1 for both.
543334|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 volume rose 5% YoY to 5.3 million tons and EBITDA rose 7% YoY to INR572 crore, the company's highest-ever first-quarter volume and EBITDA. Realisation rose about INR320 per ton QoQ, largely offset by about INR230 per ton of cost inflation (power and fuel, raw material, packing bags, freight, fixed-cost deleverage), leaving a net EBITDA gain of about INR90 per ton. Management said the Surat grinding unit (2 mtpa) was inaugurated on 11 July 2026, ahead of schedule, and Kutch clinker and grinding remain on track for phased start from Q3 FY27. Management guided Q2 cost increase of about INR100 per ton, with power and fuel up INR30-40 per ton and packing and freight easing.

The quarter absorbed an INR898 crore non-cash impairment on the investment in CCVL (suspension PVC) and a INR150 crore exceptional charge at CCVL for onerous contracts and raw material write-down. Management said suspension PVC spreads are at roughly breakeven on a replacement-cost basis because of Chinese carbide PVC imports, while specialty chemicals grew 13%. The Board also formed a committee of three independent directors to review strategic priorities, reorganisation and M&A.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the impairment taken and what cash-flow outlook underpins it?

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of the INR150 crore exceptional item and how will Q1 be affected?

qa_highlights.question: Is the government likely to restore the 7.5% duty, and what other measures are in play?

543363|2026-03.headline: Prevest DenPro FY26 revenue rose 13.9% to INR71.81 crore and PAT rose 12.9% to INR20.49 crore, with PAT margin at 26.7%.
543363|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue from operations grew 13.9% to INR71.81 crore, with exports up 17.58% and domestic up 9%. EBITDA rose 13.3% to INR29.62 crore, though the EBITDA margin of 38.6% moderated slightly year on year. Q4 FY26 revenue grew only 2.63% to INR18.94 crore due to geopolitical disruption and shipping issues, but Q4 profitability outpaced sales, with EBITDA margin at 40.87% and PAT up 13.23% to INR5.82 crore. Management launched disinfectant commercialisation and set up a UAE subsidiary, whose operations were delayed by the Middle East conflict.

segments.name: US (Axiodent and private label)
segments.commentary: US business grew about 37.58% (also cited as 38%) in FY26, driven by online sales, direct orders and private-label business won at US exhibitions.

segments.name: Oradox oral care
segments.commentary: Sales declined about 2% in FY26 because US MoCRA-related exports and a planned Dubai consignment did not ship. Management expects 2-3 new launches and a recovery.

segments.name: 3D printing (resins and printers)
segments.commentary: 3D resin revenue rose about 40.5% YoY. 3D printers (brand Omni, sales started November 2025) rose about 162% from a low base.

UAE subsidiary expected to start online sales in Dubai the following month, after product registration; commercial operations were delayed by the Middle East conflict.

Management expects at least 40% of dental-office procedures to have a digital workflow within five years.
Management is cautious on global uncertainty but sees the domestic market, Tier 2/3 expansion and disinfectants as growth drivers.

Import substitution of raw materials is in progress through in-house development.
Subsidiaries in the UAE (opened February 2026) and the US (Axiodent) are operating; two sales staff employed in Dubai.

Competitors named for digital dentistry include Ivoclar, Dentsply and 3Shape; management says digital dentistry is a level playing field, unlike legacy products where MNCs have first-mover advantage.
Disinfectants launched this year, with an early customer response described as highly encouraging; no revenue figure given.
Oradox was hit by US MoCRA cosmetic-regulation requirements and by the Middle East conflict, which blocked a planned Dubai consignment.

qa_highlights.question: Why has growth slowed over the last 3-4 years?

qa_highlights.question: What do the UAE and US subsidiaries do, and how is Dubai responding?
qa_highlights.answer: The US subsidiary, Axiodent, drove US growth of about 37.58% through online sales, direct orders and private labelling. The Dubai subsidiary opened in February 2026, hired two sales staff and is registering products for online sales expected next month.

qa_highlights.question: What is current capacity utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Vinay Jamwal said traditional capacity runs at 67-68% utilisation, which would imply about INR125 crore turnover at full installed capacity. New lines run at 18-20%.

qa_highlights.question: What drove domestic performance and what steps were taken?
qa_highlights.answer: Vaibhav Munjal cited expansion of Tier 2/3 distribution, a larger in-house sales team and new products such as disinfectants and Rotoflex. H1 was hit by floods and GST changes, and H2 recovered.

qa_highlights.question: How is Oradox trending?
qa_highlights.answer: Sai Kalyan said sales fell about 2% because US and Dubai exports were blocked by MoCRA rules and the war. Management expects recovery through marketing, direct-to-doctor programmes and 2-3 launches.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 3D printing opportunity and right to win?

Dubai subsidiary has not yet started commercial operations and depends on the Middle East situation.
Oradox is declining and needs the planned launches and US/Dubai registrations to recover.

543364|2026-03.headline: Markolines reported FY26 revenue of Rs 348.49 crore (up from Rs 307 crore) and PAT of Rs 26.23 crore (about 15% higher), with EPS up 17% to Rs 11.90.
543364|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue of Rs 348.49 crore against Rs 307 crore a year earlier, EBITDA of Rs 48.54 crore and PAT of Rs 26.23 crore, with EPS rising from Rs 10.16 to Rs 11.90. The call centred on the pending merger with Markolines Infra, a targeted FY27 growth of at least 30% on a standalone basis, and an active pipeline of about Rs 2,000 crore. Several answers on margins, order book and merger timing were qualitative or repeated.
