segments.name: Markolines Infra (proposed merger)
segments.commentary: Cited at about Rs 150 crore FY26 revenue; operates about 60 work orders across about 30 projects including 28 toll projects. Management said its PAT margin is 9 to 10%, above pavement, and monthly billing is about Rs 14 to 15 crore.

segments.name: School and sports infrastructure
segments.commentary: Newly entered; one open school infrastructure order and two smaller sports complex rehabilitation orders in Andhra Pradesh. No value disclosed.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of at least 30% on a standalone basis, per management; Markolines Infra revenue would be additional on merger.
Merger with Markolines Infra expected to be completed by end of FY27; management cites about six months for NCLT processes, with all queries answered and none pending.
Target closing order book of at least Rs 1,000 crore by end of FY27.
Target of Rs 1,000 crore revenue scale in about three years, with possibility to bring it forward.
Capex of about Rs 10 crore in FY27 for one or more pavers and possibly one HMP; policy of not exceeding Rs 10 crore per year.
Management expects monsoon at about 90% of average this year; first two quarters to see lower revenue.
capex_capacity: No major capex in FY26, per management.
Plan for one or a few additional pavers and possibly one HMP, about Rs 10 crore in FY27.

Eligible to bid up to Rs 500 crore projects on its own following completion of a Maharashtra tunnel project.

Active pipeline of about Rs 2,000 crore across four to five projects of Rs 300 to 500 crore each; management says it wins at least 50% of targeted orders.
L1 position on a Rs 120 crore maintenance contract with a corporation, per management.
Management says it works on a cost-plus basis with clients, so PBT and PAT margins are steady (7 to 8%), while EBITDA varies with client capex pass-through.
Management says maintenance is about 15% of road cost in India versus about 40% globally, which it sees as a long-term driver.
Government allowed sovereign and international funds to participate in PPP highway construction, which management sees as increasing demand for O&M partners.

qa_highlights.question: Status of merger with Markolines Infra and expected completion?
qa_highlights.answer: Applications filed and all queries answered in March, with few recently answered; management expects about six months to completion and a merged entity by FY27 end.

qa_highlights.question: EBITDA margins of Infra and combined FY27 margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Infra results to be released within a week after final audit; Infra margins are higher than pavement, with PAT of about 9 to 10% for services. Management later said PBT and PAT margins stay at 7 to 8%.

qa_highlights.question: FY26 and FY27 capex plans?
qa_highlights.answer: No major capex in FY26; about Rs 10 crore planned in FY27 for pavers and possibly one HMP, with equipment churned every 3 to 4 years.

qa_highlights.question: Win ratio and closing order book expectations for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Win ratio of at least 50% on targeted active orders; management targets a closing order book of at least Rs 1,000 crore, versus an 18-month typical coverage norm.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 growth and margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects growth of at least 30% standalone, driven by higher eligibility after the tunnel project; margin guidance was not given, as EBITDA is said to vary with client capex pass-through.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses fall in Q4, and what drove the 62% QoQ PAT jump?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said other expenses and material consumption must be viewed together because outsourcing shifts costs between heads, and margins should be similar. Q4 is seasonally strongest as billing concentrates in March.

risks_watch: Merger timing relies on NCLT approval; management expects completion within about six months.

Consolidated revenue was about INR17.2bn and adjusted EBITDA about INR2.6bn (15% margin) before INR1.9bn of one-time acquisition and integration costs. Legacy Tega consumables delivered strong growth and margin expansion, while the equipment business fell sharply on delayed customer clearances. Management stressed that one month of Molycop is too short to draw full-year conclusions, but said June was directionally ahead of acquisition expectations.

financial_highlights.change: Prior-year one-time costs about INR0.75-0.8bn per analyst reconciliation
Income +23% YoY from INR3.72bn; EBITDA from INR0.71bn (~19%)

segments.commentary: Revenue INR3.96bn (+36% YoY); EBITDA before one-time INR1bn at 24.1% margin (+320bps). About 23% of group revenue. Part of Q4 orders were serviced in Q1, so growth is not a clean run-rate.

segments.name: Tega Equipment
segments.commentary: Revenue INR358mn vs INR643mn (-44% YoY) due to delayed customer clearances; EBITDA roughly breakeven on lower volumes and operating leverage. About 2% of group revenue.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR12.9bn and adjusted EBITDA INR1.6bn (~13% margin, USD17.2mn); gross margin ~36%. Volume FY (12m to Jun-26) 1.204mt vs 1.223mt prior; 12m EBITDA USD191mn, up 11% from USD172mn.

Consolidated EBITDA margin expected to stay around 15% for the full year.

Tega capex (excluding Molycop) about USD40mn for FY27 including Chile; Molycop 10-month capex about USD28mn, normalised about low USD30mn annually.

Molycop volumes: 1.204mt in 12 months to June 2026 vs 1.223mt prior year.
Freeport Indonesia Grasberg: blocks 2 and 3 at planned rates; full return to planned capacity targeted by end-CY2027. Cobra Panama restart discussions ongoing.
demand_pricing: Molycop: around 85% of contracts have steel-index-linked pricing, so revenue per ton moves with steel; management tracks per-ton margin rather than percentage margin.
Molycop states above 50% market share in core regions; largest volumes in South America, with North America, Australasia and growing Africa.
Copper above USD14,000/t and gold around USD4,400/oz cited as supportive of mining investment.
Management says it has faced Chinese competition in Latin America for decades and maintains leading position via lead times, local footprint and technical support.

Freight costs have risen; Tega passes through freight in contracts with a quarter lag; Molycop hedges ocean freight and passes through land costs linked to gas prices. No material deferment of shipments seen.
Equipment shortfall attributed to customer clearance delays rather than demand loss.

qa_highlights.question: How will revenue ramp from cross-selling across Tega and Molycop networks, beyond the USD20mn cost synergies?
qa_highlights.answer: Mehul Mohanka said the revenue ramp is expected from Q3 to Q4 FY27; it is early days, and quantified guidance will come in a couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is Molycop's margin seasonal, is the current margin steady state, and are there one-off RM or macro items?
qa_highlights.answer: Patrick Koley said there is little quarter-to-quarter seasonality, June was historically Molycop's strongest quarter, and margin should be relatively flat in coming quarters. Molycop manages to per-ton margin because about 85% of contracts are steel-index linked.

qa_highlights.question: Chile plant commissioning status?
qa_highlights.answer: Mehul Mohanka said the plant is on track for soft commissioning around January 2027 and commercial production around March 2027, subject to local regulatory clearances expected within a two-month window.

qa_highlights.question: Are there any further one-time costs beyond the current quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Mehul Mohanka confirmed the Q1 one-time costs are the full amount. The analyst tallied INR110cr this year plus about INR75-80cr last year, totalling about INR190cr, which management confirmed.

qa_highlights.question: Group and Molycop debt levels and year-end expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Ravi Joshi said group total debt is INR112bn including about INR26bn of redeemable preference shares. Patrick Koley said Molycop net debt was USD672mn at June 30 and is expected to fall by year-end, with ABL swings driven by bar payments.

qa_highlights.question: Molycop capex and volume outlook, plus Latin America competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Patrick Koley said 10-month capex is about USD28mn, normalised capex is in the low USD30mn range, and volume is expected up about 5% and EBITDA up about 4% on a 10-month comparable basis. Volume was 1.204mt for the 12 months to June 2026 vs 1.223mt prior year. Lance Dawber said Molycop has competed with China for decades and retains its lead through lead times and local support.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 finance cost, Tega capex, and consumables growth and margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Ravi Joshi guided FY27 finance cost to INR110-120cr and Tega capex excluding Molycop to about USD40mn including Chile. Mehul Mohanka maintained about 15% consumables CAGR and said pass-through of costs has a one-quarter lag, supporting a 20-23% margin.

risks_watch: Integration and synergy delivery: about USD20mn targeted over 2-2.5 years; cross-sell revenue quantification deferred by a couple of quarters.
Only one month of Molycop (June 2026) is consolidated; the 10-month outlook (volume +5%, EBITDA +4%) is not yet a full run-rate read. Watch the Q2 print.
Equipment revenue fell 44% YoY on customer clearance delays; order book executable within one year is stated as INR9.6 million in the transcript, likely a typo for INR9.6bn, and needs confirmation.
Chile plant timing depends on local regulatory approvals; any slip beyond March 2027 would delay commercial production.
Freight and container availability: pass-through has about a one-quarter lag, and Molycop's land freight is linked to gas prices. Molycop's per-ton margin is exposed to steel index movements.

Deleveraging depends on non-core land divestments (no amount or timing given) and on Molycop working-capital swings from bar payments; FX exposure is partly hedged, with Spain and Australia operations outside USD.
Molycop margin figures are inconsistent in the call: about 13% (INR1.6bn on INR12.9bn) versus about 30% cited in a Q&A question, which management did not clearly reconcile.
key_quotes: Before moving to the quarterly performance update, I would like to emphasize that this is the first quarter in which Molycop's performance for the month of June 2026 has been consolidated into Tega's financial result of Q1 FY27.
It would be premature to draw conclusions regarding the full year outlook based on this number of Molycop.
So, request a couple of quarters of patience with us and we'll be able to give you a more definitive number around it.
We're maintaining our guidance of about 15% CAGR on the consumables.
We haven't seen much of deferment, but yes, that does, you know, contribute in terms of logistic challenges in terms of container availability, frequency of mother vessels coming to port.
543413|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on the legacy Tega consumables business and on Molycop's June momentum, but cautious on forward numbers, since management repeatedly said one month of Molycop is too short to draw full-year conclusions. It was more evasive on cross-sell revenue and Chile timing, deferring quantified guidance and stressing that approvals are "anyone's guess".

543415|2026-06.headline: Anand Rathi Wealth Q1 FY27 underlying PAT rose 24% YoY to INR116 crore, with AUM up 21% to INR1,06,300 crore.
543415|2026-06.overview: Management reported its 19th consecutive quarter of profit growth, with underlying consolidated revenue (excluding fair value gains, ESOP and related tax) up 18% YoY to INR336 crore and PAT up 24% to INR116 crore, a 34.4% margin. Reported revenue and PAT including fair value gains were INR430 crore and INR163 crore, with INR96 crore of the other income being mark-to-market gain on the Anand Rathi Global Finance (ARGFL) holding. Net flows were INR2,743 crore in the quarter, and client attrition was 0.09% of AUM with zero RM attrition. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of INR1,415 crore revenue and INR460 crore PAT, with Q1 delivering 24% and 25% of these respectively. The call also covered a Board approval to apply for an AMC licence, a UK subsidiary, and a GIFT City licence in progress.

segments.name: Flagship wealth management (ARWL)
segments.commentary: AUM INR1,06,300 crore, 13,941 client families after net addition of 1,600+ in last 12 months; client AUM attrition 0.09% in Q1 and zero RM attrition. AUM per RM described as rising, with 33 clients per RM.

segments.name: Digital wealth (B2B2C subsidiary)
segments.commentary: AUM INR2,526 crore, up 23% YoY; clients up 16% to 7,320.

segments.name: OFA (SaaS platform subsidiary)
segments.commentary: 6,890 subscribers and platform assets of INR1.66 lakh crore as of 30 June 2026.

segments.name: Mutual fund distribution
segments.commentary: Net equity MF sales of INR1,900 crore in Q1. Management cites FY26 market share of net flows at 2.3% (presented as 2.47%), up from 0.18% in FY19-20; distributor yield about 1.09% post-GST, with 1-3 bps possible pressure from TER changes.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of INR1,415 crore and PAT guidance of INR460 crore reiterated; Q1 achieved 24% and 25% respectively.
Management modelled AUM growth of 20-25% p.a. over next 3 years: 10-12% from mark-to-market plus net sales of INR1,100-1,200 crore per month (about 1% of AUM per month).
Long-term target of about 4% share of AMFI Category II assets (around INR6 lakh crore in ~8-10 years), requiring 22-23% asset growth.
Board approved applying for an AMC licence; GIFT City licence in process (second stage underway).
capex_capacity: Board approved AMC licence application; first stage of licensing done, second stage in process per management.
UK subsidiary operations started in Q1; management said it would be built brick-by-brick, not scaled quickly.
Management cites capacity for about 6,500 new client families with existing RMs (33 clients per RM against capacity of ~50), plus 490 trained RMs and 100 more RMs about 60% ready.
Fund of funds in UK with 11 schemes listed there for UK participants.
demand_pricing: Net flows of INR2,743 crore in Q1 despite volatile markets; equity MF net sales INR1,900 crore.

Platinum families (INR50 crore+ bucket) about 230 vs 211 earlier; target 450-500 in two years. Upgrade rate from sub-INR5 crore to INR50 crore cohort guided at roughly 10-20% per quarter (management estimate).
Model portfolio of 14 mutual fund schemes beat Nifty by about 6% in Q1 (Nifty about 7%, portfolio about 7% after costs per management; figures as stated).

Structured products: management says ARGFL products dominate the mix; third-party share kept low for credit risk. Q1 MLD primary issuance INR2,187 crore (INR1,875 crore to group companies, INR312 crore third party), up from INR1,704 crore; secondary INR968 crore vs INR755 crore.
Client retention on three RM departures to a competitor: about 90% of INR758 crore assets retained as of June end (INR658.5 crore), excluding market movement.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q1 update on Platinum families and how fast will the INR5-50 crore bucket upgrade?
qa_highlights.answer: Platinum families are about 230 vs 211 earlier, from 40-45 at launch about 2.5 years ago; upgrade rate estimated at 10-20% a quarter; management expects four-digit client counts in a few years.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a cap on AUM per RM?
qa_highlights.answer: No cap; management says AUM per RM should keep rising while client attrition stays low (0.09%), and some RMs have reached INR500-1,500 crore. The figure was INR100 crore at listing.

qa_highlights.question: How is asset allocation managed in volatile markets and why not recommend gold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the highest portfolio beta is 0.6-0.65 and it sells products it buys; it does not recommend gold given household gold holdings of about 28% of savings. Overall mix is about INR55,000 crore equity and INR4,500 crore debt plus structured products.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the other income of INR110 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: INR96 crore is mark-to-market gain on ARGFL holding, revalued semi-annually by a third-party investment banker; the rest is interest on surplus cash.

qa_highlights.question: Is there yield pressure from TER changes in mutual funds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pass-through is limited to 1-3 bps of its roughly 1.09% post-GST yield, and scale gives bargaining power; it has no plans to recommend stocks, PMS or long-only AIFs currently.

qa_highlights.question: Will ARWL enter investment banking or other capital market businesses?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said it will pursue only an AMC licence and no investment banking, focusing on intergenerational wealth rather than transaction-driven capital management.

qa_highlights.question: What is the long-term AUM growth plan and how is it sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 20-25% AUM growth from embedded client returns, capacity in existing RMs, new RMs and penetration, citing 90-95% confidence; the 4% Category II target implies 22-23% growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the RBI bank guarantee circular on derivatives volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management views the circular as positive, expecting reduced high-frequency trading volumes, and sees negligible or positive impact on ARWL.

Reported total revenue (incl. FV gains, ESOP, tax)

risks_watch: Client attrition (0.09% of AUM in Q1) and RM attrition: management's AUM-per-RM and 20-25% growth thesis depends on keeping these low; three RM departures to a competitor are being tracked (about 90% of INR758 crore retained as of June end).

Market-dependence of the growth plan: 10-12% annual mark-to-market plus INR1,100-1,200 crore monthly net sales (about 1% of AUM per month) must be delivered; management cites a Nifty historical median of about 11% for the next 3 years as support.

Other income quality: INR96 crore MTM gain on the ARGFL holding is revalued semi-annually by a third-party banker and flows through P&L; it inflated reported PAT to INR163 crore versus underlying INR116 crore.

Concentration in structured products and ARGFL: the group company dominates structured product issuance (Q1 primary MLD INR1,875 crore to group vs INR312 crore third party), a related-party exposure to monitor.

Mutual fund distributor yield: about 1.09% post-GST, with 1-3 bps possible pass-through pressure from TER changes; the RBI bank guarantee circular impact is described by management as negligible or positive, not quantified.

Execution of new initiatives: AMC licence (Board approved, application pending), GIFT City licence (second stage in process), and UK subsidiary (operations started, to be built slowly); timelines and costs were not quantified.

Cautious or evasive on quantified details for the AMC, GIFT City and UK businesses (timelines, costs, yields), and on the RM-departure retention figure, which was given as a range of 70-80% and then 80% before a precise 90%.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said platinum clients (over 1.5% of clients) keep 50-60% of their wallet with ARWL, and top 100 clients 60-70%; wealth defined as all assets, not just mutual funds.

qa_highlights.question: Will ESOP costs decline next year and employee cost growth slow?
qa_highlights.answer: Feroze Azeez said non-cash ESOP/MTM costs will reduce dramatically, narrowing the gap between PBT (INR 122 crore) and ~INR 90 crore.

qa_highlights.question: GIFT City revenue opportunity and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will bring NRI and global capital into India via GIFT City, with no revenue provisioned in FY27 guidance until proof of concept; inward-only focus both short and long term.

qa_highlights.question: Net flow split between existing and new clients and strategic priorities?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 split was 62% existing and 38% new; four growth engines cited: client performance, capacity utilisation (431 RMs, room for 8,000 clients), capacity creation (500 account managers), and wallet penetration.

qa_highlights.answer: Target INR 1.2 lakh crore AUM for the year; Q2 AUM about INR 1.08 lakh crore (+18% YoY); mark-to-market hit about INR 2,000 crore in the quarter; management said AUM is the most volatile guidance metric.

543419|2026-03.headline: Shriram Properties FY26 revenue rose 39% to INR1,357 crores and net profit crossed INR100 crores for the first time, with FY27 guidance of INR3,300-3,500 crores sales value.
543419|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue hit a record INR1,357 crores (+39% YoY) and net profit rose 30% to INR101 crores, driven by a strong Q4 handover push in Bangalore, Chennai and Kolkata. Full-year sales value was flat at INR2,354 crores, with Q4 sales of INR663 crores, as several launches slipped due to approval delays, mainly in Bangalore. Management guided FY27 to be stronger than FY26, with sales value of INR3,300-3,500 crores, collections of INR2,100-2,200 crores and handovers of 3,750-3,800 units. Analysts pressed on margins, the rising other-expense line, the cash flow trend, and the funding of new land acquisitions; management said these would be funded from completed-project cash flows and possibly intermittent debt.

segments.name: Bangalore
segments.commentary: Core market; Songs of the Earth launch sold over 85% in launch year. Management says the growth strategy is centred on Bangalore and Pune, with North Bangalore flagged for higher pricing upside.

segments.name: Pune
segments.commentary: Maiden launch at Undri (Spectrum) sold over 300 units in under a year, against roughly 850 units absorbed annually by the micro-market over the last three years. Pune revenue is recognised under percentage-of-completion.

segments.name: Kolkata
segments.commentary: Land settlement with the Government of West Bengal done; 314 acres originally, 42 acres surrendered, 100+ acres still available. Skyblooms Villas over 50% sold and Signature Square about 40% sold at launch. Approval exists for 2.3 million sq ft of apartments, with plotted development planned.

segments.name: Chennai
segments.commentary: Contributed to Q4 revenue recognition from completed projects; a launch is expected within about a week of the call.

FY27 collections of INR2,100-2,200 crores and handovers of 3,750-3,800 units.
FY27 pipeline addition of 7-8 million sq ft and GDV addition of INR5,000-6,000 crores; land-related capital commitment of INR350-400 crores.
FY27 project completions of about 3.8 million sq ft, with revenue recognition potential of about INR1,740 crores.
Mission FY28 targets: sales of INR5,000 crores, revenue of INR2,500 crores and PBT of INR250 crores; management reiterated PBT margin of 10-11%.
Management expects 8-9% PAT margin on a normalised 3-year basis, with the effective tax rate below 25% due to carried-forward losses.
Construction capital spend of INR900-1,000 crores expected in FY27, versus roughly INR90-95 crores per quarter recently.
Finance costs may decline slightly, but gross debt of about INR600 crores will continue; the company may take intermittent bridge debt.
capex_capacity: Ongoing projects: 16.7 million sq ft, 85% sold; 2.6 million sq ft unsold in ongoing projects, plus 18.6 million sq ft upcoming pipeline; total unsold potential over 21 million sq ft, GDV about INR13,950 crores.
Seven projects acquired during FY26; approvals under way; over 7 million sq ft expected to enter the launch pipeline in the next 3-6 months. Target to double the upcoming pipeline in 18-24 months.

Management flagged IT employment trends, interest rate affordability and longer sales cycles as sector risks; focus is on mid and upper-mid housing.
Kolkata: management said the new state government is positive. Long-term outlook strong, but near-term recovery expected to be slower than Bangalore or Pune.
Competition: management said the market favours branded and organised developers.

qa_highlights.question: Will rising operating cash outflows and higher new-project investment lead to a cash crunch or more debt?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said FY26 free cash flow fell slightly due to construction spend ahead of finishing stages; no additional debt is needed for construction, as liquidity is sufficient.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise from INR126 crores to INR172 crores, and will they rise further in FY27?

Hemant Buch attributed the bancassurance policy decline to one microfinance corporate agency issue and a conscious move to bigger tickets; Q4 sales count rose about 10%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook for the next year and the building blocks for expansion from here?
qa_highlights.answer: Pant said margins could be challenged over the next three years and the journey will be gradual; the company will not chase margins at the cost of insurance-for-all. Doraiswamy said ticket size and persistency are the drivers, with product mix to consolidate.

capex_capacity: No capex, capacity or commissioning discussion on the call; the call covered insurance sales, margins, capital and dividend.
Capital position: solvency ratio 2.35 at 31 March 2026 vs 2.11 a year earlier; management said it wants to build reserves ahead of risk-based capital (RBC) and that growth will also consume capital.

Digital capacity: 23,00,983 policies completed via the agent-assisted ANANDA app in FY26 vs 14,74,208 in FY25 (+56.08%); active agents on ANANDA up 29.56%. New MyLIC customer app launched (15 April 2026) and LIC Super Sales Saathi app for sales personnel under the DIVE programme.
Bima Sakhi scheme: 3,45,000 Bima Sakhis appointed, 21.94 lakh policies sold and ₹2,848 crore new business premium in FY26; coverage at 1,43,924 of 2,44,876 Gram Panchayats (59%).
demand_pricing: Market share by first-year premium 56.6% in FY26 vs 57.05% in FY25; individual market share 36.6% (vs 37.46%); group 70.11% (vs 71.19%).
Individual new business premium ₹67,676 crore (+8.29%); individual renewal premium ₹2,71,699 crore (+5.91%); group new business premium ₹1,92,912 crore out of group total ₹1,96,609 crore (+16.26%).

Non-par individual APE ₹15,214 crore (+43.78%), 35.11% of individual APE vs 27.69%. Jeevan Utsav was the main contributor to savings growth (management cited ~48.40% savings bucket growth); Jeevan Labh contributed about 40% of par savings premium.

VNB margin bridge 17.6% to 21.2%: business mix +3%, RFR +3.4%, operating assumption changes (expense and persistency realignment plus GST) -2.8%. Individual par ~42% of APE contributes ~28% of VNB; individual non-par ~22.7% of APE contributes ~53% of VNB; remainder group (~19%).

Operating experience variance of ₹92,639 crore; persistency variance +₹3,509 crore (group line strengthened, par 13th-month persistency improved, +₹2,463 crore); mortality roughly flat; expense variance positive, net of GST.

Economic variance: equity MTM fall ₹53,698 crore and debt MTM fall ₹46,853 crore. Bond-amortisation accounting change impact of about ₹11,000 crore gross, of which ~₹9,000 crore sits in participating business (no direct PAT impact per management).

Bancassurance and alternate channels NBP ₹5,076 crore (+45.19%): banks ₹3,151 crore (+22.30%), alternate channels ₹1,925 crore (+109.36%). Policy count via bancassurance fell about 36%; management attributed this to a microfinance corporate agency issue and a conscious move away from login-based low-ticket sales; Q4 policy count reportedly up ~10%.

Agency: individual agents 14,57,045 vs 14,86,851 (down ~30,000); agency sourced 98.42% of policies and 91.75% of new business premium. Management said recruitment, training and younger-age agent focus will follow.

April 2026 sales described as good and ahead of FY26 pace across participating and non-participating products; management said it is too early to judge the effect of recent market volatility on ULIP and guaranteed demand.
Pricing: management said non-par IRRs depend on investment opportunities and competition and are balanced against margins; long-duration hedges are limited. Expense ratio 11.91% (-51 bps).

543526|2026-06.headline: LIC Q1 FY27 net VNB margin rose 750 bps YoY to 22.9% and VNB grew 61.32% to ₹3,136 crore; profit after tax up 22.81% to ₹13,492 crore.
543526|2026-06.overview: LIC reported Q1 FY27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026) with total premium of ₹127,250 crore (+6.75% YoY) and individual new business premium of ₹14,351 crore (+14.48% YoY). Net VNB margin expanded to 22.9% from 15.4%, driven mainly by business mix (non-par savings and protection growth) and a 2.9% positive assumption impact, partly offset by a 1.9% negative expense impact from loss of GST input tax credit. Overall market share by first-year premium fell to 60.10% from 63.51%, with group share down to 70.90% and individual share up to 38.89%. The company also disclosed the 6.5% government OFS, taking public float to 10%.

segments.name: Group business
segments.commentary: Group total premium ₹51,834 crore (+8.61%); group APE ₹6,160 crore; group market share fell to 70.90% from 76.54% on a comparable basis.

segments.name: Par vs non-par (APE)
segments.commentary: Par individual APE ₹5,085 crore (67.51% of individual APE); non-par ₹2,447 crore (32.49%). Management cited non-par savings growth of 59.24% and non-par protection growth of 43.59%.

segments.name: Bancassurance and alternate channels
segments.commentary: NBP ₹907.14 crore (+5.25%); bank channel NBP ₹483.39 crore (-8.62%) due to delayed bank marketing plans and West Asia related remittance pressure on annuities; alternate channels ₹423.75 crore (+27.27%).

capex_capacity: The call did not discuss capex, capacity, utilisation, or commissioning timelines; no capex plans were stated.

Product pipeline: two new products launched since April 2026 (New Jeevan Sathi single premium and limited premium); Nav Jeevan Shree single premium withdrawn. Total of 59 products available for new business as of 30 June 2026.

Digital and distribution capacity: MyLIC and Super Sales Saathi apps launched in April 2026 under the DIVE initiative; agent-assisted Ananda application completed 436,925 policies in Q1 FY27 (+25.56% YoY).
Bima Sakhi rollout: 2.87 lakh women designated, covering 151,620 of 244,876 gram panchayats (62%) as of 30 June 2026; target is at least one Bima Sakhi per gram panchayat.
Agent force: 1,445,692 agents as of 30 June 2026 (-2.73% YoY); management said non-serious Bima Sakhi recruits are being weeded out, which will continue.
guidance_outlook: Management does not normally give guidance but expects VNB margin to keep improving over the next few quarters, subject to RFR movements.
Management said VNB margin should settle around the industry average and is working toward mid-20s VNB margin by year end.
Non-par growth expected to continue from Q1 to Q4 pattern; ULIP recovery expected when market normalises.
Expense ratio expected to fall with operational efficiency; GST ITC-related expense impact to be compared against last year in Q1 and Q2 only.
Bancassurance expected to recover in subsequent quarters after delayed bank marketing plans.
APE growth expected to strengthen in subsequent quarters as new business focus increases through the year.
demand_pricing: Individual protection growth above 40% YoY on a small base; individual agents drove most protection policy volume.
ULIP premium declined YoY due to market volatility; management said it expects recovery only when markets normalise and denied cannibalisation of non-par.
Average ticket size rose after minimum sum assured for the major regular-premium product was raised from ₹1 lakh to ₹2 lakh (October 2024) and annuity single-premium sales grew.
Agent count fell 2.73% YoY to 1,445,692 (market share by agent count 43.69% vs 47.11%) as non-serious Bima Sakhi recruits quit; agency sold 98.51% of policies and 93.07% of new business premium.

qa_highlights.question: What are the assumption changes in the VNB walk and is the cost impact GST-led?
qa_highlights.answer: Assumption changes contributed +2.9% (RFR, persistency alignment, CRNHR, TVOG); expense assumptions including loss of ITC contributed -1.9%. Business mix contributed about +6.5%. The GST exemption removed ITC, adding to expenses, but higher volumes should dilute per-policy expenses.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ULIP decline deliberate and will it recover in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly market-driven due to volatility; management focused on margin-accretive non-par lines. ULIP recovery depends on market improvement; no cannibalisation expected.

qa_highlights.question: Why does RWRP differ from individual APE?
qa_highlights.answer: APE annualises new business premium by frequency and excludes first-year renewal premiums received after policy completion; RWRP captures actual premium received, so the gap reflects strong first-year renewal premium.

qa_highlights.question: Why is APE growth soft despite strong VNB growth, and what is the medium-term aspiration?
qa_highlights.answer: Prior-year base had higher regular-premium share; management expects APE growth to pick up in later quarters. No numeric medium-term target given; management agreed to examine monthly APE disclosure.

qa_highlights.question: Split of VNB margin by line of business?
qa_highlights.answer: Par: 37.1% of APE with 19.4% margin; individual non-par: ₹1,678 crore APE with 49.3% margin; group: 45% of APE with 29.4% margin (figures given as shares of VNB as well as APE by the Appointed Actuary, clarified as proportion of VNB by segment).

qa_highlights.question: Why is the solvency ratio high and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: 2.42 is pre-dividend; 2.32 after subsequent dividend. Higher solvency supports protection growth, but management will await regulatory changes before deciding on any change to solvency strategy.

qa_highlights.question: Why is bancassurance individual NBP growing much slower than policy count?
qa_highlights.answer: Bank channel faced pressure from West Asia conflict affecting remittances (annuities) and market volatility (ULIPs); low-ticket policies were withdrawn after minimum sum assured rose to ₹2 lakh.

qa_highlights.question: Is VNB margin on track for mid-20s by year end?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is working toward that target.

risks_watch: Assumption and RFR movements: RFR contributed positively, but management said it is outside LIC's control and could change the margin trajectory.
Persistency weakness: 61-month premium persistency fell to 61.12% from 63.85%; 13-month number-based persistency rose to 66.45% from 64.35%; group persistency contributed negatively to assumptions.
Market share erosion: overall first-year premium share fell to 60.10% from 63.51%; group share fell sharply.
Expense ratio up 16 bps YoY to 10.63% after loss of GST input tax credit; volume growth must outpace expense growth.
Maturity claims up 12.88% YoY to ₹57,099 crore; agent count down 2.73% YoY.
Bancassurance bank channel NBP down 8.62%; recovery timing uncertain.
Solvency pre-dividend 2.42, post-dividend 2.32; any capital needs for protection growth require monitoring.
Shareholder profit from ASM funds (₹180,000 crore book value) and par surplus transfer timing (mainly Q4) affect quarterly profit comparisons.
IEV unwind and EV not disclosed quarterly; next disclosure at half-year.
543526|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on margins and profit growth, with explicit caution on ULIP, bancassurance and APE momentum, which management attributed to market volatility and timing. Management was evasive on specific assumption splits and unwind rates, deferring to the half-year EV/IEV disclosure.
key_quotes: We expect the margins to improve.
So APE and WRP cannot be equal.
We would like to see that the non-par growth continues the way it has been growing from Q1 to Q4 over the previous years that will continue in the current year as well.
We don't normally give a guidance, but we expect it to improve over the next few quarters as well, of course, keeping the one uncertain factor of the RFR.

543527|2026-06.headline: Prudent's Q1 FY27 PAT rose 44.4% YoY to INR74.8 crores, with average AUM up 21% to INR1.33 lakh crores despite a 2.8 bps gross yield cut.

Operating profit rose 32.4% YoY to INR89.1 crores and PAT rose 44.4% YoY to INR74.8 crores, helped by treasury gains. New SEBI/AMC regulatory changes from April 2026 (GST treatment, exit load removal) cut gross yield by about 2.8 bps to around 88 bps and shifted commission expense lower, which management called a one-time reset. Management said the current margin should be the run-rate for the next three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What was the gross margin last quarter and how has it moved this quarter, and what is the standalone MF contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Shah said MF margin was 91.2 bps last quarter and about 88.4 bps this quarter, a 2.8 bps fall due to the 5 bps exit load removal from TER. Segment margins are not disclosed; operating margin is the suggested proxy.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 commission-to-revenue ratio (56.2% standalone) a steady-state number?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Shah said the current margin can be used for the next three quarters and the spread should hold, as the regulatory changes were applied across the full book. Shirish Patel added that insurance mix in Q4 was higher, which also affects the ratio.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net revenue yield after commissions and will it persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Shirish Patel said current yield levels would likely persist in the near term; medium to long term it could fall 1 to 2 bps, mainly on new business.

qa_highlights.question: Can MFD partners go direct once mutual-fund-only PMS is allowed?
qa_highlights.answer: Shirish Patel said the risk is low since MFDs need a platform; a possible consolidation of licences is the bigger effect. No yield uplift is assumed from the 2.25% PMS fee structure.

qa_highlights.question: Who are the new MFD additions and what is the direct versus indirect AUM split?
qa_highlights.answer: Shirish Patel said most of the increase in registrations came from existing distributors moving to Prudent's platform. Sanjay Shah put the split at roughly 90:10 (partners versus direct).

qa_highlights.question: How should AUM growth be viewed beyond MTM, and how fast is net sales growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Shirish Patel said net sales historically add about 10-12% to AUM each year, and FY26 growth came mainly from net sales rather than MTM.

543528|2026-03.headline: Venus Pipes Q4 FY26 revenue rose 17% YoY to INR302.2 crores, with EBITDA margin at 16.3% and PAT up 7% to INR25.4 crores.
543528|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew 17% YoY to INR302.2 crores and FY26 revenue grew 22% to INR1,166.8 crores. Export sales fell to INR87.8 crores from INR112.5 crores on Middle East disruption, while domestic demand stayed robust. The company completed its seamless and welded capex program and announced a spooling foray for data centers backed by a INR185 crores LOI. Management guided to more than 20% growth in FY27 and EBITDA margin above FY26's 16.3%, rising to 18% by FY28.

qa_highlights.answer: Target start by end of calendar 2026 with about 3x asset turn and higher margin than the base business; the order is executable in about 15 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue growth of at least 20%, and EBITDA margin above FY26's 16.3%, moving to 17% and then 18% by FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the PAT stay flat at INR25-26 crores over about nine quarters despite the investment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PAT growth should follow as most capex is complete, with the value-added projects expected to lift PAT in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20% FY27 growth guidance at risk given a lower order book (INR450 crores vs about INR575 crores a year ago) and softer exports?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to the BHEL L1 orders, the data-center LOI, new fittings, and the expanded seamless capacity to 6,000 MTPA; it said FY26 was harder yet grew 22%.

qa_highlights.question: How does the spooling business differ from Ratnamani's, and could it enter nuclear spooling?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Ratnamani focuses on nuclear spooling, while Venus targets data-center spooling. Nuclear entry has limitations but is a possible long-term goal. It declined to give a margin estimate.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the BHEL order flow?

PAT rose 19.4% to INR47 crore, the company's highest-ever Q1 profit in absolute terms. Management held MRPs flat and absorbed minimum wage and input cost inflation through sourcing, supply chain and retail efficiencies. E-commerce declined as management refused to match marketplace deep discounting, and online share of revenue fell to 22% from 30%. Management described the e-commerce dip as a one-off, but gave no quantified guidance.

financial_highlights.change: Analyst cited >200 bps improvement; management attributed it to retail margins, operating leverage and supply chain
down from around INR28 crore in Q1 FY26, due to lower e-commerce platform rebates

segments.name: Footwear
segments.commentary: 56% of Q1 turnover; management says footwear carries Q1 and Q2 while apparel peaks in Q3 and Q4. Open footwear ASPs improved sequentially.

segments.name: Apparel
segments.commentary: 39% of Q1 turnover; seasonally stronger in Q3 and Q4. Category-wise YoY growth not disclosed.

segments.name: Accessories
segments.commentary: 5% of Q1 turnover. Sunglasses are in about 80% of stores; hard luggage in only 10-15% of stores as the category has shifted online.

segments.name: E-commerce
segments.commentary: Declined YoY because management declined incremental marketplace discounting. Online share fell to 22% from 30%. Management aspires to return to 30%.

segments.name: Core India retail
segments.commentary: Softer early in the quarter, improved as the quarter progressed. Management credits store-led model and better product/category mix for margin gains.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: UAE franchise stores were hit early in the quarter and recovered in the last month. UK master distributor Style Label Manchester appointed; transactions started. No export revenue guidance given.

segments.name: Sprandi (new brand)
segments.commentary: Sports brand acquired in April 2026 for India, Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan, Sri Lanka and other countries. Shoes first, then apparel. Launch in India online and retail by end-September 2026.

guidance_outlook: Store additions: 33 opened in Q1 FY27; aspiration of about 150 (150-plus) by FY27 end, versus an earlier 200-250 aspiration. Management says it will 'remain close to that number'.
EBITDA margin to be kept stable at around 20% for the year; management also expressed aspiration to increase margins.
Revenue growth: management hopes to continue the growth rate of the last 3-4 years; no quantified FY27 guidance.
E-commerce share expected to recover towards 30% of revenue; management called the Q1 dip a one-off.
Inventory target to reduce from 173 days to 150 days. Inventory build-up expected in Q2 ahead of festive season.
No MRP increases planned; management aims to offset cost inflation through efficiencies.
capex_capacity: New stores: 33 opened in Q1 FY27, with an aspiration of about 150 for FY27. Ramp-up takes 45-50 days for a 1,000 sq ft store and about 75 days for a 3,000-4,000 sq ft store.
New store formats are mostly 800-1,500 sq ft, as expansion into South, East and West India is more store-count intensive.
Store in Forum Mall, Kolkata opened; malls to be used where they are stronger than high streets, particularly in South and West India.
Inventory at 173 days; Q2 build-up expected, then reduction in Q3 and Q4.
No acquisitions in the pipeline at present; management is open to opportunities in footwear and apparel.
demand_pricing: Demand was soft early in Q1 due to macro headwinds and cautious consumer spending, then improved through the quarter.

Marketplaces pushed higher discounting; Redtape declined to match beyond levels it considered appropriate for the brand. Management said there is no fixed discount ceiling and that it decides event by event (for example BBD).

ASPs rose sequentially across footwear and apparel from product and category mix, not broad-based price hikes. MRPs were held flat despite minimum wage and input cost inflation linked to the ongoing war.
Management declined to quantify inflation, calling it 'a regular business'.
Non-BIS inventory remains; the industry has an extension of one year, with management expecting a further extension.
A September 2025 income tax search is ongoing; management says no material claim or risk has been identified so far.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the e-commerce weakness, and what is the discount level beyond which Redtape will not participate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the decline was a deliberate choice, not a structural weakness. It declined to set a fixed discount threshold, saying it depends on event size and margin impact, and that it expects e-commerce to recover.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inflation burden and will price hikes follow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said minimum wage and war-related costs were absorbed, MRPs were not raised, and it would not quantify the inflation as it is a regular business.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reason for the lower other income?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Vivek Agnihotri said lower e-commerce platform rebates cut other income to around INR8-9 crore from about INR28 crore in the prior-year quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin improvement above 200 bps?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said retail margins were stronger, with operating leverage and an optimised supply chain. No category-level margin split was given.

qa_highlights.question: Does Q1 margin mean moderation is likely for the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the intent is to keep margins intact and aspire to improve them, while noting that it will not sacrifice margins for top-line growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the income tax search from September 2025?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the process is ongoing and could take 2-3 years, with no material claim or risk identified to date.

risks_watch: E-commerce recovery to 30% of revenue is an aspiration; online share is 22% and management gave no timeline or quantified discount threshold, and the Q1 dip could persist into the BBD/festive season if marketplace discounting stays deep.

Margin stability: management aims to hold EBITDA margin around 20% and gross margin gains (>200 bps per analyst) were attributed mainly to retail margins without a category-level split, so sustainability is unverified.

Inflation exposure: minimum wage hikes in manufacturing states and war-linked input costs were absorbed without MRP increases; no quantification given, so a squeeze on margins if efficiencies fade is a watch item.
Store rollout: 33 stores opened in Q1 versus a FY27 aspiration of about 150-plus (earlier 200-250); new 800-1,500 sq ft formats in South, East and West India may ramp more slowly.
Inventory at 173 days with a Q2 build-up planned ahead of festive season; reduction to 150 days targeted, and non-BIS inventory remains outstanding.

Income tax search (September 2025) ongoing; management said it could take 2-3 years, with no material claim identified so far. Other income fell to INR8-9 crore from about INR28 crore on lower e-commerce rebates.
key_quotes: So we don't see this as a weakness. The degrowth in e-commerce was largely a conscious outcome of our channel strategy during the quarter.
We would like to believe it's a one-off thing.
Not really. It's a regular business for us.
We would like to remain as it is now. We'd like to be stable.
But as of now there's been no claim of any material and there's no risk of any material.

543959|2026-06.headline: SBFC Q1 FY27: PAT rose 29% YoY to INR 130 crores and spreads widened 39 bps QoQ to 9.48%, while 0+ DPD rose 70 bps and AUM grew 6% QoQ.
543959|2026-06.overview: AUM reached INR 11,922 crores (up 27% YoY, 6% QoQ), with MSME AUM at INR 9,271 crores and gold loan AUM at INR 2,631 crores. Spreads improved to 9.48% and NIM to 10.6%, helped by a 90 bps YoY drop in cost of borrowing to 8.42%. Management cited headwinds: lower gold-loan eligibility after April 1, 2026 rules, a regulatory cap on bank collateral for sub-20 lakh MSME tickets that hit co-origination, and softer login-to-disbursal conversion (34% vs 42%). Asset quality weakened QoQ, with 0+ DPD up 70 bps and GNPA at 2.66%, but Stage 2 ECL was raised to 16% from 6% and total provisioning reached 1.91% of assets.

financial_highlights.change: up by similar bps as spread (QoQ)
Stage 2 ECL raised to 16% from 6%; about 2x regulatory minimum

segments.name: MSME / small-ticket LAP
segments.commentary: MSME AUM INR 9,271 crores (+4.5% QoQ) and disbursements INR 809 crores (+3% QoQ). Co-origination, about 20% of disbursals and book, reset to about 10% after RBI collateral rule for sub-20 lakh MSME tickets; management expects a return to usual run rate from this quarter.

segments.name: Gold loan
segments.commentary: AUM INR 2,631 crores (+11% QoQ). Gold yields rose in the quarter and were the main driver of the 29 bps QoQ yield increase; management expects gold yields to stay range-bound, with at most a marginal decline.

guidance_outlook: Opex to average AUM to fall 25 bps in FY27 (reiterated), and to be closer to 4% or below by year-end as new branches mature.
Credit cost expected at 1.4%-1.5% for at least the next two quarters; Q1 was 1.45%.
Yield expected to stabilise in the 17.50%-17.75% range; spreads to be held above 9%.
Cost of borrowing expected to stabilise at current levels after upfronting borrowings and liquidity build-up.
Branch expansion limited to 10-15 in FY27, after 5 branches added in Q1 (total 256), with further expansion tied to returns from recent branches.

capex_capacity: Branch count 256 as of June 2026 after adding five in Q1; roughly 52 branches opened over the last year, with the bulk in H2 FY26.
Plan for FY27 is 10-15 new branches, with expansion gated on profitability of recently opened branches.
Closing liquidity INR 1,864 crores; management intends to hold higher liquidity as it grows toward INR 15,000 crores AUM.
Capital adequacy ratio 32%; tangible net worth INR 3,613 crores.
demand_pricing: Login-to-disbursal conversion fell to 34% from 42%; management expects it to hold near 35% as higher logins and co-origination recover.

Sub-10 lakh household segment showing leveraged stress; CIBIL scores above 700 for about 90% of the portfolio, but eligibility is the binding constraint.
Competitors pricing aggressively or offering larger loan amounts; management chose to walk away from some business to protect spreads.
Gold-loan eligibility norms reset from April 1, 2026, and falling gold prices reduced the loan amount reaching customers.

qa_highlights.question: Where is the sub-10 lakh segment in its credit cycle, and how does that affect FY27 growth and profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said conditions there have not improved and it is watchful. Aseem Dhru cited household DSR near 14% per CLSA, and said the company does not know whether it is early or mid-cycle.

qa_highlights.question: Will SBFC add new products in the next 12-18 months beyond small-ticket LAP and gold loans?

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Increments were rolled out, and about 20-25 branches opened in Q4 FY26 plus 5 in Q1 brought their full-year staff costs into this quarter. Cost to AUM should fall as those branches mature over the next nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Was the 30 bps yield increase driven by higher risk-taking?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanket Agrawal said gold yields rose this quarter, adding to the yield improvement. Company yield is expected to stabilise at 17.50%-17.75%, with spreads held above 9%.

qa_highlights.question: Is credit cost stable at about 1.4% for the full year?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management expects credit cost of 1.4%-1.5% for at least the next two quarters; Q1 was 1.45%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for incremental yield and gold yields?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental yield is in the same 17.50%-17.75% range, slightly up because of gold. Gold yields are expected to be range-bound with at most a marginal fall; the recent 25-30 bps rise should not be extrapolated.

So, we don't want to, at this stage look at anything different or new.

543959|2026-09.headline: SBFC Q2 FY27 PAT rose 27% YoY to INR 139 crore, with ROE at 15.04% and AUM up 27% YoY to INR 12,592 crore.
543959|2026-09.overview: SBFC reported its 36th consecutive quarter of sequential AUM and profit growth, with AUM at INR 12,592 crore (up 6% QoQ, 27% YoY) and PAT of INR 139 crore (up 7% QoQ, 27% YoY). Credit cost eased to 1.37% from 1.44% and Opex fell to 4.07%, while spreads widened to 9.63%. Management said the gold-loan delinquency rise after the RBI circular was the main source of higher Stage 2 assets, and that the MSME book has stabilised rather than improved. Management kept its 5-7% quarterly AUM growth guidance and warned against treating 9.6% spreads as a new norm.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME AUM INR 9,669 crore (77% of AUM), up 18% YoY and 4.3% QoQ; on-book grew 20% and co-origination 10%. MSME disbursements INR 855 crore, up 6% QoQ, the third straight quarter of growth.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan AUM INR 2,906 crore (about 23% of AUM); added INR 275 crore in Q2, roughly INR 40 lakh net growth per branch per month across 236 gold branches. Management is deliberately cautious on volume and LTV expansion.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guided at 5-7% per quarter going forward; management said MSME disbursements should grow in double digits second-half over second-half.
Opex expected to fall by a further 25 bps in FY27, with a further reduction over the next two quarters.
Spread guided around 9-9.25%, but management asked investors not to model 9.6% as the norm due to rising gold competition and likely pricing rationalisation.
Credit cost seen stabilising at around 1.37% or marginally lower unless El Nino or state waivers materially change the outlook; 1.45% in Q1 described as likely peak.
Capital sufficient to an AUM of about INR 20,000 crore before the next capital raise; ROE expansion expected as leverage rises.
PLR raised 25 bps in October 2026; management expects spreads to hold as variable-rate MSME assets reprice.
CARE and India Ratings revised outlook from stable to positive.
capex_capacity: Branch count 257 as of September 2026 (1 added in Q2, 6 in H1); 236 branches do gold loans.
Collection team about 850 including supervisors (about 700 front-end), up 150-200 in the period.
LCR at 194%; closing liquidity INR 1,782 crore in Q2 versus INR 1,864 crore in Q1.
AI voice ran the first full pre-due collection cycle in October: more than 4 lakh calls to 35,000 accounts, 84% reached, 53% paid, replacing roughly a 60-person team.
demand_pricing: Banks are moving to higher-ticket prime borrowers at single-digit pricing, leaving INR 10-25 lakh and INR 25+ lakh MSME segments with headroom for SBFC.
Sub-INR 7 lakh book is being run down and is no longer originated; it is under 6% of AUM per management.
Gold competition rising as large players open branches; gold yields range 18-21%, with management expecting roughly 23% and possibly 25%.
Co-origination rose to INR 112 crore from INR 78 crore in Q1.
Management expects MSME disbursements to stabilise and grow; Q2 was the highest disbursement level in the MSME business since listing per management.

qa_highlights.question: Gold loan stress and how the industry is positioned, given larger players entering gold.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not chase high-volume gold growth, as it expects pricing to be compromised; it said gold yields are 18-21% and competition has risen in the last 1-1.5 months, with some large players opening 500-1,000 branches.

qa_highlights.question: Why slippages (GS2+GS3) rose QoQ, and whether the ARC sale was gold or MSME.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the rise in Stage 2 is entirely from gold loans after the RBI circular reset scheme design, as customers move from bullet to monthly interest payments. The ARC sale was a lower-ticket vintage LAP portfolio; no gold loans were sold.

qa_highlights.question: Gold price sensitivity and LTV risk.
qa_highlights.answer: LTV fell to 67% from about 70% last quarter (versus about 60s in June 2025). Auctions are triggered after 85-90% LTV and delinquency, with a 7-30 day window per management; out-of-money risk described as not significant.

qa_highlights.question: Timing of MSME disbursement pick-up.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the repositioning is done and restaffing is complete in most locations; it expects second-half over second-half disbursement growth of at least double digits.

qa_highlights.question: Steady-state 0+ DPD and credit cost.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 0+ rose from around 7% to above 9% and is now stabilising; it expects 0+ to hold in the 8-9.2% range, not return to 7%, and credit cost to stabilise near 1.37%.

qa_highlights.question: Whether 4.5% ROA can be sustained as guidance.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ROA has held above 4.5% for 7-8 quarters despite higher leverage; holding 4.6% over the long run will be difficult, but it should hold in the short term.

qa_highlights.question: Collection headcount and bandwidth.
qa_highlights.answer: About 700 front-end collectors and 850 including supervisors; average caseload of 40-45 per collector, varying from 25-30 in Assam to about 50 in South India.

risks_watch: Gold: competitive pricing pressure, possible yield compression, and a possible fall in gold prices (LTV fell to 67%; October saw a drop).
El Nino and drought: rainfall deficit concentrated in Karnataka and Maharashtra; state-level waivers could affect repayment behaviour.
Rising rates: 25 bps repo hike and cost of funds expected to rise; management expects spreads to hold, but pass-through of MCLR-linked debt is still to come.
Draft regulatory circular that management said may affect profitability.
Stage 2 and 0+ DPD trends, with 0+ above 9% versus about 7% historically; track whether they keep stabilising in Q3.

segments.name: Formulations

API:formulation mix expected around 80:20 with a plus or minus 2-3% range.

Working capital intensity expected to be in line with historical levels; inventory days should normalise in FY27 H1.

Unit 4 expected to reach breakeven by next year.
Four units support peak revenue potential of about INR 3,000 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins not improve in Q4 and what is the GST drag and lease accounting?

qa_highlights.question: Shrinjana Mittal (MS Capital): Is upper upscale underperforming midscale because of downtrading, and why is GST drag above 2%?

qa_highlights.question: Vaibhav Muley (Haitong): Why did F&B growth slow to about 4%, and what is the GIC partnership scope?

Management moved some high working-capital banks' customers to other banks to prioritise cash flow, which slows program fees. Management said it is not moving away from the 40% consolidated guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Will management give EBITDA margin guidance, and how should margins trend from here?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin is about 8.2% and it will guide on margin in coming quarters once DICE revenue kicks in. About INR3 crore of DICE cost came in over the last two months of Q1 with no revenue, since revenue starts July 1.

qa_highlights.question: What were the expensed items that were previously capitalised, and why are they only partly expensed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no selective capitalisation; the company is moving toward expensing more over time, subject to auditor agreement. One immediate client-required product cost about INR6 crore was fully expensed in Q1, and some infra and product development costs are involved.

qa_highlights.question: Has DICE payment-rail integration been completed and will payments revenue come from DICE from Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Majority of integration is done; the last part is due by August 31 or at latest September 10. Management said payments-related DICE revenue from Q3 is certain.

qa_highlights.question: What is revenue per customer, and what is the program fee growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue per customer is about INR10.6 lakh (INR423 crore over about 4,000 customers). Management called the roughly 10% program fee growth 'by design' and said it expects improvement in coming months, with cash flow and calibrated capitalisation prioritised over the program fee number.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 13-15% EBITDA margin target still stand, and when will margins stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins have been in the 9-10% range for the last eight quarters and the 14-15% target is a 5-7 year aspiration. Cash flow turnaround to positive would take about 15-18 months.

qa_highlights.question: When will AI become a meaningful revenue driver, and what is the DICE revenue outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said internal AI use helped cut about 12.5% of the FY26 cost base and reduced feature launch timelines by up to 50%. DICE FY26 revenue was about INR12 crore; FY27 target is INR15-16 crore at 90%+ gross margin.

544009|2026-03.headline: Blue Jet FY26 revenue fell 8% to INR947 crores on PI/API destocking, while Q4 contrast media revenue rose 91% YoY to INR193 crores.

544009|2026-06.headline: Blue Jet Q1 FY27 revenue rose 25% QoQ to INR293 crore and EBITDA hit INR98 crore, with PI/API restart offset by INR30 crore contrast media goods in transit.

qa_highlights.question: Is the cost-to-income decline sustainable and can it fall below 60%?

qa_highlights.question: What is the CASA outlook and cost of funds risk from rate hikes?

qa_highlights.question: Will the guarantee scheme cover the full book and what if it does not?

qa_highlights.question: Why is gold loan and micro LAP flat, and when will growth pick up?

qa_highlights.question: Any risks to achieving 100% PAT growth guidance?

qa_highlights.question: How will NIM move in H2 amid rising rates?

qa_highlights.question: What is the growth outlook by segment and do drought and geopolitical risks affect the book?

544119|2026-03.headline: Rashi Peripherals Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 51% YoY to INR 4,489 crores, with PAT up 65% to INR 87 crores.
544119|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue from operations grew 51% YoY to INR 4,489 crores, EBITDA rose 41% with margin at 2.95%, and PAT grew 65% to INR 87 crores (1.93% margin). For FY26, revenue grew 15% to INR 15,827 crores, EBITDA rose 53% to INR 459 crores (2.90% margin, up 72 bps), and PAT rose 35% to INR 282 crores. Management attributed H2 growth mainly to price increases in the PES category, with H1 growth driven by volume and customer additions. Management guided to a ~20% CAGR and said the PC super cycle could last another 1-2 years, while flagging a possible 5-10% unit decline in CY26 and H2 consumer softness.

segments.name: Semiconductor

Working capital days expected to stay in a similar range in FY27 (CFO).

Management said demand is not softening currently; affordability risk in consumer segment in H2.

qa_highlights.question: How much of top-line growth came from pricing vs volume, and what is normalised growth for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Price increases were minimal in H1 and substantial in H2; H2 growth of 46-47% H2-on-H2 included about 20-22 points from price. Management reiterated 20% CAGR for 20 years and expects to maintain it.

qa_highlights.question: What is a PC classified as an AI PC, and how big is that segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Devices with an NPU or high-end processors/GPUs capable of AI workloads; about 25% of PCs and notebooks sold in India are AI PCs, expected to grow further over 1-2 years, lifting ASPs.

qa_highlights.question: Is refresh demand being delayed by price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Some corporates extended refresh cycles initially, but the trend is reversing as buyers realise delay could cost 30-40% more; refresh expected to normalise as in prior years.

qa_highlights.question: Does the semiconductor business carry high working capital, and when will it affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital is higher (100-plus days cited), but gross margins and ROCE are higher than the regular business; the business is small, so meaningful margin impact is a few years away.

qa_highlights.question: How will RP Tech participate in AI data centre projects given capital needs and lower margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Funnels of about INR 20,000-25,000 crores are under consideration; the company will pick projects selectively on ROI without compromising 15-20% regular growth; margins vary by project.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of revenue from large deals, enterprise and core distribution?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 had no large AI deals (only INR 5-15 crore deals); enterprise non-AI growth is high, driven by NVIDIA solutions; growth ex-Yotta was 31%.

qa_highlights.question: How does the ST Finserv channel finance programme affect working capital and credit risk?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a non-recourse channel finance programme for channel partners; the company bears no credit risk or funding cost unless it draws funds early, which it normally does not.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PAT margin aspiration, and what caused the Q4 gross margin dip?

544119|2026-06.headline: Rashi Peripherals Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 62% YoY to Rs 5,102 crore, with PAT up 69% to Rs 105 crore and ROCE near 19.5%.
544119|2026-06.overview: Management reported record consolidated revenue, EBITDA, PAT and annualised ROCE for the quarter ended June 2026, driven by price increases in memory, storage and CPUs plus a rise in unit volume. Management said about 30-35% of the revenue growth came from price, 20-25% from quantity, 5-10% from new products and brands, and about 10% from market share gains. Pillars cited were the core distribution engine, the VDA Infosolutions acquisition (67% stake) and a semiconductor JV with Restar Japan (74:26). Management guided to similar growth in Q2 but a slower pace of price increases.

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited economic strength, digitisation and education focus, plus data centre-related demand; commercial demand is holding up while consumer demand is slowing on affordability.

qa_highlights.question: Split of Q1 growth between price, volume and mix?

qa_highlights.question: Is there a supply constraint risk in H2?

qa_highlights.question: Why not pursue large AI data centre deals aggressively?

qa_highlights.question: How will FY28 look after the tailwinds fade?

NIM improved to 4.21% from 4.06% a year ago, helped by deposit repricing and a higher average CD ratio of 83%. Asset quality improved, with GNPA at 2.47% and NNPA at 1.14%, as the bank raised PCR to 54.5%. Management guided to stable NIM near 4.2% for FY27, ROA of 1.35-1.4% for FY27, and 22% advance growth.

broadly in line with last year

qa_highlights.question: Why PCR has been rising over recent quarters and whether it will stay stable

qa_highlights.question: Headroom for cost of deposit repricing and ROA path

qa_highlights.question: What keeps NIM stable at around 4.2% given cost-of-deposit and yield pressure
