Three Tritium products (TRI-FLEX inverter and two others) launching May-July 2026; management cites about INR 850 crores of combined FY28 revenue potential, subject to pilots. TRI-FLEX hyperscaler factory acceptance test ongoing, potentially $30-35 million FY28 revenue.
Gurgaon production to shift majority to Hyderabad over the next 2-3 months; inventory build expected to normalise over coming quarters.

Additional open opportunities of about INR 400 crores beyond the INR 1,000 crore Critical Power order book, including about INR 100 crores of new BharatNet tenders and about INR 150 crores of uncovered-village Phase-2.
capex_capacity: Hyderabad plant (newly inaugurated early March 2026) became fully operational in Q4 FY26 after Q3 trials; added depreciation is reflected in Q4 numbers.
Gurgaon plant still running; majority of production to move to Hyderabad over the next 2-3 months, with some production retained in Gurgaon.
Tritium manufacturing in Tennessee, US; R&D in Brisbane, Australia; Exicom R&D in Gurgaon (hardware) and Bangalore (software), with 130+ engineers.
Ring-topology PC charger: first pilot in Q4 FY26, mass production planned in FY27.
Exicom One: 80 sites executed in Q4 under this integrated products-and-services program.
demand_pricing: Critical Power pricing on BharatNet and other government contracts is fixed, so Q4 contribution margin was slightly below Q3 due to input cost increases from forex, commodities and geopolitical factors.
Management said large high-volume orders (e.g. a DC power system order above INR 100 crores with a leading Indian telco) help offset input cost inflation.
Standalone gross margin expanded to 27% on richer EVSE mix and fewer low-margin lithium battery sales.
EV demand: FY26 described as a record year with monthly EV sales above 200,000 across categories; electric car penetration cited as 5% and three-wheeler penetration 32%.

Competition noted in BESS and the market was described as large and competitive; BESS cell supply is import-dependent (China) until local cell manufacturing arrives, expected next year or the year after.

qa_highlights.question: What charging infrastructure is needed for commercial EV adoption and where is it happening?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said adoption is in fixed-route captive use such as ports, cement distribution and mining with 200-300 trucks; intercity commercial electrification is still about two years away.

qa_highlights.question: What is the product and revenue potential of the TRI-FLEX inverter and its applications?
qa_highlights.answer: TRI-FLEX converts grid power to high-voltage DC for DC microgrids, BESS integration and 800V data centres. A hyperscaler pilot is in testing and, if successful, could unlock significant FY28 revenue ($30-35 million cited).

qa_highlights.question: How will the company win customers for the two other new Tritium products in the US and Europe?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said development was done with existing strategic customers, and it has line of sight to long-term contracts once pilots succeed.

qa_highlights.question: Does Exicom have OEM tie-ups for supplying chargers with vehicles?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Exicom is the largest home charger maker, with about a 50% chance a new EV in India comes with an Exicom charger, and it has OEM partnerships for home and fast chargers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the BESS offering and its scaling path over 3-5 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it targets commercial and industrial modular BESS, not utility, transmission, distribution or home. About 10-20 small projects were deployed in Q4, with an FY26 target above INR 50 crores, and BESS could reach about 30% of Critical Power over 2-3 years.

risks_watch: Consolidated FY26 EBITDA -INR 103 crores and adjusted PAT -INR 258 crores; breakeven depends on Tritium reaching 3x revenue and EBITDA breakeven in Q4 FY27.
Tritium margin normalisation as low-cost acquired inventory is consumed after about one quarter.
Working capital: inventory build from parallel Gurgaon and Hyderabad operations and higher receivables; collections and normalisation to be tracked.
Input cost inflation (forex, commodities, geopolitics) against fixed-price government BharatNet contracts.
Telecom tower installations slipped slightly in Q4; Critical Power demand depends on telco capex.
New Tritium products depend on hyperscaler pilot success and multi-month launch timelines (May-July 2026).
BESS cell supply dependent on imports until local cell manufacturing arrives.
544133|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, EVSE momentum and Tritium turnaround, while cautious on near-term Tritium margins, working capital and geopolitical or supply-chain headwinds. The CFO was less specific on the reasons for the full-year PAT loss and on receivables quality.
key_quotes: This reflects better product mix, sharper execution and Tritium beginning to scale commercially.
But we are firmly on our path for EBITDA breakeven at Tritium in Quarter 4 of FY '27 and the 3x revenue growth paved the way for it.
This is by design. We are stocking up both facilities to ensure smooth production continuity during this transition and to support an order book we are seeing in FY'27.

544133|2026-06.headline: Exicom Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 57% YoY to INR237 crore with EBITDA margin at 8.8%; consolidated EBITDA loss narrowed to INR22 crore.
544133|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 57% YoY to INR236.8 crore, with Critical Power up 80% to INR176 crore and EV up 15% to INR61 crore. Standalone EBITDA more than doubled to INR20.9 crore (8.8% margin), helped by operating leverage and richer mix. Consolidated revenue rose 61% to INR331.1 crore, but consolidated EBITDA was a loss of INR21.9 crore (down from INR38.6 crore loss), as Tritium margins normalised after drawing down low-cost acquired inventory. Management guided to consolidated EBITDA breakeven within two quarters and Tritium breakeven by Q4 FY27, while working capital rose on parallel Gurgaon and Hyderabad plant operations and higher receivables.

segments.name: Critical Power (standalone)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR176-177 crore, up 73-80% YoY and down ~11% QoQ; BharatNet is among the largest contributors, with a 60% share in that project per management. Export sales about INR15 crore (~8% of Critical Power).

segments.name: EV Charging (standalone)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR61 crore, up 15% YoY but down QoQ from Q4 DC-charger pull-forward; consolidated EV grew 50%. FY26 standalone EV revenue was INR277 crore, about 30% of total.

segments.name: Tritium (consolidated, US DC fast charging)
segments.commentary: Revenue about USD10-10.5 million in Q1, second consecutive quarter above USD10 million; bookings about USD20.8-21 million, roughly double the usual ~USD10 million per quarter.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated EBITDA breakeven expected within the next two quarters (management could not specify Q2 or Q3).
Tritium EBITDA breakeven targeted by Q4 FY27, with 3x revenue growth versus last year targeted.
Standalone Critical Power exports targeted to rise from ~8% to ~15% of Critical Power sales within FY27.
AC charger monthly run rate expected to rise ~50% over the next three months.
Parallel-run fixed costs (~INR8.7 crore in Q1) expected to phase out as Gurgaon transition completes over coming quarters.
Tritium large strategic contracts (USD20-30 million for CY27 from Fortune 100 trials, USD20 million GRID-FLEX from hyperscaler) contingent on trial success.
capex_capacity: Hyderabad plant commissioned in Q4 FY26 and fully in production in Q1 FY27; management says it gives 3x production capability versus Gurgaon.
Standalone depreciation rose ~67% YoY, and management said standalone D&A increase was INR10-12 crore.
Management said DC charger utilisation is ~65% (90-100% for DC power system lines), AC charger ~100%, and PCBA and battery lines ~100%.
Ordered an additional AC charger line; management said the Hyderabad plant was built for ~2x AC capacity.
Tritium US factory capacity is about USD100 million a year versus ~USD10 million current quarterly revenue run rate (about one-quarter utilised).
demand_pricing: Critical Power order book ~INR1,000 crore; consolidated order book INR1,400 crore-plus as of 30 June 2026.
Large DC power system order of INR85 crore from a leading Indian telco; supply agreement with a large tower company for power systems and batteries.
BharatNet: INR700 crore open orders plus ~INR800 crore of service orders over 10 years; BSNL Phase 2 expected ~2,000 sites at INR90-100 crore.
BESS (commercial and industrial, mostly under 0.5 MWh): ~15 MWh orders worth ~INR20 crore in hand and ~34 MWh (INR45 crore) in advanced pipeline.
EV charger order book about INR200 crore for AC/DC chargers in India plus ~USD2 million export orders; 10 new export countries won; 15 new network operators added in Q1.
Margins on some large orders were hit by forex and commodity price increases, partly offset by volumes.
Supply disruptions in semiconductors, plastics and copper were cited as the main constraint, not capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Consolidated EBITDA swung from breakeven in Q4 FY26 to a INR22 crore loss in Q1; what drove the sequential drop and when does breakeven return?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Q4 seasonality in Indian business and Tritium's low-cost acquired inventory eroding, lowering Tritium margins. It still expects Tritium EBITDA breakeven in Q4 FY27 and consolidated breakeven within the next two quarters, without specifying Q2 or Q3.

qa_highlights.question: When will Tritium's doubled order intake convert to revenue, and is the 3x growth and Q4 FY27 breakeven target still intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the USD20 million backlog as of 1 July plus new bookings and large strategic wins (double-digit million dollars, executing from calendar 2027 Q1) give confidence in 3x revenue growth and Q4 FY27 EBITDA breakeven.

qa_highlights.question: What is Hyderabad plant utilisation and where will it reach in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Hyderabad was built for about 2x AC charger capacity and roughly 4,000 DC chargers. Utilisation is about 65% on DC chargers, close to 100% on AC chargers, 90-100% on DC power system lines, and close to 100% on PCBA and battery lines. AC charger monthly run rate is expected to rise about 50% over the next three months, and another AC line has been ordered.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the EV revenue mix and growth outlook, and why is the AC capacity figure inconsistent with the annual report (42,000 to 222,000 units)?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 standalone EV revenue was INR277 crore, about 30% of revenue, with mix expected to stay similar or rise slightly. Management said the 222,000 figure is right and that 48,000 was single-shift, with the doubling based on double-shift operation; it will revert with an exact answer.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone depreciation rise, and what is the Tritium capitalisation impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone depreciation rose about 67% YoY to INR10.3 crore, with management attributing an increase of INR10-12 crore to the new plant. Tritium's higher depreciation reflects capitalised R&D and acquisition-related servicing costs, which management expects to be amortised over 5-7 years.

qa_highlights.question: Can EV charger market share and unit volumes be estimated from EV registrations, and why was standalone EV growth only 15% when AC demand is strong?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has a very high share of wallbox chargers but not portable chargers, and volume depends on whether OEMs bundle wallboxes. Its DRHP cited 60% wallbox share, and it estimates current wallbox share at north of 50%. The 15% standalone EV growth reflects Q4 DC charger pull-forward; AC may have grown about 30% and DC about 10%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US Tritium factory capacity and utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the US factory can service about USD100 million a year, about 2.5x the current ~USD10 million quarterly revenue, and it is running at about one-quarter of that today due to the ongoing turnaround.

risks_watch: Consolidated EBITDA breakeven timing is not pinned down (Q2 or Q3 FY27), and Tritium breakeven is targeted only for Q4 FY27; the Tritium margin cushion from acquired low-cost inventory has already eroded.
Tritium strategic contracts (USD20-30 million for CY27 from Fortune 100 trials, USD20 million GRID-FLEX) are contingent on trial success and calendar 2026 conversion.

Working capital pressure from parallel Gurgaon and Hyderabad operations: elevated inventory and receivables, plus ~INR8.7 crore of Q1 parallel-run fixed costs expected to phase out over coming quarters.
Margin pressure from forex, commodity and US-led input cost increases on large orders, and supply disruption in semiconductors, plastics and copper.
Depreciation step-up (standalone +67% YoY, consolidated +57%) will weigh on PAT until plant utilisation and Tritium revenue scale.
Unresolved query on AC charger capacity figures (42,000 vs 222,000 units vs 2x expansion); management to revert with an exact answer.
Shift in EV growth from DC to AC chargers and reliance on Q4 pull-forward; watch whether standalone EV growth accelerates beyond 15% YoY.
key_quotes: So the overall performance on a stand-alone revenue rose by 57% year-on-year to INR237 crores and our EBITDA more than doubled to INR21 crores lifting the EBITDA margins to 8.8%.
But on a consolidated basis, the breakeven may be over the next 2 quarters itself. I can't specify whether quarter 2 or 3.
Some of the challenges today is not capacity, it's supply chain disruption.
So I think it's just a timing issue. But this growth is not 1x. It's continuing.
544133|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on order book, Tritium turnaround and the Hyderabad capacity build-out, but cautious on timing, as management repeatedly declined to specify exact quarters for breakeven. Some answers were loose or deflected (for example the capacity-figure reconciliation and blended EV market share), with the management promising to revert.

544134|2026-06.headline: Platinum Industries Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue fell to INR 108.9 crore (from INR 115.4 crore) and PAT to INR 11.13 crore as Palghar ramp-up weighed.
544134|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue declined about 5.6% YoY to INR 108.9 crore while EBITDA fell to INR 13.44 crore at a 12.34% margin, versus INR 15.16 crore at 13.14% a year earlier. Standalone revenue grew about 7.3% YoY to INR 110.4 crore, but standalone EBITDA margin was 11.64%. The expanded Palghar facility only became fully operational on 21 May 2026, so the quarter carried ramp-up costs and lower lead-free PVC offtake. Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth of 30-40% and kept Egypt commercial production targeted before 31 December 2026.

segments.commentary: Margin currently about 18% against a target of 20-21% by Q4 FY27, which management says depends on demand recovery and local raw material sourcing. Gross margin in CPVC has risen from 6-7% to 17-18%, per management.

segments.commentary: Q1 offtake was lower, which management cited as the main reason for the margin decline because this is a high-margin product. Management names Baerlocher and Reagens as main competitors in lead-free.

segments.commentary: Q1 revenue about INR 5.3 crore. FY27 target of INR 65-70 crore per management, with INR 150-200 crore targeted over three years. Seed marketing is via CDMO, with exports to Malaysia and Turkey, and own manufacturing is planned in about 1.5 years.

segments.commentary: Business model still being defined. Some revenue began this quarter, with collaborations with overseas companies under negotiation. No figure given.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of 30-40% reiterated, though management said the Egypt contribution is now lower than earlier planned.
Egypt revenue for FY27 cut to INR 30-35 crore from an earlier INR 50-60 crore estimate.
EBITDA margin guidance of 13-15% and PAT margin of 11-12% for coming months, reaffirmed from the previous call.
Egypt plant (60,000 tpa, about INR 67-68 crore capex) to start commercial production before 31 December 2026; Egypt top line of INR 250-300 crore over three years.

Stearates plant (6,000 tpa) now expected September/October 2026 versus earlier August, due to an equipment delay.
Oleo FY27 revenue INR 65-70 crore (management), vs analyst question of INR 55-60 crore; management said it was 'very positive'.

Total Indian capacity expected to reach 85,000+ tpa on full ramp-up of the expanded facility.

CPVC: a demand-supply gap exists with supply exceeding demand, so the company pushed sales in Q1. Management expects margin recovery only in Q3 or Q4 FY27.

Raw material supply disrupted by shipping and war-related freight costs; some raw materials bought locally, which pressured margins. Management says the company cannot pass on sudden freight, CFS and transport costs in this environment.
Management said pricing is not under pressure: competitors and the company 'understand the same pricing levels'. Competitors in lead-free: Baerlocher, Reagens; Goldstab mainly lead-based.

Lubrizol/Aditya Birla CPVC resin capacity, plus Reliance and Meghmani resin plans, described by management as complementary to its CPVC additives business. Supply to Supreme and Prince Pipes for 1-2 years.

qa_highlights.question: How did pipe demand look in July and August, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pipe demand degrew in Q1 across pipe companies, picked up from August, and is expected to stay good through December as PVC prices stabilised and turned upward.

qa_highlights.question: What were Oleo sales in Q1 FY27 and can the segment reach INR 55-60 crore by year-end?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 Oleo revenue was about INR 5.3 crore. Management said it is 'very positive' on the year-end target; the analyst's INR 55-60 crore figure was not confirmed, and the INR 65-70 crore FY27 target was given later in the call.

qa_highlights.question: When will CPVC margins recover toward 20-22%?
qa_highlights.answer: CPVC margin is about 18% now and management targets 20-21% by Q4 FY27. Recovery depends on demand, since supply currently exceeds demand, and on local raw material sourcing, which is adding cost.

qa_highlights.question: Volume, price and mix split, new customers, and stabilizer versus specialty volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to share product volume data and suggested the analyst connect offline.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the EBITDA margin is structural versus temporary?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower sales-related expenses, since the company skipped exhibitions in Q1, and lower ECL provisions offset the drop in contribution margin, leaving EBITDA margin impact negligible. Lead-free PVC offtake was lower, which hurt mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the utilisation of the existing stabilizer capacity and the threshold to sustain margins?
qa_highlights.answer: The expanded plant was fully operational only from 21 May 2026, so utilisation is expected to be around 30-35% in Q2 and Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Were there one-off items in other income or forex in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: A forex gain of about INR 1 crore was reflected in other income.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 revenue growth guidance of 30-40% still maintained, and how much Egypt revenue is included?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reaffirmed 30-40% growth for FY27 and said the company is already on track, though demand was weak due to the war. Egypt is only partly included: FY27 Egypt estimate is cut to INR 30-35 crore from INR 50-60 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Oleo revenue potential over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 Oleo target is INR 65-70 crore and the three-year target is INR 150-200 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of Lubrizol and Aditya Birla CPVC resin capacity on Platinum?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the resin capacity is complementary, since additives are about 25% of a CPVC compound and resin about 75%. The company has supplied Supreme and Prince Pipes for 1-2 years, and the transition will take time.

qa_highlights.question: Competitive intensity and pricing pressure in lead-free and CPVC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no direct CPVC additive competition in India apart from one other Indian company. In lead-free, Baerlocher and Reagens are the main competitors, Goldstab is mainly lead-based, and pricing levels are understood by all players.

qa_highlights.question: Margin outlook versus the roughly 23% margins of FY23-FY24?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the change to a mix shift from high-margin lead-free to lower-margin CPVC, which started at a 3-7% contribution margin. Guidance is PAT margin of 11-12% and EBITDA margin of 13-15%, reiterated from the previous call.

qa_highlights.question: Project-wise capex, timelines and revenue potential for Egypt and Palghar?
qa_highlights.answer: Egypt is expected by December 2026, with INR 250-300 crore top line over three years. Palghar peak potential is INR 700-800 crore over three years, and top-line CAGR is about 35% over three years.

qa_highlights.question: What bottlenecks could delay commissioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not expect much delay.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the stearates plant and its effect on revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: The 6,000 tpa stearates plant has slipped to September/October 2026 from August due to a delay in one equipment item. Management said it would not materially affect FY27 revenue growth.

qa_highlights.question: Status of Rivadu Lifesciences pharma and the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Business model is still being defined. Some revenue started this quarter, with collaborations with overseas companies under negotiation. No figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Raw material inflation pass-through and contractual mechanisms?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it can pass on raw material price rises in normal conditions, but in the current war and shipping environment it cannot pass on sudden freight, CFS and transport costs. Lower lead-free PVC offtake was cited as the main Q1 margin driver.

qa_highlights.question: Egypt versus Palghar capex and why revenue potential differs?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is about INR 67 crore for Egypt and INR 71 crore for Palghar. Both have about 60,000 tpa capacity, but Egypt is mainly lead stabilisers, priced at INR 110-150 per kg versus INR 250-300 for CPVC and INR 170-220 for calcium zinc in India.

qa_highlights.question: Incremental working capital needed for Egypt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects roughly a three-month working capital cycle.

qa_highlights.question: Expected margins in Oleo chemicals in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins are expected to rise after the company builds its own manufacturing facility; for now it is using CDMO for seed marketing.

risks_watch: CPVC margin recovery to 20-21% is pinned to Q3-Q4 FY27 and depends on demand that management says has only just picked up from August.
Palghar utilisation of around 30-35% in Q2-Q3 FY27 is low against a capacity expansion of about 60,000 tpa, so fixed costs and depreciation may keep margins under pressure.

544136|2026-03.headline: R K Swamy Q4 FY26 consolidated total income rose about 15% YoY to INR 351.73 crore, with EBITDA up 31.6% to about INR 55 crore.

Profit before exceptional item (labour code impact) rose about 30%, and management said Q4 also saw higher top line, bottom line and margins. The company stated it is investing ahead of client needs in CX centres, a digital video studio, a consulting group and AI tools, while the balance sheet remains debt-free. On the call, management said client budgets are not being cut but commitments may be delayed amid macro and geopolitical volatility.

We are operating at regular EBITDA with an escalated cost.
Once we reach an optimum capacity utilization, I would say that we can expect similar EBITDA, like we are thinking of Steel Cord or something like that in percentage.
We will cap our CAPEX at about INR 200 crore-INR 250 crore every year to give us runway for each year.

544209|2026-09.headline: Bansal Wire posted record Q2 FY27 revenue of Rs 1,308 crore (+24% YoY) and EBITDA of Rs 105 crore, with EBITDA/ton near Rs 8,000 aided partly by inventory gain.
544209|2026-09.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as a record quarter for revenue, EBITDA, PAT and EBITDA per ton, recovering from a Q1 hit from industrial gas disruption and higher input costs. Sales volume was about 1,29,000 tons versus 1,14,609 tons in Q2 FY26, and operating cash flow was Rs 218 crore in the quarter and Rs 339 crore in H1. Management said about Rs 200/ton of EBITDA was a one-time inventory gain and guided to Rs 7,000-7,500/ton for H2. Raw material (wire rod) shortages hit October output, which management said is a short-term issue.

segments.name: IHT / OHT specialty wire
segments.commentary: IHT wire reached positive EBITDA last quarter; management cites Rs 15,000-20,000/ton EBITDA for the specialty wire group. IHT capacity is 9,000 tons, with 6,000 tons OHT being installed to reach 15,000 tons in one to two quarters.

segments.name: Steel tyre cord
segments.commentary: Current capacity about 20,000 tons, with a goal of 2 lakh tons. Pricing is about Rs 130-140/kg. First trial order received in Q2, with a second trial order expected in 10-15 days; commercialisation possible within this year.

segments.name: Bead wire
segments.commentary: Nameplate capacity about 30,000 tons, with 10,000-15,000 tons currently run annually. Management cites Rs 12,000-15,000/ton EBITDA. Approvals not yet started; focus to resume in one to two quarters.

segments.name: LRPC
segments.commentary: Less than 1% of sales. Management said it earns modest margins (about Rs 5,000-8,000/ton typical) due to industry overcapacity.

segments.name: B2C (farming, fencing, poultry)
segments.commentary: About 10-12% of Q2 volumes; management says B2C EBITDA is at least 50% higher than B2B.

guidance_outlook: Volume growth of 20% YoY for H2 FY27 (Q3 and Q4 vs prior-year H2); management said Q1 losses cannot be recovered.
EBITDA per ton guidance of Rs 7,000-7,500/ton for H2 FY27; management said Rs 7,000-8,000/ton is achievable for FY27 barring major geopolitical change.
Operating cash flow target of about Rs 800 crore across FY27 and FY28 combined; about Rs 350 crore already generated in H1 FY27.
Capacity to rise from 6.8 lakh tons to about 8.3 lakh tons by end of next year (60,000 tons Dadri brownfield plus about 90,000 tons Sanand greenfield).
Indicative annual capex of Rs 200-225 crore (also cited as Rs 200-250 crore per year), funded from internal accruals.
Long-term EBITDA/ton target of Rs 8,000-10,000, and above Rs 10,000 as specialty wire scales.
capex_capacity: Dadri: 60,000 tons additional low and high carbon wire capacity, mostly built; capitalisation expected by end of Q3 or Q4 FY27. Also 6,000 tons OHT wire, expected in Q3 or Q4 FY27.

Sanand (southern Gujarat) greenfield: about 90,000 tons of stainless steel and low carbon wire, with about Rs 150 crore capex excluding land (land acquired about a year ago). Some capitalisation expected from next quarter or the quarter after.
CWIP closing balance Rs 177 crore.
Steel tyre cord: 20,000 tons current capacity, with a 2 lakh ton goal; a bigger capex will follow customer approvals.
Management expects 4-5x asset turnover on new capacity.
demand_pricing: Management described demand as healthy across automotive, infra, agriculture, power and transmission, and general engineering. Constraint is raw material supply rather than demand.
Wire rod shortage over the last 1.5-2 months as suppliers shifted output to TMT. Company holds about 1.5 months of inventory; October output was hit at some plants, which management says is now back.
Low carbon was about 55% of volume in Q2 (lower end of 55-60% target), supporting blended margin.
Gas prices are about 2.5x the regular level, passed through to customers. Availability has been stable for about one quarter.

Steel tyre cord India demand is 2.5-3 lakh tons, mostly imported. Management expects radialisation (about 60% in India truck/bus) to drive growth. Management says there is no Indian domestic competitor; Bekaert is the main competitor.
Management says it will cap any single customer at 20-25% of total sales for steel cord.

qa_highlights.question: When will steel tyre cord and IHT/OHT translate into revenue and EBITDA, and what is the EBITDA per ton for specialty wire?
qa_highlights.answer: Steel tyre cord is in trials, with a second trial order expected in 10-15 days and commercialisation possible within the year. Specialty wire EBITDA is about Rs 15,000-20,000/ton, and IHT has turned EBITDA positive.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q2 EBITDA/ton came from inventory gains, and is Rs 7,000-7,500 conservative?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory gain was about Rs 200/ton, so underlying EBITDA was about Rs 7,800-7,900/ton. Management said its own strategy is Rs 7,000-7,500 and it is not guiding above that.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20% volume growth guidance for H2 only, and is it at risk from raw material shortages?
qa_highlights.answer: It applies to H2 FY27, meaning Q3 and Q4 volumes up 20% YoY. Management said raw material shortages are temporary and that lost days can be made up the following month.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of Sanand and Dadri CWIP and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: CWIP is Rs 177 crore, mostly Dadri 60,000 tons. Sanand needs about Rs 150 crore capex excluding land.

qa_highlights.question: Steel cord capacity plan and realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Current capacity is 20,000 tons, the target is 2 lakh tons, and realisation is about Rs 130-140/kg. Management said a major capex will follow customer approvals.

qa_highlights.question: Is Rs 7-7.5/kg the right base for H2 earnings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rs 7,000-7,500/ton is the H2 EBITDA commitment, and a better outcome is possible but not guided.

risks_watch: Raw material (wire rod) availability: shortages in October and supplier breakdowns could cut Q3 and Q4 volumes below the 20% growth guidance.
Gas prices at about 2.5x normal; management says pass-through to customers is in place, but this is a margin risk.
Q2 EBITDA/ton includes about Rs 200/ton inventory gain, so sustainability of the Rs 7,800-8,000 level is uncertain.
Steel cord commercialisation depends on customer approvals; management expects the first two quarters of ramp-up to be slow.
Sanand greenfield and Dadri ramp-up execution; capex may move beyond the stated timelines.
LRPC is loss-making at the margin due to industry overcapacity; management says it is less than 1% of sales.
544209|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on results and guidance, with management saying it prefers to guide conservatively. It was candid about near-term raw material disruption and the Q1 gas hit. Answers on steel cord timelines were more hedged, using phrases such as "hopefully" and "if everything goes well".
key_quotes: We have achieved our highest ever quarterly revenue, EBITDA, and profit after tax.
So, we will rather be a little conservative than not delivering on our guidance.
Sir, our thought process is that we should maintain our margins at about Rs. 7,000 to Rs. 7,500.
In the long run, yes, we would definitely look at Rs. 8,000 to Rs. 10,000.

544210|2026-06.headline: Emcure Q1 FY27 revenue rose 22.8% YoY to INR 2,580 crore, with EBITDA of INR 508 crore (19.7% margin) and PAT up 35-36%.
544210|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 22.8% YoY to INR 2,580 crore, led by international markets (up 34.2% to INR 1,485 crore) while India grew 10.2% to INR 1,095 crore. EBITDA rose 25.8% to INR 508 crore with margin up 50 bps to 19.7%, and PAT grew about 36% to INR 292 crore. Gross margin fell to 58.4% on geographic and product mix, and net debt rose to INR 1,103 crore. Management reiterated low-to-mid teens FY27 revenue growth (now toward the higher end) and 70-100 bps EBITDA margin expansion. Board changes were announced: Chairman Berjis Desai retires at AGM and CEO Satish Mehta becomes Chairman; Samit Mehta becomes COO and CEO of Gennova, which is now 100% owned.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,095 crore, +10.2% YoY. Ex-Sanofi OAD and Roche in-licensed brands, growth was about 6-7%. Price contributed about 4-5%, new launches 1-2%. Management says no channel filling in the quarter.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 537 crore, +32.8% YoY, driven by base business and liposomal amphotericin B (Ampho). Ampho is introduced in pretty much all countries, but tender-based procurement means lumpy orders.

segments.name: Canada
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 427 crore, +24.6% YoY, on new launches and share gains. Semaglutide filing expected in the next few months; Quebec launch via Dr. Reddy's is uncertain.

segments.name: Rest of World
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 522 crore, +44.8% YoY, led by ARV. About two-thirds of ROW was ARV this quarter; management expects ARV at about 50-55% of ROW for the full year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at low-to-mid teens, with management now more comfortable at the higher end of that range, driven by ARV order book visibility.
EBITDA margin expansion of 70-100 bps for FY27 reiterated.
FY27 gross margin guided at about 59% (earlier 60-61% framing), as higher international and ARV mix dilutes gross margin while EBITDA is accretive.
R&D for FY27 guided at 4-5% of revenue; spend expected to pick up in the rest of the year.
India growth expected in line with industry in Q2 FY27 and faster than industry in H2 FY27 as the Zuventus base effect eases.
Net debt expected to rise to about INR 1,450 crore by end-Q2 FY27 after the Mantra and Gennova payouts (INR 450-500 crore), then turn net cash by end-FY28.
Management expects sequential improvement each quarter.
capex_capacity: No capacity, utilisation or capex figures were given on the call.
Gennova consolidated to 100% after acquiring a 12.05% minority stake; Mantra acquisition payout completed in July 2026.
demand_pricing: International constant-currency growth about 12% (about 12-13% per later answer), against about 6-7% FX tailwind at company level.
India price growth about 4-5% YoY; new launches 1-2%; the remainder is volume.

Poviztra (semaglutide biosimilar with Novo Nordisk) is growing month on month, but management says 40-50 brands have launched in the market and it is hard to separate channel stocking from consumption. Pricing was set very competitively.
Gross margin pressure reflects B2B-type international businesses (lower gross margin, higher EBITDA contribution), with Europe and ARV growing faster.
Management says Zuventus is stabilised and consolidated, now moving to acceleration.

qa_highlights.question: Is India's double-digit growth clean, or is there channel filling after Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no channel filling this quarter; growth is normalised and expected to improve further in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What share of ROW is ARV, and does FY27 base make FY28 harder?
qa_highlights.answer: About two-thirds of ROW is ARV this quarter; full-year ARV share is expected at about 50-55% of ROW, with growth in both ARV and non-ARV.

qa_highlights.question: When will domestic growth be back in line with the market, and what is organic growth ex-in-licensed brands?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 FY27 is expected to be in line with industry and H2 faster. Ex-Sanofi OAD and Roche, growth was about 6-7%. Poviztra is a new launch; OAD moves into the base next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is constant-currency international growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Company-level FX impact was about 6-7%; international growth would have been about 12% in constant currency (12-13% in later answer).

qa_highlights.question: Why is Canada semaglutide a second-wave filing, and what is the Quebec launch timing with Dr. Reddy's?
qa_highlights.answer: Filing expected in the next few months, delayed because semaglutide was pursued as a global development. Quebec timing depends on Dr. Reddy's supply; management will defer to them.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin decline and where does it settle?
qa_highlights.answer: Mix from Europe and ARV growth; FY27 gross margin guided at about 59%. Management says B2B international businesses are EBITDA-accretive despite lower gross margin.

qa_highlights.question: When will net debt turn to net cash and how does it trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt expected at about INR 1,450 crore by end-Q2 after acquisition payouts; net cash by about end-FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 R&D spend?
qa_highlights.answer: R&D is guided at 4-5% of revenue for FY27.

financial_highlights.change: from INR 99 crore in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR 1,103 crore (CFO also cited INR 1,560 crore in Q&A)

risks_watch: India growth: management guides Q2 FY27 in line with industry and H2 faster as the Zuventus base eases; Q1 organic ex-in-licensed growth was about 6-7%, so watch whether the Q2 and H2 acceleration materialises.

Poviztra (semaglutide biosimilar) competition: 40-50 brands launched, management cannot separate channel stocking from consumption and says the market needs 3-6 months to play out; pricing set very competitively.
Gross margin dilution from Europe, ARV and B2B international mix; FY27 guided at about 59% versus earlier 60-61% framing.

Net debt: reported INR 1,103 crore in the presentation, but the CFO cited INR 1,560 crore in Q&A; guidance of about INR 1,450 crore by end-Q2 FY27 and net cash by end-FY28 depends on working capital normalising.
Canada semaglutide: filing expected in the next few months (second wave); Quebec launch timing depends on Dr. Reddy's supply and management is deferring to them.
Lumpy European Ampho orders due to tender-based procurement, and ARV dependence in ROW (about 50-55% of ROW for FY27).
key_quotes: There is no channel filling in this quarter, Kunal. This is a normalized growth that we have.
I don't have a crystal ball here . As far as we are concerned, we are marketing innovation.
So, by the end of next quarter, we should have a net debt of close to around INR 1,450 crore.
I think we will defer to Reddy's on this. Whenever we have the product with us, we'll be able to launch it out.
544210|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on the quarter, the 5-year plan and the Zuventus turnaround, with repeated bullish language on domestic acceleration. Management was more cautious and evasive on Poviztra market share and channel stocking, on Quebec semaglutide timing (deferred to Dr. Reddy's), and on the net debt figure, which differed between the CFO's remarks.

544213|2026-03.headline: Aelea Commodities H2 FY26 standalone revenue Rs 189.50 cr with 13.10% EBITDA margin and Rs 12.35 cr PAT; FY26 revenue up 112% to Rs 363.12 cr.
544213|2026-03.overview: Management reported H2 FY26 standalone revenue of Rs 189.50 cr, EBITDA of Rs 24.82 cr (13.10% margin) and PAT of Rs 12.35 cr (6.52% margin), versus losses a year earlier. For FY26, standalone revenue rose 112.07% to Rs 363.12 cr, EBITDA was Rs 40.20 cr (11.07% margin) and PAT Rs 21.19 cr, with EPS of Rs 10.40 versus Rs 0.65. Consolidated FY26 revenue was Rs 381.50 cr (up 109.46%) and PAT Rs 21.32 cr. The call was dominated by a 10-year (FY37) strategy presentation, with the Q&A focused on higher finance costs, working capital and inventory build, CNSL plant timing, and FY27 guidance, which was not quantified.

financial_highlights.metric: Standalone revenue from operations, H2 FY26

financial_highlights.change: Compared with losses in the corresponding period last year

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated revenue from operations, H2 FY26

segments.name: Cashew kernel processing (core)
segments.commentary: Processes raw cashew nuts (RCN) into wholes and pieces; average mix 63% wholes and 37% pieces, with average kernel realisation of about Rs 590-595/kg. Around 16,000 tonnes of RCN processed in H2 and a similar volume in H1. About 95% of raw material is African-origin, sourced via merchant traders.

segments.name: CNSL / by-products (oil extraction, solar)
segments.commentary: CNSL extraction facility of above 50 MT is under construction, with management guiding to benefits from around H2 FY27 and a product-level EBITDA margin of about 10%. Rooftop solar is installed; ground-mounted solar awaits government approval. B2C consumer pouches are about 1% of sales.

guidance_outlook: FY27: management expects top-line and bottom-line growth at rates similar to FY26, but declined to give a revenue number; an analyst's Rs 500 cr FY27 revenue figure was not confirmed.
FY28: too early to comment; management said it will revisit after about six more months of work.
EBITDA margin: management says the company normally operates at around 10-11% EBITDA margin, which it says it has broadly met.
Finance cost: management expects it to stay at similar or higher levels as the company deepens its value chain, and said absolute figures will grow with scale.
CNSL plant: construction nearly complete with about 30 days of works remaining; commissioning depends on government approvals. Phase 3 capex is expected later in the year.
B2C: targeted at roughly 13-15% EBITDA margin in the long run, pursued through a product basket rather than e-commerce.
capex_capacity: Capacity scaling from 40 MT/day to 140 MT/day, which management says is backed by IPO proceeds; current utilisation about 94-95%.
Phase 2 (CNSL) capex is already committed and underway, with only a small amount pending; Phase 3 capex is expected in the later part of the year.
Ground-mounted solar is pending government approval because of changes to norms for consuming solar power; rooftop solar is complete.
Long-term 2037 strategy targets 1,000 MT/day cashew capacity, plus almond, walnut, pistachio and makhana processing (makhana with a 50-tonne capacity plan).
A Maharashtra cultivation project and capex was flagged by an analyst as not updated; management said it is still being worked on and not crystallised.
demand_pricing: Management said processing is constrained by raw-material quality rather than machine capacity; the company says it fully used its enhanced capacity during H2.
Raw-material sourcing has moved deeper into the value chain (direct sourcing at about 60-65%), which lifted margins but raised working capital and finance costs.
Geopolitical disruption: longer sea transit from Africa, currency swings of around 50 paise a day, and higher RCN price volatility, with no material price impact yet.
Institutional clients are a stated priority for longer-term visibility, but institutions are about one-fifth the size of general trade in the market.
Inventory rose to about Rs 100 cr and management expects it to increase further with growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance cost rise from about Rs 2 cr to Rs 8 cr?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company moved deeper into the value chain, where suppliers do not give credit, but margins are better. Finance cost is expected to stay at similar or higher levels.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 and FY28 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 growth is expected to be similar to FY26 in rate, with no numbers given. FY28 comment deferred about six months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CNSL plant timeline and contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Construction nearly complete with approvals pending; benefits expected around H2. Management said CNSL adds EBITDA rather than top line, at about 10% product-level EBITDA margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity utilisation and RCN volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is about 94-95%. About 16,000 tonnes of RCN were processed in H2, roughly the same as H1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sourcing mix between Africa and India?
qa_highlights.answer: About 95% of processing is African-origin, sourced through merchant traders based in Singapore or Dubai, and 5% is local.

qa_highlights.question: What is the B2C strategy and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: B2C is about 1% of sales. Management said it will grow organically rather than through heavy marketing, targeting roughly 13-15% EBITDA margin on a product basket.

risks_watch: Working capital and finance cost: rising short-term borrowing and inventory (about Rs 100 cr) as sourcing deepens; management gave no debt-to-equity red line.
CNSL and ground-mounted solar commissioning depends on government approvals, which have no fixed timeline.
Geopolitical and shipping disruption from Africa, with longer transit and higher currency and RCN price volatility.
Management declined to quantify FY27 or FY28 numbers; watch whether growth matches the stated similar rate.
Related-party or structural details on the Maharashtra project remain unclear and not yet crystallised.
544213|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the 10-year strategy and FY26 results, but evasive on forward numbers: it repeatedly declined to give FY27 or FY28 figures, the Maharashtra project and timelines, and it deflected on B2C sales and the cause of higher finance cost.
key_quotes: So, for FY27, we are likely to continue our growth rate.

At the end of the day, it's cashew and you, me, or whoever goes at buying it would like to see what is the per gram, per 100 gram price and compare it with wherever you are, other source of buying is.
So we have roughly 95% of the entire processing depending on the African origins only.

544222|2026-03.headline: Akums Q4 FY26 adjusted EBITDA rose 61.6% YoY to INR152 crore (13.1% margin), with FY26 revenue up 5.8% to INR4,359 crore.
544222|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR1,158 crore, up 9.7% YoY and flat QoQ, while adjusted EBITDA reached INR152 crore, driven by CDMO profitability and trade generics turning EBITDA positive. Reported Q4 PAT of INR81 crore was held down versus the prior year by a large deferred tax asset benefit in the base; PBT rose to INR121 crore from INR75 crore. FY26 PAT fell to INR256 crore from INR344 crore, which included a INR106 crore DTA benefit in FY25. Management guided to double-digit CDMO volume growth in H1 FY27, a sharp narrowing of API losses, and a Zambia supply contract of about $25 million per year from Q2 FY27.

financial_highlights.change: +13.3% vs INR461 crore; margin vs 11.2% in FY25
vs INR344 crore in FY25, which included INR106 crore DTA benefit
+61.6% YoY vs INR94 crore; +3.3% QoQ vs INR147 crore; margin vs 8.9% in Q4 FY25 and 12.7% in Q3
vs INR150 crore in Q4 FY25 (DTA-inflated); vs INR68 crore in Q3 FY26
vs INR75 crore in Q4 FY25
vs INR465 crore in FY25; mainly European contract assignment
vs 91 days; inventory build secured by advance payments to creditors

segments.name: CDMO
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR3,485 crore (+8.6%) and EBITDA INR467 crore (+2.9%). Q4 revenue INR952 crore (+13.4% YoY, +4% QoQ) and EBITDA INR137 crore (+54.9% YoY, +9.1% QoQ); management cited operating leverage from better utilisation and newer facilities.

segments.name: Domestic branded formulations (Akumentis)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR446 crore (+2.9%) and EBITDA INR90 crore (+17%). Q4 revenue INR102 crore (-1.5% YoY, -11.1% QoQ) and EBITDA INR22 crore, flat YoY and down 13.2% QoQ.

segments.name: International branded formulations
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR143 crore (flat) and EBITDA INR36 crore (+32.3%). Q4 revenue INR36 crore (-9.7% YoY, -28.5% QoQ) and EBITDA INR10 crore (+14.7% YoY); Q4 margin around 28%, helped by marketing investment and about 3.5-4% gross margin uplift from forex gains.

segments.name: Trade generics
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR100 crore (-13.2%) and EBITDA negative INR10 crore vs negative INR28 crore. Q4 revenue INR27 crore (+22.6% YoY) and EBITDA positive INR1.4 crore, first positive quarter versus negative INR3 crore in Q3.

segments.name: API
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR184 crore (-15.9%) and EBITDA negative INR40 crore vs negative INR44 crore. Q4 revenue INR41 crore (-18.8% YoY, -24.9% QoQ) and EBITDA negative INR12 crore, against negative INR6 crore in Q4 FY25 and negative INR7 crore in Q3.

guidance_outlook: CDMO: double-digit volume growth expected in Q1 and Q2 FY27; management declined to guide on Q3/Q4 pricing or full-year revenue and gave visibility of 45-60 days of the revenue book.

Zambia: about $25 million (roughly INR230 crore at current rates) of annual supplies from Indian facilities in FY27 and FY28, expected to start by end Q2 FY27 at margins similar to CDMO; supplies cease after FY28.
European CDMO contract: about EUR35 million per year on a MAT basis from launch through 2032, fixed-price; management expects margins similar to CDMO or in the high teens.
Akumentis: expected to grow at or above IPM rates, targeting low-double-digit growth; exports expected to grow double digits in FY27.

API: losses expected to fall sharply in FY27 but full-year EBITDA may still be negative; monthly EBITDA-positive is a goal to be assessed over a couple of quarters. European audit of API facility expected in the upcoming quarter.

Tax: effective tax rate about 32% currently, with 29% to be built into the model; normalising towards 25% depends on loss-making API and trade generics turning profitable. FY27 capex target INR300 crore vs INR222 crore in FY26.
capex_capacity: Plant 2 received EU GMP accreditation in January 2026; dossier filings and country registrations under way in multiple European markets, with commercial supplies targeted from FY28.
Plant 3 received ANVISA approval in FY26 in addition to European GMP approval; the injectable facility is ANVISA approved and a separate oral liquids facility is EU GMP approved.
New injectable facility utilisation is in the early teens; management expects significant ramp-up during FY27.
Oral solids facility expansion has started because volumes grew about 20% plus over two quarters; part of the FY27 capex of INR300 crore is for this.
Zambia local plant: total investment about $45 million, 51% borne by Akums; revenue from the local facility expected from calendar 2029.
Haridwar land lease executed to add land for capacity expansion, utilities and support.
demand_pricing: CDMO volume growth in H2 FY26 was led by existing customers with existing brands, from in-house production switches and other CDMOs; management says it is broad-based.

API prices fell about 20-25% as a basket over FY26, then rose by single-digit percentages after the post-war geopolitical situation, but remain below April 2025 levels; management does not expect a sharp fall from current levels.
CDMO pricing is a percentage markup on input cost, so absolute gross profit moves with API prices; the business is pass-through for raw material cost.
Domestic formulations took very little price increase in FY26 and focused on volume; management expects this to change, with double-digit top-line growth in domestic formulations targeted.
Trade generics scaled down from about INR400 crore in FY22 due to elongated working capital; it is now kept at similar revenue and EBITDA levels.
GLP-1: management is still evaluating entry timing, API partners and dosage forms, citing volatile and falling prices.

qa_highlights.question: Volume growth above 25% in the last two quarters: what drives it and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth is from existing customers and existing brands, not new geographies, and management expects double-digit growth to continue into Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 3.5% negative price variance reverse as API prices rise, and can CDMO grow at double digits?
qa_highlights.answer: API prices are up single-digit percent but still below April 2025; management believes they will not fall sharply from current levels and sees H1 volume growth as the driver.

qa_highlights.question: Tax rate outlook for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Current effective rate is about 32% due to loss-making entities; management plans for 29% overall and expects a move toward the normal rate once API and trade generics are profitable.

qa_highlights.question: Capex for FY26 and FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 capex was INR222 crore; the FY27 target is INR300 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a FY27 top-line target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a full-year FY27 revenue target.

qa_highlights.question: How is the European contract structured and what are the margins?
qa_highlights.answer: It is an established product, fixed-price through 2032 and priced at current API levels, with about EUR35 million per year on a MAT basis and margins similar to CDMO or in the high teens.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Zambia contract's duration and investment?
qa_highlights.answer: Supplies of $25 million a year in FY27 and FY28 from India; a local plant with about $45 million total investment (51% Akums) to start revenue in calendar 2029.

qa_highlights.question: How is cash to be deployed, given the 18% payout and large cash balance?
qa_highlights.answer: Priorities are oral solids capacity expansion and inorganic niche acquisitions, including branded portfolio deals, though management said current brand valuations are high.

risks_watch: API losses: FY26 EBITDA was negative INR40 crore for a third straight year; the European audit of the API facility and the pace of loss reduction are key to watch.
Raw material inflation from crude-linked solvents and the Middle East situation; management says CDMO is pass-through, but absolute margins fall when input prices fall.
Working capital days rose to 105 from 91, driven by inventory build and advance payments to creditors.

544252|2026-09.headline: Bajaj Housing Finance Q2 FY27: PAT up 18% YoY to INR757 crore, AUM at INR1.58 lakh crore growing 25%, with management flagging ~25 bps NIM compression ahead.

Cost of funds fell 17 bps QoQ to about 7.0% from fixed-to-floating NCD conversion, offsetting a 10 bps portfolio yield decline, so NIM dipped 2 bps to 3.7%. Management said the repo hike will pass through roughly 80% to both liabilities and assets, but acquisition pricing from banks is still unclear and is the main margin and attrition risk. Guidance on AUM growth (21-23%) and NIM compression (~25 bps for the year) was not revised.

segments.commentary: AUM growth 26% YoY. GNPA down 1 bp QoQ to 61 bps; NNPA down 4 bps to 21 bps.

Floating-rate assets: 25-30% linked to repo; internal FRR book (about 54% of assets, or 60-62% of floating assets) linked to PLR. PLR raised 15 bps effective 16 October 2026; new acquisition pricing expected to rise about 15-20 bps.
Bank MCLR hikes by leading public sector banks and an early 15-20 bps move by one or two banks were cited; a clearer picture expected around 24-25 October.
Management said prime pricing competition from PSU and private banks is an ongoing feature; if acquisition pricing lags, prime attrition may rise and the company will lean on non-prime growth.

Insurance commission regulation draft: management estimated 10-11% of PBT comes from cross-sell income; about 4-5% can be offset, leaving 6-7% of PBT at risk. Sambhav fees and prime efficiencies may offset part of this, mainly on a longer-term basis.

qa_highlights.question: Why did developer finance decline QoQ, and what is the strategy for the DF book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said higher repayments from project cash flows plus slower disbursements drove the decline, not a conscious strategy. DF sanctions rose sharply in H1, and the target is 15-17% of the portfolio, with recovery expected in Q3-Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Will the repo hikes compress margins and how much pass-through is possible on the prime side?
qa_highlights.answer: About 80-82% of repo hikes flow through to cost of funds and to portfolio pricing, so the main margin risk is on acquisition pricing. If prime acquisition pricing lags, attrition and BT-out rise and the company shifts toward non-prime.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the fall in fee income?
qa_highlights.answer: Fee income rose on higher insurance income (attachment rates higher with Sambhav growth) and higher foreclosure income in the quarter, not a decline. Fee-related expenses are marginal and range-bound.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20 bps cost of funds decline a one-off, and what is the exit COF?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a starting point, not a one-off, though part came from one-time maturity of high-priced borrowings. Three 25 bps hikes would take COF up about 61 bps, from roughly 7% in September to about 7.6% by March.

qa_highlights.question: Why did home loan originations decline QoQ, and what is the YoY growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarterly movements are seasonal and the company tracks AUM rather than disbursals. Home loan disbursal growth was 24% YoY, close to the company's 25% disbursement growth.

qa_highlights.question: Will guidance be revised given NIM expansion this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no revision for now. NIM compression of about 25 bps is still expected, and AUM growth could slow to 22-23% if acquisition pricing lags, given the rise in BT-out rates.

risks_watch: Acquisition pricing pass-through by banks after the repo hike, due around 24-25 October; a lag could increase prime attrition and cut AUM growth from 25% toward 22-23%.

Developer finance book: a QoQ decline and 13% YoY growth; watch whether disbursements recover in Q3-Q4 as management expects.
Rising salary costs (19% YoY in Q2) as Sambhav and senior hires build out; management expects elevated costs for 1.5-2 years.
Home loan GNPA rose to 36 bps from 34 bps; watch for further upward movement, and whether the single LRD slippage stays isolated.

544253|2026-06.headline: Kross Q1 FY27 revenue rose 32.3% YoY to INR184.3 crore, with EBITDA margin at 12.23% (up 63 bps) and PAT up 24.4% to INR133.12 million.

Management attributed growth to volumes across M&HCV, trailers and tractors, and said the extrusion axle beam line is now in production. Steel and conversion-cost pass-throughs are being settled, with the tractor industry already settled from April 1 and CV settlement pending. Management said Q1 is in line with its FY27 targets, though June-July demand is seasonally subdued.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export target and the size of the European tier 1 order?

qa_highlights.question: Is the trailer-axle growth of about 34% share gain, given single-digit industry growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth was largely Q4 FY26 order spillover. Management declined to comment on market share; capacity expansion should allow further growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is the worst margin quarter behind us, with QoQ expansion ahead?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects QoQ margin expansion. Steel pass-through is retrospective but will come in gradually. Conversion cost increase is the larger factor.

qa_highlights.question: Why did top-five customer revenue fall between DRHP and FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the top-five share fell from about 60-63% to 58-59% through diversification, and it would check the INR figures.

qa_highlights.question: What are utilisation and debt plans, and does capex need to increase?

544254|2026-03.headline: Tolins Tyres FY26 consolidated revenue rose about 12% to INR327.12 crore, but EBITDA fell to INR47.8 crore and PAT to INR35.69 crore.
544254|2026-03.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue from operations grew about 12% YoY to INR327.12 crore, while EBITDA (excluding other income) declined to INR47.8 crore from INR57.91 crore, with margin at 14.6%. PAT fell to INR35.69 crore from INR38.67 crore, and basic EPS was INR9.03. Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 12% to INR77.99 crore, but Q4 EBITDA fell to INR11.22 crore (14.4% margin) from INR13.57 crore, with PAT of INR8.94 crore. Management attributed the pressure to a GST rate mismatch on retreading materials, higher inventory, longer receivable cycles and West Asia disruption, and gave only a soft FY27 outlook of maintaining FY26 performance.

qa_highlights.question: When will operating cash flow turn positive, and what is the sales and marketing strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said credit periods were extended by about one month due to GST and geopolitical uncertainty, with the aim of reducing them over a few quarters. Management said branding spend is small and that it relies on a strong marketing manager team.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status and margin of the Ras Al Khaimah UAE plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is 1,200 MT with utilisation below 50%. The CFO said UAE margins are better than India's, and utilisation could fall to 30-40% in the next three months before recovering to 40-50%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins decline in Q4 and FY26, and when will GST be corrected?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO attributed the decline to margin pressure in retreads from the GST imbalance and weaker dealer off-take. The industry body has asked for a 5% retread GST rate, and the government is considering it.

qa_highlights.question: What are the three biggest growth drivers beyond FY27?

544263|2026-03.headline: KRN Heat Exchanger FY26 standalone total income rose 57.36% to Rs.689.95 crore; Q4 standalone net profit up 22.69% to Rs.16.87 crore.
544263|2026-03.overview: FY26 standalone total income grew 57.36% YoY to Rs.689.95 crore, with EBITDA up 19.41% to Rs.84.79 crore and net profit up 42.11% to Rs.71.31 crore. Consolidated FY26 total income was Rs.609.81 crore (+38.06%), EBITDA Rs.112.48 crore (+59.52%) and net profit Rs.76.47 crore (+44.62%). Q4 consolidated EBITDA rose 77.56% to Rs.33.55 crore, while Q4 standalone total income rose 55.06% to Rs.204.93 crore. Management said the new Neemrana HVAC facility is still ramping up, with working capital building in inventory and receivables, and a board-approved enabling fund raise of up to Rs.500 crore whose objective is not yet finalised.

financial_highlights.value: Around 3x YoY (per analyst question, not disputed)

segments.name: Heat exchangers (fin and tube, KRN Heat Exchanger)
segments.commentary: Management said the old facility was fully utilised in FY26; fin and tube still accounts for about 95% of revenue, with other products about 5%. Fin and tube growth expected above 80-90%, mainly from data centres.

segments.name: HVAC / new facility (KRN HVAC Products)
segments.commentary: Utilisation of the new facility was about 15% in FY26 for HVAC. Management targets 50% in FY27 and 80% in FY28 across about eight new products and new geometries.

segments.name: Data centre
segments.commentary: Data centre was about 16% of revenue in FY26 per one answer and about 18.7-19% in Q4 per another answer; management expects this to rise quarter on quarter. Top-10 customers include three data centre customers.

segments.name: Bus AC
segments.commentary: Bus AC revenue was about Rs.10 crore in FY26; management targets at least 15% market share in FY27 and has a Rs.150 crore revenue target shown in the presentation, with two to three OEMs onboarded.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export was about Rs.100 crore in FY26 and management aims for roughly double in FY27; export order book is about Rs.120 crore including data centre orders. Geographies cited: UAE, US/North America and Europe.

segments.name: Railways / refrigeration
segments.commentary: Bar and plate heat exchanger approved by Indian Railways for field trial; company says it was L1 in three recent tenders. Full HVAC system for railways needs about 6-8 months of approvals, so limited FY27 contribution expected.

guidance_outlook: New facility utilisation targets: about 50% in FY27 and about 80% in FY28; old facility to stay fully utilised.
Management expects next eight quarters to be the highest ever, with Q4 described as an average quarter and quarter-on-quarter improvement expected.
Export to roughly double in FY27 versus about Rs.100 crore in FY26.

Margins expected to improve slightly, helped by a 5% PLI benefit in FY26, a likely RIFS state incentive of about 1.56% of top line for 10 years on the new facility, export mix and solar power savings, offset by higher depreciation and overheads.
Inventory expected to come under control within about three quarters; minimum six months to normalise per management.
Analyst cited a Rs.2,250-2,850 crore revenue target; management did not confirm the target or its timing.
capex_capacity: New Neemrana facility inaugurated 11 March 2026; production commissioning began May 2025 and the plant was shifted to fully in the week before the call.

Current facility is fully commissioned; about eight new products added, including WOT condenser, roll-bond evaporator, frost-free evaporator, skin condenser, bar and plate, dry air cooler, ammonia evaporator and bus AC, plus new fin geometries.
Further capex on existing facility is about Rs.30-40 crore over the next two years, mainly for line balancing for data centre geometry, per management's rough estimate.
Micro-channel (MCHX) product expected by end 2026 or early 2027; plate-and-plate heat exchanger (CDU) under study for next year.
Solar plant installed and operational.
demand_pricing: Raw material pass-through: management said copper LME, aluminium LME and USD-INR changes are passed to customers on a quarterly basis, with freight and logistics also passed through; it said close to 100% pass-through is possible.
UAE dispatches were disrupted in March 2026 due to the geopolitical situation; dispatches restarted in May 2026. Freight costs rose and are being passed on.
North America and Europe dispatches unaffected per management; Europe is early-stage and North America is larger than Europe for data centre exports.
Company says it competes with European and North American suppliers, not Chinese players, given customised, low-volume products.
Data centre demand: some Indian customers issue one-month firm orders on a rolling basis; one long-lead customer booked six to seven months.
Vertiv vendor approval received after QA audit; billing expected to start in coming weeks or months; Schneider Electric is the biggest domestic data centre customer.

qa_highlights.question: Are new products for liquid-cooled AI data centres in development?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said liquid cooling is early in India; fin and tube remains the core product for chillers and dry coolers, with micro-channel due by end 2026 or early 2027 and plate heat exchanger for CDUs under study.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company pass raw material costs to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, management said copper, aluminium and USD-INR movements are passed through quarter on quarter and close to 100% can be passed on under current contracts; there is a one-quarter lag.

qa_highlights.question: Why is inventory up about 3x and receivables up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited about Rs.15-20 crore of UAE material held after March dispatch was blocked, about Rs.8 crore of export dispatched in March but not billed, minimum stock for new products, BIS-related pre-buying of inner groove tube, and new customer onboarding. Normalisation expected in about six months, with inventory days around two and a half months currently.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise equity when internal cash flow may suffice?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the IPO proceeds were exceeded by investment in the current facility and working capital will be short; the board approved an enabling resolution up to Rs.500 crore, with objectives not yet concluded. Bank funding is also an option.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q4 revenue share from products other than fin and tube?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not have the figure on the call; it said non-fin-and-tube business is about 5% of revenue overall.

qa_highlights.question: Is the bus AC Rs.150 crore target backed by orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said two to three OEMs have been onboarded and regular supply has started, with about 15% market share targeted; no specific Rs.150 crore order book was quantified.

risks_watch: Working capital and receivables build-up; inventory normalisation timeline (about six months) and the Rs.500 crore equity raise, whose use is unconfirmed.
BIS certification issue on inner groove tube (deadline around 20-28 May 2026) could drive imports and inventory build-up.
Copper and aluminium price volatility in recent weeks, which management said is beyond expectation; pass-through has a one-quarter lag.
Geopolitical disruption to UAE dispatches and freight costs.
Ramp-up pace of the new facility versus 50%/80% utilisation targets; Q4 incremental revenue from the new facility was about Rs.15-16 crore per an analyst's estimate.
Concentration of data centre revenue (about 16-19%) and dependence on a few large customers such as Schneider Electric.
Depreciation and overhead rising ahead of revenue.
544263|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on growth, data centre demand and utilisation targets, but evasive on the Rs.500 crore fund raise, the Rs.120 crore UAE order, the Q4 non-fin-and-tube share and the specific data centre order book. Several answers were vague or deferred to later updates.
key_quotes: Yes, even I can say next eight quarters will be highest ever. So, this quarter also will be average but number I cannot disclose.
So, now we have eight new businesses, so that is also we have to build the inventory.
Of course, slight improvement will be there, but honestly in the last two, three weeks in this copper and aluminum silver price is beyond the expectation because they sharply increase.

544264|2026-03.headline: Diffusion Engineers Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 38.08% YoY to INR1,415.74 million, with FY27 revenue growth guided above 20%.
544264|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue was INR1,415.74 million (+38.08% YoY) and EBITDA excluding other income was INR206.89 million (+39.96%), at a 14.61% margin. Consolidated FY26 revenue was INR4,066.28 million (+21.28%) with PAT of INR504.1 million (+39.87%). Standalone growth was weaker: Q4 revenue +12.18% and Q4 PAT down 3.05%, which management attributed to capacity constraints in wear plates, wear parts and heavy engineering running at about 85-90% utilisation. Order book stood at about INR200 crores as of 30 April 2026, up from about INR100 crores a year earlier. New Unit 4 capacity is being commissioned from Q1 FY27 onward.

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated revenue from operations Q4 FY26
Consolidated EBITDA excl. other income Q4 FY26
Consolidated EBITDA excl. other income FY26
Standalone EBITDA excl. other income Q4 FY26
Standalone EBITDA excl. other income FY26

segments.name: Welding consumables (products)
segments.commentary: Management cited roughly 30% of revenue; under 3% (said 2-3%) of the business is conventional, with the rest special hard-facing and repair electrodes. Wires line at 85-90% utilisation; new wire line expected July 2026.

segments.name: Wear plates, wear parts and heavy engineering
segments.commentary: Cited at roughly 30% of revenue combined with heavy engineering; running at 85-90% utilisation, and expected to grow faster than consumables. Roller-press rolls, steel mill rollers and VRM rollers are cited as growth areas; first VRM order won.

segments.name: Services
segments.commentary: Roughly 10% of revenue per management. Covers on-site breakdown repair, hot kiln alignment and bulk deposition, with about 50-60 welding technicians deployed. UAE subsidiary set up for service and overlay work is now operational and expected to contribute from FY27.

segments.name: Railways (developmental)
segments.commentary: L1 in multiple contracts and some letters of intent received for Vande Bharat ecosystem components; execution 6-9 months, with substantial revenue expected from next year at likely lower initial margins.

segments.name: Defence (Tejorup Sunmay Systems)
segments.commentary: Investment made in February 2026 for VSHORADS work; still in prototype stage with a DRDO sanction order for 200 launchers and 1,200 rockets. No revenue expected in FY26 or in FY27 in any significant amount.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth expected to be more than 20%, supported by capacity additions, order inflows and higher-margin engineered products.
FY27 EBITDA margin expected to rise by about 80-100 basis points, aided by operating leverage and cost consolidation; gross margin may come under pressure from raw material volatility.
Medium-term aspiration of INR650 crore-plus revenue at 15-16% EBITDA margin, expected to be reached in under 3 years (2-3 years on annual run-rate basis).

Capex of about INR100 crores from IPO proceeds (INR70 crores for wear part/plate/heavy engineering, INR30 crores for electrode and slitting facility) is expected to support INR800-900 crores revenue; no additional capex planned for INR650 crores.
Debtor days targeted at 80-85 for FY27 and inventory days at 60-65; FY26 debtor days were 98 and inventory days 66.
International revenue share expected to rise to about 15%, with international sales growing above 20%.
capex_capacity: New 10 tons-per-day electrode plant commissioned around November-December 2025, along with an in-house strip-slitting line for flux-cored wires.
Wear plate capacity expanded by about 25% and now commissioned.

Unit 4 (about 170,000-180,000 sq ft) for wear plates, wear parts and heavy engineering: partial utilisation from May 2026, most capacity live by end of Q1 FY27 (quarter ending June 2026), with the facility expected to be fully commissioned by end of Q1 2027 per management.
Current utilisation: wires about 85-90%; wear plates and heavy engineering about 85-90%. Management expects utilisation to fall to roughly 50-60% once new shop floors are live.
New wire line expected to be delivered in July 2026.
demand_pricing: Order book about INR200 crores as of 30 April 2026, up from about INR100 crores on 31 March 2025; management expects 80-90% to execute in FY27, with staggered power-project deliveries extending beyond.
Over 80% of revenue from repeat customers; end-market demand from cement, steel, power, mining and engineering described as steady, with no project holds despite the West Asia crisis.

Raw material volatility (tungsten, nickel, cobalt, molybdenum, chromium) is affecting margins; price variation clauses cover under 10% of the order book, with the rest fixed-price contracts. Management books raw materials on order and gives short offer validity on volatile items.
Price increases are ongoing, linked to input costs; management says customers are aware of raw material conditions.

Exports reach more than 35 countries including Southeast Asia, Middle East and Africa; Turkey operations are maturing, a new West Africa partner has been identified, and Singapore sales rose significantly in FY26.
Competitors named: Ador Fontech (merged into Ador Welding) and EWAC Alloys (now part of ESAB) in welding consumables and wear plates; ThyssenKrupp, ISGEC and Walchandnagar in heavy engineering.

qa_highlights.question: Why is standalone growth flat relative to consolidated, and will it normalise in FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said standalone plants were already at about 85% utilisation, capping execution in wear plates, wear parts and heavy engineering; new capacity from Q1 FY27 should lift standalone growth to match consolidated.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin volatility (13% to 14.8%) driven by?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it mainly to raw material price lags on fixed-price contracts; gross margin may fall, but fixed and operating costs have been consolidated, so net margins improved with scale.

qa_highlights.question: How is the debtor-day gap versus Ador Fontech explained?
qa_highlights.answer: Debtors are at 98 days for FY26 due to large heavy-engineering shipments in March (about INR140 crores of Q4 sales, including roughly INR20 crores of rollers). Target is 80-85 days for FY27; welding consumables are cash-and-carry; heavy engineering is typically 60 days contractually but extends to 75-90 days in practice.

qa_highlights.question: Will the INR650 crore revenue target be reached faster, with growth accelerating above 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects growth to rise as new facilities come online and expects INR650 crores in 2-3 years on run-rate basis; no additional capex is needed for that level, and INR100 crores of capex could support INR800-900 crores.

qa_highlights.question: When will railway and defence businesses contribute meaningful revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Railway developmental orders take 6-9 months to execute, with substantial revenue from next year after approved-vendor listing. Tejorup defence revenue is not expected in FY26 or significantly in FY27, pending prototype approval.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue contribution from new products such as steel mill rollers and VRM rollers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify, citing confidentiality; said steel mill roller revenue was significant last year, a first VRM order has been won, and shredder spare parts are under development.

risks_watch: Raw material volatility (tungsten, cobalt, nickel) on fixed-price contracts; gross margin pressure in FY27 with a lag in passing through costs.
Standalone profitability: Q4 standalone PAT fell 3.05% YoY despite revenue growth, and standalone growth depends on Unit 4 commissioning on schedule by end of Q1 2027.
Receivable days at 98 in FY26 with heavy-engineering payment cycles of 75-90 days; management's 80-85 target needs to be met.
Quarterly concentration: Q4 is seasonally large, and management expects Q4 to remain the biggest quarter.
Tejorup defence and railway developmental businesses carry lower initial margins and long gestation periods.
Management's stated 20%+ FY27 growth and 80-100 bps margin expansion are to be tracked against Q1 FY27 results.

544264|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 36.5% YoY to INR1,101.08 million, with order book up 20.4% QoQ to INR209 crores.
