Standalone PAT fell YoY to INR99.79 million, but this reflects a one-time ~INR5 crore subsidiary dividend in the year-ago quarter. The order book reached INR209 crores at 30 June 2026, with more than 80% stated as executable in FY27, and a ~INR100 crore capacity expansion is coming on stream in phases at Nagpur.

segments.name: Heavy Engineering
segments.commentary: Order book of INR159 crores at 30 June 2026. Management says ~70% of heavy engineering is new project build and ~30% spare parts for installed base; capacity being raised from 9,000 to 18,000 metric tons.

segments.name: Wear Plates and Wear Parts
segments.commentary: Order book of INR26.42 crores. Management said growth in Q1 came across consumables, wear plates/parts and heavy engineering.

segments.name: Welding Consumables
segments.commentary: Order book of INR24.22 crores, described as a strong sequential increase driven by customers consolidating yearly requirements. Management said there was no one-off windfall.

segments.name: Defence
segments.commentary: Contributes approximately 1.5% to 2% of revenue. Management said it has not yet won competitive bids for subassemblies; Tejorup (10% stake) is developing a VSHORADS prototype.

segments.name: Exports / International
segments.commentary: Management said domestic drove most of Q1 growth because Q1 FY26 had large export orders; Turkey has turned out of loss, and UAE facility is expected to contribute revenue from Q2 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Management expects around 20% growth in FY27 and FY28 and continuing for 3-4 years, with an aim to double revenue in about three years.
EBITDA margin expected to rise 100-200 basis points over FY27 and FY28; management said Q1 margin should return to prior-year Q1 levels.
Management expects Q2 FY27 growth at similar levels to Q1, supported by seasonal monsoon-linked maintenance demand.
More than 80% of the INR209 crore order book is executable in FY27; customers are asking to prepone deliveries.
Railway (Vande Bharat, locomotives) revenue expected to convert within 9-12 months after workshop approval; management said new development items are a longer gestation cycle.
No new capex finalised; management wants to start the next expansion once newly installed capacity reaches 70-80% utilisation.
capex_capacity: Roughly INR100 crore expansion program across electrodes, wear plates and heavy engineering, with new strip slitting capability for backward integration.
Heavy engineering capacity being expanded from 9,000 to 18,000 metric tons (includes wear parts and flux-cored wires used internally); new Nagpur shop floor coming live in phases since Q1.
New capacity expected to contribute from the next quarter, but management said ramp-up will take 2-3 years; electrode capacity started in Q4 FY26 with similar 2-3 year ramp.
About INR67 crore of IPO proceeds still unutilised; management expects full utilisation by year-end, with savings to be redeployed subject to shareholder approval.
Units 1, 2 and 3 have no capacity change; utilisation there was described as 2-3% in one answer, while management said Units 1 and 3 operate at optimal levels.
demand_pricing: Finished steel production grew ~8.3% in April-June 2026 quarter; cement volume growth expected at 7-8% in FY27.

Named Q1 orders: INR9.88 crore VRM/separator parts (cement), INR8.16 crore roller-press rolls, INR10.63 crore roller assemblies, INR7.49 crore flux-cored wire (defence), INR26.31 crore RAPH rotor assembly (power); aggregate ~INR62.47 crore.
Raw material costs: steel up ~20%, some ferro-alloys like tungsten up several hundred percent; management said gross margin compressed by ~1-1.5% and customers have accepted higher prices.
Heavy engineering payment terms: 10-20% advance, 70-80% post-dispatch, balance after warranty documentation.
Top 10 customer concentration not disclosed on call; management said 60-70% expected, to be confirmed later.

qa_highlights.question: Raw material volatility and margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said prices remain high but volatility has eased and customers have accepted higher prices. Gross margin contraction was about 1-1.5%, with steel up ~20% and some ferro-alloys up several hundred percent.

qa_highlights.question: Executable portion of the INR210 crore order book in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: More than 80% is executable in FY27, and customers have asked to prepone some deliveries scheduled for next year.

qa_highlights.question: Share of profit from associate (LSN Diffusion) of INR4.4 crore: anomaly or steady?
qa_highlights.answer: Historical run-rate is INR1-2 crore per quarter, so management expects INR1-2 crore going forward and treats the rest of the Q1 amount as a one-off extra.

qa_highlights.question: FY27-28 revenue and margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects ~20% growth in FY27-28 and an aim to double in three years, with EBITDA margin up 100-200 bps over FY27-28.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone margin fall from ~18% peak to ~13%, and is Q1 the bottom?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Q1 FY26 standalone PAT included a one-time ~INR5 crore subsidiary dividend. Management expects margins to return to prior-year Q1 levels and rise 100-200 bps over the next 1-1.5 years.

544277|2026-06.headline: Waaree Q1 FY27 revenue rose 79.2% YoY to INR7,932 crore and order book hit a record INR61,500 crore, though operating EBITDA margin was 18.2%.
544277|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 79.2% YoY to about INR7,932 crore, with operating EBITDA up 44.4% to about INR1,440 crore at an 18.2% margin and PAT of INR892 crore (11% margin, up 15.4%). Management attributed margin pressure to higher global raw material costs, softer US exports from delayed clearances, and inventory built ahead of second-half-weighted dispatches. Order book rose to INR61,500 crore after INR16,000 crore of net inflows against about INR7,300 crore executed. Management reaffirmed FY27 operating EBITDA guidance of INR7,000-7,700 crore, pinning the margin recovery on rising captive cell integration and US local manufacturing.

segments.name: Revenue mix

segments.name: Retail (B2C)
segments.commentary: Revenue of INR2,289 crore, up 130% YoY; management guides INR9,000-10,000 crore for FY27.

segments.name: Overseas / US
segments.commentary: US domestic revenue INR1,322 crore and direct exports INR287 crore. US plant produced about 230 MW in Q1, earning roughly USD12-13 million of IRA incentives.

segments.name: Cell manufacturing (India)
segments.commentary: 5.4 GW capacity at 62% utilisation; about 800 MW of DCR cell made in Q1. Integrated cell lines show 35-40% margin per management.

segments.name: Modules (India and US)
segments.commentary: India module capacity 24.2 GW at about 50% annualised utilisation; US module capacity 1.6 GW at about 59%. Management expects US utilisation of 75-80% in coming quarters.

segments.name: BESS / storage
segments.commentary: Automated BESS container capacity of 5.15 GWh started, versus 3.5 GWh originally planned. A 1,520 MWh BESS EPC order was won.

segments.name: Transmission and transformers
segments.commentary: Waaree Transpower began commercial production of a 17.6 MVA inverter-duty transformer. WRTL acquired about 55% of Associated Power Structures for about INR1,225 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 operating EBITDA guidance of INR7,000-7,700 crore reaffirmed.
FY28 ballpark of about INR7,000 crore EBITDA mentioned by Varun Goenka; FY28 expected to see about 16-18 GW module and about 10 GW cell production.
Cell-to-module integration ratio to rise from about 20% to about 65% within 2-3 quarters.
Cell production to rise from about 800 MW in Q1 to about 1.2 GW in Q2 and about 1.5 GW in Q3.
Module utilisation to reach 70-75% in Q3 and Q4; management expects 80-85% over 2-3 quarters as integration rises.
US IRA incentive receipts expected quarterly from Q3-Q4 FY27 via refund or sale of credits; US production of 400-500 MW per quarter from Q3.
Management aspires to a near INR1 lakh crore revenue vision in less than 4-5 years.
capex_capacity: Announced capex programme about INR31,500 crore; about INR9,450 crore deployed as of 30 June. Phasing is about 30% in FY27, 40% in FY28 and 30% in FY29.

FY27 additions: 2.6 GW US modules, 10 GW Indian cell (Gujarat, ALMM-II applied, equipment on site, commercial start expected from about Q3), 100 KTPA T&D EPC, 20 GVA transformers, 4 GW inverters, 1 GW electrolysers.

qa_highlights.question: Gaurav Malhotra: What is the effective tax rate this year and next?

qa_highlights.question: Lokesh Manik (Vallum Capital): Why did depreciation rise, and why did GTV fall from ₹6,800 crore to ₹6,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Telematics devices are depreciated over two years, so depreciation is front-loaded with the device investment. GTV now reports tolling only, with fuelling removed because of fuel price uncertainty.

risks_watch: Fuel business recovery: no timeline given, and fuel loyalty spend is discretionary.
Tolling volume: tolling transactions fell 3% QoQ, and tolling GTV growth (16%) lags NETC and the CV market.
Super Loads investment: spending rises each quarter, and segment-level disclosure is not expected for 3-4 quarters.
Reported PAT volatility from deferred tax; the Q4 loss-utilisation reassessment could move reported earnings.
Potential competition from Delhivery in tolling, fuelling and vehicle finance.
544288|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on telematics, tolling recovery and Super Loads momentum, but cautious on fuel recovery, with no timeline given. Management deflected granular Super Loads metrics and unit economics, citing limited disclosure.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 margins fall and what is the underlying margin?

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 EBITDA guidance be cut further and what drives it?

544292|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 47% QoQ to INR4,282 million and EBITDA reached INR919 million, while management reiterated the FY28 target of US$400 million revenue at ~40% EBITDA margin.
544292|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 showed a sharp sequential recovery after a weak Q3, driven by the start of invoicing for drug-device combinations (DDC) and the India Semaglutide launch at the end of the quarter. Full-year revenue fell 2% YoY to INR14,216 million and EBITDA fell about 35%, both hit by delayed Semaglutide approvals. Management deferred the Steriscience injectables and Brooks merger scheme, citing smaller-investor valuation concerns and a lower listed-company share price, and said it will revisit in about two years. Capacity expansion remains on track, with a new DDC line expected to be available from next quarter and three lines installed by end FY27.

segments.name: DDC (drug-device combinations) / Semaglutide
segments.commentary: Invoicing began this year; Canada approvals received for two partners, and shipments to both Canadian partners have commenced. Current line is fully committed back-to-back, and the new 500-litre-capable line is expected to be available from next quarter.

segments.name: Injectables and soft gelatin (base business)
segments.commentary: Signed 10 new licences, launched 15-plus products and added customers during the year. Soft gelatin capacity is expected to be fully utilised within the current period, and a fourth injectable line is coming in unit two.

segments.name: Biologics (nascent)
segments.commentary: Funnel expanded almost 4x YoY; a European biosimilar partner, a US biosimilar major and a second animal-health project from a top-three global player were added. Management expects a meaningful contribution in FY28 and commercial manufacturing from FY29; no revenue or EBITDA split was disclosed.

guidance_outlook: FY28 guidance reiterated: US$400 million organic revenue at around 40% EBITDA margin; FY27 guidance not given beyond expecting a strong year and a sequential improvement in revenue and EBITDA each quarter.
Medium-term target of 50%-plus ROCE.
Working capital is expected to normalise during FY27 after elevated levels this year.
Soft gelatin and injectables trending close to the US$100 million mark, with further growth expected.
Saudi Arabia Semaglutide launch described as imminent, now that freedom to operate is in place.
Scheme with Steriscience injectables and Brooks deferred; to be revisited in about two years if strategic intent holds.
capex_capacity: Part of a US$100 million capex programme; the new line installed a couple of months ago is in qualification and expected to be available from Q1 FY27 (next quarter), with commercial availability in Q2.
Two additional lines are planned this year, giving three lines by end FY27; a fourth injectable line is coming in unit two.

Existing line capped at 200-litre batch size; new lines can go to 500 litres, and up to 750-1,000 litres in the longer term. Moving from 200 to 500 litres raises output about 2.5x (about 60,000 pens/day at 200 litres).
Sterile manufacturing capacity framed as about 225 sterile days per line, roughly 675 days across three lines.
Capacity expansion fully funded through incremental domestic and international bank borrowings; the company added about 400 people at its flagship site.
demand_pricing: Management says demand exceeds supply for at least the next two years; customers have reserved capacity with upfront fees and take-or-pay contracts.
India Semaglutide: partners were present on day one across multiple brands, and the customer base holds almost two-thirds of the Indian generic market by value as of end April.
The company is first and only CDMO for the first three generic Semaglutide approvals in US and Canada; ANVISA approval received, positioning it for Brazil.
Brazil is said to be the largest market outside North America for Semaglutide; no Brazil market-size numbers were given. CDMO terms are ex-works, so tariffs fall on customers.
Oral Semaglutide seen as taking 25% to one-third of the market, with injectables remaining dominant.
Customer advances broadly unchanged from the INR250 crore reported last quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why inventories rose from INR158 crore (March 2025) to INR440 crore (March 2026) for a service provider.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the inventory is customer-funded and fungible, pooled across customers, and is adjusted against customer advances with no material P&L risk; the P&L impact is limited to conversion fees.

qa_highlights.question: Why opex and staff costs rose despite lower revenue.
qa_highlights.answer: Opex is supporting the capacity expansion ahead of the second and third DDC lines, which underpins the FY28 guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Timing of DDC capacity and utilisation.
qa_highlights.answer: The new line is available from next quarter and will ease pressure on the existing line; three lines are expected by end FY27, and the sequential revenue and EBITDA improvement is tied to these additions.

qa_highlights.question: Biologics contribution timing and profitability.
qa_highlights.answer: Agreements are expected over FY27 and FY28, with a meaningful contribution in FY28 and commercial manufacturing from FY29. Management declined to give biologics revenue or EBITDA-loss figures.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year FY27 numbers and Canadian approvals for other clients.

Working capital and inventory build (customer-funded), with normalisation expected in FY27.

Second half (October–March) margins expected to be better than the same period last year.
Devprayag (Uttarakhand, 22 rooms, leased from UP Tourism Board) to start in Q2 FY27; ADR guided at ₹5,000–6,000; capex up to ₹1 cr; lease rental ₹28,000 per year.

Mathura (IHG Holiday Inn Express, scaled to 105 rooms) targeted for FY28 opening; revenue estimate ₹18–20 cr/yr, with management comfortable even at ₹12 cr; project cost ₹49 cr with ₹32 cr HDFC debt at 8.14%; lease rental 5% of gross revenue or ₹54 lakh, whichever higher.

Sheopur Fort (60-key heritage hotel, 90-year lease, competitive bid) to open 35–40 rooms in 1H FY28 with the rest in FY29; budget ₹25 cr (₹10.5 cr internal, ~₹17.5 cr HDFC loan); first-year revenue expected at least ₹12 cr.
Kukru Jungle Camp (Melghat, 15–20 tents, ₹7–7.5 cr capex) expected operational by end-FY28 (March 2028).

capex_capacity: Current portfolio 8 operational properties with 137 keys (3 owned, 5 leased/managed); 4 pipeline properties.

Mathura: planned capacity expanded from 60 to 105 rooms plus banqueting and dining; project cost ₹49 cr; partly funded by ₹11.5 cr IPO component and ₹32 cr HDFC loan; ₹8.79 cr already invested in subsidiary Madhuvan Hospitality.
Sheopur Fort: development commenced; ₹3.5 cr spent on Sheopur and Pench renovation under CWIP; ₹7 cr standalone tangible assets increase YoY largely CWIP.
Parsili project discontinued after regulatory constraints; ₹1.22 cr premium refundable, ₹0.50 cr performance security to be returned; IPO proceeds redeployed to Sheopur.
Panna, Satpura, Sariska and Jawai at advanced/exploration stage; Ratapani land held, construction expected to start shortly.
demand_pricing: Seasonality: safari season October–March drives ADR and revenue; April–June slower; park closed June/July–September, properties remain open with discounts.

Management said competition has not yet hurt ADR or margins, positioning on naturalist-led experience rather than five-star luxury.
Holiday Express brand chosen for Mathura; IHG fee structure of around 7–8% of revenue across four or five components.

qa_highlights.question: What ADR growth can be expected for full-year FY27, given Q1 ADR up ~5% YoY and H2 seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed October–March (H2) should deliver better ADR and revenue than April–June, but gave no formal FY27 number; it said it is 'quite hopeful' of ~5% YoY ADR growth. FY26 property ADRs cited: Pench ₹9,248, Tadoba ₹12,300, Kanha ₹9,500, Rukhad ₹11,800, Bison ₹3,500.

qa_highlights.question: Is 40% FY26 occupancy low, and can it improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the park is closed for about three months (July–September), so 40% is ~54% on the open period; wildlife occupancy tops out near 60%, with Tadoba at 57%. Mathura and other new properties are expected to lift the numbers, with a 12-month operating model for Mathura and Sheopur.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA spike in FY27 or stay flat, and how quickly do new properties break even?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Devprayag and Palash Kothi will add top-line and bottom-line growth this year. New properties take about 4–6 months, up to 6 months, to stabilise, and management agreed break-even around six months after commissioning is a fair read.

qa_highlights.question: What are the revenue terms for Palash Kothi and Devprayag, and what ADRs are guided?
qa_highlights.answer: Palash Kothi (20 rooms, Bandhavgarh) pays Jungle Camps a 13% revenue fee and operates October to June, ADR ₹8,000–12,000. Devprayag (22 rooms, leased from UP Tourism) starts in Q2 FY27 with ADR ₹5,000–6,000, capex up to ₹1 cr, and lease rental ₹28,000 per year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt build-up, interest rate and repayment schedule for Mathura and Sheopur?
qa_highlights.answer: Mathura project cost is ₹49 cr with ₹32 cr HDFC debt at 8.14%; Sheopur budget ₹25 cr with ~₹17.5 cr HDFC loan and ₹10.5 cr internal. Both loans have a 2-year moratorium then 7-year repayment, combined EMI ~₹53 lakh/month (~₹6.5 cr/yr). Management said debt reaching ~₹50 cr by FY28 is correct and no working capital debt is needed.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue is expected from Mathura and Sheopur, and is debt serviceable at downside?
qa_highlights.answer: Mathura revenue estimate ₹18–20 cr/yr, with management comfortable even at ~₹12 cr. Sheopur first-year revenue at least ₹12 cr on ~35 rooms, with 8–10 weddings a year and ~15% other occupancy cited as a cushion. Mathura lease rental is 5% of gross revenue or ₹54 lakh, whichever is higher.

qa_highlights.question: How were the two land-related incidents (Parsili and a second site) handled, and what due-diligence changes followed?

Management said due diligence now includes forest department engagement upfront and checks of revenue, police and court records. It said there is no significant challenge at Sheopur or Mathura, but development timelines apply.

risks_watch: Execution on Mathura (105 rooms, FY28) and Sheopur (35–40 rooms in 1H FY28): both are bank-funded and analysts flagged a possible one-to-two-quarter delay.
Debt rising to ~₹50 cr by FY28 against a small base (FY26 PAT ₹4.22 cr), with combined EMIs of ~₹6.5 cr/yr from the 2-year moratorium ending.
Margin dilution from new properties (ramp-up 4–6 months, up to 6 months) versus management's ~30% target; Q1 margin fell to 27% from 32%.
Land and title risk: a forest-linked issue and a land dispute led to a write-off (~₹50 lakh) and ₹1.35 cr received of the amount due, with a suit filed on the balance.
Lease terms for Sheopur (competitive bid, 90-year lease) and Devprayag; management said no cancellation clause if the property is developed, but the risk of renegotiation was raised.
Kukru (Melghat) still awaiting permissions and water infrastructure; operational target end-FY28 (March 2028).
Parsili refund: ₹1.22 cr premium plus ₹0.50 cr performance security to be returned; management said it could come 'at any time now', with GST not refunded.
Investor relations: an institutional investor complained that requested information was still outstanding after 2–3 months; the company said it would follow up.

It was evasive on several specifics: the Sheopur lease cancellation question, the outstanding IR request, and the timing of the Parsili refund.

544305|2026-06.headline: MobiKwik posted Q1 FY27 PAT of INR76 million, its third straight profitable quarter, with payments GMV up 50% YoY to INR587 billion.
544305|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as its most profitable quarter yet, with PAT of INR76 million and EBITDA of INR158 million, up INR470 million YoY. Payments gross profit rose 31% YoY to INR777 million and financial services gross profit grew 5.6x to INR433 million. Lending disbursements dipped in Q1, while payments revenue fell as card-linked categories were paused under regulatory pressure and UPI (near-zero take rate) grew. Management targets full-year PAT of about INR400 million and EBITDA of about INR750 million including other income, and is scaling a merchant acquiring business that is still loss-making.

financial_highlights.change: Swing of INR495 million vs Q1 FY26; up from INR45 million in Q4 per management
+50% YoY; 14th straight quarter of payments GMV growth

segments.name: Payments
segments.commentary: Gross profit INR777 million (+31% YoY) on revenue of about INR208 crore versus INR59 crore a year ago on similar revenue; net payments take rate 13-15 bps in recent quarters, guided at 12-14 bps long term. Zaakpay (payment gateway) GMV INR25.6 billion; revenue not disclosed.

segments.name: Financial services (lending)
segments.commentary: Gross profit INR433 million (5.6x YoY). Net financial services margin 4.1% in Q3, 5.4% in Q4 and 5.9% in Q1; management guides 4.5-5.5% long term. About 18% of gross lending revenue came from write-backs on past books (about INR16 crore).

segments.name: Merchant (Zaakpay online + offline acquiring)
segments.commentary: Merchant GMV INR125 billion, up 17% QoQ. Business is loss-making with an expected full-year burn of INR50-60 crore; breakeven targeted for FY28. Management expects 10x ramp over two years.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 PAT target of about INR40 crore (INR400 million) and EBITDA of about INR75 crore (INR750 million) including other income; management said it is 'fairly confident'.
Lending disbursements to rise from about INR700 crore per quarter to INR1,000 crore per quarter; management says Q2 is already running at that rate.
Consumer payments revenue expected to grow 5-6% QoQ; merchant revenue expected to grow about 25% QoQ.
Merchant business burn for FY27 capped at INR50-60 crore; breakeven targeted in FY28.
Long-term net payments take rate guided at 12-14 bps; net financial services margin guided at 4.5-5.5%.
Paused card-linked payment categories expected to be relaunched in Q2 FY27.
Digital lending business transfer to wholly-owned subsidiary expected to close in August 2026; own NBFC launch still 'some time away'.
capex_capacity: About INR25 crore of IPO proceeds remains available for buying more merchant devices (soundboxes, EDC, QR); management does not expect more than this needed for FY27.
Merchant ramp: 10x over two years targeted; merchant counts, device counts and merchant revenue not disclosed yet.
Employee benefit expense rose from INR46 crore in Q4 to INR53 crore in Q1, mostly merchant business manpower; expected to rise 5-15% YoY, linked to breakeven.
Lending partner base: nine major NBFC partners in Q1 (10-15 total); top-three lender concentration cut from about 91% (Q2-Q3 FY26) to 87% in Q4 and 71% in Q1.
demand_pricing: Payments revenue dipped because high-take-rate card-linked categories (credit and debit) were paused, while low or zero take-rate UPI and merchant volumes grew; management attributes the pause to regulatory guardrail changes on categories such as rent and education.
Wallet transactions up 68% YoY but GMV up only 24%, as users shift to lower-ticket wallet-on-UPI payments on which no PPI MDR is earned.

UPI: MobiKwik's transactions grew 5x faster than the industry; ranked 13th in NPCI UPI stack rankings and described as second fastest-growing TPAP. No MDR on UPI; PPI-on-UPI MDR mandated by RBI but not rolled out by NPCI.

Lending: Q1 disbursements dipped; 60% of loans went to repeat customers and credit quality improved 25%. Cross-sell from about 96 million engaged non-lending users targeted at INR150-250 crore extra disbursement per quarter; AI funnel engine targeted at about INR100 crore per quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why has quarterly revenue growth been muted over the last seven to eight quarters, and what levers will accelerate it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 was spent re-stabilising businesses and Q1 is the baseline. Lending disbursements are to rise from about INR700 crore to INR1,000 crore per quarter via new lending partners, pre-approved offers to about 96 million engaged users, and an AI funnel engine. Card-linked categories were paused in Q4 and Q1 and are to be relaunched, while merchant revenue is to scale.

qa_highlights.question: Non-UPI GMV trend and whether take rate is falling?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-UPI GMV rose to INR317 billion from INR300 billion in Q4 (about 6%). Management said card-linked categories with higher take rates de-grew under regulatory pressure. Net payments take rate guidance remains 12-14 bps long term, at gross profit level, versus 13-15 bps in recent quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Merchant roll-out: what numbers and how should it be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Merchant GMV was INR125 billion, up 17% QoQ from INR107 billion. Management targets a 10x ramp over two years, expects merchant revenue to grow about 25% QoQ and consumer payments revenue 5-6% QoQ. Merchant counts, device counts and merchant revenue were withheld as too early. About INR25 crore of IPO proceeds remains for devices, and no more is expected to be needed in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Own NBFC timing and FLDG share of lending?
qa_highlights.answer: Digital lending transfer to a wholly-owned subsidiary is expected to close in August 2026 after shareholder approval on 2 July, then CoR will be sought; own NBFC lending is 'still some time away'. As of Q1, 32% of lending was pure distribution and 68% FLDG, with a possible 40/60 mix by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 guidance of INR750 million EBITDA and INR400 million PAT still valid after Q1 operating EBITDA ex other income of about INR80 million?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident in the baseline and expects about INR400 million PAT for FY27 with some growth, plus about INR750 million EBITDA including other income. Q1 PAT of INR76 million annualises to about INR302 million, and improving by INR20-30 million per quarter would reach about INR400 million.

qa_highlights.question: Why did lending disbursements fall in Q1, and what is the top-three lender concentration?
qa_highlights.answer: Top-three lender concentration was cut from about 91% in Q2-Q3 FY26 to 87% in Q4 and 71% in Q1, with two new partners added in Q1. Management said the digital lending transfer to the subsidiary consumed focus in Q1, and it is already at the INR1,000 crore run rate in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why did wallet transactions grow 68% but GMV only 24%, and is PPI-on-UPI monetised?
qa_highlights.answer: Users shifted to lower-ticket wallet-on-UPI payments and card-linked pauses removed high-ticket transactions. No MDR is earned on PPI-on-UPI although RBI mandated it; NPCI has not rolled it out in about 2.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Merchant business burn, breakeven timing and employee cost trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Merchant burn for FY27 is capped at INR50-60 crore (about INR15-16 crore in Q1); breakeven targeted for FY28. Employee benefit expense rose to INR53 crore from INR46 crore in Q4, and merchant-related manpower cost may grow 5-15% YoY, linked to breakeven.

risks_watch: Payments revenue dip from paused card-linked categories (credit and debit, rent, education); relaunch targeted for Q2 FY27 and not yet proven.
Lending disbursements fell in Q1; Q2 INR1,000 crore run rate depends on the digital lending transfer closing in August 2026 without disruption.
Gross take-rate compression as UPI (near-zero take rate) and merchant volumes grow; net payments take rate guided at 12-14 bps long term versus 13-15 bps recently.
Net financial services margin of 5.9% in Q1 includes write-backs (about 18% of gross lending revenue); management guides 4.5-5.5% long term.
Merchant business still loss-making (FY27 burn INR50-60 crore); merchant revenue, device and merchant counts not disclosed; breakeven FY28.
Regulatory dependence: PPI-on-UPI MDR mandated by RBI but not rolled out by NPCI; no timeline given.
Own NBFC launch still 'some time away'; CoR pending until digital lending transfer completes.
Q1 PAT of INR76 million rests on one quarter; full-year PAT of about INR400 million requires sustained sequential improvement of about INR20-30 million per quarter.
key_quotes: Q1 FY27 has been our most successful and profitable quarter yet.
We are targeting full-year PAT profitability for this financial year, and Q1 is of course the baseline.
So yes, INR75 crores EBITDA and INR40 crores PAT is the kind of numbers that we are fairly confident of achieving.
It's too early. Apart from the GMV for merchant, we are not revealing any other numbers yet.
544305|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on profitability and guidance, with a repeated 'fairly confident' stance on FY27 PAT and EBITDA targets. Cautious and evasive on merchant metrics (no merchant counts, devices or revenue, calling it 'too early'), on regulatory issues around UPI MDR (expressed frustration), and on the timing of its own NBFC.

544306|2026-06.headline: Sai Life Sciences Q1 FY27 revenue rose 12% YoY to INR553 crore, with CRO up 26% and CDMO up 6%; management guides to a stronger H2.
544306|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR553 crore against INR496 crore a year earlier, up about 12% YoY. CRO (about 40% of revenue) grew about 26% YoY, while CDMO (about 60%) grew about 6%. Management said the quarter was in line with expectations and reiterated a stronger H2 as new capacity comes online, with the Discovery facility already commissioned and sold out and Bidar production block 1 due in H2/Q3. Management reaffirmed the mid-term revenue growth guidance of 15-20% and EBITDA margin of 28-30%, and FY27 capex of INR1,100-1,300 crore.

financial_highlights.change: about +12% YoY vs INR496 crore in Q1 FY26

segments.name: CRO / Discovery
segments.commentary: Revenue up about 26% YoY. About 65% of customers now use integrated discovery services, mainly biotech; a pilot with a large pharma converted to a long-term high-volume discovery chemistry partnership. Discovery capacity came on stream in Q1 and is already sold out.

segments.name: CDMO / CMC
segments.commentary: Revenue up about 6% YoY, described as lumpy. Portfolio is 33 active commercial molecules and 14 late-phase molecules. Three of the four commercial contracts expected this year were added in Q1; management said three are commercial supplies, primary supplier in about two of three (anecdotal).

guidance_outlook: Mid-term (3-5 year) revenue growth guidance of 15-20% reiterated; management said guidance should be viewed over a longer horizon, not quarterly.
EBITDA margin range of 28-30% reiterated.
H2 FY27 expected to be stronger than H1, with capacity coming on stream by end-Q2 or early Q3; management referenced a 40/60 historical H1/H2 split, with FY26 at about 48/52.
FY27 capex guidance INR1,100-1,300 crore unchanged; no FY28 capex guidance yet.
Target of about 1,150 KL capacity by FY27 reconfirmed.
Expects to convert at least two large pharma customers to integrated models in FY27.
Formulation (oral solids up to Phase 2) expected to be operational in about six months, within the current fiscal year.
capex_capacity: Discovery capacity came on stream in Q1 FY27 and is sold out, ahead of the one-to-1.5-year fill timeline management had assumed.
Bidar: two production blocks of 225 KL each (450 KL total); first block due for completion and operation in H2/Q3 FY27, on track.
First dedicated peptide development lab coming online shortly for a top-tier pharma company; GMP pilot-scale peptide facility coming online soon for clinical supply.
Commercial peptide manufacturing at a new greenfield site near Hyderabad expected to be operational in 2028; groundbreaking planned. Peptide spend to end-2028 likely below INR300 crore.
XDC Center of Excellence close to opening; ADC pilot-scale space under build.
demand_pricing: Management said Indian outsourcing demand is strengthened by geopolitical concerns and IP worries, with customers using India for diversification.

FTE (dedicated team) model: one top-tier pharma FTE relationship expanded from small scale to a sizable dedicated contract running end-to-end from discovery to commercial; another large pharma process development FTE deal expected to close by end-Q2, with work from Q3.

Pipeline sourced via three routes: biotech molecules acquired by pharma partners, molecules transferred from acquirers, and FTE-led progression. Five of six late-phase molecules added in 15 months came via large pharma FTE relationships.
Phase 3 pipeline: one customer approved in FY26, two more with regulatory milestones in FY27, one expected Q2 FY28.
Modalities: about 4-5% of revenue from new modalities, all in development and discovery, none in commercial. Peptide work is mainly early-stage discovery.
Sai works with 19 of the top 25 pharma companies. Five FDA-approved molecules in calendar 2025 involved Sai in discovery, development or commercial manufacturing.

qa_highlights.question: Has the shift to integrated CRDMO and big pharma FTE engagements accelerated this calendar year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is still early, with relationships growing from one service at a time; FTE model started about 15 months ago and acceleration is seen mainly in scale and scope.

qa_highlights.question: Is the H2-weighted FY27 guidance due to capacity, given the historical split?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management said FY26 was about 48/52 H1/H2 versus a historical 40/60, and capacity additions are behind the stronger H2 call.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex threshold and what would cause a slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Internal hurdle rates are set above the company's ROCE/ROE targets. Capacity-addition capex can be slowed if demand slows; capability-building capex is harder to defer absent severe circumstances.

qa_highlights.question: Why guide 15-20% when the pipeline is large and recent quarters slowed?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is framed over 3-5 years given lumpiness; management said it is not constraining growth and FY26 grew close to 30%, with quarterly revenue driven by delivery timing.

qa_highlights.question: Is the AI initiative the same as the high-throughput experimentation platform?
qa_highlights.answer: No. HTE generates more data points per experiment; the AI initiative targets non-value-added chemist and operator work, with an update expected before year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the commercial profile of the four new commercial contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Three of four are commercial supplies, described as decently sized by value; one is a lower-volume product. Primary supplier in about two of three, anecdotally.

risks_watch: CDMO growth of about 6% YoY and quarterly lumpiness; H2 recovery depends on Bidar block 1 and formulation start-up timelines.
Capex of INR1,100-1,300 crore is heavy; FY28 capex guidance not yet given.
Formulation entry (oral solids to Phase 2, China+1 driven) is new; management says it is not yet commercial and profitability was questioned.
Management did not disclose revenue at the individual molecule or customer level, and declined to discuss mAb strategy or fermentation capex.
Commercial peptide capacity not due until 2028.
544306|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on demand and the FTE model, with a long-term framing; cautious and evasive on quarterly guidance, customer-level revenue, and capex phasing beyond FY27. Management said the quarter was in line with expectations.
key_quotes: We remain confident in our ability to sustain our longer-term revenue growth guidance of 15% to 20%, and the EBITDA range of 28% to 30%.
Generally, we don't quantify what we're doing with each customer.

544307|2026-03.headline: Vishal Mega Mart Q4 FY26 revenue rose 22.2% to INR 3,114 crore with same-store sales growth of 13.2%, while management flagged input inflation from May.
544307|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR 3,114 crore (+22.2% YoY), with same-store sales growth (SSSG) accelerating to 13.2% from 11% for FY26. Adjusted EBITDA margin widened to 8.8% from 8.2% and PAT rose 45.9% to INR 168 crore. Management attributed the strength to a consumption uptick after income tax and GST cuts, plus heavier promotions ahead of the spring/summer season. Management said input inflation, mainly petroleum-linked materials and fabric, began in late April and May, and it committed to keep private-brand discounts to third-party brands at least at current levels (about 40% on apparel).

segments.name: Apparel (fast fashion, biggest category)
segments.commentary: Q4 SSSG by price point: entry 11.1%, mid-price 13.6%, fashionable (top 2-3 price points) 14.7%. Management said fashion was the fastest-growing segment in Q4 and FY26.

segments.name: Private brands
segments.commentary: 74.1% of FY26 revenue; two brands above INR 1,000 crore and six more above INR 500 crore revenue.

segments.name: Quick commerce
segments.commentary: Expanded to 745 stores across 505 cities; registered users reached 1.3 crore.

segments.name: Small format stores
segments.commentary: 13 stores in total, 3 opened in Q4 FY26; management said store EBITDA and revenue per sq ft match large-format stores.

guidance_outlook: No numerical FY27 guidance given; management said it is difficult to model the West Asia situation and fuel price impact.
Private-brand discount to market leaders on apparel (about 40%) to remain at least the same, with a possible wider gap.
Store expansion will not slow; management said it aims to open more stores where practical.
Input inflation (petroleum-linked plastics, polyester, detergent inputs) is starting to flow through; full impact expected in the balance of May and June.
Fabric prices rising about 10-11%, per management's current range for suppliers.
Working capital cycle expected to stay at FY26 levels, per the CFO.
capex_capacity: Store count 795 at March 2026 after 105 openings in FY26 (25 in Q4); presence in 535 cities after adding 77 cities in FY26.
47 of the 105 FY26 openings were in South India (Kerala, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka); 5 in Gujarat and 3 in Maharashtra.
Trading area 1.34 crore sq ft at March 2026.
Karnataka store areas reduced in many stores; sales per sq ft has risen and is now in line with the national average, per CFO.
Lease escalation about 15% every three years (about 5% a year), per CFO.
demand_pricing: Management attributed Q4 SSSG acceleration to a consumption uptick after income tax and GST rate cuts, plus extra investment in growth and promotions.
FY26 SSSG of 11% split: 7 points from new customers and transactions, 2 points from more items per customer, 2 points from higher price points.

Pricing is set by price point: no uniform price increases; opening and low price points are protected, higher fashion price points get more room, and management aims for price increases to be volume-neutral.
Suppliers facing gas and labour shortages earlier in the period; management said vendor supply is improving but labour has not fully returned.
Competition: management believes it is gaining share, citing 7 of the 11 SSSG points coming from new customers; it did not name V2 or V-Mart directly.
Management expects down-trading benefits if demand weakens, given private brands are 30-50% cheaper than third-party brands in food and grocery.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 SSSG acceleration, and was there pre-buying?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a general consumption uptick after income tax and GST cuts, plus higher growth investment in the quarter. It did not frame it as pre-buying.

qa_highlights.question: How will private-label pricing respond to rising leader-brand prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management committed to keep the discount to leader brands at least at 40% for apparel, and to try to widen it if possible.

qa_highlights.question: How did the company handle the cotton inflation of 2021-22?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it took a margin hit then, absorbed much of the increase, and used cost initiatives such as removing poly bags, using gunny bags, shipping shoes without outer cartons, and CAD cutting to reduce waste.

qa_highlights.question: Are price increases neutral, incremental or negative to apparel sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it aims for neutral, since high-fashion price points show lower elasticity, and it avoids raising opening price points.

qa_highlights.question: What is the dividend policy given strong free cash flow?

qa_highlights.question: Are the new small-format and newer-state stores performing?

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 gross margin compress, and why did working capital improve?

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for rent and operating leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said rent rises about 5% a year under lease terms, so double-digit SSSG should keep producing operating leverage. He said Q4 rent looked low because of lease renewals in Q4 FY25.

Dividend policy remains undecided despite strong cash generation.

544307|2026-06.headline: Vishal Mega Mart Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18.7% to INR 3,727 crore on 10% same-store sales growth; operating EBITDA margin 10.4%.
544307|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations reached INR 3,727 crore, up 18.7% YoY, driven by 10% same-store sales growth. Operating EBITDA was INR 387 crore (up 19.3%, margin 10.4% vs 10.3%) and PAT was INR 259 crore (up 25.6%, margin 6.9% vs 6.6%). Gross margin improved to 28.7% from 28.4%, mainly from lower promotional spend rather than price hikes. The company added 27 stores to reach 819 across 559 cities, with management flagging elevated inflation as a demand headwind expected to ease in later quarters.

No further price increases planned beyond those already taken, assuming current conditions persist.

demand_pricing: Same-store sales growth of 10%: new customer acquisition up 8%, existing customer spend up 3%.

Highest-priced apparel fashion grew 13.9% same-store sales growth.
Gross margin gain came mainly from lower promotional intensity, with little contribution from price hikes.
Management says no new competitors entered apparel and expansion pace from existing players did not rise sharply this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why is small-format expansion slow when small towns may suit it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said small-format stores were a test phase; they now match larger formats on revenue per sq ft and ROCE, and expansion will accelerate, with UP and Haryana as the only states so far. Large-format stores are still being opened alongside.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin improve despite cost pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin rose from 28.4% to 28.7%, mainly because promotional spend was lower YoY; prices were held to protect same-store sales, with little price-hike effect.

qa_highlights.question: What is the organisational change and the foreign ownership cap?
qa_highlights.answer: Sashi Gumma replaces Manoj, who is leaving after more than 10 years, in the same role, with no change to the org structure. The 49.99% foreign cap is to stay Indian owned and controlled; it applies because subsidiary Airplaza runs multi-brand retail.

qa_highlights.question: What is quick commerce's contribution and profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Quick commerce contributes 2-9% of store revenue, with most locations at 5% or more; average bill is about INR 800, slightly above offline, and 20% of quick commerce customers are new to Vishal.

qa_highlights.question: Is the rise in employee cost per sq ft structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Gupta said the increase came from significant minimum wage hikes across several states, which is a structural change; management will try to optimise but cannot fully offset it.

qa_highlights.question: What is closing inventory and status of the new format?
qa_highlights.answer: Closing inventory was INR 1,900 crore. The new format is near its first pilot store launch, with one or two more pilots planned before a roll-out decision.

risks_watch: Elevated inflation weighing on demand; management expects easing but gave no firm timeline.
Gross margin sustainability: the gain depends on lower promotions and holding prices; West Asia developments are an open risk.
Structural rise in employee costs from minimum wage increases across several states.
Competitive pressure in apparel from value retailers; management says the competitor set is unchanged, but pace is a watch item.
Leadership change: COO Manoj departs and Sashi Gumma replaces him; further org changes not discussed.
Small-format and RFID roll-outs are gradual; timing and benefits remain to be proven at scale.

544307|2026-09.headline: Vishal Mega Mart Q2 FY27 revenue rose 14% to INR3,399 crore, but same-store sales growth slowed to 5.4% as festivals shifted into Q3.
544307|2026-09.overview: Revenue from operations grew 14% YoY to INR3,399 crore in Q2 FY27, with same-store sales growth (SSSG) of 5.4%, which management says would have been about 9% without the festival shift. Operating EBITDA rose 3.7% to INR262 crore, but margin fell to 7.7% from 8.5% on operating deleverage from low fixed-cost absorption. Adjusted PAT grew 6.4% to INR172 crore, with margin at 5.1% versus 5.4%. Store network reached 844 with 26 gross additions in the quarter, and management said it sees no demand moderation despite inflation.

segments.commentary: 18 small-format stores now, with 2 added in Q2. Management sees potential for upwards of 3,000 stores nationally, but will open them only where large-format opportunity diminishes.

segments.commentary: First pilot store launched in Q2 targeting young affluent urban shoppers. Management reports footfall-to-purchase conversion above 50% but says it is still learning and has not set a rollout plan.

segments.commentary: Expanded to 781 stores across 532 cities, with over 1.5 crore registered users. Management is increasing advertising and digital spend, starting in Delhi.

EBITDA margin expected to improve about 30 bps a year over time, assuming double-digit growth against 6-7% store-level cost inflation.

Inventory days were around 65 in the base period versus 59-60 in H1 FY27 per an analyst's calculation; management attributed the gap to the festival shift, with the stock build happening three weeks later this year.
Weather and rainfall were uneven, causing one- to two-day revenue disruptions in some regions, but no regional demand weakness was reported.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 3-4% festive shift carry into Q3, and what Q3 SSSG is needed for a 9% first-half-equivalent?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed Q3 SSSG must be above 10% for the nine months to look double-digit, since festivals (Durga Puja, Dussehra, Navratri) moved from September to October.

qa_highlights.question: Will vendor price hikes hurt gross margin in Q3 and Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cost re-engineering has protected gross margin and vendors are already charging higher prices, so no material impact is expected in Q3 or Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost rise about INR10 crore QoQ, and what SSSG offsets the wage pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the rise reflects incremental ESOP cost and new stores, with minimum wage increases already in Q1. He said 8-10% SSSG is enough to offset the higher employee cost.

qa_highlights.question: How are price increases split across price points, and will there be more?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no further price increases are planned at the current inflation level, including after the festive season, and that opening price points were protected.

qa_highlights.question: How are new store openings split by region, and will Tier 1 entry follow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 24 of 26 Q2 openings were in Tier 2/3 towns and 15 were in South. It is piloting in Maharashtra and Gujarat, with stores in Ahmedabad, Surat, Pune and Baroda.

qa_highlights.question: How will the cash on the balance sheet be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to more stores each year, Belong & Co. and small-format capacity, warehouses in East, South and West India, and quick commerce advertising. It said the board is still evaluating options.

We would not want to inflate our gross margin.

544309|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 18.5% YoY to INR857 crore and EBITDA margin hit about 35%, with PAT of INR206 crore, alongside a pending TruBridge acquisition.
544309|2026-03.overview: Management reported its sixth consecutive quarter of growth, with Q4 FY26 revenue of about INR857 crore (up 18.5% YoY, 5.2% QoQ), EBITDA of about INR300 crore (35% margin), and PAT of INR206 crore (up 39% YoY). FY26 revenue was INR3,193 crore (up 20%), EBITDA INR1,091 crore (up 34%) and PAT INR721 crore (up 48%). Management said the company is pivoting its go-to-market toward land-and-expand with system-owned provider groups, and is pursuing AI-native products and the pending TruBridge acquisition. Headcount rose to 13,331 from 12,661 but fell 5.2% QoQ. Management declined to give quantitative guidance beyond an FY27 effective tax rate of about 22%.

segments.commentary: Management described RCM as the primary buying entry point for system-owned provider groups, with ambulatory RCM recognised by KLAS and Black Book. Management also cited a top health system win for RCM and value-based care.

segments.commentary: Select is a multi-variant AI scribing product, with a clinician in the loop for complex encounters and fully AI for simpler ones; management cited high accuracy in two specialties. MyCare Hub is a multi-agent patient engagement product that ThinkDTM brought in through an acqui-hire, and it and the cycle engine are now available on Epic Connection Hub.

segments.commentary: Management announced a win for the entire IKS platform at Holyoke Medical Center. It did not give a financial size.

Effective tax rate for FY27 is expected at about 22% for the IKS standalone business; consolidated ETR will be shared after the TruBridge deal closes.

Aspirational target: grow from about INR1,000 crore (LTM Dec 2025) to INR3,000 crore by FY30, with net zero debt targeted in that period.
Management expects the TruBridge deal to be leveraged at about 3x at close, with deleveraging through internal accruals; regulatory approvals are in progress.

TruBridge acquisition (EHR in about 700 to 800 hospitals; about 2,200 hospitals in the segment, per management) is awaiting regulatory approval after signing.

About 90% of revenue is repeat business; top 10 and top 5 client vintage averages 5 to 6 years.
Pricing is partly outcome-based, which management said gives a margin advantage when AI reduces effort; management said AI-led deflation pressure has not been seen yet.
Competition is split into EHR vendors, point-solution vendors and platform players; management said entry barriers are lowest for point-solution players and that consolidation is expected.
Management said the company has not received any pricing pushback so far and that its AI pricing is per feature, not per seat.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company approaching a possible CommonSpirit Health opportunity and Epic marketplace listings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment on specific opportunities. It said CommonSpirit is on its radar as ministries are unbundled from the Tenet arrangement, and that it has a history working with several CommonSpirit ministries.

qa_highlights.question: How will the tech stack for the ambulatory and acute platforms converge after integration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is zero actual overlap in customers, but it will modernise the EHR to PostgreSQL and integrate its AI corpus, a roughly two-year journey for the core EHR.

qa_highlights.question: What is the risk from cheaper AI for the business model?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cheaper AI generation is a tailwind, since IKS builds its own AI and is paid for outcomes rather than effort.

qa_highlights.question: When will growth stop being lumpy, and can the company catch up on growth after six quarters of strong growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give guidance and said the journey is not linear. It pointed to the 3x revenue target to FY30 and a 12% share of its TAM.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company seeing AI-driven productivity pressure on pricing, as IT and BPO peers reported?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its pricing is outcome-based and not purely effort-based, so AI productivity gains flow to margins. It said some workflows are easily automated and get priced accordingly.

qa_highlights.question: What are the cost run-rate and ETR outlook for FY27, and is the ETR for IKS or consolidated?
qa_highlights.answer: The FY27 ETR of about 22% applies to IKS standalone; consolidated figures will come after the TruBridge deal closes. Management does not guide on individual cost parameters and uses incentives to align employees.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any overlap between TruBridge's EHR and IKS's offerings, and what is the plan for EHR share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said TruBridge's EHR serves about 700 hospitals, roughly 35% of a segment of about 2,200 hospitals, dominated by MEDITECH and MEDHOST. The priority is modernising the EHR and deploying IKS services, not gaining EHR share, and management said it would not bank on share gains.

qa_highlights.question: Would the company consider acquisitions, and how will the TruBridge deal be financed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said TruBridge would be funded with debt at about 3x leverage at close, with deleveraging from accruals. It expects tuck-in deals to continue, but not transformative ones soon, and it wants to avoid equity dilution.

risks_watch: TruBridge acquisition: regulatory approvals pending, about 3x leverage at close, and one-time deal costs in Q1 FY27.
Q1 FY27 seasonality: US patient footfall is weakest in Q1 CY, and management flagged higher other expenses.
EHR modernisation to PostgreSQL is a roughly two-year process with migration risk. Management said the RCM business is independent, but the migration could impede EHR-linked product rollout.
Competitive intensity from private equity-backed RCM players (for example Carlyle deals) and consolidation in the US RCM market.
Client count is falling (about 600 from about 700 at IPO) through tail-client pruning, and the company is pivoting to system-owned provider groups with an unproven land-and-expand motion.
Q4 PAT margin quality: finance costs fell after a Q3 one-off write-off, and the ROE decline is partly due to revaluation and rupee depreciation.
544309|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on growth, margin and AI strategy, with explicit reluctance to give guidance or predict quarterly rates. Evasive on TruBridge integration details and specific client opportunities, citing the pending deal and confidentiality.

544309|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 21% YoY (12% constant currency) to INR893 crores, with reported EBITDA of INR294 crores at 33% margin.

qa_highlights.question: What organic constant-currency growth is healthy over the medium term, and is margin expansion coming from currency?

qa_highlights.question: How does SLM fit with LLMs, and where does glass-box/explainable AI sit?

qa_highlights.question: Why acquire TruBridge and what criteria govern acquisitions?

Criteria: strategic thesis first, leverage tolerable relative to EBITDA, and accretive price; $68 million EBITDA bought for ~$550 million.

qa_highlights.question: Is TruBridge's margin of 22-23% fixable, and does the INR3,000 crore target rule out M&A?
qa_highlights.answer: Levers include existing and in-build technology plus offshore human-in-the-loop to restore early-to-mid 30s margins. INR3,000 crores is achievable without another acquisition, but M&A is not ruled out; white space seen as large.

qa_highlights.question: Does Abridge's platform move threaten IKS, and is pricing under pressure in renewals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management respects Abridge but sees ~30 vendors aspiring to platforms and rising competition. Recent five-year deal signed at healthy price; pricing pressure expected but margin leverage maintained.

qa_highlights.question: Is TruBridge still EPS accretive for FY27 after revenue reset?

risks_watch: TruBridge revenue reset: steady-state revenue cut to about $300 million from $340 million, with ~$8 million a quarter of non-profitable service lines to be exited and ~$2-3 million a quarter of customer discounts during transformation; track whether the $68 million EBITDA holds through the reset.

Revenue from operations reached INR 3,980 million (up 31%), EBITDA INR 2,445 million (up 39%, margin 61.4%) and PAT INR 1,858 million (up 43%). H1 revenue grew 27%, EBITDA 34% and PAT 37%. Management said H2 will keep outperforming, but did not give a new numeric target. India standalone EBITDA margin fell about 340 bps to 69.5% due to people, marketing and commission spend.

segments.name: LGD jewellery certification
segments.commentary: Grew 47% in Q2 and 46% in H1. Management cited growth in Europe, Latin America and Australia alongside the US.

segments.name: Natural diamond certification
segments.commentary: Natural loose certification grew 8% in Q2 (up 5% QoQ) and 7% in H1. Natural jewellery certification grew only 3% in the quarter.

segments.commentary: Grew 331% in Q2 and 261% in H1, largely from the AGL consolidation since January. AGL added about 3% to group revenue growth in Q2 and H1.

segments.name: Overseas subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Subsidiary revenue grew 49% in Q2; 31% excluding AGL. Overseas certification revenue grew 31% without AGL.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance from May was 15% revenue growth and 20% EBITDA growth. Management now says it expects to outperform this for the full year, similar to H1 (revenue +27%, EBITDA +34%), but gave no new numeric target.
Management said no LGD slowdown is expected in coming quarters, citing grower capacity additions. Natural diamond business is expected to keep momentum for the next two quarters.
October trends were described as rock solid, with Diwali on 8 November 2026 versus 20 October 2025, which shifts some festive stocking into October.
Capital allocation order: growth investment first, then M&A, then dividends. Dividend decisions are made by the Board with each results set.
Management expects EBITDA growth to keep outpacing revenue growth through operating leverage, but did not give a steady-state margin figure.
capex_capacity: Large Indian growers are adding reactors and doubling capacity within 3 years, per management; supply is described as at its base rather than its peak.
Operations started in Italy this year, Saudi Arabia is being prepared, and a company was set up in Botswana in September.
AI-based work allocation and scheduling is now in use in labs, letting the same team grade more stones faster without changing grading standards.
AGL colour-stone methods are being rolled out in IGI's other labs, with dedicated setups planned for large customers. Global expansion of AGL services is planned but locations were not disclosed.
demand_pricing: Lab-grown wholesale prices have stabilised in the INR 118-120 range per management's Investor Day deck. Certification costs 2-3% of retail price.

Q2 ARP rose 4% YoY to INR 891: AGL added 2%, and the base business added 2% from a higher LGD mix (54% vs 52%). Sequentially, ARP fell about 12% on a lower LGD loose mix (down 4%) and a higher jewellery mix.
Natural diamond buyers are delaying purchases due to high and volatile gold prices.
Management said 4Cs grading remains the reporting standard and that it sees no demand shift to simplified classification. It said there are no printing rights for certificates granted to anyone.

qa_highlights.question: Is the LGD revenue surge a pre-festive stocking effect, and will Q3 taper?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said LGD revenue has been steady at about INR 2,100 million in Q1 and Q2 and expects no slowdown, citing grower capacity additions. Natural growth is expected to pick up, with traction starting and momentum expected to continue for two more quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Should guidance be raised given H1 overshoot?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 will outperform the 15% revenue and 20% EBITDA guidance, similar to H1. It did not give a new number, but confirmed when asked that H2 growth would be above the original guidance.

qa_highlights.question: How will the surplus cash be used: M&A or higher dividends?
qa_highlights.answer: Priority is growth investment first (Italy, Saudi Arabia), then M&A, then dividends. The September interim dividend was INR 2.55 per share.

qa_highlights.question: Is there grading inconsistency at IGI, and are the top Surat manufacturers printing certificates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management denied giving printing rights to anyone. It said grading involves multiple checks, is ISO accredited for 18 years, and that there is no gap versus other labs.

qa_highlights.question: Does the AI push allow smaller labs to compete cheaply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said IGI's image dataset from c.4.5 million certificates a quarter is hard to replicate and is used to build its AI and ML capability, improving turnaround times.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin in India fall and when will the investments pay off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the India margin drop of about 340 bps to leadership hiring, marketing and commission spend. It gave no timeline for payback, but said the group margin was 60.1% for FY26, 60.4% in Q1 and 61.4% in Q2.

risks_watch: Natural diamond certification growth of 8% lags LGD, and natural jewellery grew only 3%. Watch whether festive-season recovery materialises.
India standalone EBITDA margin fell to 69.5% from 72.8%. Watch whether the people and marketing spend yields a return.
Diwali timing shift means some Q2 festive demand was pulled from Q3 by September stocking. Watch Q3 for payback.
AGL integration: gemstone growth is driven by acquisition and the organic base is not disclosed. Watch the AGL contribution and the global rollout.
Grading consistency questions were raised by a市场 participant and a Surat source. Management denied them. Monitor for any disputes or customer complaints.
544311|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth and tailwinds, but evasive on quantifying the new FY27 target and on Surat grading and printing-rights questions. Management pushed back on pricing and competition questions with general statements rather than data.
key_quotes: This has been the best quarter in IGI's history.
We expect to keep outperforming for the full year as well, similar to the H1 delivery.
We don't anticipate any slowdown as far as lab-grown business is concerned for the coming quarters as well.

Gross margin 54.6% vs 60.8%; management cited lower export share (exports higher margin, about 60% gross margin vs about 42-43% domestic on order book), adverse mix (lower co-extrusion), and H2 commodity inflation; 6.2 pp EBITDA margin impact.

Russia: no revenue yet; only a couple of converting machines shipped; branch office approved for CIS.

544319|2026-06.headline: Senores Q1 FY27 revenue rose 36% YoY to INR180 crores and EBITDA 87% to INR54 crores (~30% margin); FY27 guidance is 30-40% revenue and 50-60% PAT growth.

segments.name: GScale Energy (AI data-centre products and turnkey)
segments.commentary: Targeting ~INR250 crore revenue (management clarified revenue, not bookings) by end-FY27; five customers in advanced discussions (three global MNCs, two Indian). Expects 23-25% EBITDA margin and ~20% ROCE on ~INR500 crore investment; plant ~4 lakh sq ft, first phase operational by November.

segments.name: GL Hakko (Japan glass-lining technology partner)
segments.commentary: GL Hakko revenue ~INR200 crore; target INR400 crore in 2-3 years. Shell-and-tube glass-lining heat exchangers already being made in India (80% built in Japan, 20% finished locally); exports planned from FY28.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue guidance ~INR1,450 crore (core ~INR1,200 crore plus GScale ~INR250 crore).
Core business growth guided at 40-50% for FY27, up from earlier 25-30% minimum; management excluded current order book from the change.
EBITDA margin to be maintained at 17-18% going forward; GScale margin expected 23-25%.
Working capital days to fall below 200 in FY27 (September-half expected), and GScale targeted at 100-150 days.
GScale data-centre projects targeted at 18-20 months versus 24-36 months industry typical; ROCE expected ~20%.
FY28 GScale and consolidated revenue guidance deferred ('we will guide soon'); no quantified margin expansion from semiconductor glass-lining yet.
capex_capacity: GScale has acquired ~4 lakh sq ft factory space; ~2 lakh sq ft in full execution with robotic equipment ordered from multiple countries, arriving by mid-September.
GScale operations targeted to start by November 2026; further 2 lakh sq ft (factories 3 and 4) to be added by December 2026.
Total GScale investment cited at ~INR500 crore.
Management said full-fledged manufacturing setup to be complete around March (2027).
Manufacturing mix: GScale to make 60-70% of equipment in-house and source the balance; management says this can be increased.
Semiconductor-grade glass-lining reactors: glass sourced from Japan, fabrication and glass spraying in India; no technology transfer agreement currently.
demand_pricing: Management cites India data-centre capacity of 1.8 GW expected to grow to ~10.2-10.5 GW by ~2030-31; investment of USD5-7 million per MW, of which ~65% is products and installation.
GScale has one big order from a top Indian client for semiconductor-related glass-lining reactors (GL Hakko-linked); pilot-plant order for LED/electronic chemicals also cited.
Shell-and-tube glass-lining heat exchanger price cut claimed: from ~INR30 lakh to ~INR12-15 lakh per unit (>50% lower), with management arguing it is a client benefit and margin-accretive.
India glass-lining TAM cited at ~INR1,500 crore; shell-and-tube heat exchanger TAM ~INR2,000 crore in India and ~USD2 billion globally.
Management claims no global competitor makes the GL Hakko shell-and-tube glass-lining heat exchanger or low-leaching glass; unverified.
Export share remained low at 2-3% in Q1 due to global uncertainty; shipping costs cited by an analyst as up ~4x.

qa_highlights.question: What is the GScale business, margins, and timing of order conversion?
qa_highlights.answer: Brahma Reddy said five customers (three global MNCs, two Indian) are in LOI or near-order stage; target is ~INR250 crore revenue by end-FY27, clarified as revenue not order booking. Margin guided at 23-25% EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Margin expansion from semiconductor glass-lining products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins will rise slightly as shell-and-tube and semiconductor products scale from September, but gave no quantified figure.

qa_highlights.question: Is there an unexecuted order book for core business?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, ~INR1,400 crore after Q1 billing, with some billing expected in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why is margin down and is it structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the decline to mechanisation in two units, which reduced consumable consumption; employee costs rising with recruitment. Management said margins will be maintained at 17-18%.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital days and drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said days were ~320 last year, targeted below 200 by September, driven by customer advances and receivable collection with stock held flat.

qa_highlights.question: Royalty on imported technology?
qa_highlights.answer: No royalty currently; licensing model, with JV and technology-transfer discussions ongoing.

qa_highlights.question: Data-centre project timelines and value-add?

risks_watch: GScale execution: equipment arrival (mid-September), November start, and ramp to INR250 crore revenue in FY27 with only ~2 lakh sq ft initially in full execution.
Working capital: management's <200 day target versus ~320 days last year; GScale projects may carry advances and receivables.
Margin pressure: the 17.5% EBITDA margin reflects rising employee and other costs; management says 17-18% is sustainable.
Dependence on GL Hakko technology: critical glass manufacturing remains in Japan with no technology transfer agreement; GL Hakko stake to step up to 51% only on targets.
Forward guidance gaps: FY28 numbers for GScale and consolidated revenue not yet guided; a Q&A figure of ~INR3,000 crore for FY28 was not confirmed by management.
Customer concentration: GScale's five named-stage customers are unnamed; claims of no global competitor are unverified.
key_quotes: This has been another record quarter for us, and I want to say this clearly , this is not a one-time achievement.
Working capital days I think last year 320 days, 320 days. And this year we are that is going to coming down to below 200 days.
Margins? No. No.
Mr. Shiva, go ahead.
Brahma Reddy: We will guide soon.
