544335|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 61% YoY to INR820 crore and PAT rose 77.8% to INR44.92 crore; order book stood at about INR1,235 crore at 31 March 2026.
544335|2026-03.overview: B.R.Goyal Infrastructure reported FY26 revenue from operations up 61% YoY to INR820 crore, with EBITDA (excluding other income) up about 82% to INR75 crore and EBITDA margin up 105 bps to 9.13%. H2 FY26 revenue was INR478 crore (up 61% YoY) with EBITDA of INR47.48 crore at a 9.93% margin. Management said the order book declined YoY to about INR1,235 crore, which it attributed to bidding for larger-ticket projects and faster execution. The company also flagged a preferential warrant issue of up to INR13.09 crore, higher borrowing limits, a maiden dividend of INR0.25 per share, and entry into wastewater civil works.

segments.name: EPC (roads, buildings, urban)
segments.commentary: Management cited an EPC EBITDA margin of about 14% for FY26 (13-15% range), up from 12-13% last year. FY26 revenue split by business: road/EPC about 49%, RMC about 3%, toll collection about 47%. Sector revenue cited: road/building EPC about INR395 crore, RMC about INR20 crore, wastewater about INR6 crore, toll about INR388 crore.

segments.name: Toll collection contracts (TCC)
segments.commentary: Toll EBITDA margin about 4% in FY26 (about 3% last year); management also cited a toll segment margin of about 2.5%. Toll strike rate is above 70%. Recent NHAI toll awards include Kathpur INR91.71 crore, Simliya INR86.7 crore, Aashpur INR70.39 crore, Khambara INR47.83 crore, Paraghat INR33.27 crore.

segments.name: Wastewater treatment
segments.commentary: Entered in FY26 with a Tamil Nadu project of about INR167 crore; wastewater order book about INR162 crore. Management cited a 15-20% EBITDA margin for the vertical, but work is currently subcontracted or on name-lending basis with no technology tie-up. Target contribution of 20-25% of revenue in the near future.

segments.name: Ready-mix concrete and real estate
segments.commentary: RMC revenue about INR20 crore in FY26. Residential plotting in Indore has about 1.8 lakh sq ft unsold inventory, with WIP/inventory about INR15 crore. The company also holds a 10% stake in Virtuoso Infra Meditech LLP, a Indore commercial real-estate build with about 3-3.5 lakh sq ft saleable area and expected revenue of about INR150 crore.

guidance_outlook: Management targets 20-25% revenue growth annually; for FY27 it aims for EBITDA margin of 10-11% against 9.13% in FY26 (about 9-9.25% blended in its margin discussion).
Top FY27 priority is order inflow of about INR2,000 crore, across roads, wastewater and toll contracts.
Bids of about INR1,500-2,000 crore are pending opening; about INR2,500 crore of orders identified for bidding in the current month.
Bid capacity cited at about INR2,000 crore; individual EPC bid capacity INR600-700 crore; building about INR150 crore; toll collection described as unlimited based on net worth.
Plans to bid PPP, HAM and BOT projects in the current fiscal, including NHAI asset monetisation of about 17 road projects.
Management said it would not commit to the projected INR1,000-1,200 crore of project completions in FY27.
capex_capacity: Equipment base of 230+ construction equipment and vehicles; workforce above 1,100 employees.
Operates 37 ongoing projects across nine states; executed more than 40 projects in total.
Preferential issue of convertible warrants up to INR13.09 crore approved; proceeds targeted at working capital needs in about 10-12 months.
Borrowing limits enhancement proposed to support larger projects.
Acquired 10% stake in Virtuoso Infra Meditech LLP (Indore real-estate build, completion in about 2-2.5 years).
demand_pricing: Management said tender flow has not slowed; the YoY order book decline reflects a shift to larger projects and faster execution of earlier orders, with about INR811 crore executed in FY26.
Strike rate: about 10-15% in EPC road building and above 70% in toll collection contracts.
Wastewater competition is intensifying: for a INR200 crore BUIDCO bid there were 15-20 bidders; the company was L2 in one and L3 in another bid.
Fuel and crude price volatility: force majeure and price-escalation clauses are being invoked; management says a short-term hit of about 1-1.5 months has since stabilised.
Company prefers centrally funded projects (NHAI, NHIDCL, MoRTH); working capital cycle cited at 30-45 days.
Company prefers large tickets: NH projects above INR500 crore and building projects above INR50 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the order book fall YoY, and is tender flow slowing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no slowdown; the company is bidding for larger projects and executed INR811 crore in FY26 against a INR1,313 crore opening order book. It said about INR1,500-2,000 crore has been bid and is not yet opened.

qa_highlights.question: What margin should investors expect going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended EBITDA margin is 9-9.25% currently; FY26 toll EBITDA was about 4% and EPC about 14%. Target for the current year is 10-11% blended.

qa_highlights.question: What is the wastewater margin, and how will mix evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Wastewater EBITDA margin was cited at 15-20%. Management expects wastewater at about 20-25% of revenue in the near future, with the balance from roads, buildings, RMC and toll. It is currently subcontracting or name-lending because it lacks credentials.

qa_highlights.question: How did FY26 growth split across business lines?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave FY26 revenue split of about 49% road, 3% RMC, 47% toll, with wastewater very small. Road and toll drove the growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company exposed to fuel price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said contracts include force majeure and price-variation provisions; some agencies have issued SOPs, and the company expects price variations to offset the increase.

qa_highlights.question: What are the biggest opportunities and risks?
qa_highlights.answer: Opportunities cited are large TOT-model toll contracts of INR1,500-2,000 crore and the return of BOT projects. Execution risk remains, though management said it has 40 years of experience and works in nine states.

risks_watch: Order book fell YoY to about INR1,235 crore; conversion of about INR1,500-2,000 crore pending bids is key to FY27 growth.
Wastewater margin claims (15-20%) are unproven; the company lacks credentials and works as subcontractor or name-lender; competition is intense.
Management declined to commit to FY27 completions of INR1,000-1,200 crore, citing geopolitical and macro uncertainty.
Toll segment margin (about 2.5-4%) is much lower than EPC, so mix shift toward toll dilutes margin.
Operating cash flow was negative in FY25 and turned positive in FY26; sustainability is management's expectation, not guaranteed.
Management did not provide an order book figure as of 31 May 2026.
544335|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on growth and margin direction, but evasive on specifics: management declined to commit to FY27 project completion figures and offered inconsistent segment margin and revenue-mix figures. Answers on wastewater and PPP/HAM strategy were broad and aspirational.
key_quotes: Sir, we expect around a 20% to 25% growth rate, trying to maintain that.
So, we are trying to stay around 40% in EPC road and building from revenue.
We don't think we are conservative in out bidding we think we shouldn't unnecessarily have an order book of INR5,000 crores and then not be able to execute the work for 5, 10 years.

544339|2026-03.headline: Laxmi Dental Q4 FY26 revenue rose 21.9% YoY to Rs 74 crore with EBITDA margin at 18.3%, and FY26 revenue grew 16.2% to Rs 277.9 crore.
544339|2026-03.overview: Management described Q4 FY26 as a recovery quarter with highest-ever quarterly revenue of Rs 74 crore, up 21.9% YoY, and broad-based growth across dental lab, aligners and pediatric segments. EBITDA rose 41.8% YoY to Rs 13.5 crore and PAT reached Rs 10.1 crore, helped by a Rs 1.3 crore tax benefit tied to a labour code gratuity item. FY26 closed with revenue of Rs 277.9 crore, EBITDA of Rs 43.4 crore and PAT of Rs 28.9 crore, against a weak Q3. Management declined to give FY27 margin or growth guidance, and cited the company's Rs 99 crore cash balance and ongoing scanner deployment as strategic priorities.

financial_highlights.change: Minor sequential improvement; ~76% excluding scanner sales
vs Rs 4.3 crore in Q4 FY25; includes Rs 1.3 crore tax benefit
vs Rs 1.3 crore last year; company debt-free

financial_highlights.metric: Cash and bank balance incl. investments

segments.name: Dental lab (total)
segments.commentary: Record quarterly revenue of Rs 45.9 crore, up 27% YoY, with international lab up 40.9% YoY and domestic lab up 16.3% YoY to Rs 23.7 crore. Digital penetration in domestic lab is about 80%, with a medium-term target above 90%.

segments.name: Bizdent (domestic clear aligners)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 10.9% YoY in Q4 after a sequential recovery; management said margins were prioritised over pricing, which had been under pressure in prior quarters.

segments.name: Vedia (aligner raw material, mainly export)
segments.commentary: Revenue of Rs 7.3 crore, stable sequentially. Some March shipments slipped to April because freight costs roughly doubled, and in some cases nearly tripled, which delayed revenue recognition.

segments.name: Kids-e-Dental (pediatric)
segments.commentary: Quarterly revenue of Rs 5.4 crore. International registrations are in progress, with some regulatory steps cleared; no firm timeline given.

segments.name: Scanners
segments.commentary: Scanner sales were 211 units in Q4 FY26 and 1,009 units in FY26. Scanners carry lower margins and weighed on consolidated gross margin in Q4.

guidance_outlook: No numerical FY27 guidance. Management said it wants to do better than the 16.2% FY26 growth over the next two to three years, but did not endorse a 20% CAGR.

Management did not reaffirm the earlier target of 18-20% EBITDA margin, 75-80% gross margin and 13-15% PAT margin by FY27 or FY28. It said Q4 margins were in line with that range but would not give a timeline today.
Operating leverage is expected as people costs grow less than revenue; COGS will scale in proportion to sales. Automation and digital dentistry investments are planned.
Capex for FY27 will be set based on operational needs and revenue growth, funded from IPO proceeds still on hand.
US tariff is now about 10% (was about 50%). Management said this is not a deal breaker and expects US business to keep growing.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex was about Rs 18.4 crore. FY27 capex will be balanced against operational capabilities and revenue growth, with no fixed amount given.
Scanner deployment remains a strategic priority: 211 units in Q4 FY26 and 1,009 units in FY26. Management wants to place as many as possible before scanners become commoditised.
Investment in automation and AI (AI Dent) continues to support cost structure and digital dentistry.
demand_pricing: Export share of revenue is about 33-34%. US is about 20% of revenue, and management said it is well diversified across customers, not dependent on Heartland Dental.
Management said the US tariff eased to about 10% from about 50%, and it absorbed higher tariff costs in the first half of Q4. It said the scale-up in the US was gradual and cautious.
Domestic aligner pricing was under pressure in prior quarters; management chose to protect margins, with Bizdent recovering in Q4.
Vedia orders were delayed by freight costs, but management said YoY growth is good and the business is not facing structural uncertainty.

The iScope 360 remote oral-health and aligner-monitoring product launched about two weeks before the call. It is sold through dentists at about Rs 2,000 retail with points-based subscription, and it may also be offered in export markets.
Competition is rising in domestic aligners and from funded players. Management said 22,000 dentists are active with Laxmi, against about 3 lakh dentists in India.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Bizdent revenue stay flat FY25 to FY26, and how much of the Q4 recovery came from pricing versus volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it chose to protect margins over price cuts during the pricing pressure. It did not split Q4 recovery between price and volume, and said it will keep balancing price against growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Vedia lower QoQ despite rupee depreciation?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight costs roughly doubled, and in some cases nearly tripled, which delayed March shipments into April. Management said YoY growth is good and there is no structural problem.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the lab business run rate of about Rs 40-45 crore per quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it cannot give a number today, but expects growth in both domestic and international lab over the next two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for margins and growth for FY27 and beyond?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give FY27 guidance. It said it wants to improve margins over the next two to three years and that Q3 was an exception. Q4 EBITDA margin was 18%.

qa_highlights.question: Is Heartland Dental's contract under review, and are more US DSOs coming?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there has been no change to the Heartland contract. It said more DSOs are being added but will not be announced individually, and that the business is diversified.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company considering acquisitions with its cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will evaluate opportunities that add value and will disclose them only once completed. It gave no specifics.

risks_watch: US tariff regime remains volatile. Current 10% rate could change, and the US is about 20% of revenue.
Freight costs and global shipping disruption caused Vedia export delays, which could recur at quarter-end.
Bizdent faces pricing pressure from domestic and funded competitors. Management is weighing margin against growth.
Gross margin is diluted by scanner sales, which carry lower margins. Scanner margin trajectory matters for consolidated margin.
Management has not reaffirmed the earlier margin targets. Watch whether FY27 margins hold at Q4 levels.
Kids-e-Dental international registration timing is uncertain.
Recent labour code changes affected Q3 gratuity and tax; Q4 PAT included a Rs 1.3 crore tax benefit that will not recur.
544339|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the quarter and long-term opportunity, but cautious on forward numbers. Management repeatedly declined to give FY27 margin or growth guidance and cited external micro factors and tariffs. It was evasive on Bizdent price versus volume and on the Heartland contract.
key_quotes: we close the year with a strong exit quarter, delivering highest ever quarterly numbers across key metrics.
Excluding scanner sales, our gross margin for core dental business remains stable at around 76% in Q4 FY '26.
I wish I could guide you at this point in time.
Scanner business is for us an enabler.

544339|2026-06.headline: Laxmi Dental Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13.9% y-o-y to about INR75 crore, a record, with EBITDA margin at 19.2% and PAT up 23.8%.
544339|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue, with consolidated revenue from operations of INR74.7 crore against INR65.6 crore a year earlier. Gross margin was 78.6% and EBITDA rose 20.6% y-o-y to INR14.4 crore at a 19.2% margin, helped by favourable mix and a scanner trading contribution. Dental lab grew 23.5% y-o-y, with international up 37.4%, while aligners grew 28.6%. Management flagged a new US CEO hire, a planned Palghar land purchase to replace rented facilities, and FY27 scanner deployment of 800 to 1,000 units. The company remains debt-free.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR65.6 crore in Q1 FY26 (about +13.9% y-o-y)
vs INR12.5 crore in Q1 FY26; driven by freight, ECL provisions and AI automation
vs INR14.8 crore in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Dental lab
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 23.5% y-o-y across domestic and international. Domestic lab excluding scanners grew about 12% y-o-y in Q1, per the analyst's question and management's confirmation.

segments.name: International (within dental lab)
segments.commentary: Grew 37.4% y-o-y. CFO said USD moved from about INR85 to INR95, roughly 12% y-o-y currency tailwind, so constant-currency growth is lower but still strong.

segments.name: Aligner solutions
segments.commentary: Grew 28.6% y-o-y. Bizdent grew 27.8% and Vedia grew 29.3%. Management linked growth to the iScope at-home monitoring launch and dentist education.

segments.name: Kids-e-Dental (paediatric)
segments.commentary: Grew 54.4% y-o-y in the quarter. The company holds 60% of its PAT in its adjusted EBITDA calculation.

segments.name: Scanners (trading)
segments.commentary: Sold at about INR3 lakh average to dentists with a trading margin of about 15% to 20%. Scanner mix causes quarter-to-quarter margin swings.

guidance_outlook: Aspiration: 15% to 20% revenue growth and 18% to 20% EBITDA margin. Management said it expects to be in that range, after FY26 margins of about 15.6%.
Domestic lab growth expected to accelerate in Q2, Q3 and Q4 FY27 as satellite labs and scanner-linked customers mature.
Scanner deployment of 800 to 1,000 units targeted for FY27, with the company saying it is on track.
AI-led automation costs are elevated this year and expected to fall next year as scale rises.
Margin expected to be maintained or improved through the year; gross margin should stay stable excluding scanner mix effects.
capex_capacity: Planned FY27 investment in new machinery to modernise and expand manufacturing capacity; no amount disclosed.

Letter of intent executed to acquire land in Palghar, Maharashtra, to replace two rented domestic facilities (Illusion Dental Lab and aligners). Rent is about INR2 crore a year; management said a 3x-size owned facility could otherwise cost INR5 to 6 crore in rent.
No disruption to revenue or productivity expected during the transition, which will be phased. Management cited a 2020 export-unit move from Kandivali to Boisar as precedent.
Aligner capacity utilisation about 70%, with reasonable headroom. Lab utilisation is at a constant 90% to 95% because of custom work.
Digital penetration in domestic network about 75% to 80% (dental lab and aligner combined); international is mostly digital.
demand_pricing: Domestic lab growth slowed to about 12% y-o-y ex-scanners, which management attributed to scanner-led adoption maturing with a 6-month to 18-month gestation period.
Scanner penetration in the industry estimated at about 7% to 8%, with management saying the adoption curve (J-curve) has not yet clearly started.
Management said competition in aligners persists but declined to detail it, citing counter-strategies such as cross-selling.
Aligners are sold only through dentists, not B2C. Management targets general dentists and orthodontists alike.
Branding push includes a brand ambassador, in-clinic branding and social media. Management described itself as the only branded player in crowns.

qa_highlights.question: What differentiates Laxmi Dental products for dentists after the iScan Pro scanner, given no exclusive tie-ups?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 36 years of trust, global quality standards and ISO-certified systems, and innovation, and said it is the only branded crown player.

qa_highlights.question: What is scanner gross margin and how lumpy will margins be?
qa_highlights.answer: Scanners are a trading item with a 15% to 20% margin. Excluding scanners, margins are stable and rising; Q1 margin was 19.2% vs about 15% in the previous quarter and 18% a year ago.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity and utilisation for lab and aligners?
qa_highlights.answer: Aligners at about 70% utilisation. Lab runs at a constant 90% to 95% because of custom work.

qa_highlights.question: Why acquire Palghar land and will there be disruption?
qa_highlights.answer: Goal is to move from two rented sites to one owned facility to cut about INR2 crore rent and gain room to expand. Management expects no revenue disruption.

qa_highlights.question: Why is domestic lab growing only about 12% and when will it improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was 12% y-o-y, attributed to satellite labs adding customer proximity, and expects faster growth from Q2 onwards.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the international growth is currency?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the USD moved from about INR85 to INR95, roughly 12% y-o-y, with the rest from existing DSO and retail business. Management expects the tailwind to persist for some quarters but is unsure beyond that.

qa_highlights.question: Scanner deployment and FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 800 to 1,000 scanner deployments in FY27 and an 18% to 20% margin aspiration; it said Q1 margin supports that range.

risks_watch: Scanner mix drives quarterly gross margin swings; a strong scanner quarter dilutes margin.

544340|2026-03.headline: Rikhav Securities H2 FY26 PAT fell to INR1.20 crore (EPS 0.31) on cash-market investment losses; FY26 PAT INR18.96 crore.
544340|2026-03.overview: H2 FY26 total income was INR1,604 crore (as stated), EBITDA INR6.57 crore and PAT INR1.20 crore. FY26 total income was INR1,991 crore, EBITDA INR32.53 crore and PAT INR18.96 crore, with EPS of 4.95. Management attributed the weak profit to a loss of roughly INR18-23 crore on legacy cash-market equity investments, valuation losses at the 31 March 2026 market low, higher depreciation from about INR5.40 crore of technology spend, and an unrecognised SLBM profit of INR4.33 crore expected to be realised in coming quarters. Management is cutting cash-market exposure and SME inventory, and is building institutional broking, ETF market making and commodity arbitrage. Several answers were vague or deferred to email, and the call was disrupted by line dropouts.

financial_highlights.change: Expected to realise in coming quarters; management said April in one answer

segments.name: Broking (retail/HNI)
segments.commentary: Brokerage per client is about INR5,000-6,000, with about 50% of revenue from brokerage and float income exceeding brokerage. Management said retail and HNI brokerage has been hard to grow over the last six months.

segments.name: Proprietary trading / algo and arbitrage
segments.commentary: In-house algo and arbitrage were the only area that improved, per management. Algo and delta-hedging income is guided to grow 20-25% in FY27.

segments.name: Market making (SME and ETF)
segments.commentary: SME exposure was cut to about 30% of last year's level, roughly INR20-25 crore. Market making in ETFs has started with Kotak Mutual Fund, with two or three more mutual funds planned.

segments.name: Institutional broking
segments.commentary: Empanelled Kotak Mutual Fund, Bank of India and RBL Bank, and 8-10 FPIs have started. Management said real revenue will start next year and expects SBI and LIC empanelment.

segments.name: Non-auto components

Finance costs are expected to be temporary and normalise as acquisition-related debt is repaid.
Management said export markets (US, Europe, Middle East, Turkey, Egypt) have not yet recovered and expects normalisation to take more time.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone gross margin hold while EBITDA margin fell ~200 bps QoQ?

544345|2026-03.headline: Denta FY26 revenue rose over 23% to Rs 2,503.8 mn with order book of Rs 7,278 mn, but Q4 EBITDA margin fell to about 19%, and management gave no firm order-inflow guidance.
544345|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue from operations of Rs 2,503.8 mn (over 23% growth), EBITDA of Rs 834.9 mn and PAT of Rs 609 mn, with an order book of about Rs 7,278 mn across 38 ongoing projects as of March 31, 2026. Analysts pressed on a sharp Q3/Q4 run-rate slowdown and a Q4 EBITDA margin of about 19% versus roughly 33% in the first three quarters, which management attributed to the Iran-US war, petroleum-linked raw material costs and a mix shift to smaller projects. Order-book inflow was described as pending new tenders under the new Karnataka government, with no order value committed. Working capital of about Rs 295 crore (inventory, receivables and other assets) is expected to convert largely in December-January, and management guided to about 20% FY27 revenue growth with an EBITDA margin of around 25%.

segments.name: Water management (core)
segments.commentary: Management says about 90% of the water order book sits in the water sector, covering drinking water, STP, irrigation and tank regeneration. The company has bagged 3-4 FTP projects covering about 15-16 cities in Karnataka.

segments.name: Amrut 2 and Jal Jivan Mission
segments.commentary: One Amrut 2 order of Rs 232 crore (Kuknuru and Yelburga, Koppal) and four Jal Jivan Mission projects in Karnataka. Management says about 70% of these projects is complete, with the balance 30% targeted this year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of about 20% stated as the minimum projection; closing remarks cited a 20-25% target.
EBITDA margin guided at about 25% (confirmed in Q&A), down from about 33% run-rate in Q1-Q3 FY26.
No firm order-inflow number given; management expects to announce new orders shortly and aims for a healthy order-book increase by end-March 2027.
Management declined to give an absolute FY27 profit figure, saying it depends on project execution and raw material investment.
Government payments expected to accelerate from July-August 2026, with many payments in Q2-Q3 FY27, per management.
Possible price-escalation relief for HDPE/PVC items expected in July or Q2 FY27, per management.
capex_capacity: Inventory, receivables and other assets of about Rs 295 crore are tied up in working capital; management expects about 60% (about Rs 200 crore) to be realised in FY27, mainly by December-January.
Payment on supply is roughly 55% after material is laid, with the balance 35% on laying and the remainder on completion, per management.
Company is adopting NEBR and CAMUS-based STP technologies, claiming about 95% purity, largely through subcontracting to patent holders.
Bidding pipeline of about 5-6 projects worth about Rs 600 crore; management is aggressively bidding for 5-6 tenders and 2-3 major tenders.
Four to five projects identified in Madhya Pradesh under the National Water Management Programme (NWMP); a Mahanadi barrage tender in Odisha is yet to be floated.
demand_pricing: Karnataka's new government (formed late May/early June 2026) is expected to push infrastructure tenders after a roughly six-month slowdown.
Raw material risk: 20-30% of raw material is UPVC and HDPE pipe, with prices up in Q4 FY26, April and May 2026 after the Iran-US war; some suppliers seeking higher prices.
Price escalation clauses exist on projects above Rs 100 crore but not on smaller projects, per management.
Management said the company is taking smaller-value projects (Rs 10-50 crore) alongside larger ones (up to Rs 300 crore), which dilutes margin.
Q3 and Q4 FY26 execution slowdown was attributed to war-related disruption and irregular payments.

qa_highlights.question: Trajectory of order flow and government payment status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is aggressively bidding for 5-6 tenders and expects to announce new orders in the coming quarter; payments are expected to pick up from July-August 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Margin trajectory and FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management first said margin would be maintained around 30%, then confirmed a 25% EBITDA margin guidance for FY27 after repeated questioning; it said smaller projects will dilute margin.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital liquidation timeline (Rs 295 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects cash in December-January, with about 60% (about Rs 200 crore) targeted in FY27, after laying and completion of projects by October.

qa_highlights.question: Order book fall from Rs 841 crore (Dec 2025) to Rs 727 crore (Mar 2026)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the reduction to revenue conversion and investment in completing old projects, and said the audit team would provide the exact reconciliation; it did not confirm any cancellation.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 revenue and profit outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to a minimum of 20% revenue growth but declined to give an absolute profit number, saying it depends on project implementation and raw material investment.

qa_highlights.question: Diversification beyond Karnataka and into private industrial segments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited NWMP projects in Madhya Pradesh and a biogas project with a partner holding GAIL and BPCL contracts; no firm private industrial wins were disclosed.

risks_watch: Margin dilution: Q4 EBITDA margin about 19% versus about 33% in Q1-Q3; FY27 guidance of 25% implies lower profit growth against a 20% revenue rise.
Working-capital conversion: about Rs 295 crore in inventory, receivables and other assets; collection timing rests on government payments.
Order book fell from about Rs 841 crore (Dec 2025) to Rs 727 crore (Mar 2026), with no reconciliation provided on the call.
Government dependence and political transition in Karnataka; payment timing is uncertain.
Raw material inflation from petroleum-linked pipes (UPVC and HDPE), with suppliers seeking higher prices.
Management answers on key numbers were vague or deferred to later written follow-up, including order-book reconciliation, margin split by project size and profit guidance.

Up about Rs 12 crore vs Q4 FY25 (Rs 541.52 million) per management

544350|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue crossed INR 2,000 crore (up 21.6% to INR 2,080 crore) with PAT up 52.4% to INR 168 crore; FY27 plans 60 new facilities.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex breakdown and the acquisition-related cash outflow?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex is INR 380-400 crore including the CMS facility; acquisition payments are about INR 60-65 crore, versus about INR 85 crore in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What losses do new greenfield facilities carry, and will they recur?
qa_highlights.answer: New FY26 branches had unit-level operating losses of about INR 30 crore (FY25 cohort about INR 21 crore). Management expects a similar drag in FY27, with per-branch losses falling from FY27 onwards, mainly in Delhi.

qa_highlights.answer: Q4 one-off merger costs of about INR 80 lakh; corporate office rent of about INR 1 crore for the year; about INR 3.3 crore extra Facebook marketing spend. Merger costs are one-off, rent recurs.

qa_highlights.question: What limits the pace of openings?

risks_watch: New-facility drag of about INR 30-40 crore per year could weigh on margins if FY27 openings are weighted to Delhi NCR and the North.

544397|2026-06.headline: Ather Energy Q1 FY27: wholesale volumes up 81% to 83,000 units, first-ever positive EBITDA of Rs 9 crore (~0.8% margin), AGM down to 22.4%.
544397|2026-06.overview: Management described a sharp demand upswing driven by policy support, fuel-availability concerns and TCO gains, with registrations up 102% YoY and paid preorders up 158% to 1.5 lakh. Production was constrained at the Hosur plant (35,000 units/month max, reached near full utilisation by June), leaving dealer inventory at about 3 days versus 14 days earlier. Commodity costs rose sharply, cutting adjusted gross margin by 5.6 percentage points to 22.4%, partly offset by an average selling price rise to Rs 1.61 lakh and disciplined fixed-cost control that delivered the first positive EBITDA. Management expects further commodity hits of 100-200 bps, to be largely offset by price increases that were only partly reflected in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Will Ather enter electric motorcycles soon?

544397|2026-09.headline: Ather Energy Q2 FY27: wholesale volume up 42% YoY to 93,000 units, first positive PAT, and gross margin at 24% (H1 FY27: 23%).
544397|2026-09.overview: Management reported strong demand with preorders up about 108% and inquiries up about 109% YoY, supporting wholesale volume of 93,000 units (up 42% YoY) and registrations of about 92,500 (up nearly 60%). Average ex-showroom price rose to INR164,000 from INR150,000 in Q4 FY26, and adjusted gross margin reached 24% in Q2 FY27 versus 25.4% in Q4 FY26 after commodity headwinds. EBITDA turned positive at 4.9% (from -9.6% a year earlier) and the company reported its first positive PAT. Management is raising installed capacity to 11.4 lakh units per year by Q2 FY28 because demand exceeds supply, and Konarc launched in phases from late August.

segments.commentary: Industry registrations grew 82% YoY to about 6 lakh in Q2. Ather growth was 82% in South, 85% in Middle India and 79% in Rest of India; Rest of India was the fastest-rising zone as Konarc rolled out in northern states and sales were prioritised there.

segments.commentary: Launched 29 August 2026 with only one month of sales in Q2 and fewer than 10,000 units sold by quarter-end. Mid variants SR2 and SR3 are live, SR1 is due by Q4 FY27, and the Z variant is not yet in production.

segments.name: Non-vehicle revenue
segments.commentary: Non-vehicle revenue was 15% of total. AtherStack Pro is more than 50% of it, with accessories and servicing split roughly equally. Management indicated gross margins of about 30-40% for accessories, 40-45% for spares and 80-90% for AtherStack Pro.

guidance_outlook: Installed capacity to rise from 9.2 lakh units/year to 11.4 lakh units/year by Q2 FY28, through Hosur (+6,000 units/month, live later this quarter) and AURIC Phase 1 (base 42,000 units/month, plus 12,000 units/month incremental).

AURIC Phase 1 trial production expected in the next few weeks (Q3 FY27), with capex installation complete by Q4 FY27; full capacity realisation takes a couple of quarters, with ramp-up expected within FY28.
Dealer/experience-centre network expansion to restart from around end of Q3 FY27, with noticeable numbers from Q4 FY27; fewer than 50 experience centres were added in the last two quarters.

No further price hikes in Q3 FY27 and no planned price increases on the current portfolio for the next few quarters; Konarc's entry variants may lower average ex-showroom price without hurting gross margin.
Management expects like-to-like Konarc gross margin to be 6-7% better than Rizta in the long term; Konarc is already a few thousand rupees cheaper than Rizta on a like-to-like basis.
Commodities seen as flat in recent weeks; management says Q3 is not expected to be worse than Q2 but volatility remains high. Subsidy is broadly unchanged QoQ.
Electric motorcycle launch: no timeline given.
capex_capacity: Current manufacturing capacity averaged 33,000 units/month in Q2 FY27, up from 28,000 in Q1; Hosur is at 35,000 units/month capacity and is described as at its limit.
Hosur expansion adds 6,000 units/month, live later in Q3 FY27. Total installed capacity is about 77,000 units/month after AURIC Phase 1 base (42,000) before the additional expansion.
AURIC Phase 1 (Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar) adds 12,000 units/month of incremental capacity by Q2 FY28, taking installed capacity to 11.4 lakh units/year from 9.2 lakh units/year.
Management estimates about 20,000 units/month of unrealised retail demand at current run-rate, with demand in the 50,000-60,000 units/month range.
Ather Node (apartment EV charging) is being industrialised and will begin deployment in the next few months; Ather Bedrock 5th-gen battery packs are live across 450, Rizta and Konarc.
demand_pricing: Preorders rose about 108% YoY to about 1.8 lakh; inquiries rose about 109% YoY to over 10 lakh; Ather searches rose about 94% vs about 34% for EV searches industry-wide.
Pan-India E2W penetration crossed 10% for the first time, at about 11.2% for Q2 FY27 (industry commentary cites 11.6% as the quarterly figure).
Average ex-showroom price rose to INR164,000 from INR150,000 in Q4 FY26, helped by price hikes and SKU/incentive management. Management says part of the gain is temporary.
Commodity inflation (aluminium, copper, plastics, memory chips) hit gross margin by about 9.4%. Management says SKU management recovered 2.7pp of this, a more temporary lever.
Structural gross-margin gains of about 5.3pp over two quarters came from price hikes, VAVE and cost reduction.
Konarc early Stack Pro attach rates are said to be as strong as Rizta, but management wants at least two quarters before assuming ~90% attach for Konarc, given a more non-South-heavy mix.

qa_highlights.question: How quickly will the new AURIC Phase 1 capacity ramp up, given it is greenfield, and when will the 6.5 lakh figure be realised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AURIC Phase 1's base 42,000 units will take about two quarters to ramp; the additional 12,000 units going live in Q2 FY28 may ramp faster. Full ramp is expected within FY28, while Hosur ramp is expected to be rapid from the end of Q3.

qa_highlights.question: How much pricing headroom remains if commodities stay elevated into next calendar year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not want to raise prices on the current portfolio for the next few quarters. Konarc's more aggressive entry portfolio gives better unit economics, so it could lower average ex-showroom price without hurting gross margin.

qa_highlights.question: How are Konarc bookings and cannibalisation trending in launched regions?
qa_highlights.answer: Konarc has only one month of sales in Q2 and fewer than 10,000 units sold by quarter-end. Inquiries, preorders and walk-ins are up several times in Rajasthan and UP, and Konarc Z demand is strong.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ASP rise driven by scooter buyers or motorcycle buyers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the buyers are still scooter buyers paying for better experience, quality and features, not motorcycle buyers. Stack Pro attach is high across the base.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 5.3% margin gain sustainable, and does the 2.7% SKU lever reverse?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 5.3% is broadly structural (price hikes, VAVE, cost reduction). The 2.7% SKU/incentive lever is more temporary and can be reopened if supply is tight or commodities stay high, but it is not one-off.

qa_highlights.question: How are dealer network expansion and experience-centre additions planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Fewer than 50 experience centres were added in the last two quarters as dealer expansion was held back. Expansion restarts around end of Q3 FY27, with noticeable numbers from Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Konarc variant rollout sequenced with mid variants first and entry variants later?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity constraints on 450 and Rizta changed the plan. SR2 and SR3 launched first, SR1 is due by Q4 once Aurangabad capacity is available, and Z comes later. Geographic rollout started in the North.

risks_watch: Commodity costs (aluminium, copper, plastics, memory) have stayed elevated for longer than expected; management says Q3 is unlikely to be worse than Q2, but the outlook is volatile.
The 2.7pp SKU and incentive lever is temporary and may reverse if supply eases, which could weigh on gross margin.

Capacity ramp risk: AURIC Phase 1 takes about two quarters to ramp, and the 12,000 units/month add-on is due by Q2 FY28; demand is 50,000-60,000 units/month against 77,000 installed capacity after Hosur and AURIC.
Konarc ramp and attach-rate uncertainty: early Konarc attach rates are strong, but its mix is less South-heavy, and management wants at least two quarters of data.
PAT is positive for the first time but management says it can fluctuate; PAT is not the near-term focus.
Dealer network expansion has been slowed; it restarts around end of Q3 FY27, so store additions and reach may lag demand.
Electric motorcycle timeline is not guided.

544447|2026-06.headline: Smartworks Q1 FY27 revenue rose 44% YoY to INR 546 crores, with normalized EBITDA margin at 19.6% and guidance of 28-30% revenue growth reaffirmed.
544447|2026-06.overview: Revenue reached INR 546 crores, up 44% YoY and 5% QoQ, while normalized EBITDA grew 74% YoY to INR 107 crores at a 19.6% margin. Normalized PAT nearly tripled YoY to INR 39 crores. Growth was supported by mature-centre occupancy (committed 92%) and a higher share of 1,000+ seat clients, GCCs and multi-city clients, though overall occupancy dipped to 81% from 82% QoQ as new centres filled up. Management reaffirmed FY27 guidance (28-30% revenue growth, 19-20% normalized EBITDA margin, 13 million sq ft by March 2027) and started a heavy capex cycle of INR 550-600 crores for the year.

financial_highlights.change: vs 16.2% in Q1 FY26 and 19% in Q4 FY26
vs negative INR 4.9 crores a year ago
vs INR 22 crores in same quarter last year

segments.name: Core rental (enterprise annuity)
segments.commentary: Enterprise annuity demand is 92% of rental revenue; 1,000+ seat cohort is 41% of revenue (37% in FY26). Committed contracted revenue is about INR 5,400 crores, covering 87% of FY27 revenue.

segments.name: GCC clients
segments.commentary: GCCs contribute 21% of revenue, up from 15% in FY26. Recent wins include a Swiss bank and a manufacturing GCC; a Japanese NBFC subsidiary took space in Mumbai.

segments.name: Singapore
segments.commentary: Work Studio acquired, taking the portfolio to over 1,500 seats (about 2% of revenue); 400-450 seats now available to sell, funded from Singapore cash flows. Management says no further meaningful expansion planned.

segments.name: Value-added services (VAS)
segments.commentary: Non-lease rental revenue rose to over INR 68 crores from INR 22 crores YoY, and is take-rate based with no direct cost. VAS guidance is not built into the FY27 projections.

guidance_outlook: Reaffirmed FY27 revenue growth of 28-30%, normalized EBITDA margin of 19-20%, and operational footprint above 13 million sq ft by March 2027.
Plans to add 2.5-3 million sq ft of operational space in FY27; more than 3.5 million sq ft signed, giving a buffer of about 0.7-0.8 million sq ft.
Capex guided at INR 550-600 crores for FY27, with heavy spend in the next two quarters.
Management expects ROCE to expand meaningfully through FY28 as capex cohorts mature.
Revenue jump expected mainly in Q3 or Q4 as new centres ramp up (about 12 months to ramp).
capex_capacity: Operational footprint 10.4 million sq ft as of June 2026; 1.9 million sq ft under fit-out; 0.3 million sq ft added in Q1 and 2.1 million sq ft over the last 12 months.

About 3 million sq ft to come online over the next 9 months, including Eastbridge (Mumbai) and Eastside (Pune), both landing in H2 FY27. Vikhroli asset is 8.15 lakh sq ft, described as the world's largest standalone managed campus.
New fit-out capex is INR 1,350 per sq ft, rising about 5% a year; refurbishment is about 15% of initial capex every three years (around INR 5 per sq ft per year, by management's estimate).
Every building needed for the next two years is secured; FY29 work has begun. Long-term rights give 10-15 years of access.
Security deposits of INR 33 crores paid to landlords to lock buildings for FY28 and part of FY29.
demand_pricing: Occupancy 81% (vs 82% in Q4 FY26), reflecting new centres still filling. Mature centres at 89% on 9.1 million sq ft; committed occupancy 92%. Management guides 80-85% occupancy over the next three quarters.

Seat retention 74% in Q1, with client count down while occupied seats and revenue rose. Management says the churn is deliberate repricing of older, lower-rate clients; the annual retention range it cited was 80-88%.
Realization on incremental mature-footprint seats leased in Q1 FY27 was about INR 181 per sq ft per month, up from about INR 170 a year earlier. Management cited a rental INR 185 per seat figure.
Mix: IT/ITES down to 35% of clients (from over 40%); target 25-30/35%. Multi-city clients 35% of revenue (31% in FY26).
Pre-commitment: about 30-35% of new buildings is pre-committed by existing or incoming clients. Landlord mix is about 65% non-institutional and 35% institutional.

qa_highlights.question: Rationale for the Singapore Work Studio acquisition, expected revenue and occupancy, and whether fit-out costs of INR 1,350 face inflation.
qa_highlights.answer: Acquired from internal cash flows at roughly construction cost; the target was about 60% occupied. Singapore is about 80,000 sq ft in total and 2% of revenue, with 400-450 seats now available to sell. Expansion will not be meaningful, and capex is set at INR 550-600 crores for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the expansion is speculative, and how much is pre-leased?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 30-35% of any new building is pre-committed by existing clients, and occupancy ramps to 80-85% within 13-14 months, as seen on prior centres.

qa_highlights.question: Is the drop in retention a sign of demand weakness, and will similar churn continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 74% was Q2-seasonal churn; mature committed occupancy is 92%, and most churned space is already re-let. Churn is expected to fall in Q3 and Q4, as in prior years.

qa_highlights.question: Is there supply risk from developer delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Supply is covered by a buffer of 0.7-0.8 million sq ft over the 2.5-3 million sq ft target, and management is working with institutional developers such as DLF, Hiranandani, Tata, Panchshil and Salarpuria.

qa_highlights.question: How is the 28-30% guidance built, given the existing base is at 92% committed occupancy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the base is almost fully sold, so growth depends on new centres that take about 12 months to ramp. Growth is expected to show mainly in Q3 or Q4, and the range is one management is confident about.

qa_highlights.question: Why did OCF/EBITDA dip, and what about VAS margins and pricing power?
qa_highlights.answer: The dip reflects INR 33 crores of security deposits paid to landlords. VAS is take-rate based with no direct cost, so it is margin accretive, but it is only in pilot stages and not in FY27 projections. Management said the nearest competitor prices 10-15% higher than Smartworks.

risks_watch: Occupancy may stay at 80-85% in the next three quarters as large new centres ramp, and it could drop further.
Revenue guidance depends on new-centre ramp-up and handover timing, with most of the uplift in Q3-Q4 FY27.
Capex of INR 550-600 crores is front-loaded; FCF is negative (INR -56 crores in Q1) and depends on OCF recovering after deposit payments.
IT/ITES share is falling, and management could not give a call-centre (AI-exposed) breakdown.
Retention of 74% in Q1 needs to recover in the seasonally stronger H2 to validate the 80-88% annual range management cited.
Revenue and EBITDA margin depend on keeping the 19-20% range while absorbing new cohorts.
Management corrected several numbers during the call (Singapore occupancy, seat count, IT/ITES share, retention), so the transcript figures should be checked against the presentation.
544447|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and promotional. Management was emphatic about visibility, compounding margins and supply security. It was more defensive on retention (74%), the OCF/EBITDA dip, and the Q1 occupancy decline, which it attributed to new centres and deliberate repricing.
key_quotes: Smartworks compounds.
Tomorrow's campuses are contracted today.
We don't manage for the quarter; we are building for the decade.
Fewer, bigger, longer-duration clients - that is by design.

544449|2026-03.headline: Anthem FY26 consolidated revenue Rs 2,124 crore (+18% incl. other income), with Q4 record revenue Rs 611 crore (+26% YoY) and Q4 EBITDA margin 48.1%.
544449|2026-03.overview: Anthem closed FY26 with its highest-ever quarterly revenue in Q4, up 26% YoY to Rs 611 crore, with CRDMO up 31% and specialty ingredients up 8%. FY26 EBITDA reached Rs 990 crore (43.4% margin, +31%) and PAT Rs 592 crore (+31%), though full-year revenue growth of about 15% fell short of the company's stated 20% aspiration. Management said destocking by customers is largely behind it and refused to give FY27 or FY28 guidance. Capex is shifting to Unit 4, with Phase 1 of about Rs 1,200 crore to finish by March 2028.

financial_highlights.change: Revenue growth about 15% per CFO; total revenue incl. other income Rs 2,280 crore, +18%
Includes forex and RoDTEP gain Rs 63 crore and financial/other non-operating income Rs 92 crore
+130% YoY; includes Rs 98 lakh exceptional credit from Labour Code impact

segments.name: CRDMO
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue Rs 1,773 crore (83% of total), +18%; Q4 Rs 513 crore, +31% YoY. Management split: commercial molecules about 60%, late-stage/Phase 3 development and manufacturing batches about 15%, R&D about 8-9%, with specialty ingredients the balance.

segments.name: Specialty ingredients
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue Rs 352 crore (17%); Q4 Rs 98 crore, +8% YoY, the first revenue growth after flat first three quarters. Management aspires to around 20% growth; products include serratiopeptidase, vitamins, probiotics and enzymes, sold mainly to India and RoW markets.

guidance_outlook: No FY27 or FY28 guidance given; management aspires to around 20% growth in revenue, EBITDA and PAT, citing a 10-year revenue CAGR near 20%.
FY26 revenue growth was about 15% versus a 20% aspiration; management says EBITDA and PAT growth of 30%+ more than compensated.
EBITDA margin: asked whether 38-40% is a fair assumption, CFO said the company has delivered these levels and will continue to deliver, with operating leverage expected to hold margins steady.
Destocking is described as behind the company; management expects restocking to lift FY27 top and bottom line.
Biosimilar project expected to hit P&L next year (FY27) and would be classified under CRDMO.
Unit 3 expected to be EBITDA-positive this year; Unit 4 ready by next financial year per CEO closing remarks.
capex_capacity: Unit 4 is the largest project, with Phase 1 at about Rs 1,200 crore across FY27 and FY28, targeted for completion in the latter half of March 2028.
Phase 1 adds about 365 kilolitres custom synthesis (vs current 425 KL) and 100 KL fermentation (vs current 180 KL), roughly doubling custom synthesis and adding about 50% fermentation capacity.
Capex guidance: about Rs 700 crore in FY27, then about Rs 500 crore per year after that (including maintenance).
Unit 2 expanded from 246 KL to about 376 KL (50% addition); Unit 3 fully operational, and more Unit 2/3 expansion sits in CWIP in H1 FY27.
Unit 4 has two further phases after Phase 1; Phase 1 at least doubles capacity and Phase 2 could triple overall size.
Unit 3 added lab space to handle more projects; management says the company can handle 200 projects versus 100 today.
demand_pricing: Management said destocking happened in FY26 across many customers, and restocking is now under way.
Orders are coming in for both chemistry and biology, with growth in peptides and RNAi (oligonucleotide) work.
Four commercial molecules went live in FY26 (one with big pharma, three with emerging biotechs); they contribute about 8-9% of revenue now, with a 2-3 year ramp expected.

Commercial pipeline rose to 14 molecules; Phase 3 pipeline stands at 10 molecules, all from emerging biotechs (four added in FY26, non-lateral), spanning ADC, peptides, oligonucleotides and biotransformation.

Two new direct big pharma relationships added in FY26; more than 100 early-stage R&D projects. Biotech funding up about 50% YoY through April (per CFO); early-stage requests rising in number though smaller in size.
Management sees tariffs as no impact so far, since commercial big pharma products have separate arrangements with the US administration.

qa_highlights.question: How should FY27 growth for CRDMO research and manufacturing be framed, and are destocking issues resolved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aspires to about 20%+ growth as per track record but gave no FY27 guidance; it says destocking is largely behind and restocking should benefit FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is capacity a constraint for adding big pharma customers?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Unit 2 expansion (246 to about 376 KL) and Unit 3 give headroom until Unit 4 comes online; capacity is not a constraint now.

qa_highlights.question: Capex outlook for FY27 and the medium term?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is about Rs 700 crore in FY27 and about Rs 500 crore thereafter, with Unit 4 Phase 1 at about Rs 1,200 crore over two years.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin improvement and EBITDA margin sustainability?
qa_highlights.answer: Backward integration into one intermediate was completed, improving material margins in Q3 and Q4 FY26; management expects 38-40% EBITDA margins to be sustained with operating leverage.

qa_highlights.question: Phase 3 pipeline composition?
qa_highlights.answer: All four Phase 3 additions were non-lateral, from the emerging biotech funnel; the basket of 10 spans ADC, peptides, oligos and biotransformation, with at least one molecule per modality.

qa_highlights.question: Contribution from the four newly commercial molecules?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO estimated about 8-9% of current revenue, with peak sales estimated four to five years after launch and a two-to-three-year ramp.

risks_watch: FY26 revenue growth of about 15% fell short of the 20% aspiration; management declined to commit to FY27 numbers.
Specialty ingredients growth is patchy because its capacity shares space with CRDMO; a dedicated facility in Unit 4 is planned.
Unit 4 capex execution (Rs 1,200 crore over FY27-FY28) and Phase 1 completion by March 2028.
Maintaining 38-40% EBITDA margins at high growth; management acknowledged inflationary pressures and the Middle East war as headwinds.
Ramp-up of the four newly launched commercial molecules; launch timing depends on partner filings and registrations across geographies.
GLP-1 generic opportunity depends on customer formulation approvals, with timing given as six to eight months; the company is in talks with big players to replace China-sourced APIs.
Q4 PAT includes a Labour Code-related exceptional credit of Rs 98 lakh.

So, capacity is not a constraint for us now.
Unit 3 is already turning around and it's going to be in the positive territory this year.

544449|2026-06.headline: Anthem Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue fell to Rs 418 crore with 39.6% EBITDA margin; management guides to H2-weighted recovery, not a number.
544449|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was Rs 418 crore, with CRDMO at Rs 341 crore (81.5%) and Specialty Ingredients at Rs 78 crore (18.5%). EBITDA including other income was Rs 176 crore (39.6% margin), PAT Rs 120 crore (27.1% margin), and net cash stood at Rs 1,720 crore at June 30, 2026. Management attributed the soft quarter to customers deferring deliveries into Q2–Q4 rather than to demand weakness, and reiterated full-year growth in line with historical double-digit performance. Analysts pressed on the roughly 25% YoY decline in Q1; management pushed investors to judge the business on a YoY and full-year basis.

segments.name: CRDMO
segments.commentary: Rs 341 crore in Q1 FY27 (81.5% of revenue); management says order book is about 60% of full-year plan after replenishment, with deliveries deferred to Q2–Q4. Analyst cited roughly 25% YoY decline in Q1.

segments.name: Specialty Ingredients
segments.commentary: Rs 78 crore in Q1 FY27 (18.5% of revenue); India-focused B2B business with rolling forecasts revised every 3 to 6 months. Management cited raw material and supply chain pressure from the war and expects decent growth by year-end.

guidance_outlook: Management says Q1 FY27 is the softest quarter of the year and expects sequential growth from Q2 onward, with recovery in Q2, Q3 and Q4.

EBITDA and PAT margins expected to be broadly intact for FY27; management sees no margin challenge this year given the order book.
FY27 capex target about Rs 700 crore; capex elevated in FY28 due to Unit 4, then declining.
Tax rate expected to normalise to about 25% to 25.5% for the full year as Neo Anthem moves toward breakeven and profitability.
Semaglutide API commercial supply to domestic players expected after CDSCO approval, guided as likely within a quarter or two and in any case this year.
capex_capacity: Unit 1 utilisation about 78% in Q1 FY27 (about 74% at FY26 end), custom synthesis.
Unit 2 utilisation about 50% in Q1 on expanded custom synthesis capacity (about 130 kilolitres added); fermentation about 50% on 140 kilolitres. Unit 2 averaged about 65% in FY26.
Unit 3 (Neo Anthem) utilisation about 30% to 35% in Q1 FY27, up from about 15% in FY26; new projects including peptide synthesis and oncology manufacturing being moved in.

Groundbreaking last year; civil work nearly done; equipment orders starting; capex split about 50:50 across FY27 and FY28; commissioning by end FY28.
Management expects all units to approach optimum utilisation within about two years.
demand_pricing: Added one new Big Pharma customer in the quarter; agreement not yet signed, expected to contribute in later quarters of FY27. Management describes it as multi-dimensional (R&D, new projects, supply diversification).

One large biotech customer was acquired by a Big Pharma; management says impact is not material for the rest of FY27 and no meaningful discussions with the acquirer yet. The affected contract is a late-Phase 3 development contract, not commercial.

Four new molecules commercialised by customers last year; sizeable supplies expected only after a couple of years of market penetration. About 14 commercial molecules and 10 late-phase molecules, with 100+ early-stage programmes; commercialisation of late-phase molecules 18 to 24 months away. Two late-phase programmes are ADC-related.
Q1 deferrals attributed to customers rerouting stock between geographies and approval delays for growing molecules; management says confirmed orders remain in place.
Semaglutide: sampled almost all large domestic players; sales not yet started, pending CDSCO approval. Regulatory work started for other markets but none targeted yet.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity utilisation at Units 1, 2 and Neo Anthem, and US FDA or EU inspection timing for Unit 3?
qa_highlights.answer: Unit 1 about 78%, Unit 2 about 50% (fermentation also about 50%), Unit 3 about 30% to 35%. Unit 3 growth is from new projects rather than shifting volume from existing units. Management did not give an inspection timeline in the answer.

qa_highlights.question: Visibility on the next quarter and the split of the remaining 40% of the year's business across CRDMO, R&D and Specialty Ingredients?
qa_highlights.answer: The 60% order book figure applies to the whole business. Specialty Ingredients is month-to-month with rolling forecasts; CRDMO orders are placed in advance due to raw material procurement and manufacturing lead times. The remaining volume is expected from new customers and volume increases from existing ones.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year CRDMO growth after a weak Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said growth prospects remain intact and in line with historical double-digit growth, with recovery expected in Q2 to Q4 and margins mostly intact. CEO asked investors to judge on a YoY basis and not to treat any single quarter as a benchmark.

qa_highlights.question: Semaglutide commercial supply timing and inbound interest from domestic peers facing scale-up issues?
qa_highlights.answer: No commercial supply yet; awaiting CDSCO approval, expected this year. Management said the company is ready to scale, has sampled most large players, and was not responding to a peer's scale-up problem.

qa_highlights.question: Unit 4 capex, timeline and FY27 capex total?
qa_highlights.answer: Rs 1,200 crore Phase 1 outlay, about 50:50 across FY27 and FY28, with commissioning by end FY28. FY27 capex target about Rs 700 crore; FY28 stays elevated before declining.

qa_highlights.question: Margin sustainability over 3 to 5 years, and what drives it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites a 60% order book and known cost base for FY27, and points to flow chemistry and biocatalysis as cost reducers. Material margin rose in Q1 despite lower revenue. Management expects some PAT dilution when new units start.

risks_watch: Lumpy CRDMO deliveries: Q1 soft due to customer deferrals; Q2 to Q4 must absorb the shortfall to hold full-year growth.
Semaglutide CDSCO approval timing; delay would push back the GLP-1 revenue ramp.
Acquisition of a large biotech customer by a Big Pharma; ramp-up timing and volume impact uncertain.
Unit 4 execution (Rs 1,200 crore, commissioning end FY28) and FY28 capex; PAT dilution as new units start.
Specialty Ingredients under raw material and supply pressure; management expects growth by year-end but gave no figure.
Neo Anthem (Unit 3) turning breakeven this year is needed to support the 25% tax rate assumption.

544450|2026-03.headline: Chembond Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue hit a record Rs 101.4 crore, but management flagged a ~3% margin hit from war-driven input cost inflation.
544450|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 consolidated revenue of Rs 326.15 crore (up 12%), EBITDA of Rs 51 crore (up 7%) and PBT of Rs 45 crore (up 7%), with H2 revenue of Rs 188 crore, up 35% over H1. Q4 FY26 revenue of Rs 101.4 crore and EBITDA of Rs 15.7 crore were the highest of the last nine quarters. Management said margins are under pressure from metal-linked raw material costs that rose after the war declaration, with force majeure invoked and public-sector customers resisting price changes. The call was held after the demerger, which moved the water and construction businesses into the new listed entity.

financial_highlights.change: Highest of last nine quarters; management said above Q4 FY25 and Q4 FY24

financial_highlights.value: Rs 46.3 crore (presentation also cites Rs 51 crore), 14% of sales
financial_highlights.change: Rs 51 crore is +7% YoY per management

segments.commentary: About 87% of FY26 revenue and the fastest-growing unit; H2 revenue Rs 162 crore, up 36% over H1, with volume of 4,813 MT vs 3,205 MT... (H1 volume stated as 9,905 MT in transcript, which conflicts with H2 4,813 MT; not reconciled on call). Record single-month revenue of about Rs 32 crore in March.

segments.name: Construction chemicals
segments.commentary: About 7% of revenue; H2 revenue Rs 13 crore vs H1 Rs 11 crore (+18-20%), H2 volume 2,590 MT (+30%). Management claimed PBT margin of about 20%; DSO about 88 days at 31 March 2026.

segments.name: Distribution
segments.commentary: About 6% of revenue; H2 revenue Rs 12.5 crore vs H1 Rs 9 crore (+40%), H2 volume 1,049 MT vs 594 MT in H1; DSO about 80 days.

segments.name: Cleaning and hygiene (JV with Calvatis)
segments.commentary: About 1% of revenue; H2 growth of 15%. Management described it as subpar for seven years, with early traction from integration into water channel.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27 volume growth expected at about 15-20% in construction chemicals and about 10% in water chemicals.
Management said next four quarters at Rs 100 crore-plus are possible, subject to Q1 seasonality, and sequential quarters should improve on the prior year.
Around 3% margin impact seen in the immediate month from input cost inflation; a couple of quarters expected to pass costs through, with new contracts bid at higher prices.
Rs 1,000 crore revenue within four years described as an aspiration, not a commitment.
Water business entering FY27 with a strong chemicals and equipment order book; chemical contracts run to around mid-year, and FY27 budget already reflects the volume trend.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex of about Rs 20-21 crore, mainly PPE transferred on the demerger and office renovation (management).
About Rs 65 crore of cash on books; management said some would go to network growth and geographic expansion, with no new plant planned.
Construction chemicals: de-bottlenecking of production lines; repair mortars outsourced to contract manufacturers.
Limited surplus water chemical inventory was rationed across customers during the force majeure period; volumes were kept below potential.
demand_pricing: Growth was mainly volume-driven, with new customer acquisition as the main driver; price growth contributed very little in FY26.
Construction chemicals realisation fell to about Rs 51,274/MT in H2 from about Rs 55,584/MT in H1, which management attributed to product mix (admixtures vs sealants).
Distribution realisation fell to about Rs 1.19 lakh/MT in H2 from about Rs 1.51 lakh/MT in H1, attributed to product mix.

Input costs: metal-linked raw materials (zinc, molybdenum) rose from late February/March; management said 15 A-group items are up more than 120%.
Competitors named: Ecolab, Nalco, Solenis, Suez/Veolia, Ion Exchange, Thermax; Vasu Chemicals now owned by Dorf Ketal.
Largest customer under 5-6% of revenue; Nigeria export business exited after the customer refused LC terms.

qa_highlights.question: Can the Rs 100 crore-plus quarterly run-rate continue for the next four quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes is possible, with Q1 seasonally slower than Q4, but quarter-on-quarter and year-on-year comparisons should improve.

qa_highlights.question: How much margin pressure from input costs, and can margins return to last year's levels?
qa_highlights.answer: About 3% margin impact in the immediate month; cost pass-through takes a couple of quarters, and new contracts are being priced at higher baselines. Chemical prices have softened only slightly.

qa_highlights.question: Why is other income negative this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Fair-value adjustment on investments: net gain was lower than in the prior quarter and the loss on fair value of investments was higher.

qa_highlights.question: Why are construction and distribution realisations lower in H2 than H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Product mix; admixtures lower realisation, sealants higher. Distribution is purely trading, so mix depends on customer demand.

qa_highlights.question: Can water business margins reach construction-level PBT of about 20%, and why are they lower?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said peer margins are at par, within about 0.5 percentage points; employee cost is about 18% of revenue in water versus 14% in other businesses.

qa_highlights.question: What is the public/private split in water and how is force majeure being handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Public sector is about 28-30% and private about 70%. Private customers accepted temporary increases; public-sector customers refused, and the company is preparing contingency actions if disruption extends beyond another month.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation in metal-linked raw materials; about 3% immediate margin impact and pass-through lag of a couple of quarters.
Public-sector water customers (28-30% of water revenue) refusing price amendments; force majeure invoked and contingency plans in place if disruption extends beyond about one month.

Construction and distribution realisation decline from product mix; water realisation not disclosed on the call.
