544484|2026-06.headline: BlueStone Q1 FY27 revenue rose 49% YoY to INR 733 crore, with pre-Ind AS EBITDA up 135% to INR 55 crore and margin at 7.5%.
544484|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 49% YoY to INR 733 crore and pre-Ind AS EBITDA rose 135% to INR 55 crore, lifting operating margin to 7.5% (up 273 bps). Management attributed this to operating leverage despite a custom duty hike on gold from 6% to 15% that softened demand in May before June and July recovered. Same-store sales growth was 39%, repeat revenue share rose to about 60%, while new customer additions reportedly fell from about 50,000 to about 40,000 per quarter, which management tied to merchandise dislocation during the sharp gold rise. Management reiterated a long-term target of roughly INR 12,000 crore revenue in four years, around 30% SSSG and about 20% store distribution growth, though analysts questioned the arithmetic.

financial_highlights.value: About INR 50 crore, about 6.9% of revenue
financial_highlights.change: Flat vs 6.9% in same quarter last year
Up from INR 2,650 crore at March

segments.name: Online / omnichannel
segments.commentary: Management said more than 80% of sales originate online, with stores converting intent built online. Company describes itself as a consumer internet business that sells jewellery.

segments.name: Stores
segments.commentary: Network of 352 stores; recent stores are around 4,500 sq ft frontage, and management said operational sq ft and per-store unit economics are unchanged. Store additions guided to about 20% CAGR over four years, with a 70-80 annual run rate referenced.

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: About 95% of products sold are manufactured in-house; management estimates a 300-400 bps margin delta versus peers but stresses design control as the main rationale.

guidance_outlook: Long-term target of roughly INR 12,000 crore revenue in four years (from INR 2,440 crore in FY26), with around 30% SSSG on mature cohorts plus about 20% distribution growth.
Operating EBITDA margin expected to expand from 7.5% toward about 15% over four years, driven mainly by corporate and marketing scale leverage.
Marketing spend guided to fall from 6.6% of revenue in FY26 to about 4.5-4.6% over five years, with FY27 expected below 6.6%.
Blended inventory turn expected to improve towards 1.7-1.8x over four years, with improvement visible in FY27.
Store additions described as non-linear, but the 20% distribution growth trend line is expected to be retained through FY27.
capex_capacity: Store area grew about 25.5% YoY while rent expense grew about 35%; annual lease escalation is 3-5%.
Newer stores are larger (around 4,500 sq ft frontage) to add capacity, with management saying per-store rent and revenue are not materially different.
Older cohorts are said to deliver store-level ROIC around 40% at 1.8-2.0x inventory turns.
Around 20% distribution (store) CAGR guided over next four years; store additions expected to be non-linear.
demand_pricing: Demand softened in May after the gold import duty hike (6% to 15%), then recovered through June; management said July trends were similar to June.
Gold exchange volumes rose as gold prices climbed; management said no significant change in the last 1-2 weeks.
New customer additions fell from about 50,000 to about 40,000 per quarter, which management attributed to merchandise dislocation; repeat revenue growth was strong.
Repeat AOVs are said to be 20-30% higher than new-customer AOVs; blended AOV about INR 78,000.
Management says no 9-carat plans; 14-carat experiments are used in lower price points. Lab-grown diamonds are said to be under 1% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: How is demand trending into July after the May softness from the duty hike?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand softened in May, recovered through June, and July is tracking similarly to June with no major difference.

qa_highlights.question: How should growth be thought of in H2 as gold inflation tapers, and the company lapping sharp gold rises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said stable gold is most supportive for demand and that Q3 last year was its slowest quarter in history during the sharpest gold rise; it does not expect a headwind.

qa_highlights.question: Why has new customer addition fallen to about 40,000 and what is being done?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged the drop, attributed it to merchandise dislocation being fixed, and said month-on-month new customer trends are improving.

qa_highlights.question: Math behind the 50% revenue CAGR given 30% SSSG and 20% distribution growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 30% refers to mature-cohort SSSG at maturity (years 3-6), not reported SSSG, and that reported SSSG would be higher due to new stores.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin expanded about 100 bps excluding inventory gain; what drove it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said mix changes in studded share were not material; contribution margin, the more relevant metric, has been largely stable, and EBITDA expansion comes from operating leverage.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory: what is the figure and why did it rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory is about INR 2,800 crore at end June versus INR 2,650 crore in March; management said store additions and gold prices drive the balance and turns should improve.

qa_highlights.question: Why 20% distribution growth rather than a slower pace?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most operating leverage comes from corporate and marketing scale rather than store-level profit, so faster distribution growth is preferred.

qa_highlights.question: Marketing spend trend and percent of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Marketing was about INR 50 crore, 6.9% of revenue, same as last year; it fell from about 9.2% four years ago to 6.6% in FY26.

risks_watch: Gold price volatility and import duty changes (6% to 15%) affecting demand, merchandise mix and inventory levels.
Slowing new customer additions (about 40,000 vs about 50,000 earlier) and whether merchandise dislocation is resolved.
Gap between reported SSSG and the 30% long-term SSSG used to underpin the 50% revenue CAGR target.
Rent growth (35%) outpacing store area growth (25.5%), and whether store productivity keeps pace with expansion.
Inventory turn trajectory from current level toward 1.7-1.8x, and inventory balance at the next quarter-end.
544484|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, margins and long-term targets, but evasive on reported SSSG arithmetic, new customer targets and inventory data (declined to give kg or detailed AOV). Management stressed that quarterly numbers are noisy and that analysts should focus on cohort and per-store metrics.
key_quotes: Q1 marks a strong start to the year.
That relationship, revenue scaling against a cost base that rose far more slowly, is the operating leverage in our model becoming visible.
So if gold stays range-bound, it's even better for us.
We are the only jewellery company that has built its entire technology stack in-house.

544484|2026-09.headline: BlueStone Q2 FY27 revenue grew 44% YoY to INR 738 crore, EBITDA more than doubled, and the company posted its fourth consecutive standalone profitable quarter.
544484|2026-09.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 revenue of INR 738 crore, up 44% YoY, with EBITDA more than doubling and a fourth straight profitable quarter on a standalone basis. Management said about 29% of the 44% growth came from AOV increase, with the rest from buyer growth, and that SSSG was around 28% in the quarter. The company crossed 1 million customers, opened 27 stores across 7 new cities, and reset entry-level price points, which lowered sequential AOV. Management said festive-season timing shifted some demand into Q3, and that early Q3 trends were in line with expectations, with most big buying days still ahead.

financial_highlights.change: YoY as stated, no figure given
Q2 FY27 as cited by analyst
Close to 30% AOV growth per analyst
Management expects about 4.5% in roughly four years
Below FY25 and FY26 levels per analyst

segments.name: Online and store retail
segments.commentary: Online is the primary acquisition channel with no BTL spend; stores opened 27 in the quarter across 7 new cities, mostly Tier-2 and Tier-3, with some in existing metros. Store count was about 340 in FY26, with the company targeting about 380 now and closer to 500 in coming months (per analyst).

guidance_outlook: Management expects further inventory turn improvement at the aggregate level as older cohorts mature and gold prices stabilise.
Management guided A&P spend to fall to around 4.5% of revenue over roughly the next four years.
Management reiterated a long-term revenue ambition of INR 12,000 crore by 2030 (per analyst question; not re-confirmed in management answer).
Management expects Q3 to show clearly whether buyer growth offsets slower AOV growth as gold prices stabilise.
Board gave in-principle approval for an INR 300 crore NCD raise, primarily to retire higher-cost debt; coupon and tenure not disclosed.
capex_capacity: Store expansion: 27 stores opened in Q2 FY27 across 7 new cities (mostly Tier-2 and Tier-3).
Flagship store at Park Street, Kolkata launched as an experiment; management may open one or two more, featuring handmade and Kundan products.
Design portfolio exceeds 10,500 designs; new handcrafted and antique range launched at Park Street.

Working capital: management said the IPO-raised INR 750 crore for working capital is exhausted (per analyst); funding now relies on internal accruals, low net debt-to-equity, and customer advances and schemes.
Inventory and store productivity: older cohorts (5 to 7 years) win more inventory only if they achieve 1.8 to 2 turns with continued growth.
demand_pricing: AOV fell sequentially as entry-level price points were reset; management said the AOV decline was intentional and is producing results.
Management said repeat customers buy at higher AOV than new customers, and that repeat is strong (rejecting an analyst's flattish-repeat characterisation).
Management said new-customer growth was weaker last year after gold rose 50-70%, and that entry price points were redesigned from Q3 FY26.
Festive timing: Navratri started late, so only 10-11 days of the season were visible at the time of the call; Karwa Chauth and Dhanteras are still ahead.
Lab-grown diamonds: management said consumers in stores are not asking for LGD; the company's solitaire share is under 1%, and LGD is taking share mainly from solitaires.
Hedging: 50% hedging policy unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the SSSG was shifted into Q3 due to the festive timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is hard to quantify the shift, but acknowledged a reasonable impact and gave no number.

qa_highlights.question: Can AOV growth continue if gold prices are flat, and what is the buyer growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth has not swung much with gold prices; about 10-15% ticket growth comes from repeat customers maturing, with buyer growth expected to contribute more as gold stays stable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cohort data status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give quarterly cohort data, saying cohorts are better reviewed in blocks; some disclosure already exists.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Tier-3 expansion different in assortment and price points?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sees no meaningful price-point difference between Tier-1, 2 and 3 customers, and that marketing stays online with no BTL.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for the 2030 INR 12,000 crore revenue target and the working capital need?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said funding comes from internal accruals as stores mature, low net debt-to-equity, and third-party liabilities such as customer advances and schemes; it sees no funding challenge.

qa_highlights.question: What is the INR 300 crore NCD for, and what is the coupon?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is an in-principle Board approval to retire higher-cost debt and lower blended cost of debt; coupon and tenure will be disclosed when finalised.

risks_watch: AOV growth normalises as gold prices stabilise; buyer growth must offset it in Q3.
Festive demand timing: part of Q2 demand shifted into Q3, and Q3 trends are not yet visible.
Contribution margin and studded mix: margin fell about 50 bps YoY while studded share declined; management declined to break down drivers.
Inventory: management gave no target inventory level or kilogram figure; GMROI on reported basis is lower than prior years, and management points to cohort vintage.
Financing: NCD terms unknown; the cost of debt reduction is not quantified.
Management declined to give cohort data quarterly, reducing visibility into vintage performance.
544484|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on growth, customer reach and margin health, but evasive on quantification: management declined to size festive shift, cohort data, contribution margin drivers, NCD terms and the cost reduction.
key_quotes: Revenue grew 44% year-on-year to INR 738 crores, EBITDA more than doubled, and this is our fourth consecutive profitable quarter on a standalone basis.
It took us 15 years to reach our first million customers. The next million will come much faster.
So, I think there is no point in giving cohort data every quarter, and there is no intention to do that, as well.

544485|2026-03.headline: Regaal FY26 operating income rose 23.9% to INR 1,134.2 crore and PAT reached INR 55.6 crore; 1,650 TPD expansion commissioned 26 May 2026, with no formal guidance until H1 FY27.
544485|2026-03.overview: FY26 showed strong growth, with operating income up 23.9% YoY to INR 1,134.2 crore, value-added revenue up 18% to INR 295.8 crore, and PAT of INR 55.6 crore (4.9% margin). Q4 FY26 operating income was INR 244.6 crore, operating EBITDA INR 32.5 crore (13.3% margin) and PAT INR 16.5 crore. Crushing capacity was raised to 1,650 TPD on 26 May 2026 with liquid glucose, maltodextrin and a 10 MW power addition, and the capex estimate rose from about INR 430 crore to INR 540 crore. Management declined to give FY27 volume, margin or revenue guidance, promising a firm outlook by end of Q1/H1 FY27.

financial_highlights.change: Operating EBITDA margin 10.7% in Q3 per management

financial_highlights.value: INR 0.25 per share, subject to shareholder approval

segments.name: Native and modified starch, edible starch
segments.commentary: Native maize starch, edible starch, white/yellow dextrin and oxidised starch form the core; management said native starch was about 65% of the 825 TPD output in FY26, with co-products about 30% and value-added about 2-3%.

segments.name: Value-added / derivatives (new capacity)
segments.commentary: Liquid glucose at 180 TPD and maltodextrin powder at 50 TPD were commissioned 26 May 2026; 230 tons of DMH/DAH already commissioned. Management targets value-added at about 20-25% of revenue in FY27 and about 35% at full capacity.

segments.name: Consumer products and co-products
segments.commentary: Maize flour, custard powder, baking powder, icing sugar, germ, gluten, fibre and steep liquor are produced; management said co-product prices rose from March 2026 and starch prices recovered on reopened export markets.

segments.name: Trading of maize
segments.commentary: Trading contributed around 30%+ of revenue in the prior year per an analyst; management said it will fall to near zero as the new capacity absorbs the raw material.

guidance_outlook: No formal FY27 earnings guidance; management will provide a firm outlook between Q1 and H1 FY27 after the plant stabilises.
Ramp-up to full 1,650 TPD expected within about 15-20 days ('weeks, not months'), subject to no issues; management expects to reach 100% of rated capacity fairly quickly.
Management said revenue should at least double at full capacity, with cycles tied to maize prices; maize prices expected to be about 10% lower than last year, roughly INR 2 per kg.
Value-added share of revenue expected at about 20-25% in FY27 and about 35% at peak capacity; value-added margin delta guided at about 20-25% over starch prices.
Cash conversion cycle expected to move between 50 and 75 days, rising in Q1-Q2 with working capital peaking mid-year.
Total debt expected at about INR 700-750 crore during FY27 including working capital, against net debt of about INR 545.65 crore now.
Remaining capex of about INR 140 crore for FY27 after INR 401 crore spent by 31 March 2026 on a total of about INR 540 crore.
White-labelling volumes, currently 2-2.5% of starch volume with 4 partner companies, expected to rise considerably within H1 FY27.
capex_capacity: Crushing capacity expanded to 1,650 TPD, commissioned 26 May 2026, from 825 TPD in FY26; the largest maize milling facility in Eastern India per management.
Captive co-generation capacity raised by 10 MW to 15.8 MW total; 5 MW of the new 10 MW is being drawn at present. Approx. 81% of FY26 power needs were met captively.

Capex revised upward from about INR 430 crore to about INR 540 crore; INR 401 crore spent by 31 March 2026 and INR 140 crore to be spent in FY27. Commissioning of all facilities is expected over FY27.

Dextrose anhydrous (DAH) and dextrose monohydrate (DMH) to launch in Q3 to Q4 FY27 (around December-January); modified starch additions include cationic, carboxymethyl and pre-gel starch, gulal, spray starch and hydrol.
Storage: 65,000 MT of maize silos and godowns, plus about 240,000 MT of contracted warehouse capacity; procurement via 27 FPCs across six to seven districts; the 55-acre site has room for expansion.
demand_pricing: Maize prices are down versus last year (last year about INR 18-23/kg); management expects FY27 procurement prices about 10% lower, around INR 2/kg less, with farmer deliveries only starting from mid-May 2026 due to rain.
Starch prices recovered as export markets reopened; co-product (germ, gluten, fibre) prices rose sharply from March 2026 into Q1 FY27.
Management cited improved global cost competitiveness after the softening of raw material prices and a sizeable export order secured; South-East Asia is the focus market.
Customer base is 345 as of March 2026, with 134 added in FY26; dealer channel is 65.5% of annual revenue.
Management declined to disclose the revenue split across food, pharma and agriculture end-markets.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating margin fall QoQ from 19% to 14% per an analyst, when peers improved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management disputed the figures, saying operating EBITDA margin rose from 10.7% in Q3 to 13.3% in Q4; EBITDA fell in absolute terms due to costs ramped up ahead of the expansion, with steady-state margins expected from Q2 or Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Bihar interest subvention and how is it accounted?
qa_highlights.answer: Subvention covers loan interest up to 10% per annum, capped at INR 20 crore over five years; receipts have typically come within about a quarter of application. It is booked as a receivable and credited against interest cost, so the 5% effective interest rate already reflects it.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital pattern and cash conversion cycle outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital rises in Q1, peaks around Q2 and falls from Q3 to Q4; the cash conversion cycle is expected to range between 50 and 75 days.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other current assets rise from INR 56 crore to INR 170 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Advances to maize suppliers and warehouses were given in March ahead of the 1,650 TPD ramp-up; advances rose from INR 45 crore to about INR 150 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How much value-added revenue is expected and at what uplift?
qa_highlights.answer: Value-added share is expected to rise from about 2-3% in FY26 to about 20-25% in FY27 and about 35% at full capacity; the delta over starch prices is about 20-25%, with a detailed margin guide promised in H1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue will the 1,650 TPD plant generate, and when will it run at optimum?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said revenue will at least double, with fluctuations tied to maize prices; the plant should ramp within about 15-20 days, but no firm date or utilisation guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is maize trading going to continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Trading will drop to near zero because the new capacity absorbs the raw material; any residual buying is to capture size discounts on MOQs, not for revenue.

risks_watch: Ramp-up of the 1,650 TPD plant and the DAH/DMH launch timing (Q3-Q4 FY27) are not yet proven; management has refused guidance until Q1/H1 FY27.
Debt is rising from about INR 546 crore net to roughly INR 700-750 crore total, and the working capital cycle is expected to swing between 50 and 75 days.
Revenue depends on maize price cycles; a sharp fall in maize prices could reduce turnover, and co-product and starch prices remain volatile.
The Bihar interest subvention is capped at INR 20 crore over five years and its timing depends on government processing; a delay would lift the effective cost of debt.
Sharp decline in FY26 Q4 EBITDA in absolute terms and a Q3 to Q4 margin dispute suggest the pre-commissioning cost base is still high.
Peak utilisation, value-added share and the detailed value-added margin guidance are expected by H1 FY27; the 20-25% starch-price premium is an unverified management estimate.
544485|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth and capacity, but notably cautious on near-term numbers: management repeatedly declined to give FY27 guidance, volume, margin or revenue figures, deferring them to Q1/H1 FY27. It was evasive on the value-added capex split and end-market revenue, and somewhat defensive when questioned about the QoQ margin decline.
key_quotes: We view this as a high -conviction allocation of capital, and commissio ning of all the above facilities is expected over the course of FY27.
We believe this approach better serves our investors by ensuring that any guidance we provide is grounded in demonstrated operating performance rather than early -stage assumptions.
Sir, delta change of course the maize prices compared to last year's is less, sir.
It's going to be a double engine growth vehicle.

544485|2026-06.headline: Regaal Q1 FY27 operating income fell 18% YoY to Rs 202.15 cr as trading was cut, while value-added margin rose to 39.8% and PAT grew 47% to Rs 13.33 cr.
544485|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was a transition quarter: the doubled crushing capacity (825 to 1,650 TPD) was commissioned on 26 May 2026, with operations ramping from early June. Operating income fell 18% YoY to Rs 202.15 cr because low-margin trading was deliberately reduced (3.3% of revenue vs 19.5% in Q1 FY26). Value-added revenue grew 30.3% to Rs 80.53 cr and EBITDA rose 26.6% to Rs 30.98 cr, with margin up 540 bps to 15.3%. Capacity utilisation was 71.4%, with management guiding to progressive improvement from Q2 FY27 and a shift to deleveraging after the capex cycle.

segments.name: Trading
segments.commentary: Contribution fell to 3.3% of revenue in Q1 FY27 from 19.5% in Q1 FY26 as low-margin trading was deliberately cut.

segments.name: Value-added products (liquid glucose, maltodextrin, starches)
segments.commentary: Value-added revenue Rs 80.53 cr (+30.3% YoY) at 39.8% margin. Liquid glucose at about 70% of its capacity; maltodextrin powder still ramping, with 2-3 more months needed to reach target.

segments.name: Maize starch / core crushing
segments.commentary: Crushing of 69,689 MT in Q1, with about 5,500 MT of incremental volume attributed by management to liquid glucose and a small part maltodextrin.

guidance_outlook: FY27 crushing expected at about 4 lakh tons (minimum), vs about 2.65 lakh tons in FY26.
Q2 FY27 crushing guided to 100,000-110,000 tons, contingent on smooth stabilisation and integration.
Value-added share of turnover expected at about 20-22% in FY27 (vs about 3% last year); later guided to about 30-35% of turnover on capacity mix.
Management declined to give EBITDA per ton or EBITDA margin guidance, citing maize and product price dependence; said operating leverage and value-add mix should improve margins at constant prices.
Net interest cost (net of subvention) for FY27 expected at about Rs 39-40 crore, broadly flat vs FY26.
Total project outlay about Rs 664 crore, of which about Rs 552 crore incurred as of 30 June 2026.
Working capital debt expected to decline in H2; management cited a prior pattern of about 40% reduction by Q4.
Dextrose Anhydrous, Dextrose Monohydrate and Hydrol expected by about Q4 FY27; modified starches (cationic, carboxymethyl, pre-gel, spray) trials to be fully online by September 2026.
No new capex decided; management said focus is on stabilising at 90-95% utilisation and deleveraging before considering next expansion.
capex_capacity: Crushing capacity doubled from 825 to 1,650 MT per day, commissioned 26 May 2026; operations started early June; described as largest maize wet milling facility in eastern India.
New liquid glucose facility 180 TPD, maltodextrin powder facility 50 TPD, captive cogeneration expanded from 7.1 MW to 15.8 MW.
Q1 utilisation 71.4%; about 9 shutdown days during April-May integration cost roughly 7,200 MT of output (management estimate).
Planned additions: 50,000 MT storage across two new silos, a 50,000 sq ft maize godown, and a 1.6 MW methane gas-based power plant.
Bihar interest subvention applies to new capex debt; management said the subvention cap was amended to Rs 40 crore but final policy notification was still awaited.

Maize procurement: about 80% of annual requirement bought in the Rabi season (Apr-Jul), 10-15% from other states; Bihar maize quoted at about Rs 22.5-23/kg delivered vs market talk of Rs 24.
Liquid glucose sold mainly September to March; big MNC customers now billed directly, and white-labelling customer base has grown.

544497|2026-03.headline: Anlon FY26 consolidated income rose 42.98% to INR 172.22 crore and PAT 41.77% to INR 29.09 crore, but Q4 PAT fell to INR 11.07 crore from INR 16.65 crore.
544497|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 consolidated total income of INR 172.22 crore (+42.98% YoY), EBITDA of INR 47.77 crore (+47.55%) and PAT of INR 29.09 crore (+41.77%), driven by the Apiqo and Bizotic acquisitions. Q4 total income rose to INR 50.90 crore from INR 48.97 crore, but PBT was flat at INR 14.44 crore and PAT fell to INR 11.07 crore, which management attributed to higher operating and development expenses and raw material cost spikes linked to the Middle East conflict. Management guided FY27 revenue to INR 380-400 crore, FY28 to INR 700-800 crore in one answer (INR 600-700 crore in another), and consolidated EBITDA margin of 24-25% as a floor, with a sharp reduction in receivables and cash-flow positivity targeted by end FY27. Several answers were inconsistent (EBITDA margin guidance ranged from 24-25% to 30-35%; FY28 revenue from 600-700 to 700-800 crore), and the call was disrupted by poor audio for several analysts.

Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of ₹350-400 cr and a ~30% three-year revenue CAGR, but gave limited quantitative detail on Remember India.

544515|2026-06.headline: Urban Company Q1 FY27 consolidated NTV rose 42% YoY to ₹1,465 crore; Services NTV grew 29% and InstaHelp loss narrowed to ₹(132) crore.

Core Services NTV accelerated for a fourth straight quarter to 29% growth (₹1,056 crore), and Services adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 6.9% of NTV. Consolidated loss was ₹(65) crore, almost entirely from InstaHelp, while the rest of the business delivered an adjusted EBITDA of ₹67 crore. Management retained its guidance of consolidated adjusted EBITDA breakeven by Q3 FY28 and ₹1,000 crore adjusted EBITDA by FY31, and framed InstaHelp as the main investment area.

financial_highlights.change: +5.2 pp YoY (stated as 170 bps improvement in the margin line in the Q&A)

segments.commentary: NTV ₹237 crore, up 76% YoY (58% ex-currency). UAE and Singapore both grew strongly; the Saudi Arabia JV is approaching profitability. UAE and Saudi JV are described as nearing or at profitability, and the company is not planning new international markets.

guidance_outlook: Retains guidance of consolidated adjusted EBITDA breakeven by Q3 FY28.
Retains guidance of ₹1,000 crore adjusted EBITDA by FY31.

Management said competitors in the InstaHelp category have pricing of ₹80-120 per hour for full-month subscriptions and that competitive intensity is high; it said the company has no reason to comment on rival strategies.
Management said the 3 major players have limited their household coverage to about 3.5-4 million households; the company believes most spending goes to subsidised repeat orders.
Management said the company has 'underestimated' the Tier 2 opportunity, with Tier 2 cities performing as well as Tier 1.

Management said it is seeing acceleration in MAUs, DAUs and MTUs, with conversion rates improving; the marketing spend in Services was about ₹25 crore in the quarter versus ₹24 crore a year ago (flat).

qa_highlights.question: Morgan Stanley: is the Cheaper, Faster, Better flywheel now visible enough to call a bold trajectory shift in Services NTV growth, and can growth be guided higher?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the flywheel comes from densifying many micro-markets, which improves partner utilisation, lowers churn and supports trust. It cited UC Instant (30-60 minute service) as a new driver. It declined to give growth guidance, said the 29% was helped by a muted prior-year base from unseasonal rains and monsoon, and said the margin of 6.9% is in line with the 9-10% long-term target, which is not a trade-off against growth.

qa_highlights.question: Morgan Stanley: why should InstaHelp get capital and attention, and how will capital be allocated over two years between Services, new segments and international?
qa_highlights.answer: InstaHelp is strategically relevant because its high frequency keeps users on the app weekly. Services is to be profitable and cash generating; UAE and Singapore are profitable wholly owned subsidiaries; the Saudi JV is nearing profitability. InstaHelp needs two years or more of investment, with capital allocation revisited at adjusted breakeven, hopefully within about 18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Goldman Sachs: why not export the UAE and Saudi model to new international markets, given Core Services is generating cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited bandwidth as the main constraint. It said playbooks need local customisation plus some luck, and that earlier Australia and US launches did not succeed. It will stay focused on UAE, Saudi Arabia and India, with no plans for new international markets for now.

qa_highlights.question: Goldman Sachs: where does Services margin go from 6.9% of NTV versus the 9-10% target, and would the company cap margin around 10% or reinvest?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the goal is to reach the 9-10% range without rushing and without trading growth for margin. Priority one is growing fast, priority two is margin expansion. Once it reaches about 10%, it will decide whether to lift margins further or reinvest for faster growth.

qa_highlights.question: Goldman Sachs: is the InstaHelp TAM structurally lower, and would the company operate at a narrow loss if competition leaves room for only two players?
qa_highlights.answer: The base case is INR 7,000-8,000 crore NTV and the bull case is INR 10,000-12,000 crore, with 3 orders per user per month. Management said the 3 major players have limited coverage to about 3.5-4 million households and that subsidised repeat orders dominate spend. It expects a low single-digit market share outcome and says it will not spend heavily on the category to drive share, while being opinionated about winning micro-markets.

qa_highlights.question: Bank of America: what AOV is needed for InstaHelp to break even, and is there scope for growth above 29%?
qa_highlights.answer: Sustainable professional payout is INR 130-160 per hour, with INR 150 as the rule of thumb. Gross breakeven needs about INR 200 per hour, and an AOV of about INR 300 is needed for InstaHelp to break even. Management said breakeven could take a couple of years or up to 5 years, and it declined to give growth guidance beyond the 29%.

qa_highlights.question: Bank of America: how is AI being used and how much margin benefit is there?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 90-95% of the code is now written by AI, and that support, supply-side onboarding, quality audits and fraud detection are increasingly AI-led. Marketing and Finance/HR run AI end-to-end. It said the margin benefit has started to show but there is a long way to go.

qa_highlights.question: Kotak: is Beauty acceleration sustainable, and are the 30-40 annual transactions per user assumption and consolidation prospects realistic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Beauty has seen a resurgence after retraining and retooling partners, and that the company had underinvested there a couple of years back. Two-wheeler access for Beauty professionals is now a majority. It expects 3 transactions per month, not 30-40, for the 10-12 lakh household case. It expects private players to keep burning cash and believes it will be the eventual winner in the category.

qa_highlights.question: Bellwether: what is driving the 5 lakh quarter-on-quarter user addition, what marketing spend is involved, and what training and capacity constraints exist in InstaHelp and Core Services?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the user growth is largely from MAU, DAU and MTU growth and better conversion, and that marketing spend in Services was about INR 25 crore versus INR 24 crore a year ago. For Core, it said capacity is comfortable but is being scaled up, with all hands on deck, to match trainer and infrastructure growth. It said InstaHelp supply is also being expanded.

qa_highlights.question: Emkay: is the shift to premium products a sign of a premium customer base, and will the company expand beyond water purifiers and smart locks?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its products, such as the M3 water purifier with a 3-year no-service, no-filter-change design, are aimed at lowering lifecycle cost. It said it is not building a durables company and will keep its focus on a small number of categories, mainly water purifiers and smart locks, with the aim of serving the top households in India.

risks_watch: InstaHelp losses: the loss was INR (132) crore; management expects 2+ years of investment and an adjusted breakeven target within about 18 months. Track loss per order, which improved from INR (447) in Q4 to INR (346) in Q1.

Services margin: current 6.9% of NTV against a 9-10% long-term target; the timing of expansion remains unspecified.
Capacity and trainer scaling for Core Services as user additions accelerate.
544515|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the Services growth trend and the balance sheet, but cautious and deliberately non-committal on forward growth, TAM and the timing of InstaHelp breakeven. Management repeatedly declined to set expectations beyond the 29% trend.

544600|2026-03.headline: Lenskart Q4 FY26 revenue rose 41% YoY to ₹2,516 crore, with reported EBITDA up 61% and pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin at 12.8%.

India and international both grew, with India same-store sales growth at 24% and international revenue up 35.4%. FY26 crossed ₹1,700 crore EBITDA, ₹1,000 crore pre-Ind AS EBITDA and ₹500 crore PAT for the first time. Management kept the steady-state pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin at about 25% and guided FY27 net store additions to roughly FY26 levels (542 in India plus 61 international in FY26).

No material demand impact seen in India or abroad; Middle East dip was small and brief.

qa_highlights.question: How was the India gross margin held near 64% in a low-ASP quarter, and does SSSG of ~25% with ~15% price imply ~10% volume growth?

Management said the 10% volume estimate was not correct and that volume SSS is meaningfully higher; it does not disclose value/volume split.

qa_highlights.question: How will employee productivity and cost leverage trend, especially internationally?

qa_highlights.question: Does Tier 2 strength expand the 4,500-store runway and allow faster expansion?

544608|2026-06.headline: Emmvee Q1 FY27 revenue rose 51% YoY to INR 1,555 crore, EBITDA margin 35%, PAT INR 380 crore (+103% YoY); order book 9.9 GW.

PAT was INR 380.3 crore, helped by finance costs falling to INR 11.1 crore from INR 53.1 crore a year earlier. Module and cell production both hit record quarterly levels, with cell utilisation up to 83%, and order book rose to 9.9 GW after 1,484 MW of inflows. Management reiterated stable EBITDA per watt (module about INR 2.5/W, cell INR 6.0-6.5/W) and a 6 GW TOPCon cell and module expansion on schedule.

Full-year FY26 revenue was Rs 26,545 million (+72.3%) and PAT Rs 3,041 million (11.5% margin). Capacity expansion continued at Ratlam, with the 2 GW solar panel plant commissioned, though the inverter and battery lines slipped to 2027. A fire at the Bawal lead-acid battery facility (1.3 GW capacity) has suspended operations, with third-party arrangements covering supply. Management guided FY27 revenue up 50% and PAT margin of 11% to 13%.

segments.commentary: Capacity rose from 1,143 MW to 2,180 MW during FY26. Inverter line at Ratlam is expected to be commissioned in Q1 2027.

segments.name: Lithium-ion batteries
segments.commentary: Capacity rose from 45 MWh to 545 MWh during FY26. Battery machinery orders are placed, with commissioning expected in Q2 2027.

segments.name: Lead-acid batteries (Bawal)
segments.commentary: Facility with 1.3 GW capacity suspended after a fire; no casualties. Management said it is covered by insurance and third-party capacity is being used.

FY27 PAT margin guided at 11% to 13%; management said margins are stable to improving.
Indicative FY27 quarterly revenue split: Q1 about Rs 900 crore, Q2 about Rs 800 crore, Q3 about Rs 800 crore, Q4 about Rs 1,500 crore.
Ratlam 2 GW integrated facility expected to reach peak revenue of about Rs 5,000 crore, fully utilised by Q4 FY28; utilisation about 50% in FY27 and about 80% in FY28.

capex_capacity: Solar panel capacity at Ratlam (2 GW integrated facility) commissioned; inverter line machinery received and commissioning expected Q1 2027; battery lines Q2 2027.

demand_pricing: Channel network crossed 8,900 partners by March 2026, after adding 80+ distributors, 450+ dealers and 30 exclusive outlets in Q4.
FY26 sales were about 1 GW of integrated SPGS systems; management said growth was volume-led, roughly 70% in GW terms.
Demand driven by off-grid and hybrid backup in Tier 2/3 towns and villages; management said Tier 1 on-grid sales were now being added.
Management said over 7 million PM Surya Ghar installations remain untapped, about 25 GW opportunity; ALMM List-II is expected soon and will require DCR cells.
Management said it is passing margin to customers to acquire distributors and dealers, and that competition is mainly in ground-mounted business.
Receivables are from distributors only; revenue cycle about 14 days.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory rise sharply, and what is the raw material vs finished goods split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the increase is mainly raw material for new locations (Dadri, Noida, Ratlam); raw material is above Rs 500 crore of about Rs 900 crore total inventory, and finished goods inventory days are similar to last year. Management expects inventory days to fall once lines ramp up.

qa_highlights.question: Bawal fire: is the facility operational and what is the margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Operations are suspended and the cause is under investigation. Management said margin impact is slight, offset by third-party lead-acid capacity bought at good prices, and that the incident will not have a material long-term impact.

qa_highlights.question: BIS seizures: what was affected and what is the penalty exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 10 to 15 of about 500 SKUs, mainly inverters and batteries, are under BIS query. The maximum penalty equals the seizure value, but management expects a lower outcome. It said there is no impact on the Dadri or Ratlam ramp-up or PM Surya Ghar participation.

qa_highlights.question: What are the revenue and margin contributions from the Ratlam and TOPCon cell lines?
qa_highlights.answer: Ratlam peak revenue is about Rs 5,000 crore when fully utilised. The TOPCon cell line adds no revenue, only backward integration and margin benefit. Management said it is passing DCR margin to customers rather than retaining it.

qa_highlights.question: Long-term PAT margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided FY27 PAT margin at 11% to 13%, said margins are stable to improving, and cited AI-led opex reduction. It did not give a 36-month target.

risks_watch: Bawal fire: cause unknown, operations suspended, and reliance on third-party lead-acid supply.
BIS query on 10 to 15 SKUs (inverters and batteries), with a court decision pending.

Ratlam ramp-up is slipping: inverter and battery lines are delayed to 2027 and utilisation is 50% in FY27.
Competitive intensity as new capacity comes online; management said it may trade margin for distributor growth.
Management declined to disclose segment-wise or megawatt volumes, which limits verification of the 50% guidance.

qa_highlights.question: How should full-year revenue and profit be modelled after a strong Q1?

qa_highlights.question: Will backward integration lift margins or be passed on to customers?

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Bawal fire loss is recoverable?

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the TOPCon line and the lead-acid plant after the fire?

544679|2026-03.headline: Amagi FY26 revenue rose 30% to INR 1,506 crores and turned PAT positive at INR 72 crores, swinging about INR 140 crores from a FY25 loss.
544679|2026-03.overview: Amagi reported its first full year as a listed company, with FY26 revenue of INR 1,506 crores (up 30% reported, 23% constant currency) and Q4 revenue of INR 397 crores (up 29%). Adjusted EBITDA rose to about INR 156 crores (10% margin) from INR 23 crores, and PAT was INR 72 crores versus a loss of INR 69 crores in FY25. Management stressed net revenue retention of 126% and growth across all three segments, while flagging Q4 gross margin compression tied to customer pricing, AI costs and parallel-running of lower-cost alternatives. NEWSPULSE, the first agentic AI product, has its first paying customer and is in trials with news networks.

segments.name: Streaming unification
segments.commentary: Largest segment at INR 838 crores, up 26% YoY, roughly more than half of revenue; serves OTT, FAST and CTV platforms.

segments.name: Monetization and marketplace
segments.commentary: INR 381 crores, up 36% YoY, about a quarter of revenue and the fastest-growing segment; monetized impressions grew about 62% YoY. Management does not yet report marketplace separately.

segments.name: Cloud modernization
segments.commentary: INR 286 crores, up 32% YoY, about a fifth of revenue; AccuWeather migration to Amagi Cloud completed end-to-end this quarter.

guidance_outlook: No prescriptive FY27 guidance; management aspires to keep growing at a healthy clip, citing the trajectory of the last three years.
Focus areas for FY27 are durable revenue growth, operating leverage and cash conversion.
Current margin levels are not steady state; management sees headroom and upside, and will make ahead-of-curve AI investments.

Gross margin: management said not to extrapolate quarterly moves to full year and expects volume growth to offset modest CPM/price compression; the gross margin impact of NEWSPULSE is too early to quantify.
Seasonality: Q1 is about 22% of full-year revenue and about 11% of adjusted EBITDA; H1 is about 45% of revenue and H2 about 55%, with EBITDA about 37% in H1 and 63% in H2.
Management said no hedging book is in place; it is considering hedging this year given the net USD revenue position.
capex_capacity: Cost-side plan: R&D is being redirected toward next-generation agentic products; R&D fell from 33% to 23% of revenue over FY24-FY26.
Cloud modernization is in early innings; serviceable addressable revenue grew about 11% to USD 1.9 billion this year.
Management is scanning for buy-or-build acquisitions in glass-to-glass gaps, with no deal size fixed and no specific target named.
demand_pricing: Dollar-based NRR is north of 120%, in a 120% to 125% range for several years; management says it is comfortable even after currency adjustment.
Monetized impression growth of about 62% YoY came with revenue growth of 36%, implying modest CPM pressure offset by volume.
Q4 gross margin fell sequentially on customer pricing (renegotiation), AI costs (minor) and double-running costs of lower-cost alternatives on mission-critical workflows.
NEWSPULSE targets traditional news networks; tens of POCs are running, and management said it is too early to share sales-cycle or unit-economics detail.
No competitor seen as credible at platform level; management says customers prefer one unified platform over many point solutions.
Partnerships: ADAMS (Latin America), Anoki (ad partner), Vodafone deal in Germany, with progress in Australia and the US.

qa_highlights.question: Split of NEWSPULSE paid customers between cross-sell to existing Amagi clients and new logos, and unit economics or gross margin of the agentic product.
qa_highlights.answer: Existing customers are the first port of call, but NEWSPULSE is also landing new logos; tens of POCs are running and detail will come in coming quarters. Gross margin impact is too early to quantify; outcome-based pricing mixed with fixed fees, and no major margin impact seen so far.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin compression QoQ: how much was client renegotiation versus AI and investment costs, and will it persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Three drivers: customer pricing, AI cost (minor), and double-running costs of lower-cost alternatives. Management says full-year gross margin has held at about 69% and sees volume growth offsetting modest price compression.

qa_highlights.question: Sales headcount efficiency and how many accounts one salesperson can handle over 3 to 5 years.
qa_highlights.answer: Account management is sublinear in scale given NRR of 126%; product-led growth and AI tooling should lift efficiency. No revenue-share model; commissions are sliding-scale by hunter or farmer role.

qa_highlights.question: Does accelerating monetized impression growth reflect market conditions, and how exposed is revenue to advertising macro?
qa_highlights.answer: Impression growth reflects the shift to streaming. Customers' ad economics flow through to Amagi pricing with a lag; no impact seen yet, though geopolitics is a risk.

qa_highlights.question: Customer count trend and new customer additions, which have slowed on a quarterly basis.
qa_highlights.answer: Customer count rose to 492 in FY26 from 463 and 396 earlier; Q4 added 27 and churned 30, mainly year-end cleanup of sub-USD 1,000 accounts. Growth is coming from the existing base and upmarket enterprise deals.

qa_highlights.question: Cash deployment and acquisition plans, and CC NRR.
qa_highlights.answer: Corp Dev is scanning buy-or-build options in glass-to-glass gaps, with no size set and no irrational valuations. Dollar-based NRR is above 120%.

qa_highlights.question: Path to higher PAT margin and whether 5% is steady state.
qa_highlights.answer: Management says current margins are not steady state and that there is headroom, but will keep making ahead-of-curve AI investments.

risks_watch: Gross margin: Q4 compression from customer pricing and dual-running costs; the June quarter trend and whether pricing pressure outruns volume gains.
AI monetisation: NEWSPULSE has one paying customer so far; gross margin and unit economics remain unproven.
Customer churn and count: 30 accounts churned in Q4, and the net count rose only modestly.
Currency: most revenue is USD; about 30% of costs are direct costs and about 20% are USD-linked sales costs, with no formal hedge book.
Advertising macro: revenue is linked to customer ad spend, and management flagged geopolitical risk.
Acquisitions: cash of about INR 1,664 crores with no size or target set; deal and integration risk if pursued.
544679|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and balanced on FY26 delivery and retention metrics, with explicit caution that Q4 gross margin and NEWSPULSE economics are early. Management was evasive on FY27 numeric guidance, offering only qualitative aspirations.

So, I would apply the full year lens versus thinking about it quarter-on-quarter at steady state.
I wouldn't think about quarterly gross margin as an extrapolation factor for full year, right?
I wouldn't call these current levels steady state

544679|2026-06.headline: Amagi's July 7, 2026 "AI in Media" webinar was industry-level only; no quarterly financials, guidance or Amagi-specific metrics were disclosed.
544679|2026-06.overview: This transcript is of an educational investor webinar titled "AI in Media", hosted by Amagi on July 7, 2026 and filed under Regulation 30, not an earnings call. The moderator stated upfront that company financial performance, outlook and operational metrics would not be addressed. The CEO Baskar Subramanian framed AI as reshaping the video value chain across production, preparation (metadata, encoding, scheduling), distribution (agent-to-agent deals) and consumer discovery. He cited a claim that every $1 spent on technology brings $2 to $4 of human toil, and said most customers view AI as expansionary rather than a cost-saving tool today. No Q1 FY27 results, segment data or guidance were given.
guidance_outlook: No company guidance given; the moderator stated financial performance, business outlook and operational metrics would not be addressed.
Management described AI-driven production cost deflation as a multi-year shift, saying the next few years would bring a fundamental change, without quantifying it.
Management said outcome-based pricing is early and not yet visible in media, and that the core system is expected to stay as is while expansion revenue is driven by outcomes.
capex_capacity: Management said AI workloads are pushing customers from on-premise to cloud because they lack in-house GPUs and servers, and expects more progression in that direction; no Amagi capex or capacity figures were given.
Management said GPU costs are significant for video AI but did not quantify them; token cost is a small part of AI cost in video.
demand_pricing: Management says most customers are pursuing expansion (more channels, revenue opportunities) rather than AI cost savings today, citing Jevons' paradox.
Outcome-based pricing (per transaction, per result, per success) is being discussed in some markets, but management says it is not yet visible in media.

Management says token cost is a small part of AI cost in video; GPU costs are significant. It also cited an example of a scheduler's work falling from 8 hours to about 10 minutes of review under an agentic system.
Management described the metadata and preparation workload as a headcount constraint, with media companies creating about 6 hours of unique news daily and running content across 40-plus countries.

qa_highlights.question: What safeguards exist against hallucination and unpredictability given strict 99.9999% SLAs with clients?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the approach is to bring determinism to a non-deterministic problem through guardrails and engineered systems, noting that getting AI from demos to production is the hard part.

qa_highlights.question: Is AI improving prep-work speed and reducing pricing through deflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI mainly reduces human cost in preparation (e.g., speech-to-text making subtitling unnecessary) and expands what can be done rather than directly reducing price.

qa_highlights.question: Can AI move production and pre-production workflows to the cloud?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI workloads are pushing customers from on-premise to cloud because they lack in-house GPU and server capacity, and expects more of this shift.

qa_highlights.question: Are there real-life examples of cost reduction or higher OTT/cable content from AI?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said adoption is early, with some creators using AI for VFX and background creation, and microdrama as the most active area.

qa_highlights.question: Is there evidence of cost savings, given higher token costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said token cost is small relative to video GPU and human costs, and most customers are using AI for expansion, with cost savings secondary.

qa_highlights.question: Do agent-to-agent communications create network effects and first-mover advantage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said connecting two or more ecosystem parties through agentic infrastructure has high network-effect value, but the space is very early and standards are still forming.

qa_highlights.question: Does AI deepen client engagement and threaten horizontal SaaS or hyperscalers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management argued that vertical, mission-critical media software has a moat in enterprise context, which it sees as more durable than generic reasoning models.

qa_highlights.question: Will agentic AI materially cut customer operating costs and create pricing pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said per-job costs may deflate, but the volume of work customers want to do is expanding, which it characterised as a Jevons' paradox effect.

qa_highlights.question: How will vendor-client commercial models change as agentic AI spreads?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said outcome-driven pricing is being explored in other industries, but it is early and not yet prominent in media.

risks_watch: Hallucination and unpredictability of agentic AI against strict uptime SLAs, which management said it addresses with guardrails but gave no metrics for.
Rising GPU and infrastructure costs for video AI, which management said are material but did not quantify.
Possible shift in vendor pricing toward outcome-based models, which would change revenue recognition, though management said it is not yet visible.
The webinar did not address Amagi's own Q1 FY27 numbers, so the company's operating and financial trajectory remains unassessed; the company directed investors to ir@amagi.com for follow-up.
544679|2026-06.management_tone: Management was enthusiastic and expansive on long-term AI themes, but deliberately avoided Amagi-specific answers, redirecting company questions to generic industry views. Cautious on near-term monetisation, describing most AI use as early and expansionary rather than cost-saving.
key_quotes: So, a lot of work that our company, and I'm sure lots of companies are doing, is to bring determinism to an indeterministic problem.
for every dollar that they've been spending on technology, there's $2 to $4 of human toil.
Most of our customers are looking at more of an expansionary aspect, not as a cost saving capability as it stands today.

544681|2026-03.headline: INDO SMC guided FY27 revenue to INR450-500 crores on an INR237 crore order book plus INR125 crore fresh orders, with margins targeted at 15%+.
544681|2026-03.overview: FY26 was the first full year after listing, with management saying revenue roughly doubled and PAT more than doubled, driven by higher-value CT/PT, bus duct, meter cubicle and panel products. Management attributed a softer March-quarter SMC and FRP output to geopolitics-driven resin and petroleum-product price swings and supply gaps. The company shifted to shorter (2-3 month) orders with price-escalation clauses (5% trigger) and said it is now choosing orders on margin. Inventory rose to about INR85 crores (around 100 days) because of pre-stocked raw materials, and the working capital cycle was cut from 83 to about 40 days. Management did not give a precise FY26 revenue or margin figure in the call; the 15% EBITDA margin cited by analysts was not confirmed by management.

financial_highlights.metric: Fresh orders from April 1 to call date (as cited by management)
Combined order book (per management, including fresh orders)
EBITDA margin (as cited by analyst, not confirmed by management)

segments.name: CT/PT and LTCT (instrument transformers, electrical engineering)
segments.commentary: About INR120-125 crores of the order book; management said CT/PT is more engineering-intensive with margins above SMC/FRP, targeting above 18% EBITDA on standardised products. Currently operating at 11 kV and 33 kV, with 66 kV and above still in planning.

segments.name: Bus ducts, meter cubicles and panels
segments.commentary: Meter cubicle orders of INR10-15 crores were added, with new meter cubicle orders of INR10 crores-plus taken in the current period. Management described these as higher-margin lines bundled with SMC and CT/PT.

segments.name: SMC
segments.commentary: About INR80 crores of order book being executed month to month. Management said FY26 SMC and FRP output fell in March due to resin and petroleum-product shortages; the call did not give segment revenue figures.

segments.name: FRP (pultrusion, gratings) and tarpaulin
segments.commentary: Remainder of the order book, executed against monthly clearances. Plan to add about 300 tons of FRP production capacity.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Early-stage: Oman and Gulf orders, samples sent to US and Germany, Dubai electrical fair planned from September. Management said UL 94 certification is a requirement for the US and that certification takes 1-2 months.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of INR450-500 crores, subject to geopolitics and material availability; management said it can be met with existing capacity plus automation machinery.
H1 FY27 inflow target of INR200 crores-plus, lowered from an earlier INR250 crores-plus; management said H2 is expected to be stronger than H1.
EBITDA margin target of 15% or above; management said it expects to maintain FY26 margins in FY27 and aims for 1-2% better if conditions allow.
Medium-term aim of INR1,000 crores-plus revenue in about three years, with railways a major contributor from FY28 onward.
Railway clearance expected by end of the following month after the call, pending lab expansion; management said trial orders would grow over the next three years.
capex_capacity: Capex of INR25 crores (as disclosed in the IPO) is the first priority, covering machines and facilities across SMC, FRP and electrical engineering.
A 2,000-ton-plus SMC press is expected in 2-3 months, to enable larger railway products and big boxes; SMC capacity target is 6,000 tons-plus.
Nashik (Maharashtra) plant needs capex and more space; a second plant at Nashik has started production readiness. Ahmedabad is running well on utilisation.
Management said revenue above INR750 crores could come from the full capex once complete, and the company has land available so no major new building is needed.
Plans for 33 kV CTs and meter cubicles; a lab expansion funded from the IPO is expected to be completed by the end of the month after the call.
demand_pricing: Management said the utilities and electrical industry (SMC, FRP, CT/PT, LTCT, bus ducts, switchgear) is growing fast; it cited about 20 states served and a push to expand pan-India and export.
Pricing: management said recent orders are priced around INR450 per unit versus INR350-360 earlier, and that buyers are accepting the higher prices.
Competition in higher-kV CT/PT is limited: management said few players hold approvals, and cited ABB Crompton as operating at 66, 120 and 240 kV.

Raw materials: resin (SMC/FRP) and petroleum-linked inputs were the main pressure; glass fiber held in about 3 months' stock; copper and steel costs passed through at order time. Management said it took a hit on resin in March.
Order inflow pace: management cited INR3-4 crores in new orders on the day of the call and said small orders are taken to limit price-risk exposure.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SMC and FRP fall while CT/PT rose, and what is the order book breakup?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SMC and FRP fell from March due to geopolitics-driven resin and petroleum shortages and rate swings. Order book: about INR125 crores in CT/PT and LTCT, about INR80 crores in SMC, and the rest in FRP and tarpaulin.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins rise above 15%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 15%-plus is the target and the margin is sustainable, with the company now choosing higher-margin orders and CT/PT expected to earn above 18% on standardised products.

qa_highlights.question: How will working capital be funded, and will there be dilution or debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the working cycle improvement plus IPO cash should avoid a funding need this year; any future funding would be decided after September based on six-month results, with debt or equity depending on order size.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it began exports to Oman and the Gulf, sent samples to the US and Germany, plans to attend a Dubai electrical fair from September, and needs client approvals that take 1-2 months.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company reach INR1,000 crores revenue, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it targets INR1,000-plus crores in about three years, with railways contributing a significant share from FY28.

risks_watch: Resin and petroleum-product availability and price swings; management says price-escalation clauses apply only when moves exceed 5%.
Working capital: inventory at about INR85 crores (about 100 days) and the stated need to keep the cycle at 40-45 days.
Railway approvals delayed beyond the March expectation; management now expects clearance about a month after the call.
H1 FY27 inflow target cut to INR200 crores-plus from INR250 crores-plus; management did not give a full-year order inflow figure.
Dependence on government and utility orders; CRGO cores are imported from Korea, China, Japan and Taiwan.
544681|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on medium-term growth and margins, but cautious and hedged on near-term execution, citing geopolitics and material costs repeatedly. Several answers were vague or repeated, and some figures (order book breakup, 15% margin) were restated by analysts rather than confirmed by management.
key_quotes: Our target for this year is to achieve INR450 crores plus, and we are focused on that.
Yes, it is sustainable. We want to work at this minimum level and will target even better margins.
But standardized we will almost want to work above 18% EBITDA.

544684|2026-03.headline: Digilogic FY26 revenue rose 8.4% to INR78.27 crore and PAT 33.8% to INR10.43 crore, but a ~INR22 crore spillover from delayed imported hardware missed the 20-25% growth guidance.
544684|2026-03.overview: FY26 total income rose 8.4% YoY to INR78.27 crore, with EBITDA up 16.5% to INR15.18 crore and margin expanding 152 bps to 19.6%. PAT grew 33.8% to INR10.43 crore, and operating cash flow turned positive at INR12.63 crore. Management attributed the shortfall versus its January 2026 growth guidance to delayed imported OEM hardware, which pushed about INR22 crore of orders into FY27. Management guided to 20-25% growth for FY27, contingent on converting INR100-plus crore of orders by September 2026, and announced new subsidiary Abhedhya (RF systems), an SBC R&D effort, and Project UDAN manufacturing expansion.

segments.name: Measurement equipment
segments.commentary: About 49% of FY26 revenue; management said most of its value comes from software content with little material cost, supporting the margin gain.

segments.name: Checkout systems
segments.commentary: About 22% of FY26 revenue; ATEs about 17%. Management said ATE and checkout value was broadly flat YoY, and the share fell because measurement equipment grew.

segments.name: Prototyping vs production
segments.commentary: Management estimated roughly 30% of revenue from prototyping and 70% from production orders. This was not reconciled with a reported figure and was described as approximate.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 20-25%, reiterated on the call; management said it is confident of meeting it.
Management targets INR100-plus crore of purchase orders by end-September 2026, with billing for FY27 expected to be supported by that order intake.
Order book was about INR30-plus crore as of 30 May 2026, with most expected to bill by August 2026.

Project UDAN (new manufacturing facility, about four times the current capacity) expected operational by mid-2028; indicative revenue INR11-13 crore in FY29, INR28-30 crore in FY30, INR57-61 crore in FY31.
Current setup capacity estimated at INR150-160 crore revenue potential.
Abhedhya (RF subsidiary) expected to demonstrate systems in 8-12 months; management indicated revenue in FY28, not FY27.
capex_capacity: Project UDAN: a manufacturing and environmental testing facility, about four times current size; mid-2028 target; can deliver 20-25 systems per six months versus about six currently.
Guest house under construction; capitalised finance cost on exposure of about INR2.1 crore (not fully drawn), borrowing at REPO plus 2.5%.
Abhedhya, a new RF subsidiary for radar, EW and communication subsystems, with a 1-year build-and-demonstrate timeline.
R&D: custom single board computer (SBC) built in-house by an eight-member team, about 1.5-2 years old; qualification range -20 to +85 degrees C; environmental testing not yet completed.
Management said two to three new R&D products are in development.
demand_pricing: FY26 execution was held back by imported hardware from US/European OEMs; lead time rose from about 2 months to about 4 months, leaving roughly INR22 crore spilled into April 2026. Management said about INR20 crore additional revenue would otherwise have closed in FY26.

Order book fell to about INR31 crore from INR46 crore; the tender pipeline fell to about INR110 crore from INR200 crore. Management attributed this to Government fund reallocation and said projects are delayed 6-8 months rather than lost.
Management said OEMs are rerouting shipments, adding a week or 10 days and roughly 1-2% cost.
Competitors named: Data Patterns and Zen Technologies, mainly in prototyping. Management said production work under DCPP is nomination-based with limited competition.
Customer base is 100% government in substance (DRDO, BDL, BEL, public sector defence production agencies), with some transactions billed through BDL.
Management said the export route is via DRDO and BDL systems, and MoUs with Sperry and Eirad are at the evaluation stage toward Tier-1 aerospace supply chains.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY26 guidance of 20-25% growth missed, and what supports FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Imported hardware arrived about 4 months after order rather than 2, leaving roughly INR22 crore of spillover. Management cited INR30-plus crore of orders in hand by 30 May and a target of INR100-plus crore of POs by September.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the order book fall from INR46 crore to INR31 crore and the pipeline from INR200 crore to INR110 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said government fund reallocation changed priorities and projects are delayed 6-8 months rather than cancelled. The INR100-plus crore target covers only projects with budgets allocated or tenders out.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the revenue comes from production versus prototyping?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said roughly 30% prototyping and 70% production, and deferred exact figures to the CFO. No reported split was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why set up Abhedhya as a separate company rather than a division?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said RF work needs different people, salaries, infrastructure and design expertise than TMS, and separate accountability is needed. Tender qualification is to be built by demonstrating products first.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the ATE and checkout share fall from about 44% to 22%?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said measurement equipment, mostly software value add with low material cost, grew to a similar scale, and ATE and checkout value was broadly unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for the order book converting to revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Current orders should bill by about August 2026. Pipeline orders are expected as POs by end-September, with 2-3 months of build and about one month of installation, and cash collection around Aug-Oct.

risks_watch: Import dependence: US and European OEM hardware lead times stretched to about 4 months, and a repeat would repeat the FY26 spillover.
Order book of INR31 crore against FY27 growth target; the INR100-plus crore PO target by September 2026 is the key checkpoint.
Tender pipeline down from INR200 crore to INR110 crore; delays of 6-8 months attributed to Government budget reallocation.
Revenue mix is a management estimate (30% prototyping, 70% production), not a reported figure.
Project UDAN and Abhedhya are not yet operational; Abhedhya revenue is expected only in FY28, and the SBC still needs environmental qualification.
Governance: management's FY26 growth guidance was missed, and the call shows the company's first results call as a newly listed SME.
544684|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on FY27 targets and on the causes of the FY26 miss, which management attributes to imported-hardware delays. Less specific on the revenue split, timelines for UDAN and Abhedhya, and the exact reasons for the pipeline fall. Several answers were deferred to the CFO or to a future call.

Imagine a scenario, everything would have gone in the right direction without this international disturbances had these items come on time, I would have comfortably closed additionally INR20 crores apart from INR76 crores what we have closed.
Only thing is that might get delayed by few months, maybe 6 to 8 months, which might spill over to subsequent financial year. But opportunities are not lost.

financial_highlights.change: Turned positive; prior year not stated

544684|2026-09.headline: Digilogic H1 FY27 revenue rose 91% to INR34.96 crores and PAT rose 151% to INR4.76 crores, with management reiterating 25-30% FY27 top-line growth.
544684|2026-09.overview: H1 FY27 revenue grew 91% to INR34.96 crores from INR18 crores, EBITDA rose 126% to INR7.81 crores, and PAT grew 151% to INR4.76 crores. Management said H2 is seasonally much stronger in defense, citing FY26 revenue of INR78 crores split as H1 INR19 crores and H2 INR59 crores. Order book of INR20 crores is to be billed by mid-February 2027, with a further INR54 crores in pipeline at various tender stages. Management also reiterated 25-30% top-line and 30-35% EBITDA/PAT growth guidance for FY27, though analysts noted that the EBITDA guidance was lowered from 45-50% and that H1 margin gains were partly driven by FD interest income.

financial_highlights.value: INR78 crores (H1 INR19 crores, H2 INR59 crores)

segments.name: Test, measurement and simulation systems (TMS)
segments.commentary: Core business, described as the heart of operations; 36 projects executed in H1 FY27 valued at around INR33.18 crores. Customers include PSUs and DRDO agencies. Management expects TMS to keep growing at 20-30% a year.

segments.name: Abhedya Systems (wholly owned subsidiary, R&D)
segments.commentary: New experts hired for R&D; commercial production expected in H2 FY29 if plans hold. Management did not disclose financials.

segments.name: Project Udaan (new facility, build-to-print and build-to-spec)
segments.commentary: Civil construction is ongoing, with first-floor roof concrete complete; completion targeted by March 2027 and operations by end-2027. Management expects certification around Q1 2028 and commercialisation in about two years, with contribution starting FY28.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line growth guidance of 25-30%, which management said it expects to meet; CFO said the company expects to touch its guidance number.
EBITDA and PAT growth guidance of 30-35%. The CFO said the 40-45% figure in the earlier outlook included FD interest income, and core growth stays at 30-35%.
Management said the current margins are sustainable, with no guidance to expand or contract.
Order book of INR20 crores and pipeline of INR54 crores targeted for billing by mid-February 2027.
Project Udaan: civil construction completion by March 2027, internal testing by December 2027, inspection and certification in Q1 2028, and about three months to get the certificate.
High Precision GIMBAL System and custom single-board computer products expected to be marketable around mid-2027, adding an estimated INR3-4 crores a year initially, with break-even thereafter.
Ongoing internal SOP and technology upgrade expected to finish between December 2026 and March 2027.
capex_capacity: Project Udaan is a new facility whose civil construction is in progress. Management expects operations from end-2027 and certification around Q1 2028.
Abhedya Systems (wholly owned subsidiary) is expected to start commercial production in H2 FY29.
Management said the Udaan facility will cover both build-to-spec (in-house design) and build-to-print (production of designs supplied by clients), with build-to-print expected to contribute first.

544698|2026-03.headline: H2 FY26 total income rose 28% YoY to INR12,656.59 lakh and net profit rose 158% to INR432.20 lakh; FY26 PAT was INR750.29 lakh.
544698|2026-03.overview: PAN HR Solution's first earnings call, held 12 June 2026 after its February 2026 BSE SME listing, covered H2 and full-year FY26 results. Management reported H2 total income of INR12,656.59 lakh (+28% YoY) and H2 net profit of INR432.20 lakh (+158% YoY), against a prior-year H2 that was smaller. Full-year PAT of INR750.29 lakh looked moderate because FY25 included a one-time INR6.5 crore prior-period income. The company ended FY26 with net worth of INR3,751 lakh, cash of INR2,434 lakh and no debt, and set out a plan to reach INR1,000 crore revenue by FY29.

financial_highlights.change: Full-year YoY comparison not stated; FY25 base included INR6.5 crore one-time exceptional prior-period income

segments.name: Manpower outsourcing / workforce deployment
segments.commentary: Deployed workforce grew from about 10,000 at IPO to over 11,000 on payroll as of the call. Clients are concentrated in e-commerce, quick commerce, logistics, warehousing and manufacturing; management cited more than 17 clients.

segments.name: Emerging services (3PL, payroll, compliance, HR outsourcing, white-collar hiring)
segments.commentary: Management said these are new or being scaled: 3PL and B2B models were not previously done, and white-collar one-time staffing has started. No revenue figures were given for these lines.

guidance_outlook: Target to grow FY27 turnover by approximately 40%.
Target revenue of INR1,000 crore by FY29 (within three years), with the 3PL model named as the first growth lever.
Priorities for FY27: deploy IPO proceeds into working capital, move toward pay-and-collect contracts, expand into new geographies and sectors, and grow payroll, compliance and HR services.
Management expects a higher-margin mix over time, but said some contracts carry lower margins while creating operating leverage.
capex_capacity: Workforce deployment rose from about 10,000 at IPO to more than 11,000 on payroll; the company said it now operates in the South and West as well as North and East.
Management said internal infrastructure is underused and that new services can run on existing infrastructure without major new investment.
IPO proceeds are to go mainly to working capital expansion, and acquisitions are under consideration; no specific acquisition target or deal size was named.

Competitive positioning rests on compliance credibility (operating since 2015), balance-sheet strength, and an integrated single-window model covering salary, compliance and workforce management.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors read moderate full-year growth versus strong H2 numbers?

qa_highlights.question: How will the IPO capital be deployed?

qa_highlights.question: What drives the INR1,000 crore FY29 revenue goal?

qa_highlights.question: Will margins come under pressure with growth?

qa_highlights.question: What are the return-ratio expectations (ROE, ROCE)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said return ratios are a priority; temporary dips are possible while capital is deployed for growth. No ROE or ROCE figures were given.

risks_watch: Full-year PAT comparison is distorted by the FY25 one-time INR6.5 crore income; the underlying base needs confirming.
Revenue was hit by contract repricing and billing-cycle changes in FY26; watch whether these persist in FY27.

The 40% FY27 turnover target and INR1,000 crore FY29 goal depend on working-capital deployment, pay-and-collect contracts (which raise working-capital needs) and acquisitions with no named targets yet.
Margin dilution from lower-margin contracts and the new 3PL, white-collar and pay-and-collect mix.
