544699|2026-06.headline: Aye Finance Q1 FY27: AUM up 28% YoY to INR7,324 crores, PAT up 144% to INR75 crores, credit cost eased to 4.01%.
544699|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 disbursements rose 22% YoY to INR1,219 crores, the strongest first quarter on record, and AUM grew 28% YoY to INR7,324 crores. Gross NPA fell 28 bps QoQ to 4.49% and credit cost fell 29 bps QoQ to 4.01%, which management says is already at the top of the 3.5%-4% guidance band. Net total income rose 38% YoY to INR322 crores and NIM improved 20 bps QoQ to 15.9%. Fee income dropped QoQ on lower direct assignment volumes and a one-off FX gain last quarter, and management kept the FY27 guidance unchanged while signalling possible refinement at H1.

segments.name: Hypothecation loans
segments.commentary: Core product, ~24-month tenor, average ticket ~INR1.5 lakh, ~78% of portfolio; portfolio ROI ~27.5%-28%; PAR X ~7.5%, PAR 30 ~6.6%, PAR 90 ~5.35%.

segments.name: Mortgage / Micro LAP
segments.commentary: ~22% of portfolio; portfolio ROI ~23.5%; PAR X ~5%, PAR 30 ~5%, PAR 90 ~3%; LTV ~35%-40%. Management expects only marginal mix increase in FY27, with a longer-term target of ~30%-35%.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guided at 25%-30% for FY27; Q1 AUM growth was 28% YoY.
Credit cost guided at 3.5%-4% for FY27; management says Q1 at top of band and expects improvement, with narrower guidance possible by end of H1. Long term, ~3%-3.5% once mortgage share reaches ~30%.
NIM guided flat at 14.25%-14.75%, with management flagging possible upside given Q1 NIM of 15.9%.
Opex-to-assets guided at 8.25%-8.75%; Q1 at 8.9%, with Q1-Q2 likely above band and Q3-Q4 expected inside it.

Borrowing cost expected to fall a further 10-15 bps after the India Ratings upgrade (IND A to A+, stable; CP to IND A1+). Lower cost on incremental borrowings is 20-25 bps over the year per the earlier statement.
Plan to add ~40-50 branches in FY27 (~10% of branch base, counting large branches). Team to grow ~10%. Medium-term opex target of 7%-7.5% over 3 years.

Medium term: vision of INR24,000 crores AUM within 5 years (~27%-28% CAGR). Product mix target over 3 years: 60%-70% hypothecation, ~30% Micro LAP, ~10% other secured products such as gold loans and solar loans.
Leverage at 3.15x; fresh equity needed at 4x-4.5x, which management says gives 2-2.5 years of growth runway (book to ~INR14,000 crores). Targeted ROA 4.5%-5% post-tax at 3.5%-4% credit cost.
capex_capacity: 571 branches across 18 states and 3 union territories as of June 2026; plan to add ~40-50 branches in FY27, with additions and splits visible between Q2 and Q3.
Branch strategy: ~10% annual growth in large-branch equivalents plus splits of mature branches (~44 splits last year, reported profitable from day one).
Team growth ~10% (13%-15% manpower increase mentioned for new branches), against a base of ~11,000 employees.
AUM per employee up 12% YoY.
demand_pricing: Credit policy tightened: approval share fell from ~55% to ~45% of logged cases, while customer additions still rose 38% YoY.

Management says the micro-enterprise market is under-penetrated (Aye has penetrated ~2%-3% of it); digital fintech and UPI lenders are seen as a limited overlap, with 7%-8% of fresh sourcing from digital channels.
Seasonality: Q1 typically ~20%-22% of annual disbursements; H1 ~40%, H2 ~60%. April was seasonally weak but May-June collection efficiency was ~99.3%.
Non-OD collection efficiency 99.2%; Bucket 1 collection 54.5%. Post-PAR 90 collection ~29%-30%, per management.
Pre-closure rate ~3%-3.5% annualised for hypothecation and ~5%-5.5% blended. Direct assignment target kept at 5%-7% of AUM (about 5% today).

financial_highlights.change: +28% YoY, +4% QoQ from INR7,044 crores in March 2026
-28 bps QoQ from 4.77%; vs 4.6% a year ago
-29 bps QoQ; includes ~INR6 crores management overlay
vs 9.5% at end of FY26; guidance 8.25%-8.75%
DA income ~INR20 crores absent; ~INR12 crores FX gain moved to OCI

qa_highlights.question: Why is the 3.5%-4% credit cost guidance well above peers despite tighter underwriting?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said hypothecation (~24-month tenor, ~INR1.5 lakh ticket) differs from peers' Micro LAP book; terminal losses are ~5.5%-6% for both products, translating to ~3.5% annual credit cost, with ~3% possible in a good year. Q1 is already at the top of the band; guidance could narrow by end-H1.

qa_highlights.question: Fee and other income fell QoQ: what drove it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed ~INR32-33 crores of decline to no direct assignment in Q1 (DA ~INR20 crores last quarter) and ~INR12 crores FX gain last quarter now moved to OCI, plus lower cross-sell on lower disbursements. Cross-sell insurance income was INR9 crores in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Can NIM exceed the upper end of 14.25%-14.75% guidance, and how do yield and cost of funds move?
qa_highlights.answer: Weighted cost of borrowing fell to 10.78% from 10.87%; incremental borrowing cost ~10.20%, ~60 bps lower. Further 10-15 bps drop expected from the India Ratings upgrade. Portfolio yield 22.4% expected to drift slightly lower as mortgage grows, but NIM guidance held flat.

qa_highlights.question: How much management overlay is in the credit cost and on the balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: Around INR6 crores of overlay was created within the Q1 4.01% credit cost; total overlay on balance sheet is INR11 crores, in Stage 2 and Stage 3. Target overlay is about 0.5% of book, used to smooth cross-cycle credit cost within 3.5%-4%.

qa_highlights.question: Medium-term: how achievable is INR24,000 crores AUM in 5 years, and what is the product mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a 2%-3% market penetration and branch-led origination; target mix over 3 years is 60%-70% hypothecation, ~30% Micro LAP and ~10% other secured products such as gold and solar loans. About 55,000 declined customers are seen seeking gold loans, with 20%-plus doing so.

qa_highlights.question: Will PAR X at ~7% be sufficient to deliver the 3.5%-4% credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes: at ~7% PAR X, credit cost of 3.5%-4% and post-tax ROA of 4.5%-5% are achievable. Management also guided sustainable PAR X at about 6%-6.5% and expects Q3-Q4 PAR to moderate from 7.01%.

risks_watch: Opex-to-assets at 8.9% in Q1 is above the 8.25%-8.75% guidance band; management expects Q1-Q2 above band and Q3-Q4 inside it.
PAR X at 7.01% and PAR 90 for mortgage (~3%) vs hypothecation (~5.35%); management has limited deep-bucket collection capacity in mortgage and says improvement depends on it.
Monsoon below normal (IMD ~92% of LPA) with stress possible in central India and southern peninsula; management says large states are not expected to be affected.
Credit cost guidance and NIM guidance may be refined at end-H1; management flagged possible upside on both.
Fee income is lower with no DA in Q1; DA target kept at 5%-7% of AUM, currently about 5%.
Q1 disbursements are seasonal (about 20%-22% of annual); Q2 and Q3 branch additions are back-loaded and the 40-50 branch plan needs to show up in those quarters.
Capital adequacy and leverage: leverage 3.15x, with fresh equity needed at 4x-4.5x (about 2-2.5 years of runway); ROE currently low due to IPO capital.
key_quotes: Quarter 1 has definitely been encouraging where we are already at the top of that band that we are talking of, and as we move into the subsequent quarters, we do feel that this number should improve further.

So, answer to your question is that yes, 7% is good enough. It will deliver to us the credit cost that we're talking of, 3.5% to 4%, and it will deliver the ROA which we are targeting, which is probably 4.5% to 5%.
So, I think right now, 8.9% versus the highest 8.75%, I think we are very much there.
We are targeting an AUM growth, as we had said in the guidance, between 25% to 30% for this year.
544699|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, asset quality and funding, with management stating that Q1 credit cost and opex are already close to guided bands. Cautious on exact guidance: refinement is deferred to end-H1, and management declined to quantify slippage and deeper-bucket recovery.

544699|2026-09.headline: Aye Finance Q2 FY27: PAT more than doubled to INR87 crore (+151% YoY) as credit cost fell to 3.82% and NIM hit 15.6%, above the 14.25-14.75% guidance.
544699|2026-09.overview: AUM rose 26% YoY to INR7,597 crore (+4% QoQ) and Q2 disbursements were INR1,403 crore (+10% YoY, +15% QoQ), with repeat loans down 3% YoY. Credit cost fell for a seventh straight quarter to 3.82%, now inside the 3.5-4% guidance, and GNPA eased to 4.20%. Opex ratio fell to 8.6% from 8.9% QoQ, and management says NIM is running ahead of guidance partly because a rating upgrade to IND A+ was not factored in. Management reiterated FY27 guidance and flagged that the second half, which carries about 60% of disbursements, is where delivery will be tested.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR65 crore in H1 FY26 (+148%)

segments.name: Hypothecation loans (core)
segments.commentary: Management describes itself as the dominant player with no meaningful competition in this segment. Productivity per loan officer reached 4.85 files per month in Q2, against about 4.2 in FY26 and a FY27 budget of about 5.

segments.name: Micro-LAP / mortgage
segments.commentary: Mortgage PAR X rose about 1 percentage point over the last quarter to around 6%, still below hypothecation. Management tightened policy and disbursements are being slowed, mainly in parts of MP and Gujarat. Mortgage foreclosures are rising to about 22-23% of the portfolio.

segments.name: Cattle / dairy
segments.commentary: Cattle book is held at roughly 25-28% of AUM, underwritten with a minimum of four to six high-yielding cattle, and static-pool data is described as marginally better than the market. Management does not plan to grow it aggressively.

segments.name: Gold loans (planned)
segments.commentary: Under evaluation as a pilot, with new branch setups in cities where existing branches sit. Around 20% of micro-enterprise customers already hold gold loans. Management expects to update on the plan later in the year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM growth guidance of 25-30% reiterated; management says it is in the range and 30% is possible but not committed. Three-year vision of 28-33% AUM CAGR and 4-4.5% ROA was shared in July.
FY27 credit cost guided at 3.5-4%, with management expecting to average around 3.5% plus or minus a few bps and exit the year lower.
NIM guidance of 14.25-14.75% maintained for now; management may revisit it in Q3 if the upside persists.
FY27 opex ratio guided at 8.25-8.75%; management expects it to move into range in H2 and to be around 8.5% for FY27.
FY27 ROA guided at 4-4.5%, with ROA expected to move into range as H2 volumes build.

Next year (FY28) levers cited: about 50 bps opex-ratio benefit, 10-25 bps lower credit cost, and about 25 bps lower interest cost, with ROA guidance said to be unaffected by insurance commission changes.
PAR X targeted below 7% by H1 and below 6.5% by year-end. Non-OD collection efficiency expected in the 99.2-99.3% range.
No fresh equity needed for about 2 years at current capital; management sees leverage moving to 4-4.5x, implying ROE in the high teens to low 20s over time.
capex_capacity: Branches held at 571 at the end of H1 FY27. More than 30 new branches are to become operational in Q3 FY27, and about 80 branches (35-40 new plus about 40 splits) are planned for the year.
Existing branch infrastructure is said to support about INR4,000-4,500 crore of additional AUM over the near term.
AUM per branch was INR13.3 crore in Q2 (INR12.8 crore in Q1). AUM per employee was INR0.67 crore vs INR0.57 crore a year ago.
Employee count budgeted to grow 12-15% in FY27. Headcount is expected to rise 5-7% in H2, mostly in Q3, for distribution and collections.
Pilot gold loan branches are planned for this year and are not expected to strain the opex budget.
demand_pricing: Repeat loans fell 3% YoY in Q2 (up 10% QoQ). Management attributes this to festive timing shifting into Q3 and expects a stronger Q3.
Management says it is not using average ticket size to grow the book; growth is coming from productivity.

Drought has been declared in parts of Maharashtra, Karnataka and Madhya Pradesh, which account for about 18% of AUM. Disbursements are being consciously slowed there, with branch-level calls in MP and Gujarat.

Bucket 1 collection efficiency was 52.8%, dipping over the last three to four months (UP included). Management attributes this to pre-festive cash-flow tightness and expects improvement after November.
Non-OD collection efficiency was 99.2%. Bihar, UP and Rajasthan, the largest states, were largely unaffected by the monsoon.
Borrowing rose to about INR1,100 crore in Q1 and about INR1,200 crore in Q2. The bank share of borrowings rose to 35% from 32%, with no tightening seen from banks.
About 8-9% of primary borrowers overlap with MFI loans (about 30-32% at household level), and FOIR includes MFI obligations.

qa_highlights.question: How confident is management of reaching the top end of FY27 AUM growth (30%) given the H2 weighting?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the H2 is about 60% of disbursements and that it is in the 25-30% range. Reaching the higher end is possible, depending on H2 execution, with repeat loans, gold loans and new branches as levers.

qa_highlights.question: Target ROE and dilution risk over the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: ROA of about 4.5% combined with 4-4.5x leverage implies ROE in the high teens to low 20s, built up gradually as debt is added. Management does not expect dilution over the next two financial years, given net worth of about INR2,600 crore plus.

qa_highlights.question: Asset quality and credit cost outlook for H2, and cattle portfolio behaviour in inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Credit cost is expected to fall toward 3.5% with a lower exit rate. Cattle underwriting requires four to six high-yielding cattle and avoids marginal dairy farmers; static-pool data is marginally better than peers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ECL provisions change, and what was the write-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management overlays were added to Stage 2 and Stage 3 this quarter (Stage 2 moved from INR42 crore to INR48 crore). Write-offs rose modestly to about INR95 crore, including about INR45 crore already fully provided, so credit cost was flat.

qa_highlights.question: Fundraising conditions given rising rates and liquidity tightening?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reported no difficulty. Borrowings were about INR1,100 crore in Q1 and about INR1,200 crore in Q2, the bank share rose to 35%, and the incremental cost was 10.04%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the insurance commission impact can be offset?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about 50 bps of opex-ratio benefit, 25 bps of lower interest cost even after a 25 bps rate rise, and 10-25 bps of lower credit cost next year, which together should absorb the impact without repricing. A 50 bps rate hike is estimated at 7 bps ROA impact in FY27 and 15 bps in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why is NIM guidance kept at 14.25-14.75% when Q2 is 15.6%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited expected yield pressure from the growing ML book and slow repeat business, plus higher borrowing costs. It will revisit guidance in Q3 if the upside holds.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company insured against drought or natural catastrophe?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said insuring the full book would not be ROA-accretive given low loss rates. CGFMU cover is used selectively, at about INR200-300 crore of the book. Credit life insurance would not help in a drought.

risks_watch: H2 execution: about 60% of disbursements fall in H2, and management says the top end of the 25-30% AUM growth guidance depends on how H2 plays out. Repeat loans (down 3% YoY in Q2) and new branches (30+ operational in Q3) are the levers.

Asset quality: Bucket 1 collection efficiency fell to 52.8% over the last three to four months, with UP included; management expects improvement after November. Watch whether PAR X falls below 7% by H1 and below 6.5% by year-end.

Drought exposure: Maharashtra, Karnataka and MP (about 18% of AUM) are under drought declarations; disbursements are slowed there and micro-LAP is tightened in parts of MP and Gujarat. Mortgage PAR X rose about 1 percentage point in a quarter to around 6%.

Insurance commission regulation: management says ROA guidance is unchanged even with potential changes, offset by about 50 bps opex-ratio benefit, 25 bps interest cost benefit and 10-25 bps lower credit cost. Actual regulatory outcome is still open.
NIM: Q2 NIM of 15.6% is above the 14.25-14.75% guidance, which is kept for now due to expected yield pressure from the ML book, slow repeat business and rate hikes. Management will revisit in Q3.
Gold loan pilot: planned new branch setups in existing cities; management expects to update later in the year. Watch opex impact and any rollout scale.
Funding: bank share of borrowings rose to 35% from 32%, and incremental cost is 10.04%. Watch for any tightening as rates rise.
key_quotes: So, this solid first half has significantly enhanced our conviction to deliver on our stated FY27 guidance.
Whether we will be in the closer to 30%, I wouldn't like to commit now. But is it possible? Yes, it is definitely on our hindsight.
The primary reason is that our guidance had factored in more aggressive increase in repo rates.
I think our guidance for ROA should stay untouched.
544699|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on headline numbers (NIM, credit cost, PAT) and on FY27 guidance, though the CEO declined to commit to the top end of AUM growth and deferred the NIM guidance revision to Q3. Management was more cautious on the near-term collection trend, attributing the Bucket 1 dip to pre-festive cash-flow tightness rather than a structural cause.

544700|2026-06.headline: Fractal Q1 FY27 revenue rose 20% YoY to INR 912.5 crore (9% constant currency), with TMT down 22% weighing on growth.

Growth came mainly from EPC (revenue up 129% to INR1,391 million), while manufacturing revenue fell slightly to INR3,824 million from INR3,932 million. Finance cost of INR362 million absorbed about 55% of EBITDA, and PAT was INR211 million. Management said the IPO-funded debt repayment of about INR4,900 million, completed in Q2 FY27, will lower finance cost from later quarters; the company did not give numerical guidance for FY27.

financial_highlights.change: up from INR296 million YoY; about 55% of EBITDA
manufacturing INR14,327 million; EPC INR13,557 million

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: Revenue INR3,824 million (vs INR3,932 million YoY), EBITDA about INR388 million, implying roughly 10% margin. Management described manufacturing profitability as broadly stable; cable-to-conductor split is about 90:10.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,391 million (+129% YoY) and EBITDA INR276 million (vs INR93 million), a margin of about 20%. Management said quarterly EPC margins can vary and guided to a typical range of 15-20%.

guidance_outlook: No specific FY27 guidance given; management pointed to a long-run revenue growth of about 15-16% (5-year CAGR) and said EBITDA margins should stay stable.
Debt repayment of about INR4,900 million from IPO proceeds was completed in Q2 FY27; gross debt is about INR3,600 million and fixed deposits about INR2,400 million, leaving net debt negligible.
Annualised interest saving of roughly INR40 crore at PBT level, based on about 9% cost of debt on INR490 crore repaid.
Deferred tax benefit from FY23 carry-forward losses (about INR125-130 crore in total) to be used up in FY27; cash taxes resume from FY28.
Working capital days typically 100-120; management expects the INR8,000 million of projects started in Q4 FY26 to work through over coming quarters.
capex_capacity: Three manufacturing units with aggregate installed capacity of about 85,000 metric tons (up from about 62,000 metric tons three years earlier, per an analyst question).
Current capacity utilisation at about 62% per management's answer to an analyst's question on overall utilisation; cable utilisation was described as roughly 80% in an analyst question.
Management's strategy is to add capacity once utilisation reaches about 75-80%; the 85,000 MT figure is an optimised rating, with 90-95% achievable.
Capex will be phased and tied to customer demand; the company holds land within its factory footprint for future expansion.
Built extra capacity for AECC/HTLS products ahead of orders; utilisation may stay low initially before settling.
demand_pricing: India's conductor market reportedly grew from about 102 billion (FY20) to about 185 billion (FY25), with 230-250 billion expected by FY30 (CRISIL, as cited by management).

Utilities floated tenders worth about INR3,500 crore for HTLS conductors and re-conductoring in the last year; Laser has bid for about INR1,250 crore. Bids are under evaluation and no HTLS revenue has been booked yet.
High-voltage cables rose from 9% to about 29% of total revenue over the last nine quarters, per management.
Management estimated EBITDA margin difference of about 2-3 points between normal and HT cables; conventional conductors are the lowest-margin product.
EPC revenue is 100% from government and utility customers; manufacturing is about 50:50 government and private.

qa_highlights.question: Expected margin expansion over 12-18 months from new conductor products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects margins to remain stable, with revenue growing at around 15-16% as in the past five years; HTLS revenue should improve margins once prices open, but no timeline was given beyond 'next few quarters'.

qa_highlights.question: Interest saving after IPO debt repayment?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR40 crore a year at PBT level, based on a roughly 9% cost of capital and INR490 crore repaid.

qa_highlights.question: Are Laser the only bidders for the TS-technology re-conductoring tenders?
qa_highlights.answer: Not necessarily; tenders are technology-neutral, and some have few bidders and others many. Management said Laser's technology tie-up from March 2025 gave it the headroom to bid.

qa_highlights.question: Why has production stayed flat while capacity rose from 62,000 to 85,400 MT?
qa_highlights.answer: The mix has shifted to specialised, higher-value products that are lower in volume but add to revenue and profit.

qa_highlights.question: Tax: what is the deferred tax position?
qa_highlights.answer: Carry-forward losses from an FY23 acquisition give a tax saving of about INR125-130 crore, booked as deferred tax; cash taxes start after FY27, and P&L tax expense is already stated after tax.

risks_watch: Finance cost (INR362 million, 55% of EBITDA in Q1) must fall after the debt repayment for PAT to convert better; the Q1 figure does not yet include the benefit.
Working capital build: about INR90 crore of FG and WIP inventory rise in June 2026, and a near-zero operating cash flow in Q1.
Outcome of about INR1,250 crore of HTLS/re-conductoring tenders, which are the main driver of the new product thesis.
Manufacturing revenue declined YoY, and production volumes were roughly flat over three years despite higher capacity.
Reliance on government/utility customers; EPC revenue is entirely government-sourced.
Reporting is standalone; one SPV subsidiary has nil revenue. An analyst pointed out that a prior-year one-time gain of about INR32 crore distorts the PAT comparison.
544822|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on long-term demand and the HTLS opportunity, but cautious on near-term numbers: management repeatedly declined to give FY27 guidance and attributed quarterly swings to project timing. Several answers were vague on specifics such as the HTLS revenue timeline, the peak cable revenue, and the tender outcomes.
key_quotes: Our order book stood at approximately INR27,884 million as of June '26.
We are not actually trying to provide any specific guidance on how the FY27 will look like.
And as we grow, now our mix and everything are more or less optimized, as we grow, you will see that growth in coming time.
So, the comparable number would be around INR120 crores. From there we have to compare things.

544824|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue grew 6% YoY to a 60% sequential rise; closing order book reached ₹626 crores, up 57% YoY, with EBITDA margin at 36.1%.
544824|2026-09.overview: Management framed Q2 FY27 as resilient: revenue grew 6% YoY and rose sharply QoQ, while H1 FY27 revenue grew 18% YoY, driven by aftermarket and defence. Product revenue was lower YoY on customer delivery timing and supply chain factors. EBITDA margin was 36.1% in Q2 and 35.7% in H1, down YoY on mix and people costs but up sequentially. Order inflows were strong (H1 ₹330 crores, up 95% YoY), and capex is largely complete, with growth to be funded mainly from internal accruals.

financial_highlights.value: Q2 up ~41% YoY; H1 up 29% YoY; 27% of revenue in H1

financial_highlights.metric: Free cash flow after capex (H1 FY27)

financial_highlights.value: ₹36 crores in Q2 FY27 vs ₹12 crores in Q1 FY27

segments.name: Industrial Gears (product)
segments.commentary: Product revenue was lower YoY on delivery timing and supply chain factors; management says gearbox orders deliver in a 6-8 month cycle. Of the ₹626 crores order book, ₹156 crores is for FY27 from Gears.

segments.name: Aftermarket
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue up ~41% YoY and H1 up 29%, contributing 27% of H1 revenue. Management is building export aftermarket via hiring and agent partnerships; aftermarket orders deliver in 3-6 months.

segments.name: Defence and Marine
segments.commentary: Defence revenue scaled meaningfully from a low base (analyst cited 3.3x YoY in Q2 and 4.7x in H1; company did not give absolute figures). Of the ₹626 crores order book, ₹81 crores is for FY27 from Defence; defence orders are lumpy with 12-month or longer cycles.

guidance_outlook: No revenue or margin guidance given; management declined to give FY27 or FY28 forecasts.
Medium-term ambition: growth above 25% YoY (CAGR) over the next five to seven years.
Management expects EBITDA margin to stay at 35% or above over the medium to long term and does not expect defence/aftermarket mix shift to be margin dilutive.
Some H2 book-and-bill is needed to meet internal targets; management says it is secured. Orders pushed from Q2 to Q3 FY27; Q3 and Q4 outlook described as 'extremely encouraging'.
Further capex expected to be balancing, routine and small capacity enhancements, not substantial; next capex trigger at about 80-85% capacity utilisation.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 capex ₹41 crores; the ₹340 crores capex programme (split evenly between gears and defence) is almost fully complete.
Combined capex is said to support production of about ₹700 crores based on gearbox mix, plus defence capability revenue (defence figure not disclosed).
Next capacity trigger is 80-85% utilisation; management declined to say when that would be reached.
New defence facility inaugurated; management expects production there to support defence growth over coming quarters.
Data-centre and space gearbox product expected to be ready for launch in the current quarter.
demand_pricing: Middle East and African orders were significant in Q2; delayed STG pump and Middle East orders expected to finalise, timing shifting quarter to quarter. Management cited ADNOC pump and compressor orders via OEMs.
Global high-speed industrial gearbox market (OEM plus aftermarket) about $1.1 billion in 2026, growing 6-7% through 2033; 7-9 global competitors ex-China, largest with about 15% share.

Competition: a global competitor in South India has been present for a few years; management says TPTL's market share is unchanged. Indian compressor gear market is small; compressor competition is mainly in Europe.
Domestic compressor and gearbox demand tied to oil and gas capex; management said oil at $120 is an opportunity, and TPTL is qualified with ADNOC.
Defence procurement: FY27 Ministry of Defence allocation ₹7.85 lakh crore; defence capital outlay ₹2.19 lakh crore (21.8% above FY26 BE); ₹1.39 lakh crore earmarked for domestic industry procurement.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the ₹626 crore order book is scheduled for H2 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not split by quarter. It said ₹156 crores of the book is for FY27 from Gears and ₹81 crores from Defence.

qa_highlights.question: Is the EBITDA margin decline from ~45% to ~36% finished, given people costs?
qa_highlights.answer: A few more small hires are planned. Management asked analysts to judge margins on a rolling four-quarter or full-year basis, with a preference for full year.

qa_highlights.question: Defence revenue in absolute terms and FY28 expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not disclose defence segment revenue; it said segment reporting may be considered in the future.

qa_highlights.question: Medium-term growth outlook and book-and-bill for H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no FY27 numbers; medium-term ambition is above 25% CAGR over five to seven years. Some H2 book-and-bill is needed and management says it is secured.

qa_highlights.question: Export order book and outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Export product orders rose to ₹36 crores in Q2 from ₹12 crores in Q1. Management expects significant expansion over coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will utilisation reach full capacity by FY29-FY30, and when is the next capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a timeline; next capex phase triggered at about 80-85% utilisation, which has not yet been reached.

risks_watch: Revenue lumpiness: product timing and defence procurement cycles can move revenue quarter to quarter; order conversion in H2 needs book-and-bill.
Middle East order timing is delayed by regional turbulence; management says orders are delayed, not cancelled.
Working capital remains high at 188 core days; receivables and inventory build may move with project milestones.
Margin: YoY EBITDA margin declined to 36.1% from about 45%, with people costs and mix as stated drivers.
Next quarter: order conversion into revenue, export order momentum, defence order wins, and data-centre product launch.
544824|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on order book, exports and defence long term, but cautious on near-term timing; management repeatedly declined forward numbers on revenue, utilisation, defence revenue and Middle East timing. Candid about Q2 product softness and the margin decline.
key_quotes: Q2 FY27 revenue grew by 6% YoY and improved significantly sequentially.
The closing order position on the 30th of September 2026 was ₹626 crores, up 57% from ₹398 crores a year earlier.
Our growth ambition is certainly to deliver growth over a medium -term basis, let me say five - seven years basis of over 25% year-on-year.
In the medium to long -term, I do not expect it to be margin dilutive at all.

544829|2026-06.headline: SBI Funds Q1 FY27 operating revenue rose 15% YoY to ₹1,149 crore and PAT reached ₹873 crore, up 37% QoQ.
544829|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the first earnings call after the company's IPO listing. Mutual fund QAAUM reached ₹12.6 trillion (up 11% YoY) with a 15.1% overall market share, while operating revenue of ₹1,149 crore and operating profit of ₹907 crore grew 15% and 17% YoY. Management attributed margin gains mainly to asset-mix shift from passive funds toward equity, hybrid, arbitrage and gold/silver ETFs, and said the TER cut was passed on to distributors with a net neutral-to-positive effect. Management declined to give guidance, citing the silent period.

segments.name: Mutual fund (core)
segments.commentary: Accounts for about 90-92% of operating revenue. Equity yield stated at 62 bps; gold and silver ETFs earn about 44-45 bps spread; arbitrage fund yield about 30 bps versus about 11 bps for liquid funds.

segments.name: Alternates (PMS, advisory, international, AIF)
segments.commentary: Together about 8% of operating revenue. Management said AIF and PMS are more attractive than equity on margin, and the company plans one more AIF product this quarter.

segments.name: Passive
segments.commentary: Passive QAAUM ₹4 trillion, up 12% YoY; management said low-yield passive concentration has declined, adding about 2 bps to overall margin.

guidance_outlook: No quantitative guidance given; management cited the silent period for QAAUM, opex and ESOP details.
Second SIF strategy (Ex-Top 100 long-short) to launch this quarter; SBI Balanced Hybrid Fund being launched; SBI Nifty Midcap 150 Momentum 50 ETF FOF NFO underway.
Management expects SBI channel share of SIP flows to remain about one-third, with the aim of holding a 35:65 split versus other and direct channels.
Opex to focus on technology, AI and human resources; training costs expected to rise in Q2-Q3 FY27.
Management reiterated a new public dividend policy has been published; payout subject to board and AGM approval.
capex_capacity: Management said 94% of investor transactions are processed digitally on a hybrid cloud infrastructure.
About 50,000 distributors now use the partner app and portal for analytics and reporting.
In-house research platform Neo is being enhanced with AI capabilities.
Distribution footprint: over 23,000 SBI branches, over 124,000 independent financial advisors, nearly 10,000 national distributors, over 90 banking partners; coverage of 98%+ pin codes.
Alternate business hiring underway; one more AIF product to be launched this quarter.
demand_pricing: Industry QAAUM grew about 15% YoY and was broadly stable QoQ; industry monthly SIP inflows above ₹31,000 crore.
Fresh SIPs added in the quarter were 1.7 million (about 16 lakh); live SIPs reached 16 million.

B30 locations: management cited 19% MAAUM market share and more than 25% B30 market share; about 65% of SIP count and 44% of SIP amount from B30; about ₹2,500 crore of the ₹4,000 crore monthly SIP flow.
Flow market share is in line with AUM market share; equity and hybrid market share around 11-12%.
TER reduction under the new regulation was passed to distributors from April, with management calling the net effect neutral to slightly positive.

qa_highlights.question: Share of operating revenue from mutual funds versus alternates?
qa_highlights.answer: Mutual funds contribute about 90-92% of operating revenue; PMS, advisory and international make up about 8%.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the operating margin improvement; is it TER pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said TER pass-through was neutral and not the driver. Margin gains came from asset mix: lower passive share replaced by equity and hybrid, adding about 2 bps to overall yield.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SIP flows slip slightly from March to June?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the flattish trend to market volatility and geopolitical conditions; monthly SIP flow of about ₹4,000 crore was maintained.

qa_highlights.question: What is the SBI channel share of equity AUM and SIP flows?
qa_highlights.answer: SBI contributes about 35% of active equity AUM and about 20% of overall AUM. SBI channel share of SIP flow is about one-third (₹1,300 crore of ₹4,000 crore); management aims to keep this split.

qa_highlights.question: Is the employee cost decline of 1% YoY sustainable; when do salary increments come in?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the decline reflects the new labour code implementation; training costs will rise in Q2 and Q3, and employee benefits are unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Are AIF and PMS more margin-accretive than equity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said alternates are more selective and more attractive than equity on margin, with easier regulation.

risks_watch: Regulatory TER and base expense ratio changes, and removal of exit loads, could compress net margins if distributor pass-through rises.
SIP flow growth was flat QoQ; monitor whether SIP inflows regain momentum versus industry flows.
Debt AUM saw institutional redemptions and tight liquidity; a debt slowdown could hurt yield mix.
Alternates (AIF ₹6,800 crore, PMS) remain small and early-stage; execution on new launches is an open question.
Other income was lower YoY due to mark-to-market losses on the company's own portfolio; this may recur with market volatility.
Dividend payout is subject to board and AGM approval; no amount was specified.

Overall, you can say, it is more attractive than equity.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee and other expenses rise sharply QoQ and YoY, and what is the full-year outlook?

qa_highlights.question: Is the slight yield dip QoQ due to telescopic structure or something else; any distribution-mix change?

qa_highlights.question: How is investor sentiment tracking, and any divergence between assisted and fintech channels?

qa_highlights.question: What is the AIF strategy and capital commitment?

qa_highlights.question: Is there any SBI-channel versus other-channel flow split?

qa_highlights.question: What is the emerging EBITDA margin trajectory, and when could emerging reach break-even?
qa_highlights.answer: No timeframe was given. Management said MarTech is higher margin and growing fast from a small base, and that growth is the main lever for margin improvement.

qa_highlights.question: Why did core CAC rise to about INR3,600 from INR3,100 a year ago?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CAC fluctuates with experiments across channels and reactivation, has held steady for years, and is not seasonal. It said the focus is break-even, with CAC of about INR3,000 recovering margin quickly.

qa_highlights.question: Are 3PLs moving into D2C and SMB, and does that threaten Shiprocket?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its model is to integrate with leading 3PLs and that the D2C segment, which makes up most of INR32,000 crore GMV, is its focus. It said data and integrated stack are its advantage.

qa_highlights.question: Why did power ARPU rise about 25% while power merchant count fell slightly?
qa_highlights.answer: Top merchants are growing faster, and the company is expanding the merchant funnel to convert more merchants into power merchants over time. Management said near-term results depend on macro conditions.

qa_highlights.question: Is there seasonality in the business?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Q3 is typically weakest, because merchants shift marketing spend to marketplaces during the festive season. No other seasonality was cited.

qa_highlights.question: Why has realization per shipment fallen (from about INR96 in FY24 to about INR72 now, per analyst's calculation)?
qa_highlights.answer: The 216 million figure is total unique transactions, not core shipments. Management said the decline reflects the mix shift toward emerging (30% of revenue) and a rise in transactions, while margins as a percentage improved. Core shipment count was not disclosed.

544911|2026-06.headline: Kanohar Q1 FY27 revenue rose 103.5% YoY to INR137.1 crore, with EBITDA margin of 28.3% and order book of about INR2,026 crore.

544912|2026-06.headline: Prasol Q1 FY27 revenue rose 35.7% YoY to INR433.6 crores and EBITDA to INR90.3 crores, helped by one-off inventory gains of about INR25 crores.

FY27 guidance of INR1,550-1,650 crores revenue and INR240-250 crores adjusted EBITDA excludes these gains, and management described a 15-16% year-end EBITDA margin. A Phase 1 capex of INR250-300 crores for existing products (about 60,000 tpa of added capacity) was outlined.

segments.commentary: 27% of Q1 FY27 revenue, stated as stable or growing despite West Asia disruption to Dubai and Africa shipments.

544913|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 36% YoY to Rs.107 crore and EBITDA rose 9% to Rs.23 crore, with margin at 21.3% and a Rs.982 crore order book.
544913|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was Rs.107 crore, up 36% YoY, led by domestic facade (Rs.62 crore, +93%) and fenestration (Rs.6 crore, +127%), while international fell 12% to Rs.39 crore on delivery timing. EBITDA grew 9% to Rs.23 crore, and margin fell to 21.3% because of lower international contribution and a shift to DDP freight billing at cost. Management attributed about 1.5 points of the margin gap to freight pass-through and said the underlying margin is in line with FY26. PAT of Rs.17 crore grew more slowly than EBITDA due to lower other income (prior-year property sale gain) and higher depreciation from new capacity. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of about 25% revenue growth, 23-25% EBITDA margin and 18-20% PAT margin, while flagging a weak first half and a heavier Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why has margin risen above pre-COVID levels on lower revenue?

544914|2026-06.headline: Steamhouse Q1 FY27 PAT rose 80.25% YoY to INR18.34 crore on 16.7% steam volume growth; EBITDA margin 24.05%.

qa_highlights.question: Is there seasonality in the business across quarters, and what explains the Q1 volume jump over Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no real consumption seasonality, but monsoon is challenging (wet fuel, flooded industrial clusters). Q1 volume growth was attributed to chemical and pharma demand recovering and repeat customers.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the 345 TPH capacity is contracted, and can customers terminate contracts early?
qa_highlights.answer: About 70% of the 345 TPH installed capacity is tied up under contracts. Tenure ranges 1 to 10 years with non-exit clauses, and management said customers rarely move to captive boilers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the value proposition to win customers from competitors or in-house boilers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is generally no competitor in most geographies. Claimed cost saving versus captive furnace oil, LDO or natural gas is 25% to 35%, while coal-fired large textile users may be only at par.

qa_highlights.question: What capex is needed to reach 705 TPH and when will projects go live?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR60 crore more for the four under-construction projects, targeted to go live in FY27. Another INR170 crore over 15-18 months for IPO-funded and Tarapur projects; Tarapur 60 TPH by Q4 FY28, Dahej/Ankleshwar/Panoli by Q1 FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Is utilisation of 41% consistent with the planned ramp, and where does the company target it?

qa_highlights.question: What are receivable days and CFO to EBITDA ratio, and what are the related-party steam purchases from Sanjoo Dyeing?
qa_highlights.answer: Fortnightly billing with payments typically 7th to 15th day. Operating cash flow was about 1.2 times EBITDA last time, expected to hold or be slightly lower. Steam purchases from Sanjoo Dyeing for the Sachin location continue for at least the next few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin is expected on the Una project and what is the revenue-share structure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about 8%-10% clear margin per ton, passed through to end consumers, with no capex. The 9% revenue share to Himachal Pradesh Bulk Drug Park Infrastructure Ltd is to be recovered from steam customers. Agreement not yet signed.

qa_highlights.question: What is a sustainable volume growth rate and can company-level 20%-25% volume growth be achieved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 5%-10% growth at existing locations, with new capacity adding further. CFO said 20%-25% company-level volume growth is achievable 'very comfortably'.

qa_highlights.question: Is INR1,000 EBITDA per ton sustainable, and what about Q2 seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: EBITDA per ton of about INR1,000 is expected to hold for the next few quarters, with Q2 an exception due to monsoon. Structural changes cited: coal purchases moved from credit to cash, solar power installed, inventory optimisation. Full-year to be at par or better than Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Why is there government interest in community boilers and are more such opportunities in the pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management linked it to Bulk Drug Park and PM MITRA Park schemes from 2021-22 and a March 2024 CPCB guideline pushing SMEs to common boilers. Gujarat Bulk Drug Park tender is live; PM MITRA and Textile Ministry discussions are ongoing.

qa_highlights.question: Why did steam revenue rise 46% when volume rose 17%?
qa_highlights.answer: Realisation improved from better utilisation and asset leverage, plus higher waste-to-energy usage at Vapi. Growth also came from chemical and pharma recovery and new tyre and food processing (Haldia) customers.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital guidance and cash purchases?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital cycle guided at 35-40 days positive. Coal was bought on credit until May 2026 and has since moved entirely to cash purchases, which management said lowers fuel cost.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue split between own-generated and traded steam, and margin split by business?
qa_highlights.answer: Own-boiler steam was 73.7% of Q1 revenue and traded steam 22.2%. Management declined to split margins between generation and trading, citing competitive sensitivity.

qa_highlights.question: Is the EBITDA CAGR guidance of 30%-35% going to be beaten?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will try to maintain the Q1 growth momentum for the full year on both EBITDA and revenue, but said 'We are not saying that we will maintain'.

risks_watch: Utilisation is still 41.40% versus a 60%-65% target; newer boilers ramp only to about 50% in initial months, so margin expansion depends on execution.
Gross debt rose to INR359.48 crore from INR281.62 crore; IPO proceeds are expected to reduce high-cost debt, but the timing and extent of finance-cost moderation need tracking.
Q2 seasonality from monsoon (wet fuel, flooded clusters) is expected to dent EBITDA per ton below INR1,000; watch Q2 FY27 print.
Coal trading exit and undisclosed split of margins between own generation and traded steam (22.2% of revenue) limit visibility into core-segment profitability.
Four under-construction projects (Jhagadia, Vapi, Nandesari, AMC Pirana) must go live in FY27; about INR60 crore capex remains plus INR170 crore for IPO and Tarapur projects.
Una EPC (INR311 crore, 300 TPH) is not yet signed; the 8%-10% per-ton margin is unconfirmed and depends on fuel price pass-through.
Related-party steam purchases from Sanjoo Dyeing & Printing continue for at least a few quarters; watch the size and terms.
Nitrogen business is small (350 Nm3/hr PSA) and ASU/LIN/LOX plans are under evaluation with no firm capex or partner decision.

544917|2026-06.headline: Karamtara Q1 FY27 revenue rose 72% YoY to INR1,581 crore, EBITDA INR174 crore (~11% margin), PAT INR87 crore; FY27 growth target 60-65%.

Management said the quarter was hit by elevated freight and tariff-related costs, which it expects to ease, and reiterated FY27 revenue growth of 60-65%. Management gave no FY28 numbers and no explicit margin guidance.

544921|2026-06.headline: Arcil Q1 FY27 standalone PAT rose 107% to INR143 crores on INR1,066 crores recoveries (up 151%), with acquisitions seasonally light at INR353 crores.

AUM was INR19,574 crores (up 16% YoY) and borrowings fell sequentially to INR1,100 crores, with management expecting to draw down more in the coming quarters. qa_highlights.answer: No AUM target was given; AUM is expected to rise with acquisitions balanced by equal resolutions, roughly 20-25% of opening AUM resolved each year. Mix reflects asset availability, with no target balance.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is fee income, given fee income is about 2.4% of AUM annualised versus 1.4% a year ago?
qa_highlights.answer: Management fee nearly doubled YoY and is about 45-50% of total fees. Fee income also depends on collections and resolution, not AUM alone. Management said the momentum should be maintained, and fees are earned only on recoveries, with the legacy book carrying no fee.

qa_highlights.question: What are the IRR and vintage profile of the book, and how is the 15% minimum SR investment used?

Responses on the write-back line and the borrowing plan were direct, while the answer on consumer stress was deferred as too early to comment.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gold loan blended yield?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated a blended 11% to 12%, with agri PSL benefits possibly pushing it to 11.25%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the bank pushing a higher fixed-rate book if costs are rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said fixed-rate loans at 11% to 15% insulate yields if rates fall later, and 20 to 30 bp of cost increase is manageable.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors think about full-year NIM given the Q2 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 NIM should be 4%+ but full-year guidance of 3.7% to 3.8% is not changed and will be reviewed at end-September. Downside is limited, though a fall to 3.6% to 3.5% would be a concern.

qa_highlights.question: How will the normalisation of write-off recoveries affect ROA over the next 2 to 3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said lower write-offs could cut ROA by about 25 bp, not 40-45 bp. Offsets: non-fund income (TPP and guarantees), and 10-15 bp from CASA cost and 10 bp from other income.

risks_watch: Write-off recoveries are lumpy and fell to INR103 crore; full-year target of INR500 to 600 crore is at risk if recoveries stay subdued.
Competition and retention pressure: yield on advances expected to fall 10 bp next quarter, and cost of deposits to rise 5 to 10 bp.
Credit cost and ECL transition: management said the ECL impact is premature to quantify; a normalised credit cost will be indicated in about 10 to 11 months.
SMA-30 rose from 0.17% to 0.22%; slippage ratio is guided below 1%. Textile (about 5% of book), ceramics, logistics and the El Nino/monsoon delay are the main sector watch items.
Gold price declines and El Nino could affect agri gold loans (92% of agri book); management said LTV is 63.7% for agri and 56.83% for non-agri.
key_quotes: I am pleased to report that we could successfully navigate the quarter and maintain our net interest margin at 4.26 .

So that way, if we are going to move to 3.6% and 3.5%, that's a cause of concern. But we are not on the trajectory, and we are trying our level best to manage the portfolio, product mix, all these things and all.
it will be premature at this stage to indicate any normalized credit cost under the new region.
YTD growth, this first quarter growth should not be considered as an indicator for the full year growth at the same tempo.

590003|2026-09.headline: KVB Q2 FY27: net profit INR788 crores (+37% YoY), NIM held at 4.26%, credit cost 0.43%, and advances growth guided to 18-20% for FY27.
590003|2026-09.overview: Karur Vysya Bank reported a strong Q2 FY27 with net profit of INR788 crores, up 4% QoQ and 37% YoY, and operating profit of INR1,162 crores (+14% YoY, +6% QoQ). Total business reached INR2,39,712 crores (+5% QoQ, +18% YoY), with advances up 7% QoQ to INR1,11,589 crores and deposits up 5% QoQ to INR1,28,123 crores. Management guided to 18-20% credit growth, NIM of 4% plus, ROA of about 2% and GNPA below 1.5% for FY27, while flagging that funding costs and loan-yield competition may pressure margins in coming quarters. Management also said the write-off recovery contribution has fallen sharply, and that the bank will rely more on core earnings.

financial_highlights.change: +INR1 crore QoQ; AS-15 provisions lower by INR28 crores

financial_highlights.value: 0.43% annualised (INR94 crores NPA/standard/restructured + INR25 crores floating provision)

segments.name: Retail advances
segments.commentary: Grew 5% QoQ led by mortgages (+12% QoQ) and personal loans (+11% QoQ); retail jewel loans fell 1% to a total jewel book of INR32,153 crores (29% of advances), with LTV of 67% for agri gold and 59% for non-agri gold.

segments.commentary: Portfolio grew 12% QoQ (14% of advances), with average ticket size of INR42 crores; credit substitutes grew about INR500 crores in the quarter.

segments.name: Commercial business (SBG and BBG)
segments.commentary: Grew 8% QoQ, with disbursements up about 24% QoQ; tailor-made products (GST surrogate, open term loan) crossed INR450 crores outstanding.

segments.name: Deposits and CASA
segments.commentary: Deposits up 5% QoQ; CASA rose INR1,489 crores in Q2 (current accounts +INR592 crores, savings +INR897 crores); retail term deposits 73% of total deposits, growing 6% QoQ (+INR3,902 crores).

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agri loans grew 4% QoQ; agri jewel loans are 92% of the agri book.

guidance_outlook: Advances growth guided at 18-20% for FY27 (YTD 13%); management cautioned that YTD growth is not an indicator for full-year growth.
NIM for FY27 guided at 4% plus; management said it expects to cross 4% for the next 2 quarters but would not commit to 4.26% being retained.
ROA for FY27 guided at about 2%, with 2.1% reported for Q2.
GNPA guided below 1.5%, NNPA below 1%, slippages below 1%; cost-to-income expected below 45% over the next 2 quarters.
Branch expansion: 50 branches planned for FY27, with 26 to be opened by end-December 2026 and the balance by year-end.
Liquidity coverage ratio to be maintained in the 115-120% range versus 129% reported.
capex_capacity: 20 branches opened in H1 FY27 (including 2 in Q1); 50 planned for FY27.
Branch expansion focus: South India first, then Maharashtra and Gujarat, then Central and North, and East last.
Working capital utilisation steady at 76-79% over 1-1.5 years; US-export textile borrowers at about 55-56% utilisation.

demand_pricing: Credit demand in corporate and institutional segment came from EPC, infrastructure, commercial real estate, capital market participants and selective textile and NBFC capex.

Vehicle loans trending down as a tactical choice: higher delinquency, 150% risk weight, and funding tightness; funds redirected to gold and mortgages.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any stress in gold loans given rising gold loan NPAs seen in bureau data for some peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has not seen stress on the ground. It tightened margin-call monitoring over the last 1.5 years via a digitised system with a centralised cell, and says auctions are few because customers bring family ornaments and top up or repay. Retail gold is priced at about 14%, agri gold at 10.75%.

qa_highlights.question: How much bancassurance income is at risk from the proposed IRDA commission changes, and how will it be recouped?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated commissions could fall 60-70% in some cases. It said LI penetration of about 1.6% would need to rise to 3.8-3.9% to make up the lost income, implying roughly 50% recoupment needed, and it is reworking product mix and penetration, which ranges from 0.9% to 2.2-2.3% across geographies.

qa_highlights.question: How resilient are non-core income sources (treasury and write-off recoveries) to ROA?
qa_highlights.answer: Treasury contributed 0.06% of the Dupont in both Q1 and Q2. Write-off recovery fell to 0.21% of Dupont from 0.65-0.9% earlier. Management said ROA would still be around 2% if recoveries fall another 10 bps, and that the bank has a pool of about INR2,500 crores of assets to recover from.

qa_highlights.question: What is the total stock of floating and contingency provisions, and what is the split?
qa_highlights.answer: Total provisions are 1.65% of advances including standard and floating; excluding them it is about 1.0-1.04%. Floating provision is INR100 crores (ECL-related, two years ago) plus INR25 crores added this quarter, on top of standard and restructured provisions. Restructured-book provision cover is 40.1%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the corporate and SME demand driven by working capital drawdown or capex, and what is the textile utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said working capital utilisation is steady at 76-79% over 1-1.5 years. US-export textile borrowers are at 55-56% utilisation, and capex demand is limited. Textile is about 5% of advances, split 40% upstream, 22% midstream and 38% downstream. Growth comes from takeovers and fresh acquisitions.

qa_highlights.question: Why did RWA rise and what is driving the vehicle loan decline?
qa_highlights.answer: RWA density moved to 58% from a 65% target, driven by selective NBFC exposure (150% risk weight if the bank is not in the rating), corporate growth, consumer credit (125% risk weight), and unhedged FX provisions. Vehicle loans are declining as a tactical call due to fixed rates, dealer commissions, high delinquency, 150% risk weight and deposit tightness; funds moved to gold and mortgages.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins trend down from 4.26%, and what is the repricing outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not commit to retaining 4.26%. It expects 4%+ for the next 2 quarters, citing gold loan repricing from MCLR to fixed now complete, corporate yields of 9%+, and possible 3-6 month pricing pressure. EBLR book is about 56-57%, with working capital repricing 25 bps immediately.

risks_watch: Funding cost pressure: management expects deposit rates to stay up for 2-3 months; cost of deposits rose 4 bps QoQ, and a 25 bps repo hike was announced.

NIM sustainability: management would not commit to retaining 4.26% and expects pricing pressure from banks flush with FCNR liquidity over the next 3-6 months, with some accounts possibly repriced lower.
Mortgage and gold loan competition: mortgage poaching at lower rates, and some account losses as the bank declined to match; LTV and margin-call monitoring on gold loans.
Non-core income dependence: write-off recoveries fell to 0.21% of Dupont from 0.65-0.9%, and treasury contributed 0.06%; ROA guidance depends on core earnings.

Regulatory: pending IRDA bancassurance commission changes could cut income 60-70% in some cases; ECL transition timing still being assessed (about 1-1.5 months more clarity), with a 1.65% provision cover.
Leadership: CEO succession search committee formed; the current MD's tenure is under two years.

So 4.26% retention that I cannot say anything on that. So -- but 4% and above, I can assure.

590013|2026-03.headline: Xpro Q4 FY26 revenue fell to INR134.37 crore (vs INR158.2 crore) while PBT rose to INR16 crore; FY26 PBT fell to INR41 crore on forex loss and pre-operating costs.
590013|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR134.37 crore against INR158.2 crore a year earlier, while quarterly PBT rose to INR16 crore from INR11.5 crore. Full-year net revenue fell 5.6% to INR505.5 crore and production fell 5% to 31,335 MT, driven by lower Coex (refrigerator sheet and liner) volumes. Full-year PBT fell to INR41 crore from INR58 crore, hit by competitive pricing, input cost volatility, a forex loss of INR11 crore (INR11.14 crore unrealised) and pre-operating costs. The new Barjora dielectric film line entered commercial production on 27 March 2026, and management said polymer prices are rising steeply after the West Asia crisis.

qa_highlights.question: Mix between Coex and Biax, and whether there was an inventory gain in Biax in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Mix moved to 71% Biax and 29% Coex from 75:25 a year earlier, because Coex fell. Management said any inventory gain is short-term and that price increases will flow through later as inventory turns.

qa_highlights.question: What utilisation is expected on the new Barjora line?
qa_highlights.answer: Target of at least 50% during the year, 'if not more'; management declined to give a detailed marketing or production plan.

qa_highlights.question: When will the RAK (UAE) line start and what volumes are expected in FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Trial production expected August-September 2026, commercial operations by Q3 FY27. Full utilisation of the two India lines expected next year, and UAE line above 50% in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Biggest concerns for FY28 sales volumes: raw materials, pricing or new entrants?
qa_highlights.answer: New entrants are not a major concern; the main risks are West Asia-driven polymer supply and specialised grade availability, and forex volatility. Pricing is pass-through but price elasticity limits it.

qa_highlights.question: What share of Biax revenue could come from 2-3 micron films in 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 2-3 micron as the modal mix is unrealistic near term; weighted average thickness is expected to move to about 4-5 micron within 2-3 years, with development efforts aimed higher than 10%.

qa_highlights.question: Raw material availability and visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: The company holds more than 3 months of imported raw material stock and is booking as material becomes available; European supply faces shipping cost and timing risk.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin expectation for the new line and Biax in FY27-FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give margin figures and said only volume expectations were shared; EBITDA break-even on the second line was not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Price increase sustainability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said industrial pricing varies with polymer prices and exchange rates; it wants prices to stabilise at a decent level, with specialties keeping a premium.

590051|2026-03.headline: Saksoft Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 4% YoY to INR 249 crore, with FY26 crossing INR 1,000 crore; management says pipeline is at a record ~USD 25 million.
590051|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was about INR 249 crore, up roughly 4% YoY and down about 0.8% QoQ, while EBITDA grew 24% YoY to INR 45 crore at an 18.19% margin. FY26 revenue was about INR 1,007 crore (up ~14%), EBITDA INR 187 crore (18.57% margin) and net profit INR 133 crore (up 23%). Management said decision-making by customers has slowed amid AI-related uncertainty, though the pipeline has grown sharply, and it guided to 30% growth as a stretch target with 14-15% as the floor. Management was clear that the AI theme is pervasive, and it expects some margin compression near term from AI-driven renewal price cuts.

qa_highlights.question: Would acquisitions be possible given the cash balance?

qa_highlights.question: Can 17-18% EBITDA margins be sustained in FY27?

qa_highlights.answer: Emerging verticals first, then BFSI and logistics. Digital commerce has the most headwinds.

qa_highlights.question: Why is employee cost falling and what will new senior hires add?
qa_highlights.answer: Headcount falls from AI productivity, AI agents in support functions, and a shift to outcome-based deals. Two senior hires were funded by repurposing costs of founders who exited after earnouts, so management does not expect employee cost to rise.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company letting go of tail clients, and how is client concentration changing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed it is exiting accounts without scale potential. Top 10 concentration fell from 58% to 56%, and it has no target to reduce it further.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue comes from AI and what is the AI deal-size trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not break out AI revenue. It said every project includes AI, and pure AI work is limited to AI co-innovation labs.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue comes from the US and how will it change?
qa_highlights.answer: US share is 52% (management corrected from 55%), with a target of at least 65% in two to three years.

risks_watch: Q2 FY27 is expected to be muted, and FY27 guidance of INR 1,200-1,250 crore requires a sharp H2 recovery from a flat H1.
Deal conversion is slow as the shift to larger outcome-based deals lengthens decision cycles.
Digital commerce faces the most headwinds, and BFSI revenue is flat QoQ.
Management did not quantify the number of accounts exited; it promised to send figures later. Pipeline figure of USD 28 million is also to be confirmed in writing.
Long-term INR 500 million target (FY30) was raised by an analyst but not addressed by management.
Competition from larger IT players moving down into smaller deals.
Appraisals next quarter could push up employee costs.
590051|2026-06.management_tone: Cautious on near-term demand and conversion, with management openly saying Q2 will be muted and that they do not expect improvement soon. It is more confident on the medium-term pipeline, AI productivity and the move to managed services, but it gave few hard numbers beyond the FY27 guidance it reiterated.
key_quotes: Decision making is getting delayed unfortunately, and we are pushing as hard as we can, but there is a limit to how much you can fight the industry
Numbers will come, growth will come, it won't happen overnight.
Nothing is normalizing.
Nothing is pilot, everything is in production.
